paras.en: Christ, appearing to the disciples after the resurrection, said: [[Luke 24:44|all things must needs|Necesse est]], he says, [[Luke 24:44|be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses and in the prophets and in the psalms, concerning me|impleri omnia quæ scripta sunt in lege Moysis et Prophetis et psalmis de me]]. After Christ had named the law of Moses and the Prophets, what need was there to make special mention of the psalms, as though the author of the psalms did not belong to the number of the Prophets? Only that in the psalms Christ is prophesied of in a special way, that is, more fully and more evidently than in the other writings of the Prophets. Therefore, as far as can be done, care must always be taken that the psalms be understood of Christ.

paras.t: Titulus autem psalmi præsentis est iste: In finem, in carminibus, intellectus David. Per David, sancti Prophetæ Christum frequenter intelligunt. Unde apud Jeremiam scriptum est: Non dominabuntur Jacob amplius alieni, sed servient Domino Deo suo, et David regi suo, quem suscitabo eis, id est Christo, ut omnes exponunt. Est itaque tituli sensus: Intellectus David, id est, sensus psalmi istius convenit Christo: intellectus, inquam, dirigens nos in finem, id est in Deum seu vitam æternam; in carminibus, ita ut Deo semper in adversis et prosperis gratiæ referantur, sicut et Christus egit ac docuit.
paras.en: Now the title of the present psalm is this: [[54:1|Unto the end, in verses, understanding for David.|In finem, in carminibus, intellectus David]] By David the holy Prophets often understand Christ. Hence it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 30:8|strangers shall no more rule over him|Non dominabuntur Jacob amplius alieni]] [Denis reads “over Jacob” for “over him”], [[Jer 30:9|But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up to them|sed servient Domino Deo suo, et David regi suo, quem suscitabo eis]], that is, Christ, as all expound it. So the sense of the title is this: [[54:1|understanding for David|Intellectus David]], that is, the sense of this psalm fits Christ: an [[54:1|understanding|intellectus]], I say, directing us [[54:1|unto the end|in finem]], that is, to God or to eternal life; [[54:1|in verses|in carminibus]] [carmina = “songs”, hence of praise and thanksgiving], so that thanks may always be given to God in adversity and in prosperity, as Christ also both did and taught.

paras.t: Igitur Dominus noster Jesus Christus, qui (ut ait Lucas) erat pernoctans in oratione Dei, secundum quod homo passibilis et viator, ante passionem sic ait: Exaudi, Deus Pater, seu Trinitas unus Deus, orationem meam, qua oro pro accidentali præmio conversationis, humiliationis passionisque meæ. Christus enim sua humilitate et morte, sibi ipsi promeruit præmium accidentale, non essentiale, videlicet judiciariam potestatem, festinatam resurrectionem, corporis glorificationem et ascensionem. Propter quod ipsemet de se ipso et Deo Patre loquens, sic ait: Potestatem dedit ei et judicium facere, quia Filius hominis est. Et Apostolus: Humiliavit semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis: propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum, etc. Hinc quoque in Isaia de Christo prædictum est, Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur: non utique gaudio præmii essentialis, quia hoc Christus non meruit; sed accidentalis, quod Christus partim habet, saltem extensive, vel quantum ad manifestationem, ex salvatione electorum. Unde et regnum militantis Ecclesiæ, seu multiplicatio fidelium, Christo pro præmio apud Isaiam promittitur: Si posuerit animam suam pro peccato, videbit semen longævum, et voluntas Domini in manu ejus dirigetur. Et iterum Dominus de Christo dicit: In scientia sua justificabit ipse servus meus multos, et iniquitates eorum ipse portabit; ideo dispertiam ei plurimos, et fortium dividet spolia: id est, multos ad ejus fidem convertam, et dæmonum spolia, hoc est animas quæ factæ sunt dæmonum prædæ per peccatum originale vel actuale, eripiet, non omnium, sed electorum, quemadmodum ait per Osee: Ero mors tua, o mors; morsus tuus ero, inferne.
paras.en: So our Lord Jesus Christ, who (as Luke says) [[Luke 6:12|passed the whole night in the prayer of God|erat pernoctans in oratione Dei]], speaks thus before His passion, as man, capable of suffering and a wayfarer [viator: one still on the way to the goal, not yet in the state of final glory]: [[54:2|Hear, O God|Exaudi, Deus]] the Father, or Trinity, one God, [[54:2|my prayer|orationem meam]], with which I pray for the accidental reward of my life among men, of my humiliation and of my passion. For Christ by His humility and death merited for Himself an accidental reward, not the essential one [the essential reward of the blessed is the vision and enjoyment of God, which Christ's soul had from the first instant; an accidental reward is a further good or glory added to it]: namely, the power of judging, a hastened resurrection, the glorification of His body, and the ascension. Wherefore He Himself, speaking of Himself and of God the Father, says thus: [[John 5:27|hath given him power to do judgment, because he is the Son of man|Potestatem dedit ei et judicium facere, quia Filius hominis est]]. And the Apostle: [[Phil 2:8|He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross|Humiliavit semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis]]: [[Phil 2:9|For which cause, God also hath exalted him|propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum]], etc. Hence too it was foretold of Christ in Isaias: [[Is 53:11|Because his soul hath laboured, he shall see and be filled|Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur]]: not, to be sure, with the joy of the essential reward, since Christ did not merit this, but of the accidental reward, which Christ has in part, at least extensively, or as regards its manifestation, from the salvation of the elect. Hence also the kingdom of the Church militant, or the multiplying of the faithful, is promised to Christ as a reward in Isaias: [[Is 53:10|if he shall lay down his life for sin, he shall see a longlived seed, and the will of the Lord shall be prosperous in his hand|Si posuerit animam suam pro peccato, videbit semen longævum, et voluntas Domini in manu ejus dirigetur]]. And again the Lord says of Christ: [[Is 53:11|by his knowledge shall this my just servant justify many, and he shall bear their iniquities|In scientia sua justificabit ipse servus meus multos, et iniquitates eorum ipse portabit]]; [[Is 53:12|Therefore will I distribute to him very many, and he shall divide the spoils of the strong|ideo dispertiam ei plurimos, et fortium dividet spolia]]: that is, I will convert many to faith in Him, and He shall snatch away the spoils of the demons, that is, the souls that became the prey of demons through original or actual sin; not of all, but of the elect, as He says by Osee: [[Osee 13:14|O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite|Ero mors tua, o mors; morsus tuus ero, inferne]].

paras.t: Et ne despexeris deprecationem meam, quam feci pro his pro quibus incarnatus et passus sum. Unde Christus dixit ad Petrum in persona Ecclesiæ: Ego pro te rogavi, ut non deficiat fides tua. Intende mihi: id est, respiciendo adimple precem qua pro mei ipsius liberatione a morte, seu resuscitatione, precatus sum, dicens: Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora. Et exaudi me orantem pro nominis tui honorifica clarificatione, videlicet ut ab omnibus agnoscaris ac venereris. Hoc enim oravit Christus: Pater, inquiens, clarifica nomen tuum.
paras.en: [[54:2|And despise not my supplication|Et ne despexeris deprecationem meam]], which I have made for those for whom I became incarnate and suffered. Hence Christ said to Peter, in the person of the Church: [[Luke 22:32|I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not|Ego pro te rogavi, ut non deficiat fides tua]]. [[54:3|Be attentive to me|Intende mihi]]: that is, look upon and fulfil the prayer that I prayed for my own deliverance from death, or raising up, saying: [[John 12:27|Father, save me from this hour|Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora]]. [[54:3|And hear me|Et exaudi me]] as I pray for the honourable glorifying of Thy name, namely that Thou be acknowledged and worshipped by all. For Christ prayed this: [[John 12:28|Father|Pater]], He says, [[John 12:28|glorify thy name|clarifica nomen tuum]].

paras.t: Contristatus sum in exercitatione mea: id est, in prædicando atque miracula faciendo, dolui de cæcitate et ingratitudine Judæorum: quemadmodum scriptum est, Contristatus est Jesus super cæcitate cordis eorum. Hæc autem tristitia inordinata non fuit, sed ex vera caritate manavit, quoniam malis atque perversis condoluit. Propterea quoque Salomon asserit: Non contristabit justum quidquid ei acciderit. Itemque quod de Christo prædictum est, Non erit tristis neque turbulentus, intelligendum est de sæculari et inordinata tristitia, quæ (teste Apostolo) mortem operatur; et de qua in Ecclesiastico legitur: Tristitiam longe expelle a te; multos enim occidit tristitia, et non est utilitas in ea. Passione quoque instante, cœpit Jesus pavere et tædere, ac dicere: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem.
paras.en: [[54:3|I am grieved in my exercise|Contristatus sum in exercitatione mea]]: that is, in preaching and working miracles I grieved over the blindness and ingratitude of the Jews, as it is written that Jesus was [[Mark 3:5|grieved for the blindness of their hearts|Contristatus est Jesus super cæcitate cordis eorum]]. Now this sadness was not inordinate, but flowed from true charity, since He grieved with the wicked and perverse. Hence too what Solomon declares, [[Prov 12:21|Whatsoever shall befall the just man, shall not make him sad|Non contristabit justum quidquid ei acciderit]], and likewise what was foretold of Christ, [[Is 42:4|He shall not be sad, nor troublesome|Non erit tristis neque turbulentus]] [the margin gives Is. xiii, 4; the words are Is 42:4], are to be understood of worldly and inordinate sadness, which (as the Apostle witnesses) [[2 Cor 7:10|worketh death|mortem operatur]], and of which we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 30:24|drive away sadness far from thee|Tristitiam longe expelle a te]]; [[Ecclus 30:25|For sadness hath killed many, and there is no profit in it|multos enim occidit tristitia, et non est utilitas in ea]]. When His passion was at hand, too, Jesus [[Mark 14:33|began to fear and to be heavy|cœpit Jesus pavere et tædere]], and to say: [[Mark 14:34|My soul is sorrowful even unto death|Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem]].

paras.t: Et conturbatus sum a voce inimici: id est, propter detractiones et accusationes ac falsas interpretationes populi Judæorum, opera mea atque doctrinam blasphemantium, contemnentium, et Beelzebub adscribentium, turbatus sum, non inordinata turbatione, sed ad rationabilem iram, timorem seu tristitiam, aut similem vehementem affectionem libere motus sum: quemadmodum apud Marcum dicitur, Circumspiciens eos Jesus cum ira, etc. Alibi quoque: Nunc anima mea turbata est. Et in ipsa Cœna turbatus est Jesus, sicut Evangelista testatur: Quum hæc, inquiens, dixisset Jesus, turbatus est spiritu, et protestatus est, et dixit: Unus vestrum me tradet.
paras.en: [[54:3|And am troubled|Et conturbatus sum]] [[54:4|At the voice of the enemy|a voce inimici]]: that is, on account of the detractions and accusations and false interpretations of the Jewish people, who blasphemed and despised my works and teaching and ascribed them to Beelzebub, I was troubled; not with an inordinate trouble, but I was freely moved to a reasonable anger, fear or sadness, or some like vehement affection: as is said in Mark, [[Mark 3:5|looking round about on them with anger|Circumspiciens eos Jesus cum ira]], etc. And elsewhere: [[John 12:27|Now is my soul troubled|Nunc anima mea turbata est]]. And at the Supper itself Jesus was troubled, as the Evangelist witnesses, saying: [[John 13:21|When Jesus had said these things, he was troubled in spirit; and he testified, and said|Quum hæc, inquiens, dixisset Jesus, turbatus est spiritu, et protestatus est, et dixit]]: [[John 13:21|one of you shall betray me|Unus vestrum me tradet]].

paras.t: Conturbatus sum etiam et a tribulatione peccatoris, id est ex consideratione amarissimæ passionis mihi instantis: quemadmodum legitur, Factus Jesus in agonia, prolixius orabat, et factus est sudor ejus sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentes in terram. Et ad Hebræos de Christo ait Apostolus: Cum clamore valido et lacrimis orationem obtulit. Denique in ipsa passione conturbatus est Jesus secundum modum prædictum, a tribulatione peccatoris, id est a persecutione populi ipsum conspuentis, flagellantis, transfigentis et occidentis.
paras.en: I was troubled also [[54:4|and at the tribulation of the sinner|et a tribulatione peccatoris]], that is, by the thought of the most bitter passion at hand for me: as we read, [[Luke 22:43|being in an agony, he prayed the longer|Factus Jesus in agonia, prolixius orabat]], [[Luke 22:44|And his sweat became as drops of blood, trickling down upon the ground|et factus est sudor ejus sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentes in terram]]. And to the Hebrews the Apostle says of Christ: [[Heb 5:7|with a strong cry and tears|Cum clamore valido et lacrimis]] He offered up prayer. Lastly, in the passion itself Jesus was troubled in the way described, [[54:4|at the tribulation of the sinner|a tribulatione peccatoris]], that is, by the persecution of the people that spat on Him, scourged Him, pierced Him and killed Him.

paras.t: Quoniam declinaverunt in me iniquitates: id est, Judæi multa mihi scelera imposuerunt: quemadmodum ab Evangelista dictum est, Cœperunt autem illum accusare, dicentes: Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram, et prohibentem tributa dari Cæsari. Et iterum: Stabant, inquit, principes sacerdotum et Scribæ constanter accusantes eum. Sed et ante passionem frequenter calumniabantur eum Judæi. Propter quod scriptum est: Dicebant, Quoniam in furorem versus est. Et rursus: Dæmonium habet et insanit; quid eum auditis? Unde superius de Christo dixit Psalmista: Quoniam declinaverunt in te mala, cogitaverunt consilia quæ non potuerunt stabilire. Et apud Osee Christus ait: Vastabuntur, quia prævaricati sunt in me; et ego redemi eos, et locuti sunt contra me mendacia. Et in ira molesti erant mihi: id est, perversi incredulique Judæi, ex ira quam conceperunt adversum me, persecuti sunt me: quorum persecutio mihi erat molesta, non quia adversa et dura invitus impatienterque pertulerim, sed quia eorum cæcitati condolui.
paras.en: [[54:4|For they have cast iniquities upon me|Quoniam declinaverunt in me iniquitates]]: that is, the Jews laid many crimes to my charge; as was said by the Evangelist, [[Luke 23:2|And they began to accuse him, saying: We have found this man perverting our nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar|Cœperunt autem illum accusare, dicentes: Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram, et prohibentem tributa dari Cæsari]]. And again: [[Luke 23:10|And the chief priests and the scribes stood by, earnestly accusing him|Stabant, inquit, principes sacerdotum et Scribæ constanter accusantes eum]]. But even before the passion the Jews often slandered Him; wherefore it is written: [[Mark 3:21|For they said: He is become mad|Dicebant, Quoniam in furorem versus est]]. And again: [[John 10:20|He hath a devil and is mad. Why hear you him?|Dæmonium habet et insanit; quid eum auditis?]]? Hence the Psalmist said of Christ earlier: [[Ps 20:12|For they have intended evils against thee: they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish.|Quoniam declinaverunt in te mala, cogitaverunt consilia quæ non potuerunt stabilire]] [the same verb, declinaverunt, that the Douay-Rheims renders “cast” in this verse]. And in Osee Christ says: [[Osee 7:13|they shall be wasted because they have transgressed against me: and I redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me|Vastabuntur, quia prævaricati sunt in me; et ego redemi eos, et locuti sunt contra me mendacia]]. [[54:4|and in wrath they were troublesome to me|Et in ira molesti erant mihi]]: that is, the perverse and unbelieving Jews, out of the anger they had conceived against me, persecuted me; and their persecution was troublesome to me, not because I bore hard and adverse things unwillingly and impatiently, but because I grieved over their blindness.

paras.t: Cor meum conturbatum est in me, ex magna affectione, non ex aliqua deordinatione, sicut expositum est. Unde superius dictum est: Factum est cor meum tanquam cera liquescens. Et formido mortis cecidit super me, id est, naturalis timor de morte instante fuit in me, præsertim quando ter Patrem oravi, ut si fieri posset, transferret a me calicem passionis.
paras.en: [[54:5|My heart is troubled within me|Cor meum conturbatum est in me]], from great affection, not from any disorder, as has been explained. Hence it was said earlier: [[Ps 21:15|My heart is become like wax melting|Factum est cor meum tanquam cera liquescens]]. [[54:5|and the fear of death is fallen upon me|Et formido mortis cecidit super me]], that is, a natural fear of the death at hand was in me, above all when I thrice prayed the Father that, if it could be, He would take the chalice of the passion from me[[Matt 26:39||]][[Matt 26:42||]][[Matt 26:44||]].

paras.t: Timor animæ seu interioris appetitus, et tremor corporis ex interiori timore causatus, venerunt super me, non sine prædeliberatione, sed ex prævia ratione. Passiones namque appetitus sensitivi, in Christo rationem non prævenerunt, sed sponte assumebantur a Christo, atque ad rationis imperium cessaverunt. Hujusmodi autem timor et tremor irruerunt præsertim in Christum, quando ex inæstimabili mentis angustia factus est sudor ejus sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentes in terram. Et contexerunt me tenebræ: id est, magnæ et pœnalissimæ adversitates me penitus operuerunt, quoniam in corpore et anima plenus fui doloribus, quia in omnibus membris corporis et animæ viribus patiebar. Vel sic: Contexerunt me tenebræ, id est, peccatores peccatis obtenebrati irruerunt undique in me. De peccatoribus namque conversis ait Apostolus: Fuistis aliquando tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino. Propter quod ante de Christo inductum est: Quoniam circumdederunt me canes multi.
paras.en: [[54:6|Fear|Timor]] of the soul, or of the inner appetite, [[54:6|and trembling|et tremor]] of the body caused by the inner fear, [[54:6|are come upon me|venerunt super me]], not without forethought, but out of reason going before. For the passions of the sensitive appetite [that is, movements of the lower, bodily powers of the soul, such as fear and sorrow] did not in Christ run ahead of reason, but were taken up by Christ of His own will, and ceased at the command of reason. Now such fear and trembling fell upon Christ above all when, from the inestimable anguish of His mind, [[Luke 22:44|his sweat became as drops of blood, trickling down upon the ground|sudor ejus sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentes in terram]]. [[54:6|and darkness hath covered me|Et contexerunt me tenebræ]]: that is, great and most painful adversities covered me completely, since I was full of sorrows in body and soul, for I suffered in all the members of the body and the powers of the soul. Or thus: [[54:6|darkness hath covered me|Contexerunt me tenebræ]], that is, sinners darkened by their sins rushed upon me from every side. For the Apostle says of converted sinners: [[Eph 5:8|you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord|Fuistis aliquando tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino]]. Wherefore it was put earlier in the mouth of Christ: [[Ps 21:17|For many dogs have encompassed me|Quoniam circumdederunt me canes multi]].

paras.t: Et dixi, mentaliter cogitando, vel ore loquendo: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut columbæ, et volabo, et requiescam? Christus pennas contemplationis et caritatis ab exordio incarnationis incessabiliter habuit. Quas ergo pennas se desiderare insinuat? nisi, vel pennas resurrectionis et ascensionis, quibus de tumulo volet ad inferos, de inferno ad credentes in mundo atque ad cœlos, et ad Patris dexteram requiescat; vel pennas fugæ a Judæis, donec impleretur passionis suæ tempus præordinatum a Deo, secundum quod Joannes evangelista fatetur, dicendo: Jesus ergo jam non in palam ambulabat apud Judæos, sed in desertis locis morabatur cum discipulis suis, juxta civitatem quæ dicitur Ephrem. Ad hæc igitur loca Christus penna fugæ volavit, id est, velociter transiit, quia transiens per medium illorum ibat (quum eum lapidare tentarent et præcipitare, quemadmodum scriptum est), id est, invisibiliter manus Judæorum elapsus est. In his quoque locis Christus a Judæorum tumultu et persecutionibus requievit.
paras.en: [[54:7|And I said|Et dixi]], thinking in my mind or speaking with my mouth: [[54:7|Who will give me wings like a dove, and I will fly and be at rest?|Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut columbæ, et volabo, et requiescam?]]? Christ had the wings of contemplation and of charity without ceasing from the beginning of the incarnation. What wings, then, does He hint that He desires? Either the wings of the resurrection and ascension, by which He might fly from the tomb to the underworld, from hell to the believers in the world and to the heavens, and rest at the right hand of the Father; or the wings of flight from the Jews, until the time of His passion foreordained by God should be fulfilled, as John the Evangelist declares, saying: [[John 11:54|Wherefore Jesus walked no more openly among the Jews|Jesus ergo jam non in palam ambulabat apud Judæos]], but stayed in desert places with His disciples, near [[John 11:54|a city that is called Ephrem|civitatem quæ dicitur Ephrem]] [the margin gives Joann. xi, 51; the words are John 11:54]. To these places, then, Christ flew on the wing of flight, that is, passed over swiftly; for [[Luke 4:30|he passing through the midst of them, went his way|transiens per medium illorum ibat]] (when they tried to stone Him[[John 8:59||]] and to cast Him down headlong[[Luke 4:29||]], as it is written), that is, He slipped invisibly out of the hands of the Jews. In these places too Christ rested from the tumult and persecutions of the Jews.

paras.t: Ideo subdit: Ecce elongavi me a Judæis me persequentibus, fugiens ad loca deserti; et mansi cum discipulis meis in solitudine seu deserto. Præterea, antequam Christus prædicare incepit, ductus est a Spiritu utique Sancto in desertum; eratque cum bestiis, et angeli ministrabant ei.
paras.en: Therefore He adds: [[54:8|Lo, I have gone far off|Ecce elongavi me]] from the Jews who persecuted me, [[54:8|flying away|fugiens]] to the places of the desert; [[54:8|and I abode|et mansi]] with my disciples [[54:8|in the wilderness|in solitudine]], or desert. Moreover, before Christ began to preach, He [[Matt 4:1|was led by the spirit|ductus est a Spiritu]], the Holy Spirit, that is, [[Matt 4:1|into the desert|in desertum]]; [[Mark 1:13|And he was with beasts: and the angels ministered to him|eratque cum bestiis, et angeli ministrabant ei]].

paras.t: Expectabam eum qui salvum me fecit: id est, ego Christus ordinationem Dei Patris præstolabar, ut illa compleretur in me, quatenus tempore ab eo præordinato me manifestarem, atque occiderer. Non enim fugi ne morerer, qui ad hoc veni ut mundum moriendo redimerem; sed ne ante præfixum tempus occumberem. Propter quod evangelista Joannes sæpius dicit: Nemo misit in eum manum, quia nondum venit hora ejus. Sic itaque, Expectabam eum qui salvum me fecit, a pusillanimitate spiritus, id est ab excessivo timore mortis et mundi, et tempestate, id est ab impetuoso animi motu et turbulentia mentis. Hoc Christus affirmat, non quod unquam fuerit in eo pusillanimitas spiritus et tempestas, quum utrumque sit vitiosum; sed quia anima ejus divina virtute præservata fuit a motibus illis.
paras.en: [[54:9|I waited for him that hath saved me|Expectabam eum qui salvum me fecit]]: that is, I, Christ, awaited the ordinance of God the Father, that it might be fulfilled in me, so that at the time foreordained by Him I might make myself known and be put to death. For I did not flee so as not to die, I who came for this, to redeem the world by dying[[John 18:5||]][[John 18:8||]]; but so as not to fall before the appointed time. Wherefore John the Evangelist says more than once: [[John 7:30|no man laid hands on him, because his hour was not yet come|Nemo misit in eum manum, quia nondum venit hora ejus]][[John 8:20||]]. So then: [[54:9|I waited for him that hath saved me|Expectabam eum qui salvum me fecit]] [[54:9|from pusillanimity of spirit|a pusillanimitate spiritus]], that is, from excessive fear of death and of the world, [[54:9|and a storm|et tempestate]], that is, from violent movement of the soul and turbulence of mind. Christ says this not because there was ever in Him pusillanimity of spirit or storm, since both are vicious, but because His soul was preserved by divine power from those movements.

paras.t: Deinde Christus orat pro dejectione adversariorum suorum, secundum sensum in præcedentium psalmorum expositione clare inductum : et ait : Præcipita, Domine Pater, et divide linguas eorum, id est, confunde, falsifica, condemna et destrue verba Judæorum mihi detrahentium, et de modo capiendi et occidendi me consilia vana habentium. Horum linguas, id est sermones, præcipita, dejice, et ab effectu optato ne differas impedire, non ut non occidant me, sed ut non detinear in morte, neque ab hominum cognitione abscondar: sed resuscita me, et nomen meum clarifica, eos vero in æternum præcipita, et in præsenti vita disperge, ita ut, sicut ipsi sibi imprecati sunt, veniat sanguis meus super eos filiosque eorum. Hæc omnia jam in Judæis impleta videmus. Intendebant namque Judæi sic Christum occidere, ut neque resurgeret, neque de cetero in hominum memoria remaneret, quemadmodum apud Jeremiam dicunt : Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra. Sed hujus oppositum accidit, quoniam Christus per mortem omnimode clarificari honorificarique meruit, juxta illud Apostoli : Videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis gloria et honore coronatum, ut gratia Dei pro omnibus gustaret mortem.
paras.en: Next Christ prays for the casting down of his adversaries, in the sense clearly brought out in the exposition of the preceding psalms; and he says: [[54:10|Cast down, O Lord|Præcipita, Domine]] Father, [[54:10|and divide their tongues|et divide linguas eorum]]: that is, confound, prove false, condemn and destroy the words of the Jews who speak against me and who hold vain counsels about how to seize and kill me. Cast down their tongues, that is, their speeches; throw them down, and do not delay to hinder them from the outcome they desire: not that they may not kill me, but that I may not be held in death, nor be hidden from the knowledge of men[[Ps 82:5||]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxii, 5 here, where the enemies say: let the name of Israel be remembered no more]; but raise me up and glorify my name[[John 17:5||]]; and cast them down for ever, and scatter them in the present life, so that, as they called down upon themselves, my blood may come upon them and their children[[Matt 27:25||]]. All these things we now see fulfilled in the Jews. For the Jews meant so to kill Christ that he should neither rise again nor remain thereafter in the memory of men, as they say in Jeremias: Let us [[Jer 11:19|cut him off from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more|Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra]]. But the opposite of this happened, since through his death Christ merited to be glorified and honoured in every way, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Heb 2:9|we see Jesus|Videmus Jesum]] [[Heb 2:9|for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour: that, through the grace of God he might taste death for all|propter passionem mortis gloria et honore coronatum, ut gratia Dei pro omnibus gustaret mortem]].

paras.t: Et hæc ideo oro, quoniam ego Christus, qui cuncta cognosco, et qui scivi quid esset in homine, vidi iniquitatem, id est propositum interficiendi me, et contradictionem adversus me et meam doctrinam, in civitate, id est in populo in Jerosolyma commorante : vel, Contradictionem eorum inter se mutuo, quia nonnulli resistebant volentibus me occidere. Unde Nicodemus dixit adversus Judæos incredulos : Numquid lex nostra judicat aliquem, nisi audierit ab ipso prius, et cognoverit quid faciat ? Et rursus scriptum est : Multi ex principibus crediderunt in Jesum, videlicet ante passionem.
paras.en: And I pray for this, [[54:10|for|quoniam]] I, Christ, who know all things and who knew what was in man, [[54:10|have seen iniquity|vidi iniquitatem]], that is, the purpose of killing me, [[54:10|and contradiction|et contradictionem]] against me and my teaching, [[54:10|in the city|in civitate]], that is, in the people dwelling in Jerusalem; or, [[54:10|contradiction|contradictionem]] among themselves, one with another, since some resisted those who wished to kill me. Hence Nicodemus said against the unbelieving Jews: [[John 7:51|Doth our law judge any man, unless it first hear him and know what he doth?|Numquid lex nostra judicat aliquem, nisi audierit ab ipso prius, et cognoverit quid faciat]] And again it is written: [[John 12:42|many of the chief men also believed in him|Multi ex principibus crediderunt in Jesum]] [the margin gives John xi, 45, where many of the Jews believed; Denis's words are those of John 12:42], namely before the Passion.

paras.t: Die ac nocte, id est indesinenter, circumdabit eam super muros ejus iniquitas : id est, in principalibus populi Judæorum, qui esse debuerant firmamentum et murus aliorum, confirmando eos in bono, fuit magna et summa malitia, quoniam principes sacerdotum alios instigaverunt ad Christi occisionem. Vel, Circumdabit eam super muros ejus iniquitas, quia ad litteram custodes murorum Jerusalem, quasi in canticum verterunt Jesum Christum, assidue eum deridendo, sicut inferius clarius dicitur : Adversum me loquebantur qui sedebant in porta, et in me psallebant qui bibebant vinum.
paras.en: [[54:11|Day and night|Die ac nocte]], that is, unceasingly, [[54:11|shall iniquity surround it upon its walls|circumdabit eam super muros ejus iniquitas]]: that is, in the chief men of the Jewish people, who ought to have been the support and wall of the others by confirming them in good, there was great and utmost malice, since the chief priests stirred up the others to the slaying of Christ[[Matt 27:20||]][[Mark 15:11||]]. Or, [[54:11|shall iniquity surround it upon its walls|circumdabit eam super muros ejus iniquitas]], because literally the watchmen of the walls of Jerusalem turned Jesus Christ as it were into a song, continually mocking him, as is said more clearly further on: [[Ps 68:13|They that sat in the gate spoke against me: and they that drank wine made me their song|Adversum me loquebantur qui sedebant in porta, et in me psallebant qui bibebant vinum]].

paras.t: Et labor in medio ejus et injustitia, id est, pœnalis malitia et injustitia fuit quasi in toto populo civitatis Jerusalem. Peccatum enim labor vocatur, quoniam (Augustino teste) animus inordinatus sibi ipsi est pœna. Veram enim quietem et pacem excludit, et remorsum conscientiæ habet adjunctum. Magnus labor et injustitia maxima erat in medio civitatis seu populi hujus, quando respondens universus populus, dixit ad præsidem : Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros.
paras.en: [[54:11|and in the midst thereof are labour|Et labor in medio ejus]] [[54:12|And injustice|et injustitia]]: that is, painful malice and injustice was as it were in the whole people of the city of Jerusalem. For sin is called *labour* [Latin *labor*, toil, hardship], since (as Augustine bears witness) the disordered mind is a punishment to itself: for it shuts out true rest and peace, and has remorse of conscience joined to it. Great labour and the greatest injustice were in the midst of the city, or of this people, when [[Matt 27:25|the whole people answering, said|respondens universus populus, dixit]] to the governor: [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]].

paras.t: Et non defecit de plateis ejus, id est de habitatoribus platearum Jerusalem, usura et dolus. Judæi enim avari atque dolosi fuerunt : propter quod Christus de templo vendentes et ementes ejecit. Et apud Michæam legitur : Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem; et alibi, A minore usque ad majorem omnes avaritiæ student.
paras.en: [[54:12|have not departed from its streets|Et non defecit de plateis ejus]], that is, from the dwellers in the streets of Jerusalem, [[54:12|usury and deceit|usura et dolus]]. For the Jews were greedy and deceitful: for which reason Christ cast out of the temple those that sold and bought[[Matt 21:12||]]. And in Micheas we read: [[Mich 7:2|every one hunteth his brother to death|Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem]]; and elsewhere: [[Jer 6:13|from the least of them even to the greatest, all are given to covetousness|A minore usque ad majorem omnes avaritiæ student]].

paras.t: Consequenter Christus peccatum traditoris sui exaggerat. Quoniam si inimicus meus, id est, qui nunquam ante amicus meus fuisset, vel cui ego aliquid mali fecissem, vel cui tot signa dilectionis non ostendissem, maledixisset mihi, vendendo atque prodendo me hostibus meis; sustinuissem utique, id est, tolerabilius reputassem, et minus corde afflictus fuissem; neque tam dire vindicassem sicut ultus sum peccatum Judæ, quem justo judicio desperare, et se ipsum laqueo necare permisi : quod erat vindicta gravissima in præsenti, quam sequitur pœna durissima in futuro. Tanto equidem gravius peccatum Deus ulciscitur, quanto peccantem in graviora peccata cadere patitur.
paras.en: Next Christ makes much of the sin of his betrayer. [[54:13|For if my enemy|Quoniam si inimicus meus]], that is, one who had never before been my friend, or to whom I had done some evil, or to whom I had not shown so many signs of love, [[54:13|had reviled me|maledixisset mihi]] by selling and betraying me to my foes, [[54:13|I would verily have borne with it|sustinuissem utique]]: that is, I would have reckoned it more bearable and been less afflicted in heart; nor would I have avenged it as terribly as I avenged the sin of Judas, whom by a just judgment I allowed to despair and to kill himself with a halter[[Matt 27:5||]]: which was the heaviest vengeance in the present, and the harshest punishment follows it in the future. For God punishes a sin the more heavily, the more he lets the sinner fall into graver sins.

paras.t: Et si is qui oderat me, id est, qui se inimicum meum fuisse palam dixisset et ostendisset, super me magna locutus fuisset, id est, verba supplantationis et conculcationis contra me adversariis meis dixisset; abscondissem me forsitan ab eo, id est, tam familiaris vel præsens sibi non exstitissem ut exstiti Judæ, a quo etiam non abscondi me sicut interdum a Judæis mihi aperte insidiantibus me abscondi. Non tamen putandum est, quod Christus finaliter se aliquo modo occultasset quoniam mortem evadere noluit.
paras.en: [[54:13|And if he that hated me|Et si is qui oderat me]], that is, one who had openly said and shown that he was my enemy, [[54:13|had spoken great things against me|super me magna locutus fuisset]], that is, had spoken to my adversaries words to trip me up and trample me down, [[54:13|I would perhaps have hidden my self from him|abscondissem me forsitan ab eo]]: that is, I would not have been as familiar with him or as present to him as I was to Judas, from whom I did not even hide myself, as I sometimes hid myself from the Jews who openly lay in wait for me[[John 8:59||]]. Yet it is not to be thought that Christ would in the end have hidden himself in any way, since he did not wish to escape death.

paras.t: Tu vero, o Juda, homo unanimis mihi, quantum ad apparentiam et verborum professionem, et etiam forte secundum veritatem, quantum ad tempus; dux meus, id est, quem ego cum aliis Apostolis constitui ducem populi mei, mittens te ante passionem cum illis prædicare regnum Dei et sanare infirmos, et notus meus, tanquam cohabitans familiarisque mihi.
paras.en: [[54:14|But thou|Tu vero]], O Judas, [[54:14|a man of one mind|homo unanimis]] with me, as to appearance and the profession of words, and perhaps even in truth, for a time; [[54:14|my guide|dux meus]] [Latin *dux*, which also means leader], that is, whom I, with the other Apostles, appointed leader of my people, sending thee before the Passion with them [[Luke 9:2|to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick|prædicare regnum Dei et sanare infirmos]]; [[54:14|and my familiar|et notus meus]], as one living with me and intimate with me.

paras.t: Qui simul mecum dulces capiebas cibos, eo tempore quo procurator meus fuisti, comedens panem in mensa mecum qui caritative ac dulciter tecum vescebar. Præsertim autem in Cœna novissima accepit Judas a Christo et cum Christo dulces cibos, id est corpus ejus et sanguinem. In domo Dei, id est in synagogis Judæorum et templo Jerusalem, seu congregatione fidelium discipulorum meorum, ambulavimus, id est conversati sumus, cum consensu. Eo etenim modo ambulaverunt Christus et Judas cum consensu, quo unanimes erant.
paras.en: [[54:15|Who didst take sweetmeats together with me|Qui simul mecum dulces capiebas cibos]], at the time when thou wast my steward [Latin *procurator*: Judas kept the common purse], eating bread at table with me, who ate with thee lovingly and sweetly. But above all at the Last Supper Judas received from Christ and with Christ sweet food[[John 13:26||]], that is, his body and blood. [[54:15|in the house of God|In domo Dei]], that is, in the synagogues of the Jews and the temple of Jerusalem, or in the congregation of my faithful disciples, [[54:15|we walked|ambulavimus]], that is, we lived together, [[54:15|with consent|cum consensu]]. For Christ and Judas walked with consent in the same way as they were of one mind.

paras.t: Patet autem ex his, illas persecutiones atque injurias esse molestiores, quæ a propinquis et amicis seu familiaribus inferuntur, præcipue quando de eorum dilectione præsumimus, et aliud nihil nisi bonum apud eos meruimus. Propter quod passio Christi amarior fuit, quia a discipulo vendebatur, et a populo electo ac peculiari occidebatur. Et ideo per Michæam ait : Popule meus, quid feci tibi? aut quid molestus fui tibi? Et alibi : Quid ultra debui facere vineæ meæ, et non feci?
paras.en: It is clear from this that those persecutions and injuries are the more grievous which are inflicted by kinsmen and friends or intimates, above all when we presume on their love and have deserved nothing but good from them. For this reason the Passion of Christ was the more bitter, because he was sold by a disciple and slain by a chosen and peculiar people. And so he says by Micheas: [[Mich 6:3|O my people, what have I done to thee, or in what have I molested thee?|Popule meus, quid feci tibi? aut quid molestus fui tibi?]] And elsewhere: [[Is 5:4|What is there that I ought to do more to my vineyard, that I have not done to it?|Quid ultra debui facere vineæ meæ, et non feci?]]

paras.t: Veniat mors super illos, qui discipulum meum sic corruperunt, vel ei pares exsistunt. Hoc Christus ait non desiderando, sed prænuntiando, nisi intelligatur hoc desiderare zelo justitiæ, secundum ordinem divinæ æquitatis, non autem inordinato appetitu vindictæ. Veniat, inquam, mors animæ et corporis super illos, videlicet ut gratia Dei priventur, et ab adversariis trucidentur : quemadmodum ab exercitu Romanorum Judæi occisi sunt. Et descendant in infernum viventes, in die judicii cum corpore et anima æternaliter condemnandi. Hoc enim promeruerunt. Quoniam nequitiæ, id est multæ et perversæ malitiæ, in habitaculis eorum, id est in cordibus ipsorum, in quibus homines cogitando morantur ; vel, In habitaculis eorum, id est in habitatoribus tabernaculorum ; in medio eorum : ita quod omnes communiter nequiter agunt.
paras.en: [[54:16|Let death come upon them|Veniat mors super illos]] who so corrupted my disciple, or who are like him. Christ says this not desiring it but foretelling it; unless it be understood that he desires it out of zeal for justice, according to the order of divine equity, and not from a disordered craving for vengeance. Let death, I say, of soul and body come upon them: that is, that they be deprived of the grace of God and slaughtered by their enemies, as the Jews were slain by the army of the Romans. [[54:16|and let them go down alive into hell|Et descendant in infernum viventes]], to be condemned eternally in body and soul at the day of judgment; for this they have deserved. [[54:16|For there is wickedness|Quoniam nequitiæ]], that is, many and perverse malices, [[54:16|in their dwellings|in habitaculis eorum]], that is, in their hearts, in which men dwell by their thoughts; or, [[54:16|in their dwellings|In habitaculis eorum]], that is, in those who dwell in the tents; [[54:16|in the midst of them|in medio eorum]]: so that all alike act wickedly.

paras.t: Ego autem, Christus Filius Dei, ad Deum clamavi : sicut in psalmi hujus exordio patuit ; et Dominus, id est Deus Pater seu Trinitas sancta, salvavit me, de morte ad immortalem vitam resuscitans me : juxta illud Apostoli de Christo, Qui in diebus carnis suæ preces supplicationesque fundens ad eum, qui possit illum a morte salvum facere, exauditus est pro sua reverentia.
paras.en: [[54:17|But I|Ego autem]], Christ the Son of God, [[54:17|have cried to God|ad Deum clamavi]], as was clear at the opening of this psalm; [[54:17|and the Lord|et Dominus]], that is, God the Father or the Holy Trinity, [[54:17|will save me|salvavit me]] [Denis reads *salvavit*, "hath saved"; the Vulgate has *salvabit*, "will save"], raising me from death to immortal life: according to that saying of the Apostle about Christ: [[Heb 5:7|Who in the days of his flesh|Qui in diebus carnis suæ]], [[Heb 5:7|offering up prayers and supplications to him that was able to save him from death, was heard for his reverence|preces supplicationesque fundens ad eum, qui possit illum a morte salvum facere, exauditus est pro sua reverentia]].

paras.t: Vespere, scilicet in nocte Cœnæ, et mane, id est in die Parasceves, et meridie, pendens in cruce, narrabo mente, et annuntiabo ore : id est, veritatem dixi, salutarem sapientiam docui, causam meam ac precem Domino obtuli, pro crucifixoribus exoravi, et animam meam Patri commendavi. Christus enim in vespere Cœnæ pulcherrimum sermonem fecit discipulis suis, et mane sequenti se Christum esse confessus est, atque in cruce pendens alta voce clamavit : Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum. Et exaudiet vocem meam. Christus enim in omni oratione quam ex deliberata ratione effudit, auditus est, quemadmodum Martha ait ad eum : Scio quia quæcumque poposceris a Deo, dabit tibi Deus.
paras.en: [[54:18|Evening|Vespere]], that is, on the night of the Supper, [[54:18|and morning|et mane]], that is, on the day of the Parasceve [the day of Preparation, Good Friday], [[54:18|and at noon|et meridie]], hanging on the cross, [[54:18|I will speak|narrabo]] in mind [[54:18|and declare|et annuntiabo]] with the mouth: that is, I spoke the truth, taught saving wisdom, offered my cause and my prayer to the Lord, prayed for those who crucified me, and commended my soul to the Father. For on the evening of the Supper Christ gave a most beautiful discourse to his disciples, and the following morning he confessed that he was the Christ, and hanging on the cross he cried with a loud voice: [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]. [[54:18|and he shall hear my voice|Et exaudiet vocem meam]]. For Christ was heard in every prayer that he poured out from deliberate reason [that is, with the considered will of his reason, as distinct from the natural shrinking of his senses, as in the agony in the garden], as Martha says to him: [[John 11:22|I know that whatsoever thou wilt ask of God, God will give it thee|Scio quia quæcumque poposceris a Deo, dabit tibi Deus]].

paras.t: Redimet in pace, id est, redimendo constituet in vera ac stabili pace, animam meam, id est me ipsum, seu vitam meam, transferendo me de vita mortali ad impassibilem vitam : redimet itaque animam meam ab his qui appropinquant mihi, id est a Judæis et aliis qui accesserunt ad me ut me comprehenderent, ligarent, atque occiderent ; quoniam inter multos erant mecum : id est, ideo me exaudivit Deus, quoniam isti Judæi ita accedentes ad me, sæpe interfuerunt prædicationibus meis inter plurimos alios in me credentes, et ita excusationem non habent. Propter quod ait Salvator : Ego semper docui in templo et synagogis, quo omnes Judæi conveniunt ; et iterum : Si non venissem et locutus eis fuissem, peccatum non haberent ; nunc autem excusationem non habent.
paras.en: [[54:19|He shall redeem|Redimet]] [[54:19|in peace|in pace]], that is, by redeeming he will establish in true and stable peace [[54:19|my soul|animam meam]], that is, myself, or my life, bringing me over from mortal life to the life that cannot suffer. So he shall redeem my soul [[54:19|from them that draw near to me|ab his qui appropinquant mihi]], that is, from the Jews and the others who came up to me to seize me, bind me and kill me; [[54:19|for among many they were with me|quoniam inter multos erant mecum]]: that is, God therefore heard me because these Jews, who thus came up to me, were often present at my preaching among very many others who believed in me, and so they have no excuse. For which reason the Saviour says: [[John 18:20|I have always taught|Ego semper docui]] in the temple and in the synagogues, [[John 18:20|whither all the Jews resort|quo omnes Judæi conveniunt]]; and again: [[John 15:22|If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin: but now they have no excuse|Si non venissem et locutus eis fuissem, peccatum non haberent ; nunc autem excusationem non habent]].

paras.t: Exaudiet Deus precem meam, et humiliabit illos superbos, in præsenti et in futuro. Nunc autem humiliati sunt Judæi, quia privati sunt omni gloria legis paternæ, regno, loco, sacerdote et principe ; et in futuro quoque cum ceteris superbis in ima inferni humiliati labentur. Qui est ante sæcula, id est Deus æternus, ante omnia sæcula in se subsistens.
paras.en: [[54:20|God shall hear|Exaudiet Deus]] my prayer, and [[54:20|shall humble them|et humiliabit illos]], the proud, in the present and in the future. Now indeed the Jews have been humbled, for they have been deprived of all the glory of their fathers' law, of kingdom, place, priest and prince; and in the future too, humbled with the rest of the proud, they shall sink into the depths of hell. [[54:20|the Eternal|Qui est ante sæcula]] [Latin *qui est ante sæcula*, "who is before the ages"], that is, the eternal God, subsisting in himself before all ages.

paras.t: Non enim est illis commutatio de malo et infidelitate ad pœnitentiam et fidem christianam, quemadmodum in Jeremia legitur : Induraverunt facies suas super petram, et noluerunt reverti. Et ad Judæos Dominus per Isaiam ait : Scio quia durus es tu, et nervus ferreus cervix tua, et frons tua ærea. Et non timuerunt Deum, cujus Filium occiderunt. Extendit manum suam in retribuendo : id est, Deus virtutem suæ potentiæ præparavit, ut illis […] justam mercedem retribuat.
paras.en: [[54:20|For there is no change with them|Non enim est illis commutatio]] from evil and unbelief to penance and the Christian faith, as we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 5:3|they have made their faces harder than the rock, and they have refused to return|Induraverunt facies suas super petram, et noluerunt reverti]]. And the Lord says to the Jews by Isaias: [[Is 48:4|I knew that thou art stubborn, and thy neck is as an iron sinew, and thy forehead as brass|Scio quia durus es tu, et nervus ferreus cervix tua, et frons tua ærea]]. [[54:20|and they have not feared God|Et non timuerunt Deum]], whose Son they killed. [[54:21|He hath stretched forth his hand to repay|Extendit manum suam in retribuendo]]: that is, God has made ready the might of his power, to repay them […] a just reward.

paras.t: Contaminaverunt testamentum ejus, id est, prædicti Judæi legem Dei non servaverunt, sed polluerunt, inique contra eam agentes, eamque inhonorantes, atque carnaliter intelligentes. Divisi sunt per totum mundum ab ira vultus ejus, id est a justa vindicta divinæ justitiæ. Nam propter sua peccata Deus eos a propria terra ejecit, per orbem dispersit, a caritate et fide Christi, electorumque numero separavit. Et appropinquavit cor illius : id est, voluntas divina seu pietas Dei, reprobatis Judæis, ad gentiles conversa est, sicut Dominus ad Judæos per Prophetam ait : Non est mihi ultra voluntas in vobis, quia magnum nomen meum in gentibus. Et Apostolus ait : Cæcitas ex parte contigit in Israel, donec plenitudo gentium intraret; et iterum, Illorum delicto salus est gentibus, id est occasio salvationis gentilium, quoniam Judæis non credentibus, justa facta est ad gentes transmigratio.
paras.en: [[54:21|They have defiled his covenant|Contaminaverunt testamentum ejus]], that is, the aforesaid Jews did not keep the law of God but polluted it, acting wickedly against it, dishonouring it, and understanding it carnally. [[54:22|They are divided|Divisi sunt]] throughout the whole world [[54:22|by the wrath of his countenance|ab ira vultus ejus]], that is, by the just vengeance of divine justice. For on account of their sins God cast them out of their own land, scattered them through the world, and separated them from the charity and faith of Christ and from the number of the elect. [[54:22|and his heart hath drawn near|Et appropinquavit cor illius]]: that is, the divine will, or the loving-kindness of God, the Jews being rejected, turned to the Gentiles, as the Lord says to the Jews by the Prophet: [[Mal 1:10|I have no pleasure in you|Non est mihi ultra voluntas in vobis]] [Denis adds *ultra*, "any more"], [[Mal 1:11|for my name is great among the Gentiles|quia magnum nomen meum in gentibus]]. And the Apostle says: [[Rom 11:25|blindness in part has happened in Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles should come in|Cæcitas ex parte contigit in Israel, donec plenitudo gentium intraret]]; and again: [[Rom 11:11|by their offence salvation is come to the Gentiles|Illorum delicto salus est gentibus]], that is, the occasion of the salvation of the Gentiles, since, the Jews not believing, there was a just passing over to the Gentiles.

paras.t: Molliti sunt sermones ejus super oleum, id est, doctrina et prædicatio Christi oleo suaviores fuerunt et sunt, quoniam regnum cœlorum et viam pœnitentiæ prædicavit. Unde superius de Christo præhabitum est: Diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis. Et Lucas ait : Mirabantur omnes in verbis gratiæ quæ procedebant de ore ejus. Et ipsi sunt jacula : id est, infideles Judæi tanquam sagittæ repugnaverunt doctrinæ atque operibus Christi, pungentes eum verbis blasphemis, et clavis tandem confodientes.
paras.en: [[54:22|His words are smoother than oil|Molliti sunt sermones ejus super oleum]], that is, the teaching and preaching of Christ were and are sweeter than oil, since he preached the kingdom of heaven and the way of penance. Hence it was said of Christ earlier on: [[Ps 44:3|grace is poured abroad in thy lips|Diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis]]. And Luke says: [[Luke 4:22|they wondered at the words of grace that proceeded from his mouth|Mirabantur omnes in verbis gratiæ quæ procedebant de ore ejus]]. [[54:22|and the same are darts|Et ipsi sunt jacula]]: that is, the unbelieving Jews, like arrows, fought against the teaching and works of Christ, piercing him with blasphemous words, and at last transfixing him with nails.

paras.t: Sed tu, o Christiane, illis sic pereuntibus, Jacta super Dominum curam tuam : id est, inordinatas atque superfluas sollicitudines fuge, et in Domino vigilans esto, ordinatam curam habendo, videlicet ut sollicitus ac timoratus exsistas quomodo Deo complaceas; de temporalibus vero noli vel ante tempus, vel nimis anxie sollicitari, sed secundum quod ad spiritualem profectum necessaria sunt sive utilia. Sic ergo committe te Deo, sed non sic ut negligas facere quod in te est ; fac autem quod tibi possibile est, et scito quod tua providentia tibi non sufficit. Idcirco confide in Domino, et curam tuam in ipso dispone ac ordina : quia superius dictum est, Dominus sollicitus est mei. Ipsi quoque de omnibus cura est, quemadmodum Sapiens dicit. Et ipse te enutriet, id est, de necessariis tibi providebit : sicut Christus spopondit, Quærite primum regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis. Et iterum : Nolite, inquit, solliciti esse in crastinum ; scit enim Pater vester cœlestis, quod his omnibus indigetis. Hinc ait S. Petrus : Omnem sollicitudinem vestram projicientes in eum, quoniam ipsi cura est de vobis.
paras.en: But thou, O Christian, while they thus perish, [[54:23|Cast thy care upon the Lord|Jacta super Dominum curam tuam]]: that is, flee disordered and superfluous anxieties, and be watchful in the Lord, having an ordered care, namely that thou be anxious and fearful how thou mayest please God; but about temporal things do not be anxious either before the time or too anxiously, but only so far as they are necessary or useful for spiritual progress. So then commit thyself to God, but not in such a way that thou neglect to do what is in thee; do what is possible to thee, and know that thy own foresight is not enough for thee. Therefore trust in the Lord, and set and order thy care in him; for it was said earlier: [[Ps 39:18|the Lord is careful for me|Dominus sollicitus est mei]]. He too has care of all things, as the Wise Man says[[Wis 12:13||]]. [[54:23|and he shall sustain thee|Et ipse te enutriet]] [*enutriet*, "will nourish"], that is, he will provide thee with what is necessary, as Christ promised: [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|Quærite primum regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis]]. And again: [[Matt 6:34|Be not|Nolite]], he says, [[Matt 6:34|solicitous for to morrow|solliciti esse in crastinum]]; [[Matt 6:32|For your Father knoweth that you have need of all these things|scit enim Pater vester cœlestis, quod his omnibus indigetis]] [Denis adds *cœlestis*, "heavenly"]. Hence St Peter says: [[1 Pet 5:7|Casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you|Omnem sollicitudinem vestram projicientes in eum, quoniam ipsi cura est de vobis]].

paras.t: Non dabit in æternum fluctuationem justo. Hoc dupliciter intelligi potest. Primo sic : Deus nunquam permittet fluctuare justum, id est a se recedere, seu esse instabilem, quia per gratiam fixus manet in Deo, in omni tentatione atque eventu, sicut inferius de viro justo inducitur : Paratum cor ejus sperare in Domino, confirmatum est cor ejus ; non commovebitur. Unde Dominus per Jeremiam ait : Si abstuleris offendicula tua a facie mea, non commoveberis. Peccata equidem faciunt hominem fluctuantem atque instabilem, juxta illud : Peccatum peccavit Jerusalem, propterea instabilis facta est. Et alibi : Tenebit justus viam suam, et mundis manibus addet fortitudinem. Et iterum ait Scriptura : Justus in sapientia permanet ut sol ; stultus autem mutatur ut luna. Non tamen intelligenda sunt hæc, quasi justus peccare non posset ; sed quid justo conveniat, secundum quod justus est, locus iste declarat. Secundo intelligitur sic : Non dabit in æternum fluctuationem justo, id est, quamvis ad tempus sinat eum Deus tentari, tribulari, et anxiari, veniet tamen tempus quo in bono firmabitur, atque ab omni instabilitate et inquietudine eripietur.
paras.en: [[54:23|he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever|Non dabit in æternum fluctuationem justo]]. This can be understood in two ways. First thus: God will never allow the just man to waver, that is, to draw back from him or to be unstable, because by grace he remains fixed in God in every temptation and event, as is brought in further on concerning the just man: [[Ps 111:7|His heart is ready to hope in the Lord|Paratum cor ejus sperare in Domino]]: [[Ps 111:8|His heart is strengthened, he shall not be moved|confirmatum est cor ejus ; non commovebitur]]. Hence the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 4:1|if thou wilt take away thy stumblingblocks out of my sight, thou shalt not be moved|Si abstuleris offendicula tua a facie mea, non commoveberis]]. For sins make a man wavering and unstable, according to that saying: [[Lam 1:8|Jerusalem hath grievously sinned, therefore is she become unstable|Peccatum peccavit Jerusalem, propterea instabilis facta est]]. And elsewhere: [[Job 17:9|the just man shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger|Tenebit justus viam suam, et mundis manibus addet fortitudinem]]. And again Scripture says: The just man [[Ecclus 27:12|continueth in wisdom as the sun: but a fool is changed as the moon|in sapientia permanet ut sol ; stultus autem mutatur ut luna]] [the Vulgate has *Homo sanctus*, "a holy man"; Denis reads *Justus*]. Yet these things are not to be understood as if the just man could not sin; but this place declares what befits the just man insofar as he is just. Secondly it is understood thus: [[54:23|he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever|Non dabit in æternum fluctuationem justo]]: that is, although God allows him for a time to be tempted, troubled and distressed, yet the time will come when he will be made firm in good and delivered from all instability and disquiet.

paras.t: Tu vero, Deus, omnium justus judex, deduces eos, id est Judæos Christo rebelles, in puteum interitus, id est, in lacum inferni, vel in obstinationem et profundissimam cæcitatem eos deduci permittes, propter eorum malitiam : sicut de eis scriptum est, Computrescere faciam superbiam populi hujus pessimi, qui nolunt audire verba mea.
paras.en: [[54:24|But thou, O God|Tu vero, Deus]], the just judge of all, [[54:24|shalt bring them down|deduces eos]], that is, the Jews who rebel against Christ, [[54:24|into the pit of destruction|in puteum interitus]], that is, into the lake of hell; or thou wilt allow them to be led down into obstinacy and the deepest blindness on account of their malice: as it is written of them: I will make to rot the pride[[Jer 13:9||]] of [[Jer 13:10|this wicked people, that will not hear my words|populi hujus pessimi, qui nolunt audire verba mea]].

paras.t: Viri sanguinum, id est peccatores, et dolosi non dimidiabunt dies suos, id est, tam diu non vivent ut æstimant ; et sæpe medietatem temporis quod sibi restare arbitrantur, non attingunt : quia statim dum completa fuerit eorum iniquitas, a Domino auferuntur. Secundum quod de divite sibi longam vitam pollicente, ait Salvator : Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetunt a te. Propter quod ait et alia scriptura : Viri iniqui ante tempus suum sublati sunt. Vel sic : Viri prædicti non dimidiabunt dies suos, videlicet ut, sicut præteritum vitæ suæ tempus consumpserunt in voluptate ac vitiis, sic tempus residuum expendant in pœnitentia atque virtutibus ; sed dato tempore abutuntur, perseverando in culpa, sicut de quolibet tali in libro beati Job dicitur : Deus dedit illi locum pœnitentiæ, et ille abutitur eo in superbiam. Hi enim assimilantur diabolo, quia diabolicum est perseverare in malo. Unde de talibus per Jeremiam Dominus conqueritur : Quare aversus est populus iste aversione contentiosa?
paras.en: [[54:24|Bloody|Viri sanguinum]] [literally "men of blood"], that is, sinners, [[54:24|and deceitful men shall not live out half their days|et dolosi non dimidiabunt dies suos]]: that is, they will not live as long as they reckon; and often they do not reach half the time which they think remains to them, because as soon as their iniquity is complete they are taken away by the Lord. In keeping with this the Saviour says of the rich man who promised himself a long life: [[Luke 12:20|Thou fool, this night do they require thy soul of thee|Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetunt a te]]. For which reason another scripture also says: [[Job 22:15|wicked men|Viri iniqui]] [[Job 22:16|were taken away before their time|ante tempus suum sublati sunt]] [the margin gives Job xxxii, 15, 16; the passage is Job 22:15–16]. Or thus: the aforesaid men [[54:24|shall not live out half their days|non dimidiabunt dies suos]]: that is, so that, as they spent the past time of their life in pleasure and vices, they might spend the time remaining in penance and virtues; but they abuse the time given them, persevering in sin, as is said of every such man in the book of blessed Job: [[Job 24:23|God hath given him place for penance, and he abuseth it unto pride|Deus dedit illi locum pœnitentiæ, et ille abutitur eo in superbiam]]. For these are made like the devil, since it is devilish to persevere in evil. Hence the Lord complains of such men by Jeremias: [[Jer 8:5|Why then is this people in Jerusalem turned away with a stubborn revolting?|Quare aversus est populus iste aversione contentiosa?]]

paras.t: Ego autem sperabo in te, Domine. Christus ut homo et aliquo modo viator, videlicet in quantum passibilis, speravit in Deo, exspectando ab eo bona, quæ nondum habuit, sed adipisci oravit, ut corporis glorificationem, ascensionem, etc.
paras.en: [[54:24|but I will trust in thee, O Lord|Ego autem sperabo in te, Domine]]. Christ, as man and in some way a wayfarer [Latin *viator*: one still on the way to the vision of God], namely insofar as he could suffer, hoped in God, awaiting from him good things which he did not yet have but prayed to obtain, such as the glorification of his body, the ascension, etc.

paras.t: Ecce jam liquet, quam vere et proprie psalmus iste exponatur de Christo. Quum ergo evangelica, itemque apostolica auctoritate compellamur quosdam psalmos ad litteram de Christo exponere, in quibus tamen quædam habentur quæ Christo secundum se nullatenus competunt, ut sunt psalmi tricesimus nonus et quadragesimus, scilicet, Exspectans exspectavi Dominum, in quo inter cetera dicitur, Comprehenderunt me iniquitates meæ, et non potui ut viderem ; et, Beatus qui intelligit, in quo legitur, Sana animam meam, quia peccavi tibi : quanto magis psalmus iste, atque consimiles, in quibus nil ponitur quod Christo secundum se non conveniat, erit ad litteram intelligendus de Christo?
paras.en: See, it is now plain how truly and properly this psalm is expounded of Christ. Since, then, we are compelled by the authority of the Gospel and likewise of the Apostle to expound literally of Christ certain psalms in which, nevertheless, some things are found that in no way befit Christ in himself [that is, in his own person, as distinct from his members], such as the thirty-ninth and fortieth psalms, namely [[Ps 39:2|With expectation I have waited for the Lord|Exspectans exspectavi Dominum]], in which among other things it is said: [[Ps 39:13|my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see|Comprehenderunt me iniquitates meæ, et non potui ut viderem]]; and [[Ps 40:2|Blessed is he that understandeth|Beatus qui intelligit]], in which we read: [[Ps 40:5|heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee|Sana animam meam, quia peccavi tibi]] [the Gospel applies Ps 40 to Christ at John 13:18, and the Apostle Ps 39 at Heb 10:5–7]: how much more shall this psalm, and those like it, in which nothing is set down that does not befit Christ in himself, be understood literally of Christ?

54.title: EXPLANATIO EJUSDEM PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI QUARTI TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS, DE ECCLESIA SEU UNOQUOQUE FIDELI.
54.title_en: Tropological or moral explanation of the same fifty-fourth psalm, concerning the Church or each of the faithful.

paras.t: Constat autem per David designari Ecclesiam, seu quemlibet vere fidelem; et ita sensus tituli erit : In finem, in carminibus intellectus David : id est, intellectus hujus psalmi, in finem, id est in Christum nos dirigens, convenit David, id est Ecclesiæ seu credenti multipliciter tribulato, in carminibus, id est in adversis gratias referenti ac læto.
paras.en: Now it is clear that by David is signified the Church, or any one of the truly faithful; and so the sense of the title will be: [[54:1|Unto the end, in verses, understanding for David|In finem, in carminibus intellectus David]]: that is, the [[54:1|understanding|intellectus]] of this psalm, [[54:1|Unto the end|in finem]], that is, directing us unto Christ, belongs to [[54:1|David|David]], that is, to the Church, or to the believer troubled in many ways, [[54:1|in verses|in carminibus]] [carmina, "songs"], that is, to one who gives thanks and is glad in adversity.

paras.t: Ait ergo : Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam. Idem sensus sub aliis verbis hic quater repetitur, quatenus ipse orantis affectus in se ipso fervescat, totiesque accendatur quoties sensus ipse repetitur. Itaque, Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam, propter tuam bonitatem, et ne despexeris deprecationem meam, propter meam imperfectionem ac fragilitatem ; intende mihi, oculo paternæ pietatis respiciendo in me, et exaudi me orantem pro vitiorum omniumque malorum ablatione, et virtutum ac præmiorum adeptione.
paras.en: He says, then: [[54:2|Hear, O God, my prayer|Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam]]. The same sense is repeated here four times in other words, so that the very affection of the one who prays may grow fervent within itself, and be kindled as often as the sense is repeated. So: [[54:2|Hear, O God, my prayer|Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam]], because of thy goodness, [[54:2|and despise not my supplication|et ne despexeris deprecationem meam]], because of my imperfection and frailty; [[54:3|Be attentive to me|intende mihi]], looking upon me with the eye of fatherly love, [[54:3|and hear me|et exaudi me]] as I pray for the taking away of vices and of all evils, and for the gaining of virtues and rewards.

paras.t: Contristatus sum in exercitatione mea. Duplicem esse exercitationem, videlicet interiorem et spiritualem, exteriorem quoque et corporalem, docet Apostolus, ad Timotheum dicens : Exerce te ipsum ad pietatem ; nam corporalis exercitatio ad modicum utilis est, pietas autem ad omnia utilis est. In utraque autem exercitatione boni tristantur, non de ipsa exercitatione, sed propter imperfectiones adjunctas et culpas commissas, et quia in hac valle lacrimarum exsulando peregrinantur a Domino, adspicientes ipsum mundum vitiis erroribusque repletum : sicque ex pia compassione errantium contristantur, maxime tamen propter Dei injuriam et offensam, tanquam Dei zelum habentes. Hæc est bona tristitia, quæ (secundum Apostolum) operatur salutem. De qua Salomon protestatur : Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia ; et iterum, Melius est ire ad domum luctus, quam ad domum convivii. Jam enim est tempus lugendi et flendi, quemadmodum Dominus apud Joelem admonet, dicens : Convertimini ad me in toto corde vestro, in fletu et planctu. Nec enim postea gloriabuntur cum Christo, qui jam eligunt jucundari cum mundo.
paras.en: [[54:3|I am grieved in my exercise|Contristatus sum in exercitatione mea]]. That there is a twofold exercise, namely an interior and spiritual one, and also an exterior and bodily one, the Apostle teaches, saying to Timothy: [[1 Tim 4:7|exercise thyself unto godliness|Exerce te ipsum ad pietatem]]; [[1 Tim 4:8|For bodily exercise is profitable to little: but godliness is profitable to all things|nam corporalis exercitatio ad modicum utilis est, pietas autem ad omnia utilis est]]. In both kinds of exercise the good are grieved, not at the exercise itself, but because of the imperfections joined to it and the faults committed, and because, exiled in this [[Ps 83:7|vale of tears|valle lacrimarum]], they are pilgrims absent from the Lord, beholding this world full of vices and errors: and so they are grieved out of loving compassion for those who go astray, yet most of all because of the wrong and offence done to God, as having zeal for God. This is the good sorrow which (according to the Apostle) worketh salvation[[2 Cor 7:10||]] [the margin gives "Ibid. vii, 10", though the note before it is to the Psalms; the Apostle's words are 2 Cor 7:10]. Of it Solomon declares: [[Eccles 7:5|The heart of the wise is where there is mourning, and the heart of fools where there is mirth.|Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia]] And again: [[Eccles 7:3|It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to the house of feasting|Melius est ire ad domum luctus, quam ad domum convivii]] [the margin gives Eccle. vii, 5 for both sayings; this second one is Eccles 7:3]. For now is the time to mourn and to weep, as the Lord warns by Joel, saying: [[Joel 2:12|Be converted to me with all your heart|Convertimini ad me in toto corde vestro]], [[Joel 2:12|in weeping, and mourning|in fletu et planctu]]. For they will not afterwards glory with Christ who now choose to make merry with the world.

paras.t: Et conturbatus sum a voce inimici, id est ab injuriis verborum, et a tribulatione peccatoris, id est ab injuriis verberum seu damnorum. Duplex autem est conturbatio, scilicet bona, de qua in præcedenti expositione dictum est ; et mala, qua aliquis plus debito irascitur, timet, tristatur, aut simili modo inordinate afficitur, ita quod actus rationis impeditur. Conturbari itaque bona conturbatione a voce inimici et a tribulatione peccatoris, est perfectorum, qui adversa æquanimiter ferunt, sed conturbantur, id est, male agentibus vehementer compatiuntur, aut simili modo rationabiliter afficiuntur, qualis erat Apostolus qui ait : Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor? et Job qui dicit : Antequam comedam, suspiro, et quasi inundantis aquæ, sic rugitus meus. Conturbari vero secundo modo, imperfectorum est, qui omnia nondum tranquille sufferre, atque in adversis lætari didicerunt. Quos Jacobus in sua Canonica instruens : Omne, inquit, gaudium existimate, fratres mei, quum in tentationes varias incideritis. Unde et Christus ait : Beati estis quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes ; gaudete et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis. Non ergo propter adversa injuriasque turbemur, nec propter verba dura ac pessima nobis illata tristemur, nisi peccantibus condolendo.
paras.en: [[54:3|and am troubled|Et conturbatus sum]] [[54:4|At the voice of the enemy|a voce inimici]], that is, by injuries of words, [[54:4|and at the tribulation of the sinner|et a tribulatione peccatoris]], that is, by injuries of blows or of losses [verborum, verberum: "of words", "of blows", a play on two like-sounding Latin words]. Now trouble is of two kinds: the good, of which we spoke in the preceding exposition; and the evil, by which one is angered, afraid or sorrowful more than is due, or is in some like way disorderly affected, so that the act of reason is hindered. To be troubled with the good trouble, then, at the voice of the enemy and at the tribulation of the sinner, belongs to the perfect, who bear adversity with an even mind, yet are troubled, that is, feel keen compassion for those who do evil, or are moved in some like way according to reason; such was the Apostle, who says: [[2 Cor 11:29|Who is weak, and I am not weak?|Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor?]] and Job, who says: [[Job 3:24|Before I eat I sigh: and as overflowing waters, so is my roaring|Antequam comedam, suspiro, et quasi inundantis aquæ, sic rugitus meus]]. But to be troubled in the second way belongs to the imperfect, who have not yet learned to bear all things calmly and to rejoice in adversity. James instructs them in his Canonical Epistle: [[Jas 1:2|count it all joy|gaudium existimate]], he says, [[Jas 1:2|My brethren|fratres mei]], [[Jas 1:2|when you shall fall into divers temptations|quum in tentationes varias incideritis]]. Hence Christ too says: [[Matt 5:11|Blessed are ye when they shall revile you, and persecute you, and speak all that is evil against you, untruly|Beati estis quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes]]; [[Matt 5:12|Be glad and rejoice for your reward is very great in heaven|gaudete et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]]. Let us not, then, be troubled by adversities and injuries, nor be saddened by the harsh and most wicked words spoken against us, except in grieving with those who sin.

paras.t: Denique merito conturbatum me dico, Quoniam declinaverunt in me iniquitates, id est, peccata mihi injuste imposuerunt maligni : propter quod perfecti turbantur turbatione virtuosa, ut dictum est, gloriantes in hoc quod Christo aliqualiter conformantur, qui a Judæis falsissime criminabatur ; imperfecti vero interdum turbantur ex hoc turbatione iræ et impatientiæ. Et in ira (non per zelum, sed per vitium) quam conceperunt adversus me, molesti erant mihi verbis, signis seu factis, id est, vindicando se de me, gravabant me : quod ego moleste sustinui, non tam propter meam injuriam, quam propter illorum ruinam ac damnationem. Hoc modo Paulus moleste tulit mala sibi illata : quia ad instar indulgentissimi patris, qui quanto a filio phrenetico plura verba patitur, tanto insano magis compatitur ; sic quanto homines impii Paulum durius flagellabant, tanto ipse eorum errori amplius condolebat.
paras.en: Finally, I rightly say that I am troubled, [[54:4|For they have cast iniquities upon me|Quoniam declinaverunt in me iniquitates]], that is, the wicked have unjustly laid sins upon me: for which reason the perfect are troubled with a virtuous trouble, as has been said, glorying in this, that they are in some measure made like to Christ, who was most falsely accused by the Jews; but the imperfect are at times troubled by it with the trouble of anger and impatience. [[54:4|and in wrath|Et in ira]] (not through zeal, but through vice) which they conceived against me, [[54:4|they were troublesome to me|molesti erant mihi]] by words, signs or deeds; that is, in avenging themselves on me they weighed upon me: which I bore with distress, not so much for the wrong done to me as for their ruin and damnation. In this way Paul was distressed at the evils done to him[[Acts 14:18||]][[Acts 16:23||]][[Acts 21:27||]] [the margin gives Act. xiv, 18; xvi, 23–25; xxi, 27–33]: for like a most indulgent father, who the more words he suffers from a frenzied son, the more he pities the madman, so the more harshly the ungodly scourged Paul, the more did he grieve over their error.

paras.t: Cor meum conturbatum est in me : id est, appetitus meus interior sensitivus seu intellectivus, vehementer seu excessive motus est aliqua passione seu affectione, ex qua ipsum quoque cor corporale turbatur, id est, innaturaliter agitatur, quoniam passiones fiunt cum corporali transmutatione. Et formido mortis cecidit super me, id est, tam graviter sum afflictus, ut mori verebar. Vel, Formido mortis, id est horror peccati, quod est mors animæ, cecidit super me, quia videlicet ex perturbatione mihi inflicta timui impatientiæ, iræ, rancoris, aut similis vitii motum et culpam mortalem incidere, vel tentationibus dæmonum, mundi et carnis formidabam succumbere : quod est spiritualiter mori atque deficere, juxta illud : Venit super te plaga, et defecisti ; tetigit te, et conturbatus es. Timor animæ et tremor exterior, venerunt super me, propter mala et tormenta seu pericula mihi imminentia et futura. Timor enim est de malo futuro, sicut dolor de malo præsenti. Et omnino expediens est ut talis timor et tremor in nobis sint, propter mille pericula nobis instantia, et propter futurum judicium, infernique tormenta : quia in medio laqueorum versamur, et contra invisibiles ac nequissimos hostes luctamur. Et contexerunt me tenebræ, id est, adversitates et pœnæ seu vitia circumdederunt et operuerunt me totum, ita quod malis multis repleta est anima mea : quemadmodum ait Apostolus, Foris pugnæ, et intus timores. Per varias enim tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cœlorum. Propter quod sanctus Job ait : Exspectabam bona, et venerunt mihi mala ; præstolabar lucem, et eruperunt tenebræ.
paras.en: [[54:5|My heart is troubled within me|Cor meum conturbatum est in me]]: that is, my inner appetite, sensitive or intellectual, is vehemently or excessively moved by some passion or affection, from which the bodily heart too is troubled, that is, unnaturally agitated, since the passions come about with a bodily change. [[54:5|and the fear of death is fallen upon me|Et formido mortis cecidit super me]], that is, I am so grievously afflicted that I was afraid of dying. Or, [[54:5|the fear of death|Formido mortis]], that is, the horror of sin, which is the death of the soul, [[54:5|is fallen upon me|cecidit super me]], because, namely, through the disturbance inflicted on me I feared to fall into the stirring and the mortal guilt of impatience, anger, rancour or some like vice, or dreaded to give way to the temptations of the demons, the world and the flesh: which is to die and to faint spiritually, according to that saying: [[Job 4:5|the scourge is come upon thee, and thou faintest: It hath touched thee, and thou art troubled|Venit super te plaga, et defecisti ; tetigit te, et conturbatus es]]. [[54:6|Fear|Timor]] of soul [[54:6|and trembling|et tremor]] without [[54:6|are come upon me|venerunt super me]], because of the evils and torments or dangers that threaten me and are to come. For fear is of a future evil, as sorrow is of a present one. And it is altogether expedient that such fear and trembling be in us, because of the thousand dangers that beset us, and because of the judgment to come and the torments of hell: for we move in the midst of snares, and wrestle against invisible and most wicked enemies. [[54:6|and darkness hath covered me|Et contexerunt me tenebræ]], that is, adversities and punishments, or vices, have surrounded and covered me wholly, so that my soul is filled with many evils: as the Apostle says, [[2 Cor 7:5|Combats without: fears within|Foris pugnæ, et intus timores]]. For [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God|Per varias enim tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cœlorum]] [Denis has "through divers tribulations" and "the kingdom of heaven"]. For which reason holy Job says: [[Job 30:26|I expected good things, and evils are come upon me: I waited for light, and darkness broke out.|Exspectabam bona, et venerunt mihi mala ; præstolabar lucem, et eruperunt tenebræ]]

paras.t: Et dixi intra me : Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut columbæ? id est, quam libenter haberem pennas virtutum, videlicet veram et columbinam simplicitatem et innocentiam, quatenus mala prædicta evadere, et immaculatam vitam ducere valeam inter iniquos ! Et volabo penna contemplationis, speculando cœlestia, propter quorum amorem terrena despicio, adversaque libenter sustineo ; et requiescam in Deo, per fidem et caritatem et pacem internam, a terrenarum rerum tumultu, et inquietudine passionum ac sollicitudine temporalium rerum : sicut superius dictum est, In pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam.
paras.en: [[54:7|And I said|Et dixi]] within myself: [[54:7|Who will give me wings like a dove|Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut columbæ]]? that is, how gladly would I have the wings of the virtues, namely a true and dovelike simplicity and innocence, so that I might escape the evils aforesaid, and lead a spotless life among the wicked!
