Hæc autem vota sunt tua, id est tibi placentia, et mea, quoniam mihi a te sunt collata. Quæ reddam laudationes tibi, ea implendo, sicque per vitam bonam te collaudando. Dum enim promissa implemus, piosque affectus ad effectum perducimus, Deum laudamus, et sacrificium justitiæ immolamus.
paras.en: [[55:12|In me, O God, are vows to thee|In me sunt, Deus, vota tua]] [the Latin *vota tua* is literally "thy vows"], that is, the promises or affections by which I have bound myself to serve thee, and by which I desire to honour thee. And these vows are thine, that is, pleasing to thee, and mine, since they have been bestowed on me by thee. [[55:12|which I will pay, praises to thee|Quæ reddam laudationes tibi]], by fulfilling them, and so praising thee by a good life. For when we fulfil our promises and bring our holy affections to effect, we praise God and offer the sacrifice of justice.

paras.t: Quoniam eripuisti animam meam de morte æterna et infernali, sanguinem tuum pro me fundendo; de morte quoque peccati mortalis, indulgentiam conferendo; et vivificasti animam meam, caritatem et gratiam influendo. Et pedes meos, id est affectus meos et opera, eripuisti de lapsu, id est a ruina peccati, dirigendo cor meum ac opera secundum tenorem legis divinæ, quemadmodum de populo tuo per Prophetam testaris: Ego quasi nutricius Ephraim, portavi eos in brachiis meis. Hæc autem ideo mihi fecisti, ut placeam coram Deo, quando ad Christi tribunal perductus fuero, salvusque fiam, in lumine viventium, id est in regione vivorum, et in lumine gloriæ, illud divinitus participando. De quo lumine superius dictum est: In lumine tuo videbimus lumen. Et beatus Job scribit: Numquid est numerus militum Dei? Et super quem non splendet lumen ipsius?
paras.en: [[55:13|Because thou hast delivered my soul from death|Quoniam eripuisti animam meam de morte]], eternal and infernal death, by shedding thy blood for me; from the death too of mortal sin, by granting pardon; and thou hast quickened my soul by pouring in charity and grace. And [[55:13|my feet|pedes meos]], that is, my affections and works, thou hast delivered [[55:13|from falling|de lapsu]], that is, from the ruin of sin, by directing my heart and works according to the tenor of the divine law, as thou testifiest of thy people by the Prophet: [[Osee 11:3|I was like a foster father to Ephraim, I carried them in my arms|Ego quasi nutricius Ephraim, portavi eos in brachiis meis]]. And thou hast done this for me [[55:13|that I may please in the sight of God|ut placeam coram Deo]], when I have been brought before the judgment seat of Christ and am saved, [[55:13|in the light of the living|in lumine viventium]], that is, in the land of the living, and in the light of glory, sharing in it by God's gift. Of which light it was said above: [[Ps 35:10|in thy light we shall see light|In lumine tuo videbimus lumen]]. And blessed Job writes: [[Job 25:3|Is there any numbering of his soldiers? and upon whom shall not his light arise?|Numquid est numerus militum Dei? Et super quem non splendet lumen ipsius?]]

paras.t: Ecce psalmum vere affectuosum audivimus: in quo primo Christi atque justorum tribulationes commemorantur; deinde mens in Deo per spem confortatur, beneficia Dei ad memoriam reducuntur. Impleamus igitur psalmi præsentis doctrinam, in omni tribulatione ad Deum suppliciter confugiendo, spem veram in ipso excitando, corque magnanime et imperterritum assumendo, vitam nostram Domino annuntiando, sermones nostros ad ipsius gloriam ordinando, vota promissionum ac desideriorum ei reddendo, ejusque beneficia intime recolendo, quatenus ei soli in futuro, et non alicui in hoc mundo, placere optemus.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm truly full of feeling: in which first the tribulations of Christ and of the just are recalled; then the mind is strengthened in God through hope, and the benefits of God are brought back to memory. Let us therefore fulfil the teaching of the present psalm: by fleeing to God as suppliants in every tribulation, by stirring up true hope in him, by taking a great and undaunted heart, by declaring our life to the Lord, by ordering our words to his glory, by paying him the vows of our promises and desires, and by inwardly recalling his benefits, so that we may desire to please him alone in the life to come, and not anyone in this world.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Pone, Domine, lacrimas nostras in conspectu tuo, et erue pedes nostros a lapsu desperato: ut caute ambulantes, Verbum tibi consubstantiale Dominum Christum rite laudemus, et per eum in regione viventium tibi placeamus.
paras.en: Prayer. Set, O Lord, our tears in thy sight, and deliver our feet from the fall of despair: that, walking warily, we may duly praise the Lord Christ, the Word consubstantial with thee, and through him may please thee in the land of the living.

56.title: EXPLANATIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI SEXTI : MISERERE MEI, DEUS, MISERERE MEI.
56.title_en: Explanation, of Christ, of the fifty-sixth psalm: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi istius : In finem, ne disperdas David, in tituli inscriptione, quum fugeret a facie Saul in speluncam. Primo libro Regum legitur sanctus David a facie Saul bis in speluncam fugisse : primo, in speluncam Odollam ; secundo, in speluncam in quam descendit etiam Saul ut ventrem purgaret ; in qua abscidit David summitatem chlamydis Saul, prohibuitque Abisai ne Saulem occideret. Ab hac autem fuga intitulatur hic psalmus : qui licet exponi posset de David, sicut in sequenti expositione de quolibet justo exponetur, convenientius tamen de Christo per David significato exponitur, præsertim quum David non legatur titulum erexisse. Est itaque sensus tituli hujus : In finem, id est psalmus iste in Christum nos erigens, ne disperdas David, id est, ne Christum neges verbo aut facto regem ac Dominum omnium, sicut significabatur in tituli inscriptione, qua scripsit Pilatus de Christo, Hic est rex Judæorum ; quum fugeret David a facie Saul, id est, quum Christus a Judæorum cognitione recessit, illisque se abscondit in spelunca, id est in carne sua mortali, in qua ejus divinitas latuit, incredulisque se Judæis abscondit.
paras.en: The title of this psalm: [[56:1|Unto the end, destroy not, for David, for an inscription of a title, when he fled from Saul into the cave|In finem, ne disperdas David, in tituli inscriptione, quum fugeret a facie Saul in speluncam]]. In the first book of Kings we read that holy David twice fled from the face of Saul into a cave: first, into the cave of Odollam[[1 Kings 22:1||]]; secondly, into the cave into which Saul also went down to ease nature, in which David cut off the hem of Saul's cloak and forbade Abisai to kill Saul [in the cave of 1 Kings 24 David restrains his men; it is at 1 Kings 26:8–9, in Saul's camp, that he forbids Abisai]. It is from this flight that the psalm takes its title: and though it could be expounded of David, as in the following exposition it will be expounded of any just man, yet it is more fittingly expounded of Christ, who was signified by David, especially since we do not read that David set up a title. So the sense of this title is: [[56:1|Unto the end|In finem]], that is, this psalm, raising us up to Christ; [[56:1|destroy not, for David|ne disperdas David]] [Denis takes *David* as the object: "destroy not David"], that is, do not deny by word or deed that Christ is King and Lord of all, as was signified [[56:1|for an inscription of a title|in tituli inscriptione]] [Denis reads: "in the inscription of the title"], by which Pilate wrote of Christ: This is the King of the Jews; [[56:1|when he fled|quum fugeret]] David [[56:1|from Saul|a facie Saul]], that is, when Christ withdrew from the knowledge of the Jews and hid himself from them, [[56:1|into the cave|in spelunca]], that is, in his mortal flesh, in which his divinity lay hidden, and so hid himself from the unbelieving Jews.

paras.t: CHRISTUS itaque passioni jam proximus, ex parte hominis assumpti adhuc mortalis, et mortem naturaliter abhorrentis, orat ad Patrem : Miserere mei, Deus, ab hoc passibili statu ad immortalem statum me transferendo, miserere mei orantis pro corpore meo mystico, ut fructum passionis meæ consequatur ; quoniam in te confidit anima mea : id est, in tua bonitate ego spero, secundum quod homo passibilis, et viator aliquo modo, non ut Deus et comprehensor. Et in umbra alarum tuarum, id est in defensione ac ope misericordiæ atque potentiæ tuæ, sperabo, donec transeat iniquitas, id est, donec finem accipiat malitia Judæorum adversum me, scilicet quamdiu in hac vita vivo mortalis. Christus enim semper a Deo protectus est, nec aliquid ei nocere valebant Judæi donec ipsemet voluit.
paras.en: Christ, then, now close to his passion, speaking on the part of the manhood he had taken, which was still mortal and naturally shrank from death, prays to the Father: [[56:2|Have mercy on me, O God|Miserere mei, Deus]], by bringing me over from this passible state to the immortal state; [[56:2|have mercy on me|miserere mei]] as I pray for my mystical body, that it may obtain the fruit of my passion; [[56:2|for my soul trusteth in thee|quoniam in te confidit anima mea]]: that is, I hope in thy goodness, insofar as I am a passible man, and in some manner a wayfarer, not as God and comprehensor [a *wayfarer* (*viator*) is one still on the way to the vision of God; a *comprehensor*, one who already possesses it]. [[56:2|And in the shadow of thy wings|Et in umbra alarum tuarum]], that is, in the defence and help of thy mercy and might, [[56:2|will I hope, until iniquity pass away|sperabo, donec transeat iniquitas]], that is, until the malice of the Jews against me comes to an end, namely as long as I live mortal in this life. For Christ was always protected by God, and the Jews could do him no harm until he himself willed it.

paras.t: Clamabo, id est, passione instante, mente et ore orans clamavi, ad Deum altissimum : sicut fatetur Apostolus, Cum clamore valido et lacrimis Christus preces fudit ad Deum ; Deum qui benefecit mihi, id est, multa mihi beneficia contulit, pie exaudivit, omnique virtute et dono ac gratia Spiritus Sancti replevit, quantum capere potuit natura creata, a principio creationis et conceptionis meæ humanitatis. Non enim ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum homini Christo.
paras.en: [[56:3|I will cry|Clamabo]], that is, with my passion at hand I cried out, praying with mind and mouth, [[56:3|to God the most high|ad Deum altissimum]]: as the Apostle declares, [[Heb 5:7|with a strong cry and tears|Cum clamore valido et lacrimis]] Christ poured out prayers to God; [[56:3|to God who hath done good to me|Deum qui benefecit mihi]], that is, who has bestowed many benefits on me, has graciously heard me, and has filled me with every virtue and gift and grace of the Holy Ghost, as far as created nature could receive it, from the beginning of the creation and conception of my manhood. For [[John 3:34|God doth not give the Spirit by measure|Non enim ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum]] to the man Christ.

paras.t: Misit de cœlo, et liberavit me : id est, Deus Pater desuper adjutorium mihi impendit, et angelum confortantem me misit, et de manibus Judæorum in die resurrectionis me penitus eripuit. Dedit in opprobrium conculcantes me, id est, persecutores crucifixoresque meos confudit, confusione dignos ostendit, contemptibiles fecit in præsenti et in futuro, privans eos propria terra, omnique gratia : sicut de eis apud Jeremiam prædictum est, Induc super eos diem afflictionis, et duplici contritione contere eos, Domine Deus noster ; et apud Danielem, Civitatem et sanctuarium (id est habitatores Jerusalem qui Christum occiderunt, et templum) dissipabit populus cum duce venturo, id est exercitus Romanorum cum Tito. Misit Deus misericordiam suam et veritatem suam, id est, effectum suæ misericordiæ atque justitiæ effudit super me : quia in omni opere Dei commiscentur misericordia et justitia. Misit autem Deus misericordiam suam, dum animam Christi tam gratiose in omni benedictione prævenit ; et veritatem, quando eam, sicut per Prophetas prædixit, inseparabiliter corpori reunivit.
paras.en: [[56:4|He hath sent from heaven and delivered me|Misit de cœlo, et liberavit me]]: that is, God the Father gave me help from above, and sent an angel to strengthen me[[Luke 22:43||]], and on the day of the resurrection rescued me wholly out of the hands of the Jews. [[56:4|He hath made them a reproach that trod upon me|Dedit in opprobrium conculcantes me]], that is, he confounded my persecutors and crucifiers, showed them worthy of confusion, and made them contemptible in the present and in the future, depriving them of their own land and of all grace: as was foretold of them in Jeremias: [[Jer 17:18|bring upon them the day of affliction, and with a double destruction, destroy them|Induc super eos diem afflictionis, et duplici contritione contere eos]], O Lord our God; and in Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|the city, and the sanctuary|Civitatem et sanctuarium]] (that is, the inhabitants of Jerusalem who killed Christ, and the temple) [[Dan 9:26|a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy|dissipabit populus cum duce venturo]], that is, the army of the Romans with Titus. [[56:4|God hath sent his mercy and his truth|Misit Deus misericordiam suam et veritatem suam]], that is, he poured out upon me the effect of his mercy and justice: for in every work of God mercy and justice are mingled. And God sent his mercy when he so graciously prevented the soul of Christ with every blessing[[Ps 20:4||]] [*prevent* in the old sense: to go before]; and his truth when, as he had foretold by the Prophets, he reunited it inseparably to the body.

paras.t: Ideo subditur : Et eripuit animam meam, in die resurrectionis, de medio catulorum leonum, id est de multitudine superborum atque ferocium Judæorum, ad immortalem statum me suscitans. Dormivi, in morte et monumento, conturbatus, id est conculcatus, oppressus, occisus. Filii hominum, non filii Dei, videlicet prædicti adversarii mei, dentes eorum arma et sagittæ, id est, similes sunt armis, itemque sagittis : quia quemadmodum aliquis per arma impugnatur, et per sagittam læditur ; sic Judæi verbis, quæ ore et dentibus formantur, me impugnabant ac lædi procurabant, Pilato dicentes : Si non esset hic malefactor, non tibi tradidissemus eum. Et lingua eorum gladius acutus : quia clamabant, Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum. Propterea scriptum est, Sagitta vulnerans lingua eorum.
paras.en: Hence it is added: [[56:5|And he hath delivered my soul|Et eripuit animam meam]], on the day of the resurrection, [[56:5|from the midst of the young lions|de medio catulorum leonum]], that is, from the multitude of the proud and savage Jews, raising me up to the immortal state. [[56:5|I slept|Dormivi]], in death and in the tomb, [[56:5|troubled|conturbatus]], that is, trodden down, oppressed, slain. [[56:5|The sons of men|Filii hominum]], not sons of God, namely my adversaries aforesaid, [[56:5|whose teeth are weapons and arrows|dentes eorum arma et sagittæ]], that is, they are like weapons, and likewise like arrows: for as a man is assailed with weapons and wounded by an arrow, so the Jews assailed me with words, which are formed by mouth and teeth, and sought to have me harmed, saying to Pilate: [[John 18:30|If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up to thee|Si non esset hic malefactor, non tibi tradidissemus eum]]. [[56:5|And their tongue a sharp sword|Et lingua eorum gladius acutus]]: for they cried out: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]. Therefore it is written: [[Jer 9:8|Their tongue is a piercing arrow|Sagitta vulnerans lingua eorum]].

paras.t: Deinde Propheta Christum sic conculcatum et passum conspiciens, ejus resurrectionem, ascensionem et glorificationem desiderans : Exaltare, inquit, super cœlos, Deus, id est, tu, Christe, verus Deus, super omnes cœlos ascende : sicut ait Apostolus, Qui descendit, ipse est et qui ascendit super omnes cœlos. Et in omni terra gloria tua, id est, per totum mundum prædicetur excellentia tua, manifestetur potentia tua, et notitia tua hominibus reveletur : secundum quod apud Isaiam legitur : In doctrinis glorificate Dominum in insulis maris ; a finibus terræ audivimus laudes, gloriam Justi. Unde post resurrectionem Christus ait discipulis : Eritis mihi testes in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ.
paras.en: Then the Prophet, beholding Christ thus trodden down and suffering, and longing for his resurrection, ascension and glorification, says: [[56:6|Be thou exalted|Exaltare]], [[56:6|O God, above the heavens|super cœlos, Deus]], that is, do thou, O Christ, true God, ascend above all the heavens: as the Apostle says: [[Eph 4:10|He that descended is the same also that ascended above all the heavens|Qui descendit, ipse est et qui ascendit super omnes cœlos]]. [[56:6|And thy glory above all the earth|Et in omni terra gloria tua]], that is, let thy excellence be preached throughout the whole world, thy power be made manifest, and the knowledge of thee be revealed to men: according to what is read in Isaias: [[Is 24:15|glorify ye the Lord in instruction|In doctrinis glorificate Dominum]] [[Is 24:15|in the islands of the sea|in insulis maris]]; [[Is 24:16|from the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the just one|a finibus terræ audivimus laudes, gloriam Justi]]. Hence after the resurrection Christ says to the disciples: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me|Eritis mihi testes]] [[Acts 1:8|in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]].

paras.t: Laqueum mortis, id est insidias occidendi, paraverunt Judæi pedibus meis, id est mihi ipsi ; et incurvaverunt, id est, humiliaverunt et persecuti sunt, animam meam, calumniando ac detrahendo verbis, operibus atque miraculis meis, dicentes, Seducit turbas ; et, Homo vorax ; et, In Beelzebub ejicit dæmones. Vel, Incurvaverunt animam meam, id est, a via justitiæ et ab ipsa veritate eam conabantur deflectere adulando, dicentes : Magister, scimus quia verax es. Foderunt ante faciem meam foveam : id est, mortis devorationem seu crucis passionem mihi aperte præparaverunt ; et inciderunt in eam : quia me interficiendo meruerunt a Romanis occidi, æternaliterque damnari. Qui enim alteri nocere disponit, primo se ipsum interimit, juxta illud : Propter malitiam tuam circumdatus es laqueis, et conturbat te formido subita.
paras.en: [[56:7|A snare|Laqueum]] of death, that is, a plot to kill, the Jews [[56:7|prepared|paraverunt]] [[56:7|for my feet|pedibus meis]], that is, for me myself; [[56:7|and they bowed down|et incurvaverunt]], that is, they humbled and persecuted, [[56:7|my soul|animam meam]], by slandering and disparaging my words, works and miracles, saying: [[John 7:12|he seduceth the people|Seducit turbas]]; and: [[Matt 11:19|a man that is a glutton|Homo vorax]]; and: [[Luke 11:15|He casteth out devils by Beelzebub|In Beelzebub ejicit dæmones]]. Or: [[56:7|they bowed down my soul|Incurvaverunt animam meam]], that is, they tried to turn it aside from the way of justice and from the truth itself by flattery, saying: [[Matt 22:16|Master, we know that thou art a true speaker|Magister, scimus quia verax es]]. [[56:7|They dug a pit before my face|Foderunt ante faciem meam foveam]]: that is, they openly made ready for me the devouring of death, or the passion of the cross; [[56:7|and they are fallen into it|et inciderunt in eam]]: for by killing me they deserved to be slain by the Romans and to be damned eternally. For he who plans to harm another first destroys himself, according to the words: [[Job 22:5|for thy manifold wickedness|Propter malitiam tuam]] [[Job 22:10|art thou surrounded with snares, and sudden fear troubleth thee|circumdatus es laqueis, et conturbat te formido subita]] [the margin gives Job xxii, 5 and 10: Denis joins words of the two verses].

paras.t: Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum ad agendum et sustinendum quæcumque tibi placita sunt, et humanæ redemptioni necessaria. Et hoc est quod Christus ait ad Patrem : Verumtamen non sicut ego volo, sed sicut tu ; et iterum, Calicem quem dedit mihi Pater, non bibam illum? Descendi enim (inquit) de cœlo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem ejus qui misit me. Cantabo, et psalmum dicam, id est, verbo et opere te laudabo, et gratias referam. Psalmus enim bonam operationem designat.
paras.en: [[56:8|My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready|Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum]] to do and to bear whatever is pleasing to thee and needful for man's redemption. And this is what Christ says to the Father: [[Matt 26:39|Nevertheless, not as I will but as thou wilt|Verumtamen non sicut ego volo, sed sicut tu]]; and again: [[John 18:11|The chalice which my father hath given me, shall I not drink it?|Calicem quem dedit mihi Pater, non bibam illum?]] For [[John 6:38|I came down|Descendi]] (he says) [[John 6:38|from heaven, not to do my own will but the will of him that sent me|de cœlo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem ejus qui misit me]]. [[56:8|I will sing, and rehearse a psalm|Cantabo, et psalmum dicam]], that is, I will praise thee by word and deed, and give thanks. For a psalm signifies good working.

paras.t: Exsurge, gloria mea, id est, dignitas gratiæ, omnisque excellentia meæ humanitati collata, appare, et hominibus manifestare per prædicationem Apostolorum atque credentium, quatenus sciant gloriam mihi divinitus datam. Sic quoque, exsurge, psalterium, id est doctrina mea evangelica, qua Dei insignia docui: quæ doctrina ad instar psalterii suaviter sonat; et cithara, id est doctrina mea moralis et vita exemplaris ac passio mortis, videlicet ut doctrina mea et vita ac passio ad hominum agnitionem exsurgant, easque credendo assequi studeant. Hinc enim apud Isaiam prophetam Christus ait : Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes, et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus. Exsurgam de clauso sepulcro, diluculo, id est valde mane: juxta illud, Surgens Jesus mane prima sabbati.
paras.en: [[56:9|Arise, O my glory|Exsurge, gloria mea]], that is, the dignity of grace and all the excellence bestowed on my manhood, appear, and be made manifest to men through the preaching of the Apostles and of believers, so that they may know the glory given me by God. So too: [[56:9|arise psaltery|exsurge, psalterium]], that is, my gospel teaching, in which I taught the great things of God, a teaching that sounds sweetly like a psaltery; [[56:9|and harp|et cithara]], that is, my moral teaching, and my exemplary life, and the passion of my death: namely, that my teaching and life and passion may rise up to the knowledge of men, and that they may strive to attain them by believing. For hence Christ says in the prophet Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes]], [[Is 66:19|and they shall declare my glory to the Gentiles|et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus]]. [[56:9|I will arise|Exsurgam]] from the closed sepulchre [[56:9|early|diluculo]], that is, very early in the morning: according to the words: [[Mark 16:9|rising early the first day of the week|Surgens Jesus mane prima sabbati]] [Denis reads "Jesus rising"].

paras.t: Confitebor tibi confessione laudis, in populis, Domine, scilicet in Judæis, quibus per me ipsum prædicavi, teque laudavi et honoravi; et psalmum, id est laudem bonæ operationi conjunctam, dicam tibi, id est ad nominis tui honorem, in gentibus ad fidem conversis. Christus enim in mundo conversans, etiam quibusdam gentibus prædicasse ostenditur ex evangelica relatione, sicut dum ibat per Tyrum et Sidonem. Quidam quoque gentiles veniebant inter Judæos ad ejus prædicationem, secundum quod in Evangelio Joannis apostoli scribitur, quod quidam gentilium qui simul ascenderant in Jerusalem, dixerunt ad Philippum : Domine, volumus Jesum videre. Verum, quoniam Christus raro et parum gentilibus prædicavit, et quod modicum est pro nihilo reputatur, secundum Philosophum: idcirco istis non obviat quod Christus asseruit, Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel. Ideo quod Christus nunc dicit, Psalmum dicam tibi in gentibus, magis per discipulos quam per se ipsum effecit. Illis enim quibus ante passionem dixit, In viam gentium ne abieritis; post resurrectionem locutus est, Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ; et iterum, Euntes docete omnes gentes.
paras.en: [[56:10|I will give praise to thee|Confitebor tibi]] with the confession of praise, [[56:10|O Lord, among the people|in populis, Domine]], namely among the Jews, to whom I preached in my own person, and praised and honoured thee; [[56:10|I will sing a psalm|et psalmum]], that is, praise joined to good working, [[56:10|to thee|dicam tibi]], that is, to the honour of thy name, [[56:10|among the nations|in gentibus]] converted to the faith. For Christ, while he lived in the world, is shown by the gospel narrative to have preached even to some Gentiles, as when he went through Tyre and Sidon[[Matt 15:21||]]. Some Gentiles also came among the Jews to his preaching, as is written in the Gospel of John the apostle, that certain of the Gentiles who had come up together to Jerusalem said to Philip: [[John 12:21|Sir, we would see Jesus|Domine, volumus Jesum videre]]. But since Christ preached to the Gentiles rarely and little, and what is slight is reckoned as nothing, according to the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle], therefore what Christ declared does not stand against this: [[Matt 15:24|I was not sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]]. Therefore what Christ now says, [[56:10|I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations|Psalmum dicam tibi in gentibus]], he brought about more through his disciples than through himself. For to those to whom before the passion he said, [[Matt 10:5|Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles|In viam gentium ne abieritis]], after the resurrection he spoke thus: [[Mark 16:15|preach the gospel to every creature|Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]; and again: [[Matt 28:19|Going|Euntes]] [[Matt 28:19|teach ye all nations|docete omnes gentes]].

paras.t: Ideo autem, o Domine, confitebor tibi, Quoniam magnificata est usque ad cælos misericordia tua, id est, quia misericordiæ tuæ effectus magnus factus est, pertingendo a terra usque ad cives cælestes, quoniam per gratiam tuam homines peccatores convertuntur, atque ad angelorum consortium perducuntur. In futura siquidem resurrectione, nec nubent, neque nubentur; sed erunt tanquam angeli Dei. Et usque ad nubes veritas tua: id est, veritatis et sapientiæ tuæ illuminatio magna facta est, pertingens usque ad sanctos Apostolos, divinique verbi prædicatores atque doctores: qui nomine nubium intelliguntur, quia a sole justitiæ et fonte sapientiæ Domino Jesu Christo prius ac plenius illustrati sunt, quam ceteri homines in terra morantes, quemadmodum nubes aeris prius recipiunt radios solis, quam terra. Dicuntur quoque Apostoli et doctores, nubes: quia de eis velut de nubibus Deus tonat mandatis, fulgurat signis, et pluit salutaribus documentis. De his namque scriptum est: Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant? Et rursus: Assument pennas ut aquilæ; current, et non laborabunt; volabunt, et non deficient.
paras.en: And therefore, O Lord, [[56:10|I will give praise to thee|confitebor tibi]], [[56:11|for thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens|Quoniam magnificata est usque ad cælos misericordia tua]], that is, because the effect of thy mercy has become great, reaching from the earth even to the citizens of heaven, since by thy grace sinful men are converted and brought into the fellowship of the angels. For in the resurrection to come [[Matt 22:30|they shall neither marry nor be married, but shall be as the angels of God|nec nubent, neque nubentur; sed erunt tanquam angeli Dei]]. [[56:11|And thy truth unto the clouds|Et usque ad nubes veritas tua]]: that is, the illumination of thy truth and wisdom has become great, reaching even to the holy Apostles, and the preachers and doctors of the divine word: who are understood by the name of clouds, because they were enlightened by the Sun of justice and fount of wisdom, the Lord Jesus Christ, sooner and more fully than the rest of men dwelling on the earth, as the clouds of the air receive the rays of the sun before the earth does. The Apostles and doctors are also called clouds because from them, as from clouds, God thunders with commandments, flashes with signs, and rains with saving teachings. For of them it is written: [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant]]? And again: [[Is 40:31|they shall take wings as eagles, they shall run and not be weary|Assument pennas ut aquilæ; current, et non laborabunt]]; they shall fly, [[Is 40:31|and not faint|et non deficient]] [the Vulgate has *ambulabunt*, "they shall walk"; Denis reads *volabunt*, "they shall fly"].

paras.t: Exaltare super cœlos, Deus, etc. Versus iste, qui jam videtur satis elucidatus, repetitur, propter sententiæ suæ dignitatem, et quia Christi exaltatio, omnium præcedentium actionum et passionum ejus finis censetur.
paras.en: [[56:12|Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens|Exaltare super cœlos, Deus]], etc. This verse, which seems already sufficiently explained, is repeated because of the dignity of its meaning, and because the exaltation of Christ is reckoned the end of all his preceding actions and sufferings.

56.title: EXPLANATIO TROPOLOGICA SEU MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI SEXTI.
56.title_en: Tropological or moral explanation of the same fifty-sixth psalm.

paras.t: Denique, juxta tropologicum sensum, per David fugientem a Saul in speluncam, intelligitur quilibet Christianus a tentante et persequente mundo seu dæmone fugiens ad Christum, atque in ejus vulneribus se abscondens, in quibus est omni fideli summum tutissimumque refugium, juxta illud: Ingredere in petram, abscondere in fossa humo, id est, accede ad Christum, et in corpore ejus propter te vulnerato te ipsum absconde. Unde per Isaiam iterum Dominus ait: Vade, populus meus, intra cubicula tua, claude ostia tua super te, abscondere modicum ad momentum, donec pertranseat indignatio mea, id est tempus persecutionis præsentis.
paras.en: Lastly, according to the tropological sense, by David [[56:1|when he fled from Saul into the cave|fugientem a Saul in speluncam]] is understood any Christian who flees from the world or the devil, which tempts and persecutes him, to Christ, and hides himself in His wounds, in which every one of the faithful has the highest and safest refuge, according to that saying: [[Is 2:10|Enter thou into the rock, and hide thee in the pit|Ingredere in petram, abscondere in fossa humo]], that is, draw near to Christ, and hide thyself in His body, wounded for thy sake. Whence the Lord says again through Isaias: [[Is 26:20|Go, my people, enter into thy chambers, shut thy doors upon thee, hide thyself a little for a moment, until the indignation pass away|Vade, populus meus, intra cubicula tua, claude ostia tua super te, abscondere modicum ad momentum, donec pertranseat indignatio mea]] [Denis reads "my indignation"], that is, the time of the present persecution.

paras.t: Ecclesia ergo, seu quilibet Christianus qui per multas tribulationes tendit ad patriam, illudque sancti Job pensat, Ecce non est auxilium mihi in me, divinam invocet opem, et dicat: Miserere mei peccatoris vilissimi, Deus piissime, veniam conferendo; miserere mei, gratiam infundendo, qui sum miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus, putans me aliquid esse, quum nihil sim; qui ad illorum pertineo numerum, de quibus scriptum est, Exacerbastis eum qui fecit vos, Deum æternum. Quoniam in te confidit anima mea, quia tu solus potes facere mundum de immundo, meque salvare. Scio enim veraciter scriptum: Maledictus qui confidit in homine, et ponit carnem brachium suum, et a Domino recedit cor ejus. Nam de his qui in rebus creatis et bonis caducis spem suam constituunt, apud Isaiam scriptum est: Confidunt in nihili, et loquuntur vanitates. Et Amos propheta ait: Væ, qui lætamini in nihili; qui dicitis, Numquid non in fortitudine nostra assumpsimus nobis cornua? Omnia enim creata, per comparationem ad Deum immensum, sunt velut nihilum et inane, secundum quod per Isaiam dictum est de Deo sublimi et benedicto: Extendit velut nihilum cœlos. Ecce quam fructuosus, dulcis et salutaris est iste versiculus, quamque incessanter est nobis mente et ore revolvendus. Dicamusque eum cum plena et amorosa fiducia, quoniam quantum adipisci confidimus, tantum utique recipiemus et exaudiemur, orantes: Fiat misericordia tua, Domine, super nos, quemadmodum speravimus in te.
paras.en: Let the Church, then, or any Christian who is making his way to the fatherland through many tribulations, and who ponders that saying of holy Job, [[Job 6:13|Behold there is no help for me in myself|Ecce non est auxilium mihi in me]], call upon the help of God and say: [[56:2|Have mercy on me|Miserere mei]], a most vile sinner, [[56:2|O God|Deus]] most loving, by granting pardon; [[56:2|have mercy on me|miserere mei]], by pouring in grace, for I am [[Apoc 3:17|wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus]], thinking myself to be something when I am nothing[[Gal 6:3||]]; I who belong to the number of those of whom it is written: [[Bar 4:7|you have provoked him who made you, the eternal God|Exacerbastis eum qui fecit vos, Deum æternum]]. [[56:2|for my soul trusteth in thee|Quoniam in te confidit anima mea]], because Thou alone canst make the clean out of the unclean[[Job 14:4||]], and save me. For I know that it is truly written: [[Jer 17:5|Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord|Maledictus qui confidit in homine, et ponit carnem brachium suum, et a Domino recedit cor ejus]]. For of those who set their hope in created things and in perishable goods it is written in Isaias: [[Is 59:4|they trust in a mere nothing, and speak vanities|Confidunt in nihili, et loquuntur vanitates]]. And the prophet Amos says: [[Amos 6:1|Woe to you|Væ]], [[Amos 6:14|that rejoice in a thing of nought: you that say: Have we not taken unto us horns by our own strength?|qui lætamini in nihili; qui dicitis, Numquid non in fortitudine nostra assumpsimus nobis cornua?]]? For all created things, compared with the immeasurable God, are as nothing and void, according to what was said through Isaias of God most high and blessed: He [[Is 40:22|stretcheth out the heavens as nothing|Extendit velut nihilum cœlos]]. See how fruitful, sweet and wholesome this little verse is, and how unceasingly we should turn it over in mind and mouth. And let us say it with full and loving confidence, since as much as we trust to obtain, so much indeed shall we receive and be heard, praying: [[Ps 32:22|Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee|Fiat misericordia tua, Domine, super nos, quemadmodum speravimus in te]].

paras.t: Et in umbra alarum tuarum, id est in protectione tua, sperabo, donec transeat iniquitas, id est, quamdiu in hac vita, in qua sine peccato non vivitur, præsertim quum justus septies cadat in die, permansero. Quum enim in medio laqueorum positi sumus, nunquam securi esse debemus, nec desperare, sed sub divinæ pietatis alis indesinenter nos ipsos statuere, atque in Domino Deo, sicut in patre indulgentissimo et affectuosissimo semper sperare. Clamabo, non tam alta voce quam ingenti affectu, ad Deum altissimum, die et nocte ejus gratiam invocando; Deum qui benefecit mihi, multa beneficia conferendo, videlicet dona naturæ, et munera gratiæ: et quia hucusque benefecit mihi, confido quod de cetero quoque benefaciat mihi.
paras.en: [[56:2|And in the shadow of thy wings|Et in umbra alarum tuarum]], that is, in Thy protection, [[56:2|will I hope, until iniquity pass away|sperabo, donec transeat iniquitas]]: that is, as long as I remain in this life, in which no one lives without sin, especially since the just man falls seven times a day[[Prov 24:16||]]. For since we are set in the midst of snares, we ought never to be secure, nor yet to despair, but to place ourselves unceasingly under the wings of God's loving-kindness, and always to hope in the Lord God as in a most indulgent and most affectionate father. [[56:3|I will cry|Clamabo]], not so much with a loud voice as with great affection, [[56:3|to God the most high|ad Deum altissimum]], calling upon His grace day and night; [[56:3|to God who hath done good to me|Deum qui benefecit mihi]] by bestowing many benefits, namely the gifts of nature and the endowments of grace; and because He has done good to me until now, I trust that He will do good to me henceforth also.

paras.t: Deinde beneficia ejus plenius enarrantur. Nam Misit Deus Pater de cœlo unigenitum Filium suum, et liberavit me Pater per Filium, seu Filius per passionem et sanguinem suum, de originali peccato et morte æterna. Hoc est quod Isaias precabatur: Emitte Agnum, Domine, dominatorem terræ, de petra deserti ad montem filiæ Sion; et rursus: Rorate, cœli, desuper, et nubes pluant Justum; aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem. Quæ omnia impleta esse ostendit sacratissimus evangelista Joannes: In hoc (inquiens) apparuit caritas Dei in nobis, quoniam Filium suum unigenitum misit Deus in mundum, ut vivamus per eum. Propter quod et Petrus scribit: Non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis, sed pretioso sanguine quasi agni immaculati Christi. Dedit in opprobrium conculcantes me: id est, Filius Dei, mundi Salvator, pro me dejecit et expugnavit adversarios meos, utpote mundum atque diabolum. Ipse enim, sicut in Evangelio scriptum est, fortem armatum, id est dæmonem, ligavit, et vasa ejus, id est peccatores, de manu ejus diripuit. Propter quod, passione instante, Christus dixit: Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras, id est, de mentibus hominum expelleretur. Quod autem Christus vicerit mundum, constat ex eo quod ipse ait discipulis: In mundo pressuram habebitis; sed confidite, ego vici mundum. Christus namque suâ conversatione ac passione gratiam nobis promeruit, formamque monstravit vincendi omnia delectabilia et terribilia mundi, ita quod nec prospera sæculi nos delectent, nec adversa deterreant, sed Christi in omnibus imitantes vestigia, gradiamur regia via, de qua scriptum est: Hæc est via; ambulate in ea, et non declinetis neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram.
paras.en: Next His benefits are told more fully. For God the Father [[56:4|hath sent|Misit]] [[56:4|from heaven|de cœlo]] His only-begotten Son, [[56:4|and delivered me|et liberavit me]]: the Father through the Son, or the Son through His passion and His blood, from original sin and eternal death. This is what Isaias prayed for: [[Is 16:1|Send forth, O Lord, the lamb, the ruler of the earth, from Petra of the desert, to the mount of the daughter of Sion|Emitte Agnum, Domine, dominatorem terræ, de petra deserti ad montem filiæ Sion]]; and again: [[Is 45:8|Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the just: let the earth be opened, and bud forth a saviour|Rorate, cœli, desuper, et nubes pluant Justum; aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem]]. That all this has been fulfilled the most holy evangelist John shows, saying: [[1 John 4:9|By this|In hoc]] (he says) [[1 John 4:9|hath the charity of God appeared towards us, because God hath sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we may live by him|apparuit caritas Dei in nobis, quoniam Filium suum unigenitum misit Deus in mundum, ut vivamus per eum]]. For this reason Peter also writes: [[1 Pet 1:18|you were not redeemed with corruptible things, as gold or silver, from your vain conversation of the tradition of your fathers|Non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis]], [[1 Pet 1:19|But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb unspotted|sed pretioso sanguine quasi agni immaculati Christi]]. [[56:4|he hath made them a reproach that trod upon me|Dedit in opprobrium conculcantes me]]: that is, the Son of God, the Saviour of the world, cast down and overcame my adversaries for me, namely the world and the devil. For He, as is written in the Gospel, bound the strong man armed, that is, the devil, and plundered his vessels, that is, sinners, out of his hand[[Luke 11:21||]][[Matt 12:29||]] [no margin reference here; Denis joins the "strong man armed" of Luke with the binding and the plundered vessels of Matthew]. For this reason, when His passion was at hand, Christ said: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]], that is, he would be driven out of the minds of men. And that Christ has overcome the world is plain from what He said to His disciples: [[John 16:33|In the world you shall have distress. But have confidence. I have overcome the world|In mundo pressuram habebitis; sed confidite, ego vici mundum]]. For by His way of life and His passion Christ merited grace for us, and showed us the pattern of overcoming all the delights and terrors of the world, so that neither the prosperity of the world may delight us nor its adversities frighten us, but following the footsteps of Christ in all things we may walk along the royal road, of which it is written: [[Is 30:21|This is the way, walk ye in it: and go not aside neither to the right hand, nor to the left|Hæc est via; ambulate in ea, et non declinetis neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram]].

paras.t: Misit Deus misericordiam suam et veritatem suam, id est Filium suum, qui dicitur, Misericordia Dei, quantum ad gentiles, quibus sola misericordia datus est; et, Veritas, quantum ad Judæos, quibus ex promissione est datus: sicque ratio quædam justitiæ consideratur in hoc, quod ad Judæos descendit. Vel sic: Misit Deus misericordiam suam, id est, gratiam copiosam infudit hominibus, maxime tempore evangelicæ legis; et veritatem suam, id est, sicut in veteri lege prædixit, ita per Christum implevit, secundum quod scriptum est: Lex per Moysen data est; gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est. Et eripuit Deus Pater, per Filium suum dilectum, animam meam de medio catulorum leonum, id est de exercitu dæmonum: de quorum unoquoque Petrus disseruit, Adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret. Dum enim a peccatis eripimur, de medio dæmonum liberamur, quum idem sit, esse servum peccati, et dæmonis. Christus autem ab omni nos labe peccati redemit, juxta illud: Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Dormivi conturbatus: id est, antequam gratiam Christi recepi, peccatis subjacui, interiusque inordinatus fui: quod ad mortis pertinet somnium. Propter quod taliter dormienti, videlicet in vitiis permanenti, clamat Apostolus: Surge, qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis, et illuminabit te Christus. Hujus autem versiculi sensum Christus apud Osee pulchre inducit, dicendo: De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos.
paras.en: [[56:4|God hath sent his mercy and his truth|Misit Deus misericordiam suam et veritatem suam]], that is, His Son, who is called the Mercy of God with regard to the gentiles, to whom He was given out of mercy alone, and the Truth with regard to the Jews, to whom He was given by promise: and so a certain ground of justice is seen in this, that He came down to the Jews. Or thus: [[56:4|God hath sent his mercy|Misit Deus misericordiam suam]], that is, He poured out abundant grace upon men, above all in the time of the law of the Gospel; [[56:4|and his truth|et veritatem suam]], that is, as He foretold in the old law, so He fulfilled it through Christ, according to what is written: [[John 1:17|the law was given by Moses: grace and truth came by Jesus Christ|Lex per Moysen data est; gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est]]. [[56:5|And he hath delivered|Et eripuit]], God the Father, through His beloved Son, [[56:5|my soul from the midst of the young lions|animam meam de medio catulorum leonum]], that is, from the army of demons: of each of whom Peter declared: [[1 Pet 5:8|your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|Adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret]]. For when we are rescued from sins, we are set free from the midst of the demons, since to be the servant of sin and to be the servant of the devil is the same thing. And Christ has redeemed us from every stain of sin, according to that saying: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. [[56:5|I slept troubled|Dormivi conturbatus]]: that is, before I received the grace of Christ I lay under sins, and was disordered within; which belongs to the sleep of death. For this reason the Apostle cries to one who sleeps thus, namely who remains in vices: [[Eph 5:14|Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead: and Christ shall enlighten thee|Surge, qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis, et illuminabit te Christus]]. And Christ beautifully brings in the sense of this little verse in Osee, saying: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos]].

paras.t: Filii hominum Ecclesiam persequentium, justis detrahentium, seu false docentium; dentes eorum, id est maligni sermones, sunt arma, quibus electos impugnant, et sagittæ, quibus eorum famam denigrant, et animas lædere cupiunt; et lingua eorum, id est perversa doctrina, gladius acutus, usque ad interiora pertinens, animam a Deo separans, eamque spiritualiter occidens. Nam, teste Apostolo, sermo talis ut cancer serpit.
paras.en: [[56:5|The sons of men|Filii hominum]] who persecute the Church, disparage the just, or teach falsely: [[56:5|whose teeth|dentes eorum]], that is, their malicious words, [[56:5|are weapons|sunt arma]], with which they attack the elect, [[56:5|and arrows|et sagittæ]], with which they blacken their good name and seek to wound their souls; [[56:5|and their tongue|et lingua eorum]], that is, their perverse teaching, is [[56:5|a sharp sword|gladius acutus]], reaching to the inmost parts, separating the soul from God and killing it spiritually. For, as the Apostle bears witness, such speech [[2 Tim 2:17|spreadeth like a canker|ut cancer serpit]].

paras.t: Exaltare super cœlos, Deus, id est, ab omnibus cœlestibus civibus exalteris ac honoreris. Quod dicit Ecclesia, non orando, sed divinæ beatitudini congratulando, suum affectum Beatis conformando. Et in omni terra gloria tua. Gloria proprie dicitur clara cum laude notitia. Orat ergo vir justus, ut Deus ab universis in terra clare per fidem agnoscatur, atque per caritatem laudetur: quod tempore Christi præcipue adimpletum videtur, prout apud Isaiam legitur: Repleta est terra scientia Domini.
paras.en: [[56:6|Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens|Exaltare super cœlos, Deus]], that is, mayest Thou be exalted and honoured by all the citizens of heaven. This the Church says not by way of prayer, but by rejoicing in the divine beatitude, conforming her affection to that of the Blessed. [[56:6|and thy glory above all the earth|Et in omni terra gloria tua]] [Denis reads "in omni terra", "in all the earth"]. Glory is properly defined as clear knowledge joined with praise. So the just man prays that God may be clearly known by all on earth through faith, and praised through charity: which seems to have been fulfilled above all in the time of Christ, as we read in Isaias: [[Is 11:9|the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord|Repleta est terra scientia Domini]].

paras.t: Laqueum paraverunt pedibus meis. Hoc est quod Christus discipulis et in eorum persona toti Ecclesiæ ait: Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur, quia non est servus major domino suo. Invisibiles etiam hostes laqueum, id est deceptiones, parant pedibus nostris, id est operibus et desideriis nostris. Vadit enim diabolus, et assumit septem spiritus nequiores se, qui si intromittantur, habitant in corde humano. Et incurvaverunt a via justitiæ animam meam, vel saltem conati sunt eam incurvare a recto Dei itinere. Vel, Incurvaverunt, id est, tribulaverunt, sicut testatur Apostolus: Dejicimur, sed non perimus. Foderunt ante faciem meam foveam, id est, aperte insidiati sunt mihi, et contumeliis atque injuriis affecerunt me; et inciderunt in eam, id est, se ipsos in foveam culpæ, mortemque animæ præcipitaverunt. Omnia enim, etiam dura et mala, cooperantur electis in bonum; sed iniqui eos persequentes, sibimetipsis nocent, et damnationem lacus infernalis acquirunt.
paras.en: [[56:7|They prepared a snare for my feet|Laqueum paraverunt pedibus meis]]. This is what Christ says to His disciples, and in their person to the whole Church: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]], for [[John 15:20|The servant is not greater than his master|non est servus major domino suo]]. The invisible enemies too prepare a snare, that is, deceptions, for our feet, that is, for our works and our desires. For the devil, as it is written, [[Luke 11:26|he goeth and taketh with him seven other spirits more wicked than himself|Vadit enim diabolus, et assumit septem spiritus nequiores se]]; and if they are let in, they dwell in the human heart. [[56:7|and they bowed down|Et incurvaverunt]] from the way of justice [[56:7|my soul|animam meam]], or at least they tried to bend it from the right road of God. Or, [[56:7|they bowed down|Incurvaverunt]], that is, they afflicted me, as the Apostle bears witness: [[2 Cor 4:9|We are cast down: but we perish not|Dejicimur, sed non perimus]]. [[56:7|They dug a pit before my face|Foderunt ante faciem meam foveam]], that is, they laid snares for me openly, and assailed me with insults and injuries; [[56:7|and they are fallen into it|et inciderunt in eam]], that is, they have cast themselves headlong into the pit of guilt and into the death of the soul. For all things, even hard and evil ones, work together unto good for the elect[[Rom 8:28||]]; but the wicked who persecute them harm themselves, and earn the damnation of the pit of hell.

paras.t: Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum. Hoc est quod quotidie in Oratione dominica dicimus: Fiat voluntas tua sicut in cœlo et in terra. Unde ait Apostolus: Non ex tristitia aut necessitate; hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus. Hanc sanctam cordis parationem facit propriæ voluntatis abnegatio, obedientia vera, et caritas fervida. Studeamus ergo, carissimi, cor paratum habere ad universa agenda ac patienda quæ Deo sunt placita; nec aliquid nobis contingens moleste feramus, sed divinæ voluntati nos pure et integre offeramus, commendemus et relinquamus. Nec possumus Deum amplius venerari, quam ita: imo, quo istud perfectius agimus, eo magis meremur, Deo cariores atque in omni virtute perfectiores efficimur. Implemus enim quod Apostolus ad Romanos tradidit: Probetis quæ sit voluntas Dei bona, beneplacens et perfecta.
paras.en: [[56:8|My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready|Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum]]. This is what we say every day in the Lord's Prayer: [[Matt 6:10|Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven|Fiat voluntas tua sicut in cœlo et in terra]]. Whence the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 9:7|not with sadness or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver|Non ex tristitia aut necessitate; hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus]]. This holy readiness of heart is brought about by the denial of one's own will, true obedience, and fervent charity. Let us strive, then, dearly beloved, to have a heart ready to do and to suffer all things that are pleasing to God; and let us take nothing that befalls us amiss, but offer, commend and abandon ourselves purely and wholly to the divine will. Nor can we honour God more than in this way; nay, the more perfectly we do it, the more we merit, and the dearer to God and the more perfect in every virtue we become. For we fulfil what the Apostle handed down to the Romans: [[Rom 12:2|that you may prove what is the good and the acceptable and the perfect will of God|Probetis quæ sit voluntas Dei bona, beneplacens et perfecta]].

paras.t: Exsurge, gloria mea, id est anima mea imagine Trinitatis insignita: exsurge, inquam, a lecto, a peccato, a torpore et omni ignavia, et age quod admonet Jeremias: Consurge, lauda in nocte, in principio vigiliarum, et effunde sicut aquam cor tuum ante conspectum Domini Dei tui. Isaias quoque: Excutere (inquit) de pulvere, consurge, sede, Jerusalem, id est anima sancta. Primo enim oportet ut anima ab inferioribus et terrenis se rebus excutiat, deinde ad cœlestia ac summa consurgat, sicque in quiete contemplationis resideat. Vel, Exsurge, gloria mea, id est, omnis gloriatio mea, in Deum ascende, ut in me ipso non glorier, sed acquiescam Apostolo admonenti: Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. Unde et apud prophetam Isaiam legitur: Addent mites in Domino lætitiam, et pauperes homines in Sancto Israel exsultabunt. Vel, Exsurge, gloria mea, id est, gratia mihi collata, omnisque habitualis perfectio mihi divinitus in Baptismo infusa seu postmodum data, in actum procede et efficaciter operare: quemadmodum jubet Apostolus, Noli negligere gratiam quæ in te est, quæ data est tibi, etc. Exsurge, psalterium, id est, laus psalmodiæ excitetur in me; et cithara, id est operatio coram Deo suavis atque sonora, ut est exercitatio pietatis ad omnia utilis.
paras.en: [[56:9|Arise, O my glory|Exsurge, gloria mea]], that is, my soul, marked with the image of the Trinity: arise, I say, from thy bed, from sin, from torpor and all sloth, and do what Jeremias counsels: [[Lam 2:19|Arise, give praise in the night, in the beginning of the watches: pour out thy heart like water, before the face of the Lord|Consurge, lauda in nocte, in principio vigiliarum, et effunde sicut aquam cor tuum ante conspectum Domini Dei tui]]. And Isaias: [[Is 52:2|Shake thyself|Excutere]] (he says) [[Is 52:2|from the dust, arise, sit up, O Jerusalem|de pulvere, consurge, sede, Jerusalem]], that is, O holy soul. For first the soul must shake itself free of lower and earthly things, then rise up to heavenly and highest things, and so sit at rest in the quiet of contemplation. Or, [[56:9|Arise, O my glory|Exsurge, gloria mea]], that is, all my glorying, go up into God, so that I may not glory in myself but obey the Apostle when he counsels: [[1 Cor 1:31|He that glorieth may glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]]. Whence we also read in the prophet Isaias: [[Is 29:19|the meek shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel|Addent mites in Domino lætitiam, et pauperes homines in Sancto Israel exsultabunt]]. Or, [[56:9|Arise, O my glory|Exsurge, gloria mea]], that is, the grace bestowed on me, and every habitual perfection poured into me by God in Baptism or given afterwards, go forth into act and work effectively; as the Apostle bids: [[1 Tim 4:14|Neglect not the grace that is in thee, which was given thee|Noli negligere gratiam quæ in te est, quæ data est tibi]], etc. [[56:9|arise psaltery|Exsurge, psalterium]], that is, let the praise of psalmody be stirred up in me; [[56:9|and harp|et cithara]], that is, a working sweet and resounding before God, such as is the exercise of godliness, which is [[1 Tim 4:8|profitable to all things|ad omnia utilis]].

paras.t: Exsurgam ab imperfectione ad vitam perfectiorem, diluculo, id est, quum splendor gratiæ tuæ, o Domine, radiaverit in me. Et ad litteram, consurgendum est diluculo ad laudandum Altissimum, juxta illud, Justus cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum; et illud, Anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritu meo in præcordiis meis, de mane vigilabo ad te. Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine, id est, in medio fratrum ac proximorum atque fidelium te laudabo: sicut ait Apostolus, Unanimes uno ore honorificetis Deum; et psalmum dicam tibi in gentibus, laudem tuam eis narrando, et de earum conversione tibi regratiando, ipsas quoque ad tua præconia incitando. Cetera ex præcedenti patent expositione.
paras.en: [[56:9|I will arise|Exsurgam]] from imperfection to a more perfect life, [[56:9|early|diluculo]], that is, when the splendour of Thy grace, O Lord, has shone upon me. And according to the letter, one must rise early to praise the Most High, according to that saying: The just man [[Ecclus 39:6|will give his heart to resort early to the Lord|cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum]]; and that: [[Is 26:9|My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me in the morning early I will watch to thee|Anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritu meo in præcordiis meis, de mane vigilabo ad te]] [the margin gives Is. xxxvi, 9; the words are Is 26:9]. [[56:10|I will give praise to thee, O Lord, among the people|Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine]], that is, I will praise Thee in the midst of my brethren and neighbours and of the faithful: as the Apostle says, [[Rom 15:6|with one mind and with one mouth you may glorify God|Unanimes uno ore honorificetis Deum]]; [[56:10|I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations|et psalmum dicam tibi in gentibus]], by telling them Thy praise, and thanking Thee for their conversion, and stirring them up as well to proclaim Thee. The rest is clear from the foregoing exposition.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum vere suavem, nobilem et […] ignitum audivimus, cujus virtutem gustat ardens amator, ac purus laudator. Conformemus igitur vitam nostram sensui hujus psalmi, ut vere nobis in eo conscripta conveniant; nec unquam ab alis divinæ defensionis anima nostra recedat, dicens Deo cum sancto Job: Pone me juxta te, et cujusvis manus pugnet contra me.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm truly sweet, noble and […] fiery, whose power the ardent lover and the pure praiser taste. Let us therefore conform our life to the sense of this psalm, so that what is written in it may truly befit us; and may our soul never withdraw from the wings of God's protection, saying to God with holy Job: [[Job 17:3|set me beside thee, and let any man's hand fight against me|Pone me juxta te, et cujusvis manus pugnet contra me]].

paras.t: Precatio. In umbra alarum tuarum, Domine, sperantibus, et ad te Deum altissimum clamantibus, Deus, miserere; mitte misericordiam tuam et veritatem tuam, quæ auferant a nobis opprobrium hostium conculcare nos volentium: ut erepti de medio eorum, gloriam potentiæ tuæ magnificemus in perpetuum.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, have mercy on those who hope, O Lord, [[56:2|in the shadow of thy wings|In umbra alarum tuarum]], and who cry to Thee, [[56:3|God the most high|Deum altissimum]]; send Thy mercy and Thy truth, to take away from us the reproach of the enemies who would trample upon us: that, rescued from the midst of them, we may magnify the glory of Thy power for ever.

57.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI SEPTIMI, […] IN PERSONA CHRISTI AD INFIDELES JUDÆOS : SI VERE UTIQUE JUSTITIAM LOQUIMINI.
57.title_en: Exposition of the fifty-seventh psalm, in the person of Christ to the unbelieving Jews: If in very deed ye speak justice.

paras.t: Est denique titulus psalmi istius : In finem, ne disperdas David, in tituli inscriptione. Omnia tituli hujus verba in titulo psalmi præcedentis continentur, taliterque ut ibi exposita sunt, intelliguntur.
paras.en: The title of this psalm, then, is: [[57:1|Unto the end, destroy not, for David, for an inscription of a title|In finem, ne disperdas David, in tituli inscriptione]]. All the words of this title are contained in the title of the preceding psalm, and they are understood as they were expounded there.

paras.t: Christus ergo Judæos incredulos increpans, ait : Si vere utique justitiam loquimini : id est, si veraciter legem atque Prophetas legitis, intelligitis, et laudatis, et si (ut dicitis) Christum veraciter exspectatis et desideratis, si quoque ex animo me Rabbi nominatis, et viam Dei in veritate docere asseritis ; tunc recte judicate, id est, ex lege et Prophetis me esse regem Messiam advertite atque discernite, o vos Judæi, qui estis secundum carnis originem, non autem secundum Dei imitationem, filii hominum, id est rationabiliter in hoc mundo conversatorum, scilicet Prophetarum ac Patriarcharum. Ad rectum vero judicium hortatur Christus Judæos in Evangelio, dicens : Nolite judicare secundum faciem, sed justum judicium judicate. Sed vos, o Judæi, erronee judicatis : cujus ratio subditur.
paras.en: Christ, then, rebuking the unbelieving Jews, says: [[57:2|If in very deed ye speak justice|Si vere utique justitiam loquimini]]: that is, if you truly read, understand and praise the law and the Prophets, and if (as you say) you truly await and desire the Christ, if also you call me Rabbi from the heart, and declare that I [[Matt 22:16|teachest the way of God in truth|viam Dei in veritate docere]]; then [[57:2|judge right things|recte judicate]], that is, from the law and the Prophets perceive and discern that I am the King Messias, O you Jews, who are, by origin according to the flesh, though not by imitation of God, [[57:2|ye sons of men|filii hominum]], that is, of men who lived according to reason in this world, namely the Prophets and Patriarchs. Christ exhorts the Jews to right judgment in the Gospel, saying: [[John 7:24|Judge not according to the appearance: but judge just judgment.|Nolite judicare secundum faciem, sed justum judicium judicate]] But you, O Jews, judge wrongly; and the reason for this follows.

paras.t: Etenim in corde iniquitates operamini in terra : id est, dolos et mala contra me cogitatis, meque persequi et occidere proponitis. Unde apud Marcum scriptum est : Cognito Jesus spiritu suo, quod ista cogitarent apud se, dixit : Quid cogitatis ista in cordibus vestris ? Et rursus ait ad eos : Intus pleni estis hypocrisi et iniquitate ; et alibi, Nunc autem quæritis me interficere, hominem qui veritatem vobis locutus sum. Injustitias, id est opera mala, manus vestræ concinnant, id est, congregant et accumulant, quia quod corde concepistis, ad effectum perducitis, me persequendo, observando, deridendo, et occidendo.
paras.en: [[57:3|For in your heart you work iniquity|Etenim in corde iniquitates operamini]] [[57:3|in the earth|in terra]]: that is, you devise deceits and evils against me, and purpose to persecute and kill me. Hence it is written in Mark: [[Mark 2:8|Jesus presently knowing in his spirit that they so thought within themselves|Cognito Jesus spiritu suo, quod ista cogitarent apud se]], He said: [[Mark 2:8|Why think you these things in your hearts?|Quid cogitatis ista in cordibus vestris ?]] And again He says to them: [[Matt 23:28|inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity|Intus pleni estis hypocrisi et iniquitate]]; and elsewhere: [[John 8:40|But now you seek to kill me, a man who have spoken the truth to you|Nunc autem quæritis me interficere, hominem qui veritatem vobis locutus sum]]. [[57:3|injustice|Injustitias]], that is, evil works, [[57:3|your hands forge|manus vestræ concinnant]], that is, gather and heap up; for what you have conceived in the heart you bring to effect, by persecuting me, watching me, mocking me and killing me.

paras.t: Alienati sunt peccatores a vulva : id est, prædicti Judæi ab ipso nativitatis exordio a Deo aversi sunt, non quod statim nati peccaverint, sed quia peccare prævisi sunt, et ad mortem præsciti, et prius odio habiti quam nati, eo modo quo Malachias dicit : Esau odio habui. Secundum hunc sensum, erraverunt ab utero, quia præsciti erant a Deo Christum summam veritatem negaturi. Propterea Christus ad eos locutus est : Vos ex patre diabolo estis, et desideria ejus vultis perficere ; et, Ideo non auditis, quia ex Deo non estis. Locuti sunt falsa, quia me mendaciter accusaverunt : sicut de eis a Jeremia scribitur : Negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt, Non est ipse. Et alibi : Ego, inquit, redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia. Unde de eis iterum scriptum est : Dereliquerunt Dominum, blasphemaverunt Sanctum Israel, abalienati sunt retrorsum.
paras.en: [[57:4|The wicked are alienated from the womb|Alienati sunt peccatores a vulva]]: that is, the aforesaid Jews were turned away from God from the very beginning of their birth; not that they sinned as soon as they were born, but because they were foreseen to sin and foreknown for death, and were hated before they were born, in the way in which Malachias says: [[Mal 1:3|have hated Esau|Esau odio habui]] In this sense, [[57:4|they have gone astray from the womb|erraverunt ab utero]], because they were foreknown by God as those who would deny Christ, the supreme Truth. Therefore Christ said to them: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil: and the desires of your father you will do|Vos ex patre diabolo estis, et desideria ejus vultis perficere]]; and: [[John 8:47|Therefore you hear them not, because you are not of God|Ideo non auditis, quia ex Deo non estis]]. [[57:4|they have spoken false things|Locuti sunt falsa]], because they accused me falsely: as is written of them by Jeremias: [[Jer 5:12|They have denied the Lord, and said, It is not he|Negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt, Non est ipse]]. And elsewhere: [[Osee 7:13|I redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me|redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia]], He says [the number of the margin's reference to Osee is lost; the words are Osee 7:13]. Hence again it is written of them: [[Is 1:4|they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backwards|Dereliquerunt Dominum, blasphemaverunt Sanctum Israel, abalienati sunt retrorsum]].

paras.t: Furor illis secundum similitudinem serpentis. Sicut enim serpens iratus venenum effundit et necat, sic Judæi contra Christum furentes, invidiæ suæ venenum evomebant, procurantes contra eum sententiam mortis, eumque crucifigentes. De hoc Judæorum furore contra Christum, patriarcha Jacob prædixisse videtur, dum ait : Maledictus furor eorum, quia pertinax, et indignatio, quia dura. Quod licet ad litteram contra Levi et Simeon dictum putetur, de sacerdotibus tamen et Pharisæis ex illorum stirpe progenitis vere accipitur. Sicut aspidis surdæ et obturantis aures suas : id est, talis fuit Judæorum malitia contra Christum, qualis est serpentis nequitia circa incantatorem. Quemadmodum enim aspis unam aurem obstruit cauda, aliam terra, ne vocem incantantis percipiat ; sic Judæi aures suas clauserunt, unam per avaritiam, alteram per invidiam, ne Christi et ejus discipulorum prædicationem audirent. Propter quod scriptum est : Dicebant multi ex ipsis Judæis, scilicet de Jesu : Dæmonium habet et insanit ; quid eum auditis ? Et alibi : Audiebant omnia hæc Pharisæi et Scribæ, qui erant avari, et deridebant eum.
paras.en: [[57:5|Their madness is according to the likeness of a serpent|Furor illis secundum similitudinem serpentis]]. For as an angry serpent pours out its venom and kills, so the Jews, raging against Christ, spewed out the venom of their envy, procuring the sentence of death against Him and crucifying Him. The patriarch Jacob seems to have foretold this fury of the Jews against Christ when he says: [[Gen 49:7|Cursed be their fury, because it was stubborn: and their wrath, because it was cruel|Maledictus furor eorum, quia pertinax, et indignatio, quia dura]]. Although this is thought to have been said literally against Levi and Simeon, it is yet truly taken of the priests and Pharisees born of their stock. [[57:5|like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ears|Sicut aspidis surdæ et obturantis aures suas]]: that is, such was the malice of the Jews against Christ as is the wickedness of the serpent towards the charmer. For as the asp stops one ear with its tail and the other with the earth, so as not to hear the voice of the charmer, so the Jews closed their ears, one through avarice, the other through envy, so as not to hear the preaching of Christ and His disciples. For this reason it is written: [[John 10:20|many of them said|Dicebant multi ex ipsis Judæis]], namely of Jesus: [[John 10:20|He hath a devil and is mad. Why hear you him?|Dæmonium habet et insanit ; quid eum auditis ?]] And elsewhere: [[Luke 16:14|Now the Pharisees, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.|Audiebant omnia hæc Pharisæi et Scribæ, qui erant avari, et deridebant eum]] [Denis adds "and the Scribes"].

paras.t: Quæ aspis, cui videlicet assimilantur Judæi, non exaudiet vocem incantantium et venefici incantantis sapienter, secundum suæ artis principia : non enim de caverna sua egreditur. Hinc ergo Judæi viperæ conformantur. Unde Joannes Baptista ait ad eos : Progenies viperarum, quis ostendit vobis fugere a ventura ira ? Denique ipse Christus : Genimina, inquit, viperarum, quomodo fugietis a judicio gehennæ ?
paras.en: [[57:6|Which|Quæ]] asp, namely the one to which the Jews are likened, [[57:6|will not hear the voice of the charmers; nor of the wizard that charmeth wisely|non exaudiet vocem incantantium et venefici incantantis sapienter]], according to the principles of his art: for it does not come out of its hole. Hence, then, the Jews are likened to the viper. So John the Baptist says to them: [[Matt 3:7|Ye brood of vipers, who hath shewed you to flee from the wrath to come?|Progenies viperarum, quis ostendit vobis fugere a ventura ira ?]] And lastly Christ Himself: [[Matt 23:33|generation of vipers|Genimina]], He says, [[Matt 23:33|how will you flee from the judgment of hell?|viperarum, quomodo fugietis a judicio gehennæ ?]]

paras.t: Deus conteret dentes eorum in ore ipsorum, id est, malignitatem verborum quæ contra Christum dixerunt, retorquebit in eos, et proprio sermone mortem sibi acquirent, quemadmodum factum est, quando dixerunt : Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros. Ex tunc namque venit super eos ira Dei usque in finem, secundum Apostolum. Molas leonum confringet Dominus : id est, minas, verba et verbera ferocium Judæorum Christo illata, Dominus cito cessare fecit, Christum ad immortalem vitam resuscitans. Propter quod Christus in Cœna dixit : Etenim ea quæ sunt de me, finem habent.
paras.en: [[57:7|God shall break in pieces their teeth in their mouth|Deus conteret dentes eorum in ore ipsorum]], that is, He will turn back upon them the malice of the words they spoke against Christ, and by their own speech they will bring death upon themselves, as happened when they said: [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]]. For from then on [[1 Thess 2:16|the wrath of God is come upon them to the end|venit super eos ira Dei usque in finem]], according to the Apostle. [[57:7|the Lord shall break the grinders of the lions|Molas leonum confringet Dominus]]: that is, the threats, words and blows [the printed text has "verba et verba", read as "verba et verbera"] of the fierce Jews brought against Christ the Lord soon made to cease, raising Christ to immortal life. For which reason Christ said at the Supper: [[Luke 22:37|For the things concerning me have an end|Etenim ea quæ sunt de me, finem habent]].

paras.t: Ad nihilum devenerunt tanquam aqua decurrens. Judæi enim increduli per Titum et Vespasianum destructi fuerunt. Ipsi quoque spiritualiter ad nihilum devenerunt, quoniam omnem gratiam et esse gratificum penitus amiserunt. Intendit arcum suum donec infirmentur : id est, Deus præparavit arma exercitus Romanorum contra Judæos, donec omnino debilitarentur, quemadmodum Christus eis prædixit : Venient dies in te, et circumdabunt te inimici tui undique, et coangustabunt te, et ad terram prosternent te.
paras.en: [[57:8|They shall come to nothing, like water running down|Ad nihilum devenerunt tanquam aqua decurrens]] [Denis reads "they have come"]. For the unbelieving Jews were destroyed by Titus and Vespasian. They also came to nothing spiritually, since they utterly lost all grace and the being that grace gives. [[57:8|he hath bent his bow till they be weakened|Intendit arcum suum donec infirmentur]]: that is, God made ready the arms of the Roman army against the Jews, until they were altogether weakened, as Christ foretold to them: [[Luke 19:43|the days shall come upon thee: and thy enemies shall cast a trench about thee and compass thee round and straiten thee on every side|Venient dies in te, et circumdabunt te inimici tui undique, et coangustabunt te]], [[Luke 19:44|And beat thee flat to the ground|et ad terram prosternent te]].

paras.t: Sicut cera quæ fluit, auferentur. Judæi enim de terra sua subito et improvise sublati sunt. Auferentur quoque in die judicii a regione vivorum ; nuncque auferuntur quotidie a grege fidelium atque consortio electorum. Supercecidit ignis, et non viderunt solem. Solet in Scriptura per ignem quælibet magna tribulatio designari. Est igitur sensus : Super infideles Judæos venit et irruit tribulatio maxima a Romanis, propter peccatum in Christum commissum ; nec tamen ex hoc perpendebant se talia pati propter Christi occisionem, nec agnoverunt per pœnas solem justitiæ Christum, sed in tenebris infidelitatis manserunt et indurati sunt, secundum quod Isaias testatur : Populus non est reversus ad percutientem se, et Dominum non exquisierunt. Et per Amos Dominus ait : Percussi vos, etc., et nec sic estis reversi ad me.
paras.en: [[57:9|Like wax that melteth they shall be taken away|Sicut cera quæ fluit, auferentur]]. For the Jews were taken away from their land suddenly and unexpectedly. They will also be taken away on the day of judgment from the land of the living; and now they are daily taken away from the flock of the faithful and the company of the elect. [[57:9|fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun|Supercecidit ignis, et non viderunt solem]]. In Scripture any great tribulation is commonly signified by fire. The sense, then, is: upon the unbelieving Jews there came and fell a very great tribulation from the Romans, because of the sin committed against Christ; and yet they did not weigh from this that they suffered such things for the slaying of Christ, nor through their punishments did they acknowledge Christ, the sun of justice, but they remained in the darkness of unbelief and were hardened, as Isaias testifies: [[Is 9:13|And the people are not returned to him who hath struck them, and have not sought after the Lord|Populus non est reversus ad percutientem se, et Dominum non exquisierunt]]. And through Amos the Lord says: [[Amos 4:9|I struck you|Percussi vos]], etc., [[Amos 4:9|yet you returned not to me|et nec sic estis reversi ad me]] [Denis's wording, "and not even so have you returned to me", recalls the refrain of Amos 4:6–11].

paras.t: Priusquam, o increduli Judæi, intelligerent spinæ vestræ, id est pœnæ vobis inflictæ, et conscientiarum vestrarum remorsus, rhamnum, id est dæmonem vos ad mala incitantem, seu dæmonum suggestiones et vitia, propter quæ ista patiebamini ; sicut viventes, sicut in ira absorbet eos : id est, quemadmodum viventes iniqui, qui se diu victuros arbitrantur, sed subito moriuntur, et sicut iratus repente absorbet eum cui irascitur ; sic Deus absorbet, absorpsit, et absorbebit vos. Jam enim ostensum est, quam multipliciter perierunt, et quomodo ad nihilum redacti dicuntur. Unde de finali hac Judæorum dejectione Dominus per Amos prophetam dicit : Venit finis super populum meum Israel ; non adjiciam ultra ut pertranseam eum. Convenienter autem per rhamnum intelliguntur diabolus, concupiscentia, seu peccatum. Rhamnus namque est herba in principio mollis ; quum autem creverit et matura facta fuerit, durissime pungit, quoniam acutissimos aculeos tunc acquirit : ita diaboli, concupiscentiæ, atque peccata in principio delectabilia offerunt, et tanquam mollis herba dulcia ingerunt, sed consentientem ad amarissimas pœnas perducunt.
paras.en: [[57:10|Before|Priusquam]], O unbelieving Jews, [[57:10|your thorns could know|intelligerent spinæ vestræ]], that is, the punishments inflicted on you and the remorse of your consciences, [[57:10|the brier|rhamnum]] ["rhamnus", a thorny shrub, the buckthorn], that is, the devil inciting you to evil, or the suggestions of the demons and the vices for which you suffered these things; [[57:10|he swalloweth them up, as alive, in his wrath|sicut viventes, sicut in ira absorbet eos]] [the margin notes the reading "sic" for the second "sicut": "as the living, so in wrath he swalloweth them up"]: that is, as the living wicked, who think they will live long but die suddenly, and as an angry man suddenly swallows up the one he is angry with; so God swallows up, has swallowed up and will swallow up you. For it has already been shown in how many ways they perished, and how they are said to have been brought to nothing. Hence of this final casting down of the Jews the Lord says through the prophet Amos: [[Amos 8:2|The end is come upon my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more|Venit finis super populum meum Israel ; non adjiciam ultra ut pertranseam eum]]. Now by the brier are fittingly understood the devil, concupiscence or sin. For the brier is a plant that is soft at first; but when it has grown and become mature it pricks most sharply, since it then acquires the sharpest thorns: so the devil, concupiscences and sins offer delights at first, and like a soft plant they put sweet things before us, but they lead the one who consents to the bitterest punishments.

paras.t: Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam : non utique zelo vindictæ, sed justitiæ amore. Quemadmodum enim (sicut scriptum est) Deus mortem non fecit, in quantum est mors, nec directe eam intendit, nec lætatur in perditione seu pœna vivorum, in quantum est quoddam malum, sed in quantum est justitiæ effectus (juxta illud Isaiæ : Heu, consolabor super hostibus meis, et vindicabor de inimicis meis, ait Dominus ; et alibi, Complebo furorem meum, et requiescere faciam indignationem meam, et consolabor) ; simili modo homo justus lætatur, dum videt vindictam injuriæ non sibi, sed Deo illatæ, in quantum vindicta est quoddam bonum divinæ justitiæ, non in quantum est proximorum perditio. Quamvis autem justus de vindicta malorum lætetur in hoc mundo, in quantum vindicta hujusmodi est pro utilitate Ecclesiæ, vel ampliori pereuntium commodo ; tamen in die judicii magis lætabitur de ultione divina, atque in patria in æternum, quoniam tunc perfecte conformabitur et inseparabiliter unietur æquitati divinæ, placebitque ei plenissime quidquid concordat divinæ justitiæ.
paras.en: [[57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam]]: not, to be sure, from zeal for revenge, but from love of justice. For just as (as it is written) [[Wis 1:13|God made not death|Deus mortem non fecit]] in so far as it is death, nor does He intend it directly, [[Wis 1:13|neither hath he pleasure in the destruction|nec lætatur in perditione]] or punishment [[Wis 1:13|of the living|vivorum]] in so far as it is an evil, but in so far as it is an effect of justice (according to that word of Isaias: [[Is 1:24|Ah!
