Therefore the Lord says through Moses: [[Lev 19:35|Do not any unjust thing in judgment, in rule, in weight, or in measure|Nolite facere iniquum aliquid in judicio, in regula, in pondere, in mensura]]; [[Lev 19:36|Let the balance be just and the weights equal|statera justa et æqua sint pondera]], that is, [[Lev 19:36|the bushel just, and the sextary equal|justus modius, æquusque sextarius]]. [[61:10|that by vanity they may together deceive|Ut decipiant ipsi de vanitate in id ipsum]]: that is, that they may deceive one another in vain things, temporal and perishable.

paras.t: Hujus proinde oppositum consulens sanctus Propheta : Nolite, inquit, sperare in iniquitate : sicut de impiis scriptum est, Confidunt in nihili. Peccatum enim nihil est : ergo nolite in peccato confidere, quasi per injustitiam atque malitiam possitis salvari aut prosperari. Et rapinas nolite concupiscere : id est, nec manu, nec affectu auferatis alicui sua, neque raptoribus communicetis, quia non solum morte digni sunt qui faciunt, sed etiam qui consentiunt. Divitiæ exteriores si affluant copiose, nolite cor apponere, id est, voluntatem vestram nolite inordinate affigere, nolite inordinate amare, retinere, augere, nolite in eis superflue occupari, videlicet ut cum labore acquirantur, cum timore possideantur, cum dolore perdantur. Non ergo culpantur divitiæ, sed inordinatus affectus. Custodiendæ enim et amandæ seu colligendæ sunt divitiæ, secundum quod ad spiritualia bona sunt necessariæ, quatenus habentes victum et vestitum, contentemur et quiescamus, atque de eo quod superest, eleemosynam faciamus. Verumtamen difficile satis est, circa affluentes divitias cor non apponere, secundum quod Christus in Evangelio asserit : Quam difficile qui divitias habent, intrabunt in regnum cœlorum ! Nihilo minus, sicut Deus potentes non abjicit, quum ipse sit potens, nisi abutantur potentia ; sic ipse divites non repellit, quum ipse sit dives, nisi divitiarum abusi fuerint copia. Sanctus Job divitiis suis cor non apposuit, qui ait : Si lætatus sum super divitiis meis multis. Et alibi, cunctis amissis : Dominus dedit (inquit), Dominus abstulit ; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est : sit nomen Domini benedictum.
paras.en: Counselling, therefore, the opposite of this, the holy Prophet says: [[61:11|Trust not|Nolite]], he says, [[61:11|in iniquity|sperare in iniquitate]]; as it is written of the wicked: [[Is 59:4|they trust in a mere nothing|Confidunt in nihili]]. For sin is nothing [that is, sin is not a thing but a lack of the good that should be there]: therefore do not trust in sin, as though by injustice and malice you could be saved or prosper. [[61:11|and covet not robberies|Et rapinas nolite concupiscere]]: that is, take nothing that is another's, neither with the hand nor in desire, and have no part with robbers; for [[Rom 1:32|not only they that do them, but they also that consent to them|non solum morte digni sunt qui faciunt, sed etiam qui consentiunt]] are worthy of death. [[61:11|if riches|Divitiæ]], outward ones, [[61:11|abound|si affluant]] plentifully, [[61:11|set not your heart upon them|nolite cor apponere]]: that is, do not fix your will on them inordinately, do not inordinately love, keep or increase them, do not busy yourselves with them beyond need, so that they are gained with toil, possessed with fear and lost with grief. It is not riches, then, that are blamed, but inordinate affection. For riches are to be kept and loved or gathered so far as they are necessary for spiritual goods, so that, having food and clothing, we may be content and at rest, and give alms out of what is over. Yet it is hard enough not to set one's heart on riches that abound, as Christ declares in the Gospel: [[Luke 18:24|How hardly shall they that have riches enter|Quam difficile qui divitias habent, intrabunt]] into the kingdom of heaven! [the margin gives "Ibid. xviii, 24", which here can only be Luke 18:24; "kingdom of heaven" is as in Matt 19:23] Nevertheless, just as [[Job 36:5|God doth not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty|Deus potentes non abjicit, quum ipse sit potens]], unless they abuse their power, so he does not repel the rich, since he himself is rich, unless they have abused the abundance of their riches. Holy Job did not set his heart upon his riches, who says: [[Job 31:25|If I have rejoiced over my great riches|Si lætatus sum super divitiis meis multis]]. And elsewhere, when he had lost everything: [[Job 1:21|the Lord gave|Dominus dedit]], he says, [[Job 1:21|the Lord hath taken away: as it hath pleased the Lord, so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord|Dominus abstulit ; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est : sit nomen Domini benedictum]].

paras.t: Semel, id est sine retractatione, ut pote immobiliter, firmiter atque certissime, locutus est Deus, per se ipsum jam incarnatum, et per Prophetas ac Apostolos. Duo hæc audivi, in illa locutione occulta et interna, scilicet in illuminatione supernaturali facta per Spiritum Sanctum. Quæ autem sint duo hæc, subdit : quia potestas Dei est, id est justa potentia ad puniendum iniquos ; et tibi, Domine, misericordia ad coronandum bonos ultra condignum. Et hoc sic esse, constat ex eo, quia tu reddes unicuique juxta opera sua, tanquam justissimus judex. De quo in libro Job legitur : Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas ; opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet eis. Videtur autem hic potestas pro justitia accipi, quia ad exercendum justitiam præcipue est necessaria potestas. Unde de Deo alibi scriptum est : Virtus tua, justitiæ initium est. Attribuuntur itaque hæc duo Deo potissimum, quoniam omnia quæ de Deo affirmat divina Scriptura, præsertim per comparationem ad creaturas, ad ista duo reducuntur. Propter quod ante dictum est : Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas. Porro, ut tactum est, hoc quod dicitur, Semel locutus est Deus, non est referendum ad numerum, quum multifarie multisque modis locutus sit nobis, sed ad firmitatem. Juxta quem sensum in libro beati Job dicitur : Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit.
paras.en: [[61:12|once|Semel]], that is, without retracting, inasmuch as immovably, firmly and most certainly, [[61:12|God hath spoken|locutus est Deus]], through himself, now incarnate, and through the Prophets and Apostles. [[61:12|these two things have I heard|Duo hæc audivi]], in that hidden and inward speaking, namely in the supernatural enlightening wrought by the Holy Ghost. What these two things are, he adds: [[61:12|that power belongeth to God|quia potestas Dei est]], that is, just might for punishing the wicked; [[61:13|And mercy to thee, O Lord|et tibi, Domine, misericordia]], for crowning the good beyond their deserving. And that this is so is plain from this, [[61:13|for thou wilt render to every man according to his works|quia tu reddes unicuique juxta opera sua]], as the most just judge. Of whom we read in the book of Job: [[Job 34:10|far from God be wickedness, and iniquity from the Almighty|Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas]]; [[Job 34:11|For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them|opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet eis]]. Here, however, power seems to be taken for justice, because power is especially needed for exercising justice. Hence it is written elsewhere of God: [[Wis 12:16|thy power is the beginning of justice|Virtus tua, justitiæ initium est]]. These two things, then, are attributed to God above all, since everything that divine Scripture affirms of God, especially by comparison with creatures, comes back to these two. Wherefore it was said before: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]]. Further, as was touched on, the words [[61:12|God hath spoken once|Semel locutus est Deus]] are not to be referred to number, since he has spoken to us [[Heb 1:1|at sundry times and in divers manners|multifarie multisque modis]], but to firmness. In which sense it is said in the book of blessed Job: [[Job 33:14|God speaketh once, and repeateth not the selfsame thing the second time|Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit]].

paras.t: Advertendum quoque quod psalmus iste convenientissime exponi possit de Christo, quoniam anima ejus semper perfectissime fuit Deo subjecta, sicut ipse testatur : Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio ; et alibi, Quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper. Tota enim salus animæ Christi creata fuit a Deo, eratque Deus salutaris, id est beatificator, animæ Christi : propter quod apud Joannem dicitur, Non potest homo accipere quidquam, nisi ei datum fuerit desuper.
paras.en: It is also to be noted that this psalm can most fittingly be expounded of Christ, since his soul was always most perfectly subject to God, as he himself testifies: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]; and elsewhere: [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]]. For the whole salvation of Christ's soul was created by God, and God was the saviour, that is, the beatifier, of Christ's soul; wherefore it is said in John: [[John 3:27|A man cannot receive any thing, unless it be given him|Non potest homo accipere quidquam, nisi ei datum fuerit]] from above.

paras.t: Quod autem adjicitur, Non movebor amplius, sic de Christo exponendum est : Post resurrectionem non patiar magis, sed immobilis a vita (id est impassibilis) ero.
paras.en: And what is added, [[61:3|I shall be moved no more|Non movebor amplius]], is to be expounded of Christ thus: After the resurrection I shall suffer no more, but shall be immovable from life (that is, impassible).

paras.t: Quousque, o Judæi increduli, irruitis in hominem, scilicet in me Filium hominis, quem volebatis occidere? Unde ait Judæis: Vos ex patre diabolo estis, et desideria patris vestri vultis perficere. Et iterum dicit ad eos : Quid me quæritis interficere ? Interficitis universi vos, id est animas vestras, non credendo in me. Hoc ad litteram Christus dixit Judæis : In peccato vestro moriemini.
paras.en: [[61:4|How long|Quousque]], O unbelieving Jews, [[61:4|do you rush in upon a man|irruitis in hominem]], namely upon me, the Son of man, whom you wished to kill? Hence he says to the Jews: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil: and the desires of your father you will do|Vos ex patre diabolo estis, et desideria patris vestri vultis perficere]]. And again he says to them: [[John 7:20|Why seek you to kill me?|Quid me quæritis interficere ?]] [[61:4|you all kill|Interficitis universi vos]], that is, your own souls, by not believing in me. This Christ said to the Jews in so many words: [[John 8:21|you shall die in your sin|In peccato vestro moriemini]].

paras.t: Verumtamen pretium meum cogitaverunt repellere, id est, sanguinem meum voluerunt infructuosum efficere. Volebant enim nomen atque memoriam Christi delere, omnesque homines ab ejus fide avertere, ac per hoc sanguinis effusionem sine fructu statuere. Cucurri in siti, id est, vitam in hoc mundo transegi in magno desiderio humanæ salutis. Propter quod in Cœna dixit : Desiderio desideravi hoc pascha manducare vobiscum, antequam patiar. Et pendens in cruce, Sitio, inquit. Ore suo benedicebant mihi Judæi, dicentes : Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces. Et corde suo maledicebant : talia enim dicebant, ut occasionem mortis ex verbis meis elicerent.
paras.en: [[61:5|But they have thought to cast away my price|Verumtamen pretium meum cogitaverunt repellere]]: that is, they wished to make my blood fruitless. For they wished to blot out the name and memory of Christ, and to turn all men away from faith in him, and by this to make the shedding of his blood without fruit[[John 11:47||]] [the margin gives John xi, 47–50]. [[61:5|I ran in thirst|Cucurri in siti]]: that is, I passed my life in this world in great desire for the salvation of men. Wherefore at the Supper he said: [[Luke 22:15|With desire I have desired to eat this pasch with you, before I suffer|Desiderio desideravi hoc pascha manducare vobiscum, antequam patiar]]. And hanging on the cross, [[John 19:28|I thirst|Sitio]], he said. [[61:5|they blessed with their mouth|Ore suo benedicebant]] me, the Jews, saying: [[Matt 22:16|Master, we know that thou art a true speaker and teachest the way of God in truth|Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces]]. [[61:5|but cursed with their heart|Et corde suo maledicebant]]: for they said such things in order to draw from my words an occasion for my death.

paras.t: Denique Deus dicitur Christi salvator, id est a morte resuscitator ac glorificator, non a peccato redemptor. Quomodo autem cetera Christo conveniant, ex præcedentibus innotescit.
paras.en: Lastly, God is called the saviour of Christ, that is, the one who raised him from death and glorified him, not his redeemer from sin. How the rest fits Christ is clear from what has gone before.

paras.t: Ecce quam ineffabilis et admiranda est pulchritudo atque sentententia hujus psalmi: in quo ignea verba divini amoris, piam mentem totaliter inflammantia, tam copiose includuntur, totiesque repetuntur ; in quo obedientia commendatur, moralissima ac saluberrima documenta proponuntur, impii increpantur, et in ipso fine Deus pulcherrime collaudatur. Sit ergo anima nostra Deo semper subjecta, tamque reverenter ac pure intenta, ut amorosa verba psalmi præsentis ardenter et saporose pronuntiet, cor suum coram Deo confidenter effundat, nec exterioribus rebus cor apponat, sed in Deum se penitus erigat, simplificet, figat.
paras.en: Behold how unspeakable and wonderful is the beauty and meaning of this psalm: in which fiery words of divine love, setting the devout mind wholly aflame, are so abundantly contained and so often repeated; in which obedience is commended, most moral and wholesome teachings are set forth, the wicked are rebuked, and at the very end God is most beautifully praised. Let our soul, then, be ever subject to God, and so reverently and purely intent that it may utter the loving words of the present psalm ardently and with relish, pour out its heart before God with confidence[[Lam 2:19||]], and not set its heart on outward things, but raise itself wholly into God, become simple, and fix itself there.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus virtutum, a quo est omnis virtus Sanctorum, Deus auxilii et spei gloriæ nostræ, corda nostra effundimus coram te ; esto adjutor noster, Deus in æternum pius : ut te cooperante, animas nostras in patientia possideamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O God of hosts [*Deus virtutum*, also "God of powers"], from whom is all the virtue of the Saints, God of our help and of the hope of our glory, we pour out our hearts before thee: be thou our helper, God, merciful for ever; that with thee working with us we may possess our souls in patience[[Luke 21:19||]].

62.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI SECUNDI : DEUS, DEUS MEUS, AD TE DE LUCE VIGILO.
62.title_en: Exposition of the sixty-second psalm: O God, my God, to thee do I watch at break of day.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi est : Psalmus David, quum esset in deserto Idumææ : id est, psalmus iste convenit Ecclesiæ seu fideli per David significato, quum esset ipsa Ecclesia in deserto Idumææ, id est in præsenti exilio et valle hac lacrimarum, vitiis atque ærumnis repleta, a bonis vero deserta seu derelicta.
paras.en: The title of the psalm is: [[62:1|A psalm of David while he was in the desert of Edom|Psalmus David, quum esset in deserto Idumææ]]: that is, this psalm befits the Church, or the faithful soul, signified by David, when the Church herself was [[62:1|in the desert of Edom|in deserto Idumææ]] [Idumæa is the Latin name of Edom], that is, in the present exile and this vale of tears, full of vices and hardships, but bare and bereft of good things.

paras.t: Ecclesia ergo, seu quilibet justus, præsentis sæculi afflictiones expertus, divinamque consolationem efflagitans, dicat : Deus, Deus meus, id est tu, Creator omnipotens, qui es omnium Deus ratione creationis et gubernationis : specialiter vero Deus meus, propter specialem providentiam tuam circa me, qua me a malis protegis, in bonis promoves, atque ad ultimum finem recte perducis ; itemque propter singularem dilectionem et venerationem, qua te solum summe amo et colo ; ad te de luce vigilo, id est, statim quum splendor gratiæ tuæ infulserit animæ meæ, consurgo, ad te cordiali affectu mentem erigendo, ad te contemplandum, diligendum, adorandum, colendum ac promerendum. Ad litteram quoque, de luce, id est summo mane, evigilare et surgere debemus ad Dei cultum ac laudem, quatenus sobrio spiritu Deum laudantes ac invocantes, sic interiores oculi illustrentur lumine gratiæ, sicut oculi exteriores perfunduntur solis splendore. Propterea Isaias : De mane, inquit, vigilabo ad te.
paras.en: Let the Church, then, or any just man, who has known by experience the afflictions of this present world and earnestly begs for God's consolation, say: [[62:2|O God, my God|Deus, Deus meus]], that is, thou, almighty Creator, who art the God of all by reason of creation and government, but especially [[62:2|my God|Deus meus]], because of thy special providence over me, by which thou protectest me from evils, advancest me in good things, and bringest me rightly to my last end; and likewise because of the singular love and veneration with which I love and worship thee alone above all; [[62:2|to thee do I watch at break of day|ad te de luce vigilo]], that is, as soon as the splendour of thy grace has shone into my soul, I rise up, lifting my mind to thee with heartfelt affection, to contemplate, love, adore and worship thee, and to merit thee. Literally too, [[62:2|at break of day|de luce]], that is, very early in the morning, we ought to wake and rise for the worship and praise of God, so that, praising and calling upon God with a sober spirit, our inner eyes may be enlightened by the light of grace, as our outward eyes are flooded with the splendour of the sun. Therefore Isaias: [[Is 26:9|in the morning early|De mane]], he says, [[Is 26:9|I will watch to thee|vigilabo ad te]].

paras.t: Sitivit in te anima mea. Hoc est quod dixit superius, Sitivit anima mea ad Deum fortem, vivum. Sitis etenim animæ, est ingens desiderium boni nondum adepti. Est igitur sensus : Anima mea, id est appetitus meus intellectualis, puta voluntas, sitivit in te, id est, intellectuali ac magno desiderio concupivit te adipisci, consolationem tuam acquirere, a præsentibus malis salvari, atque ad te universæ beatitudinis fontem perduci : sicut Tobias ait, Domine, secundum voluntatem tuam fac mecum, et præcipe in pace recipi spiritum meum. Et Isaias : Nomen, inquit, tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ meæ. Anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritu meo in præcordiis meis, etc. Hac siti ardebat mens Pauli, dicentis : Desiderium habeo dissolvi, et esse cum Christo.
paras.en: [[62:2|For thee my soul hath thirsted|Sitivit in te anima mea]]. This is what he said above: [[Ps 41:3|My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God|Sitivit anima mea ad Deum fortem, vivum]]. For the soul's thirst is a vast desire for a good not yet attained. The sense, then, is this: [[62:2|my soul|Anima mea]], that is, my intellectual appetite, namely the will, [[62:2|hath thirsted|sitivit]] [[62:2|for thee|in te]], that is, has longed with a great intellectual desire to attain thee, to obtain thy consolation, to be saved from present evils, and to be brought to thee, the fountain of all beatitude: as Tobias says: [[Tob 3:6|O Lord, do with me according to thy will, and command my spirit to be received in peace|Domine, secundum voluntatem tuam fac mecum, et præcipe in pace recipi spiritum meum]]. And Isaias: [[Is 26:8|thy name|Nomen]], he says, [[Is 26:8|and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul|tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ meæ]]. [[Is 26:9|My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me|Anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritu meo in præcordiis meis]], etc. With this thirst burned the mind of Paul, who says: [[Phil 1:23|having a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ|Desiderium habeo dissolvi, et esse cum Christo]].

paras.t: Quam multipliciter tibi caro mea ! id est, quam multis suspiriis variisque affectibus sitivit tibi, id est ad gloriam tuam, caro mea, id est appetitus inferior sensitivus ! Insinuat iste versiculus carnem multiplicius affici ad Deum, quam animam : quod sane intelligendum est. Sive enim caro sumatur pro corpore solo, sive pro appetitu sensitivo, non conveniet ei sitire in Deum directe, proprie et immediate. Quoniam namque Deus immaterialis et simplex est, solo immateriali appetitu ad ipsum pertingitur, sicut et solo intellectuali oculo contemplatur. Carni autem secundum se, desiderium non convenit, sed in quantum anima informatur ; ipsumque desiderium potius convenit toti composito et animæ, quam carni.
paras.en: [[62:2|for thee my flesh, O how many ways|Quam multipliciter tibi caro mea]]! that is, with how many sighs and how various affections [[62:2|my flesh|caro mea]], that is, the lower, sensitive appetite, has thirsted [[62:2|for thee|tibi]], that is, for thy glory! This little verse suggests that the flesh is moved towards God in more ways than the soul: which must be rightly understood. For whether flesh be taken for the body alone or for the sensitive appetite, it will not befit it to thirst for God directly, properly and immediately. For since God is immaterial and simple, he is reached only by an immaterial appetite, just as he is beheld only by the eye of the intellect. Desire does not befit the flesh in itself, but only in so far as it is informed by the soul [that is, receives its form and life from the soul]; and desire itself belongs rather to the whole composite, and to the soul, than to the flesh.

paras.t: Quod ergo nunc dicitur caro sitire in Deum, dupliciter intelligi potest. Primo, quoniam ipsa est animæ occasio sitiendi in Deum. Corpus quippe quod corrumpitur, aggravat animam ; multasque necessitudines, sollicitudines, afflictiones ac miserias incidit anima ex unione ad corpus. Nam deprimit terrena inhabitatio sensum multa cogitantem. Hinc ergo dicitur caro multipliciter Deum sitire, etiam multiplicius quam anima : quoniam anima plures causas et incitamenta sitiendi Deum sortitur ex corpore, quam ex se ipsa. Tot enim habet causas Deum concupiscendi, quot se experitur impedimentis ab eo elongari ac retrahi. Ideo ad Romanos exclamat Apostolus : Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus? Simili sensu dicitur caro concupiscere adversus animam, non quod caro secundum se concupiscat, sed quia est animæ occasio concupiscendi adversus se ipsam. Anima enim secundum appetitum sensitivum concupiscit contra se ipsam, quantum ad appetitum intellectualem. Secundo intelligitur sic, quod caro, id est appetitus sensitivus, sitit in Deum, non directe et immediate, quasi Deus sit desiderii sui objectum ; sed quoniam ea quæ desiderat, secundum Deum desiderat, scilicet secundum rationis imperium ac directiones virtutum moralium : sititque multiplicius Deum, quam appetitus superior, quoniam plures pœnas, culpas atque miserias habet homo ex parte appetitus sensitivi, quam intellectivi, præsertim quum passiones animæ, quæ nobis sunt origo peccandi, in appetitu sensitivo fundentur.
paras.en: What is said here, then, that the flesh thirsts for God, can be understood in two ways. First, because the flesh is the soul's occasion of thirsting for God. For [[Wis 9:15|the corruptible body is a load upon the soul|Corpus quippe quod corrumpitur, aggravat animam]]; and the soul falls into many needs, cares, afflictions and miseries from its union with the body. For [[Wis 9:15|the earthly habitation presseth down the mind that museth upon many things|deprimit terrena inhabitatio sensum multa cogitantem]]. Hence the flesh is said to thirst for God in many ways, even in more ways than the soul: because the soul draws more causes and incentives for thirsting for God from the body than from itself. For it has as many causes for longing for God as the hindrances by which it finds itself kept far from him and drawn back. Therefore the Apostle cries out to the Romans: [[Rom 7:24|Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?|Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus?]] In a like sense it is said that [[Gal 5:17|the flesh lusteth against|caro concupiscere adversus]] the soul [the Apostle has "against the spirit"], not that the flesh lusts of itself, but because it is the soul's occasion of lusting against itself. For the soul, by its sensitive appetite, lusts against itself as regards its intellectual appetite. Secondly, it is understood thus: that the flesh, that is, the sensitive appetite, thirsts for God not directly and immediately, as though God were the object of its desire, but because what it desires it desires according to God, namely according to the command of reason and the direction of the moral virtues; and it thirsts for God in more ways than the higher appetite, because man has more pains, faults and miseries on the side of the sensitive appetite than of the intellectual, especially since the passions of the soul, which are for us the origin of sinning, are founded in the sensitive appetite.

paras.t: In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa, id est in corpore isto corruptibili, ab originali justitia derelicto, ad errores proclivi, et secundum se omni gratia destitutus. Caro enim non prodest quidquam. Et Apostolus : Scio, inquit, quia non habitat in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum. In hac igitur terra velut in carcere habitans ego, sic in sancto apparui tibi, id est, in sancto affectu, desiderioque cœlesti repræsentavi me ipsum tuo conspectu, effundendo cor meum coram te, atque perpendens me semper a te inspici. Itaque, non obstante corporis mole, ad cœlestia adspiramus, et mundo corde nos ipsos Deo exhibere conemur, quatenus illud beati Apostoli vere dicamus : In carne ambulantes, non secundum carnem militamus.
paras.en: [[62:3|In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water|In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa]], that is, in this corruptible body, forsaken by original justice, prone to errors, and of itself bereft of all grace. For [[John 6:64|the flesh profiteth nothing|Caro enim non prodest quidquam]]. And the Apostle: [[Rom 7:18|I know|Scio]], he says, [[Rom 7:18|that there dwelleth not in me, that is to say, in my flesh, that which is good|quia non habitat in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum]]. Dwelling, then, in this land as in a prison, [[62:3|so in the sanctuary have I come before thee|sic in sancto apparui tibi]], that is, in holy affection and heavenly desire I have presented myself in thy sight, pouring out my heart before thee and considering that I am always seen by thee [*in sancto*, "in the sanctuary", can also mean "in what is holy"; Denis takes it as "in holy affection"]. Therefore, notwithstanding the weight of the body, let us aspire to heavenly things and strive to present ourselves to God with a clean heart, so that we may truly say that word of the blessed Apostle: [[2 Cor 10:3|though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh|In carne ambulantes, non secundum carnem militamus]].

paras.t: Vel sic : In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa, id est in hoc sæculo nequam, quod est virtutibus destitutum, et lata via ducens ad mortem, inaquosum quoque, id est infructuosum et aridum. De hac terra Christus in Evangelio dicit : Quum immundus spiritus exierit ab homine, ambulat per loca arida et inaquosa. Sic in sancto apparui tibi, quia in mundo isto non sæculariter vixi, nec peccatorum vestigia sum sectatus, sed tibi in sanctitate et justitia ministravi.
paras.en: Or thus: [[62:3|In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water|In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa]], that is, in this wicked world, which is bare of virtues and is the broad way leading to death[[Matt 7:13||]], and waterless too, that is, unfruitful and dry. Of this land Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 11:24|When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through places without water|Quum immundus spiritus exierit ab homine, ambulat per loca arida et inaquosa]] [Denis's "dry and waterless places" joins Matt 12:43, "dry places", to Luke 11:24]. [[62:3|So in the sanctuary have I come before thee|Sic in sancto apparui tibi]], because in this world I have not lived in a worldly way, nor followed in the footsteps of sinners, but have served thee in holiness and justice.

paras.t: Et hoc, ut viderem in patria clare per speciem, virtutem tuam, id est omnipotentiam tuam, qua omnia in cœlo et in terra disponis, omnesque Beatos potentissime in bono confirmas ; et gloriam tuam, id est beatitudinem tuam, quatenus intrem in gaudium Domini mei, et omnem excellentiam ejus in cœlo conspiciam.
paras.en: And this [[62:3|to see|ut viderem]], in the heavenly homeland, clearly and by sight [*per speciem*: by open vision, as opposed to by faith], [[62:3|thy power|virtutem tuam]], that is, thy omnipotence, by which thou orderest all things in heaven and on earth, and most mightily confirmest all the Blessed in good; [[62:3|and thy glory|et gloriam tuam]], that is, thy beatitude, so that I may enter into the joy of my Lord[[Matt 25:23||]], and behold all his excellence in heaven.

paras.t: Vel sic : Ut viderem, o Pater æterne, virtutem tuam et gloriam tuam, id est Christum Filium tuum, qui est virtus et sapientia Patris, secundum Apostolum. Si enim, teste Scriptura, filius sapiens est gloria patris ; quanto magis Christus Dei Unigenitus, qui est ipsa æterna, immensa et increata sapientia Patris, dici potest gloria ejus ? Utroque itaque modo per virtutem et gloriam Dei, intelligitur ipsemet Deus sublimis et gloriosus. Nam propter Dei visionem per speciem, tanquam ob præmium ultimatum, finale et consummatum, omnia quæ agimus operari debemus. Propter quod ait Salvator : Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum. Et Moyses ait ad Dominum : Ostende mihi gloriam tuam.
paras.en: Or thus: [[62:3|To see|Ut viderem]], O eternal Father, [[62:3|thy power and thy glory|virtutem tuam et gloriam tuam]], that is, Christ thy Son, who is the power and wisdom of the Father, according to the Apostle[[1 Cor 1:24||]]. For if, as Scripture witnesses, a wise son is the glory of his father[[Prov 10:1||]] [the margin gives Prov. x, 1, which reads "A wise son maketh the father glad"; Denis gives the sense freely], how much more can Christ, the only-begotten of God, who is the very eternal, immeasurable and uncreated wisdom of the Father, be called his glory? In both ways, then, by the power and glory of God is understood God himself, sublime and glorious. For it is for the sake of the vision of God by sight, as for the ultimate, final and consummate reward, that we ought to do all that we do. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent|Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum]]. And Moyses says to the Lord: [[Ex 33:18|Shew me thy glory|Ostende mihi gloriam tuam]].

paras.t: Hæc autem ideo oro, Quoniam melior est misericordia tua, id est gratiæ tuæ præsentia seu pia conversatio, qua hominem in esse spirituali et gratioso conservas, super vitas, id est super omne genus vitæ naturalis. Præstantiora quippe sunt munera gratiæ donis naturæ ; meliusque exsistit, nec esse nec vivere vita naturali peccatis obnoxia, quam sine caritate et gratia esse, quemadmodum Veritas de Juda protestatur : Bonum ei erat, si natus non fuisset homo ille. Non ergo optemus vivere, nisi ut bene vivamus ; magisque optemus omnino non esse, quam miserationibus Dei carere. Labia mea laudabunt te, propter beneficia mihi ac ceteris a te clementer impensa.
paras.en: And I pray for these things [[62:4|For thy mercy is better|Quoniam melior est misericordia tua]], that is, the presence of thy grace, or thy loving converse with us, by which thou keepest man in his spiritual and grace-filled being, [[62:4|than lives|super vitas]], that is, than every kind of natural life. For the gifts of grace surpass the endowments of nature; and it is better neither to be nor to live with a natural life liable to sins than to be without charity and grace, as the Truth declares of Judas: [[Matt 26:24|It were better for him, if that man had not been born|Bonum ei erat, si natus non fuisset homo ille]]. Let us not wish to live, then, except that we may live well; and let us rather wish not to be at all than to be without the mercies of God. [[62:4|thee my lips will praise|Labia mea laudabunt te]], for the benefits mercifully bestowed by thee on me and on others.

paras.t: Sic benedicam te in vita mea, id est, toto tempore quo subsisto et in vita permaneo, te benedicam, id est, bona de te dicam, bonitatem tuam glorificando, superexaltando, et ei gratias referendo : sicut superius dictum est, Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore. Et Tobias dicit : Omni tempore benedic Deo, et pete ab eo ut vias tuas dirigat.
paras.en: [[62:5|Thus will I bless thee all my life long|Sic benedicam te in vita mea]], that is, all the time that I exist and remain in life I will bless thee, that is, I will speak good things of thee [*benedicere*, "to bless", is literally "to speak well"], glorifying thy goodness, exalting it above all, and giving it thanks: as was said above: [[Ps 33:2|I will bless the Lord at all times|Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore]]. And Tobias says: [[Tob 4:20|Bless God at all times: and desire of him to direct thy ways|Omni tempore benedic Deo, et pete ab eo ut vias tuas dirigat]].

paras.t: Vel, Benedicam te in vita mea, id est, taliter vivam, quod conversatio mea erit quædam nominis tui benedictio, quia ad nominis tui honorem, laudem et gloriam, totam vitam meam ordinabo. Etenim non minus benedicitur Deus justa vita, quam voce sonora.
paras.en: Or, [[62:5|will I bless thee all my life long|Benedicam te in vita mea]], that is, I will so live that my way of life will be a kind of blessing of thy name, because I will order my whole life to the honour, praise and glory of thy name. For God is blessed no less by a just life than by a sounding voice.

paras.t: Et in nomine tuo, id est in te atque ad tuum honorem, levabo manus meas corporales ad cœlum, ut sic spiritus promptius feratur ad Creatorem. Cæremoniæ namque corporales disponunt non modicum ad devotionem internam. Vel, Levabo manus meas, id est, desideria mea ac opera erigam atque firmabo in te, sicut in ultimo fine : sicut admonet Jeremias, Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cœlos. Unde Apostolus : Volo, inquit, viros orare in omni loco, levantes puras manus sine ira et disceptatione.
paras.en: [[62:5|And in thy name|Et in nomine tuo]], that is, in thee and for thy honour, [[62:5|I will lift up my hands|levabo manus meas]], my bodily hands, to heaven, so that the spirit may thus be borne more readily to the Creator. For bodily ceremonies dispose not a little to inward devotion. Or, [[62:5|I will lift up my hands|Levabo manus meas]], that is, I will raise up my desires and works and fix them firmly in thee, as in my last end: as Jeremias admonishes: [[Lam 3:41|Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord in the heavens|Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cœlos]]. Hence the Apostle: [[1 Tim 2:8|I will|Volo]], he says, [[1 Tim 2:8|that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands, without anger and contention|viros orare in omni loco, levantes puras manus sine ira et disceptatione]].

paras.t: Sicut adipe et pinguedine repletur, impinguatur, et alitur caro, sic repleatur anima mea consolatione interna, caritate ardenti, et gratia spiritualiter incrassante : secundum quod ait Apostolus, Æmulamini charismata meliora. Et tunc labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum : id est, exsultantibus labiis te os meum laudabit, ita quod in laude tua gaudebo, atque ex interiori lætitia ad te laudandum movebor, et signa mentalis jucunditatis foris ostendam. Amanti namque delectabile est occupari in laude dilecti ; et quanto in gratia Dei altius crescimus, tanto jucundius eum laudamus : estque signum magni amoris, in Dei laudibus exsultare.
paras.en: [[62:6|as with marrow and fatness|Sicut adipe et pinguedine]] the flesh is filled, fattened and nourished, so [[62:6|let my soul be filled|repleatur anima mea]] with inward consolation, burning charity, and grace that makes it spiritually rich [*incrassante*, literally "fattening"]: as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 12:31|be zealous for the better gifts|Æmulamini charismata meliora]]. [[62:6|And my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips|Et tunc labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum]] [Denis's text adds "then"]: that is, my mouth shall praise thee with exulting lips, so that I shall rejoice in thy praise, and be moved by inward gladness to praise thee, and show outwardly the signs of the mind's joy. For to the lover it is delightful to be busied with the praise of the beloved; and the higher we grow in the grace of God, the more joyfully we praise him: and it is a sign of great love to exult in the praises of God.

paras.t: Si, id est quia, memor fui tui, meditando, orando, plangendo, super stratum meum, id est in lecto meo tempore noctis, in matutinis meditabor in te, id est, in hora atque officio matutinali te contemplabor, et quæ tibi sunt placita cogitabo. Hoc enim consequens est, ut qui in lecto suo Dei non obliviscitur, extra lectum tempore divini obsequii ejus reminiscatur : et omnino debemus esse memores Dei in strato nostro, sic collocantes nos in lecto, quasi in tumulo.
paras.en: [[62:7|If|Si]], that is, because, [[62:7|I have remembered thee|memor fui tui]], meditating, praying, lamenting, [[62:7|upon my bed|super stratum meum]], that is, in my bed in the night-time, [[62:7|I will meditate on thee in the morning|in matutinis meditabor in te]] [*in matutinis*: "in the morning", but also "at Matins", the night office], that is, at the hour and office of Matins I will contemplate thee, and think on the things that are pleasing to thee. For it follows that he who does not forget God in his bed will remember him outside his bed, at the time of divine service: and we ought by all means to be mindful of God on our bed, laying ourselves down in bed as though in the tomb.

paras.t: Vel sic : Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, id est in quiete ac prosperitate, in matutinis, id est gratiæ tuæ radio mihi illucente, meditabor in te, recolendo bonitatem tuam atque beneficia infinita.
paras.en: Or thus: [[62:7|If I have remembered thee upon my bed|Si memor fui tui super stratum meum]], that is, in quiet and prosperity, [[62:7|in the morning|in matutinis]], that is, when the ray of thy grace shines upon me, [[62:7|I will meditate on thee|meditabor in te]], calling to mind thy goodness and thy infinite benefits.

paras.t: Quia fuisti adjutor meus, naturæ meæ infirmitatem confortando per gratiam tuam : nam gratia tua sum id quod sum. Et in velamento alarum tuarum exsultabo : id est, non in propriis viribus ero securus, nec in me ipso lætabor ; sed sub defensione tuæ potentiæ ac misericordiæ lætus quiescam, et quiete ac tute gaudebo. Nam, ut scriptum est, Deo concedente pacem, quis est qui condemnet? Hinc enim Sponsa ait : Sub umbra illius quem desiderabam, sedi, et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo.
paras.en: [[62:8|Because thou hast been my helper|Quia fuisti adjutor meus]], strengthening the weakness of my nature by thy grace: for by thy grace I am what I am. [[62:8|And I will rejoice under the cover of thy wings|Et in velamento alarum tuarum exsultabo]]: that is, I will not be secure in my own strength, nor rejoice in myself, but I will rest gladly under the defence of thy power and mercy, and rejoice in quiet and safety. For, as it is written, [[Job 34:29|when he granteth peace, who is there that can condemn|Deo concedente pacem, quis est qui condemnet]]? Hence the Bride says: [[Cant 2:3|I sat down under his shadow, whom I desired: and his fruit was sweet to my palate|Sub umbra illius quem desiderabam, sedi, et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo]].

paras.t: Adhæsit, o Domine, anima mea post te, id est, per caritatem tibi inhæsit, ad te pervenire conatur, in anteriora extendens se ipsam, Christi vestigia sequens, et clamans cum Sponsa : Trahe me post te, curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum. In hac adhæsione pax nostra et salus tota consistit. Propter quod Jeremias ait ad Dominum : Ego non sum turbatus, te pastorem sequens. Hanc quoque adhæsionem facit ac roborat ardens dilectio Creatoris. Me pœnitentem, orantem, confitentem, teque laudantem, suscepit, et exaudivit, dextera tua, id est favor gratiæ tuæ, seu pia tua præsentia, quæ me pie prævenit, clementer conservat, et ad consummationem benigne perducit.
paras.en: [[62:9|My soul hath stuck close to thee|Adhæsit, o Domine, anima mea post te]] [Denis's text adds "O Lord"], that is, it has clung to thee by charity and strives to come to thee, stretching itself forth to the things that are before[[Phil 3:13||]], following the footsteps of Christ, and crying out with the Bride: [[Cant 1:3|Draw me: we will run after thee to the odour of thy ointments|Trahe me post te, curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum]]. In this cleaving all our peace and salvation consist. Wherefore Jeremias says to the Lord: [[Jer 17:16|I am not troubled, following thee for my pastor|Ego non sum turbatus, te pastorem sequens]]. This cleaving, too, is brought about and strengthened by a burning love of the Creator. When I repented, prayed, confessed and praised thee, it [[62:9|hath received me|suscepit]], and hath heard me [Denis's text adds "and hath heard"], [[62:9|thy right hand|dextera tua]], that is, the favour of thy grace, or thy loving presence, which lovingly goes before me, mercifully keeps me, and kindly brings me to fulfilment.

paras.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsierunt animam meam : id est, quoniam dextera Dei me suscepit ac sustinet, propterea hostes mei visibiles et invisibiles frustra conati sunt vitam meam spiritualem exstinguere, animam meam seducere, aut alio modo nocere. Introibunt, propter peccata sua, in inferiora terræ, id est in lacum inferni, de quo alibi scriptum est : Verumtamen ad infernum detraheris, in profundum laci.
paras.en: [[62:10|But they have sought my soul in vain|Ipsi vero in vanum quæsierunt animam meam]]: that is, because the right hand of God has received me and upholds me, therefore my enemies, visible and invisible, have tried in vain to extinguish my spiritual life, to lead my soul astray, or to harm it in some other way. [[62:10|They shall go|Introibunt]], for their sins, [[62:10|into the lower parts of the earth|in inferiora terræ]], that is, into the pit of hell, of which it is written elsewhere: [[Is 14:15|But yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, into the depth of the pit.|Verumtamen ad infernum detraheris, in profundum laci.]]

paras.t: Tradentur in manus gladii, partes vulpium erunt, id est, hominum fraudulentorum et diabolorum fallacium participes erunt in pœnis.
paras.en: [[62:11|They shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes|Tradentur in manus gladii, partes vulpium erunt]], that is, they shall be partakers in punishment with deceitful men and lying devils.

paras.t: Rex vero, id est se ipsum rationabiliter regens, et ad regale Christi sacerdotium pertinens, lætabitur in Deo, in quo solo est vera ac pura lætitia. Propter quod in libro Job legitur : Si reversus fueris, tunc super Omnipotentem deliciis afflues, et elevabis ad Deum faciem tuam. Hanc autem in Deo lætitiam habere non potest hypocrita et dolosus, quemadmodum Job ait : Numquid Deus audiet vocem hypocritæ? aut poterit in Omnipotente delectari?
paras.en: [[62:12|But the king|Rex vero]], that is, one who rules himself according to reason and belongs to the royal priesthood of Christ, [[62:12|shall rejoice in God|lætabitur in Deo]], in whom alone is true and pure gladness. Wherefore we read in the book of Job: [[Job 22:23|If thou wilt return|Si reversus fueris]], [[Job 22:26|Then shalt thou abound in delights in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face to God|tunc super Omnipotentem deliciis afflues, et elevabis ad Deum faciem tuam]]. But this gladness in God the hypocrite and the deceitful cannot have, as Job says: [[Job 27:9|Will God hear|Numquid Deus audiet]] the voice of the hypocrite [Job has "his cry"; the hypocrite is named in the verse before]? [[Job 27:10|Or can he delight himself in the Almighty|aut poterit in Omnipotente delectari]]?

paras.t: Laudabuntur omnes, id est, a Deo et Sanctis omnibus approbabuntur, qui jurant in eo cum debitis circumstantiis operis virtuosi. Jurare namque, si debite modificetur, ordinateque fiat, est actus virtutis, scilicet latriæ. Scriptum est enim : Reddes Domino juramenta tua ; et rursus, Per nomen illius jurabis. Quod vero ait Salvator, Ego vero dico vobis non jurare omnino, non est dictum prohibitive simpliciter, sed ut sine necessitate non assuescamus jurare.
paras.en: [[62:12|all they shall be praised|Laudabuntur omnes]], that is, shall be approved by God and all the Saints, [[62:12|that swear by him|qui jurant in eo]] with the due circumstances of a virtuous act. For to swear, if it is duly measured and done in an orderly way, is an act of virtue, namely of latria [the worship due to God alone]. For it is written: [[Matt 5:33|thou shalt perform thy oaths to the Lord|Reddes Domino juramenta tua]]; and again: [[Deut 6:13|thou shalt swear by his name|Per nomen illius jurabis]]. But what the Saviour says, [[Matt 5:34|But I say to you not to swear at all|Ego vero dico vobis non jurare omnino]], is not said as a simple prohibition, but so that we may not grow used to swearing without necessity.

paras.t: Vel, Laudabuntur omnes qui jurant in eo, id est, qui fortiter bonum proponunt seu spondent, illudque fideliter prosequuntur ac implent. Quia obstructum est os loquentium iniqua. Jam enim obstructum est per prohibitionem divinam ; in die quoque judicii obstruetur per condemnationem æternam. Nihilo minus reprobi mala loquentur in æternum : nam et in inferno Deum jugiter blasphemabunt, eo quod tantam potentiam habeat, qua eos sic cruciat, eisque prævaleat.
paras.en: Or, [[62:12|all they shall be praised that swear by him|Laudabuntur omnes qui jurant in eo]], that is, those who firmly purpose or promise what is good, and faithfully pursue and fulfil it. [[62:12|because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things|Quia obstructum est os loquentium iniqua]]. For it is already stopped by the divine prohibition; and on the day of judgement it will be stopped by eternal condemnation. None the less the reprobate will speak evil things for ever: for in hell too they will blaspheme God without ceasing, because he has such power, by which he so torments them and prevails over them.

62.title: DECLARATIO ALLEGORICA EJUSDEM PSALMI SEXAGESIMI SECUNDI DE CHRISTO.
62.title_en: Allegorical declaration of the same sixty-second psalm, concerning Christ.

paras.t: Quod autem beatus David a facie Saul fugiens, in deserto moratus est, hoc præfiguravit quod evangelista Joannes de Christo commemorat : Conspiraverunt, inquit, Judæi, ut eum occiderent. Jesus ergo jam non in palam ambulabat, sed erat in desertis locis cum discipulis suis, juxta civitatem quæ dicitur Ephrem.
paras.en: Now that blessed David, fleeing from the face of Saul, abode in the desert[[1 Kings 23:14||]], prefigured what the evangelist John records of Christ: The Jews, he says, conspired to kill him[[John 11:53||]]. [[John 11:54|Wherefore Jesus walked no more openly|Jesus ergo jam non in palam ambulabat]], but was in desert places with his disciples, near [[John 11:54|a city that is called Ephrem|civitatem quæ dicitur Ephrem]].

paras.t: Christus igitur ut homo in hoc degens exsilio, ait ad Deum Patrem seu totam beatissimam Trinitatem, unum verum ac summum Deum : Deus, Deus meus, qui es specialissimo modo Deus meus, secundum quod homo sum, quia summe honoratus atque dilectus a me, ad te de luce vigilo, id est, per claritatem lucis divinæ, animæ meæ infusæ, tibi semper intendo. Erat enim in anima Christi a suæ creationis principio non solum lux gratiæ, sed etiam excellentissimum lumen gloriæ, per quod incessabiliter vigilavit ad Deum, eum amando ac intuendo. Non enim somnus, cibus, potus, prædicatio, aut alia quælibet occupatio, animam Christi ab actuali Dei contemplatione unquam impedivit ; sed ipse sine intervallo jugiter Deo intendit.
paras.en: Christ, then, dwelling as man in this exile, says to God the Father, or to the whole most blessed Trinity, the one true and supreme God: [[62:2|O God, my God|Deus, Deus meus]], who art in a most special manner my God, according as I am man, because thou art supremely honoured and loved by me, [[62:2|to thee do I watch at break of day|ad te de luce vigilo]], that is, through the brightness of the divine light poured into my soul, I am ever intent upon thee [*de luce*, "at break of day", is literally "from the light"]. For in the soul of Christ, from the beginning of its creation, there was not only the light of grace but also the most excellent light of glory, through which he watched unceasingly towards God, loving and beholding him. For neither sleep, food, drink, preaching, nor any other occupation ever hindered the soul of Christ from the actual contemplation of God; but he was continually intent upon God without interval.

paras.t: Sitivit in te anima mea : quantum ad id quod erat viatrix atque passibilis. Anima namque Christi, quantum ad vires superiores ad Deum relatas, semper erat in beatifica Dei fruitione : nec sic proprie sitivit in Deum, quum sitis sit desiderium boni absentis ; sed amabat et amplectebatur ipsum Deum. Quantum vero ad vires inferiores, erat anima Christi viatrix et passibilis : sicque sitivit in Deum, desiderando præmium accidentale, et liberationem ab omni passibilitate. Unde et ipse discipulis dixit : Si diligeretis me, gauderetis utique, quia vado ad Patrem.
paras.en: [[62:2|For thee my soul hath thirsted|Sitivit in te anima mea]]: as regards that in which it was a wayfarer and capable of suffering [*viatrix*, "wayfarer": still on the way, not yet in the homeland; *passibilis*: able to suffer]. For the soul of Christ, as regards its higher powers, directed to God, was always in the beatific enjoyment of God: and so it did not properly thirst for God, since thirst is the desire of an absent good; but it loved and embraced God himself. But as regards its lower powers, the soul of Christ was a wayfarer and capable of suffering: and so it thirsted for God, desiring the accidental reward [the joys added to the essential reward, which is the vision of God] and deliverance from all passibility. Hence he himself said to the disciples: [[John 14:28|If you loved me you would indeed be glad, because I go to the Father|Si diligeretis me, gauderetis utique, quia vado ad Patrem]].

paras.t: Quam multipliciter tibi caro mea ! Corpus etenim Christi multo pluribus passionibus subjacebat quam anima, quia mortale fuit, non glorificatum : idcirco multipliciter sitivit in Deum, desiderando resuscitationem, ascensionem et glorificationem : pro quibus etiam frequenter oravit, dicendo, Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora ; et, Pater, clarifica Filium tuum. Nonne utique anima corpusque Christi sitivit in Deum, dum dixit : O generatio incredula, quamdiu apud vos ero ? quamdiu vos patiar ? et alibi, Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me ? Quomodo autem corpori competit sitire in Deum, dictum est in præcedenti expositione.
paras.en: [[62:2|for thee my flesh, O how many ways|Quam multipliciter tibi caro mea]]! For the body of Christ was subject to far more sufferings than the soul, because it was mortal, not glorified: therefore it thirsted for God in many ways, desiring resurrection, ascension and glorification; for which he also often prayed, saying: [[John 12:27|Father, save me from this hour|Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora]]; and: Father, [[John 17:1|Glorify thy Son|clarifica Filium tuum]]. Did not the soul and body of Christ indeed thirst for God when he said: [[Mark 9:18|O incredulous generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you?|O generatio incredula, quamdiu apud vos ero ? quamdiu vos patiar ?]] and elsewhere: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me]]? How it befits the body to thirst for God was said in the preceding exposition.

paras.t: In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa, id est in mundo isto vitioso, errabundo, et infecundo, sic in sancto desiderio apparui tibi. Nam Christus inter homines vivens, vitia hominum ignoravit ; sed divino adspectui semper se ipsum repræsentavit in sancto desiderio, quo Dei Patris honorem et mundi salutem ardentissime concupivit.
paras.en: [[62:3|In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water|In terra deserta et invia et inaquosa]], that is, in this world, vicious, wandering and barren, [[62:3|so in the sanctuary|sic in sancto]], that is, in holy desire, [[62:3|have I come before thee|apparui tibi]] [*in sancto*, "in the sanctuary", can also mean "in what is holy"; Denis reads it with *desiderio*, "in holy desire"]. For Christ, living among men, had no part in the vices of men; but he always presented himself to the divine gaze in holy desire, with which he most ardently longed for the honour of God the Father and the salvation of the world.

paras.t: Ut viderem virtutem tuam, id est, quatenus experimentaliter intuerer potentiam tuam, qua per me passionemque meam, principem hujus mundi superare et mortem destruere decrevisti. Nam Christus divina virtute diabolum vicit, et mundum redemit. Et gloriam tuam, id est, ut viderem excellentiam gratiæ in præsenti, et gloriæ in futuro, quam merito meæ passionis dare disposuisti electis. Hanc gloriam Dei in electis Christus maxime desideravit, quoniam propter eam mori dignatus est.
paras.en: [[62:3|to see thy power|Ut viderem virtutem tuam]], that is, that I might behold by experience thy might, by which thou hast decreed, through me and my passion, to overcome the prince of this world and to destroy death. For Christ by divine power conquered the devil and redeemed the world. [[62:3|and thy glory|Et gloriam tuam]], that is, that I might see the excellence of grace in the present and of glory in the future, which thou hast appointed to give to the elect by the merit of my passion. This glory of God in the elect Christ desired most of all, since for its sake he deigned to die.

paras.t: Vel sic : Ut viderem, non solum spirituali ac interiori, sed etiam oculo corporali corporis glorificati, virtutem tuam et gloriam tuam, post ascensionem in cœlo : intelligendo per virtutem et gloriam effectus divinæ potentiæ, in quibus virtus et gloria Dei relucet. In talium enim visione corporali, præmium accidentale partim consistit. Unde post diem judicii corpora cœlestia et elementa splendidiora erunt quam modo, ut in eorum corporali visione Beati delectentur, divinamque in eis virtutem et gloriam admirentur. Sæpe equidem in divinis Scripturis per virtutem et gloriam Dei, intelliguntur effectus divinæ potestatis, sicut Christus ait ad Martham : Si credideris, videbis gloriam Dei, id est gloriosum miraculum resuscitationis fratris tui. Et in libro Paralipomenon : O Juda et Jerusalem, nolite timere ; cras videbitis majestatem Dei in vobis, id est, opus magnæ potestatis Dei cernetis.
paras.en: Or thus: [[62:3|To see|Ut viderem]], not only with the spiritual and inward eye but also with the bodily eye of the glorified body, [[62:3|thy power and thy glory|virtutem tuam et gloriam tuam]], after the ascension, in heaven: understanding by power and glory the effects of the divine might, in which the power and glory of God shine forth. For the accidental reward consists in part in the bodily sight of such things. Hence after the day of judgement the heavenly bodies and the elements will be more splendid than now, so that the Blessed may delight in seeing them with the body, and admire the divine power and glory in them. Indeed, in the divine Scriptures the power and glory of God often mean the effects of the divine might, as Christ says to Martha: [[John 11:40|if thou believe, thou shalt see the glory of God|Si credideris, videbis gloriam Dei]], that is, the glorious miracle of thy brother's raising. And in the book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 20:17|O Juda, and Jerusalem: fear ye not|O Juda et Jerusalem, nolite timere]]; tomorrow you shall see the majesty of God in you [the verse reads "you shall see the help of the Lord over you"; Denis gives it freely], that is, you shall behold a work of the great might of God.

paras.t: Quoniam melior est, o Deus Pater, misericordia tua, id est gratia qua me prævenisti, implesti et perfecisti, super vitas, id est super omnem vitam naturæ, gratiæ et gloriæ omnium electorum. Major enim, dignior ac melior fuit gratia Christo collata, gratiis omnium intellectualium creaturarum, quia non ad mensuram dedit Deus Spiritum Christo homini. Labia mea laudabunt te. Interioribus labiis, id est intellectu, memoria et affectu, anima Christi indesinenter sine omni interruptione Deum laudavit, sicut Beati in patria. Corporalibus quoque labiis eum laudavit, loco et tempore opportunis. Unde, Confiteor (inquit) tibi, Pater, id est, laudo te.
paras.en: [[62:4|For thy mercy is better|Quoniam melior est, o Deus Pater, misericordia tua]], O God the Father, that is, the grace by which thou didst go before me, fill me and perfect me, [[62:4|than lives|super vitas]], that is, than every life of nature, of grace and of glory of all the elect. For the grace bestowed on Christ was greater, worthier and better than the graces of all intellectual creatures, because [[John 3:34|God doth not give the Spirit by measure|non ad mensuram dedit Deus Spiritum]] to Christ as man [the margin gives John iii, 31; the words are John 3:34]. [[62:4|thee my lips will praise|Labia mea laudabunt te]]. With the inward lips, that is, with intellect, memory and affection, the soul of Christ praised God unceasingly, without any interruption, as the Blessed do in the homeland. With his bodily lips too he praised him, at fitting places and times. Hence: [[Luke 10:21|I confess|Confiteor]] (he says) [[Luke 10:21|to thee, O Father|tibi, Pater]], that is, I praise thee.

paras.t: Sic benedicam te in vita mea. Christus utique verbo et opere Deo perfectissime benedixit. Propter quod testatur : Ego honorifico Patrem meum, et non quæro gloriam meam. Et in nomine tuo, id est in tua virtute, vel ad nominis tui honorem, levabo manus meas, id est, omnia desideria mea ac opera ad te Deum altissimum dirigam, et ad cœlestem beatitudinem aliis per me promerendam ordinabo. Vel, Levabo manus meas corporales ad te in oratione, quam fudi passione instante, atque in cruce, dum obtuli me ipsum tibi hostiam beneplacentem.
paras.en: [[62:5|Thus will I bless thee all my life long|Sic benedicam te in vita mea]]. Christ indeed blessed God most perfectly in word and deed. Wherefore he testifies: [[John 8:49|I honour my Father|Ego honorifico Patrem meum]], and [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|non quæro gloriam meam]]. [[62:5|And in thy name|Et in nomine tuo]], that is, in thy power, or for the honour of thy name, [[62:5|I will lift up my hands|levabo manus meas]], that is, I will direct all my desires and works to thee, God most high, and order them to the heavenly beatitude that others are to merit through me. Or, [[62:5|I will lift up my hands|Levabo manus meas]], my bodily hands, to thee in the prayer which I poured out when my passion was at hand, and on the cross, when I offered myself to thee as a well-pleasing sacrifice[[Phil 4:18||]].

paras.t: Sicut adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea gaudio præmii accidentalis, præsertim de salvatione electorum. Christus autem pro augmento caritatis, gratiæ habitualis, seu præmii essentialis, non oravit, quia in talibus anima ejus a principio perfectissima fuit, nec in talibus proficere potuit. Et labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum, id est, hilari ore et corde jucundo gratias tibi agam pro omni beneficio per me electis collato, tuamque, o Deus, bonitatem exsultanter laudabo.
paras.en: [[62:6|Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness|Sicut adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea]] with the joy of the accidental reward, especially over the salvation of the elect. But Christ did not pray for an increase of charity, of habitual grace [the abiding grace that makes the soul holy], or of the essential reward, because in these his soul was most perfect from the beginning, and could not advance in them. [[62:6|and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips|Et labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum]], that is, with cheerful mouth and joyful heart I will give thee thanks for every benefit bestowed on the elect through me, and I will praise thy goodness, O God, with exultation.

paras.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum : id est, quia in cruce in qua infirmatus et mortuus sum, memor fui tui, dicendo, o Pater, Ut quid dereliquisti me? et, Pater, ignosce illis ; et, Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum ; in matutinis, id est tempore resurrectionis, meditabor in te. Tunc enim Christus sine omni tristitia bonitatem et beneficia Patris, propriamque passionem recoluit, dicens discipulis : Nonne hæc oportuit pati Christum? Quia fuisti adjutor meus, cooperando mihi in redemptione generis humani, atque a morte resuscitans me.
paras.en: [[62:7|If I have remembered thee upon my bed|Si memor fui tui super stratum meum]]: that is, because on the cross, on which I was made weak and died, [[62:7|I have remembered thee|memor fui tui]], saying: O Father, [[Matt 27:46|why hast thou forsaken me|Ut quid dereliquisti me]]? and: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them|Pater, ignosce illis]]; and: [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]; [[62:7|in the morning|in matutinis]], that is, at the time of the resurrection, [[62:7|I will meditate on thee|meditabor in te]]. For then Christ, without any sorrow, called to mind the goodness and benefits of the Father, and his own passion, saying to the disciples: [[Luke 24:26|Ought not Christ to have suffered these things|Nonne hæc oportuit pati Christum]]? [[62:8|Because thou hast been my helper|Quia fuisti adjutor meus]], working with me in the redemption of the human race, and raising me from death.

paras.t: Et in velamento alarum tuarum exsultabo, id est, de tua protectione semper lætabor. Hinc enim Christus dixit Judæis : Pater non reliquit me solum.
paras.en: [[62:8|And I will rejoice under the cover of thy wings|Et in velamento alarum tuarum exsultabo]], that is, I will always be glad of thy protection. Hence Christ said to the Jews: The Father [[John 8:29|hath not left me alone|non reliquit me solum]].

paras.t: Adhæsit anima mea post te, quia toto corde, tota fortitudine, totaque mente te semper dilexit, et præceptum caritatis perfecte in hac vita implevit : quod nulli viatori exstat possibile. Me suscepit dextera tua in ascensione, quando me collocasti ad dexteram tuam in cœlis. Vel, Me suscepit dextera tua, id est, naturam meam humanam assumpsit Verbum ac Filius tuus. Quemadmodum enim Spiritus Sanctus vocatur digitus Dei, quoniam Deum atque occulta per illuminationem demonstrat et edocet ; sic Filius appellatur brachium et dextera Patris, quoniam ipse est virtus Dei, et verbo virtutis suæ omnia portat, secundum Apostolum.
paras.en: [[62:9|My soul hath stuck close to thee|Adhæsit anima mea post te]], because it always loved thee with all its heart, with all its strength and with all its mind, and fulfilled the commandment of charity perfectly in this life: which is possible for no other wayfarer. [[62:9|thy right hand hath received me|Me suscepit dextera tua]] at the ascension, when thou didst set me at thy right hand in heaven[[Mark 16:19||]]. Or, [[62:9|thy right hand hath received me|Me suscepit dextera tua]], that is, thy Word and Son assumed my human nature. For as the Holy Ghost is called the finger of God[[Luke 11:20||]], because he shows and teaches God and hidden things through illumination, so the Son is called the arm and right hand of the Father, because he is [[1 Cor 1:24|the power of God|virtus Dei]], and is [[Heb 1:3|upholding all things by the word of his power|verbo virtutis suæ omnia portat]], according to the Apostle.

paras.t: Ipsi vero, puta Judæi increduli, in vanum, id est contra animarum suarum salutem, quæsierunt animam meam corporalem, ut eam exstinguerent. Introibunt, propter peccata in me commissa, in inferiora terræ, id est in profundum inferni ; tradentur in manus gladii, id est in potestatem gladii Romanorum, scilicet Titi ac Vespasiani, qui eos igne et gladio periment ; partes vulpium erunt, id est portio atque possessio dæmonum summe fallacium : quia non credendo in Christum, facti sunt filii dæmonum, atque ad eorum portionem pertinentes. Propter quod Christus ait ad eos : Vos ex patre diabolo estis. Ad litteram quoque Judæi facti sunt partes vulpium, dum eorum cadavera insepulta, tradita sunt vulpibus, feris et avibus devoranda.
paras.en: [[62:10|But they|Ipsi vero]], namely the unbelieving Jews, [[62:10|in vain|in vanum]], that is, against the salvation of their own souls, [[62:10|have sought my soul|quæsierunt animam meam]], my bodily life [*anima*, "soul", also means "life"], to extinguish it. [[62:10|They shall go|Introibunt]], for the sins committed against me, [[62:10|into the lower parts of the earth|in inferiora terræ]], that is, into the depth of hell; [[62:11|They shall be delivered into the hands of the sword|tradentur in manus gladii]], that is, into the power of the sword of the Romans, namely of Titus and Vespasian, who were to destroy them with fire and sword; [[62:11|they shall be the portions of foxes|partes vulpium erunt]], that is, the portion and possession of the most deceitful demons: because by not believing in Christ they became children of the demons and belong to their portion. Wherefore Christ said to them: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]. Literally too the Jews became the portions of foxes, when their unburied corpses were given to foxes, wild beasts and birds to be devoured.

paras.t: Rex vero, scilicet Christus. De quo in Apocalypsi legitur : Vocatur nomen ejus Verbum Dei, et habet in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum : Rex regum et Dominus dominantium. Hic rex lætabitur indesinenter in Deo, sicut de eo superius dictum est : Domine, in virtute tua lætabitur rex, et super salutare tuum exsultabit vehementer. Laudabuntur omnes qui jurant in eo : secundum sensum in præcedenti expositione positum. Secundum quem modum juraverunt, de quibus secundo libro Paralipomenon dicitur : In omni corde suo juraverunt Domino, et in tota voluntate sua quæsierunt eum et invenerunt.
paras.en: [[62:12|But the king|Rex vero]], namely Christ, of whom we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:13|his name is called: THE WORD OF GOD|Vocatur nomen ejus Verbum Dei]], and [[Apoc 19:16|he hath on his garment and on his thigh written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|habet in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum : Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]]. This king [[62:12|shall rejoice|lætabitur]] unceasingly [[62:12|in God|in Deo]], as was said of him above: [[Ps 20:2|In thy strength, O Lord, the king shall joy; and in thy salvation he shall rejoice exceedingly.|Domine, in virtute tua lætabitur rex, et super salutare tuum exsultabit vehementer]] [[62:12|All they shall be praised that swear by him|Laudabuntur omnes qui jurant in eo]]: in the sense given in the preceding exposition. In that way swore those of whom it is said in the second book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 15:15|with all their heart they swore, and with all their will they sought him, and they found him|In omni corde suo juraverunt Domino, et in tota voluntate sua quæsierunt eum et invenerunt]].

paras.t: Quia obstructum est os loquentium iniqua. Jam utique obstructum est os Judæorum Dominum Jesum blasphemantium et interficientium. Dixerunt enim : Ne forte veniant Romani, et tollant nostrum locum et gentem. Volebant quoque nomen atque memoriam Jesu prorsus delere, et ecce Deus comprehendit astutos in astutia eorum, quoniam oppositum contigit. Nam et ipsi locum suum seu terram natalem et populum perdiderunt, nomenque Domini Salvatoris post passionem multo latius clarificatum est quam ante.
paras.en: [[62:12|because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things|Quia obstructum est os loquentium iniqua]]. Already indeed the mouth of the Jews who blasphemed and killed the Lord Jesus has been stopped. For they said: [[John 11:48|the Romans will come, and take away our place and nation|Ne forte veniant Romani, et tollant nostrum locum et gentem]] [Denis's text: "lest perhaps the Romans come and take away our place and nation"]. They wished, too, to blot out entirely the name and memory of Jesus; and behold, God [[Job 5:13|catcheth the wise in their craftiness|comprehendit astutos in astutia eorum]], since the opposite came to pass [Denis's verb, *comprehendit*, is that of 1 Cor 3:19, where St Paul quotes this verse]. For they themselves lost their place, that is, their native land, and their people; and the name of the Lord and Saviour was glorified far more widely after the passion than before.

paras.t: Ecce quam dulcissimus atque affectuosissimus psalmus : cujus virtutem ac suavitatem mens sapit devota et amorosa. Studeamus igitur semper mentaliter vigilare ad Dominum, sicut ad Timotheum ait Apostolus : Tu vero vigila, in omnibus labora, sobrius esto. Et Christus ad discipulos : Vigilate, inquit, et orate, ne intretis in tentationem. Sitiat anima nostra ad Deum : et in carne viventes, non carnaliter conversemur ; sed Domino Deo nostro in sancto desiderio appareamus, summeque solliciti simus ; imo semper stemus in gratia Dei, potiusque optemus non esse, quam sine omni Dei misericordia, sine caritate et gratia esse. Deum in omni tempore, loco et vita laudemus, et puras ad eum manus levemus, atque in divino amore semper proficere satagamus.
paras.en: Behold how most sweet and most full of feeling a psalm this is, whose power and sweetness the devout and loving mind savours. Let us therefore strive always to watch in mind towards the Lord, as the Apostle says to Timothy: [[2 Tim 4:5|But be thou vigilant, labour in all things|Tu vero vigila, in omnibus labora]], [[2 Tim 4:5|Be sober|sobrius esto]]. And Christ to the disciples: [[Matt 26:41|Watch ye|Vigilate]], he says, [[Matt 26:41|and pray that ye enter not into temptation|et orate, ne intretis in tentationem]]. Let our soul thirst for God; and, living in the flesh, let us not conduct ourselves after the flesh[[2 Cor 10:3||]], but appear before the Lord our God in holy desire, and be supremely careful; nay, let us always stand in the grace of God, and rather wish not to be at all than to be without all mercy of God, without charity and grace. Let us praise God at every time and place and in all our life, and lift up pure hands to him, and strive always to advance in divine love.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus, Deus noster, fac nos in oratione de luce Spiritus tui ad te vigilare, ac in te sitire : ut tua præstante gratia, adipe et virtutum pinguedine repleatur anima nostra, quo tibi adhærentem eam in cœlestibus suscipiat dextera tua.
paras.en: Prayer. [[62:2|O God|Deus]], our God, grant that in prayer we may [[62:2|watch|vigilare]] [[62:2|to thee|ad te]] by the light of thy Spirit [*de luce*, the psalm's "at break of day", here read as "by the light"], and thirst [[62:2|for thee|in te]]; that by the gift of thy grace our soul may [[62:6|be filled|repleatur]] [[62:6|with marrow|adipe]] and with the [[62:6|fatness|pinguedine]] of the virtues, so that, [[62:9|stuck close to thee|tibi adhærentem]], it may be received in heaven by [[62:9|thy right hand|dextera tua]].

63.title: EXPOSITIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI SEXAGESIMI TERTII : EXAUDI, DEUS, ORATIONEM MEAM QUUM DEPRECOR.
63.title_en: Exposition concerning Christ of the sixty-third psalm: Hear, O God, my prayer, when I make supplication.

paras.t: Denique titulus psalmi præsentis est : In finem, psalmus David : id est, psalmus iste in ultimum finem nos dirigens, convenit Christo per David præfigurato.
paras.en: Lastly, the title of the present psalm is: [[63:1|Unto the end, a psalm for David|In finem, psalmus David]]: that is, this psalm, which directs us to our last end, befits Christ, who was prefigured by David.

paras.t: Christus igitur ut homo viator passibilis, passioni jam proximus, ait ad Deum Patrem : Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam quum deprecor : vel pro me ipso, sicut dum dixi : Pater, si fieri potest, transfer a me calicem istum; verumtamen non mea voluntas fiat; et iterum, Pater, clarifica me claritate quam habui priusquam mundus esset. Vel, pro corpore meo mystico, sicut dum dixi : Ego pro te rogavi, Petre, ut non deficiat fides tua; et iterum, Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo, quos dedisti mihi. A timore inimici eripe animam meam. Christus qui pro mundo mori advenit, atque in bono confirmatus fuit, non oravit absolute ut non occideretur, aut ne inordinate formidando vitium laberetur. Quid ergo oravit, dicendo, A timore inimici eripe animam meam? nisi ut naturalis timor mortis ab eo recederet, vel ut ad impassibilem vitam suscitaretur, in qua nullus eum terrere posset aut persequi. Tunc enim ab omni timore adversariorum ereptus est, quando ad immortalem statum surrexit.
paras.en: Christ, then, as man, a wayfarer [that is, one still on the way to the heavenly homeland, not yet in its glory] able to suffer and now close to his passion, says to God the Father: [[63:2|Hear O God, my prayer, when I make supplication to thee|Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam quum deprecor]]: either for myself, as when I said: [[Luke 22:42|Father, if thou wilt, remove this chalice from me|Pater, si fieri potest, transfer a me calicem istum]] [Denis's "if it be possible" is the wording of Matt 26:39]; [[Luke 22:42|but yet not my will|verumtamen non mea voluntas]] be done; and again, [[John 17:5|glorify thou me, O Father|Pater, clarifica me]] [[John 17:5|with the glory which I had, before the world was|claritate quam habui priusquam mundus esset]]. Or for my mystical body, as when I said: [[Luke 22:32|I have prayed for thee|Ego pro te rogavi]], Peter, [[Luke 22:32|that thy faith fail not|ut non deficiat fides tua]]; and again, [[John 17:11|Holy Father, keep them in thy name whom thou hast given me|Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo, quos dedisti mihi]]. [[63:2|deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy|A timore inimici eripe animam meam]]. Christ, who came to die for the world and was confirmed in good, did not pray absolutely that he might not be slain, nor that he might not fall into sin through inordinate fear. What then did he pray for in saying, [[63:2|deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy|A timore inimici eripe animam meam]]? Only that the natural fear of death might leave him, or that he might be raised to an impassible life, in which no one could frighten or persecute him. For he was delivered from all fear of his adversaries when he rose to the immortal state.

paras.t: Protexisti me a conventu malignantium, id est a fallaci consilio Judæorum, qui me frequenter tentabant, quatenus me caperent in sermone et accusarent. Ab hoc conventu Deus Christum protexit, quia per sapientiam animæ suæ infusam, fecit eum irreprehensibiliter respondere, ita ut ipsi ejus adversarii dicerent : Nunquam sic locutus est homo, sicut hic loquitur. Prote[…]xisti me etiam, o Domine Pater, a multitudine operantium iniquitatem, id est a Judæis volentibus me a supercilio montis præcipitare, atque in porticu Salomonis lapidare : tunc enim divina virtute evasi, quia invisibilis eis effectus sum. Unde Joannes dicit : Jesus autem abscondit se ; et iterum, Quærebant eum Judæi apprehendere, et exivit de manibus eorum. Potuit namque Christus se ipsum, dum vellet, invisibilem aliis reddere.
paras.en: [[63:3|Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant|Protexisti me a conventu malignantium]], that is, from the deceitful counsel of the Jews, who often tempted me, so as to catch me in my speech and accuse me[[Matt 22:15||]]. From this assembly God protected Christ, for through the wisdom infused into his soul he made him answer beyond reproach, so that his very adversaries said: [[John 7:46|Never did man speak like this man|Nunquam sic locutus est homo, sicut hic loquitur]] [the margin gives Matt. xxii, 15, which fits the snare in speech just before; these words are John 7:46, where Denis has "as this man speaks" for "as this man"]. Thou hast protected me […] also, O Lord Father, [[63:3|from the multitude of the workers of iniquity|a multitudine operantium iniquitatem]], that is, from the Jews who wished to cast me down headlong from the brow of the hill[[Luke 4:29||]], and to stone me in Solomon's porch[[John 10:31||]]: for then I escaped by divine power, since I was made invisible to them[[Luke 4:30||]]. Hence John says: [[John 8:59|But Jesus hid himself|Jesus autem abscondit se]]; and again, [[John 10:39|They sought therefore to take him: and he escaped out of their hands|Quærebant eum Judæi apprehendere, et exivit de manibus eorum]] [the margin prints "Ibid. x, 39" after Luke iv, 30; the words are John 10:39]. For Christ could, when he willed, make himself invisible to others.

paras.t: Quia exacuerunt infideles Judæi ut gladium linguas suas, verba mortifera dicendo adversus me, scilicet : Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum. Intenderunt arcum rem amaram, id est, dolos atque insidias mihi præparaverunt, dicentes : Non in die festo, ne forte tumultus fieret in populo : et item : A discipulo suo venditur et tradatur, a præside condemnetur, ab ejus militibus occidatur; nos totum faciamus, et nihil fecisse videamur. Hæc autem fecerunt, ut sagittent in occultis immaculatum, id est, ut Christum agnum sine macula, lædant ac perimant in occulto, id est aliis ignorantibus eorum versutiam, atque latenter. Sic enim volebant principes sacerdotum cum suis fautoribus Christum occidere, ut nec Pilatus, nec alii scirent eorum falsas adinventiones contra Christum, et ut ipse quoque Christus improvise caperetur ab eis, quia putabant eum nescire eorum consilia.
paras.en: [[63:4|For they have whetted|Quia exacuerunt]], the faithless Jews, [[63:4|their tongues like a sword|ut gladium linguas suas]], speaking deadly words against me, namely: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]. [[63:4|they have bent their bow a bitter thing|Intenderunt arcum rem amaram]], that is, they prepared tricks and snares for me, saying: [[Matt 26:5|Not on the festival day, lest perhaps there should be a tumult among the people|Non in die festo, ne forte tumultus fieret in populo]]; and again: Let him be sold and handed over by his own disciple, condemned by the governor, put to death by his soldiers; let us do the whole of it, and seem to have done nothing. And this they did [[63:5|To shoot in secret the undefiled|ut sagittent in occultis immaculatum]], that is, to wound and destroy Christ, the lamb without spot, in secret, that is, covertly, without others knowing their cunning.
