For the chief priests and their supporters wanted to kill Christ in such a way that neither Pilate nor anyone else should know their false contrivances against Christ, and also that Christ himself should be taken by them unawares, for they thought he did not know their counsels.

paras.t: Subito sagittabunt eum, id est, Christum repente occident. Non enim tenebant eum diu in vinculis, sed captum mox tradiderunt Pilato, et die eodem crucifixerunt. Et non timebant Deum in tanto piaculo. Nam exacerbavit et obstinavit malitia eorum. Propterea sequitur :
paras.en: [[63:6|They will shoot at him on a sudden|Subito sagittabunt eum]], that is, they will suddenly kill Christ. For they did not keep him long in bonds, but having taken him they soon delivered him to Pilate[[Matt 27:2||]], and on the same day crucified him[[Matt 27:31||]] [the margin gives "Ibid. xxvii, 2, 31": Matthew, the only Gospel with that many chapters]. [[63:6|and will not fear|Et non timebant]] God in so great a crime. For their malice had embittered and hardened them. Therefore there follows:

paras.t: Firmaverunt sibi sermonem nequam, id est, pertinaciter quæsierunt a præside, ut Jesum occiderent. Unde Lucas dicit : At illi instabant vocibus magnis postulantes ut crucifigeretur, et invalescebant voces eorum. Quanta enim fecit Pilatus ut eum erueret! Sed illi firmaverunt sibi sermonem nequam, dicentes : Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris. Quo audito, Pilatus timens hominem magis quam Deum, sedit pro tribunali, et Sanctum Sanctorum damnavit ad mortem.
paras.en: [[63:6|they are resolute in wickedness|Firmaverunt sibi sermonem nequam]] [literally, "they have made fast to themselves a wicked word"], that is, they stubbornly demanded of the governor that they might put Jesus to death. Hence Luke says: [[Luke 23:23|But they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And their voices prevailed|At illi instabant vocibus magnis postulantes ut crucifigeretur, et invalescebant voces eorum]]. How much Pilate did to rescue him! But they stood firm, [[63:6|resolute in wickedness|firmaverunt sibi sermonem nequam]], saying: [[John 19:12|If thou release this man, thou art not Caesar's friend|Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris]]. Hearing this, Pilate, fearing man more than God, [[John 19:13|sat down in the judgment seat|sedit pro tribunali]], and condemned the Holy of Holies to death[[John 19:16||]].

paras.t: Narraverunt, id est, inter se tractaverunt, ut absconderent laqueos, id est, quatenus causas ac insidias mortis Christo occulte pararent. Ideo namque mane in die Parasceves duxerunt eum in consilium suum, dicentes, Si tu es Christus, dic nobis : ut responsione sua audita, accusarent eum coram Pilato. Quemadmodum et fecerunt, dicendo : Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit. Dixerunt inter se : Quis videbit eos ? id est, quis cognoscet nostra fraudulenta machinamenta contra hunc Jesum ? Non enim putabant suam malitiam ita omnibus manifestandam ut factum est. Nam, ut in Actibus Apostolorum legitur, volebant se excusare de morte Christi, dicentes Apostolis : Ecce replestis Jerusalem doctrina vestra, et vultis super nos inducere sanguinem hominis hujus.
paras.en: [[63:6|They have talked|Narraverunt]], that is, they discussed among themselves, [[63:6|of hiding snares|ut absconderent laqueos]], that is, how they might secretly prepare grounds and snares of death for Christ. For this reason, early on the day of the Parasceve [that is, the day of preparation, Good Friday], [[Luke 22:66|they brought him into their council saying: If thou be the Christ, tell us|duxerunt eum in consilium suum, dicentes, Si tu es Christus, dic nobis]]: so that, having heard his answer, they might accuse him before Pilate. And so they did, saying: [[John 19:7|We have a law; and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God|Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit]]. [[63:6|they have said|Dixerunt]] among themselves: [[63:6|Who shall see them?|Quis videbit eos ?]] that is, who will discover our deceitful schemes against this Jesus? For they did not think that their malice would be made known to all, as it was. For, as we read in the Acts of the Apostles, they wished to clear themselves of the death of Christ, saying to the Apostles: [[Acts 5:28|behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine: and you have a mind to bring the blood of this man upon us|Ecce replestis Jerusalem doctrina vestra, et vultis super nos inducere sanguinem hominis hujus]].

paras.t: Scrutati sunt iniquitates : id est, cum magna deliberatione atque industria excogitaverunt modum et vias quibus Christum occiderent, quemadmodum apud Joannem dicitur : Collegerunt pontifices et Pharisæi concilium, et dicebant : Quid facimus, quia hic homo multa signa facit? Et Matthæus : Concilium, inquit, fecerunt, ut Jesum dolo tenerent et occiderent. Defecerunt, id est, optato effectu frustrati sunt, scrutantes scrutinia, id est Judæi investigantes consilia, quomodo Christum exstinguerent. Ideo namque eum interfecerunt, ne venientibus Romanis, gentem et locum amitterent ; volebantque Jesum non solum occidere, sed turpissima morte damnare, quatenus nomen atque memoria ejus omnino perirent, quemadmodum apud Jeremiam legitur : Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra. Et ecce oppositum contigit. Nam et ipsi vel occisi sunt a Romanis, vel expulsi et omni gloria legis paternæ privati. Christus vero ex ipsa sua passione fructificavit, quia totius mundi conversionem ad fidem promeruit. Propter quod ipse dicit : Nisi granum frumenti cadens in terram, mortuum fuerit, ipsum solum manet ; si autem mortuum fuerit, multum fructum affert. Se ipsum equidem grano comparavit, quoniam ipse erat granum malitia Judæorum mortificandum, conversioneque gentium multiplicandum.
paras.en: [[63:7|They have searched after iniquities|Scrutati sunt iniquitates]]: that is, with great deliberation and diligence they devised the manner and the ways by which they might kill Christ, as is said in John: [[John 11:47|The chief priests, therefore, and the Pharisees gathered a council and said: What do we, for this man doth many miracles?|Collegerunt pontifices et Pharisæi concilium, et dicebant : Quid facimus, quia hic homo multa signa facit?]] And Matthew: [[Matt 26:4|they consulted together|Concilium]], he says, [[Matt 26:4|that by subtilty they might apprehend Jesus and put him to death|fecerunt, ut Jesum dolo tenerent et occiderent]]. [[63:7|they have failed|Defecerunt]], that is, they were cheated of the result they hoped for, [[63:7|in their search|scrutantes scrutinia]] [literally, "searching their searchings"], that is, the Jews, searching out counsels how they might destroy Christ. For they killed him so that, when the Romans came, they should not lose their nation and their place[[John 11:48||]]; and they wished not only to kill Jesus but to condemn him to a most shameful death[[Wis 2:20||]], so that his name and memory might perish altogether, as we read in Jeremias: Let us [[Jer 11:19|cut him off from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more|Eradamus eum de terra viventium, et nomen ejus non memoretur ultra]]. And behold, the opposite came about. For they themselves were either slain by the Romans, or driven out and robbed of all the glory of the law of their fathers. But Christ bore fruit from his very passion, for he merited the conversion of the whole world to the faith. Hence he himself says: [[John 12:24|unless the grain of wheat falling into the ground die|Nisi granum frumenti cadens in terram, mortuum fuerit]], [[John 12:25|Itself remaineth alone. But if it die it bringeth forth much fruit|ipsum solum manet ; si autem mortuum fuerit, multum fructum affert]]. He compared himself to a grain, since he was the grain that was to be put to death by the malice of the Jews and multiplied by the conversion of the Gentiles.

paras.t: Accedet homo et cor altum, id est, homo Christus mediante corde suo alto seu sapientissimo, ad passionem sponte procedit, sicut superius dixit : Holocaustum et pro peccato non postulasti ; tunc dixi, Ecce venio. Et, teste Joanne, ait : Nemo tollit animam meam a me, sed ego pono eam. Oblatus est enim quia voluit. Per hoc autem quod dicitur, Accedet homo et cor altum, idem significatur. Juxta quem modum alibi scriptum est, Ego autem et anima mea in Deo lætabimur : non quod homo et anima sint diversi lætantes ; sed quoniam anima est quasi proxima causa lætitiæ, quia per eam homo lætatur, sicut per eam vivit et ratiocinatur. Simili modo jam dicitur : Accedet homo et cor altum. Nam cor, id est, intellectus, est homini causa accedendi ad ea quæ Deo sunt placita, quoniam intellectus dirigit actus humanos. Alii habent sic : Accedet homo ad cor altum, id est, Christus per considerationem accedet ad intuendum profundum ac mysticum Dei consilium, pensando videlicet quomodo a summa Trinitate decretum erat ut ipse sua passione mundum salvaret. Ad hoc enim cor Christus accessit, dum deprecans dixit : Verumtamen non mea voluntas fiat, sed tua ; et iterum, Quia sic scriptum est, et sic oportet fieri.
paras.en: [[63:7|Man shall come|Accedet homo]], and a deep heart [Denis reads *et cor altum*, "and a deep heart", where the Clementine text and the Douay-Rheims have "to a deep heart"; he gives that reading further on], that is, the man Christ, by means of his deep or most wise heart, goes of his own will to his passion, as he said above [that is, in Psalm 39]: [[Ps 39:7|Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require|Holocaustum et pro peccato non postulasti]]: [[Ps 39:8|Then said I, Behold I come|tunc dixi, Ecce venio]]. And, as John bears witness, he says: [[John 10:18|No man taketh it away from me: but I lay it down|Nemo tollit animam meam a me, sed ego pono eam]]. For [[Is 53:7|He was offered because it was his own will|Oblatus est enim quia voluit]]. And by the words [[63:7|Man shall come|Accedet homo]], and a deep heart, one and the same is meant. In the same manner it is written elsewhere, [[Tob 13:9|And I and my soul will rejoice in him|Ego autem et anima mea in Deo lætabimur]]: not that the man and his soul are two different beings that rejoice, but because the soul is as it were the proximate cause of joy, since it is through the soul that a man rejoices, as through it he lives and reasons. In like manner it is said here: [[63:7|Man shall come|Accedet homo]], and a deep heart. For the heart, that is, the understanding, is to a man the cause of his coming to those things that are pleasing to God, since the understanding directs human acts. Others read thus: [[63:7|Man shall come to a deep heart|Accedet homo ad cor altum]], that is, Christ by consideration will come to behold the deep and mystical counsel of God, weighing, namely, how it had been decreed by the supreme Trinity that he should save the world by his passion. For Christ came to this heart when he said in prayer: [[Luke 22:42|but yet not my will, but thine be done|Verumtamen non mea voluntas fiat, sed tua]]; and again, [[Luke 24:46|Thus it is written|Quia sic scriptum est]], and [[Matt 26:54|so it must be done|sic oportet fieri]] [the margin gives Luke xxiv, 46, which goes on "and thus it behoved Christ to suffer"; Denis's ending is the wording of Matt 26:54].

paras.t: Et exaltabitur Deus, id est, Christus, qui in passione homo accessit, in resurrectione agnoscetur esse Deus. Deus enim exaltatus est, non quod divinitas perfectior aut sublimior fiat, sed quoniam in mentibus creatis sublimatur, dum quem ignorabant, aut non timebant, agnoscere, adorare et colere inchoant. Sicque in resurrectione exaltatus est Dominus Jesus, quemadmodum inducit Apostolus : Videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum. Vel sic : Exaltabitur Deus, id est, Deus Trinitas per Christi accessum ad cor altum, ab ipso Christo glorificabitur, atque per totum mundum clarificabitur, et in honore habebitur. Ideo namque Christus incarnatus et passus est, quatenus Deus a toto mundo agnosceretur et honoraretur. Propter quod apud Joannem ait : Pater juste, mundus te non cognovit; ego autem te cognovi, et notum feci eis nomen tuum. Et in prima sua Canonica Joannes apertius loquens : Scimus, inquit, quoniam Filius Dei venit, et dedit nobis sensum, ut cognoscamus Deum verum.
paras.en: [[63:8|And God shall be exalted|Et exaltabitur Deus]], that is, Christ, who as man came forward in his passion, will in his resurrection be acknowledged to be God. For God is exalted, not that the Godhead becomes more perfect or more sublime, but because he is raised up in created minds, when those who did not know him, or did not fear him, begin to acknowledge, adore and worship him. And so the Lord Jesus was exalted in his resurrection, as the Apostle brings forward: [[Heb 2:9|we see Jesus|Videmus Jesum]] [[Heb 2:9|for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour|propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum]]. Or thus: [[63:8|God shall be exalted|Exaltabitur Deus]], that is, God the Trinity, through Christ's coming to the deep heart, will be glorified by Christ himself, and made glorious through the whole world, and held in honour. For this is why Christ was made flesh and suffered, that God might be acknowledged and honoured by the whole world. Hence he says in John: [[John 17:25|Just Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee|Pater juste, mundus te non cognovit; ego autem te cognovi]], [[John 17:26|And I have made known thy name to them|et notum feci eis nomen tuum]]. And John, speaking more plainly in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 5:20|we know|Scimus]], he says, [[1 John 5:20|that the Son of God is come. And he hath given us understanding that we may know the true God|quoniam Filius Dei venit, et dedit nobis sensum, ut cognoscamus Deum verum]].

paras.t: Sagittæ parvulorum factæ sunt plagæ eorum, etc. Istud multipliciter intelligi potest. Primo sic : Sagittæ parvulorum, id est insidiæ et persecutiones Judæorum Christo illatæ, factæ sunt plagæ eorum, quia per eas meruerunt a Romanis occidi, æternaliterque damnari : imo et se ipsos spiritualiter occiderunt. Dicuntur autem Judæi parvuli, non propter humilitatem, sed propter invidiam, quæ omnem invidum facit parvulum, juxta illud : Virum stultum interficit iracundia, et parvulum occidit invidia. Invidus enim eo ipso quo alteri invidet, diminutum et bono alterius se indigentem ostendit : quoniam invidia est tristitia de bono alterius, secundum quod æstimatur propriæ excellentiæ diminutivum, ut ait Philosophus. Et infirmatæ sunt contra eos linguæ eorum, id est, sermones, accusationes atque consilia Judæorum, intento effectu privati sunt, sicut jam patuit : et hoc contra eos, id est in malum eorum, quoniam malum quod Christo paraverunt, ipsimet inciderunt, et sermo ille quem dixerant, Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros, fecit eos morti obnoxios.
paras.en: [[63:8|The arrows of children are their wounds|Sagittæ parvulorum factæ sunt plagæ eorum]], etc. This can be understood in many ways. First thus: [[63:8|The arrows of children|Sagittæ parvulorum]] [*parvulorum*, "of little ones", the word Denis goes on to explain], that is, the plots and persecutions of the Jews brought against Christ, [[63:8|are their wounds|factæ sunt plagæ eorum]], because through them they deserved to be slain by the Romans and to be damned eternally; indeed they also slew themselves spiritually. Now the Jews are called little ones, not on account of humility but on account of envy, which makes every envious man little, according to the saying: [[Job 5:2|Anger indeed killeth the foolish, and envy slayeth the little one|Virum stultum interficit iracundia, et parvulum occidit invidia]]. For the envious man, by the very fact that he envies another, shows himself diminished and in want of the other's good: since envy is sorrow at another's good, inasmuch as that good is reckoned to lessen one's own excellence, as the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle] says. [[63:9|And their tongues against them are made weak|Et infirmatæ sunt contra eos linguæ eorum]], that is, the words, accusations and counsels of the Jews were robbed of the effect they intended, as has just been shown: and this [[63:9|against them|contra eos]], that is, to their own harm, since they themselves fell into the evil they had prepared for Christ, and the word they had spoken, [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]], made them liable to death.

paras.t: Secundo sic : Sagittæ parvulorum, id est prædicationes et verba humilium Christi Apostolorum, factæ sunt plagæ eorum, scilicet Judæorum. Nam per prædicationem Apostolorum clarificatus est Christus, et Judæi confusi sunt, victi et exterminati. Et infirmatæ sunt contra eos, videlicet Christi Apostolos, aliosque credentes, linguæ eorum, utpote Judæorum. Non enim resistere poterant verbis atque miraculis discipulorum Domini Salvatoris. Unde scriptum est : Videntes principes sacerdotum Petri et Joannis constantiam, comperto quod homines sine litteris essent et idiotæ, mirabantur; et rursus, Non poterant resistere sapientiæ et Spiritui qui loquebatur per Stephanum.
paras.en: Secondly thus: [[63:8|The arrows of children|Sagittæ parvulorum]], that is, the preaching and the words of Christ's humble Apostles, [[63:8|are their wounds|factæ sunt plagæ eorum]], that is, the wounds of the Jews. For through the preaching of the Apostles Christ was glorified, and the Jews were confounded, overcome and destroyed. [[63:9|are made weak|Et infirmatæ sunt]] [[63:9|against them|contra eos]], namely against the Apostles of Christ and the other believers, [[63:9|their tongues|linguæ eorum]], that is, the tongues of the Jews. For they could not withstand the words and miracles of the disciples of the Lord and Saviour. Hence it is written: The chief priests, [[Acts 4:13|seeing the constancy of Peter and of John, understanding that they were illiterate and ignorant men, they wondered|Videntes principes sacerdotum Petri et Joannis constantiam, comperto quod homines sine litteris essent et idiotæ, mirabantur]]; and again, [[Acts 6:10|they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit that spoke|Non poterant resistere sapientiæ et Spiritui qui loquebatur]] by Stephen.

paras.t: Tertio sic : Sagittæ parvulorum factæ sunt plagæ eorum : id est, plagæ quas Judæi Christo intulerunt, similes erant sagittis puerorum : quoniam sicut puerorum sagittæ inanes sunt, nec nocent, et si aliqualiter lædant, vulnus inflictum cito sanatur; sic plagæ a Judæis Christo illatæ, vanæ fuerunt, nec eum in morte detinere poterant : quin potius Christus tertia die ab omni læsione sanus et immortalis surrexit. Et infirmatæ sunt contra eos linguæ eorum : id est, Judæi proprias assertiones probare non poterant, neque defendere. Quemadmodum legitur, quum custodes sepulcri dixissent quæ viderant, scilicet terræ motum et angelum descendentem, principes Judæorum dederunt eis copiosam pecuniam, quatenus dicerent discipulos Jesu eum fuisse furatos ipsis dormientibus. Hoc autem ficticium facile improbatur. Si enim custodes dormierant, scire non poterant a quibus vel quomodo Christi corpus esset sublatum. Sed nec apparentiam habet quod discipuli, qui omnes a Magistro adhuc vivo aufugerant, inter armatos milites jam defunctum requirerent. Denique impossibile quasi est quod adeo fortiter dormivissent, ut in revolutione lapidis a monumento excitati non exstitissent. Erat namque lapis magnus valde, et diligenter signatus, fortiterque impressus : propter quod sine ingenti strepitu ab homine auferri non potuit.
paras.en: Thirdly thus: [[63:8|The arrows of children are their wounds|Sagittæ parvulorum factæ sunt plagæ eorum]]: that is, the wounds that the Jews dealt Christ were like the arrows of children: for as children's arrows are idle things and do no harm, and if they hurt at all, the wound they make is quickly healed, so the wounds dealt Christ by the Jews were in vain, and could not hold him in death: rather, Christ rose on the third day whole from every hurt, and immortal. [[63:9|And their tongues against them are made weak|Et infirmatæ sunt contra eos linguæ eorum]]: that is, the Jews could neither prove nor defend their own assertions. As we read, when the guards of the sepulchre had told what they had seen[[Matt 28:11||]], namely the earthquake and the angel descending, the chief men of the Jews gave them a great sum of money[[Matt 28:12||]], so that they should say that the disciples of Jesus had stolen him while they slept[[Matt 28:13||]]. But this invention is easily disproved. For if the guards were asleep, they could not know by whom or how the body of Christ had been taken away. Nor is it even plausible that the disciples, who had all fled from their Master while he was still alive[[Matt 26:56||]], should come looking for him among armed soldiers once he was dead. Lastly, it is all but impossible that they should have slept so soundly as not to be woken when the stone was rolled from the tomb. For the stone was very great, carefully sealed and firmly set in place, so that no man could have taken it away without a great noise.

paras.t: Conturbati sunt, id est compuncti, et ad pœnitentiam moti, omnes qui videbant eos, id est qui cognoverunt Judæos in Christi occisione tam dire peccasse, sanguinem innocentem fundendo. Hinc enim de centurione in Evangelio dicitur, quia videns quod sic exspirasset Jesus, timuit valde, et glorificavit Deum, et dixit : Vere Filius Dei erat iste. Et Lucas ait : Omnis turba eorum qui simul aderant ad spectaculum istud, et videbant quæ fiebant, percutientes pectora sua, revertebantur. Post resurrectionem quoque, prædicante Petro, compuncti sunt corde, et conversa sunt ad Christum octo millia Judæorum. Tunc enim impletum est quod Christus ante passionem prædixit : Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum.
paras.en: [[63:9|All that saw them|omnes qui videbant eos]] [[63:9|were troubled|Conturbati sunt]], that is, were pricked at heart and moved to penance: all, that is, who knew that the Jews had sinned so dreadfully in slaying Christ, shedding innocent blood. Hence it is said in the Gospel of the centurion that, seeing that Jesus had so expired, he feared greatly, and glorified God, and said: [[Matt 27:54|Indeed this was the Son of God|Vere Filius Dei erat iste]] [no margin reference here; Denis joins Mark 15:39, Matt 27:54 and Luke 23:47]. And Luke says: [[Luke 23:48|all the multitude of them that were come together to that sight and saw the things that were done returned, striking their breasts|Omnis turba eorum qui simul aderant ad spectaculum istud, et videbant quæ fiebant, percutientes pectora sua, revertebantur]]. After the resurrection, too, when Peter preached, [[Acts 2:37|they had compunction in their heart|compuncti sunt corde]], and eight thousand of the Jews were converted to Christ [that is, the three thousand of Acts 2:41 and the five thousand of Acts 4:4]. For then was fulfilled what Christ foretold before his passion: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]].

paras.t: Et timuit omnis homo : non simpliciter omnis homo, sed ut sit distributio pro generibus singulorum, quia de omni genere hominum quidam ad Christum conversi sunt, et Deum timuerunt. Annuntiaverunt opera Dei, id est, prædicti jam christiani effecti, laudaverunt, et aliis nuntiaverunt opera atque miracula Christi, præsertim Apostoli, de quibus istud specialiter dicitur. De quibus et subjungitur : et facta ejus, scilicet Christi, intellexerunt, per illuminationem Spiritus Sancti, præcipue post diem Pentecostes, quando Christus implevit quod eis repromisit : Ego, inquiens, mittam promissum Patris mei in vos; et iterum, Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem.
paras.en: [[63:10|And every man was afraid|Et timuit omnis homo]]: not every man without qualification, but taking "every" as a distribution by kinds of individuals [that is, "some of every kind", not "each and every one"], since from every kind of men some were converted to Christ and feared God. [[63:10|they declared the works of God|Annuntiaverunt opera Dei]], that is, those just mentioned, now made Christians, praised the works and miracles of Christ and made them known to others, above all the Apostles, of whom this is said in particular. Of them too it is added: [[63:10|and understood|intellexerunt]] [[63:10|his doings|et facta ejus]], that is, Christ's, through the enlightening of the Holy Ghost, especially after the day of Pentecost, when Christ fulfilled what he had promised them: [[Luke 24:49|I|Ego]], he says, [[Luke 24:49|send the promise of my Father upon you|mittam promissum Patris mei in vos]]; and again, [[John 16:13|when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth|Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem]].

paras.t: Lætabitur justus gratia Christi justificatus, et sanguine ejus redemptus, in Domino, non in rebus illicitis et caducis, ut ait Apostolus : Gaudete in Domino semper; iterum dico, gaudete. Et sperabit in eo, id est in misericordia Dei, non in sua justitia, sperans per meritum Christi ad beatam immortalitatem perduci ; et laudabuntur a Christo judice, omnes recti corde, qui Deo in sanctitate et justitia servierunt. Illis enim Christus dicturus est : Venite, benedicti Patris mei, etc.
paras.en: [[63:11|The just shall rejoice|Lætabitur justus]], justified by the grace of Christ and redeemed by his blood, [[63:11|in the Lord|in Domino]], not in things unlawful and passing, as the Apostle says: [[Phil 4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always: again, I say, rejoice|Gaudete in Domino semper; iterum dico, gaudete]]. [[63:11|and shall hope in him|Et sperabit in eo]], that is, in the mercy of God, not in his own justice, hoping through the merit of Christ to be brought to blessed immortality; and [[63:11|shall be praised|et laudabuntur]] by Christ the judge [[63:11|all the upright in heart|omnes recti corde]], who have served God in holiness and justice. For to them Christ will say: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]], etc.

63.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI SEXAGESIMI TERTII.
63.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same sixty-third psalm.

paras.t: Quemadmodum tertium psalmum pœnitentialem quidam doctores catholici, inter quos est Cassiodorus, exponunt ad litteram de sancto Job; sic psalmum præsentem quidam ad litteram exponunt de Daniele, imitantes (ut dicunt) in hoc antiquos Hebræorum doctores. Verumtamen, sicut psalmus ille tertius pœnitentialis convenientius explanatur de quolibet vere pœnitente, sic psalmus præsens congruentius elucidatur de quocumque justo in afflictionibus posito, præcipue in persona martyrum, quorum quilibet dicere potest :
paras.en: As some Catholic doctors, Cassiodorus among them, expound the third penitential psalm[[Ps 37:1||]] literally of holy Job, so some expound the present psalm literally of Daniel, following in this (as they say) the ancient doctors of the Hebrews. Yet, as that third penitential psalm is more fittingly explained of any true penitent, so the present psalm is more aptly expounded of any just man placed in afflictions, and above all in the person of the martyrs, any one of whom can say:

paras.t: Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam quum deprecor, id est, de cordiali affectu te precor. Translatio Romana habet, Quum tribulor. In tribulationibus namque potissimum exaudiri et conservari indigemus. Qui autem sic Deum deprecatur, utique exaudietur, quemadmodum Moyses ait : Quum quæsieris Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum; si tamen toto corde quæsieris eum, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ.
paras.en: [[63:2|Hear O God, my prayer, when I make supplication to thee|Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam quum deprecor]], that is, I beseech thee with heartfelt affection. The Roman version [that is, the Roman Psalter, the older Latin text of the psalms] has: When I am in tribulation. For it is above all in tribulations that we need to be heard and kept safe. And he who so beseeches God will surely be heard, as Moses says: [[Deut 4:29|when thou shalt seek there the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him: yet so, if thou seek him with all thy heart, and all the affliction of thy soul|Quum quæsieris Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum; si tamen toto corde quæsieris eum, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ]] [*tribulatione*, "tribulation", which the Douay-Rheims renders "affliction": hence the link with the Roman reading].

paras.t: A timore inimici eripe animam meam : non ut non tenter a dæmone, nec in mundo persecutionem sustineam, quum per multas tribulationes oporteat nos intrare in regnum cœlorum ; sed ut non formidem inordinato pavore inimicos animæ meæ, magis vero adimpleam quod tu, Domine Jesu, jubes : Ne terreamini ab his qui corpus occidunt ; et : In mundo pressuram habebitis ; sed confidite, ego vici mundum. Hinc apud Isaiam legitur : Nolite timere opprobrium hominum et blasphemias eorum.
paras.en: [[63:2|deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy|A timore inimici eripe animam meam]]: not that I may not be tempted by the devil, nor suffer persecution in the world, since [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God|per multas tribulationes oporteat nos intrare in regnum cœlorum]] [Denis has "of heaven" for "of God"]; but that I may not dread the enemies of my soul with inordinate fear, but rather fulfil what thou, Lord Jesus, commandest: [[Luke 12:4|Be not afraid of them who kill the body|Ne terreamini ab his qui corpus occidunt]]; and: [[John 16:33|In the world you shall have distress. But have confidence. I have overcome the world|In mundo pressuram habebitis ; sed confidite, ego vici mundum]]. Hence we read in Isaias: [[Is 51:7|fear ye not the reproach of men|Nolite timere opprobrium hominum]], and [[Is 51:7|their blasphemies|blasphemias eorum]] [the margin gives Is. ii, 7; the words are Is 51:7].

paras.t: Protexisti me a conventu malignantium, ita quod eorum iniquum consilium mihi non nocuit, neque eorum malignitati cor meum consensit. Hoc modo Deus martyres sanctos protexit, qui coram tyrannis insuperabiliter perstiterunt, atque ab omni fraude eorum erepti sunt. Protexisti me quoque a multitudine operantium iniquitatem, ne cum perversis perverterer, aut eorum multitudine territus superarer. Istud etiam quilibet dicere potest, qui dæmonum tentationibus viriliter restitit, et Deo protegente, eorum laqueos victor evasit : præcipue autem claustrales, qui mundum et omnia quæ in mundo sunt, propter Christum reliquerunt, et in cœnobiis Deo efficaciter militant, hunc versum dicere habent, Deo gratias referendo. Vere enim protexit eos Deus a conventu malignantium, id est a turbis propinquorum et amicorum carnaliter viventium, et claustralem conversationem dissuadentium. Sunt et protecti a multitudine operantium iniquitatem, id est a mundanis hominibus. De quibus in prima sua Canonica ait Joannes : Quidquid est in mundo, concupiscentia carnis est, et concupiscentia oculorum, et superbia vitæ. Sunt autem protecti ab his, non quod penitus sint securi, sed quia jam unum pedem habent in paradiso : quia de eis ait Salvator, Qui reliquerit patrem aut matrem, etc., centuplum accipiet, et vitam æternam possidebit.
paras.en: [[63:3|Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant|Protexisti me a conventu malignantium]], so that their wicked counsel did me no harm, nor did my heart consent to their malice. In this way God protected the holy martyrs, who stood unconquerable before the tyrants and were delivered from all their deceit. Thou hast protected me also [[63:3|from the multitude of the workers of iniquity|a multitudine operantium iniquitatem]], lest with the perverse I should be perverted[[Ps 17:27||]], or be overcome, terrified by their numbers. Anyone too can say this who has manfully resisted the temptations of the demons and, with God's protection, escaped their snares as a victor; but above all those in the cloister, who have left the world and all that is in the world for Christ's sake and fight effectively for God in their monasteries, have reason to say this verse, giving thanks to God. For truly God has protected them [[63:3|from the assembly of the malignant|a conventu malignantium]], that is, from the crowds of kinsfolk and friends who live after the flesh and try to dissuade them from the cloistered life. They are also protected [[63:3|from the multitude of the workers of iniquity|a multitudine operantium iniquitatem]], that is, from worldly men, of whom John says in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 2:16|all that is in the world is the concupiscence of the flesh and the concupiscence of the eyes and the pride of life|Quidquid est in mundo, concupiscentia carnis est, et concupiscentia oculorum, et superbia vitæ]]. Now they are protected from these, not that they are wholly secure, but because they already have one foot in paradise: for of them the Saviour says, [[Matt 19:29|every one that hath left|Qui reliquerit]] [[Matt 19:29|father, or mother|patrem aut matrem]], etc., [[Matt 19:29|shall receive an hundredfold, and shall possess life everlasting|centuplum accipiet, et vitam æternam possidebit]].

paras.t: Quia exacuerunt tyranni et persecutores, justorum detractores Deo odibiles, ut gladium linguas suas, præparantes os suum ad proferendum verba acuta, pungitiva, invidiosa, accusatoria atque letalia. Intenderunt arcum rem amaram, id est, fraudulentas insidias excogitaverunt, ut sagittent in occultis immaculatum, id est, quatenus virum innocentem in lege Domini ambulantem, occulte affligant, lædant, diffament aut perimant.
paras.en: [[63:4|For they have whetted|Quia exacuerunt]], the tyrants and persecutors, [[Rom 1:30|Detractors|detractores]] of the just, [[Rom 1:30|hateful to God|Deo odibiles]], [[63:4|their tongues like a sword|ut gladium linguas suas]], making ready their mouths to utter words that are sharp, stinging, envious, accusing and deadly. [[63:4|they have bent their bow a bitter thing|Intenderunt arcum rem amaram]], that is, they have devised deceitful snares, [[63:5|To shoot in secret the undefiled|ut sagittent in occultis immaculatum]], that is, so as secretly to afflict, hurt, defame or destroy the innocent man who walks in the law of the Lord.

paras.t: Subito sagittabunt eum, id est, nocumentum ei improvise inducent. Unde Christus ait discipulis : Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur, quia non est servus major domino suo. Et non timebunt Deum : quia nonnunquam sic exæcantur invidia atque malitia, ut nec peccare se putent, ut Dominus protestatur : Venit hora, ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo. Firmaverunt sibi sermonem nequam, nolentes remittere minas, nec ad pietatem ac veritatem reduci ; sed quod animo conceperunt, ad effectum perducere satagunt. Narraverunt ut absconderent laqueos : id est, tam homines mali, quam dæmones, inter se tractaverunt quomodo bonis hominibus vias perditionis expandant, et in foveam peccati, mortis aut damni alicujus, eos præcipitent. Incessabiliter enim moliuntur insidias contra devotos. Dixerunt inter se : Quis videbit eos, scilicet laqueos nostros ? Frequenter namque student occulte nocere, maxime dæmones, qui sub specie boni mala proponunt, atque (ut dicit Apostolus) in angelos lucis se transformant.
paras.en: [[63:6|They will shoot at him on a sudden|Subito sagittabunt eum]], that is, they will bring harm upon him unawares. Hence Christ says to the disciples: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]], for [[John 15:20|The servant is not greater than his master|non est servus major domino suo]][[John 13:16||]]. [[63:6|and will not fear|Et non timebunt]] God: for sometimes they are so blinded by envy and malice that they do not even think they are sinning, as the Lord declares: [[John 16:2|the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doth a service to God|Venit hora, ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo]]. [[63:6|they are resolute in wickedness|Firmaverunt sibi sermonem nequam]], unwilling to give up their threats or to be brought back to piety and truth, and striving to carry into effect what they have conceived in their mind. [[63:6|They have talked of hiding snares|Narraverunt ut absconderent laqueos]]: that is, evil men as well as demons have discussed among themselves how they may spread ways of perdition before good men, and cast them headlong into the pit of sin, of death or of some loss. For they ceaselessly contrive snares against the devout. [[63:6|they have said|Dixerunt]] among themselves: [[63:6|Who shall see them?|Quis videbit eos]], that is, our snares? For they often strive to do harm in secret, the demons above all, who put forward evil under the appearance of good, and (as the Apostle says) transform themselves into angels of light[[2 Cor 11:14||]].

paras.t: Scrutati sunt iniquitates, id est, modos nocendi diligenter indagati sunt, sicut apud Michæam scriptum est : Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem. Defecerunt scrutantes scrutinia : quia justos a fide et veritate avertere non potuerunt, quemadmodum Christus in Evangelio justis promittit : Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt contradicere et resistere omnes adversarii vestri. Denique, nonne tyranni qui nomen Christianorum prorsus exstirpare conabantur, penitus defecerunt ? Nam quo horribiliora tormenta martyribus intulerunt, eo Deus gloriosus et fortis sanctos suos excellentius mirificavit; sicque fides catholica inter tormenta multo amplius crevit, quam modo tempore pacis : in quo utique omnipotens virtus Christi et fidei veritas lucidissime comprobantur, dum tam experimentaliter ostenditur operata Divinitas.
paras.en: [[63:7|They have searched after iniquities|Scrutati sunt iniquitates]], that is, they have diligently tracked out ways of doing harm, as it is written in Micheas: [[Mich 7:2|every one hunteth his brother to death|Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem]]. [[63:7|they have failed in their search|Defecerunt scrutantes scrutinia]]: for they could not turn the just away from faith and truth, as Christ promises the just in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt contradicere et resistere omnes adversarii vestri]]. In short, did not the tyrants who tried to root out the Christian name altogether fail utterly? For the more horrible the torments they inflicted on the martyrs, the more excellently did God, glorious and mighty, make his saints wonderful[[Ps 15:3||]]; and so the Catholic faith grew far more amid torments than it does now in a time of peace: and in this the almighty power of Christ and the truth of the faith are most clearly proved, since the Godhead is shown so plainly, by experience, to have been at work.

paras.t: Accedet homo fidelis contemplativus, ad cor altum, id est ad considerationes profundas, speculando mirabilia de lege Dei, quomodo quæ stulta sunt mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat sapientes, et infirma mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat fortia; quomodo etiam Deus in hoc mundo reprobos prosperari, electos autem multipliciter affligi permittat, et qualiter per incarnationem ac mortem unigeniti Filii sui mundum liberare decrevit.
paras.en: [[63:7|Man shall come|Accedet homo]], the faithful contemplative, [[63:7|to a deep heart|ad cor altum]], that is, to deep considerations, contemplating the wonders of God's law[[Ps 118:18||]]: how [[1 Cor 1:27|the foolish things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the wise: and the weak things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the strong|quæ stulta sunt mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat sapientes, et infirma mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat fortia]]; how too God permits the reprobate to prosper in this world and the elect to be afflicted in many ways; and how he decreed to set the world free through the incarnation and death of his only-begotten Son.

paras.t: In hoc vero hominis accessu ad cor altum, et exaltabitur Deus : quia ex horum contemplatione divinam sapientiam admiramur, divinam justitiam formidamus, majestatemque divinam venerari optamus. Unde ait sermo divinus : Ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes qui sibi videntur esse sapientes ; et rursum, Ecce Deus excelsus in fortitudine sua, et nullus ei similis in legislatoribus.
paras.en: And in this coming of man to the deep heart, [[63:8|God shall be exalted|exaltabitur Deus]]: for from the contemplation of these things we wonder at the divine wisdom, we dread the divine justice, and we long to revere the divine majesty. Hence the word of God says: [[Job 37:24|Therefore men shall fear him, and all that seem to themselves to be wise, shall not dare to behold him|Ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes qui sibi videntur esse sapientes]]; and again, [[Job 36:22|Behold, God is high in his strength, and none is like him among the lawgivers|Ecce Deus excelsus in fortitudine sua, et nullus ei similis in legislatoribus]].

paras.t: Sagittæ parvulorum factæ sunt plagæ eorum. Sicut in præcedenti articulo versus iste tripliciter expositus est, respectu Christi et Judæorum ; sic nunc exponi potest per comparationem ad tyrannos et martyres sanctos, seu justos afflictos. Nam et ipsi tyranni ac persecutores justorum, sagittis et plagis, quas inferunt virtuosis hominibus, semetipsos damnant, spiritualiterque occidunt. Sagittæ quoque parvulorum, id est prædicatio et responsa justorum ac martyrum, factæ sunt plagæ impiorum, quia fidelibus mundum impleverunt, idololatriam destruendo, et persecutoribus prævalendo. Ipsi quoque persecutores sæpius vehementissime cruciabantur propter responsa martyrum Christi, sicut in legendis sancti Vincentii, Agathæ, aliorumque legitur.
paras.en: [[63:8|The arrows of children are their wounds|Sagittæ parvulorum factæ sunt plagæ eorum]]. As in the preceding article this verse was expounded in three ways, with regard to Christ and the Jews, so now it can be expounded by comparison with the tyrants and the holy martyrs, or the afflicted just. For the tyrants themselves and the persecutors of the just damn themselves and slay themselves spiritually with the arrows and wounds they inflict on virtuous men. Again, [[63:8|The arrows of children|Sagittæ quoque parvulorum]], that is, the preaching and the answers of the just and of the martyrs, [[63:8|are their wounds|factæ sunt plagæ impiorum]], that is, the wounds of the wicked [Denis has *impiorum*, "of the wicked", for the psalm's *eorum*, "their"], because they filled the world with believers, destroying idolatry and prevailing over the persecutors. The persecutors themselves, too, were very often most grievously tormented by the answers of Christ's martyrs, as we read in the legends of St Vincent, of St Agatha and of others.

paras.t: Conturbati sunt ad pœnitentiam omnes qui videbant eos, id est, qui consideraverunt prædictorum impiorum ruinam ac damnationem æternam ; et timuit, ex pœna eorum, omnis homo rationabiliter vivens, ne sibi simile accidat, si Deum offenderit. Cetera patent ex præcedenti expositione.
paras.en: [[63:9|All that saw them|omnes qui videbant eos]] [[63:9|were troubled|Conturbati sunt]] to penance, that is, those who considered the ruin and eternal damnation of the wicked just spoken of; and, from their punishment, [[63:10|every man|omnis homo]] who lives according to reason [[63:10|was afraid|et timuit]], lest the like befall him if he offends God. The rest is plain from the preceding exposition.

paras.t: Ecce quam mysterialis et pulcher est psalmus præsens, in quo Christi mysteria continentur. Omnino igitur laboremus sequi Caput nostrum, desiderantes communicare passionibus ejus, et in præsenti sæculo vilipendi, nesciri, variisque tribulationibus emundari : quatenus vita hac fallaci ac labili consummata, statim mereamur a Domino Christo amplexari et coronari, a quo tanto sublimius erigemur, quanto nunc ob ejus amorem nos ipsos amplius abnegamus, humiliusque deprimimus. Propter quod ait Salvator : Quod hominibus altum est, abominatio est apud Deum.
paras.en: See how full of mystery and how beautiful the present psalm is, in which the mysteries of Christ are contained. Let us therefore strive with all our might to follow our Head[[Eph 4:15||]], desiring to share in his sufferings[[1 Pet 4:13||]], and in this present world to be held cheap, to be unknown, and to be cleansed by various tribulations: so that, when this deceitful and slippery life is ended, we may straightway deserve to be embraced and crowned by the Lord Christ, by whom we shall be raised the higher, the more we now deny ourselves for love of him and the more humbly we abase ourselves. Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 16:15|that which is high to men is an abomination before God|Quod hominibus altum est, abominatio est apud Deum]].

paras.t: PRECATIO. Benigna et summa potestas, Deus, a timore inimicorum eripe animas nostras : ut qui scrutari iniquitates contra salutem nostram non cessant, tuo insuperabili abacti brachio, deficiant a nobis scrutantes scrutinia.
paras.en: Prayer. O kind and supreme Power, O God, deliver our souls [[63:2|from the fear of the enemy|a timore inimicorum]]: that they who without ceasing have [[63:7|searched after iniquities|scrutari iniquitates]] against our salvation may be driven back by thine invincible arm and fall away from us, [[63:7|failed in their search|deficiant a nobis scrutantes scrutinia]].

64.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SEXAGESIMI QUARTI : TE DECET HYMNUS, ETC.
64.title_en: Literal exposition of the sixty-fourth psalm: A hymn, O God, becometh thee, etc.

paras.t: Habet interea psalmus jam exponendus hunc titulum : In finem, psalmus David, canticum Jeremiæ et Aggæi, de verbo peregrinationis, quum inciperent proficisci. Psalmum præsentem David conscripsit de reditu Judæorum a captivitate Babylonis et reædificatione templi. Unde secundum sensum litteralem titulus planus est. Sic enim intelligi debet : Psalmus iste sancti David, in finem, id est in Christum, nos dirigens, est canticum, id est exsultatio seu gratiarum actio, Jeremiæ et Aggæi prophetarum : canticum, inquam, loquens de verbo peregrinationis, seu populo transmigrationis, ut alii habent, quum inciperent proficisci de Babylone ad Judæam. Tractat enim hic psalmus de peregrinatione et transmigratione ac reductione Judæorum. Et dicitur canticum Jeremiæ seu Ezechielis, et Aggæi, non quod ipsi psalmum hunc fecerint, sed quoniam eis appropriatur, ob hoc quod Jeremias atque Ezechiel reditum Judæorum a Babylonia prædixerunt ; Aggæus vero reversis prophetavit de templi reædificatione, sicut et Zacharias. Propter quod (ut videtur) posset in titulo poni canticum Zachariæ tam bene, sicut Aggæi aut Jeremiæ, præsertim quum omnia ista, videlicet, Canticum Jeremiæ, etc., usque ad finem, sint quædam additiones expositorum : non enim in Hebræo habentur, nec in translatione Hieronymi juxta Hebræum.
paras.en: The psalm now to be expounded has this title: [[64:1|To the end, a psalm of David|In finem, psalmus David]]. [[64:1|The canticle of Jeremias|canticum Jeremiæ]] and Aggeus, concerning the word of the pilgrimage, [[64:1|when they began|quum inciperent]] to set out [Denis's title follows another reading; the Douay-Rheims, with the Clementine Vulgate, has "The canticle of Jeremias and Ezechiel to the people of the captivity, when they began to go out"]. David wrote the present psalm on the return of the Jews from the captivity of Babylon[[1 Esd 1:1||]] and the rebuilding of the temple. Hence according to the literal sense the title is plain. For it is to be understood thus: This psalm of holy David, [[64:1|to the end|in finem]], that is, directing us unto Christ, is a [[64:1|canticle|canticum]], that is, an exultation or thanksgiving, of the prophets Jeremias and Aggeus: a canticle, I say, speaking concerning the word of the pilgrimage, or (as others have it) [[64:1|to the people of the captivity|populo transmigrationis]], [[64:1|when they began|quum inciperent]] to set out from Babylon for Judea. For this psalm treats of the pilgrimage and transmigration and bringing back of the Jews. And it is called the canticle of Jeremias, or of Ezechiel, and of Aggeus, not because they made this psalm, but because it is appropriated to them, for this reason: that Jeremias[[Jer 29:10||]] [the margin gives Jer. i, 28, which does not exist; the return after seventy years is foretold at Jer 29:10] and Ezechiel[[Ezech 34:22||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xxxiv, 21–28] foretold the return of the Jews from Babylonia, while Aggeus prophesied to those who had returned about the rebuilding of the temple[[Agg 1:1||]] [the margin gives Agg. i, 1–11], as did Zacharias also[[Zach 1:16||]]. Therefore (as it seems) the canticle of Zacharias might be put in the title just as well as of Aggeus or Jeremias, especially since all these words, namely "The canticle of Jeremias", etc., to the end, are additions of the expositors: for they are not found in the Hebrew, nor in Jerome's translation from the Hebrew.

paras.t: Loquens igitur David in persona populi a prædicta captivitate cum ingenti lætitia redeuntis, ait : Te decet hymnus, id est laus divina cum cantico, o Deus, in Sion, id est in loco quo templum a Babyloniis dissipatum fuerat situm, quia hunc locum Deus elegit ad suum cultum, quemadmodum in libro Paralipomenon ostenditur ; et tibi reddetur votum, id est, promissio persolvetur, vel desideria sancta offerentur, in Jerusalem : quia in ea erat templum construendum, in quo offerebantur quæ per votum Domino debebantur.
paras.en: Speaking, then, in the person of the people returning with great joy from the aforesaid captivity, David says: [[64:2|A hymn|Te decet hymnus]], that is, divine praise with song, [[64:2|O God, becometh thee in Sion|Deus, in Sion]], that is, in the place where the temple stood that the Babylonians had destroyed, because God chose this place for his worship, as is shown in the book of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 7:12||]]; [[64:2|and a vow shall be paid to thee|et tibi reddetur votum]], that is, the promise shall be discharged, or holy desires shall be offered, [[64:2|in Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]]: because in it the temple was to be built, in which were offered the things owed to the Lord by vow.

paras.t: Exaudi orationem meam, quam pro civitatis ac templi reparatione effundo ; ad te omnis caro veniet, id est, de omni natione aliqui venient, templo restaurato, quatenus te in eo adorent. Nam et multi gentilium ad ipsum convenerant, ut in Actis legitur de eunucho reginæ Candacis. Et in libro Machabæorum habetur, quod templum illud toto orbe famosissimum erat, ita ut Seleucus rex Asiæ maximas ad ipsum immolationes transmitteret.
paras.en: [[64:3|O hear my prayer|Exaudi orationem meam]], which I pour forth for the restoring of the city and the temple; [[64:3|all flesh shall come to thee|ad te omnis caro veniet]], that is, some will come from every nation, once the temple is restored, so as to adore thee in it. For many of the gentiles too had come together to it, as we read in the Acts of the eunuch of queen Candace[[Acts 8:27||]]. And it is recorded in the book of Machabees that that temple was most famous in all the world[[2 Mach 3:2||]], so that Seleucus, king of Asia, sent very great offerings for sacrifice to it[[2 Mach 3:3||]].

paras.t: Verba iniquorum prævaluerunt super nos, id est, dicta et facta Babyloniorum oppresserunt nos propter scelera nostra ; et impietatibus nostris tu propitiaberis, eas dimittendo, quemadmodum per Jeremiam dixisti, quod septuaginta annis expletis, reduceres nos, templumque et civitatem Jerusalem reædificares.
paras.en: [[64:4|The words of the wicked have prevailed over us|Verba iniquorum prævaluerunt super nos]], that is, the words and deeds of the Babylonians have oppressed us because of our crimes; [[64:4|and thou wilt pardon our transgressions|et impietatibus nostris tu propitiaberis]], by forgiving them, as thou didst say through Jeremias that when seventy years were completed thou wouldst bring us back, and rebuild the temple and the city of Jerusalem[[Jer 25:12||]].

paras.t: Beatus est jam in spe, quem elegisti et assumpsisti, ut eum ad terram Judææ reducas, et in ea tibi servire habitareque facias. Propterea Baruch ait : Filii, patienter sustinete iram quæ superveniet vobis ; qui enim induxit vobis mala, ipse rursus adducet vobis sempiternam jucunditatem cum vestra salute. Inhabitabit in atriis tuis, id est in locis ac domibus circa templum situatis, in quibus sacrificia, orationes lectionesque legis fiebant. Replebimur in bonis domus tuæ : nam temporalium spiritualiumque bonorum sufficientiam contulit Deus reversis a Babylone ; ministri quoque templi ex oblatis in templo copiose sustentabantur.
paras.en: [[64:5|Blessed|Beatus]] already in hope is he [[64:5|whom thou hast chosen and taken to thee|quem elegisti et assumpsisti]], so that thou mayest bring him back to the land of Judea and make him serve thee and dwell in it. Hence Baruch says: [[Bar 4:25|My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you|Filii, patienter sustinete iram quæ superveniet vobis]]; [[Bar 4:29|For he that hath brought evils upon you, shall bring you everlasting joy again with your salvation|qui enim induxit vobis mala, ipse rursus adducet vobis sempiternam jucunditatem cum vestra salute]]. [[64:5|he shall dwell in thy courts|Inhabitabit in atriis tuis]], that is, in the places and buildings situated about the temple, in which sacrifices, prayers and readings of the law took place. [[64:5|We shall be filled with the good things of thy house|Replebimur in bonis domus tuæ]]: for God bestowed a sufficiency of temporal and spiritual goods on those who returned from Babylon; and the ministers of the temple too were plentifully maintained from the offerings made in the temple.

paras.t: Sanctum est templum tuum materiale, id est ad sanctum tuum obsequium deputatum ; mirabile in æquitate : quia in eo sacerdotes causas dubias atque difficiles judicabantur, prout Dominus Moysi jussit. Vel : Sanctum est templum tuum, id est, congregatio populi tui quam reducis ad terram tuam, est sancta et mirabilis in æquitate : quia in ea fuerant sanctissimi atque justissimi viri, utpote Esdras, Nehemias, et alii multi.
paras.en: [[64:5|holy is thy temple|Sanctum est templum tuum]], the material temple, that is, set apart for thy holy service; [[64:6|wonderful in justice|mirabile in æquitate]]: because in it the priests judged doubtful and difficult cases, as the Lord commanded Moses[[Deut 17:8||]]. Or: [[64:5|holy is thy temple|Sanctum est templum tuum]], that is, the congregation of thy people, which thou art bringing back to thy land, is holy and [[64:6|wonderful in justice|mirabilis in æquitate]]: because in it there were most holy and most just men, such as Esdras, Nehemias and many others.

paras.t: Exaudi nos, Deus salutaris noster, ut templum istud secundum præferatur in gloria templo primo a Salomone constructo : sicut Aggæus promittit, Magna, inquiens, erit gloria domus hujus novissimæ, magis quam primæ. Spes omnium finium terræ, id est spes omnium hominum in toto orbe morantium, et in mari longe : non enim ponenda est spes, nisi in Deo ; et qui alibi eam ponit, errat.
paras.en: [[64:6|Hear us, O God our saviour|Exaudi nos, Deus salutaris noster]], that this second temple may be preferred in glory to the first temple, built by Solomon: as Aggeus promises, saying: [[Agg 2:10|Great|Magna]] [[Agg 2:10|shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first|erit gloria domus hujus novissimæ, magis quam primæ]]. [[64:6|who art the hope of all the ends of the earth|Spes omnium finium terræ]], that is, the hope of all men dwelling in the whole world, [[64:6|and in the sea afar off|et in mari longe]]: for hope is not to be placed save in God; and whoever places it elsewhere errs.

paras.t: Præparans montes in virtute tua. Tanquam dicat : Tu, Domine Deus, exaudire nos potes, et bona Israel promissa facile adimplere, qui es tantæ potestatis, ut sis præparans, id est fundans, sustentans, et pro tua voluntate disponens, montes terræ, quorum nonnulli mirabiliter alti sunt. Et hoc agis in virtute tua propria, non aliunde adepta : subest enim tibi, quum volueris, posse. Unde inferius dicitur : Ascendunt montes et descendunt campi in locum quem fundasti eis.
paras.en: [[64:7|Thou who preparest the mountains by thy strength|Præparans montes in virtute tua]]. As if he were saying: Thou, O Lord God, canst hear us, and easily fulfil the good things promised to Israel, who art of such power that thou art he who [[64:7|preparest|præparans]], that is, foundest, sustainest and disposest at thy will, the mountains of the earth, some of which are wondrously high. And this thou doest [[64:7|by thy strength|in virtute tua]], thine own, not got from elsewhere: [[Wis 12:18|for thy power is at hand when thou wilt|subest enim tibi, quum volueris, posse]]. Hence it is said further on: [[Ps 103:8|The mountains ascend, and the plains descend into the place which thou hast founded for them|Ascendunt montes et descendunt campi in locum quem fundasti eis]].

paras.t: Accinctus potentia. Hoc de Deo metaphorice dicitur. Deus namque est ipsa sua potentia, suntque in Deo omnino idem, esse, posse, et agere. Dicitur ergo Deus accinctus potentia, id est potestate et omnipotentia undique adornatus atque indutus : quoniam sicut homo armis accingitur, ut ad præliandum sit fortis, et ad exercitium expeditus ; sic Deus se ipso seu propria et consubstantiali sibi potentia, ad prævalendum omni adversæ potestati est fortis, et ad operandum quidquid sibi placuerit, promptus et expeditus.
paras.en: [[64:7|being girded with power|Accinctus potentia]]. This is said of God metaphorically. For God is his very power, and in God being, power and acting are altogether the same. God is therefore said to be [[64:7|girded with power|accinctus potentia]], that is, adorned and clothed on every side with might and omnipotence: since as a man is girded with arms, that he may be strong for battle and ready for action, so God, by himself, that is, by his own power, consubstantial with him, is strong to prevail over every adverse power, and prompt and ready to work whatever pleases him.

paras.t: Qui conturbas profundum maris, commovendo in eo varias tempestates ; sonum fluctuum ejus : id est, inundationem ac strepitum gurgitum pelagi tu auges et mitigas supra naturam, secundum propriæ voluntatis imperium. Propter quod infra habetur : Tu dominaris potestati maris, motum autem fluctuum ejus tu mitigas. Et alio in loco : Dominus misit ventum magnum in mare, et facta est tempestas magna in mari. Unde de Domino Jesu ait Evangelista : Surgens comminatus est vento, et dixit mari, Tace et obmutesce ; et facta est tranquillitas magna.
paras.en: [[64:8|Who troublest the depth of the sea|Qui conturbas profundum maris]], stirring up various tempests in it; [[64:8|the noise of its waves|sonum fluctuum ejus]]: that is, the surging and roar of the deeps of the ocean thou dost increase and calm above nature, at the command of thine own will. Hence it is said further on: [[Ps 88:10|Thou rulest the power of the sea: and appeasest the motion of the waves thereof|Tu dominaris potestati maris, motum autem fluctuum ejus tu mitigas]]. And in another place: [[Jon 1:4|the Lord sent a great wind to the sea: and a great tempest was raised in the sea|Dominus misit ventum magnum in mare, et facta est tempestas magna in mari]]. Hence the Evangelist says of the Lord Jesus: [[Mark 4:39|rising up, he rebuked the wind, and said to the sea: Peace, be still|Surgens comminatus est vento, et dixit mari, Tace et obmutesce]]; [[Mark 4:39|and there was made a great calm|et facta est tranquillitas magna]].

paras.t: Turbabuntur gentes, et timebunt qui habitant terminos, a signis tuis, id est, omnes in toto orbe manentes, admirabuntur et pavebunt propter mirabilia quæ facis in mari et terra : sicut et frequenter factum est in terræ motibus, tempestatibus aliisque prodigiis. Exitus matutini et vesperi delectabis : id est, immolationes sacrificii quod offertur mane, et ejus quod vespere immolatur, facies tibi acceptas, tuisque fidelibus delectabiles. Propter quod in Esdra scriptum est, quod templo reædificato, obtulerunt in eo holocaustum Domino mane et vespere.
paras.en: [[64:8|The Gentiles shall be troubled|Turbabuntur gentes]], and [[64:9|they that dwell in the uttermost borders shall be afraid at thy signs|timebunt qui habitant terminos, a signis tuis]], that is, all who abide in the whole world will wonder and be afraid because of the wonders thou workest on sea and land: as has often happened in earthquakes, tempests and other portents. [[64:9|thou shalt make the outgoings of the morning and of the evening to be joyful|Exitus matutini et vesperi delectabis]]: that is, the sacrifice that is offered in the morning, and that which is sacrificed in the evening, thou wilt make acceptable to thee and delightful to thy faithful. Hence it is written in Esdras that, when the temple had been rebuilt, they offered in it [[1 Esd 3:3|a holocaust to the Lord morning and evening|holocaustum Domino mane et vespere]] [in Esdras the altar is set up and these holocausts offered before the foundations of the temple are laid].

paras.t: Consequenter beatus David prophetat de ubertate terræ post reditum a prædicta captivitate : de qua etiam ubertate Jeremias atque Ezechiel clare prophetant. Ait enim de futuro per modum præteriti, propter prophetiæ certitudinem inconcussam : Visitasti terram Judææ, dando ei uberes […] et inebriasti eam, id est, pluviis opportunis eam copiose irrigasti : quemadmodum Isaias inducit, Descendit imber et nix de cœlo, et illuc ultra non revertitur, sed inebriat terram, et infundit eam. Multiplicasti locupletare eam, id est, pluribus modis terram ditasti : quoniam ex fertilitate terræ nascentium, quæ sunt naturales divitiæ, acquiruntur et augmentantur divitiæ artificiales.
paras.en: Next, blessed David prophesies of the fruitfulness of the land after the return from the aforesaid captivity, of which fruitfulness Jeremias[[Jer 31:12||]] and Ezechiel[[Ezech 28:25||]][[Ezech 28:26||]] also clearly prophesy. For he speaks of the future after the manner of the past, because of the unshakable certainty of prophecy: [[64:10|Thou hast visited the earth|Visitasti terram]] of Judea, giving it plentiful […], [[64:10|and hast plentifully watered it|et inebriasti eam]], that is, thou hast watered it copiously with seasonable rains: as Isaias puts it, [[Is 55:10|the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and return no more thither, but soak the earth, and water it|Descendit imber et nix de cœlo, et illuc ultra non revertitur, sed inebriat terram, et infundit eam]] [the psalm's *inebriasti* and Isaias's *inebriat* mean literally "made drunk", "makes drunk"]. [[64:10|thou hast many ways enriched it|Multiplicasti locupletare eam]], that is, thou hast enriched the land in many ways: since from the fertility of the things that grow from the earth, which are natural riches, artificial riches are acquired and increased [natural riches are those that meet man's needs directly, such as crops and cattle; artificial riches are money and what it buys].

paras.t: Flumen Dei repletum est aquis, id est, Jordanis aquis abundavit. Dicitur autem Jordanis flumen Dei, propter mirabilia quæ Deus in eo peregit, arefaciens alveum ejus, et aquas ejus superiores in altitudinem turris ascendere, permanereque faciens, donec filii Israel pertransissent, quemadmodum in libro Josue legitur. Parasti cibum illorum, id est, escam Judæis revertentibus præparasti, terram fecundando ; quoniam ita est præparatio ejus, id est, quia repletio Jordanis facit ad terræ fecundationem et cibi præparationem.
paras.en: [[64:10|The river of God is filled with water|Flumen Dei repletum est aquis]], that is, the Jordan abounded with water. Now the Jordan is called the river of God because of the wonders God wrought in it, drying up its bed and making its upper waters rise to the height of a tower and stay there until the children of Israel had passed over, as we read in the book of Josue[[Jos 3:16||]][[Jos 3:17||]]. [[64:10|thou hast prepared their food|Parasti cibum illorum]], that is, thou hast prepared food for the returning Jews by making the land fruitful; [[64:10|for so is its preparation|quoniam ita est præparatio ejus]], that is, because the filling of the Jordan makes for the fruitfulness of the land and the preparing of food.

paras.t: Rivos ejus inebria, id est, rivos Jordanis fac copiosum fructum producere ; multiplica generationem ejus. Hoc est expositio verbi præcedentis : multiplicatio namque geniminum seu fructuum terræ, est inebriatio rivorum. Vel, Rivos ejus inebria, id est, abundanter auge ac imple. In stillicidiis ejus lætabitur germinans, id est, in guttis aquarum Jordanis a cœlo stillantibus, terra lætabitur, id est, habitatores suos faciet gloriari. Vel, Lætabitur, metaphorice, sicut pratum ridere asserimus.
paras.en: [[64:11|Fill up plentifully the streams thereof|Rivos ejus inebria]], that is, make the streams of the Jordan bring forth abundant fruit; [[64:11|multiply its fruits|multiplica generationem ejus]] [Denis reads *generationem*, "its generation", where the Vulgate has *genimina*, "its produce"]. This is the explanation of the words before: for the multiplying of the produce or fruits of the land is the "filling" [*inebriatio*, literally "making drunk"] of the streams. Or: [[64:11|Fill up plentifully the streams thereof|Rivos ejus inebria]], that is, increase and fill them abundantly. [[64:11|it shall spring up and rejoice in its showers|In stillicidiis ejus lætabitur germinans]], that is, in the drops of the waters of the Jordan falling from the sky the land shall rejoice, that is, it shall make its inhabitants glory. Or: it shall [[64:11|rejoice|lætabitur]], metaphorically, as we say that a meadow laughs.

paras.t: Benedices coronæ, id est circumvolutioni seu circulo, anni benignitatis tuæ, id est tempori misericordiæ tuæ, dando ea quæ ad fructuum productionem exiguntur. Dicitur enim Deus benedicere tempori, quando his quæ in tempore fiunt aut sunt, benedicit, id est, gratiam seu bonitatem aliquam eis impendit. Et campi tui, id est campi culti Judææ, replebuntur ubertate fructuum diversorum.
paras.en: [[64:12|Thou shalt bless the crown|Benedices coronæ]], that is, the round or circle, [[64:12|of the year of thy goodness|anni benignitatis tuæ]], that is, the time of thy mercy, by giving what is required for bringing forth fruits. For God is said to bless a time when he blesses the things that come to be or exist in time, that is, bestows on them some grace or goodness. [[64:12|And thy fields|Et campi tui]], that is, the tilled fields of Judea, [[64:12|shall be filled with plenty|replebuntur ubertate]] of diverse fruits.

paras.t: Pinguescent speciosa deserti, id est, pinguia pascua proferent ad animalia nutrienda ; et exsultatione colles accingentur, id est, fructu seu germine homines lætificante undique implebuntur.
paras.en: [[64:13|The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat|Pinguescent speciosa deserti]], that is, they shall bring forth rich pastures for feeding the animals; [[64:13|and the hills shall be girded about with joy|et exsultatione colles accingentur]], that is, they shall be filled on every side with fruit or produce that gladdens men.

paras.t: Induti sunt lana copiosa arietes ovium : sicque non erit indigentia vestimentorum ; et valles abundabunt frumento : quia valles terræ illius aptæ dicuntur ut in eis grana bona serantur. Clamabunt, etenim hymnum dicent. Dicuntur autem inanimata, sicut terræ nascentia, atque similia, Deo benedicere et clamare materialiter, quoniam sunt materia et occasio unde homines ad laudem divinam provocentur, suaque pulchritudine, fecunditate et dispositione inducunt nos, si bene consideremus, ad clamandum, benedicendumque Dominum. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico legitur : Quam desiderabilia sunt opera Dei ! Et quis satiabitur, videns gloriam ejus ? Hinc nempe apud Danielem omnes creaturæ, etiam inanimatæ, invitantur ad benedicendum Creatori.
paras.en: [[64:14|The rams of the flock are clothed|Induti sunt lana copiosa arietes ovium]] with plenteous wool [Denis's text adds *lana copiosa*, "with plenteous wool"]: and so there will be no want of clothing; [[64:14|and the vales shall abound with corn|et valles abundabunt frumento]]: because the valleys of that land are said to be fit for good grain to be sown in them. [[64:14|they shall shout, yea they shall sing a hymn|Clamabunt, etenim hymnum dicent]]. Now inanimate things, such as what grows from the earth and the like, are said to bless God and to shout materially [that is, as the matter of praise, not by any act of their own], since they are the matter and occasion by which men are stirred to divine praise, and by their beauty, fruitfulness and order they lead us, if we consider them well, to shout and to bless the Lord. Hence we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 42:23|O how desirable are all his works|Quam desiderabilia sunt opera]]! [[Ecclus 42:26|And who shall be filled with beholding his glory|Et quis satiabitur, videns gloriam ejus]]? Hence indeed in Daniel all creatures, even inanimate ones, are invited to bless the Creator[[Dan 3:57||]] [the margin gives Dan. iii, 57–90].

64.title: […]IS EJUSDEM PSALMI SEXAGESIMI QUARTI : EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS.
64.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same sixty-fourth psalm.

paras.t: Porro moraliter titulus præinductus ita exponitur: In finem, psalmus David, id est, psalmus iste tendens in Christum, convenit David, id est Ecclesiæ militanti jam peregrinanti, et ad patriam suspiranti; cuilibet quoque fideli, de Babylone, id est de confusione vitiorum, ad terram Judææ et Sion, id est ad confessionem, laudem ac speculationem divinam redeunti. Et psalmus iste est canticum Jeremiæ et Aggæi, de verbo transmigrationis, id est, agit de re significata per transmigrationem ac reditum Judæorum a Babylone, videlicet de reditu nostro a captivitate vitiorum atque diaboli, ad pacem Ecclesiæ et libertatem filiorum Dei. Qui enim vitiis servit, a dæmone captus est, sicut ait Apostolus, de peccatoribus loquens: Resipiscant a diaboli laqueis, a quo captivi detinentur ad ipsius voluntatem. Et evangelica ait Scriptura: Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati. Revertendum ergo est nobis a confusione ad ordinationem, a culpa ad gratiam, a regno diaboli ad regnum Christi. Sicque redeuntes, cum præcordiali hilaritate dicamus:
paras.en: Now in the moral sense the title set out above is expounded thus: [[64:1|To the end, a psalm of David|In finem, psalmus David]], that is, this psalm, tending towards Christ, befits David, that is, the Church militant, now on pilgrimage and sighing for the fatherland; and also any one of the faithful returning from Babylon, that is, from the confusion of the vices, to the land of Judea and to Sion, that is, to confession, to praise and to the contemplation of God. And this psalm is [[64:1|the canticle of Jeremias|canticum Jeremiæ]] and Aggeus, on the word of the transmigration [Denis's title reads "of Jeremias and Aggeus, on the word of the transmigration"; the Clementine Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have "of Jeremias and Ezechiel to the people of the captivity"], that is, it treats of the thing signified by the transmigration and the return of the Jews from Babylon, namely of our return from the captivity of the vices and of the devil to the peace of the Church and the liberty of the sons of God. For he who serves the vices has been taken captive by the demon, as the Apostle says, speaking of sinners: [[2 Tim 2:26|they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil by whom they are held captive at his will|Resipiscant a diaboli laqueis, a quo captivi detinentur ad ipsius voluntatem]]. And the Gospel scripture says: [[John 8:34|whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin|Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati]]. We must therefore turn back from confusion to order, from guilt to grace, from the kingdom of the devil to the kingdom of Christ. And so, returning, let us say with heartfelt gladness:

paras.t: Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion, id est in sancta ac militanti Ecclesia, in qua incessabiliter Deum laudare ac honorare debemus, implentes quod ait Apostolus: Regi sæculorum immortali, invisibili, soli Deo honor et gloria. Sion namque speculatio dicitur: per quam Ecclesia designatur, quæ Christum jam fideliter contemplatur. Et tibi reddetur votum, id est, tibi perfecte solvetur promissio, in Jerusalem, illa quæ sursum est, quæ est mater nostra atque triumphans Ecclesia. Dum enim in sacro Baptismate, per votum fidelitatis, diabolo et omnibus ejus operibus abrenuntiamus, corpusque nostrum ac animam Deo offerimus, ejus nos cultui totaliter dedicantes, tenemur sic vitam nostram dirigere, ut omnis nostra cogitatio, locutio et operatio Deo semper intendat, Deum loquatur ac veneretur: in quo consistit perfecta adimpletio præcepti de caritate. Istud autem in præsenti perfecte implere non possumus, sed in patria perfecte implebitur: tunc enim corpus animam non retardabit.
paras.en: [[64:2|A hymn, O God, becometh thee in Sion|Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion]], that is, in the holy Church militant, in which we ought to praise and honour God without ceasing, fulfilling what the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 1:17|to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory|Regi sæculorum immortali, invisibili, soli Deo honor et gloria]]. For Sion is called *speculatio* [that is, "a looking-out" or "watch-tower", the usual interpretation of the name; the word also means "contemplation"]: and by it the Church is signified, which already contemplates Christ by faith. [[64:2|And a vow shall be paid to thee|Et tibi reddetur votum]], that is, the promise shall be perfectly fulfilled to thee, [[64:2|in Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]], that Jerusalem [[Gal 4:26|which is above|quæ sursum est]], [[Gal 4:26|which is our mother|quæ est mater nostra]], the Church triumphant. For when in holy Baptism, by the vow of fidelity, we renounce the devil and all his works, and offer our body and soul to God, dedicating ourselves wholly to his worship, we are bound so to direct our life that all our thought, speech and work may ever tend to God, speak of God and revere him: and in this consists the perfect fulfilment of the precept of charity. But this we cannot perfectly fulfil in the present life; it will be perfectly fulfilled in the fatherland, for then the body will not hold back the soul.

paras.t: Exaudi orationem meam, o Domine, ut te in hoc sæculo ac militanti Ecclesia tam pulchris atque devotis hymnis collaudem, quatenus quod nunc perfecte solvere nequeo, in superna illa Jerusalem sine fine feliciter reddam. Ad te omnis caro veniet, id est omnis homo, præsertim in finali judicio, quando congregabuntur ante Filium hominis omnes gentes. Ponitur itaque hic pars pro toto, videlicet caro pro toto composito: sicut in Genesi et Exodo dicitur Jacob descendisse in Ægyptum in animabus septuaginta. Sed nonne sic accipiendo carnem, equus et mulus caro sunt? Nonne veraciter scriptum est, Ægyptus homo et non Deus, et equi eorum caro et non spiritus? Numquid ergo et irrationabilia animantia ad Christum in die judicii venient? Et respondendum, quod ponit hic genus pro specie, scilicet carnem pro carne humana. Vel, sicut nomen Prophetæ antonomastice convenit David, sic caro per se posita, pro carne humana, quæ nobilissima est, sumitur.
paras.en: [[64:3|O hear my prayer|Exaudi orationem meam]], O Lord, that I may praise thee in this world and in the Church militant with hymns so beautiful and devout that what I cannot now perfectly pay, I may happily render without end in that Jerusalem on high. [[64:3|all flesh shall come to thee|Ad te omnis caro veniet]], that is, every man, especially at the final judgment, when all nations shall be gathered together before the Son of man[[Matt 25:32||]]. Here, then, the part is put for the whole, namely flesh for the whole composite [that is, the whole man, made of body and soul]: as in Genesis and Exodus Jacob is said to have gone down into Egypt in seventy souls[[Gen 46:27||]][[Ex 1:5||]]. But if flesh is taken in this way, are not the horse and the mule flesh? Is it not truly written: [[Is 31:3|Egypt is man, and not God: and their horses, flesh, and not spirit|Ægyptus homo et non Deus, et equi eorum caro et non spiritus]]? Shall the irrational animals, then, also come to Christ on the day of judgment? And the answer is that here he puts the genus for the species, namely flesh for human flesh. Or else: as the name of Prophet belongs to David by antonomasia [that is, as the name most properly his], so flesh, put by itself, is taken for human flesh, which is the noblest.

paras.t: Verba iniquorum prævaluerunt super nos. Interdum in sacra Scriptura verbum pro facto accipitur, prout dixit David: Quod est verbum quod factum est? Et Zacharias propheta: Hæc sunt, inquit, verba quæ facietis. Est igitur sensus: Verba iniquorum, id est persecutiones peccatorum, tentationesque dæmonum, prævaluerunt super nos, id est, a via justitiæ abduxerunt nos, et in magnam nos miseriam dejecerunt. Vel: Verba iniquorum, id est suggestio dæmonis, protoplastos nostros parentes tentantis, persuasio quoque Evæ, quæ virum suum infecit, et excusatio Adæ, peccatum suum in feminam retorquentis, prævaluerunt super nos, quoniam de paradiso nos expulerunt, estque grave jugum inductum super omnes filios Adæ, et originalis justitia nobis ablata est, et nascimur filii iræ, id est in originali peccato. Et impietatibus nostris tu propitiaberis, id est, peccata actualia quæ ex originali peccato incurrimus, tu pie dimittes pœnitentibus nobis, dando nobis pœnitendi tempus ac locum: quemadmodum Isaias dicit, Propterea exspectat Dominus, ut misereatur vestri. Vel: Impietatibus nostris, de quibus superius dictum est, Ecce enim in iniquitatibus conceptus sum, tu, Unigenite Dei, propitiaberis miserendo, succurrendo, et satisfaciendo pro nobis: quod nos ipsi facere non poteramus. Hinc per Isaiam Dominus ait: Servire me fecisti in peccatis tuis, præbuisti mihi laborem in iniquitatibus tuis.
paras.en: [[64:4|The words of the wicked have prevailed over us|Verba iniquorum prævaluerunt super nos]]. Sometimes in holy Scripture *word* is taken for the deed, as David said: [[2 Kings 1:4|What is the matter that is come to pass?|Quod est verbum quod factum est?]] [in the Latin, "What is the *word* that is come to pass?"]. And the prophet Zacharias: [[Zach 8:16|These then are|Hæc sunt]], he says, [[Zach 8:16|the things, which you shall do|verba quæ facietis]] [in the Latin, "the *words* which you shall do"]. The sense, then, is: [[64:4|The words of the wicked|Verba iniquorum]], that is, the persecutions of sinners and the temptations of demons, [[64:4|have prevailed over us|prævaluerunt super nos]], that is, have led us away from the way of justice and cast us down into great misery.
