Omnes enim angeli sancti, sunt ipsius Christi, sicut servi sunt dominorum suorum. Unde Christus in Evangelio de se ipso asserit : Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos. Repetitur autem, Dilecti, et sequitur, et speciei domus dividere spolia : id est, Christus qui est Dei Patris dilectus, est etiam dilectus in quantum homo, et electus dividere spolia, id est secundum diversos gradus ac status distinguere homines, quos ipse de ore inimici redemit, atque de morte eripuit, dando eis diversa munera gratiarum, quemadmodum Apostolus attestatur : Quosdam, inquiens, posuit in Ecclesia, primo Apostolos, deinde Prophetas, tertio doctores : et hoc fit speciei domus, id est ad ornamentum Ecclesiæ. Talis enim distinctio ecclesiasticarum personarum, cedit in ornamentum Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[67:13|The king of powers is of the beloved, of the beloved|Rex virtutum dilecti dilecti]]. This verse is tangled and obscure. But sometimes one translation explains another, and so it was useful that several translations were made. Now Jerome's translation from the Hebrew has it thus: The kings of armies shall be leagued together. For through the teaching of the Apostles many kings, princes, nobles and mighty men were made of one mind in the love, faith and worship of Christ. So it is said here: [[67:13|The king of powers|Rex virtutum]], that is, strong kings, taking the singular for the plural, as in Exodus the Lord says to Pharao: Dost thou yet hold back my son (that is, the children of Israel)?[[Ex 4:23||]] [the margin gives Exod. iv, 23, where God calls Israel *my son*; the words *Adhuc retines* are those of Exod 9:17, *Dost thou yet hold back my people*]. So, then: strong kings (we must supply "have become") [[67:13|of the beloved|dilecti]], that is, friends, [[67:13|of the beloved|dilecti]], that is, of Jesus Christ, of whom the Father says: [[Matt 3:17|This is my beloved Son|Hic est Filius meus dilectus]]. Or thus: [[67:13|The king of powers|Rex virtutum]], that is, God the Father, who is king of the angels, who are called the heavenly powers [*virtutes*], and they are [[67:13|of the beloved|dilecti]], that is, of Christ himself, who is the most dear Son of God. For all the holy angels belong to Christ himself, as servants belong to their masters. Hence Christ in the Gospel declares of himself: [[Matt 13:41|The Son of man shall send his angels|Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos]]. Now *Of the beloved* is repeated, and there follows: [[67:13|and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils|et speciei domus dividere spolia]]: that is, Christ, who is the beloved of God the Father, is beloved also inasmuch as he is man, and chosen to divide the spoils, that is, to distinguish according to different degrees and states the men whom he himself redeemed from the mouth of the enemy and snatched from death, giving them different gifts of graces, as the Apostle attests: [[1 Cor 12:28|some|Quosdam]], he says, he [[1 Cor 12:28|hath set|posuit]] [[1 Cor 12:28|in the church; first apostles, secondly prophets, thirdly doctors|in Ecclesia, primo Apostolos, deinde Prophetas, tertio doctores]]. And this is done for [[67:13|the beauty of the house|speciei domus]], that is, for the adornment of the Church. For such a distinction of persons in the Church makes for the adornment of the Church.

paras.t: Deinceps alloquitur sanctus David fideles, dicendo : Si dormiatis inter medios cleros, id est, si tranquilla conscientia quiescatis inter duas hereditates, seu inter duo genera bonorum divinitus concessorum, id est inter bona temporalia vitæ præsentis et bona spiritualia vitæ futuræ, sic transeundo per bona temporalia, ut non amittatis æterna ; tunc pennæ columbæ, id est virtutes ac operationes Ecclesiæ, fiunt et sunt deargentatæ, id est puræ et immaculatæ, quando temporalia non appetuntur inordinate, sed solum prout necessaria sive utilia sunt ad adipiscenda bona cœlestia ; et posteriora, id est extrema opera, dorsi ejus, id est scapularum columbæ seu Ecclesiæ, super se portantis jugum Domini, in pallore auri, id est, terminabuntur in fervore caritatis perfectæ, quæ designatur per aurum. Caritas enim non excidit, sed quæ nunc imperfecta est, in patria fit perfecta, dummodo quiescamus inter medios cleros, ut dictum est : quoniam qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit. Per cleros itaque intelliguntur hereditates, quoniam κλῆρος Græce, Latine dicitur sors : sortes autem ex divina promissione, partes hereditatis vocantur. Ecclesia quoque appellatur columba, propter innocentiam atque munditiam vitæ. Aurum vero caritatem significat, juxta illud : Suadeo tibi emere a me aurum ignitum probatum.
paras.en: Next holy David addresses the faithful, saying: [[67:14|If you sleep among the midst of lots|Si dormiatis inter medios cleros]], that is, if with a quiet conscience you rest between two inheritances, or between two kinds of goods granted by God, namely between the temporal goods of the present life and the spiritual goods of the life to come, so passing through temporal goods as not to lose the eternal; then [[67:14|the wings of a dove|pennæ columbæ]], that is, the virtues and works of the Church, become and are [[67:14|covered with silver|deargentatæ]], that is, pure and spotless, when temporal things are not sought inordinately, but only so far as they are necessary or useful for gaining the heavenly goods; [[67:14|and the hinder parts|et posteriora]], that is, the last works, [[67:14|of her back|dorsi ejus]], that is, of the shoulders of the dove, or of the Church, which carries the yoke of the Lord upon herself, [[67:14|with the paleness of gold|in pallore auri]], that is, will end in the fervour of perfect charity, which is signified by gold. For [[1 Cor 13:8|Charity never falleth away|Caritas enim non excidit]], but the charity that is now imperfect is made perfect in our heavenly country, provided we rest among the midst of lots, as has been said: since [[Matt 10:22|he that shall persevere unto the end, he shall be saved|qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit]]. By *cleri*, then, inheritances are understood, since *kleros* in Greek is called *sors* [lot] in Latin; and lots, by God's promise, are called portions of an inheritance. The Church too is called a dove because of the innocence and cleanness of her life. And gold signifies charity, according to that saying: [[Apoc 3:18|I counsel thee to buy of me gold, fire tried|Suadeo tibi emere a me aurum ignitum probatum]].

paras.t: Dum discernit cœlestis reges super eam, id est, dum Christus, qui singulariter vocatur cœlestis, quippe de quo scriptum est, Qui de cœlo venit, super omnes est : dum ergo iste rex cœlestis discernit, id est, discrete ac sapienter disponit, reges super eam, id est rectores, videlicet Apostolos et eorum imitatores, super Ecclesiam, destinando eos per totum mundum ad docendum omnes gentes ; nive dealbabuntur in Selmon, id est, super nivem purificabuntur fideles in umbra gratiæ Dei. Selmon enim uno modo est proprium nomen cujusdam montis ; alio modo est nomen commune, obscuritatem significans, sicque accipitur modo, et potest designare gratiam vitæ, quæ obscura est per comparationem ad gratiam patriæ. Vel potest ita intelligi : Nive dealbabuntur gentes, quæ ante conversionem ad fidem seu gratiam, erant in obscuritate ac tenebris.
paras.en: [[67:15|When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her|Dum discernit cœlestis reges super eam]], that is, when Christ, who is called in a singular way the heavenly one, since it is written of him: [[John 3:31|He that cometh from heaven is above all|Qui de cœlo venit, super omnes est]]; when, then, this heavenly king [[67:15|appointeth|discernit]], that is, discreetly and wisely sets, [[67:15|kings over her|reges super eam]], that is, rulers, namely the Apostles and those who follow their example, over the Church, sending them through the whole world to teach all nations[[Matt 28:19||]]; [[67:15|they shall be whited with snow in Selmon|nive dealbabuntur in Selmon]], that is, the faithful will be made pure beyond snow in the shadow of the grace of God. For Selmon in one way is the proper name of a certain mountain; in another way it is a common noun meaning darkness, and so it is taken here, and it can signify the grace of this life, which is dark in comparison with the grace of our heavenly country. Or it can be understood thus: The gentiles, who before their conversion to the faith, or to grace, were in darkness and shadows, [[67:15|shall be whited with snow|Nive dealbabuntur]].

paras.t: Et quoniam fideles taliter mundabuntur, idcirco mons Dei, id est Ecclesia militans : de qua in Isaia dicitur, Erit præparatus mons domus Domini in vertice montium. Dicitur enim Ecclesia mons propter altitudinem gratiæ Dei, sublimitatemque vitæ fidelium cœlestia contemplantium. Hic itaque mons Dei, est mons pinguis, id est spiritualibus bonis abundans, ex infusione donorum Spiritus Sancti. Est quoque hic, Mons coagulatus, id est per modum casei ex diversis personis compactus, videlicet ex simplicibus, pauperibus, et abjectis collectus ; mons pinguis : quoniam multas elegantes personas intra se habet, sicut sunt viri orthodoxi, id est gloriose fideles, alios verbo atque exemplo spiritualiter impinguantes. Quum ergo sit una Ecclesia, extra quam nullus salvatur, sicut nec extra arcam Noe aliquis salvabatur, ut quid suspicamini montes coagulatos ? id est, cur æstimatis esse separatas ecclesias, seu loca salutis extra catholicam apostolicamque Ecclesiam ?
paras.en: And since the faithful will be cleansed in this way, therefore [[67:16|The mountain of God|mons Dei]], that is, the Church militant, of which it is said in Isaias: [[Is 2:2|the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of mountains|Erit præparatus mons domus Domini in vertice montium]]. For the Church is called a mountain because of the height of the grace of God and the loftiness of the life of the faithful who contemplate heavenly things. This mountain of God, then, [[67:16|is a fat mountain|est mons pinguis]], that is, abounding in spiritual goods, from the pouring in of the gifts of the Holy Ghost. It is also [[67:16|A curdled mountain|Mons coagulatus]], that is, pressed together like cheese out of different persons, namely gathered from the simple, the poor and the despised; [[67:16|a fat mountain|mons pinguis]], since it has within itself many excellent persons, such as orthodox men, that is, gloriously faithful ones, who spiritually fatten others by word and example. Since, then, there is one Church, outside which no one is saved, as no one was saved outside the ark of Noe[[1 Pet 3:20||]], [[67:17|Why suspect, ye curdled mountains|ut quid suspicamini montes coagulatos]]? that is, why do you think that there are separate churches, or places of salvation, outside the Catholic and Apostolic Church?

paras.t: Quæ est Mons, in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo. Hic enim mons est congregatio electorum, de quibus increata Sapientia in Proverbiis ait : Deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum ; et in Apocalypsi, Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis. Etenim Dominus habitabit in finem : non ad horam, seu modicum temporis, sed usque ad finem sæculi, imo in sempiternum habitabit cum Ecclesia electorum, habitando in eis per fidem et gratiam, quemadmodum Christus promisit : Ecce, inquiens, ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi.
paras.en: For it is [[67:17|A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell|Mons, in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo]]. For this mountain is the gathering of the elect, of whom the uncreated Wisdom says in Proverbs: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum]]; and in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:3|Behold the tabernacle of God with men: and he will dwell with them|Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis]]. [[67:17|for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end|Etenim Dominus habitabit in finem]]: not for an hour, or a short time, but to the end of the world, nay, for ever he will dwell with the Church of the elect, dwelling in them through faith and grace, as Christ promised: [[Matt 28:20|behold|Ecce]], he says, [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]].

paras.t: Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex. Versus iste primo de angelis sanctis exponitur. Invitat enim Propheta angelos ad exhibendum Christo ascendenti consortium, quoniam ad magnificentiam regis pertinet comitantium multitudo, juxta illud : In multitudine populi, dignitas regis ; in paucitate vero plebis, ignominia principis. Præmittit autem Propheta ad suum propositum quoddam exemplum de multitudine angelorum adsistentium in datione legis Mosaicæ, secundum quod in Deuteronomio scribitur : Dominus de Sinai venit, et de Seir ortus est nobis ; apparuit de monte Pharan, et cum eo Sanctorum millia, haud dubium quin angelorum sanctorum. Ait ergo : Currus Dei, id est numerus angelorum Deum in se recipientium, deferentium, atque ad humanas mentes Dei notitiam circumducentium, decem millibus multiplex, id est, decem millia angelorum intra se comprehendit : non quod hic exprimatur certus numerus angelorum sanctorum ; sed ponitur finitum pro infinito, seu determinatum pro indeterminato. Nam per millenarium, qui est numerus perfectionis, decies repetitum, insinuatur inæstimabilis multitudo angelorum sanctorum. Quemadmodum enim Dionysius docet, multitudo angelorum sanctorum omnem materialem atque sensibilem multitudinem incomparabiliter excedit. Et juxta hunc sensum apud Danielem scriptum est : Millia millium ministrabant ei. Millia lætantium, id est, multitudo angelorum in Deo gaudentium, indeterminata millia continet, prout Daniel subdit : Decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei. Dominus in eis, id est, associatus fuit ipsis, in Sinai, in sancto, id est in monte Sinai, qui est mons sanctus et locus sacratus. Angelus namque qui Moysi loquebatur, habebat Deum sibi adsistentem ; omnesque angeli dationi legis adsistentes, Deum sibi præsidentem habebant, sicut Moyses ait : Omnes Sancti in manu ejus sunt.
paras.en: [[67:18|The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands|Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex]]. This verse is first explained of the holy angels. For the Prophet invites the angels to give their company to Christ as he ascends, since a multitude of attendants belongs to the magnificence of a king, according to that saying: [[Prov 14:28|In the multitude of people is the dignity of the king: and in the small number of the people the dishonour of the prince.|In multitudine populi, dignitas regis ; in paucitate vero plebis, ignominia principis]] Now the Prophet sets before his purpose an example of the multitude of angels who stood by at the giving of the law of Moses, according to what is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 33:2|The Lord came from Sinai, and from Seir he rose up to us: he hath appeared from mount Pharan, and with him thousands of saints|Dominus de Sinai venit, et de Seir ortus est nobis ; apparuit de monte Pharan, et cum eo Sanctorum millia]], doubtless of holy angels. So he says: [[67:18|The chariot of God|Currus Dei]], that is, the number of the angels who receive God into themselves, bear him, and carry the knowledge of God round to the minds of men, [[67:18|is attended by ten thousands|decem millibus multiplex]], that is, it comprises within itself ten thousand angels [Latin *decem millibus multiplex*, "manifold by ten thousands"]: not that a fixed number of holy angels is expressed here, but the finite is put for the infinite, or the determinate for the indeterminate. For by the thousand, which is the number of perfection, repeated ten times, an inestimable multitude of holy angels is suggested. For, as Dionysius teaches, the multitude of the holy angels beyond compare exceeds every material and sensible multitude. And in this sense it is written in Daniel: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him|Millia millium ministrabant ei]]. [[67:18|thousands of them that rejoice|Millia lætantium]], that is, the multitude of angels rejoicing in God contains thousands without number, as Daniel adds: [[Dan 7:10|ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him|Decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei]]. [[67:18|the Lord is among them|Dominus in eis]], that is, he kept company with them, [[67:18|in Sina, in the holy place|in Sinai, in sancto]], that is, on Mount Sinai, which is a holy mountain and a consecrated place. For the angel who spoke to Moses had God standing by him; and all the angels who stood by at the giving of the law had God presiding over them, as Moses says: [[Deut 33:3|all the saints are in his hand|Omnes Sancti in manu ejus sunt]].

paras.t: Ex his infert Propheta, quod major debuit esse multitudo angelorum associantium se Christo ascendenti, subjungens : Ascendisti, o Christe, in altum, id est in cœlum empyreum ; cepisti captivitatem, id est, in limbo detentos et captos, atque in purgatorio sufficienter mundatos eripuisti antequam ascendebas, eosque tecum ducebas ; accepisti dona in hominibus : id est, tu, Christe, prout homo es, accepisti a Deo Patre seu tota superfelicissima Trinitate, dona seu gratias conferendas hominibus. Hæc dona anima Christi accepit a primo suæ creationis instanti, quia Christus semper plenus fuit gratia et veritate, et de plenitudine ejus omnes accepimus. Erat enim in Christo non solum gratia personalis unionis, gratia quoque beatæ fruitionis, sed etiam gratia capitis, per quam ipse omnibus suis membris, seu toti Ecclesiæ influere potest, et omnes ditare, quemadmodum post resurrectionem dixit, Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra : non quod tunc primo sibi præstita fuit ista potestas, sed quia ex tunc cœpit innotescere omnia esse Christo subjecta. Sic nunc ait Propheta de Christo, Ascendisti in altum, accepisti dona in hominibus : non quod in ascensione primo accepit charismata gratiarum hominibus distribuenda, sed quia ex tunc evidentissime cœpit patere Christum omni beatitudine ac plenitudine Spiritus Sancti esse impletum. Unde in signum perfectæ glorificationis Christi, datus est Spiritus Sanctus post ascensionem in signo visibili. Propter quod apud Joannem scriptum est : Nondum erat Spiritus datus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus. Etenim non credentes inhabitare Dominum Deum : id est, tu, Christe, accepisti hoc donum, videlicet non credentes, id est infideles, inhabitare Dominum. Christo enim merito suæ passionis est datum, ut per eum infideles converterentur ad fidem, sicque in illis habitaret Deus, in quibus ante inhabitabat diabolus.
paras.en: From this the Prophet infers that the multitude of angels keeping company with Christ as he ascended must have been greater, adding: [[67:19|Thou hast ascended|Ascendisti]], O Christ, [[67:19|on high|in altum]], that is, into the empyrean heaven; [[67:19|thou hast led captivity captive|cepisti captivitatem]], that is, thou didst rescue those held captive in limbo, and those sufficiently cleansed in purgatory, before thou didst ascend, and didst lead them with thee; [[67:19|thou hast received gifts in men|accepisti dona in hominibus]]: that is, thou, O Christ, as thou art man, hast received from God the Father, or from the whole most supremely blessed Trinity, gifts or graces to be bestowed on men. These gifts the soul of Christ received from the first instant of its creation, since Christ was always [[John 1:14|full of grace and truth|plenus fuit gratia et veritate]], and [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|de plenitudine ejus omnes accepimus]]. For in Christ there was not only the grace of personal union, and also the grace of blessed fruition [that is, of the beatific vision and enjoyment of God], but also the grace of the head [that is, the grace by which Christ, as head of the Church, pours grace into his members], by which he can flow into all his members, or into the whole Church, and enrich them all; as he said after the resurrection: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]: not that this power was then first granted him, but that from then on it began to be known that all things are subject to Christ. So the Prophet now says of Christ: [[67:19|Thou hast ascended on high|Ascendisti in altum]], [[67:19|thou hast received gifts in men|accepisti dona in hominibus]]: not that at the ascension he first received the gifts of graces to be distributed to men, but that from then on it began to be most evidently plain that Christ was filled with all beatitude and the fulness of the Holy Ghost. Hence, in token of Christ's perfect glorification, the Holy Ghost was given after the ascension in a visible sign[[Acts 2:4||]] [the margin gives Act. ii, 1–4]. Wherefore it is written in John: [[John 7:39|as yet the Spirit was not given, because Jesus was not yet glorified|Nondum erat Spiritus datus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus]]. [[67:19|Yea for those also that do not believe, the dwelling of the Lord God|Etenim non credentes inhabitare Dominum Deum]]: that is, thou, O Christ, hast received this gift, namely that unbelievers, that is, infidels, should have the Lord dwelling in them [Denis reads *non credentes inhabitare Dominum* as "that the Lord should dwell in those who do not believe"]. For it was given to Christ by the merit of his passion that through him infidels should be converted to the faith, and so God should dwell in those in whom the devil dwelt before.

paras.t: Porro Apostolus scripturam istam allegans, sensum magis quam verba inducit. Ait enim : Propter quod dicit : Ascendens in altum, captivam duxit captivitatem, dedit dona hominibus. Solent namque Christus et Evangelistæ atque Apostoli in allegatione Scripturarum veteris Testamenti, magis sententiam quam verba commemorare. Nec mirum, quoniam mentem Prophetarum clarissime cognoverunt, et eam magis quam verba attenderunt.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle, in citing this scripture, brings in the sense rather than the words. For he says: [[Eph 4:8|Wherefore he saith: Ascending on high, he led captivity captive: he gave gifts to men.|Propter quod dicit : Ascendens in altum, captivam duxit captivitatem, dedit dona hominibus]] For Christ and the Evangelists and Apostles are wont, in citing the Scriptures of the Old Testament, to recall the meaning rather than the words. Nor is this surprising, since they knew most clearly the mind of the Prophets, and attended to it more than to the words.

paras.t: Constat ergo ex præinductis, quod hoc loco nomine currus seu curruum, intelliguntur deiferi angeli, qui et sedes Dei dicuntur. Et ita accipiuntur currus, ubi Dominus ait ad Synagogam seu viros Israelitas : Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, in Africam et Lydiam, in Italiam et Græciam ; et adducent omnes fratres vestros in equis et quadrigis, in lecticis et mulis. Hæc namque vehicula spiritualiter exponenda sunt, quia intelliguntur per ea sanctorum angelorum ministeria, quibus cooperabantur Apostolis in Judæorum ac gentium conversione.
paras.en: It is clear, then, from what has been brought forward, that in this place by the name of chariot, or chariots, are understood the God-bearing angels, who are also called the seats of God. And chariots are taken in this way where the Lord says to the Synagogue, or to the men of Israel: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint]], [[Is 66:19|into Africa, and Lydia|in Africam et Lydiam]], [[Is 66:19|into Italy, and Greece|in Italiam et Græciam]]; and [[Is 66:20|they shall bring all your brethren|adducent omnes fratres vestros]] [[Is 66:20|upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and on mules|in equis et quadrigis, in lecticis et mulis]]. For these carriages are to be explained spiritually, since by them are understood the ministries of the holy angels, by which they worked together with the Apostles in the conversion of Jews and gentiles.

paras.t: Secundo autem exponitur quod dictum est, Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex, de sanctis hominibus. Superius namque dixit, Mons in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo : et hunc montem nominat currum, quia fideles Deum intra se portant, sicut ait Apostolus, Glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro ; vel ideo, quoniam Deus eos dirigit, sicut auriga dirigit currum. Unde Eliseus vocat Eliam currum Israel et aurigam ejus. Nam sicut pastor gregem suum portat ac dirigit, sic Elias filios Israel portavit atque direxit. Simili quoque modo rex Israel Eliseo morituro dixit : Pater mi, currus Israel et auriga ejus. Itaque, Currus Dei, id est populus fidelis, decem millibus multiplex, id est ex innumerabilibus populis, linguis ac tribubus constans et congregatus : nam ex omni genere hominum collecta est Christi Ecclesia. Maxime vero per currum Dei, intelliguntur Apostoli et successores eorum, qui nomen Salvatoris per totum mundum vehebant, sicut de Paulo ait Salvator : Vas electionis est mihi iste, ut portet nomen meum coram regibus et gentibus et filiis Israel. Et hic currus est decem millibus multiplex, id est per innumerabilia credentium millia multiplicatus. Dicitur enim aliquis multiplicari, per multiplicationem eorum quos vel spiritualiter vel carnaliter generat. Unde Dominus ait ad Jacob : Augebo et multiplicabo te. Millia lætantium, id est, multa et innumerabilia sunt millia fidelium hominum, qui in præsenti sæculo gloriantur in Domino, ex contemplatione bonitatis beneficiorumque ejus, ex spe quoque futurorum bonorum, et de omni spirituali profectu proximorum. Dominus in eis. Nam per caritatem et gratiam demoratur in ipsis : et hoc, in Sinai, id est in mandato seu observatione mandati in Sinai præstiti. Sinai enim interpretatur mandatum. In sancto, quia mandatum sanctum est ; vel, In sancto, quoniam sanctitas est ratio propter quam Deus in nobis manet. In illis enim Deus est, manet et habitat, qui suis mandatis obediunt, prout asserit Christus : Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit ; et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus.
paras.en: Secondly, what was said, [[67:18|The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands|Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex]], is explained of holy men. For above he said: [[67:17|A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell|Mons in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo]]; and he calls this mountain a chariot because the faithful carry God within themselves, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 6:20|Glorify and bear God in your body|Glorificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro]]; or else because God guides them, as a charioteer guides a chariot. Hence Eliseus calls Elias the chariot of Israel and its driver[[4 Kings 2:12||]]. For as a shepherd carries and guides his flock, so Elias carried and guided the children of Israel. In like manner the king of Israel said to Eliseus when he was about to die: [[4 Kings 13:14|O my father|Pater mi]], [[4 Kings 13:14|the chariot of Israel, and the guider thereof|currus Israel et auriga ejus]]. So [[67:18|The chariot of God|Currus Dei]], that is, the faithful people, [[67:18|is attended by ten thousands|decem millibus multiplex]], that is, made up and gathered from innumerable peoples, tongues and tribes: for the Church of Christ is gathered from every kind of men. But above all, by the chariot of God are understood the Apostles and their successors, who carried the name of the Saviour through the whole world[[Ps 18:5||]], as the Saviour says of Paul: This man [[Acts 9:15|is to me a vessel of election|Vas electionis est mihi]], [[Acts 9:15|to carry my name|ut portet nomen meum]] before kings and Gentiles and the children of Israel. And this chariot [[67:18|is attended by ten thousands|est decem millibus multiplex]], that is, multiplied by innumerable thousands of believers. For a man is said to be multiplied through the multiplying of those whom he begets, either spiritually or in the flesh. Hence the Lord says to Jacob: [[Gen 48:4|I will cause thee to increase and multiply|Augebo et multiplicabo te]]. [[67:18|thousands of them that rejoice|Millia lætantium]], that is, many and innumerable are the thousands of faithful men who in this present world glory in the Lord, from contemplating his goodness and his benefits, from the hope too of the good things to come, and from every spiritual progress of their neighbours. [[67:18|the Lord is among them|Dominus in eis]]. For by charity and grace he abides in them; and this [[67:18|in Sina|in Sinai]], that is, in the commandment, or in the keeping of the commandment given on Sinai. For Sinai is interpreted *commandment*. [[67:18|in the holy place|In sancto]], because the commandment is holy; or, [[67:18|in the holy place|In sancto]], because holiness is the reason for which God abides in us [*in sancto* can mean both "in the holy place" and "in what is holy"]. For God is in those, abides and dwells in those, who obey his commandments, as Christ declares: [[John 14:23|If any one love me, he will keep my word. And my Father will love him and we will come to him and will make our abode with him|Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit ; et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus]].

paras.t: Ascendisti, Domine Jesu, in altum, quemadmodum de te in Actis dicitur : Videntibus illis, elevatus est, et nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum ; et alio in loco, Elevatis manibus, benedixit eis, et ferebatur in cœlum. Cepisti captivitatem, id est, totum mundum, quantum in te est, eruisti de manu diaboli, qui eum propter reatum peccati tenebat captivum ; sed a te ejectus est foras, qui ais : Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum.
paras.en: [[67:19|Thou hast ascended|Ascendisti]], Lord Jesus, [[67:19|on high|in altum]], as is said of thee in the Acts: [[Acts 1:9|while they looked on, he was raised up: and a cloud received him out of their sight|Videntibus illis, elevatus est, et nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum]]; and in another place [that is, in the Gospel of Luke]: [[Luke 24:50|lifting up his hands, he blessed them|Elevatis manibus, benedixit eis]], and he [[Luke 24:51|was carried up to heaven|ferebatur in cœlum]]. [[67:19|thou hast led captivity captive|Cepisti captivitatem]], that is, thou hast rescued the whole world, as far as lies in thee, from the hand of the devil, who held it captive because of the guilt of sin; but he has been cast out by thee, who sayest: [[John 12:32|I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]].

67.title: PROSECUTIO EXPLANATIONIS PSALMI PRÆSENTIS.
67.title_en: Continuation of the explanation of the present psalm.

paras.t: Benedictus Dominus die quotidie. Hic agit Propheta de profectu Ecclesiæ. Tanquam dicat : Laudatus sit Deus, et glorificetur ab omnibus de die in diem, propter prædicta beneficia nobis collata, et item propter beneficia conferenda. Nam prosperum iter faciet nobis : id est, beatam atque securam viam veniendi ad vitam æternam nobis ostendet, illuminando corda nostra, et dirigendo opera nostra in ultimum finem, quemadmodum ipse ait : Faciam ut in præceptis meis ambuletis, et judicia mea custodiatis et operemini. Non enim potest homo rectam viam incedere sine gratia duce. Propter quod Salomon ait : Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus. Unde Apostolus etiam deprecatur : Ipse Deus dirigat corda vestra et intelligentias vestras, ut integer spiritus vester servetur in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Itaque, Prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum, id est auctor et finis salvationum seu beatitudinum nostrarum. Octo sunt enim beatitudines, quas enumerat Christus apud Matthæum ; totque nobis salvationes largitur, a quantis peccatis atque periculis nos salvare dignatur : et omnis nostra salus ab ipso dependet. Ideo sequitur :
paras.en: [[67:20|Blessed be the Lord day by day|Benedictus Dominus die quotidie]]. Here the Prophet treats of the progress of the Church. As if he said: May God be praised, and glorified by all from day to day, for the benefits already spoken of that have been bestowed on us, and likewise for the benefits yet to be bestowed. For he [[67:20|will make our journey prosperous to us|prosperum iter faciet nobis]]: that is, He will show us a blessed and safe way of coming to eternal life, enlightening our hearts and directing our works to the last end, as He Himself says: [[Ezech 36:27|I will cause you to walk in my commandments, and to keep my judgments, and do them|Faciam ut in præceptis meis ambuletis, et judicia mea custodiatis et operemini]]. For man cannot walk the right way without grace for his guide. Wherefore Solomon says: [[Prov 16:9|The heart of man disposeth his way: but the Lord must direct his steps.|Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus]] Hence the Apostle too prays: May God Himself [[2 Thess 3:5|direct your hearts|dirigat corda vestra]] and [[Phil 4:7|minds|intelligentias vestras]], [[1 Thess 5:23|that your whole spirit|ut integer spiritus vester]] may be preserved [[1 Thess 5:23|in the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ|in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]. And so He [[67:20|will make our journey prosperous to us|Prosperum iter faciet nobis]], [[67:20|the God of our salvation|Deus salutarium nostrorum]] [the Latin is plural, *salutarium*, "of our salvations"], that is, the author and end of our salvations or beatitudes. For there are eight beatitudes, which Christ enumerates in Matthew[[Matt 5:3||]]; and He grants us as many salvations as the sins and dangers from which He deigns to save us: and all our salvation depends on Him. Therefore there follows:

paras.t: Deus noster, scilicet Christus Jesus, seu Trinitas sancta, est Deus salvos faciendi, id est salvandi. Ideo namque in Evangelio loquitur : Non venit Filius hominis ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum. Et Deo proprium est salvare, juxta illud : Ego Dominus, et salvator non est præter me. Dicitur etiam, Deus noster, Deus salvos faciendi, quoniam omnes homines vult salvari, et ad veritatis notitiam pervenire, quemadmodum etiam in libro Tobiæ dicitur : Non delectaris in perditionibus nostris. Et in Evangelio ait Salvator : Non est voluntas ante Patrem ut pereat unus ex pusillis istis. Et Domini exitus mortis. Bis ponitur, Domini, propter expressionem majorem ; et est sensus : Exitus mortis, id est egressus de morte, videlicet liberatio a morte peccati atque gehennæ, est Domini sicut auctoris, justificatoris et redemptoris, quoniam ipse solus peccata dimittit, et pœnas æternas relaxat, gratiamque infundit. Vel per hoc quod ait, Et Domini Domini exitus mortis, dubitationem quamdam absolvit. Posset namque quis dicere, Si Deus est Deus salvandi, cur igitur morimur ? Ad quod respondet, hoc mirum non esse, quia et ipsius Domini, scilicet Jesu Christi, est exitus mortis, quoniam ipse per mortem hunc mundum exivit, et amarissimam mortem sustinuit. Dicitur ergo Deus, Deus salvos faciendi, quia a morte culpæ seu animæ eripit, atque a mortalitate corporis in die novissimo liberabit, quando mortale hoc induet immortalitatem. Propterea per Osee, De manu, inquit, mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos.
paras.en: [[67:21|Our God|Deus noster]], namely Christ Jesus, or the Holy Trinity, is [[67:21|the God of salvation|Deus salvos faciendi]] [literally, "the God of making safe"], that is, of saving. For this is why He says in the Gospel: The Son of man came not [[John 3:17|to judge the world: but that the world may be saved by him|ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum]] [Denis's wording; the Gospel has: God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world]. And it belongs to God to save, according to that saying: [[Osee 13:4|I am the Lord|Ego Dominus]], and [[Osee 13:4|there is no saviour beside me|salvator non est præter me]]. It is also said, [[67:21|Our God is the God of salvation|Deus noster, Deus salvos faciendi]], because He [[1 Tim 2:4|will have all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth|omnes homines vult salvari, et ad veritatis notitiam pervenire]], as it is also said in the book of Tobias: [[Tob 3:22|thou art not delighted in our being lost|Non delectaris in perditionibus nostris]]. And in the Gospel the Saviour says: [[Matt 18:14|it is not the will of your Father|Non est voluntas ante Patrem]] [[Matt 18:14|that one of these little ones should perish|ut pereat unus ex pusillis istis]]. [[67:21|and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death|Et Domini exitus mortis]]. *Of the Lord* is put twice for greater emphasis; and the sense is: [[67:21|the issues from death|Exitus mortis]], that is, the going out from death, namely deliverance from the death of sin and of hell, are *of the Lord* as their author, justifier and redeemer, since He alone forgives sins[[Mark 2:7||]], remits eternal punishments, and pours in grace. Or else, by saying [[67:21|and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death|Et Domini Domini exitus mortis]], he resolves a certain doubt. For someone might say: If God is the God of saving, why then do we die? To which he answers that this is no wonder, since the issues of death are also of the Lord Himself, that is, of Jesus Christ, for He went out of this world by death, and endured a most bitter death. God, then, is called the God of salvation because He rescues from the death of guilt, or of the soul, and on the last day will deliver from the mortality of the body, when [[1 Cor 15:54|this mortal hath put on immortality|mortale hoc induet immortalitatem]]. Therefore He says through Osee: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand|De manu]], He says, [[Osee 13:14|of death. I will redeem them from death|mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos]].

paras.t: Verumtamen Deus confringet capita inimicorum suorum, etc. Sequendo pro viribus sensum litteralem, quæ sequuntur sic exponenda sunt : Verumtamen, id est, quamvis Deus sit Deus salvandi, quantum in se est, non tamen salvat omnes, propter eorum malitiam, sed confringet capita, id est principales et capitaneos, inimicorum suorum, videlicet principes sacerdotum. Hos Deus confregit, omne spirituale esse ab eis tollendo, eosque excæcando et in æternum damnando. Verticem capilli perambulantium in delictis suis : id est, Deus confringet et destruet per exercitum Romanorum civitatem Jerusalem, quæ erat urbs perambulantium in delictis suis, id est habitatio Judæorum, qui Christum et Prophetas atque Apostolos occiderunt, persecuti sunt, sicut ad eos Stephanus dixit : Quem Prophetarum non sunt persecuti patres vestri? Dicitur autem Jerusalem vertex capilli, id est vertex capillosus, quoniam propter turres ac muros eam cingentes, inexpugnabilis videbatur, sicut et vertex capillosus robustus est. Nihilo minus fuit subversa, quemadmodum prædixerat Christus : Quia ad terram prosternent te, et non relinquent in te lapidem super lapidem.
paras.en: [[67:22|But God shall break the heads of his enemies|Verumtamen Deus confringet capita inimicorum suorum]], etc. Following the literal sense as far as we can, what follows is to be explained thus: [[67:22|But|Verumtamen]], that is, although God is the God of saving as far as in Him lies, yet He does not save all, because of their malice, but [[67:22|shall break the heads|confringet capita]], that is, the chiefs and captains, [[67:22|of his enemies|inimicorum suorum]], namely the chief priests. These God has broken, taking from them all spiritual being, blinding them and damning them for ever. [[67:22|the hairy crown of them that walk on in their sins|Verticem capilli perambulantium in delictis suis]]: that is, God will break and destroy, by the army of the Romans, the city of Jerusalem, which was the city [[67:22|of them that walk on in their sins|perambulantium in delictis suis]], that is, the dwelling of the Jews, who killed and persecuted Christ and the Prophets and Apostles[[Matt 23:37||]], as Stephen said to them: [[Acts 7:52|Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted?|Quem Prophetarum non sunt persecuti patres vestri?]] Now Jerusalem is called the crown of hair, that is, the hairy crown, because the towers and walls that girded it made it seem impregnable, just as a crown thick with hair is strong. Nevertheless it was overthrown, as Christ had foretold: They shall [[Luke 19:44|beat thee flat to the ground|ad terram prosternent te]], and [[Luke 19:44|they shall not leave in thee a stone upon a stone|non relinquent in te lapidem super lapidem]].

paras.t: Dixit Dominus : Ex Basan convertam. Basan terra erat vicina Judææ ex uno latere : mare autem Mediterraneum ex alio latere Judææ vicinum. Vespasianus vero et Titus, ab Imperatore contra Judæam (cujus metropolis erat Jerusalem) missi, ex utroque loco seu latere contraxerunt exercitum ad devastandum Judæam. Est igitur sensus : Dixit Dominus, quoniam ex divina ordinatione fiebat devastatio Jerusalem in ultionem sanguinis Christi : Ex Basan, id est ex illo loco, convertam exercitum versus Judæam. Convertam in profundum maris, id est, exercitum Romanorum dirigam ad mare, ut inde sibi auxilium capiant, sicque combinati in unum, Judæam suppeditent. Ut intingatur pes tuus, o habitator Jerusalem, seu pugnator Romane, in sanguine occisorum, quia tot millia occidebantur, quod in sanguine defluente poterant ambulantium intingi pedes. Lingua canum tuorum etiam intingi valebat ex inimicis ab ipso, id est ab ipso sanguine ex inimicis Christi occisis manante, ita ut canes sanguinem bibere possent ad satietatem. Nempe, ut Josephus scribit in libro de Judaico bello, a principio obsidionis usque ad finem, interfecti fuerunt decies centum millia.
paras.en: [[67:23|The Lord said|Dixit Dominus]]: [[67:23|I will turn them from Basan|Ex Basan convertam]]. Basan was a land bordering on Judæa on one side, while the Mediterranean Sea bordered Judæa on the other side. Now Vespasian and Titus, sent by the Emperor against Judæa (whose capital was Jerusalem), drew together an army from both places, or sides, to lay Judæa waste. So the sense is: [[67:23|The Lord said|Dixit Dominus]], since it was by divine ordinance that the devastation of Jerusalem came about, in vengeance for the blood of Christ: [[67:23|from Basan|Ex Basan]], that is, from that place, [[67:23|I will turn|convertam]] an army toward Judæa. [[67:23|I will turn them into the depth of the sea|Convertam in profundum maris]], that is, I will direct the army of the Romans to the sea, so that they may take help for themselves from there, and so, joined together into one, may trample Judæa underfoot. [[67:24|That thy foot may be dipped|Ut intingatur pes tuus]], O dweller in Jerusalem, or O Roman warrior, [[67:24|in the blood|in sanguine]] of the slain; for so many thousands were slain that the feet of those who walked there could be dipped in the blood flowing down. [[67:24|the tongue of thy dogs|Lingua canum tuorum]] too could be dipped [[67:24|of thy enemies|ex inimicis]], [[67:24|with the same|ab ipso]] [the Latin runs *ex inimicis, ab ipso*: "from the enemies, from the same"], that is, with the very blood flowing from the slain enemies of Christ, so that the dogs could drink blood their fill. For, as Josephus writes in his book on the Jewish war [the margin gives *De bello Judaico*, book VI, ch. 9], from the beginning of the siege to the end ten hundred thousand were killed.

paras.t: Deinde ponit Propheta causam tantæ dejectionis. Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus : id est, Judæi increduli et perversi viderunt opera tua, conversationem tuam atque miracula, Domine Jesu Christe, teque prædicantem audierunt ; sed converti et credere contempserunt : idcirco vastari et opprimi meruerunt. Et hoc est quod in Evangelio affirmas : Si non venissem, et locutus eis fuissem, peccatum non haberent ; nunc autem excusationem non habent. Et rursus : Si opera non fecissem in eis, quæ nemo alius fecit, peccatum non haberent ; nunc autem et viderunt, et oderunt et me et Patrem meum gratis. Viderunt ergo ingressus Dei mei, regis mei, qui est in sancto, id est Christi Unigeniti Dei Patris, qui est Deus meus et rex meus. Ecce in hoc versu apertissime declaratur incarnatio Dei et vera divinitas Christi.
paras.en: Next the Prophet gives the cause of so great a casting down. [[67:25|They have seen thy goings, O God|Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus]]: that is, the unbelieving and perverse Jews saw Thy works, Thy manner of life and Thy miracles, O Lord Jesus Christ, and heard Thee preaching; but they scorned to be converted and to believe: therefore they deserved to be laid waste and crushed. And this is what Thou affirmest in the Gospel: [[John 15:22|If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin: but now they have no excuse|Si non venissem, et locutus eis fuissem, peccatum non haberent ; nunc autem excusationem non habent]]. And again: [[John 15:24|If I had not done among them the works that no other man hath done, they would not have sin: but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father|Si opera non fecissem in eis, quæ nemo alius fecit, peccatum non haberent ; nunc autem et viderunt, et oderunt et me et Patrem meum]] without cause [*gratis*, which Denis adds from the next verse, John 15:25]. They saw, then, [[67:25|the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary|ingressus Dei mei, regis mei, qui est in sancto]], that is, of Christ, the Only-begotten of God the Father, who is my God and my king. See how in this verse the incarnation of God and the true divinity of Christ are most plainly declared.

paras.t: Prævenerunt principes conjuncti psallentibus, id est principales inter Christianos, videlicet sancti Apostoli aut successores eorum, conjuncti mente et corpore aliis Christianis psallentibus seu Deum laudantibus, in medio juvencularum tympanistriarum, id est virginum devotarum. A principio namque Ecclesiæ erant virgines aliquæ Deo sacratæ : quæ dicuntur tympanistriæ, non quod utebantur materialibus tympanis, sed quoniam cum Apostolis insistebant laudibus Creatoris. Sic itaque principes conjuncti psallentibus in medio virginum, prævenerunt et evaserunt prædictam obsidionem Jerusalem. Nam, ut in ecclesiastica historia scribitur, ex admonitione angeli exierunt Jerusalem et Judæam, ingredientes regnum Agrippæ, quod erat confœderatum Romanis.
paras.en: [[67:26|Princes went before joined with singers|Prævenerunt principes conjuncti psallentibus]], that is, the chief men among the Christians, namely the holy Apostles or their successors, joined in mind and body with the other Christians who sang psalms, or praised God, [[67:26|in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels|in medio juvencularum tympanistriarum]], that is, of devout virgins. For from the beginning of the Church there were some virgins consecrated to God: and they are called timbrel-players, not because they used material timbrels, but because together with the Apostles they gave themselves to the praises of the Creator. So, then, the princes joined with singers in the midst of the virgins *went before* [*prævenerunt*: went ahead, got away beforehand], and escaped the siege of Jerusalem just spoken of. For, as is written in the ecclesiastical history, at the warning of an angel they left Jerusalem and Judæa and entered the kingdom of Agrippa, which was in league with the Romans.

paras.t: In ecclesiis, id est congregationibus vestris, o Christifideles, benedicite Deo, eum laudando, Domino de fontibus Israel, id est, ipsi Domino vestro benedicite, de Apostolis, id est propter gratiosum illud beneficium quod dedit Apostolis, atque per eos vobis. Illuminatio namque et gratia eis collata, salus est mundi. Appellantur autem Apostoli fontes Israel, quia ex eis suscepit Ecclesia rivos doctrinæ, originemque virtutis ac gratiæ : et sicut Christus eis dixit. Vos estis lux mundi, sic dici possunt fontes Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[67:27|In the churches|In ecclesiis]], that is, in your congregations, O faithful of Christ, [[67:27|bless ye God|benedicite Deo]] by praising Him, [[67:27|the Lord, from the fountains of Israel|Domino de fontibus Israel]]: that is, bless the Lord your God Himself *from* the Apostles, that is, for that gracious benefit which He gave to the Apostles, and through them to you. For the light and grace bestowed on them is the salvation of the world. Now the Apostles are called the fountains of Israel because from them the Church received the streams of doctrine and the source of virtue and grace: and just as Christ said to them, [[Matt 5:14|You are the light of the world|Vos estis lux mundi]], so they can be called the fountains of the Church.

paras.t: Ibi, scilicet in Ecclesia, Benjamin adolescentulus, id est Paulus de tribu Benjamin natus, ut ipsemet ad Romanos fatetur, qui juvenis ad Christum conversus est, scilicet statim post Stephani occisionem. Vel dicitur adolescentulus, quoniam ultimo, respectu aliorum Apostolorum, venit ad fidem. In mentis excessu. Nam erat in Damasco tribus diebus ac noctibus, nec manducans, nec bibens, utpote raptus usque ad tertium cœlum, in quo audivit arcana verba : unde ab omni exercitio sensuum exteriorum fuit abstractus, præsertim quum in raptu illo credatur vidisse divinam essentiam.
paras.en: [[67:28|There|Ibi]], that is, in the Church, [[67:28|is Benjamin a youth|Benjamin adolescentulus]], that is, Paul, born of the tribe of Benjamin, as he himself declares to the Romans[[Rom 11:1||]], who was converted to Christ as a young man[[Acts 7:57||]], namely straight after the killing of Stephen[[Acts 9:1||]] [the margin gives Acts vii–ix: the young man Saul at Stephen's death, and his conversion]. Or he is called *a youth* because he came to the faith last in respect of the other Apostles. [[67:28|in ecstasy of mind|In mentis excessu]]. For he was in Damascus three days and nights, neither eating nor drinking[[Acts 9:9||]], since he had been [[2 Cor 12:2|caught up to the third heaven|raptus usque ad tertium cœlum]], where he [[2 Cor 12:4|heard secret words|audivit arcana verba]]: so he was drawn away from all use of the outward senses, especially since in that rapture he is believed to have seen the divine essence.

paras.t: Principes Juda, id est quidam Apostolorum ex tribu Juda orti, duces eorum, id est, duces ac principes exstiterunt hominum ad Christi fidem conversorum. Sicut enim Christus secundum humanitatem de tribu Juda fuit, sic Joannes et Jacobus major, itemque et Jacobus minor, Simon et Judas filii sororum Virginis gloriosæ, de tribu Juda nati creduntur : et isti, tanquam Apostoli, duces fuerunt Christianorum. Principes Zabulon, et principes Nephthali, id est, nonnulli ex tribu Zabulon Nephthalique exorti, duces fuerunt populi christiani. Quemadmodum namque habetur in libro Josue, tribus Zabulon et Nephthali sortes suas pro magna parte acceperunt in Galilæa, ex qua multi Apostolorum discipulorumque Christi fuerunt : propter quod Galilæi vocati sunt, sicut angelus ad eos ait : Viri Galilæi, quid admiramini?
paras.en: [[67:28|The princes of Juda|Principes Juda]], that is, certain of the Apostles sprung from the tribe of Juda, [[67:28|are their leaders|duces eorum]]: that is, they were the leaders and princes of the men converted to the faith of Christ. For just as Christ according to His humanity was of the tribe of Juda[[Luke 1:32||]], so John and James the Greater, and likewise James the Less, Simon and Jude, sons of the sisters of the glorious Virgin, are believed to have been born of the tribe of Juda: and these, as Apostles, were the leaders of the Christians. [[67:28|the princes of Zabulon|Principes Zabulon]], and [[67:28|the princes of Nephthali|principes Nephthali]]: that is, some sprung from the tribes of Zabulon and Nephthali were leaders of the Christian people. For, as is had in the book of Josue, the tribes of Zabulon[[Jos 19:10||]] and Nephthali[[Jos 19:32||]] received their lots for the most part in Galilee, from which many of the Apostles and disciples of Christ came: for which reason they were called Galileans, as the angel said to them: [[Acts 1:11|Ye men of Galilee|Viri Galilæi]], why do you wonder? [Denis has *quid admiramini*; the Vulgate reads, why stand you looking up to heaven?]

paras.t: Deinde Propheta in persona primitivæ Ecclesiæ loquens, precatur : Manda, Deus, virtuti tuæ, id est, potestati angelicæ præcipe, ut nos protegat atque promoveat : non enim humana virtute resistere Judæis aut prævalere valemus. Hanc orationem Deus exaudisse probatur ex multis locis Actuum Apostolorum. Angelus enim Petrum de carcere liberavit. Et de principibus sacerdotum scriptum est : Posuerunt Apostolos in custodia publica ; angelus autem Domini per noctem aperiens carcerem, eduxit eos. Confirma hoc, Deus, quod operatus es in nobis, id est, doctrinam apostolicam confirma miraculis, et corda credentium Spiritu Sancto corrobora, Ecclesiamque augeri ac perfici præsta, ut perficiatur opus fidei quod operatus es in nobis, id est per nos.
paras.en: Next the Prophet, speaking in the person of the early Church, prays: [[67:29|Command thy strength, O God|Manda, Deus, virtuti tuæ]], that is, give command to the angelic power to protect us and advance us: for by human strength we cannot withstand the Jews or prevail over them. That God heard this prayer is proved from many places of the Acts of the Apostles. For an angel freed Peter from prison[[Acts 12:7||]]. And of the chief priests it is written: They [[Acts 5:18|put them in the common prison|Posuerunt Apostolos in custodia publica]]; [[Acts 5:19|But an angel of the Lord by night, opening the doors of the prison and leading them out|angelus autem Domini per noctem aperiens carcerem, eduxit eos]]. [[67:29|confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us|Confirma hoc, Deus, quod operatus es in nobis]]: that is, confirm the apostolic teaching by miracles, strengthen the hearts of believers with the Holy Ghost, and grant that the Church be increased and made perfect, so that the work of faith may be perfected [[67:29|what thou hast wrought in us|quod operatus es in nobis]] [here, the work of faith], that is, through us.

paras.t: A templo tuo in Jerusalem : quia in templo illo Apostoli publice prædicaverunt Christum resurrexisse ; vel, A templo tuo in Jerusalem, id est a congregatione fidelium, qui primo in Jerusalem sunt collecti. Et est sensus : Confirma opus fidei, quod inchoasti a templo prædicto, quatenus fides quæ ibi incepit, per universum mundum discurrat. Hinc enim primitiva Ecclesia : Domine, inquit, respice in minas eorum, videlicet Judæorum, et da servis tuis cum omni fiducia loqui verbum tuum. Et quum orassent, motus est locus in quo erant ; et repleti sunt omnes Spiritu Sancto, et loquebantur verbum Dei cum magna fiducia. Tibi offerent reges munera. Multi reges ad fidem conversi, non solum se ipsos Christo obtulerunt, sed et munera copiosa dederunt, ad sustentationem indigentium et ædificationem ecclesiarum.
paras.en: [[67:30|From thy temple in Jerusalem|A templo tuo in Jerusalem]]: because in that temple the Apostles publicly preached that Christ had risen; or, [[67:30|From thy temple in Jerusalem|A templo tuo in Jerusalem]], that is, from the congregation of the faithful, who were first gathered together in Jerusalem. And the sense is: Confirm the work of faith which Thou hast begun from the temple just named, so that the faith which began there may run through the whole world. For hence the early Church says: [[Acts 4:29|Lord|Domine]], it says, [[Acts 4:29|behold their threatenings|respice in minas eorum]], namely of the Jews, [[Acts 4:29|and grant unto thy servants that with all confidence they may speak thy word|et da servis tuis cum omni fiducia loqui verbum tuum]]. [[Acts 4:31|And when they had prayed, the place was moved wherein they were assembled: and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost: and they spoke the word of God with confidence.|Et quum orassent, motus est locus in quo erant ; et repleti sunt omnes Spiritu Sancto, et loquebantur verbum Dei cum magna fiducia]] [Denis has *cum magna fiducia*, "with great confidence"] [[67:30|kings shall offer presents to thee|Tibi offerent reges munera]]. Many kings, converted to the faith, not only offered themselves to Christ but also gave abundant gifts, for the support of the needy and the building of churches.

paras.t: Insuper orat Propheta pro dejectione adversariorum Ecclesiæ. Increpa, Domine, dejice et castiga, feras arundinis, id est crudeles tyrannos atque hæreticos, qui omni vitio et vento doctrinæ circumferuntur, tanquam arundo vento agitata : qui feræ propter crudelitatem vocantur, tanquam dilaniatores animarum propriarum et aliorum. Hæ autem feræ præsertim fuerunt Imperatores Romani, videlicet Nero, Domitianus, Diocletianus, Decius, pluresque alii, qui fidem Christi penitus eradicare conati sunt. Congregatio taurorum, id est multitudo seu grex principum superborum, et indomitorum hæreticorum, Deum nequaquam timentium, demoratur et est in vaccis populorum, id est inter homines lascivos ac leves. Nam qualis princeps, tales et ministri ejus ; et qualis magister, tales discipuli. Vel, In vaccis populorum, id est inter homines ineruditos ac simplices, quos nituntur subvertere. Ideo sequitur, ut excludant a fide et regno Christi, eos qui probati sunt argento, id est divino eloquio eruditi, credendo et obediendo sermonibus Christi. Nomine namque argenti designatur sermo divinus, sicut superius dictum est : Eloquia Domini eloquia casta, argentum igne examinatum.
paras.en: Further, the Prophet prays for the casting down of the Church's adversaries. [[67:31|Rebuke|Increpa]], O Lord, cast down and chastise, [[67:31|the wild beasts of the reeds|feras arundinis]], that is, cruel tyrants and heretics, who are carried about by every vice and [[Eph 4:14|wind of doctrine|vento doctrinæ]], like a reed shaken by the wind: they are called wild beasts for their cruelty, as rending to pieces their own souls and those of others. Now these wild beasts were above all the Roman Emperors, namely Nero, Domitian, Diocletian, Decius, and many others, who tried to root out the faith of Christ entirely. [[67:31|the congregation of bulls|Congregatio taurorum]], that is, the multitude or herd of proud princes and untamed heretics who in no way fear God, lingers and is [[67:31|with the kine of the people|in vaccis populorum]] [*in vaccis*, literally "among the cows"], that is, among wanton and fickle men. For as the prince is, [[Ecclus 10:2|so also are his ministers|tales et ministri ejus]]; and as the master is, such are the disciples [a loose quotation of Ecclus 10:2]. Or, [[67:31|with the kine of the people|In vaccis populorum]], that is, among unlearned and simple men, whom they strive to overthrow. Therefore there follows: [[67:31|who seek to exclude|ut excludant]] from the faith and kingdom of Christ [[67:31|them who are tried with silver|eos qui probati sunt argento]], that is, those instructed in the divine word, by believing and obeying the words of Christ. For by the name of silver the divine word is signified, as was said above: [[Ps 11:7|The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried by the fire|Eloquia Domini eloquia casta, argentum igne examinatum]].

paras.t: Dissipa gentes quæ bella volunt : id est, prædictos tyrannos et hæresiarchas, et omnes bonorum persecutores, qui Ecclesiæ Dei lites et inquietudines concitant, destrue, impediendo eorum effectum ab opere malo, et paci Ecclesiæ providendo. Hoc nunc impletum conspicimus, quoniam tyrannos et hæresiarchas sopitos videmus.
paras.en: [[67:31|Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars|Dissipa gentes quæ bella volunt]]: that is, destroy the tyrants and heresiarchs just spoken of, and all persecutors of the good, who stir up strife and unrest for the Church of God, by keeping them from carrying out their evil work and by providing for the peace of the Church. This we now see fulfilled, since we see the tyrants and heresiarchs laid to rest.

paras.t: Venient legati ex Ægypto. Ad litteram, multi Ægyptiorum conversi, ad Christi Apostolos accesserunt in Jerusalem et in Romam, quatenus plenius instruerentur ab eis, sicut Dionysius scribit. Quidam vero exponunt istud de Philone, a quo liber Sapientiæ editus est : qui cum sociis suis ab Alexandria Ægypti missus est Romam ad Claudium imperatorem, et ibi cum beato Petro locutus est, et ei familiaris effectus. Unde Alexandriam rediens, Ecclesiam Marci evangelistæ discipuli sancti Petri, magnifice honoravit, atque de ejus præconiis librum conscripsit : quæ omnia in libro de Viris illustribus S. Hieronymus plenius enarravit. Æthiopia præveniet manus ejus, puta Ægypti, Deo, id est ad gloriam Dei. Nam prius ad fidem conversa est Æthiopia, quam Ægyptus, quoniam evangelista Matthæus filium regis Æthiopiæ defunctum suscitavit : quo facto, regem cum filio et filia magnaque populi parte convertit et baptizavit, ipsamque Æthiopiam ecclesiis adimplevit.
paras.en: [[67:32|Ambassadors shall come out of Egypt|Venient legati ex Ægypto]]. According to the letter, many of the Egyptians, once converted, came to the Apostles of Christ in Jerusalem and in Rome, to be more fully instructed by them, as Dionysius writes. But some explain this of Philo, by whom the book of Wisdom was put forth: he was sent with his companions from Alexandria in Egypt to Rome, to the emperor Claudius, and there he spoke with blessed Peter and became his friend. Hence, returning to Alexandria, he greatly honoured the Church of Mark the evangelist, the disciple of St Peter, and wrote a book in its praise: all of which St Jerome relates more fully in his book On Illustrious Men. [[67:32|Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands|Æthiopia præveniet manus ejus]], namely of Egypt [Denis reads *præveniet manus ejus* as "shall go before its hands", that is, Egypt's: Ethiopia will come to God before Egypt], [[67:32|to God|Deo]], that is, to the glory of God. For Ethiopia was converted to the faith before Egypt, since the evangelist Matthew raised to life the dead son of the king of Ethiopia: and when this was done he converted and baptized the king with his son and daughter and a great part of the people, and filled Ethiopia itself with churches.

paras.t: Deinceps hortatur Propheta totum mundum ad Christi ascendentis præconium. Regna terræ, id est populi omnium regnorum, cantate Deo, id est Christo, qui est universorum Creator, verusque Deus ac vita æterna ; psallite Domino Christo, omnium gubernatori ac principi. Psallite Deo qui ascendit quadragesimo die post resurrectionem, super cælum cæli, id est super summum cælum cujuscumque cæli contentivum. Christus namque ascendit usque ad extremitatem cæli empyrei. Ad orientem, id est usque ad dexteram Patris, qui est supersplendidissimus Oriens, omniumque luminum orientale atque fontale principium ; vel, Ad orientem, id est ab oriente, videlicet a monte Oliveti, qui est in orientali parte juxta Jerusalem.
paras.en: Then the Prophet exhorts the whole world to proclaim the praise of Christ ascending. [[67:33|ye kingdoms of the earth|Regna terræ]], that is, peoples of all kingdoms, [[67:33|Sing to God|cantate Deo]], that is, to Christ, who is the Creator of all things, and true God and life eternal; [[67:33|sing ye to the Lord|psallite Domino]] Christ, the ruler and prince of all. [[67:33|Sing ye to God|Psallite Deo]] [[67:34|Who mounteth|qui ascendit]] on the fortieth day after the resurrection [[67:34|above the heaven of heavens|super cælum cæli]], that is, above the highest heaven, which contains every heaven. For Christ ascended to the outermost bound of the empyrean heaven [that is, the highest heaven, the heaven of fire and light, the dwelling of the blessed]. [[67:34|to the east|Ad orientem]], that is, to the right hand of the Father, who is the super-resplendent East [*Oriens*: the east, the rising of the sun], the rising and fountain-source of all lights; or, [[67:34|to the east|Ad orientem]], that is, from the east, namely from Mount Olivet, which is on the eastern side near Jerusalem.

paras.t: Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtutis : id est, Christus sermones suos, quibus se ascensurum prædixit, ad effectum potenter perducet : sicut enim per Prophetas et per se ipsum prædixit, ita effecit. Dat enim voci suæ vocem virtutis, qui verba sua opere complet. Idcirco, o omnes fideles, date gloriam Deo, scilicet Christo ascendenti, super Israel, id est propter beneficia Apostolis aliisque fidelibus præstita, qui erant veri Israelitæ. Gloria autem est clara cum laude notitia : propterea Deo gloriam dare, est nomen ipsius aliis notificare cum professione laudis divinæ, sicut dum aliquis bonitatem Dei aut beneficia ejus prædicat et extollit.
paras.en: [[67:34|Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power|Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtutis]]: that is, Christ will powerfully bring to effect His words by which He foretold that He would ascend: for as He foretold through the Prophets and through Himself, so He accomplished it. For he gives [[67:34|to his voice the voice of power|voci suæ vocem virtutis]] who fulfils his words in deed. Therefore, all ye faithful, [[67:35|Give ye glory to God|date gloriam Deo]], namely to Christ ascending, [[67:35|for Israel|super Israel]], that is, for the benefits granted to the Apostles and to the other faithful, who were true Israelites[[John 1:47||]]. Now glory is a clear knowledge joined with praise: therefore to give glory to God is to make His name known to others, professing the divine praise, as when someone preaches and extols the goodness of God or His benefits.

paras.t: Magnificentia ejus et virtus ejus in nubibus, id est, magna operatio Christi atque potentia ejus apparuerunt in nube, in qua ascendit coram discipulis, sicut in Actibus dicitur : Videntibus illis, elevatus est, et nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum. Interdum namque Scriptura ponit plurale pro singulari, et converso : et ita nunc ponit, Nubibus, pro Nube. Et forte non solum erat nubes una ; sed sicut venturus est in nubibus, ita recessit in nubibus, præsertim quum in Actibus dicatur : Quemadmodum vidistis eum ascendentem in cœlum, sic veniet. Per nubes quoque intelligi possunt angeli sancti qui Christo ascendenti ministerium præbuerunt : in quibus magnificentia et virtus Christi relucebant, prout magnificentia et potestas regis relucet in dignitate et excellentia ministrorum, et quia duo angeli adstiterunt Apostolis, eisque magnificentiam et virtutem Christi annuntiaverunt, dicendo : Hic Jesus qui assumptus est a vobis in cœlum, sic veniet. Unde Dionysius quintodecimo capitulo de Cœlesti hierarchia dicit, quod in divinis Scripturis per nubes frequenter intelligantur angeli sancti. Denique per nubes accipi possunt Apostoli : de quibus scriptum est, Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant ? In his etenim nubibus refulgebant magnificentia Christi atque potentia, quando post ascensionem dedit eis os et sapientiam, cui non poterant resistere omnes inimici eorum, præsertim quum misit eis in igneis linguis Spiritum Sanctum. Propter quod sequitur :
paras.en: [[67:35|his magnificence, and his power is in the clouds|Magnificentia ejus et virtus ejus in nubibus]]: that is, the great working of Christ and His power appeared in the cloud in which He ascended before His disciples, as is said in the Acts: [[Acts 1:9|while they looked on, he was raised up: and a cloud received him out of their sight|Videntibus illis, elevatus est, et nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum]]. For Scripture sometimes puts the plural for the singular, and conversely: and so here it puts *clouds* for *cloud*. And perhaps there was not only one cloud; but as He will come in the clouds[[Matt 24:30||]], so He departed in the clouds, especially since it is said in the Acts: [[Acts 1:11|as you have seen him going into heaven|Quemadmodum vidistis eum ascendentem in cœlum]], he [[Acts 1:11|shall so come|sic veniet]]. By the clouds too can be understood the holy angels who did service to Christ as He ascended: in them the magnificence and power of Christ shone forth, as the magnificence and power of a king shines forth in the dignity and excellence of his ministers; and because two angels stood by the Apostles and announced to them the magnificence and power of Christ, saying: [[Acts 1:11|This Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come|Hic Jesus qui assumptus est a vobis in cœlum, sic veniet]]. Hence Dionysius says in the fifteenth chapter of the Celestial Hierarchy that in the divine Scriptures the holy angels are often understood by clouds. Lastly, by the clouds the Apostles can be understood: of whom it is written, [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant]]? For in these clouds the magnificence and power of Christ shone out, when after the ascension He gave them [[Luke 21:15|a mouth and wisdom|os et sapientiam]] which all their enemies could not resist, especially when He sent them the Holy Ghost[[Acts 2:4||]] in fiery tongues[[Acts 2:3||]]. For which reason there follows:

paras.t: Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis : quoniam mirabiliter magnificavit et exaltavit Apostolos et ceteros primitivæ Ecclesiæ filios, maxime illos centum viginti qui in die Pentecostes simul receperunt Spiritum Sanctum. In his itaque mirabilis fuit, quando in tantum confortavit corda eorum, ut qui passione instante omnes fugerunt, Spiritu Sancto recepto, eum publice prædicarent : eratque supermirabile in principe Apostolorum, ut qui ante passionem propter vocem ancillæ Christum negavit, post Spiritus Sancti adventum toti multitudini Judæorum intrepide diceret : Deus patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Jesum, quem vos quidem tradidistis, et negastis ante faciem Pilati ; et petistis virum homicidam donari vobis, sanctum vero et justum negastis, et auctorem vitæ interfecistis. Sed hæc est mutatio dexteræ Excelsi. Ideo subditur : Deus Israel ipse dabit virtutem et fortitudinem plebi suæ, videlicet primitivæ Ecclesiæ. Dedit namque eis virtutem constanter loquendi, miracula faciendi, et irreprehensibiliter conversandi ; fortitudinem quoque cuncta adversa non solum æquanimiter, sed etiam exsultanter sustinendi, quemadmodum in Actibus scriptum est : Ibant Apostoli gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati.
paras.en: [[67:36|God is wonderful in his saints|Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis]]: for He wonderfully magnified and exalted the Apostles and the other sons of the early Church, above all those hundred and twenty who together received the Holy Ghost on the day of Pentecost. In these, then, He was wonderful, when He so strengthened their hearts that they who had all fled when the passion was at hand[[Matt 26:56||]], once they had received the Holy Ghost, preached Him publicly[[Acts 4:33||]]: and it was more than wonderful in the prince of the Apostles that he who before the passion denied Christ at the voice of a maidservant[[Matt 26:69||]], after the coming of the Holy Ghost said fearlessly to the whole multitude of the Jews: [[Acts 3:13|the God of our fathers, hath glorified his Son Jesus, whom you indeed delivered up and denied before the face of Pilate|Deus patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Jesum, quem vos quidem tradidistis, et negastis ante faciem Pilati]]; [[Acts 3:14|and desired a murderer to be granted unto you|et petistis virum homicidam donari vobis]]; [[Acts 3:14|But you denied the Holy One and the Just|sanctum vero et justum negastis]], and [[Acts 3:15|the author of life you killed|auctorem vitæ interfecistis]]. But [[Ps 76:11|this is the change of the right hand of the most High|hæc est mutatio dexteræ Excelsi]]. Therefore there is added: [[67:36|the God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people|Deus Israel ipse dabit virtutem et fortitudinem plebi suæ]], namely to the early Church. For He gave them power to speak steadfastly, to work miracles, and to live blamelessly; and strength too to bear all adversities not only with an even mind but even with exultation, as is written in the Acts: [[Acts 5:41|they indeed went from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus|Ibant Apostoli gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati]].

paras.t: Propter tantorum gratiam beneficiorum Christifidelibus concessorum, sit in æternum benedictus Deus, cui pro donis suis nihil dignum rependere possumus, quoniam bonorum nostrorum non eget : præcipue quum omnia nostra bona ejus sint dona, quemadmodum David devotissime ait, Tua, Domine, sunt omnia, et quæ de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi. Sed hoc nobis incumbit, ut soli Deo honorem et gloriam impendamus, eum dignissime venerando, omneque bonum ipsi attribuendo, sicut et sanctus David fecit, dicendo : Nunc ergo, Deus noster, confitemur tibi, et laudamus nomen tuum inclytum. Tua est, Domine, magnificentia et potestas et gloria atque victoria ; tibi laus, tuæ divitiæ, tu dominaris omnium.
paras.en: For the grace of such great benefits granted to the faithful of Christ, [[67:36|Blessed be God|benedictus Deus]] for ever, to whom we can repay nothing worthy of His gifts, since He has no need of our goods[[Ps 15:2||]]: above all since all our goods are His gifts, as David most devoutly says: [[1 Par 29:14|all things are thine|Tua, Domine, sunt omnia]], O Lord: [[1 Par 29:14|and we have given thee what we received of thy hand|et quæ de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi]]. But this is our duty, to render [[1 Tim 1:17|honour and glory|honorem et gloriam]] to [[1 Tim 1:17|the only God|soli Deo]], venerating Him most worthily and attributing every good to Him, as holy David also did, saying: [[1 Par 29:13|Now therefore our God we give thanks to thee, and we praise thy glorious name.|Nunc ergo, Deus noster, confitemur tibi, et laudamus nomen tuum inclytum]] [[1 Par 29:11|Thine, O Lord, is magnificence, and power, and glory, and victory: and to thee is praise|Tua est, Domine, magnificentia et potestas et gloria atque victoria ; tibi laus]]; [[1 Par 29:12|Thine are riches|tuæ divitiæ]], [[1 Par 29:12|thou hast dominion over all|tu dominaris omnium]].

paras.t: Porro quæ dicta sunt ab illo loco, Verumtamen Deus confringet capita inimicorum suorum, spiritualius atque communius intelligi possunt hoc modo: Verumtamen, id est, quamvis Deus sit Deus salvos faciendi, nihilo minus ipse conquassabit ac destruet capita inimicorum suorum. A parte totum significat, quemadmodum Philistæi dixerunt regi suo de David: Quomodo melius poterit placare dominum suum, nisi in capitibus nostris? Est itaque sensus: Deus, vel in præsenti, vel saltem in futuro, inimicos suos confringet, ulciscendo peccata eorum, eosque nunc occidendo, aut postmodum condemnando. Vel sic: Deus confringet capita inimicorum suorum, id est, superbiam eorum humiliabit, deprimet et damnabit, juxta illud Isaiæ: Dies Domini super omnem superbum et excelsum, et super omnem arrogantem, et humiliabitur. Et per alium Prophetam: Visitabo super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur.
paras.en: Moreover, what has been said from the place [[67:22|But God shall break the heads of his enemies|Verumtamen Deus confringet capita inimicorum suorum]] onward can be understood more spiritually and more generally in this way: [[67:22|But|Verumtamen]], that is, although God is [[67:21|the God of salvation|Deus salvos faciendi]], none the less he will shatter and destroy [[67:22|the heads of his enemies|capita inimicorum suorum]]. He signifies the whole by the part [that is, the head stands for the whole man], as the Philistines said to their king about David: [[1 Kings 29:4|how can he otherwise appease his master, but with our heads?|Quomodo melius poterit placare dominum suum, nisi in capitibus nostris?]] The sense, then, is: God, either in the present or at least in the future, will break his enemies, avenging their sins, slaying them now or condemning them hereafter. Or thus: [[67:22|God shall break the heads of his enemies|Deus confringet capita inimicorum suorum]], that is, he will humble their pride, bring it low and condemn it, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 2:12|the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and highminded, and upon every one that is arrogant, and he shall be humbled|Dies Domini super omnem superbum et excelsum, et super omnem arrogantem, et humiliabitur]]. And by another Prophet: [[Soph 1:9|I will visit in that day upon every one that entereth arrogantly|Visitabo super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur]].

paras.t: Confringet etiam Deus verticem capilli, id est excellentiam cogitationis, perambulantium in delictis suis, id est perseverantium in peccatis. Unde alibi scriptum est: Væ qui cogitatis inutile. Et Isaias ait: Incurvabitur sublimitas hominum, et humiliabitur altitudo virorum. Sic ergo non solum superbiam actionum, sed etiam extollentiam cogitationum Deus confringet, quemadmodum Sapientia, Omnium, inquit, excellentium et sublimium colla virtute propria calcavi. Hinc et alia scriptura ait: Quid te elevat cor tuum, et quasi magna cogitans attonitos habes oculos? Quid tumet contra Deum spiritus tuus? Nomine autem capilli, cogitatio designatur: quoniam sicut capillus ex capite nascitur, et ei adhæret, sic cogitatio procedit ex corde, et adhæret eidem.
paras.en: God will also break [[67:22|the hairy crown|verticem capilli]], that is, the loftiness of thought, [[67:22|of them that walk on in their sins|perambulantium in delictis suis]], that is, of those who persevere in sins. Hence it is written elsewhere: [[Mich 2:1|Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable|Væ qui cogitatis inutile]]. And Isaias says: [[Is 2:17|the loftiness of men shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be humbled|Incurvabitur sublimitas hominum, et humiliabitur altitudo virorum]]. So God will break not only the pride of deeds but also the exaltation of thoughts, as Wisdom says: [[Ecclus 24:11|by my power I have trodden under my feet the hearts of all the high and low|Omnium, inquit, excellentium et sublimium colla virtute propria calcavi]] [Denis's wording: "I have trodden by my own power on the necks of all the excellent and lofty"]. Hence another scripture also says: [[Job 15:12|Why doth thy heart elevate thee, and why dost thou stare with thy eyes, as if they were thinking great things?|Quid te elevat cor tuum, et quasi magna cogitans attonitos habes oculos?]] [[Job 15:13|Why doth thy spirit swell against God|Quid tumet contra Deum spiritus tuus]]? Now by the name of *hair* [capillus; the Latin of the verse reads literally "the crown of the hair"] thought is signified: for as hair grows out of the head and clings to it, so thought proceeds from the heart and clings to it.

paras.t: Dixit Dominus, id est, intra se immobiliter decrevit, atque per servos suos locutus est. Non enim faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas. Ex Basan, id est ex immunditia vitæ et confusione peccati, convertam peccatores, quatenus qui ante turpiter et inordinate vixerunt, implere incipiant illud Apostoli: Omnia autem honeste et secundum ordinem fiant in vobis. Basan enim turpitudo seu confusio interpretatur. Convertam in profundum maris: id est, gratiam conversionis mittam in hoc sæculum nequam, in corda obstinata, in gentilitatem olim fluctibus vitiorum submersam. Propter quod Petrus ait: Redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis pretioso sanguine quasi Agni immaculati. Et Paulus apertius loquens: Tempora, ait, prioris ignorantiæ despiciens Deus, nunc annuntiat hominibus ut omnes ubique pœnitentiam agant. Unde et ipse Salvator de se ipso fatetur: Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum.
