paras.en: [[67:23|The Lord said|Dixit Dominus]], that is, decreed unchangeably within himself, and spoke through his servants. For [[Amos 3:7|the Lord God doth nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets|Non enim faciet Dominus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos Prophetas]]. [[67:23|from Basan|Ex Basan]], that is, out of uncleanness of life and the confusion of sin, [[67:23|I will turn|convertam]] sinners, so that those who before lived foully and without order may begin to fulfil that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 14:40|let all things be done decently and according to order|Omnia autem honeste et secundum ordinem fiant]] among you. For *Basan* is interpreted "foulness" or "confusion". [[67:23|I will turn them into the depth of the sea|Convertam in profundum maris]]: that is, I will send the grace of conversion into this wicked world, into obstinate hearts, into the gentile world once drowned in the waves of vices. For which reason Peter says: You were redeemed [[1 Pet 1:18|from your vain conversation of the tradition of your fathers|de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis]] with [[1 Pet 1:19|the precious blood|pretioso sanguine]] [[1 Pet 1:19|as of a lamb unspotted|quasi Agni immaculati]]. And Paul, speaking more openly, says: [[Acts 17:30|God indeed having winked at the times of this ignorance, now declareth unto men that all should every where do penance|Tempora, ait, prioris ignorantiæ despiciens Deus, nunc annuntiat hominibus ut omnes ubique pœnitentiam agant]]. Hence the Saviour himself also declares of himself: [[John 3:17|God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world: but that the world may be saved by him|Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum]].

paras.t: Ut intingatur pes tuus in sanguine: id est, ad hoc Deus convertet te, o homo, ut desiderium tuum, seu actio tua, effectum et fructum sanguinis Christi consequatur, ita ut merito passionis Christi salveris, unitus, imo intinctus sanguine Christi per fidem et caritatem. Unde ait Apostolus: Vos qui eratis longe, facti estis prope in sanguine Christi. Lingua canum tuorum ex inimicis ab ipso: id est, lingua est ex infidelibus atque gentilibus ad fidem conversi; et hoc factum est ab ipso omnium Salvatore Jesu Christo, cujus pietate et gratia ex inimicis fiunt amici. Multi siquidem gentilium olim Christo contrarii, fide recepta, facti sunt prædicatores fortissimi, ut sacratissimus Dionysius, Clemens Papa, divinus Ignatius, magnus ille Polycarpus. Tales autem dicuntur fuisse inimici, secundum præsentem malitiam, seu propriorum meritorum exigentiam; secundum vero prædestinationem æternam, semper fuerunt amici, quia de talibus loquitur Christus: Majorem hac dilectionem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis. Et Apostolus dicit: Quum adhuc inimici essemus, reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem Filii sui. Erant igitur amici et inimici secundum diversos respectus.
paras.en: [[67:24|That thy foot may be dipped in the blood|Ut intingatur pes tuus in sanguine]]: that is, God will turn thee, O man, to this end, that thy desire, or thy action, may obtain the effect and fruit of the blood of Christ, so that thou mayest be saved by the merit of Christ's passion, united, nay dipped, in the blood of Christ through faith and charity. Hence the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:13|you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh by the blood of Christ|Vos qui eratis longe, facti estis prope in sanguine Christi]]. [[67:24|the tongue of thy dogs|Lingua canum tuorum]] from the enemies, by him [the Latin, ex inimicis ab ipso, reads literally "from the enemies, by him"; the Douay-Rheims has "be red with the same"]: that is, the tongue is that of one converted to the faith from among the unbelievers and gentiles; and this was done by him, Jesus Christ, the Saviour of all, by whose kindness and grace enemies become friends. For many of the gentiles who were once opposed to Christ became, on receiving the faith, most valiant preachers, such as the most holy Dionysius, Pope Clement, the divine Ignatius, the great Polycarp. Such men are said to have been enemies according to their malice at the time, or what their own deserts called for; but according to eternal predestination they were always friends, for of such Christ speaks: [[John 15:13|Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends|Majorem hac dilectionem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis]]. And the Apostle says: [[Rom 5:10|when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son|Quum adhuc inimici essemus, reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem Filii sui]]. They were therefore friends and enemies in different respects.

paras.t: Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus: id est, fideles per fidem consideraverunt conversationem tuam, Domine Christe, suntque secuti vestigia tua sanguinem effundendo, vel se ipsos quotidie mortificando, abnegando, et crucem suam post te bajulando. Viderunt etiam oculo contemplationis purissimæ ingressus tuos, id est incarnationem qua mundum intrasti, ascensionem qua cœlum introiisti, apparitiones quoque quibus post resurrectionem Apostolis apparendo, ingressus es conclave ostiis clausis, atque descensum ad inferos.
paras.en: [[67:25|They have seen thy goings, O God|Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus]]: that is, the faithful have by faith considered thy way of life, O Lord Christ, and have followed thy footsteps by shedding their blood, or by daily mortifying and denying themselves and carrying their cross after thee[[Luke 9:23||]]. They have also seen with the eye of most pure contemplation [[67:25|thy goings|ingressus tuos]], that is, the incarnation by which thou didst enter the world, the ascension by which thou didst enter heaven, the appearances too by which, appearing to the Apostles after the resurrection, thou didst enter the room with the doors shut[[John 20:19||]][[John 20:26||]], and the descent into hell[[Eph 4:9||]].

paras.t: Prævenerunt, id est, in omni opere bono alios præcesserunt, principes, id est prælati Ecclesiæ, conjuncti psallentibus, id est ovibus sibi commissis, Deum laudantibus, in medio juvencularum tympanistriarum, id est animarum devotarum: de quibus in Canticis dicitur, Adolescentularum non est numerus. Dicuntur namque animæ Christo per fidem et caritatem desponsatæ, juvenculæ, propter spiritualem juventutem interioris reformationis et gratiæ. De qua ait Apostolus: Licet is qui foris est noster homo, corrumpatur; tamen is qui intus est, renovatur de die in diem. Dicuntur quoque tympanistriæ, quoniam per labores pœnitentiæ et mortificationem carnis propriæ, dulciter in auribus Dei sonant, eumque gratissime laudant, quemadmodum ipse cuilibet animæ tali dicit: Sonet vox tua in auribus meis: vox enim tua dulcis. Itaque, Prævenerunt principes conjuncti psallentibus: et hoc est quod omni prælato ait Apostolus, Esto exemplum fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate.
paras.en: [[67:26|went before|Prævenerunt]], that is, went ahead of others in every good work, [[67:26|Princes|principes]], that is, the prelates of the Church, [[67:26|joined with singers|conjuncti psallentibus]], that is, with the sheep entrusted to them, praising God, [[67:26|in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels|in medio juvencularum tympanistriarum]], that is, of devout souls: of whom it is said in the Canticles, [[Cant 6:7|young maidens without number|Adolescentularum non est numerus]]. For souls espoused to Christ through faith and charity are called *young damsels* because of the spiritual youth of inward renewal and grace, of which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 4:16|though our outward man is corrupted, yet the inward man is renewed day by day|Licet is qui foris est noster homo, corrumpatur; tamen is qui intus est, renovatur de die in diem]]. They are also called *players on timbrels* [tympanistriæ, women who beat the timbrel], because through the labours of penance and the mortification of their own flesh they sound sweetly in God's ears and praise him most gratefully, as he himself says to every such soul: [[Cant 2:14|let thy voice sound in my ears: for thy voice is sweet|Sonet vox tua in auribus meis: vox enim tua dulcis]]. And so, [[67:26|Princes went before joined with singers|Prævenerunt principes conjuncti psallentibus]]: and this is what the Apostle says to every prelate, [[1 Tim 4:12|be thou an example of the faithful, in word, in conversation, in charity|Esto exemplum fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate]].

paras.t: In ecclesiis, id est in congregationibus catholicorum virorum, non in conventiculis hæreticorum, schismaticorum aut malignorum, a quibus omnino fugiendum est: benedicite Deo Domino de fontibus Israel, id est propter fontes Israel, utpote propter gratiam doctoribus atque pastoribus Ecclesiarum collatam: quos Deus implevit donis Spiritus Sancti, sapientia, intellectu, consilio, fortitudine, scientia, pietate, timore, ita ut ex eis quasi ex fontibus, inferiores sortiantur ac hauriant fluenta doctrinæ, exempla virtutum, gratiamque divinam.
paras.en: [[67:27|In the churches|In ecclesiis]], that is, in the congregations of catholic men, not in the conventicles of heretics, schismatics or the wicked, which are to be shunned altogether: [[67:27|bless ye God the Lord, from the fountains of Israel|benedicite Deo Domino de fontibus Israel]], that is, for the sake of the fountains of Israel [Denis takes *de* ("from") as "on account of"], namely for the grace bestowed on the doctors and pastors of the Churches, whom God has filled with the gifts of the Holy Ghost, wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, godliness and fear[[Is 11:2||]][[Is 11:3||]], so that from them as from fountains those beneath them may obtain and draw streams of doctrine, examples of virtue, and divine grace.

paras.t: Ibi, id est in unitate Ecclesiæ. Benjamin adolescentulus, id est filius dexteræ, scilicet filius Dei adoptivus, in gratia Dei incessanter proficiens: cui Deus est dexter, id est favens et pius, in eo per gratiam habitans. De tali etenim Benjamin in Deuteronomio scriptum est: Amantissimus Domini habitabit confidenter, in eo quasi in thalamo tota die commorabitur, et inter humeros illius requiescet. Talis est omnis qui gratiæ Dei totus innitur, cujus anima beneplacita est Deo: cui convenit quod Dominus per Aggæum ait, Assumam te, serve meus, et ponam te quasi signaculum, quia te elegi. Principes Juda duces eorum, principes Zabulon, principes Nephthali. Juda interpretatur confessio; Zabulon autem, habitaculum fortitudinis: Nephthali vero, dilatatio mea. Est igitur sensus: Principes christianæ confessionis sunt duces eorum, videlicet Christianorum. Hi enim principes sunt prælati Ecclesiæ, et maxime martyres sancti, qui primo et eminentius nomen Christi coram hominibus sunt confessi: idcirco aliorum constituti sunt duces, incumbitque nobis eorum imitari exempla. Sed et principes Zabulon, id est principes spiritualis fortitudinis, qui in virtutibus stabiliti sunt, et inavertibiliter Deo adhærent; et principes Nephthali, id est dilatationis, quorum corda per caritatem dilatantur ad Deum et proximum, Deum brachiis dilectionis recipiendo, amplectendo et reservando, proximis quoque per caritatem in omnibus succurrendo. Hi tales sunt duces ovium Christi. Vere enim digni sunt præesse, qui istis ornantur virtutibus. Confessio pertinet ad fidem, fortitudo ad spem, dilatatio ad caritatem.
paras.en: [[67:28|There|Ibi]], that is, in the unity of the Church, [[67:28|is Benjamin a youth|Benjamin adolescentulus]], that is, the son of the right hand, namely the adopted son of God, ever advancing in the grace of God: to whom God is on the right hand [dexter, which means both "on the right" and "favourable"], that is, favourable and kind, dwelling in him by grace. For of such a Benjamin it is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 33:12|The best beloved of the Lord shall dwell confidently in him: as in a bride chamber shall he abide all the day long, and between his shoulders shall be rest|Amantissimus Domini habitabit confidenter, in eo quasi in thalamo tota die commorabitur, et inter humeros illius requiescet]]. Such is everyone who leans wholly on the grace of God, whose soul is well pleasing to God: to whom applies what the Lord says through Aggeus, [[Agg 2:24|I will take thee|Assumam te]], [[Agg 2:24|my servant|serve meus]], [[Agg 2:24|and will make thee as a signet, for I have chosen thee|et ponam te quasi signaculum, quia te elegi]]. [[67:28|The princes of Juda are their leaders: the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali|Principes Juda duces eorum, principes Zabulon, principes Nephthali]]. *Juda* is interpreted "confession"; *Zabulon*, "dwelling of strength"; and *Nephthali*, "my enlarging". The sense, then, is: the princes of Christian confession are their leaders, namely the leaders of the Christians. For these princes are the prelates of the Church, and above all the holy martyrs, who first and most eminently confessed the name of Christ before men: therefore they have been made the leaders of others, and it is our duty to imitate their examples. And also the princes of Zabulon, that is, the princes of spiritual strength, who are established in the virtues and cleave to God without turning away; and the princes of Nephthali, that is, of enlarging, whose hearts are enlarged by charity towards God and their neighbour, receiving, embracing and keeping God in the arms of love, and helping their neighbours in all things through charity. Such as these are the leaders of Christ's sheep. For those who are adorned with these virtues are truly worthy to be set over others. Confession belongs to faith, strength to hope, enlarging to charity.

paras.t: Manda, Deus, virtuti tuæ; confirma hoc, Deus, quod operatus es in nobis. Hæc est oratio optima, quam Ecclesia omnisque fidelis Deo offerre potest et debet, deprecando ut Deus virtutem angelicam ad suam custodiam mittat, quemadmodum Tobias dixit: Bene ambuletis, et sit Dominus in itinere vestro, et angelus ejus comitetur vobiscum. Orare quoque debemus ut Deus bonum, quod ipse in nobis gratiose incipit, pie corroboret, et ad finem securum cum jugi profectu perducat. Ideo enim Paulus: Optimum (inquit) est gratia stabiliri cor.
paras.en: [[67:29|Command thy strength, O God confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us|Manda, Deus, virtuti tuæ; confirma hoc, Deus, quod operatus es in nobis]]. This is the best prayer, which the Church and every faithful soul can and ought to offer to God: praying that God may send angelic *strength* [virtus, "strength" or "power", a word also used of the angels] to keep them, as Tobias said: [[Tob 5:21|May you have a good journey, and God be with you in your way, and his angel accompany you|Bene ambuletis, et sit Dominus in itinere vestro, et angelus ejus comitetur vobiscum]]. We ought also to pray that God may lovingly strengthen the good that he himself graciously begins in us, and bring it to a safe end with continual progress. For this is why Paul says: [[Heb 13:9|it is best|Optimum]] (he says) [[Heb 13:9|that the heart be established with grace|est gratia stabiliri cor]].

paras.t: A templo tuo in Jerusalem. Deus enim in cœlesti Jerusalem seu triumphanti Ecclesia habitans, operatur in nobis quidquid boni agimus et habemus, juxta illud: Omnia opera nostra operatus es nobis. Et Apostolus: Deus est qui operatur in vobis et velle et perficere, pro bona voluntate. Et hæc operatur Deus in nobis, a templo cœlestis Jerusalem, quoniam inde nobis transmittit angelos sanctos, munera gratiarum secum portantes, nosque ad superna erigentes. Tibi offerent reges, id est omnes Christiani, qui sunt genus regium et sacerdotale, qui dominantur animo proprio, et rationis imperium fortiter prosequuntur: munera, id est sacras hostias, preces devotas, eleemosynas largas, spontaneumque obsequium, imo se ipsos.
paras.en: [[67:30|From thy temple in Jerusalem|A templo tuo in Jerusalem]]. For God, dwelling in the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Church triumphant, works in us whatever good we do and have, according to that saying: [[Is 26:12|thou hast wrought all our works for us|Omnia opera nostra operatus es nobis]]. And the Apostle: [[Phil 2:13|it is God who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish, according to his good will|Deus est qui operatur in vobis et velle et perficere, pro bona voluntate]]. And God works these things in us from the temple of the heavenly Jerusalem, since from there he sends us the holy angels, who bring the gifts of graces with them and lift us up to the things above. [[67:30|To thee|Tibi]] [[67:30|kings shall offer|offerent reges]], that is, all Christians, who are a kingly and priestly race[[1 Pet 2:9||]], who rule over their own minds and steadfastly follow the command of reason, [[67:30|presents|munera]], that is, sacred offerings, devout prayers, generous alms and willing service, nay, themselves.

paras.t: Increpa feras arundinis, etc. Hunc versum cum parte versus sequentis, dicere quilibet potest secundum explanationem inductam, orando pro conservatione Ecclesiæ et repressione adversariorum ipsius.
paras.en: [[67:31|Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds|Increpa feras arundinis]], etc. This verse, with part of the following verse [perhaps "Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars", which in the numbering used here ends v. 31], anyone can say according to the explanation given above, praying for the preservation of the Church and the repression of her adversaries.

paras.t: Regna terræ, cantate Deo. Unusquisque nostrum zelo divini honoris accensus, omnes fideles ad Dei præconium, quantum valet, inducere et incendere debet, recolendo ardenter beneficia ejus: et si solus est, potest ista in persona Ecclesiæ dicere, omnes alloquendo fideles; respicietque Deus bonitatem sui affectus, nec illum infructuosum relinquet.
paras.en: [[67:33|Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth|Regna terræ, cantate Deo]]. Each one of us, kindled with zeal for God's honour, ought, as far as he can, to lead and fire all the faithful to the praise of God, ardently calling to mind his benefits: and if he is alone, he can say these words in the person of the Church, addressing all the faithful; and God will look upon the goodness of his affection and will not leave it fruitless.

paras.t: Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtutis. Istud intelligi potest de voce illa, qua omnes evigilaturi sumus in die novissimo. De qua ait Apostolus: Ipse Dominus in jussu et in voce Archangeli et in tuba Dei descendet de cœlo. Huic voci dabit vocem virtutis, dum per eam omnes mortuos suscitabit, quemadmodum Paulus testatur: Canet tuba, et mortui resurgent incorrupti.
paras.en: [[67:34|Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power|Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtutis]]. This can be understood of that voice at which we shall all awake on the last day, of which the Apostle says: [[1 Thess 4:15|the Lord himself shall come down from heaven with commandment and with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God|Ipse Dominus in jussu et in voce Archangeli et in tuba Dei descendet de cœlo]]. To this voice he will give [[67:34|the voice of power|vocem virtutis]] when by it he raises all the dead, as Paul testifies: [[1 Cor 15:52|the trumpet shall sound and the dead shall rise again incorruptible|Canet tuba, et mortui resurgent incorrupti]].

paras.t: Date gloriam Deo super Israel, id est, nomen Domini glorificate propter omnia bona veris Israelitis, videlicet re et nomine Christianis, exhibita vel promissa. Magnificentia ejus, scilicet Christi, et virtus ejus in nubibus cœli materialibus apparebit in die novissimo, quando (ut ipse prædixit) videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cœli cum potestate magna et majestate.
paras.en: [[67:35|Give ye glory to God for Israel|Date gloriam Deo super Israel]], that is, glorify the name of the Lord for all the good things shown or promised to the true Israelites, namely to those who are Christians in deed and in name. [[67:35|his magnificence|Magnificentia ejus]], that is, Christ's, [[67:35|and his power|et virtus ejus]] will appear [[67:35|in the clouds|in nubibus]], the material clouds of heaven, on the last day, when (as he himself foretold) [[Matt 24:30|they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with much power and majesty|videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cœli cum potestate magna et majestate]].

paras.t: Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis. In Sanctis enim ante legem mirabilis fuit, sicut in Noe, quem in arca salvavit, et in Enoch, quem transtulit, in Abraham quoque et Lot ac aliis multis. Mirabilis etiam fuit in populo suo, quem de Ægypto eduxit, cui in monte Sinai terribiliter sublimiterque apparuit; in Josue quoque, ad cujus imperium sol et luna steterunt in cœlo immobiles spatio unius diei. Sic in Elia, Eliseo et aliis multis tempore legis mirabilis fuit. Maxime autem mirabilis fuit in Sanctis tempore gratiæ; et nunc usque incomprehensibiliter operatur et commoratur in Christianis, præsertim in Sacramento altaris; multa etiam signa per suos electos hucusque operari dignatur. Singuli quoque devotorum scire possunt, quam mirabiliter Deus operetur in ipsis quotidie, preces eorum exaudiendo, corda consolando, a tentationibus liberando, spiritualem profectum præstando, ignemque divini amoris in ipsorum præcordiis frequenter incendendo, augendo, ac perficiendo. Ideo enim subjungit: Deus Israel, id est hominis Deum oculo contemplativo videntis, dabit virtutem et fortitudinem plebi suæ, dando ei per gratiam, quod nec habet nec videt per naturam. Cetera satis exposita sunt.
paras.en: [[67:36|God is wonderful in his saints|Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis]]. For he was wonderful in the saints before the law, as in Noe, whom he saved in the ark[[Gen 7:23||]], and in Enoch, whom he translated[[Gen 5:24||]], in Abraham also and Lot and many others. He was wonderful too in his people, whom he brought out of Egypt[[Ex 12:42||]], to whom he appeared terribly and sublimely on Mount Sinai[[Ex 19:16||]]; in Josue also, at whose command the sun and the moon stood motionless in the sky for the space of one day[[Jos 10:13||]]. So too in Elias, Eliseus and many others was he wonderful in the time of the law. But most of all was he wonderful in the saints in the time of grace; and to this day he works and dwells incomprehensibly in Christians, above all in the Sacrament of the altar; he also deigns to work many signs through his elect even now. And each of the devout can know how wonderfully God works in them every day, hearing their prayers, consoling their hearts, freeing them from temptations, granting them spiritual progress, and often kindling, increasing and perfecting the fire of divine love in their inmost hearts. For this is why he adds: [[67:36|the God of Israel|Deus Israel]], that is, the God of the man who sees God with the contemplative eye [Israel being interpreted "a man seeing God"], [[67:36|is he who will give power and strength to his people|dabit virtutem et fortitudinem plebi suæ]], giving him by grace what he neither has nor sees by nature. The rest has been explained sufficiently.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum gloriosum, mirabilem et vere mysteriis plenum audivimus: in quo Christi resurrectio, incredulorum dejectio, Ecclesiæ institutio et promotio, Spiritus Sancti missio, Christi quoque ascensio describuntur. Conemur igitur adimplere quod psalmus iste toties exhortatur, videlicet Deo cantare, psallere, ejus præconia enarrare, suo adventui in cordibus nostris iter parare, quatenus ipse per gratiam maneat semper in nobis, nosque per dilectionem maneamus in eo, quemadmodum scriptum est: Deus caritas est, et qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a glorious psalm, wonderful and truly full of mysteries, in which are described the resurrection of Christ, the casting down of the unbelieving, the founding and advancement of the Church, the sending of the Holy Ghost, and the ascension of Christ. Let us strive therefore to fulfil what this psalm so often urges, namely to sing to God, to sing psalms, to tell forth his praises, and to prepare a way for his coming into our hearts, so that he may abide in us always by grace, and we may abide in him by love, as it is written: [[1 John 4:16|God is charity: and he that abideth in charity abideth in God, and God in him|Deus caritas est, et qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo]].

paras.t: Precatio. Rex virtutum Domine, compunctionis pluviam salutarem segrega nobis hereditati tuæ: ut qui a peccatis infirmati sumus, receptis a te rectæ intentionis viribus, ad vitam tibi placitam proficiamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, [[67:13|king of powers|Rex virtutum]], [[67:10|set aside|segrega]] for us, [[67:10|thy inheritance|hereditati tuæ]], the saving [[67:10|rain|pluviam]] of compunction: that we who have been [[67:10|weakened|infirmati]] by sins may, receiving from thee the strength of right intention, advance to a life pleasing to thee.

68.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SEXAGESIMI OCTAVI : SALVUM ME FAC, DEUS.
68.title_en: Literal exposition of the sixty-eighth psalm: Save me, O God.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi nunc declarandi est : In finem, pro his qui commutabuntur, ipsi David : id est, psalmus iste in ultimum finem, qui Christus est, nos dirigens, scriptus est pro his qui commutabuntur, id est, qui in Christo reformantur : qui sicut portaverunt imaginem primi hominis terreni et peccatoris, sic portare incipiunt imaginem secundi hominis immaculati atque cœlestis. Convenit quoque hic psalmus ipsi David prophetæ, sicut auctori ; significato autem per David, utpote Christo, convenit sicut subjecto.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is: [[68:1|Unto the end, for them that shall be changed; for David|In finem, pro his qui commutabuntur, ipsi David]]: that is, this psalm, directing us unto the last end, which is Christ, was written *for them that shall be changed*, that is, for those who are made new in Christ: who, as they have borne the image of the first man, earthly and a sinner, so begin to bear the image of the second man, spotless and heavenly[[1 Cor 15:47||]][[1 Cor 15:49||]]. This psalm belongs also to David the prophet, as to its author; but to him whom David signifies, namely Christ, it belongs as to its subject.

paras.t: Non enim dubitare permittimur quin psalmus iste ad litteram sit intelligendus de Christo : quod ex Scriptura canonica novi Testamenti multipliciter demonstratur. Apostolorum enim gloriosissimus princeps, scripturam psalmi istius dicit oportere impleri in Juda, qui tradidit Christum, propter peccatum in Christum commissum. Sic enim allegat : Fiat commoratio ejus deserta, et non sit qui inhabitet in ea. Unde quod inferius pluraliter dicitur, Fiat habitatio eorum deserta, et in tabernaculis ipsorum non sit qui inhabitet, ipse applicat ad Judam, singulariter scripturam istam allegans. Denique etiam Paulus apostolus introducit quod infra habetur, Fiat mensa eorum coram ipsis in laqueum, cum versu sequenti, dictum atque impletum in Judæis, qui Christum interfecerunt, propter scelus in ipsum patratum. In eadem quoque epistola dicit in persona Christi prædictum, quod inferius dicitur : Opprobria exprobrantium tibi ceciderunt super me. Simili modo, quod in psalmo isto habetur, Zelus domus tuæ comedit me, Joannes evangelista asserit de Christo prædictum, et in eo completum, recitans quomodo Christus flagello de funiculis facto ejecit de templo ementes et vendentes. Insuper, quod in psalmo hoc dicitur, Multiplicati sunt super capillos capitis mei qui oderunt me gratis, Christus affirmat de se prænuntiatum : Ut impleatur, inquiens, sermo qui in lege eorum scriptus est : Quia odio habuerunt me gratis. Hoc tamen superius manifeste etiam dicitur hoc modo : Non supergaudeant mihi qui adversantur mihi inique, qui oderunt me gratis. Propterea, sicut ex isto testimonio Domini Salvatoris ostenditur iste psalmus ad litteram de ipso conscriptus, sic et ille, sicut et illic plenius dixi.
paras.en: For we are not permitted to doubt that this psalm is to be understood literally of Christ: which is shown in many ways from the canonical Scripture of the New Testament. For the most glorious prince of the Apostles says that the scripture of this psalm had to be fulfilled in Judas, who betrayed Christ, because of the sin committed against Christ. For thus he cites it: [[Acts 1:20|Let their habitation become desolate, and let there be none to dwell therein|Fiat commoratio ejus deserta, et non sit qui inhabitet in ea]] [Denis reads *ejus*, "his", where the Douay-Rheims has "their"]. Hence what is said in the plural further on, [[68:26|Let their habitation be made desolate: and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles|Fiat habitatio eorum deserta, et in tabernaculis ipsorum non sit qui inhabitet]], he applies to Judas, citing this scripture in the singular. Paul the apostle, too, brings in[[Rom 11:9||]][[Rom 11:10||]] what is found below, [[68:23|Let their table become as a snare before them|Fiat mensa eorum coram ipsis in laqueum]], together with the following verse[[68:24||]], as spoken of and fulfilled in the Jews who killed Christ, because of the crime they committed against Him. In the same epistle also he says that what is said below, [[68:10|the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me|Opprobria exprobrantium tibi ceciderunt super me]], was foretold in the person of Christ[[Rom 15:3||]]. In like manner, what is found in this psalm, [[68:10|the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up|Zelus domus tuæ comedit me]], John the evangelist declares was foretold of Christ and fulfilled in Him[[John 2:17||]], relating how Christ, with a scourge made of little cords, cast out of the temple those that bought and sold[[John 2:15||]]. Moreover, what is said in this psalm, [[68:5|They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, who hate me without cause|Multiplicati sunt super capillos capitis mei qui oderunt me gratis]], Christ affirms was foretold of Himself, saying: [[John 15:25|that the word may be fulfilled which is written in their law|Ut impleatur, inquiens, sermo qui in lege eorum scriptus est]]: [[John 15:25|they hated me without cause|Quia odio habuerunt me gratis]]. Yet this is also said plainly above, in this way: [[Ps 34:19|Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: who have hated me without cause|Non supergaudeant mihi qui adversantur mihi inique, qui oderunt me gratis]]. Therefore, as this psalm is shown by that testimony of the Lord our Saviour to have been written literally of Him, so is that one also, as I said more fully there.

paras.t: Christus itaque passioni propinquans, vel in ea consistens, orans ait ad Patrem, seu sanctam Trinitatem, unum simplicissimum Deum : Salvum me fac, Deus, non a malo culpæ, quia peccare non potui, sed a malo pœnæ, videlicet a doloribus corporis et animæ mihi inflictis aut infligendis. De quibus subjungitur : quoniam intraverunt aquæ, id est tribulationes et pœnæ, usque ad animam meam, id est usque ad exstinctionem vitæ meæ corporeæ, scilicet usque ad separationem carnis et animæ. Interdum in sacra Scriptura per aquam intelligitur consolatio, juxta illud : Emisisti vinctos tuos de lacu, in quo non est aqua. Interdum vero per aquam intelligitur gravis persecutio, juxta illud in libro Job : Putabas te tenebras non visurum, et impetu aquarum inundantium non oppressum iri. Unde Isaias apertius dicit : Adducet Dominus super populum istum aquas fortes et multas, regem Assyriorum. Et ita jam per aquas designatæ sunt persecutiones.
paras.en: Christ, then, drawing near to His passion, or already in it, says in prayer to the Father, or to the Holy Trinity, the one most simple God: [[68:2|Save me, O God|Salvum me fac, Deus]]: not from the evil of guilt, for I could not sin, but from the evil of punishment, namely from the pains of body and soul inflicted or to be inflicted on me. Of which it is added: [[68:2|for the waters are come in|quoniam intraverunt aquæ]], that is, tribulations and punishments, [[68:2|even unto my soul|usque ad animam meam]], that is, even to the extinction of my bodily life, namely to the separation of flesh and soul. Sometimes in holy Scripture water is taken to mean consolation, according to that text: [[Zach 9:11|hast sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit, wherein is no water|Emisisti vinctos tuos de lacu, in quo non est aqua]]. But sometimes water is taken to mean grievous persecution, according to that text in the book of Job: [[Job 22:11|didst thou think that thou shouldst not see darkness, and that thou shouldst not be covered with the violence of overflowing waters?|Putabas te tenebras non visurum, et impetu aquarum inundantium non oppressum iri]] Hence Isaias says more plainly: [[Is 8:7|the Lord will bring upon them the waters of the river strong and many, the king of the Assyrians|Adducet Dominus super populum istum aquas fortes et multas, regem Assyriorum]] [Denis reads "upon this people" where the Vulgate has "upon them"]. And so here the waters signify persecutions.

paras.t: Infixus sum in limo profundi. Hoc quidam dicunt Christo competere ratione suæ sepulturæ, quia tunc sub terra reclusus est, quemadmodum ipse in Evangelio prædixit : Sicut fuit Jonas in ventre ceti tribus diebus et tribus noctibus, ita erit Filius hominis in corde terræ. Videtur tamen quod istud conveniat Christo etiam ratione suæ incarnationis, per quam descendit in mundum, qui dici potest limus profundi, vel propter elementum terræ limosum, vel propter vitiositatem et limositatem vitæ carnalis hominum in mundo viventium. In hoc limo Christus Deus defixus est, quoniam, teste Apostolo, descendit in inferiores partes terræ ; atque in medio nationis pravæ et perversæ multo demoratus est tempore. Et non est substantia : id est, in corpore meo non fuit stabilis uniformisque status vitæ naturalis. De Christo namque, secundum quod erat aliquo modo viator atque passibilis, verum est dicere quod apud beatum Job scriptum est : Homo natus de muliere, brevi vivens tempore, repletur multis miseriis, et nunquam in eodem statu permanet. Vel, Non est substantia, id est subsistentia seu naturalis subsistendi potestas in corpore crucifixo, exhausto, mortuo et sepulto. Vel, Non est substantia, id est, naturales divitiæ mihi defuerunt. Christus enim non habuit ubi caput suum reclinaret, et nudus cruci appensus est, habuitque pro cibo potuque acetum et fel. Ecce quid Rex gloriæ, cujus sunt cœlum et terra, et omnis ornatus eorum, pro nobis pati dignatus est. Nempe quum dives esset, propter nos egenus et sine substantia factus est, ut ejus inopia divites efficeremur.
paras.en: [[68:3|I stick fast in the mire of the deep|Infixus sum in limo profundi]]. Some say that this befits Christ by reason of His burial, since He was then shut up beneath the earth, as He Himself foretold in the Gospel: [[Matt 12:40|as Jonas was in the whale's belly three days and three nights: so shall the Son of man be in the heart of the earth|Sicut fuit Jonas in ventre ceti tribus diebus et tribus noctibus, ita erit Filius hominis in corde terræ]]. Yet it seems that it befits Christ also by reason of His incarnation, by which He came down into the world; and the world can be called *the mire of the deep*, either because of the miry element of earth, or because of the vice and miriness of the carnal life of the men who live in the world. In this mire Christ, who is God, was fixed fast, since, as the Apostle witnesses, He [[Eph 4:9|descended first into the lower parts of the earth|descendit in inferiores partes terræ]]; and He tarried a long time [[Phil 2:15|in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation|in medio nationis pravæ et perversæ]]. [[68:3|and there is no sure standing|Et non est substantia]] [*substantia*: "substance", also "firm standing", and also "means, wealth"; Denis takes it each way in turn]: that is, in my body there was no stable and uniform state of natural life. For of Christ, inasmuch as He was in some manner a wayfarer and capable of suffering, it is true to say what is written in blessed Job: [[Job 14:1|Man born of a woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries|Homo natus de muliere, brevi vivens tempore, repletur multis miseriis]], [[Job 14:2|and never continueth in the same state|et nunquam in eodem statu permanet]]. Or, *there is no sure standing*, that is, no subsistence, or natural power of subsisting, in the body crucified, drained, dead and buried. Or, *there is no sure standing*, that is, natural riches failed me. For Christ had not where to lay His head[[Luke 9:58||]], and was hung naked on the cross, and had vinegar and gall for meat and drink[[Matt 27:48||]][[Matt 27:34||]]. Behold what the King of glory, whose are heaven and earth and all their array, deigned to suffer for us. For indeed, being rich, He became poor for our sakes, and without substance, that through His poverty we might be made rich[[2 Cor 8:9||]].

paras.t: Veni, de summo cœlo et sinu Patris per assumptionem humanæ naturæ, in altitudinem maris, id est in profunditatem persecutionis et pœnæ ac mortis ; et tempestas demersit me, id est, magnitudo pœnarum mihi in crucis patibulo inflictarum occidit me : sicut in Threnis scribitur : Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum ; dixi, Perii. Solet autem per altitudinem profunditas designari, juxta illud : Puteus altus est.
paras.en: [[68:3|I am come|Veni]], from the highest heaven and the bosom of the Father, by taking on human nature, [[68:3|into the depth of the sea|in altitudinem maris]], that is, into the depth of persecution, of punishment and of death; [[68:3|and a tempest hath overwhelmed me|et tempestas demersit me]], that is, the greatness of the pains inflicted on me on the gibbet of the cross killed me: as is written in Lamentations: [[Lam 3:54|Waters have flowed over my head: I said: I am cut off|Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum ; dixi, Perii]]. Now *altitudo* [literally "height"; the Douay-Rheims renders it "depth"] is commonly put for depth, according to that text: [[John 4:11|the well is deep|Puteus altus est]].

paras.t: Laboravi clamans. Christus enim non sine labore prædicando discurrebat. Unde scriptum est : Jesus fatigatus ex itinere. Clamavit quoque, Judæos increpando, populum instruendo, evangelicam legem docendo. Maxime tamen in passione laboravit, quando et bajulans sibi crucem exivit : atque in cruce clamavit, Pater, ignosce illis ; et, Consummatum est ; et, In manus tuas commendo spiritum meum. Hinc enim de Christo apud Isaiam scriptum est : Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur.
paras.en: [[68:4|I have laboured with crying|Laboravi clamans]]. For Christ went about preaching, and not without labour. Hence it is written: [[John 4:6|Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey|Jesus fatigatus ex itinere]]. He cried out too, in rebuking the Jews, instructing the people, teaching the law of the Gospel. But most of all He laboured in His passion, when also, [[John 19:17|bearing his own cross, he went forth|bajulans sibi crucem exivit]]; and on the cross He cried out: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them|Pater, ignosce illis]]; and, [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]]; and, [[Luke 23:46|into thy hands I commend my spirit|In manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]. For hence it is written of Christ in Isaias: [[Is 53:11|Because his soul hath laboured, he shall see and be filled|Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur]].

paras.t: Raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ. Ad litteram raucæ erant fauces Christi. Raucedo namque causatur ex desiccatione humorum in faucibus et arteriis. Quoniam ergo Christus in passione sanguinem copiose effudit, prout dictum est supra, Sicut aqua effusus sum ; ideo rauca erat vox ejus. Metaphorice autem dicuntur fauces fieri raucæ, dum sermo prolatus, audienti non proficit, sed sine fructu consistit : sicque fauces Christi raucæ erant, quantum ad incredulos et perversos : quibus ipse in Evangelio ait, Sermo meus non capit in vobis.
paras.en: [[68:4|my jaws are become hoarse|Raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ]]. Literally, Christ's throat was hoarse. For hoarseness is caused by the drying up of the humours in the throat and the windpipe. Since, then, Christ shed His blood abundantly in His passion, as was said above, [[Ps 21:15|I am poured out like water|Sicut aqua effusus sum]], His voice was therefore hoarse. But metaphorically the jaws are said to become hoarse when the word spoken does not profit the hearer but remains without fruit: and so Christ's jaws were hoarse as regards the unbelieving and the perverse, to whom He Himself says in the Gospel: [[John 8:37|my word hath no place in you|Sermo meus non capit in vobis]].

paras.t: Defecerunt oculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum. Videtur hoc repugnare ei quod Christus superius ait : In Domino sperans non infirmabor. Est igitur sensus : Oculi mei interiores, videlicet contemplatio et mentalis oratio, quibus in cruce pendens Deum indesinenter adspexi, visi sunt deficere, id est frustrari, et suo effectu seu divina subventione privari, dum Deus Pater reliquit me in manibus impiorum. Propter quod ipsi dixerunt : Confidit in Deo ; liberet eum nunc, si vult. Et iterum : Si rex Israel est (vel, Si hic est Christus Dei electus), descendat nunc de cruce. Et Isaias : Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo et humiliatum. Solet enim Christus de se aliquid affirmare, juxta quod in opinione aliorum fuit. Unde apud Jeremiam : Ego, inquit, quasi agnus innocens qui portatur ad victimam; et non cognovi quia super me cogitaverunt consilia, etc. Judæi namque putabant Christum nescire ipsorum consilia contra se.
paras.en: [[68:4|my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God|Defecerunt oculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum]]. This seems to conflict with what Christ said above: [[Ps 25:1|I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened|In Domino sperans non infirmabor]]. The sense, then, is this: my inward eyes, namely contemplation and mental prayer, with which, hanging on the cross, I looked unceasingly upon God, seemed to fail, that is, to be frustrated, and to be deprived of their effect, or of divine help, while God the Father left me in the hands of the wicked. Wherefore they said: [[Matt 27:43|He trusted in God: let him now deliver him if he will have him|Confidit in Deo ; liberet eum nunc, si vult]]. And again: [[Matt 27:42|If he be the king of Israel|Si rex Israel est]] (or, [[Luke 23:35|if he be Christ, the elect of God|Si hic est Christus Dei electus]]), [[Matt 27:42|let him now come down from the cross|descendat nunc de cruce]]. And Isaias: [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God and afflicted|Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo et humiliatum]]. For Christ is wont to affirm something of Himself according to what was in the opinion of others. Hence in Jeremias: [[Jer 11:19|And I|Ego]], He says, [[Jer 11:19|was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim: and I knew not that they had devised counsels against me|quasi agnus innocens qui portatur ad victimam; et non cognovi quia super me cogitaverunt consilia]], etc. [Denis reads *innocens*, "innocent", where the Vulgate has *mansuetus*, "meek"] For the Jews thought that Christ did not know their counsels against Him.

paras.t: Vel sic : Defecerunt oculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum : id est, quando in cruce pendens, certissime confidebam me tertia die resuscitandum ; tunc oculi mei corporales defecerunt, quia obtenebrati sunt atque eversi.
paras.en: Or thus: [[68:4|my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God|Defecerunt oculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum]]: that is, when, hanging on the cross, I trusted most surely that I should be raised up on the third day, then my bodily eyes failed, for they were darkened and turned upward.

paras.t: Multiplicati sunt super capillos capitis mei, qui oderunt me gratis. Per hoc Christus insinuat multitudinem adversariorum suorum Judæorum, qui eum gratis, id est sine rationabili causa, oderunt : et forte ad litteram, numerus odientium et persequentium Christum excessit numerum crinium capitis sui. Multa enim millia fuisse videntur in populo illo, de quo Evangelista testatur : Respondens universus populus, dixit : Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros.
paras.en: [[68:5|They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, who hate me without cause|Multiplicati sunt super capillos capitis mei, qui oderunt me gratis]]. By this Christ intimates the multitude of His adversaries the Jews, who hated Him *without cause*, that is, without any reasonable cause: and perhaps, literally, the number of those who hated and persecuted Christ exceeded the number of the hairs of His head. For there seem to have been many thousands in that people of whom the Evangelist testifies: [[Matt 27:25|the whole people answering, said: His blood be upon us and upon our children|Respondens universus populus, dixit : Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]].

paras.t: Confortati sunt, qui persecuti sunt me inimici mei injuste. Omnes enim confœderati sunt in malo, et invalescebant voces eorum adversum me, non propter rationem, sed propter multitudinem. Principes sacerdotum præbuerunt auxilium Pharisæis, qui primo contra Christum conceperunt rancorem. Herodes quoque et Pilatus cooperati sunt eis, quia Herodes Christum alba veste illusit, Pilatus vero eum flagellavit atque damnavit. Et isti persecuti sunt me injuste, id est sine offensa et culpa ; imo pro beneficiis multis rependebant mihi injurias et flagella : sicut superius dictum est, Retribuebant mihi mala pro bonis. Hoc est quod in Evangelio Christus ait Judæis : Multa bona opera ostendi vobis ex Patre meo ; propter quod horum vultis me lapidare? Et per Jeremiam : Numquid redditur pro bono malum, quia foderunt foveam animæ meæ?
paras.en: [[68:5|My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me|Confortati sunt, qui persecuti sunt me inimici mei injuste]]. For all were leagued together in evil[[Luke 23:5||]], and [[Luke 23:23|their voices prevailed|invalescebant voces eorum]] against me, not by reason but by numbers. The chief priests gave help to the Pharisees, who had first conceived rancour against Christ. Herod too and Pilate worked with them, for Herod mocked Christ with a white garment[[Luke 23:11||]], and Pilate scourged Him[[John 19:1||]] and condemned Him[[John 19:16||]]. And these *have wrongfully persecuted me*, that is, with no offence or fault on my part; nay, for many benefits they repaid me with injuries and scourges: as was said above, [[Ps 34:12|They repaid me evil for good|Retribuebant mihi mala pro bonis]]. This is what Christ says to the Jews in the Gospel: [[John 10:32|Many good works I have shewed you from my Father. For which of those works do you stone me?|Multa bona opera ostendi vobis ex Patre meo ; propter quod horum vultis me lapidare?]] [Denis reads "for which of these do you wish to stone me?"] And through Jeremias: [[Jer 18:20|Shall evil be rendered for good, because they have digged a pit for my soul?|Numquid redditur pro bono malum, quia foderunt foveam animæ meæ?]]

paras.t: Quæ non rapui, id est culpam quam non contraxi, malum quod non feci, tunc exsolvebam: quoniam sine culpa propria passus sum pœnam. Pœna autem est præmium culpæ, sicut et mors est pœna peccati. Quoniam ergo Salvator ab omni peccato immunissimus exstitit, et nihilo minus acerbissimam mortem sustinuit, constat quod solvit quæ non rapuit. Satisfecit vero pro nobis, et merito suæ particularis temporalisque mortis abstulit a genere humano universalem æternalemque mortem, pro originali peccato inflictam. Unde scriptum est : Spiritus oris nostri Christus Dominus captus est ; et rursus, Ipse vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra. Porro Christus apertissime ait per Isaiam : Servire me fecisti in peccatis tuis, præbuisti mihi laborem in iniquitatibus tuis.
paras.en: [[68:5|that which I took not away|Quæ non rapui]], that is, the guilt which I did not contract, the evil which I did not do, [[68:5|then did I pay|tunc exsolvebam]]: for I suffered punishment without guilt of my own. Now punishment is the wage [*præmium*, the due return] of guilt, as death too is the punishment of sin[[Rom 6:23||]]. Since, then, the Saviour was wholly free of all sin, and none the less endured a most bitter death, it is plain that He paid what He took not away. And He made satisfaction for us, and by the merit of His particular and temporal death took away from the human race the universal and eternal death inflicted for original sin. Hence it is written: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken|Spiritus oris nostri Christus Dominus captus est]]; and again, [[Is 53:5|he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins|Ipse vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra]]. Moreover Christ says most plainly through Isaias: [[Is 43:24|thou hast made me to serve with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thy iniquities|Servire me fecisti in peccatis tuis, præbuisti mihi laborem in iniquitatibus tuis]].

paras.t: Deus, tu scis insipientiam meam, et delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita. Versus iste tripliciter explanatur. Primo sic : Deus, tu scis, etc., id est, si est in me aliquid insipientiæ et peccati, sicut Judæi affirmant, dicentes me falsa docere ac blasphemare : hoc tu nosti. Iste est enim modus loquendi eorum qui se sobrie excusant coram Deo, dum mendaciter accusantur. Tanquam dicant : Nos nobis conscii non sumus de aliquo malo ; sed si quid mali in nobis est, Deus agnovit. Et hoc modo Judas patriarcha se ipsum et fratres suos excusans de furto coram Joseph, ait : Deus invenit iniquitatem servorum tuorum.
paras.en: [[68:6|O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my offences are not hidden from thee|Deus, tu scis insipientiam meam, et delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita]]. This verse is explained in three ways. First thus: [[68:6|O God, thou knowest|Deus, tu scis]], etc., that is: if there is in me anything of folly and of sin, as the Jews affirm when they say that I teach falsehood and blaspheme, this Thou knowest. For this is the way of speaking of those who modestly excuse themselves before God when they are falsely accused; as if they said: We are not conscious to ourselves of any evil; but if there is any evil in us, God has known it. And in this way Juda the patriarch, excusing himself and his brothers of the theft before Joseph, says: [[Gen 44:16|God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants|Deus invenit iniquitatem servorum tuorum]].

paras.t: Secundo, intelligitur a contrario sensu, hoc modo : Deus, tu scis per approbationem, insipientiam meam, id est sapientiam meam, quæ a Judæis insipientia reputatur ; et delicta mea, id est virtutes et opera bona, quæ Judæi judicant esse peccata, a te non sunt abscondita, sed per approbationem nota sunt tibi. Quoniam enim Christus mundi contemptum docuit, et Deum suum Patrem vocavit ; propterea dicebant Judæi : Dæmonium habet, et insanit ; et, Quid hic sic loquitur ? blasphemat ; et, Quis est hic qui loquitur blasphemias? Unde et dixerunt Pilato : Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit. Secundum hunc modum loquendi ait Salvator : Confiteor tibi, Pater, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis : quod a contrario sensu intelligendum est, secundum Augustinum. Et ita Paulus ait : Factus sum insipiens ; vos me coegistis ; et rursus, Nos stulti propter Christum.
paras.en: Secondly, it is understood in the contrary sense [that is, as meaning the opposite of what the words say on their face], in this way: [[68:6|O God, thou knowest|Deus, tu scis]] by approving, [[68:6|my foolishness|insipientiam meam]], that is, my wisdom, which the Jews reckon folly; [[68:6|and my offences|et delicta mea]], that is, my virtues and good works, which the Jews judge to be sins, [[68:6|are not hidden from thee|a te non sunt abscondita]], but are known to Thee with approval. For since Christ taught contempt of the world, and called God His Father, the Jews therefore said: [[John 10:20|He hath a devil and is mad|Dæmonium habet, et insanit]]; and, [[Mark 2:7|Why doth this man speak thus? He blasphemeth|Quid hic sic loquitur ? blasphemat]]; and, [[Luke 5:21|Who is this who speaketh blasphemies|Quis est hic qui loquitur blasphemias?]]? Hence they also said to Pilate: [[John 19:7|We have a law; and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God|Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit]]. In this manner of speaking the Saviour says: [[Matt 11:25|I confess to thee, O Father|Confiteor tibi, Pater]], [[Matt 11:25|because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones|quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]: which, according to Augustine, is to be understood in the contrary sense. And so Paul says: [[2 Cor 12:11|I am become foolish. You have compelled me|Factus sum insipiens ; vos me coegistis]]; and again, [[1 Cor 4:10|We are fools for Christs sake|Nos stulti propter Christum]].

paras.t: Tertio, intelligitur dictum a Christo, non pro se ipso, sed pro corpore suo mystico, quod est Ecclesia. Sicque insipientiam et delicta membrorum suorum, quæ super se excepit, et pro quibus satisfecit, nominat sua, sicut alibi ait : Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? et iterum : Esurivi, et non dedistis mihi manducare ; nudus fui, et non cooperuistis me.
paras.en: Thirdly, it is understood as said by Christ not for Himself but for His mystical body, which is the Church. And so the folly and the offences of His members, which He took upon Himself and for which He made satisfaction, He calls His own, as He says elsewhere: [[Acts 9:4|Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me|Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris?]]? and again: [[Matt 25:42|I was hungry and you gave me not to eat|Esurivi, et non dedistis mihi manducare]]; [[Matt 25:43|naked and you covered me not|nudus fui, et non cooperuistis me]].

paras.t: Non erubescant in me, qui exspectant te : id est, sancti in limbo detenti, me cum ingenti desiderio præstolantes, non verecundentur quasi frustrati spe sua ; sed sicut Prophetæ prædixerunt et alii crediderunt, ita resuscita me, et fac me sanctos de limbo educere, quatenus glorientur se consequi fidei fructum et spei effectum. Sancti autem in limbo exspectabant et Christum et Deum Patrem : Christum, sicut mittendum atque localiter descensurum ; Patrem vero, sicut missurum ac spiritualiter consolaturum. Itaque, Non erubescant qui exspectant te, Domine universorum, o Domine virtutum cœlestium, scilicet angelorum : cui nihil est impossibile.
paras.en: [[68:7|Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee|Non erubescant in me, qui exspectant te]]: that is, let not the saints held in limbo, who await me with immense desire, be put to shame as though cheated of their hope; but as the Prophets foretold and others believed, so raise me up, and make me lead the saints out of limbo, so that they may glory in obtaining the fruit of their faith and the effect of their hope. Now the saints in limbo were waiting both for Christ and for God the Father[[Gen 49:18||]]: for Christ, as the one to be sent and to come down in place; for the Father, as the one who would send Him and console them in spirit. Therefore: *Let not them be ashamed who look for thee*, [[68:7|O Lord, the Lord of hosts|Domine universorum, o Domine virtutum cœlestium]] [Denis expands: "O Lord of all things, O Lord of the heavenly powers"], that is, of the angels: to whom nothing is impossible.

paras.t: Non confundantur super me, qui quærunt te, Deus Israel : id est, Apostoli aliique fideles te per fidem et opera bona quærentes, non confundantur super me, id est de mei humiliatione, persecutione et occisione ; sed corrobora eos ad confitendum me, atque ad imitandum vestigia mea. Hoc fuit impletum præcipue in die Pentecostes, Spiritu Sancto recepto.
paras.en: [[68:7|Let them not be confounded on my account, who seek thee, O God of Israel|Non confundantur super me, qui quærunt te, Deus Israel]]: that is, let not the Apostles and the other faithful, who seek Thee by faith and good works, *be confounded on my account*, that is, over my humiliation, persecution and slaying; but strengthen them to confess me and to follow in my footsteps. This was fulfilled chiefly on the day of Pentecost, when the Holy Ghost had been received.

paras.t: Quoniam propter te, id est propter nominis tui honorem, quem summe quæsivi ; vel, Propter te, id est propter sapientiæ tuæ dispositionem, qua me pati decrevisti : quemadmodum loquitur Petrus, Convenerunt adversus sanctum puerum tuum Jesum, facere quæ manus tua et consilium tuum decreverunt fieri. Vel, Propter te, id est propter justitiam meam, quam ob tuam voluntatem immobiliter observavi. Sustinui opprobrium Judæorum dicentium, Nunc cognovimus quia dæmonium habes ; et, Numquid interficiet semetipsum?
paras.en: [[68:8|Because for thy sake|Quoniam propter te]], that is, for the honour of Thy name, which I sought above all things; or, *for thy sake*, that is, because of the ordering of Thy wisdom, by which Thou didst decree that I should suffer: as Peter says, [[Acts 4:27|there assembled together|Convenerunt]] [[Acts 4:27|against thy holy child Jesus|adversus sanctum puerum tuum Jesum]], [[Acts 4:28|To do what thy hand and thy counsel decreed to be done|facere quæ manus tua et consilium tuum decreverunt fieri]]. Or, *for thy sake*, that is, for my justice, which I kept unshaken because of Thy will. [[68:8|I have borne reproach|Sustinui opprobrium]] from the Jews, who said: [[John 8:52|Now we know that thou hast a devil|Nunc cognovimus quia dæmonium habes]]; and, [[John 8:22|Will he kill himself|Numquid interficiet semetipsum]]?

paras.t: Operuit confusio faciem meam : id est, illud quod solet aliis esse causa confusionis, multipliciter irruit super me tempore passionis, quando ligatis manibus tradiderunt me præsidi, et quando coram Pilato atque Herode nihil respondi, et quando alba veste illusus sum, nudatus, columnæ alligatus, flagellisque cæsus, spinis coronatus, propriisque humeris crucem bajulans ad mortem ductus, et inter latrones suspensus. Proprie tamen non fuit in Christo confusio, quia confusio propter virtutem in viro perfecto locum non habet. Ad litteram etiam operuit confusio faciem Christi, quando viri qui tenebant eum, illudebant ei, et velaverunt eum, et percusserunt faciem ejus, dicentes : Prophetiza nobis, Christe, quis est qui te percussit?
paras.en: [[68:8|shame hath covered my face|Operuit confusio faciem meam]]: that is, what is wont to be a cause of shame to others fell upon me in many ways in the time of my passion: when they bound my hands and delivered me to the governor, and when before Pilate and Herod I answered nothing, and when I was mocked with a white garment, stripped, bound to the pillar, beaten with scourges, crowned with thorns, led to death carrying the cross on my own shoulders, and hung between thieves. Yet properly there was no shame in Christ [*confusio*, here the inward feeling of disgrace, not its outward cause], since in a perfect man shame, by reason of his virtue, has no place. Literally, too, shame covered Christ's face when the men that held Him mocked Him, and blindfolded Him, and struck His face, saying: [[Matt 26:68|Prophesy unto us, O Christ. Who is he that struck thee|Prophetiza nobis, Christe, quis est qui te percussit?]]?

paras.t: Extraneus factus sum fratribus meis, id est Judæis de genere Abrahæ mecum natis. Erat enim Christus extraneus Judæis in ipsum non credentibus, quia longe erat a corde eorum, quamvis inter eos corporaliter ambulabat. Erat quoque extraneus fratribus suis Apostolis, qui omnes, relicto eo, fugerunt. Unde sanctus Job in persona aut certe figura Christi, ait : Fratres mei elongaverunt a me, et noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me. Et peregrinus factus sum filiis matris meæ, id est Judæis filiis Saræ vel Synagogæ. Quemadmodum peregrinus seu hospes non diu sustinetur, sed de domo expellitur ; ita Judæi Christum velut vilem abjecerunt atque spreverunt, illud apud Joannem dicentes : Nos scimus quoniam Moysi locutus est Deus ; hunc autem nescimus unde sit. Idem quoque Evangelista testatur : Jam conspiraverant Judæi, ut si quis confiteretur eum esse Christum, extra synagogam fieret. Hoc modo Christum fuisse venturum, et in mundo victurum, Jeremias cum admiratione prædixit : Quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum ?
paras.en: [[68:9|I am become a stranger to my brethren|Extraneus factus sum fratribus meis]], that is, to the Jews born with me of the stock of Abraham. For Christ was a stranger to the Jews who did not believe in Him, since He was far from their heart, although He walked among them in the body. He was a stranger too to His brethren the Apostles, who all left Him and fled. Hence holy Job, in the person, or at least in the figure, of Christ, says: [[Job 19:13|He hath put my brethren far from me, and my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me|Fratres mei elongaverunt a me, et noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me]] [Denis reads "My brethren have gone far from me"]. [[68:9|and an alien to the sons of my mother|Et peregrinus factus sum filiis matris meæ]], that is, to the Jews, sons of Sara, or of the Synagogue. As an alien or guest is not long borne with, but is put out of the house, so the Jews cast Christ away as worthless and despised Him, saying those words in John: [[John 9:29|We know that God spoke to Moses: but as to this man, we know not from whence he is|Nos scimus quoniam Moysi locutus est Deus ; hunc autem nescimus unde sit]]. The same Evangelist also testifies: [[John 9:22|the Jews had already agreed among themselves that if any man should confess him to be Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue|Jam conspiraverant Judæi, ut si quis confiteretur eum esse Christum, extra synagogam fieret]]. That Christ would come in this way, and live in this way in the world, Jeremias foretold with wonder: [[Jer 14:8|why wilt thou be as a stranger in the land, and as a wayfaring man turning in to lodge?|Quare quasi colonus futurus es in terra, et quasi viator declinans ad manendum]]

paras.t: Cur autem Christus tanta pati dignatus sit, pandit subdendo : Quoniam zelus domus tuæ comedit me : id est, ardens dilectio ædificationis, informationis et conversionis Ecclesiæ, seu fidelium aut electorum, pro quorum salute sum incarnatus, me totum accendit et absorbuit et consumpsit. Propter salutem enim Ecclesiæ Christus prædicavit, Judæos increpavit, miracula fecit. Hunc quoque zelum palam ostendit, quando ejecit de templo ementes et vendentes, dicens : Nolite facere domum Patris mei domum negotiationis. Hic etiam zelus Christum comedit, id est, in morte consumpsit: quoniam propter caritatem suam ad nos, tradidit semetipsum pro nobis in mortem, sicut Paulus fatetur : In fide, inquiens, vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me; et rursus : Christus tanquam filius fidelis erat in domo sua : quæ domus sumus nos. Voluit enim Christus construere templum Deo Patri, Ecclesiamque perfectam ex vivis lapidibus, prout de ipso apud Zachariam fuit prædictum : Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus, et ædificabit templum Domino, et ipse portabit gloriam, et sedebit et dominabitur in solio suo. Hoc templum Christus construere cœpit, docendo et redarguendo errantes, quemadmodum de ipso clare prænuntiatum est. Quum enim de Christi adventu dixisset Malachias propheta, Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis; de ipsius doctrina mox addidit : Ipse enim quasi ignis conflans, et quasi herba fullonum; et sedebit conflans et emundans argentum, et purgabit filios Levi. Denique hoc templum Christus promisit se ædificaturum in suo adventu, per Amos prophetam : In die illo suscitabo, inquiens, tabernaculum David quod cecidit, et reædificabo aperturas [murorum] ejus. Quod Jacobus in Actibus Apostolorum allegat de Christo prædictum.
paras.en: And why Christ deigned to suffer such things he shows by adding: [[68:10|For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up|Quoniam zelus domus tuæ comedit me]]: that is, burning love for the building up, the instruction and the conversion of the Church, or of the faithful or the elect, for whose salvation I became incarnate, has wholly kindled, absorbed and consumed me. For it was for the salvation of the Church that Christ preached, rebuked the Jews, and worked miracles. This zeal He also showed openly when He cast out of the temple those that bought and sold, saying: [[John 2:16|make not the house of my Father a house of traffic|Nolite facere domum Patris mei domum negotiationis]]. This zeal also *ate up* Christ, that is, consumed Him in death: since for His charity towards us He delivered Himself up to death for us, as Paul confesses: [[Gal 2:20|I live in the faith|In fide]], he says, [[Gal 2:20|of the Son of God, who loved me and delivered himself for me|vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me]]; and again: [[Heb 3:6|Christ, as the Son in his own house: which house are we|Christus tanquam filius fidelis erat in domo sua : quæ domus sumus nos]] [Denis reads "as a faithful son"]. For Christ willed to build a temple to God the Father, and a perfect Church of living stones, as was foretold of Him in Zacharias: [[Zach 6:12|BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME|Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus]]: [[Zach 6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|et ædificabit templum Domino]]: [[Zach 6:13|and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit, and rule upon his throne|et ipse portabit gloriam, et sedebit et dominabitur in solio suo]]. This temple Christ began to build by teaching and reproving those in error, as was clearly foretold of Him. For when Malachias the prophet had said of Christ's coming, [[Mal 3:1|presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple|Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis]], he soon added of His teaching: [[Mal 3:2|he is like a refining fire, and like the fuller's herb|Ipse enim quasi ignis conflans, et quasi herba fullonum]]: [[Mal 3:3|And he shall sit refining and cleansing the silver, and he shall purify the sons of Levi|et sedebit conflans et emundans argentum, et purgabit filios Levi]]. Lastly, Christ promised through the prophet Amos that He would build this temple at His coming: [[Amos 9:11|In that day I will raise up|In die illo suscitabo]], He says, [[Amos 9:11|the tabernacle of David, that is fallen: and I will close up the breaches of the walls thereof|tabernaculum David quod cecidit, et reædificabo aperturas]]; which James in the Acts of the Apostles cites as foretold of Christ[[Acts 15:15||]][[Acts 15:16||]].

paras.t: Et opprobria Judæorum exprobrantium tibi, o Pater æterne, me Unigenitum tuum negando, et opera mea miraculosa atque divina dæmonibus adscribendo, ceciderunt super me, id est, in mea humanitate passibili habuerunt effectum : nam verba atque injuriæ impiorum tibi illata, divinitati nocere non poterant, sed meam humanitatem lædere et occidere valuerunt. Vel, Ceciderunt super me, id est, mihi quoque inferebantur. Quidquid enim uni divinæ Personæ irrogatur injuriæ, irrogatur et alii. Propter quod asserit Christus : Qui non honorificat Filium, non honorificat Patrem qui misit illum. Exprobrabant autem Judæi Deo Patri, imo toti Trinitati, præcipue tamen Spiritui Sancto, dum Christi miracula totius Trinitatis potestate patrata, attribuebant Beelzebub. Unde quum dixissent Scribæ, Beelzebub habet, volens Christus ostendere eos Spiritui Sancto intulisse blasphemiam : Qui blasphemaverit (ait) in Spiritum Sanctum, non habet remissionem in æternum, sed reus erit æterni delicti. Et cur hoc dixerit de Judæis, manifestat Evangelista, subjungens : Quoniam dicebant, Spiritum immundum habet.
paras.en: [[68:10|and the reproaches|Et opprobria]] of the Jews, [[68:10|of them that reproached thee|exprobrantium tibi]], O eternal Father, by denying me, Thy Only-begotten, and ascribing my miraculous and divine works to devils, [[68:10|are fallen upon me|ceciderunt super me]], that is, took effect in my passible humanity [that is, my humanity, which could suffer]: for the words and injuries of the wicked offered to Thee could not harm the Godhead, but they had power to wound and to kill my humanity. Or, *are fallen upon me*, that is, were brought upon me too. For whatever injury is done to one divine Person is done to the other also. Wherefore Christ declares: [[John 5:23|He who honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father who hath sent him|Qui non honorificat Filium, non honorificat Patrem qui misit illum]]. Now the Jews reproached God the Father, nay the whole Trinity, but above all the Holy Ghost, when they ascribed to Beelzebub the miracles of Christ, wrought by the power of the whole Trinity. Hence, when the Scribes had said, [[Mark 3:22|He hath Beelzebub|Beelzebub habet]], Christ, wishing to show that they had uttered blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, says: [[Mark 3:29|he that shall blaspheme|Qui blasphemaverit]], [[Mark 3:29|against the Holy Ghost, shall never have forgiveness, but shall be guilty of an everlasting sin|in Spiritum Sanctum, non habet remissionem in æternum, sed reus erit æterni delicti]]. And why He said this of the Jews the Evangelist makes plain, adding: [[Mark 3:30|Because they said: He hath an unclean spirit|Quoniam dicebant, Spiritum immundum habet]].

paras.t: Et operui in jejunio animam meam. Operatio virtuosa, animæ vestimentum vocatur, juxta illud : Exsultabit anima mea in Deo meo, quia induit me vestimentis salutis, et indumento justitiæ circumdedit me. Christus autem jejunavit quadraginta diebus et totidem noctibus : et ita jejunio, quod est actus temperantiæ, operuit, id est, spiritualiter vestivit, animam suam. Et factum est in opprobrium mihi, id est in occasionem tentationis a dæmone, qui ex hoc motus est ad tentandum me, in tantum ut idololatriæ speciem mihi proponeret, dicens : Hæc omnia tibi dabo, si procidens adoraveris me.
paras.en: [[68:11|And I covered my soul in fasting|Et operui in jejunio animam meam]]. Virtuous action is called the garment of the soul, according to that text: [[Is 61:10|my soul shall be joyful in my God: for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation: and with the robe of justice he hath covered me|Exsultabit anima mea in Deo meo, quia induit me vestimentis salutis, et indumento justitiæ circumdedit me]]. Now Christ fasted forty days and as many nights[[Matt 4:2||]]: and so with fasting, which is an act of temperance, He *covered*, that is, spiritually clothed, His soul. [[68:11|and it was made a reproach to me|Et factum est in opprobrium mihi]], that is, an occasion of temptation by the devil, who was moved by this to tempt me, so far as to set before me the semblance of idolatry, saying: [[Matt 4:9|All these will I give thee, if falling down thou wilt adore me|Hæc omnia tibi dabo, si procidens adoraveris me]].

paras.t: Vel sic : Operui in jejunio animam meam, id est, pallio compassionis atque tristitiæ indutus sum propter infidelitatem malitiamque perversorum. Hinc namque in Marco dicitur : Contristatus est Jesus super cæcitate cordis eorum. Sicut enim Christi refectio, est nostræ mentis ad Deum conversio, secundum quod ipse protestatur, Si quis aperuerit mihi januam, introibo ad illum, et cœnabo cum illo; sic ejus jejunium, est nostri cordis a Deo aversio. Et factum est in opprobrium mihi : id est, labor et studium quo pro hominum conversione sudavi, cucurri et laboravi, fuit Judæis occasio detractionis, irrisionis et accusationis adversum me. Dicebant enim : Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram.
paras.en: Or thus: [[68:11|I covered my soul in fasting|Operui in jejunio animam meam]], that is, I put on the cloak of compassion and sorrow because of the unbelief and malice of the perverse. For hence it is said in Mark that Jesus was [[Mark 3:5|grieved for the blindness of their hearts|Contristatus est Jesus super cæcitate cordis eorum]]. For as Christ's refreshment [*refectio*, a meal] is the turning of our mind to God, as He Himself declares, [[Apoc 3:20|If any man shall hear my voice and open to me the door, I will come in to him and will sup with him|Si quis aperuerit mihi januam, introibo ad illum, et cœnabo cum illo]]; so His fasting is the turning of our heart away from God. [[68:11|and it was made a reproach to me|Et factum est in opprobrium mihi]]: that is, the labour and toil with which I sweated, ran and laboured for the conversion of men was to the Jews an occasion of detraction, derision and accusation against me. For they said: [[Luke 23:2|We have found this man perverting our nation|Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram]].

paras.t: Et posui vestimentum meum cilicium, id est, non mollibus, sed duris vestibus usus sum. Quoniam enim Christus Joannem Baptistam de vestimentorum asperitate collaudat, vestiumque mollitiem reprobat, apparet quod ipse vestibus asperis utebatur. Cœpit equidem facere et docere. Et ad hoc facit, quia tunica ejus inconsutilis fuit, desuper contexta per totum, quemadmodum vestes cilicinæ fieri solent. Vel, Posui vestimentum meum cilicium, id est, carnem mortalem indutus sum, et ea divinitatem meam velavi : de qua carne atque cilicio superius dixi, Conscidisti saccum meum, et circumdedisti me lætitia. Et factus sum illis in parabolam, id est in similitudinem improperii et in derisum, quemadmodum in Evangelio scribitur : Audiebant hæc Pharisæi, et deridebant eum; et : Dicebant quoniam in furorem versus est.
paras.en: [[68:12|And I made haircloth my garment|Et posui vestimentum meum cilicium]], that is, I wore not soft but rough clothing. For since Christ praises John the Baptist for the roughness of his garments, and condemns softness of clothing[[Matt 11:8||]], it appears that He Himself wore rough garments. For indeed He [[Acts 1:1|began to do and to teach|Cœpit equidem facere et docere]] [that is, He did first what He taught]. And this is borne out by the fact that His coat was [[John 19:23|without seam, woven from the top throughout|inconsutilis fuit, desuper contexta per totum]], as garments of haircloth are commonly made. Or, *I made haircloth my garment*, that is, I put on mortal flesh and veiled my Godhead with it: of which flesh, or haircloth, I said above: [[Ps 29:12|thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness|Conscidisti saccum meum, et circumdedisti me lætitia]]. [[68:12|and I became a byword to them|Et factus sum illis in parabolam]] [*parabola*, a comparison, a thing held up as a figure], that is, a figure of reproach and a derision, as is written in the Gospel: [[Luke 16:14|the Pharisees, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him|Audiebant hæc Pharisæi, et deridebant eum]]; and: [[Mark 3:21|they said: He is become mad|Dicebant quoniam in furorem versus est]].

paras.t: Adversum me loquebantur qui sedebant in porta, id est sacerdotes juxta portam templi sedentes et populum instruentes, vel judices in portis civitatis ad judicandum residentes, quemadmodum jussum erat per Moysen : Judices constitues in omnibus portis tuis. Isti contra Christum loquebantur, avertentes plebem ab eo, in tantum ut tandem peterent sibi virum homicidam donari, et Jesum occidi. Et in me, id est de me et contra me, psallebant, id est, irridendo cantabant, qui bibebant vinum, id est Judæi gulosi. Cantilenas enim irrisorias composuerunt et cecinerunt de Domino Salvatore, sicut est illud : Homo vorax, potator vini, amicus publicanorum. Unde per Jeremiam dicitur : Factus est mihi sermo Domini in opprobrium et in derisum tota die. Et in Osee Christus : Ego, inquit, redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia.
paras.en: [[68:13|They that sat in the gate spoke against me|Adversum me loquebantur qui sedebant in porta]], that is, the priests sitting by the gate of the temple and instructing the people, or the judges sitting in the gates of the city to give judgement, as was commanded through Moses: [[Deut 16:18|Thou shalt appoint judges and magistrates in all thy gates|Judices constitues in omnibus portis tuis]]. These spoke against Christ, turning the common people away from Him, so far that at last they asked that a murderer be granted them, and that Jesus be put to death. [[68:13|and they that drank wine made me their song|Et in me]], that is, of me and against me, [[68:13|made me their song|psallebant]], that is, they sang in mockery, [[68:13|they that drank wine|qui bibebant vinum]], that is, the gluttonous Jews. For they made up mocking songs and sang them about the Lord our Saviour, such as this: [[Matt 11:19|a man that is a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of publicans|Homo vorax, potator vini, amicus publicanorum]]. Hence it is said through Jeremias: [[Jer 20:8|the word of the Lord is made a reproach to me, and a derision all the day|Factus est mihi sermo Domini in opprobrium et in derisum tota die]]. And in Osee Christ says: [[Osee 7:13|I|Ego]], He says, [[Osee 7:13|redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me|redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia]].

paras.t: Ego vero orationem meam ad te, Domine Deus Pater, direxi et infudi, orando pro persecutoribus meis, quemadmodum per Prophetam ad te locutus sum : Recordare quod steterim in conspectu tuo, ut loquerer pro eis bona, et averterem indignationem tuam ab eis. Et in Evangelio dixi : Pater, ignosce illis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt. Tempus beneplaciti, Deus : id est, exaudire me debes, o Deus Pater, quoniam tempus meum quo fui in mundo, est tempus reconciliationis et gratiæ. De quo ait Apostolus : Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis.
paras.en: [[68:14|But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord|Ego vero orationem meam ad te, Domine]], God the Father: that is, I directed it and poured it out, praying for my persecutors, as I spoke to Thee through the Prophet: [[Jer 18:20|Remember that I have stood in thy sight, to speak good for them, and to turn away thy indignation from them|Recordare quod steterim in conspectu tuo, ut loquerer pro eis bona, et averterem indignationem tuam ab eis]]. And in the Gospel I said: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do|Pater, ignosce illis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt]]. [[68:14|for the time of thy good pleasure, O God|Tempus beneplaciti, Deus]]: that is, Thou oughtest to hear me, O God the Father, since my time, in which I was in the world, is the time of reconciliation and grace. Of which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time: behold, now is the day of salvation|Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis]].

paras.t: In multitudine misericordiæ tuæ, id est secundum et propter magnam misericordiam tuam, exaudi me in veritate salutis tuæ, quam peto a te, videlicet ut veram beatitudinem seu salutem, quæ a te solo præstatur, dones mihi atque Ecclesiæ, pro cujus salvatione cuncta sustineo. Salus autem seu beatitudo est duplex, scilicet essentialis, quæ est fruitio Dei, et accidentalis, quæ in bonis creatis consistit. Primam beatitudinem anima Christi a principio habuit, nec eam sibi nunc petit, sed eam petit Ecclesiæ peregrinanti ac militanti. Secundam vero beatitudinem quæ est præmium accidentale, Christus postulat sibi nunc et in versibus qui sequuntur. Hinc enim Christus pro Ecclesiæ salute orans, postulat ei præmium essentiale a Patre, dicendo : Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam quam dedisti mihi. Hæc autem visio est tota merces.
