paras.en: [[68:14|In the multitude of thy mercy|In multitudine misericordiæ tuæ]], that is, according to and because of Thy great mercy, [[68:14|hear me, in the truth of thy salvation|exaudi me in veritate salutis tuæ]], which I ask of Thee: namely, that Thou give true beatitude or salvation, which is bestowed by Thee alone, to me and to the Church, for whose salvation I endure all things. Now salvation or beatitude is twofold: essential, which is the enjoyment of God, and accidental, which consists in created goods [the essential reward is the vision and enjoyment of God itself; the accidental, the further joys added to it]. The first beatitude the soul of Christ had from the beginning, and He does not ask it now for Himself, but asks it for the Church, still on pilgrimage and in warfare. But the second beatitude, which is the accidental reward, Christ asks for Himself, here and in the verses that follow. For hence Christ, praying for the salvation of the Church, asks the essential reward for her from the Father, saying: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory which thou hast given me|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam quam dedisti mihi]]. And this vision is the whole reward.

paras.t: Eripe me de luto, ut non infigar. Lutum et limus idem sunt. Quum ergo Christus superius dixit, Infixus sum in limo profundi, quomodo nunc orat eripi ut non infigatur? Dicendum ergo, quod Christus ad tempus erat infixus in limo, secundum sensum inductum; nunc vero orat educi seu eripi, ne diu aut semper maneat luto infixus. Est itaque sensus : Eripe me, Deus Pater, de luto, id est de mundo terreno, de malignorum consortio, sepulturæque loco; ut non infigar, id est, ne diutius quam a te ordinatum est, in hoc luto permaneam. Desideravit etenim Christus de hoc mundo redire ad Patrem, et de conventu malignorum ad societatem conscendere angelorum. Unde discipulis ait : Si diligeretis me, gauderetis utique, quia vado ad Patrem ; et, O generatio incredula, quamdiu apud vos ero? Libera me ab his qui oderunt me, id est a Judæis, suscitando me ad impassibilem statum, et de profundis aquarum, hoc est a vehementia persecutionum.
paras.en: [[68:15|Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast|Eripe me de luto, ut non infigar]]. *Lutum* and *limus* [the words of this verse and of verse 3, both "mire" in the Douay-Rheims] are the same thing. Since, then, Christ said above, [[68:3|I stick fast in the mire of the deep|Infixus sum in limo profundi]], how does He now pray to be drawn out, that He may not stick fast? It must be said, then, that Christ was for a time stuck fast in the mire, in the sense given above; but now He prays to be led out or drawn out, lest He remain long, or for ever, stuck fast in the mire. The sense, then, is: *Draw me out*, O God the Father, *of the mire*, that is, of the earthly world, of the company of the wicked, and of the place of burial; *that I may not stick fast*, that is, that I may not remain in this mire longer than Thou hast ordained. For Christ desired to return from this world to the Father, and to rise from the assembly of the wicked to the fellowship of the angels. Hence He says to the disciples: [[John 14:28|If you loved me you would indeed be glad, because I go to the Father|Si diligeretis me, gauderetis utique, quia vado ad Patrem]]; and, [[Mark 9:18|O incredulous generation, how long shall I be with you|O generatio incredula, quamdiu apud vos ero?]]? [[68:15|deliver me from them that hate me|Libera me ab his qui oderunt me]], that is, from the Jews, by raising me up to the state in which I cannot suffer, [[68:15|and out of the deep waters|et de profundis aquarum]], that is, from the violence of persecutions.

paras.t: Non me demergat tempestas aquæ : id est, impetus mortis mihi illatæ, de qua superius dixi, Tempestas demersit me, non me demergat penitus, scilicet ut non permaneam mortuus usque ad diem universalis resurrectionis, sed a voragine mortis tertia die eripiar. Neque absorbeat me profundum, id est fovea monumenti, videlicet ne corpus meum in sepulcro permanens corrumpatur ; sed ab hoc profundo exalta me per resurrectionem acceleratam ; neque urgeat super me puteus os suum : id est, limbus sanctorum patrum in quem descendi, non diu me teneat, nec os, id est aditum suum, super animam meam obturet seu claudat ; sed quemadmodum corpus peto educi a conclusione sepulcri, sic animam meam peto eripi a limbo inferni : sicut superius dictum est, Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno.
paras.en: [[68:16|Let not the tempest of water drown me|Non me demergat tempestas aquæ]]: that is, let the onslaught of the death brought upon me, of which I said above, [[68:3|a tempest hath overwhelmed me|Tempestas demersit me]], not *drown me* utterly, namely so that I do not remain dead until the day of the general resurrection, but am snatched from the abyss of death on the third day. [[68:16|nor the deep water swallow me up|Neque absorbeat me profundum]], that is, the pit of the tomb: namely, let not my body, remaining in the sepulchre, be corrupted; but raise me up from this deep by a speedy resurrection. [[68:16|and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me|neque urgeat super me puteus os suum]]: that is, let not the limbo of the holy fathers, into which I descended, hold me long, nor close or shut its *mouth*, that is, its entrance, upon my soul; but as I ask that my body be brought out of the enclosure of the sepulchre, so I ask that my soul be delivered from the limbo of hell: as was said above, [[Ps 15:10|Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell|Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno]].

68.title: PROSECUTIO EXPOSITIONIS LITTERALIS PSALMI SEXAGESIMI OCTAVI.
68.title_en: Continuation of the literal exposition of the sixty-eighth psalm.

paras.t: EXAUDI me, Domine Pater, in orationibus jam præmissis, quoniam benigna est misericordia tua : id est, ideo me exaudi, quia dulcis est misericordia tua, sicque propter eam exaudi me. Quamvis enim Christus justo Dei judicio exaudiri meruit merito conversationis suæ sanctissimæ, orat tamen exaudiri propter misericordiam bonitatis divinæ : primo, ut nobis præstet exemplum, quo semper innitamur misericordiæ Dei, non propriis meritis ; secundo, quoniam misericordia Dei, sicut justitiam animæ Christi creatam in infinitum excedit, sic incomparabiliter major est ratio exaudiendi propter divinam misericordiam, quam propter quamcumque justitiam creatam. Secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum respice in me oculo dilectionis paternæ, et subveni mihi sicut precatus sum. Miseratio dicitur actus misericordiæ ; misericordia autem Dei, in se una est ac simplex. Dicuntur tamen multæ misericordiæ, propter diversos effectus misericordiæ Dei, vel potius propter plenitudinem bonitatis divinæ, qua Deus novit variis modis, imo infinitis, succurrere suis. Si autem miseratio Dei dicatur ipse actus Dei miserentis, in ipso consistens, sic eodem modo miseratio Dei est una et plures, sicut de misericordia dictum est. Si vero dicatur miseratio Dei, effectus misericordiæ ejus, sic miserationes Dei sunt realiter multæ.
paras.en: [[68:17|Hear me, O Lord|EXAUDI me, Domine]] Father, in the prayers already offered, [[68:17|for thy mercy is kind|quoniam benigna est misericordia tua]]: that is, hear me for this reason, that thy mercy is sweet, and so hear me for its sake. For although Christ, by the just judgement of God, deserved to be heard by the merit of his most holy life, yet he prays to be heard on account of the mercy of the divine goodness: first, to give us an example, so that we may always lean on the mercy of God and not on our own merits; secondly, because, as the mercy of God infinitely exceeds the created justice of Christ's soul, so there is incomparably greater reason for hearing him on account of the divine mercy than on account of any created justice whatever. And [[68:17|according to the multitude of thy tender mercies|Secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum]] [[68:17|look upon me|respice in me]] with the eye of fatherly love, and help me as I have prayed. Miseratio [tender mercy: the act of pity, as distinct from misericordia, mercy] is said to be the act of mercy; but the mercy of God is in itself one and simple. Yet many mercies are spoken of, because of the diverse effects of God's mercy, or rather because of the fullness of the divine goodness, by which God knows how to succour his own in various, nay in infinite, ways. If, then, God's miseratio is taken for the very act of God showing mercy, which consists in him, then in the same way God's miseratio is both one and many, as was said of mercy. But if God's miseratio is taken for the effect of his mercy, then God's tender mercies are really many.

paras.t: Et ne avertas faciem tuam, id est pium et gratiosum tuum respectum, a puero tuo, id est a me Unigenito tuo. Quoniam tribulor usque ad mortem in die Parasceves, idcirco velociter exaudi me, non differendo ultra triduum corporis mei glorificationem.
paras.en: [[68:18|And turn not away thy face|Et ne avertas faciem tuam]], that is, thy kind and gracious regard, [[68:18|from thy servant|a puero tuo]] [puer, a boy or a servant], that is, from me, thy Only-begotten. Because [[68:18|I am in trouble|tribulor]] even unto death on the day of the Parasceve [the day of preparation, Good Friday], therefore [[68:18|hear me speedily|velociter exaudi me]], not putting off the glorification of my body beyond three days.

paras.t: Intende animæ meæ, preces ejus ac vota exaudiens ; et libera eam ab interioribus pœnis, quas habuit tempore passionis, a timore atque tristitia. Propter inimicos meos Judæos, eripe me ab omni mortalitatis passibilitatisque statu, ut odium et pravitas eorum adversus me, sit tibi occasio succurrendi Filio tuo dilecto. Vel : Propter inimicos meos, id est propter salutem eorum, eripe me de sepulcro, ne in infidelitate sua persistant, sed audita prædicatione Evangelii, convertantur ad me, sicut eis testatus sum : Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum. Quod in Actibus Apostolorum impletum ostenditur, ubi octo millia Judæorum conversa leguntur, multa quoque turba sacerdotum conversa asseritur.
paras.en: [[68:19|Attend to my soul|Intende animæ meæ]], hearing its prayers and desires; [[68:19|and deliver it|et libera eam]] from the inward pains which it had in the time of the passion, from fear and sadness. Because of [[68:19|my enemies|Propter inimicos meos]] the Jews, [[68:19|save me|eripe me]] from every state of mortality and passibility, so that their hatred and wickedness against me may be to thee an occasion of succouring thy beloved Son. Or: [[68:19|because of my enemies|Propter inimicos meos]], that is, for their salvation, [[68:19|save me|eripe me]] from the sepulchre, lest they persist in their unbelief; may they rather, having heard the preaching of the Gospel, be converted to me, as I testified to them: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]]. This is shown fulfilled in the Acts of the Apostles, where eight thousand Jews are read to have been converted[[Acts 2:41||]][[Acts 4:4||]] [three thousand at Acts 2:41 and five thousand at 4:4], and a great multitude of priests too is said to have been converted[[Acts 6:7||]].

paras.t: Tu, Domine Pater, scis improperium meum, id est injuriam verborum mihi dictorum, et confusionem meam, id est contemptum et vilipensionem adversariorum meorum, me pro nihilo æstimantium ; et reverentiam meam. Non sumitur hic reverentia pro veneratione, sed pro verecundia seu ignominia. Verecundia autem proprie sumpta, est timor dehonestationis, seu pavor de re turpi, ad vitandum difficili. Sic vero eam sumendo, non habuit locum in Christo. Scivit enim nil inhonestum a se fieri posse ; nec aliquo modo erubuit propter injurias sibi illatas, sed per patientiam in adversis gaudebat. Quomodo ergo fuerunt in eo reverentia, id est verecundia, atque confusio ? nisi quod illa quæ aliis solent esse causa confusionis et verecundiæ, abundanter in ipso fuerunt, quum ipse sit tanquam latro captus, consputus, nudatus, et inter iniquos suspensus. In conspectu tuo, id est tibi cogniti, sunt omnes qui tribulant me, videlicet sacerdotes, Scribæ, Pharisæi, ac ceteri ; et tuæ potestati subjecti sunt, potesque me de eorum manu eripere et eos opprimere.
paras.en: [[68:20|Thou|Tu]], O Lord Father, [[68:20|knowest my reproach|scis improperium meum]], that is, the wrong of the words spoken against me, [[68:20|and my confusion|et confusionem meam]], that is, the contempt and disparagement of my adversaries, who count me as nothing; [[68:20|and my shame|et reverentiam meam]] [Latin reverentia, which usually means reverence]. Reverentia is not taken here for veneration, but for bashfulness or ignominy. Now bashfulness, properly taken, is the fear of disgrace, or dread of something base that is hard to avoid. Taken in this way, it had no place in Christ. For he knew that nothing dishonourable could be done by him; nor did he blush in any way at the wrongs done to him, but through patience he rejoiced in adversity. How then were shame, that is, bashfulness, and confusion in him? Only in this, that the things which are wont to be a cause of confusion and shame to others were abundantly in him, since he was taken like a thief, spat upon, stripped, and hung among the wicked. [[68:21|In thy sight|In conspectu tuo]], that is, known to thee, [[68:21|are all they that afflict me|sunt omnes qui tribulant me]], namely the priests, Scribes, Pharisees and the rest; and they are subject to thy power, and thou canst snatch me out of their hand and crush them.

paras.t: Improperium exspectavit cor meum et miseriam. Quanto tempus passionis amplius appropinquavit, tanto Christus de viciniori exspectavit injuriam verborum et irrogationem pœnarum. Unde passionem suam Apostolis sæpe prædixit, et passione jam proxima, propter exspectationem pœnarum imminentium, in tantum expavit, quod factus est sudor ejus sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentis in terram. Et sustinui, id est, exspectavi et consideravi, qui simul contristaretur, compatiendo doloribus meis : et non fuit qui condoleret. Sustinui quoque et qui consolaretur me tristem, et non inveni. Hoc Christus asserit, non quod sibi nemo condoluit, aut consolationem sibi impendere concupivit, præsertim quum scriptum sit : Sequebatur illum multa turba populi et mulierum, quæ plangebant et lamentabantur eum. Et Apostolis dixit, passione instante : Et nunc quidem tristitiam habetis ; iterum autem videbo vos, et gaudebit cor vestrum. Sed quia pauci contristabantur respectu aliorum, et quod modicum est, pro nihilo reputatur ; idcirco asserit non fuisse qui consolaretur. Et simili modo per alium Prophetam ait : Circumspexi, et non erat auxiliator. Ad minus enim Petrus adjuvit, qui Malcho aurem abscidit.
paras.en: [[68:21|My heart hath expected reproach and misery|Improperium exspectavit cor meum et miseriam]]. The nearer the time of the passion drew, the more closely Christ expected the wrong of words and the infliction of pains. Hence he often foretold his passion to the Apostles; and when the passion was now at hand, through the expectation of the pains hanging over him, he was so greatly afraid that [[Luke 22:44|his sweat became as drops of blood, trickling down upon the ground|factus est sudor ejus sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentis in terram]]. [[68:21|And I looked for|Et sustinui]], that is, I awaited and considered, [[68:21|one that would grieve together with me|qui simul contristaretur]], by compassion with my sorrows: [[68:21|but there was none|et non fuit]] to share my grief. I looked also [[68:21|for one that would comfort me|et qui consolaretur]] in my sadness, [[68:21|and I found none|et non inveni]]. Christ says this, not because no one grieved with him or desired to give him comfort, especially since it is written: [[Luke 23:27|And there followed him a great multitude of people and of women, who bewailed and lamented him|Sequebatur illum multa turba populi et mulierum, quæ plangebant et lamentabantur eum]]; and he said to the Apostles when the passion was at hand: And you [[John 16:22|now indeed have sorrow: but I will see you again and your heart shall rejoice|nunc quidem tristitiam habetis ; iterum autem videbo vos, et gaudebit cor vestrum]]. But because few were saddened in comparison with the others, and what is little is reckoned as nothing, he therefore says there was none to comfort him. And in like manner he says through another Prophet: [[Is 63:5|I looked about, and there was none to help|Circumspexi, et non erat auxiliator]]. For Peter at least did help, he who cut off Malchus's ear[[John 18:10||]].

paras.t: Et dederunt in escam meam fel, et in siti mea potaverunt me aceto. Non leguntur Judæi Christo crucifixo fel seorsum dedisse, sed acetum felle mixtum. Dicit enim Matthæus evangelista : Dederunt ei vinum bibere cum felle mixtum. Et Marcus : Dabant ei bibere vinum myrrhatum. Joannes autem : Vas positum erat aceto plenum. Quoniam ergo in eo quod Christo offerebant, nil erat solidum comestionive aptum, nisi fel ; ideo ait, Dederunt in escam meam fel. Christus quoque in cruce corporaliter sitiebat, dicentique, Sitio, acetum porrigebant : quod et accepit, secundum Joannem. Marcus tamen dicit quod non accepit. Sed non est discordia. Parum enim quasi gustando accepit, statimque potare cessavit : propter quod scriptum est, Quum gustasset, noluit bibere. Denique, quod Matthæus affirmat vinum illud fuisse fellitum, et Marcus myrrhatum, facile concordatur : vel quia commixtum erat myrrhæ ac felli ; vel quia Marcus dicit illud myrrhatum, propter qualitatem, scilicet amaritudinem potus, non propter substantiam myrrhæ.
paras.en: [[68:22|And they gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink|Et dederunt in escam meam fel, et in siti mea potaverunt me aceto]]. The Jews are not read to have given gall by itself to Christ crucified, but vinegar mixed with gall. For Matthew the evangelist says: [[Matt 27:34|They gave him wine to drink mingled with gall|Dederunt ei vinum bibere cum felle mixtum]]. And Mark: [[Mark 15:23|They gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh|Dabant ei bibere vinum myrrhatum]]. And John: [[John 19:29|There was a vessel set there, full of vinegar|Vas positum erat aceto plenum]]. Since, then, in what they offered to Christ there was nothing solid or fit for eating except the gall, he therefore says: [[68:22|They gave me gall for my food|Dederunt in escam meam fel]]. Christ also thirsted bodily on the cross, and when he said, [[John 19:28|I thirst|Sitio]], they held out vinegar to him[[John 19:29||]]; and this he took, according to John[[John 19:30||]]. Mark, however, says that he did not take it[[Mark 15:23||]] [the margin's "Ibid. 28" and "Ibid. 29, 30" stand beside these two sentences and refer to John 19:28–30; Mark's words are at Mark 15:23]. But there is no disagreement. For he took a little, as if tasting it, and at once ceased to drink: for which reason it is written, [[Matt 27:34|When he had tasted, he would not drink|Quum gustasset, noluit bibere]]. Lastly, that Matthew affirms that wine to have been mixed with gall[[Matt 27:34||]], and Mark that it was mixed with myrrh, is easily reconciled: either because it was mingled with both myrrh and gall; or because Mark calls it myrrhed on account of its quality, namely the bitterness of the drink, not on account of the substance of myrrh.

paras.t: Fiat mensa eorum coram ipsis in laqueum : id est, cibus iste et potus, quem mihi ex invidia porrigebant, sit eis causa captivationis, fiatque eis laqueus animæ et corporis. Judæi enim propter hanc Christi felleam potationem meruerunt in obsidione a Romanis illata, inæstimabili fame ac siti torqueri, et tandem captivari. Dando etiam Christo hunc potum, illaqueata et capta est anima eorum vinculo peccatorum et laqueo vitiorum, secundum quod in Proverbiis scriptum est : Iniquitates suæ capiunt impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringitur. Fiat etiam eis et in retributiones damnationis æternæ et infernalium tormentorum, et in scandalum, id est in confusionem. Maxima enim confusio Judæorum est, quod Messiam sibi in lege promissum occiderunt. Vel, In scandalum, id est in occasionem amplioris ruinæ, quia per hanc mensam meruerunt de peccato in peccatum incidere. Vel sic : Fiat mensa eorum, id est Scriptura legis et Prophetarum, in qua refectio animæ continetur, coram ipsis in laqueum, ita ut a Christianis convincantur Christum occidisse ex propriis libris ; et in retributiones, id est in graviorem damnationem. Quanto enim se sapientiores putabant, et quanto plura de Christo legerant, tanto gravius peccaverunt quod præsentem non agnoverunt, sed negaverunt et crucifixerunt. Hinc enim Christus in Evangelio ait ad eos : Si cæci essetis, non haberetis peccatum ; nunc autem quia dicitis, Quia videmus, peccatum vestrum manet. Et in scandalum. Nam sacra Scriptura veteris Testamenti est eis occasio quotidiani erroris. Quoniam enim in Christum credere nolunt, illam extorte et false exponunt, et per falsam expositionem perfidiam suam confirmant. Ad litteram quoque mensa Judæorum facta est eis in laqueum. Nam ante obsidionem a Tito, convenerunt omnes in Jerusalem ad celebrandum paschale convivium, quod extra Jerusalem celebrari non licuit : et antequam egrederentur, a Romanis obsessi sunt, puniti, atque confusi. Hæc autem atque sequentia non optando, sed prænuntiando dicuntur. Non enim dicuntur per modum orationis, ut fiant ; sed per modum prophetiæ, quoniam fient, quemadmodum Jeremias etiam prophetavit : Tu, Domine, scis omne consilium eorum adversum me ; ne propitieris iniquitati eorum, et peccatum eorum non deleatur.
paras.en: [[68:23|Let their table become as a snare before them|Fiat mensa eorum coram ipsis in laqueum]]: that is, let this food and drink which they held out to me out of envy be to them a cause of captivity, and let it become to them a snare of soul and body. For on account of this drink of gall given to Christ the Jews deserved, in the siege brought upon them by the Romans, to be tormented with unspeakable hunger and thirst, and at last to be taken captive. Also, in giving Christ this drink, their soul was ensnared and taken with the chain of sins and the snare of vices, according to what is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capiunt impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringitur]]. Let it also become to them [[68:23|a recompense|et in retributiones]] of eternal damnation and of the torments of hell, [[68:23|and a stumblingblock|et in scandalum]], that is, a confusion. For the greatest confusion of the Jews is that they slew the Messias promised to them in the law. Or, [[68:23|a stumblingblock|In scandalum]], that is, an occasion of a greater fall, because through this table they deserved to fall from sin into sin. Or thus: [[68:23|Let their table|Fiat mensa eorum]], that is, the Scripture of the law and the Prophets, in which the refreshment of the soul is contained, [[68:23|become as a snare before them|coram ipsis in laqueum]], so that they are convicted by Christians, out of their own books, of having slain Christ; [[68:23|and a recompense|et in retributiones]], that is, a heavier damnation. For the wiser they thought themselves, and the more they had read about Christ, the more grievously they sinned in not acknowledging him when he was present, but denying and crucifying him. Hence Christ says to them in the Gospel: [[John 9:41|If you were blind, you should not have sin: but now you say: We see. Your sin remaineth|Si cæci essetis, non haberetis peccatum ; nunc autem quia dicitis, Quia videmus, peccatum vestrum manet]]. [[68:23|And a stumblingblock|Et in scandalum]]: for the sacred Scripture of the Old Testament is to them an occasion of daily error. Since they will not believe in Christ, they expound it in a forced and false way, and by this false exposition confirm their unbelief. Literally, too, the table of the Jews became a snare to them. For before the siege by Titus they all gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the paschal feast, which might not be celebrated outside Jerusalem; and before they could leave they were besieged by the Romans, punished and confounded. Now these things and those that follow are said not as wishes but as foretellings. For they are not said by way of prayer, that they may happen, but by way of prophecy, because they will happen; as Jeremias also prophesied: [[Jer 18:23|Thou, O Lord, knowest all their counsel against me|Tu, Domine, scis omne consilium eorum adversum me]]; forgive [[Jer 18:23|not their iniquity|ne propitieris iniquitati eorum]], [[Jer 18:23|and let not their sin be blotted out|et peccatum eorum non deleatur]].

paras.t: Obscurentur oculi eorum ne videant : id est, corda Judæorum, propter peccatum in Christum commissum, lumine veritatis priventur, et omnino cæca reddantur. Excæcationem Judæorum in primo adventu Christi, sancti Prophetæ copiosissime prædixerunt, et maxime sacratissimus Isaias, cujus testimonia in epistola ad Romanos Apostolus abundanter inducit. Nempe sic ait Propheta : Quis cæcus, nisi servus Domini ? Et quis surdus, nisi ad quem nun[tios] meos misi? Et alibi : Excæcatum est cor populi hujus, et auribus graviter audierunt. Et iterum Dominus ait per Isaiam de populo Judæorum : Tota die expandi manus meas ad populum incredulum. Et dorsum eorum semper incurva. Est quoddam dorsum mentis, in quo devoti portant jugum Domini seu divina præcepta. Hoc dorsum est ipsa voluntas, in qua virtus et vitium primo atque præcipue inveniuntur. Est igitur sensus : Dorsum eorum, id est voluntatem, affectum, seu appetitum Judæorum, semper incurva, id est, ad terrena et vana converte, ad falsa deflecte, ad obliquitatem culpæ inclina. Hoc videmus in Judæis impletum, quum sint avari, a summo bono aversi, suisque erroribus indesinenter intenti. Nam et in adventu Messiæ, quem putant venturum, exspectant temporale regnum adipisci, et universis hostibus suis dominari. Dicitur autem Deus dorsum eorum incurvare, non effective, sed permissive, quemadmodum dicitur Pharaonem indurasse.
paras.en: [[68:24|Let their eyes be darkened that they see not|Obscurentur oculi eorum ne videant]]: that is, let the hearts of the Jews, for the sin committed against Christ, be deprived of the light of truth and made altogether blind. The blinding of the Jews at the first coming of Christ the holy Prophets foretold most abundantly, and above all the most holy Isaias, whose testimonies the Apostle brings in abundantly in the epistle to the Romans[[Rom 9:27||]][[Rom 11:8||]] [the margin gives only the chapters, Rom. ix and xi; Isaias is quoted there at 9:27–29 and 9:33, and this verse of the Psalm at 11:9–10]. Thus the Prophet says: [[Is 42:19|Who is blind, but the servant of the Lord|Quis cæcus, nisi servus Domini]]? [[Is 42:19|Or deaf, but he to whom I have sent my messengers|Et quis surdus, nisi ad quem]]? And elsewhere: The heart of this people is blinded[[Is 6:10||]], and [[Matt 13:15|with their ears they have been dull of hearing|et auribus graviter audierunt]] [the margin gives "Ibid. xi, 10", surely Is. vi, 10 misread, and Matt. xiii, 15; Denis's words follow Matthew, but with excæcatum, blinded, for "grown gross"]. And again the Lord says through Isaias of the people of the Jews: [[Is 65:2|I have spread forth my hands all the day to an unbelieving people|Tota die expandi manus meas ad populum incredulum]]. [[68:24|And their back bend thou down always|Et dorsum eorum semper incurva]]. There is a certain back of the mind, on which the devout carry the yoke of the Lord, that is, the divine precepts. This back is the will itself, in which virtue and vice are first and chiefly found. The sense, then, is: [[68:24|their back|Dorsum eorum]], that is, the will, affection or appetite of the Jews, [[68:24|bend thou down always|semper incurva]]: that is, turn it to earthly and vain things, bend it aside to falsehoods, incline it to the crookedness of sin. This we see fulfilled in the Jews, since they are covetous, turned away from the highest good, and ceaselessly intent on their errors. For even at the coming of the Messias, whom they think is yet to come, they expect to obtain a temporal kingdom and to rule over all their enemies. Now God is said to bend their back down not by causing it but by permitting it, as he is said to have hardened Pharao[[Ex 4:21||]][[Ex 7:3||]][[Ex 11:10||]][[Ex 14:4||]] [the margin gives only the chapters, Exod. iv, vii, xi, xiv].

paras.t: Effunde super eos iram tuam, id est ultionem tuæ justitiæ, tradendo eos in manus Romanorum : et furor iræ tuæ, id est gravissima tua vindicta, comprehendat eos, videlicet ut usque in finem mundi in sua cæcitate permaneant, et vagi in nationibus sint, Christumque incessanter blasphement, et multis opprimantur ærumnis. Nisi enim furor iræ Dei eos comprehendisset, mirum videretur quomodo tam gravissime excæcari valerent, quod captivitatem suam non adverterent. Unde in Isaia ait Christus : Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea ; et in Jeremia : Facta est mihi hereditas mea, videlicet domus seu populus Israel, quasi leo in silva; dedit contra me vocem suam, ideo odivi eam. Quod alius apertius dicit : Exosos habui eos propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum; non addam ut diligam eos. Et Sophonias apertissime protestatur : Effundam super eos indignationem meam, et omnem iram furoris mei.
paras.en: [[68:25|Pour out thy indignation upon them|Effunde super eos iram tuam]], that is, the vengeance of thy justice, by delivering them into the hands of the Romans: [[68:25|and let thy wrathful anger|et furor iræ tuæ]], that is, thy most heavy vengeance, [[68:25|take hold of them|comprehendat eos]], namely so that they remain in their blindness until the end of the world, and are wanderers among the nations, and blaspheme Christ unceasingly, and are oppressed with many hardships. For unless the wrathful anger of God had taken hold of them, it would seem a wonder how they could be so very grievously blinded as not to perceive their own captivity. Hence Christ says in Isaias: [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]]; and in Jeremias: [[Jer 12:8|My inheritance is become to me|Facta est mihi hereditas mea]], namely the house or people of Israel, [[Jer 12:8|as a lion in the wood: it hath cried out against me, therefore have I hated it|quasi leo in silva; dedit contra me vocem suam, ideo odivi eam]]. Which another says more plainly: [[Osee 9:15|I hated them|Exosos habui eos]] [[Osee 9:15|for the wickedness of their devices|propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum]]; [[Osee 9:15|I will love them no more|non addam ut diligam eos]]. And Sophonias declares it most plainly: I will [[Soph 3:8|pour upon them my indignation, all my fierce anger|Effundam super eos indignationem meam, et omnem iram furoris mei]].

paras.t: Fiat habitatio eorum deserta, et in tabernaculis eorum non sit qui inhabitet. Romani enim civitatem Jerusalem et templum ac reliquas urbes Judææ penitus destruxerunt, sicut et Christus prædixit : Non relinquent in te lapidem super lapidem, eo quod non cognoveris tempus visitationis tuæ ; et Jeremias, Reliqui domum meam, dimisi hereditatem meam. Hinc et Osee propheta dixit : Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus; et erunt vagi in nationibus.
paras.en: [[68:26|Let their habitation be made desolate: and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles|Fiat habitatio eorum deserta, et in tabernaculis eorum non sit qui inhabitet]]. For the Romans utterly destroyed the city of Jerusalem and the temple and the other cities of Judea, as Christ also foretold: [[Luke 19:44|They shall not leave in thee a stone upon a stone: because thou hast not known the time of thy visitation|Non relinquent in te lapidem super lapidem, eo quod non cognoveris tempus visitationis tuæ]]; and Jeremias: [[Jer 12:7|I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance|Reliqui domum meam, dimisi hereditatem meam]]. Hence the prophet Osee too said: [[Osee 9:17|My God will cast them away, because they hearkened not to him|Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus]]; [[Osee 9:17|and they shall be wanderers among the nations|et erunt vagi in nationibus]].

paras.t: Deinceps ponitur causa tantæ dejectionis Judæorum : Quoniam quem tu percussisti, persecuti sunt, id est, Jesum Christum quem tu percuti permisisti, usque ad mortem tribulaverunt. Dicitur enim Deus Christum percussisse, quemadmodum Isaias prædixit : Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum. Petrus quoque inquit : Jesum definito consilio et præscientia Dei traditum, viri Israelitæ, interemistis. Sic enim Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret. Et super dolorem vulnerum meorum addiderunt. Judæi enim supra injuriam verberum, intulerunt Christo injuriam verborum, irridendo blasphemandoque eum. Sed et ultra dolorem Christo inflictum in proprio corpore, addiderunt injuriam infligere corpori suo mystico, scilicet primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quam graviter molestabant, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum ostenditur.
paras.en: Next is set down the cause of so great a casting down of the Jews: [[68:27|Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten|Quoniam quem tu percussisti, persecuti sunt]], that is, Jesus Christ, whom thou didst permit to be smitten, they afflicted even unto death. For God is said to have smitten Christ, as Isaias foretold: [[Is 53:8|For the wickedness of my people have I struck him|Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum]]. Peter too says: Jesus, [[Acts 2:23|being delivered up, by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God|definito consilio et præscientia Dei traditum]], you, men of Israel, have [[Acts 2:23|slain|interemistis]]. For [[John 3:16|God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son|Sic enim Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret]]. [[68:27|And they have added to the grief of my wounds|Et super dolorem vulnerum meorum addiderunt]]. For over and above the wrong of blows, the Jews did Christ the wrong of words, mocking and blaspheming him. And beyond the pain inflicted on Christ in his own body, they went on to inflict wrong on his mystical body, namely the primitive Church, which they grievously harassed, as is shown in the Acts of the Apostles.

paras.t: Appone, o Domine, non effective, sed permissive, iniquitatem super iniquitatem ipsorum, permittendo eos cadere de culpa in culpam. Quum enim homo sine gratia Dei nil boni agere possit, dum Deus hominem exigentibus vitiis suis gratia spoliat, de peccato in peccatum continuo cadit. Et non intrent in justitiam tuam. Introitus seu ostium justitiæ est fides. Justus namque ex fide vivit. Quid ergo est, Non intrent in justitiam tuam, nisi fide Christi priventur, et mandatis ejus non pareant, sed in suis perversitatibus perseverent ?
paras.en: [[68:28|Add thou|Appone]], O Lord, not by causing it but by permitting it, [[68:28|iniquity upon their iniquity|iniquitatem super iniquitatem ipsorum]], by permitting them to fall from fault into fault. For since man without the grace of God can do nothing good, when God, as a man's vices demand, strips him of grace, he falls continually from sin into sin. [[68:28|And let them not come into thy justice|Et non intrent in justitiam tuam]]. The entrance or door of justice is faith; for the [[Rom 1:17|just man liveth by faith|Justus namque ex fide vivit]][[Hab 2:4||]]. What, then, is [[68:28|Let them not come into thy justice|Non intrent in justitiam tuam]], but that they be deprived of the faith of Christ, and not obey his commandments, but persevere in their perversities?

paras.t: Deleantur de libro viventium. Liber viventium, seu liber vitæ, est prædestinatio electorum in mente divina : quia quemadmodum fixum et firmum est quod in libro fuerit scriptum, sic quod in sapientia mentis divinæ decretum est, stabile manet et variari non potest. Quomodo igitur aliquis de libro viventium valet deleri, præsertim quum nemo scriptus sit in hoc libro, nisi electus? Liber enim vitæ est notitia Dei, qua prædestinavit electos. Et respondendum, quod dupliciter dicitur aliquis in libro viventium scriptus. Primo, secundum veritatem : et taliter scriptus, deleri non potest. Unde Christus in libro vitæ scriptos perire non posse insinuans, ait : Surgent pseudoprophetæ et pseudochristi, et dabunt signa magna et prodigia, ita ut in errorem inducantur, si fieri potest, etiam electi. Secundo dicitur aliquis scriptus in libro viventium, secundum suam spem vanam et opinionem fallacem. Hoc modo erant scripti Judæi, qui se præelectos a Deo opinantes, ceteros contempserunt, et Christum occiderunt. Et simili modo Christus in Evangelio appellat eos filios regni, non quod vere erant filii regni : filius namque manet in domo in æternum. Sed filii regni erant secundum suam superbissimam opinionem, dicentes ad Salvatorem : Unum habemus patrem Deum. Quorum errorem Christus declarans : Vos, inquit, ex patre diabolo estis. Sic autem de libro vitæ deleri, aliud non est, nisi in eo non scribi, nec in divinæ pietatis memoria contineri. Idcirco, quasi exponens quod dixit, Deleantur de libro viventium, subdit : et cum justis non scribantur : non quod aliquis de novo possit libro vitæ inscribi ; sed dicitur Deus illud in libro vitæ scribere, quod finaliter approbat. Quoniam ergo reprobi nil Deo acceptum aut meritorium operantur, secundum quod tales sunt, dicuntur in libro vitæ non scribi.
paras.en: [[68:29|Let them be blotted out of the book of the living|Deleantur de libro viventium]]. The book of the living, or book of life, is the predestination of the elect in the divine mind: because, as what has been written in a book is fixed and firm, so what has been decreed in the wisdom of the divine mind remains stable and cannot be changed. How, then, can anyone be blotted out of the book of the living, especially since no one is written in this book but the elect? For the book of life is God's knowledge, by which he predestined the elect. The answer must be that a man is said to be written in the book of the living in two ways. First, according to truth: and one so written cannot be blotted out. Hence Christ, intimating that those written in the book of life cannot perish, says: [[Matt 24:24|there shall arise false Christs and false prophets and shall shew great signs and wonders, insomuch as to deceive (if possible) even the elect|Surgent pseudoprophetæ et pseudochristi, et dabunt signa magna et prodigia, ita ut in errorem inducantur, si fieri potest, etiam electi]]. Secondly, a man is said to be written in the book of the living according to his own vain hope and false opinion. In this way the Jews were written, who, thinking themselves chosen beforehand by God, despised the rest and slew Christ. And in like manner Christ in the Gospel calls them [[Matt 8:12|the children of the kingdom|filios regni]], not because they were truly children of the kingdom, for [[John 8:35|the son abideth for ever|filius namque manet in domo in æternum]] [Denis adds "in the house" from the first half of the verse]. But they were children of the kingdom in their own most proud opinion, saying to the Saviour: [[John 8:41|We have one Father, even God|Unum habemus patrem Deum]]. Declaring their error, Christ says: [[John 8:44|You|Vos]], he says, [[John 8:44|are of your father the devil|ex patre diabolo estis]]. To be blotted out of the book of life in this way, then, is nothing other than not to be written in it, nor to be held in the memory of the divine loving-kindness. Therefore, as though explaining what he said, [[68:29|Let them be blotted out of the book of the living|Deleantur de libro viventium]], he adds: [[68:29|and with the just let them not be written|et cum justis non scribantur]]: not that anyone can be newly written into the book of life; but God is said to write in the book of life what he finally approves. Since, then, the reprobate, as such, do nothing acceptable to God or meritorious, they are said not to be written in the book of life.

paras.t: Insuper Christus ait, Ego sum pauper. Pauperem namque matrem elegit, in paupertate vixit, in passione pauperrimus est effectus, quia nudus in cruce suspensus. Propter quod dixit : Vulpes foveas habent, et volucres cæli nidos ; Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput suum reclinet. Et dolens. Christus multos in hac vita dolores sustinuit, maxime tamen in passione dolorosissimus exstitit, quando a planta pedis usque ad verticem capitis, non remansit in eo sanitas. Salus tua, Deus, suscepit me : id est, beatitudo tua perfecta in resurrectione glorificavit me, quantum ad corpus; et ita salus tua, Deus Pater, suscepit me, id est, ego salutem tuam, videlicet præmium accidentale, in resurrectione suscepi.
paras.en: Moreover Christ says: [[68:30|I am poor|Ego sum pauper]]. For he chose a poor mother, lived in poverty, and in the passion became poorest of all, since he hung naked on the cross. For which reason he said: [[Matt 8:20|The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head|Vulpes foveas habent, et volucres cæli nidos ; Filius autem hominis non habet ubi caput suum reclinet]]. [[68:30|And sorrowful|Et dolens]]. Christ bore many sorrows in this life, but above all he was most full of sorrow in the passion, when [[Is 1:6|from the sole of the foot unto the top of the head|a planta pedis usque ad verticem capitis]] there remained no soundness in him. [[68:30|Thy salvation, O God, hath set me up|Salus tua, Deus, suscepit me]]: that is, thy perfect blessedness glorified me in the resurrection as regards the body; and so [[68:30|thy salvation|salus tua]], God the Father, [[68:30|hath set me up|suscepit me]], that is, I took up [suscepi: Denis turns the verb round, "thy salvation took me up", "I took up thy salvation"] thy salvation, namely the accidental reward [that is, glory added to the essential blessedness of the soul, here the glory of the body], in the resurrection.

paras.t: Laudabo nomen Dei cum cantico, id est cum spirituali lætitia et hilaritate interna, atque vocali melodia, si opus est ; et magnificabo eum in laude, id est, per laudem quam ei cantabo, dicam et offeram, confitebor et manifestabo quod Deus sit Dominus magnus atque laudabilis valde. Quemadmodum enim in Oratione dominica dicimus, Sanctificetur nomen tuum, non quod aliquid sanctitatis Deo ex nobis accrescat, sed quia per nostræ servitutis puritatem probatur et declaratur esse sanctus ; simili modo magnificamus eum.
paras.en: [[68:31|I will praise the name of God with a canticle|Laudabo nomen Dei cum cantico]], that is, with spiritual gladness and inward cheerfulness, and with vocal melody if need be; [[68:31|and I will magnify him with praise|et magnificabo eum in laude]], that is, by the praise which I will sing, speak and offer to him, I will confess and make known that God is a great Lord and exceedingly to be praised. For as in the Lord's Prayer we say, [[Matt 6:9|hallowed be thy name|Sanctificetur nomen tuum]], not that any holiness accrues to God from us, but because through the purity of our service he is shown and declared to be holy, in like manner we magnify him.

paras.t: Et placebit Deo salus et magnificatio ista, super vitulum novellum, id est anniculum, cornua producentem pro munimine capitis, et ungulas pro pedum defensione. Sacrificium namque laudis et evangelicæ laudationis, acceptabilius Deo est quam sacrificia illa legalia, quæ secundum Apostolum, nec auferre poterant peccata, nec accedentem facere perfectum.
paras.en: [[68:32|And it shall please God|Et placebit Deo]], this salvation and magnifying, [[68:32|better than a young calf|super vitulum novellum]], that is, a yearling, [[68:32|that bringeth forth horns|cornua producentem]] for the protection of its head, [[68:32|and hoofs|et ungulas]] for the defence of its feet. For the sacrifice of praise and of gospel praising is more acceptable to God than those sacrifices of the law which, according to the Apostle, could neither take away sins[[Heb 10:4||]] nor make him that comes to them perfect[[Heb 10:1||]].

paras.t: Videant omnia nunc prædicta, pauperes, id est humiles spiritu, fideliter contemplando, et lætentur in Domino de beneficiis ejus. Quærite Deum, faciendo quod in vobis est, et fide ac opere in eum tendite, et vivet anima vestra, id est, gratiam consequetur, quæ est vita animæ, sicut anima est corporis vita. Hoc est quod Isaias propheta dicit : Quærite Dominum dum inveniri potest, invocate eum dum prope est ; et in Evangelio Christus, Omnis qui quærit invenit, et pulsanti aperietur.
paras.en: [[68:33|Let the poor see|Videant omnia nunc prædicta, pauperes]] all the things now foretold (the poor, that is, the humble in spirit), contemplating them faithfully, [[68:33|and rejoice|et lætentur]] in the Lord for his benefits. [[68:33|Seek ye God|Quærite Deum]], by doing what is in you, and tend towards him by faith and works, [[68:33|and your soul shall live|et vivet anima vestra]], that is, it shall obtain grace, which is the life of the soul, as the soul is the life of the body. This is what the prophet Isaias says: [[Is 55:6|Seek ye the Lord, while he may be found: call upon him, while he is near|Quærite Dominum dum inveniri potest, invocate eum dum prope est]]; and Christ in the Gospel: Every one [[Luke 11:10|that seeketh findeth: and to him that knocketh it shall be opened|qui quærit invenit, et pulsanti aperietur]].

paras.t: Quoniam exaudivit pauperes spiritu Dominus, qui de talibus dicit : Beati pauperes spiritu. Et Isaias : Dominus sublimis in sancto habitans, ut vivificet spiritum humilium, et vivificet cor contritorum. Et vinctos suos, id est peccatores electos, qui ad tempus errant, sed in finem errare non possunt, non despexit : quoniam pœnitentes libenter ac misericorditer recipit, quemadmodum per Jeremiam loquitur : Revertere ad me, et non avertam faciem meam. Vel, Vinctos suos, id est, eos qui se ipsos divina lege constringunt, et mandatis divinis quasi vinculis quibusdam ab omni via mala coercent. Vel : Vinctos suos, id est sanctos in limbo detentos, Deus Pater, seu Christus non despexit, quia Pater per Filium eos redemit. Unde apud Isaiam Deus ait ad Christum : Dedi te in fœdus populi, ut suscitares terram, et diceres his qui vincti sunt, Exite ; et his qui in tenebris, Revelamini.
paras.en: [[68:34|For the Lord hath heard the poor|Quoniam exaudivit pauperes spiritu Dominus]] in spirit, he who says of such: [[Matt 5:3|Blessed are the poor in spirit|Beati pauperes spiritu]]. And Isaias: The Lord, [[Is 57:15|the Eminent|sublimis]], [[Is 57:15|who dwelleth in the high and holy place|in sancto habitans]], [[Is 57:15|to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite|ut vivificet spiritum humilium, et vivificet cor contritorum]]. And [[68:34|his prisoners|vinctos suos]], that is, the elect sinners, who go astray for a time but cannot go astray to the end, he [[68:34|hath not despised|non despexit]]: since he receives penitents willingly and mercifully, as he says through Jeremias: [[Jer 3:12|Return|Revertere]] to me, [[Jer 3:12|and I will not turn away my face|et non avertam faciem meam]]. Or, [[68:34|his prisoners|Vinctos suos]], that is, those who bind themselves by the divine law, and restrain themselves from every evil way by the divine commandments as by bonds. Or: [[68:34|his prisoners|Vinctos suos]], that is, the saints held in limbo, God the Father, or Christ, [[68:34|hath not despised|non despexit]], because the Father redeemed them through the Son. Hence in Isaias God says to Christ: I have [[Is 49:8|given thee to be a covenant of the people, that thou mightest raise up the earth|Dedi te in fœdus populi, ut suscitares terram]], and that [[Is 49:9|thou mightest say to them that are bound: Come forth: and to them that are in darkness: Shew yourselves|et diceres his qui vincti sunt, Exite ; et his qui in tenebris, Revelamini]].

paras.t: Laudent illum cœli et terra, id est angeli ac homines, sicut Moyses : Audite, inquit, cœli, quæ loquor ; audiat terra verba oris mei. Mare et omnia reptilia in eis laudent Deum materialiter, præbendo hominibus occasionem laudandi Creatorem in creaturis relucentem, sicut refulget natura atque perfectio causæ in suo effectu.
paras.en: [[68:35|Let the heavens and the earth praise him|Laudent illum cœli et terra]], that is, angels and men, as Moses has it: [[Deut 32:1|Hear|Audite]], he says, [[Deut 32:1|O ye heavens, the things I speak, let the earth give ear to the words of my mouth|cœli, quæ loquor ; audiat terra verba oris mei]]. Let [[68:35|the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein|Mare et omnia reptilia in eis]] praise God materially, by giving men occasion to praise the Creator shining forth in his creatures, as the nature and perfection of a cause shines out in its effect.

paras.t: Quoniam Deus salvam faciet Sion, id est militantem Ecclesiam, dando hominibus gratiam, et ædificabuntur civitates Juda, id est particulares Ecclesiæ Christo confitentes. Juda enim interpretatur confessio. Vel, Civitates Juda, id est corda confitentium, quæ ædificantur per fidem et caritatem, ac opera virtuosa, prout ait Apostolus : Quæ ædificationis sunt, in invicem custodiamus. Et inhabitabunt ibi, id est, fideles in Ecclesia commorabuntur, obediendo ejus præceptis; et hereditate acquirent eam : quoniam usque ad finem mundi durabit fides catholica, per quam fideles in Ecclesia habitare dicuntur.
paras.en: [[68:36|For God will save Sion|Quoniam Deus salvam faciet Sion]], that is, the Church militant, by giving men grace, [[68:36|and the cities of Juda shall be built up|et ædificabuntur civitates Juda]], that is, the particular Churches confessing Christ; for Juda is interpreted "confession". Or, [[68:36|the cities of Juda|Civitates Juda]], that is, the hearts of those who confess, which are built up by faith and charity and virtuous works, as the Apostle says: Let us [[Rom 14:19|keep the things that are of edification, one towards another|Quæ ædificationis sunt, in invicem custodiamus]]. [[68:36|And they shall dwell there|Et inhabitabunt ibi]], that is, the faithful shall abide in the Church, obeying her precepts; [[68:36|and acquire it by inheritance|et hereditate acquirent eam]]: because the Catholic faith, through which the faithful are said to dwell in the Church, will last until the end of the world.

paras.t: Et semen servorum ejus, id est spirituales filii Apostolorum, videlicet omnes credentes, possidebit eam, id est Ecclesiam, hereditario jure; et qui diligunt nomen ejus, id est ipsum Deum, habitabunt in ea. Dilectio enim præcipua causa est, ob quam in Ecclesia atque in Christo manere censemur.
paras.en: [[68:37|And the seed of his servants|Et semen servorum ejus]], that is, the spiritual sons of the Apostles, namely all believers, [[68:37|shall possess it|possidebit eam]], that is, the Church, by right of inheritance; [[68:37|and they that love his name|et qui diligunt nomen ejus]], that is, God himself, [[68:37|shall dwell therein|habitabunt in ea]]. For love is the chief reason for which we are reckoned to abide in the Church and in Christ.

paras.t: Videtur etiam posse exponi de triumphanti Ecclesia, quam vocat Apostolus Sion : Accessistis, inquiens, ad Sion montem et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem. Eritque sensus : Quoniam Deus salvam faciet Sion, præcipue in die judicii, quando salutem corporum dabit electis, configurando corpus humilitatis nostræ corpori claritatis suæ; et ædificabuntur civitates Juda, id est, ordines angelorum reparabuntur, et ruina cœlestis Jerusalem reformabitur per homines illuc ascendentes : sic civitates Juda, id est mansiones cœlestes, ex vivis lapidibus ædificabuntur. Et inhabitabunt ibi, id est in Ecclesia triumphanti, electi; et hereditate acquirent eam, dum Christus dicet ad eos : Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi. Et semen servorum ejus, id est imitatores Sanctorum, possidebit eam, id est terram viventium sine fine; et qui diligunt nomen ejus habitabunt in ea. Caritas enim nunquam excidit, sed cives cœlestis Jerusalem efficit.
paras.en: It seems that it can also be expounded of the Church triumphant, which the Apostle calls Sion: [[Heb 12:22|You are come|Accessistis]], he says, [[Heb 12:22|to mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem|ad Sion montem et civitatem Dei viventis, Jerusalem cœlestem]]. And the sense will be: [[68:36|For God will save Sion|Quoniam Deus salvam faciet Sion]], above all on the day of judgement, when he will give the elect the salvation of their bodies, conforming [[Phil 3:21|the body of our lowness|corpus humilitatis nostræ]] [[Phil 3:21|to the body of his glory|corpori claritatis suæ]]; [[68:36|and the cities of Juda shall be built up|et ædificabuntur civitates Juda]], that is, the orders of angels shall be restored, and the ruin of the heavenly Jerusalem [that is, the places left empty by the fall of the angels] repaired by men ascending there: thus [[68:36|the cities of Juda|civitates Juda]], that is, the heavenly mansions, shall be built of living stones. [[68:36|And they shall dwell there|Et inhabitabunt ibi]], that is, the elect, in the Church triumphant; [[68:36|and acquire it by inheritance|et hereditate acquirent eam]], when Christ shall say to them: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world|Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi]]. [[68:37|And the seed of his servants|Et semen servorum ejus]], that is, the imitators of the Saints, [[68:37|shall possess it|possidebit eam]], that is, the land of the living, without end; [[68:37|and they that love his name shall dwell therein|et qui diligunt nomen ejus habitabunt in ea]]. For [[1 Cor 13:8|Charity never falleth away|Caritas enim nunquam excidit]], but makes men citizens of the heavenly Jerusalem.

paras.t: Verumtamen, sicut quod dictum est, Fiat habitatio eorum deserta, etc., litteraliter explanatum est de urbe Jerusalem et civitatibus reliquis tribus Juda, sic nunc introducta videntur ad litteram posse exponi de civitatibus materialibus Juda, ut sit sensus : Ædificabuntur civitates Juda. Jerusalem namque et aliæ urbes a Romanis destructæ, postmodum erant reædificatæ, multoque tempore habitabant in eis veri Israelitæ et spirituales Judæi, videlicet Christiani, donec exigentibus culpis suis, hereditatem suam perdiderunt, et a Sarracenis dejecti sunt.
paras.en: However, just as what was said, [[68:26|Let their habitation be made desolate|Fiat habitatio eorum deserta]], etc., was explained literally of the city of Jerusalem and the other cities of the tribe of Juda, so the words now brought in seem able to be expounded literally of the material cities of Juda, so that the sense is: [[68:36|The cities of Juda shall be built up|Ædificabuntur civitates Juda]]. For Jerusalem and the other cities destroyed by the Romans were afterwards rebuilt, and for a long time there dwelt in them true Israelites and spiritual Jews, namely Christians, until, as their sins demanded, they lost their inheritance and were cast out by the Saracens.

68.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI SEXAGESIMI OCTAVI.
68.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same sixty-eighth psalm.

paras.t: Quoniam, sicut ait discipulus quem diligebat Jesus, Qui se dicit in Christo manere, debet sicut ille ambulavit, et ipse ambulare (non enim est servus major domino suo); idcirco mirum non est, quod psalmi illi, qui ad litteram de Christi humilitate et passione loquuntur, moraliter de corpore ejus mystico exponuntur, præsertim quum dicat Apostolus: Omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur. Hinc ergo psalmus iste, qui de Christi passione ad litteram expositus est, moraliter elucidatur de corpore ejus mystico, quod est Ecclesia.
paras.en: Since, as the disciple whom Jesus loved says, [[1 John 2:6|He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also to walk even as he walked|Qui se dicit in Christo manere, debet sicut ille ambulavit, et ipse ambulare]] (for [[John 13:16|The servant is not greater than his lord|est servus major domino suo]]), it is no wonder that those psalms which literally speak of the humility and passion of Christ are expounded morally of his mystical body; especially as the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution|Omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur]]. Hence this psalm, which has been expounded literally of the passion of Christ, is explained morally of his mystical body, which is the Church.

paras.t: Ecclesia igitur, seu fidelis quicumque, in medio laqueorum se videns, et undique tribulari se pensans, nec propriis viribus se posse prævalere expertus, proclamet ad Dominum: Salvum me fac, Deus, ab omni vulnere mentis, et si utile mihi est, etiam ab omni infirmitate corporis; quoniam intraverunt aquæ tentationum diaboli, persecutionum mundi, et impugnationum appetitus sensitivi, usque ad animam meam, id est, profunde et fortiter mihi impressæ sunt; nec possum de facili rejicere eas, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam, id est usque ad delectationem seu consensum mentis. Hoc unusquisque tentatus atque afflictus totis clamet præcordiis, dum se graviter impugnari experitur. Infixus sum in limo profundi, id est in voluptate carnali, in sæculo isto vitioso atque fallaci, ita quod vitiis sum subjectus, in turpibus rebus delectatus, mundo isti per inordinatum affectum intentus; et non est mihi substantia, id est virtus evadendi, resistendi, ac prævalendi. Vel, Non est substantia, id est substantia stabilis, quoniam vanitati subjectus sum, corde vagus, et fragilis mente.
paras.en: The Church, then, or any one of the faithful, seeing himself in the midst of snares, and reckoning that he is troubled on every side, and having found by experience that he cannot prevail by his own strength, should cry out to the Lord: [[68:2|Save me, O God|Salvum me fac, Deus]], from every wound of the mind, and, if it is profitable for me, from every infirmity of the body also; [[68:2|for the waters are come in|quoniam intraverunt aquæ]] of the temptations of the devil, of the persecutions of the world, and of the assaults of the sensitive appetite, [[68:2|even unto my soul|usque ad animam meam]], that is, they have been pressed deeply and strongly upon me; nor can I easily cast them off, [[68:2|for the waters are come in even unto my soul|quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam]], that is, even to the delight or consent of the mind. Let every one who is tempted and afflicted cry this with his whole heart, when he finds himself grievously assailed. [[68:3|I stick fast in the mire of the deep|Infixus sum in limo profundi]], that is, in carnal pleasure, in this vicious and deceitful world, so that I am subject to vices, have taken delight in shameful things, and am bent upon this world by disordered affection; [[68:3|and there is no sure standing|et non est substantia]] for me, that is, no strength to escape, to resist and to prevail. Or: There is no *substantia* [that is, “substance”, what stands firm; the Douay-Rheims has “sure standing”], that is, no stable substance, since I am subject to vanity, wandering in heart and frail in mind.

paras.t: Veni in altitudinem maris, id est in adversitates ingentes, tribulationesque maximas; et tempestas demersit me, id est, fortitudo ac impetus adversitatum hujusmodi dejecit, læsit, occidit, vel ad peccatum me induxit: sicut ait Apostolus, Nullam requiem habuit spiritus noster; et rursus, Supra modum gravati sumus, ita ut tæderet nos vivere. Dum primi nostri parentes nondum peccassent in paradiso, velut in portu erant tranquillo; perpetrato autem peccato, ipsi et omnis eorum posteritas in altitudinem maris, id est in profundum hujus mundi, projecti sunt, in quo toties nos demergit tempestas, quoties adversitati cedimus per impatientiam seu pusillanimitatem, et quoties tentationi consentimus, aut molestia aliqua frangimur. Tempestas hæc exteriorum persecutionum, demersit martyres sanctos in mortem corporalem; apostatantes vero a fide, demersit in mortem animæ spiritualem. Vel sic: Veni in altitudinem maris, id est ad gradum prælationis in mundo isto; et tempestas demersit me, id est, strepitus negotiorum sæcularium, sollicitudo temporalium rerum, occupatio exteriorum causarum, mentis quietem, lumen devotionis, ac cordis custodiam exstinxit aut minoravit in me.
paras.en: [[68:3|I am come into the depth of the sea|Veni in altitudinem maris]], that is, into huge adversities and very great tribulations; and [[68:3|a tempest hath overwhelmed me|tempestas demersit me]], that is, the force and onset of such adversities has cast me down, wounded me, slain me, or led me into sin: as the Apostle says, [[2 Cor 7:5|our flesh had no rest|Nullam requiem habuit spiritus noster]] [Denis reads “our spirit” for “our flesh”]; and again, [[2 Cor 1:8|pressed out of measure above our strength, so that we were weary even of life|Supra modum gravati sumus, ita ut tæderet nos vivere]]. While our first parents had not yet sinned in paradise, they were as in a calm harbour; but once the sin was committed, they and all their posterity were cast into the depth of the sea, that is, into the deep of this world, in which the tempest overwhelms us as often as we give way to adversity through impatience or faintheartedness, and as often as we consent to temptation, or are broken by some trouble. This tempest of outward persecutions overwhelmed the holy martyrs in bodily death; but those who fell away from the faith it overwhelmed in the spiritual death of the soul. Or thus: [[68:3|I am come into the depth of the sea|Veni in altitudinem maris]], that is, to a rank of prelacy in this world; and [[68:3|a tempest hath overwhelmed me|tempestas demersit me]], that is, the din of worldly business, care for temporal things, and preoccupation with outward affairs have quenched or lessened in me the quiet of the mind, the light of devotion, and the guard of the heart.

paras.t: Denique si velimus ista omnino ad litteram exponere, sic etiam quibusdam Christi membris convenient, videlicet sanctis martyribus in aquas projectis; quorum nonnulli divina virtute educti sunt, aliqui vero submersi; sed omnium anima est salvata. In his autem aquæ materiales ac elementares intraverunt per os usque ad animam, id est usque ad interiora, vel usque ad exstinctionem corporeæ vitæ. Hi quoque infixi sunt in limo profundi, id est in terra lutosa, in fundo aquarum, vel in carceribus aquosis atque limosis, ut erant Jeremias, Michæas, et alii multi. Unde Jeremias de se ipso scribit, quod descendit in lutum carceris usque ad renes. Venerunt etiam quidam justorum in altitudinem maris, sicut de multis beatissimis martyribus scribitur, qui de navi, ripa, aut rupe, ligatis ad eorum corpora saxis, in mare jactati sunt. Horum autem unus exstitit Jonas propheta, qui in pelago missus, et a cete absorptus, ita de ventre piscis oravit: Projecisti me, Domine, in profundum in corde maris, et flumen circumdedit me; omnes gurgites tui et fluctus tui super me transierunt; circumdederunt me aquæ usque ad animam, abyssus vallavit me, pelagus operuit caput meum.
paras.en: Finally, if we wish to expound these words wholly according to the letter, they will fit certain members of Christ in this way too, namely the holy martyrs cast into the waters, of whom some were brought out by the power of God, while others were drowned; but the soul of all of them was saved. In these, material and elemental waters came in through the mouth even unto the soul, that is, even to the inward parts, or even to the extinction of bodily life. These too were fixed [[68:3|in the mire of the deep|in limo profundi]], that is, in muddy ground, at the bottom of the waters, or in watery and miry prisons, as were Jeremias, Micheas[[3 Kings 22:27||]], and many others. Hence Jeremias writes of himself that he went down into the mud of the prison up to the reins[[Jer 38:6||]] [Jer 38:6 says only that he sank into the mire]. Some of the just also came [[68:3|into the depth of the sea|in altitudinem maris]], as is written of many most blessed martyrs, who were thrown into the sea from a ship, a bank or a rock, with stones tied to their bodies. One of these was Jonas the prophet, who, sent into the deep and swallowed by the whale, prayed thus from the belly of the fish: [[Jon 2:4|thou hast cast me forth|Projecisti me]], O Lord, [[Jon 2:4|into the deep, in the heart of the sea, and a flood hast compassed me: all thy billows, and thy waves have passed over me|in profundum in corde maris, et flumen circumdedit me; omnes gurgites tui et fluctus tui super me transierunt]]; [[Jon 2:6|The waters compassed me about even to the soul: the deep hath closed me round about, the sea hath covered my head|circumdederunt me aquæ usque ad animam, abyssus vallavit me, pelagus operuit caput meum]].

paras.t: Laboravi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ. Laborat Ecclesia deflendo sua peccata, pœnitentiamque agendo, atque pro aliorum conversione discurrendo, docendo, increpando, alliciendo; clamatque ad Dominum pro indulgentia vitiorum, pro infusione gratiarum, pro illuminatione errantium, et emendatione pravorum. Raucæ fiunt voces ipsius, dum aliis prædicando, nil proficit, vel dum difficulter ac tarde exauditur a Deo, vel etiam ex nimio dolore inflicto, aut labore assumpto, humore viribusque exhaustis. Hinc enim sanctus Job ait ad Dominum: Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me; sto, et non respicis me: mutatus es mihi in crudelem, et in duritia manus tuæ adversaris mihi; et iterum, Sagittæ Domini in me sunt, quarum indignatio ebibit spiritum meum, et terrores Domini militant contra me.
paras.en: [[68:4|I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse|Laboravi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ]]. The Church labours in bewailing her sins and doing penance, and in going about for the conversion of others, teaching, rebuking, drawing them on; and she cries to the Lord for the pardon of vices, for the infusion of graces, for the enlightening of those who err, and the amendment of the wicked. Her voice grows hoarse when she gains nothing by preaching to others, or when she is heard by God with difficulty and late, or again when, from the excessive pain inflicted or the labour undertaken, her moisture and strength are exhausted. Hence holy Job says to the Lord: [[Job 30:20|I cry to thee, and thou hearest me not: I stand up, and thou dost not regard me|Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me; sto, et non respicis me]]: [[Job 30:21|Thou art changed to be cruel toward me, and in the hardness of thy hand thou art against me|mutatus es mihi in crudelem, et in duritia manus tuæ adversaris mihi]]; and again, [[Job 6:4|the arrows of the Lord are in me, the rage whereof drinketh up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord war against me|Sagittæ Domini in me sunt, quarum indignatio ebibit spiritum meum, et terrores Domini militant contra me]].

paras.t: Defecerunt oculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum. Hoc sæpius contingit infirmis Ecclesiæ membris, qui propter duritiam ac vehementiam tentationum et tribulationum, dum non exaudiuntur pro voto a Deo, infirmantur et nutant in spe et pusillanimes fiunt. Non enim convenit eis illud beati Job: Etiamsi occiderit me (Deus), in ipso sperabo. Vel: Defecerunt oculi mei corporales, plangendo, aut penitus pereundo, dum spero in Deum meum, quia in ipso sperando incessanter affligor, aut propter justitiam seu fidem catholicam morior. Unde de David ejusque sociis scriptum est: Elevaverunt vocem suam, et fleverunt, donec deficerent in ipsis lacrimæ. Vel: Defecerunt oculi mei interioris intellectus, dum spero in Deum meum, quoniam non tam fiducialiter, amorose, et immobiliter in Deo confido, sicut deceret.
paras.en: [[68:4|my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God|Defecerunt oculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum]]. This happens quite often to the weak members of the Church, who, because of the hardness and violence of temptations and tribulations, when they are not heard by God as they wish, grow weak and waver in hope and become fainthearted. For that saying of blessed Job does not fit them: [[Job 13:15|Although he should kill me|Etiamsi occiderit me]] (God), [[Job 13:15|I will trust in him|in ipso sperabo]]. Or: [[68:4|my eyes have failed|Defecerunt oculi mei]], the eyes of the body, through weeping, or through perishing altogether, [[68:4|whilst I hope in my God|dum spero in Deum meum]], because in hoping in him I am ceaselessly afflicted, or I die for justice or for the Catholic faith. Hence it is written of David and his companions: [[1 Kings 30:4|lifted up their voices, and wept till they had no more tears|Elevaverunt vocem suam, et fleverunt, donec deficerent in ipsis lacrimæ]]. Or: [[68:4|my eyes have failed|Defecerunt oculi mei]], the eyes of the inward understanding, [[68:4|whilst I hope in my God|dum spero in Deum meum]], since I do not trust in God as confidently, lovingly and immovably as would be fitting.

paras.t: Multiplicati sunt super capillos capitis mei, qui oderunt me gratis. Multi et innumerabiles sunt hostes Ecclesiæ atque sanctorum, videlicet omnes infideles, hæretici, schismatici, falsi fratres, detractores, ambitiosi, ac invidi. Hi omnes gratis et sine rationabili causa persequuntur Ecclesiam. Habemus quoque invisibiles inimicos multos et fortes. De quibus dicit Apostolus: Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed contra principatus et potestates, contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus. Habemus etiam hostes domesticos multos ac periculosos, qui sunt propriæ passiones ac vitia. De his adversariis dicere potest Ecclesia et quilibet justus: Confortati sunt, qui persecuti sunt me inimici mei injuste; quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam, id est, pœnas quas non merui, passus sum. Hoc sanctis martyribus maxime competit, qui pro Deo, pro fide, pro justitia occubuerunt. Unde et Job: Hæc (ait) passus sum absque iniquitate manus meæ, quum mundas haberem ad Deum preces. Deus enim frequenter permittit tribulari electos sine eorum demerito, quatenus gloriosius coronentur. Nunquam tamen infert alicui damnum in bonis spiritualibus gratiæ gratum facientis, sine propria hominis culpa.
paras.en: [[68:5|They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, who hate me without cause|Multiplicati sunt super capillos capitis mei, qui oderunt me gratis]]. Many and numberless are the enemies of the Church and of the saints, namely all unbelievers, heretics, schismatics, false brethren, detractors, the ambitious and the envious. All these persecute the Church without cause and with no reasonable ground. We have also many strong invisible enemies, of whom the Apostle says: [[Eph 6:12|our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and powers|Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed contra principatus et potestates]], [[Eph 6:12|against the spirits of wickedness in the high places|contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus]]. We have also many dangerous enemies of our own household, which are our own passions and vices. Of these adversaries the Church and any just man can say: [[68:5|My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me|Confortati sunt, qui persecuti sunt me inimici mei injuste]]: [[68:5|then did I pay that which I took not away|quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam]], that is, I suffered punishments which I did not deserve. This applies above all to the holy martyrs, who fell for God, for the faith, for justice. Hence Job too: [[Job 16:18|These things|Hæc]] (he says) [[Job 16:18|have I suffered without the iniquity of my hand, when I offered pure prayers to God|passus sum absque iniquitate manus meæ, quum mundas haberem ad Deum preces]]. For God often permits his elect to be troubled without any fault of theirs, that they may be more gloriously crowned. Yet he never inflicts on anyone loss in the spiritual goods of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God] without the man's own fault.

paras.t: Deinde Ecclesia in persona infirmorum suorum loquens membrorum, seu quilibet pœnitens propriam insipientiam atque peccata humiliter confitetur, dicendo: Deus, tu scis insipientiam meam, etc. Insipiens est enim omnis qui peccat, quia in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia. Et quid tam stultum atque vesanum, quam non obedire præceptis, nec acquiescere consiliis et exhortationibus æternæ Sapientiæ? Insipientia magna est, carnis vitiis deservire, animæ salutem negligere, in statu tali vivere in quo non audet quis mori. Porro delicta nostra Deo sunt cognita, sicut ipse alibi testatur: Cognovi multa scelera vestra, et fortia peccata vestra. Hæc propriæ insipientiæ atque iniquitatis confessio, veræ sapientiæ infusionem et gratiæ justificationem meretur. De eo namque qui se ipsum æstimat sapientem, in Isaia scriptum est: Sapientia tua et scientia tua decepit te; et denuo, Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris, et coram vobismetipsis prudentes. Propterea hortatur Apostolus: Nolite esse prudentes apud vosmetipsos. Confiteamur igitur semper cum omni humilitate insipientiam nostram, quia veraciter insipientes sumus, quemadmodum scriptum est: Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua.
paras.en: Then the Church, speaking in the person of her weak members, or any penitent, humbly confesses his own foolishness and sins, saying: [[68:6|O God, thou knowest my foolishness|Deus, tu scis insipientiam meam]], etc. For every one who sins is foolish, since [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia]]. And what is so foolish and mad as not to obey the commandments, nor to yield to the counsels and exhortations of the eternal Wisdom? It is great foolishness to be a slave to the vices of the flesh, to neglect the salvation of the soul, to live in such a state as one dare not die in. Moreover our offences are known to God, as he himself testifies elsewhere: [[Amos 5:12|I know your manifold crimes, and your grievous sins|Cognovi multa scelera vestra, et fortia peccata vestra]]. This confession of one's own foolishness and iniquity merits the infusion of true wisdom and the justification of grace. For of him who thinks himself wise it is written in Isaias: [[Is 47:10|Thy wisdom, and, thy knowledge, this hath deceived thee|Sapientia tua et scientia tua decepit te]]; and again, [[Is 5:21|Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes, and prudent in your own conceits|Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris, et coram vobismetipsis prudentes]]. Therefore the Apostle exhorts: [[Rom 12:16|Be not wise in your own conceits|Nolite esse prudentes apud vosmetipsos]]. Let us therefore always confess our foolishness with all humility, since we are truly foolish, as it is written: [[Jer 10:14|Every man is become a fool for knowledge|Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia]] [Denis adds *sua*, “by his own knowledge”].

paras.t: Non erubescant in me, qui exspectant te, Domine. Dum Ecclesia seu quilibet justus injurias patitur, tentatur, aut simili modo affligitur, nisi tunc Deus ei subveniat, erubescere poterunt alii Deum exspectantes, id est in ipso sperantes, quorum ista spes est, quod (sicut affirmat divina Scriptura) Deus Ecclesiam suam non derelinquit, nec justos finaliter opprimi sinit; sed agit quod ait Scriptura, Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam; et, Non vidi justum derelictum; et, Non patietur vos tentari supra id quod potestis. Quid est ergo, Non erubescent in me, qui exspectant te, Domine? nisi, In omni necessitate atque angustia mihi succurre, ab omni persecutione et tentatione me eripe, omnesque preces meas exaudi, sicut in sacra Scriptura te facturum promittis, quatenus alii in te sperantes corroborentur in spe, videntes misericordiam tuam mihi impensam. Et ad eumdem sensum pertinet versus sequens. In his enim quæ ad affectum respiciunt, solet Scriptura frequenter eumdem sensum sub aliis verbis repetere. Ait enim: Non confundantur super me, id est propter derelictionem meam et oppressionem, qui quærunt te, Deus Israel: qui utique confunderentur et scandalizarentur, nisi viderent mihi opem et gratiam donari a te. Dicerent enim: Vanus est qui servit Domino; et quod emolumentum quia custodivimus præcepta ejus?
paras.en: [[68:7|Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord|Non erubescant in me, qui exspectant te, Domine]]. When the Church or any just man suffers wrongs, is tempted, or is afflicted in some like way, unless God then comes to his help, others who look for God, that is, who hope in him, could be ashamed; for their hope is this, that (as the divine Scripture affirms) God does not forsake his Church, nor let the just be finally crushed, but does what the Scripture says: [[Rom 12:19|Revenge is mine, I will repay|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam]]; and, [[Ps 36:25|I have not seen the just forsaken|Non vidi justum derelictum]]; and, [[1 Cor 10:13|will not suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able|Non patietur vos tentari supra id quod potestis]]. What then is [[68:7|Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord|Non erubescent in me, qui exspectant te, Domine?]], if not: In every need and distress help me, deliver me from every persecution and temptation, and hear all my prayers, as thou promisest in holy Scripture that thou wilt do, so that others who hope in thee may be strengthened in hope, seeing thy mercy shown to me? And the following verse [in the Vulgate numbering it is the second half of the same verse] belongs to the same sense; for in things that concern the affections Scripture is wont often to repeat the same sense in other words. For it says: [[68:7|Let them not be confounded on my account|Non confundantur super me]], that is, because of my being forsaken and oppressed, [[68:7|who seek thee, O God of Israel|qui quærunt te, Deus Israel]]: who would indeed be confounded and scandalized unless they saw help and grace given me by thee. For they would say: [[Mal 3:14|He laboureth in vain that serveth God, and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinances|Vanus est qui servit Domino; et quod emolumentum quia custodivimus præcepta ejus?]]

paras.t: Quoniam propter te sustinui opprobrium: id est propter justitiam, propter fidem, propter nominis tui amorem atque honorem, passus sum contumeliam, non propter meam offensam aut culpam. Hæc est vera sustinentia, patientiaque beata, quemadmodum ait Salvator: Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum; et iterum, Beati estis quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes, propter me. Quidam tamen opprobrium sustinent, non propter Deum atque justitiam, sed propter se ipsos seu propriam culpam. Et quidem hoc æquanimiter ferre, tanquam pœnam pro culpa inflictam, bonum meritoriumque consistit; sed multo minus virtuosum est hoc, quam si propter Deum sustineatur. Propter quod princeps Apostolorum dicit: Hæc est gratia, si propter conscientiam Dei sustinet quis tristitias, patiens injuste. Quæ est enim gratia, si peccantes et colaphizati, suffertis? Si autem benefacientes sustinetis, hæc est gratia apud Deum. Aliqui vero verba Salvatoris jam præinducta, quibus ait, Beati qui persecutionem, etc., inconvenienter allegant.
