Of him it is written in the Gospel: [[John 8:44|He was a murderer from the beginning: and he stood not in the truth|Homicida erat ab initio, et in veritate non stetit]]; and elsewhere, [[1 John 3:8|the devil sinneth from the beginning|Diabolus ab initio peccat]]. Deliver me also [[70:4|out of the hand of the transgressor of the law|de manu contra legem agentis]], that is, of any wicked man who persecutes the just, lest I be infected and led astray by such a man; [[70:4|and of the unjust|et iniqui]], who, breaking the laws of brotherly charity, persecutes me without cause. Most of all, however, O Lord, deliver me [[70:4|out of the hand of the sinner|de manu peccatoris]], that is, from myself the sinner, inasmuch as I am wicked, and out of the hand of myself, the transgressor of the law, by turning me to Thee, so that I may not be such as I was, but may cease to be unjust: as it is written, [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]].

paras.t: Quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine, id est causa, finis et præmium patientiæ meæ. Unde et sanctus Job ait : Ubi est præstolatio mea et patientia mea? Tu es, Domine, Deus meus. Domine, spes mea a juventute mea : vel corporali, quoniam multi a juventute jugum Domini super se portant, et in Deo confidunt, illi videlicet qui in prima vigilia convertuntur. Propter quod Jeremias testatur : Bonum est viro, quum portaverit jugum Domini ab adolescentia sua; et alius, Laudabo nomen tuum, Domine, assidue, et confitebor tibi quum adhuc junior sum, antequam oberrem. Vel, A juventute mea spirituali, id est ab illo tempore quo cœpi renovari spiritu mentis meæ, exspoliando me veterem hominem cum actibus suis, et induendo novum, qui renovatur in agnitionem Dei, secundum Apostolum. Ab hac juventute est Deus spes hominis, quia sic renovari et taliter conversari nemo potest, nisi in Domino sperans.
paras.en: [[70:5|For thou art my patience, O Lord|Quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine]], that is, the cause, the end and the reward of my patience. Whence holy Job also says: [[Job 17:15|Where is now then my expectation|Ubi est præstolatio mea]], and my patience? [so Denis; the verse itself reads "and who considereth my patience?"] Thou art, O Lord, my God. [[70:5|my hope, O Lord, from my youth|Domine, spes mea a juventute mea]]: either my bodily youth, for many bear the yoke of the Lord upon themselves from their youth and trust in God, namely those who are converted in the first watch [that is, early in life]. For which reason Jeremias testifies: [[Lam 3:27|It is good for a man, when he hath borne the yoke|Bonum est viro, quum portaverit jugum]] of the Lord [[Lam 3:27|from his youth|ab adolescentia sua]]; and another says: [[Ecclus 51:15|I will praise thy name continually|Laudabo nomen tuum, Domine, assidue]], and I will give thanks to Thee[[Ecclus 51:17||]] [[Ecclus 51:18|When I was yet young, before I wandered about|quum adhuc junior sum, antequam oberrem]] [the margin gives Eccli. ii, 15, 17, 18, for li, 15, 17, 18]. Or, from my spiritual youth, that is, from the time when I began to be renewed in the spirit of my mind[[Eph 4:23||]], stripping myself of the old man with his deeds[[Col 3:9||]], and putting on the new, who is renewed unto the knowledge of God[[Col 3:10||]], according to the Apostle. From this youth God is the hope of a man, since no one can be so renewed and live in such a way unless he hopes in the Lord.

paras.t: In te confirmatus sum ex utero, id est, tua virtute sum conservatus in esse naturali in utero matris meæ carnalis, usque ad egressum ex utero, et deinceps. Nisi enim Deus conservaret infantem in utero, esse et permanere non posset, sicut nec aliquid sine manutenentia Dei subsistere valet; et nisi infantem in utero a cunctis præservaret periculis, frequenter facileque moreretur in ventre. Propterea dicit S. Thomas et alii multi, quod infanti adhuc in utero existenti, deputatur angelus bonus qui eum custodiat. De ventre matris meæ tu es protector meus, id est, ab ortu nativitatis meæ usque in præsens, tu protexisti me per te ipsum et angelum tuum sanctum. Quamvis enim justo judicio suo permittat Deus aliquem aliquando cadere, quemlibet tamen electum in tantum defendit, quod non permittit eum in peccato mortali decedere, vel a diabolo finaliter absorberi : imo in quolibet reprobo hoc agit misericordia Creatoris, quod per angelicam custodiam a multis malis retrahitur, atque ad aliqua bona instigatur.
paras.en: [[70:6|By thee have I been confirmed from the womb|In te confirmatus sum ex utero]], that is, by Thy power I was kept in my natural being in the womb of my mother according to the flesh, until I came forth from the womb, and ever since. For unless God preserved the infant in the womb, it could not exist and endure, just as nothing can subsist without God's upholding [manutenentia, literally a "holding in the hand": God's keeping of creatures in being]; and unless He kept the infant in the womb from all dangers, it would often and easily die in the womb. Therefore St. Thomas and many others say that a good angel is assigned to the infant while it is still in the womb, to guard it. [[70:6|from my mother's womb thou art my protector|De ventre matris meæ tu es protector meus]], that is, from my birth until now Thou hast protected me by Thyself and by Thy holy angel. For although God by His just judgment permits someone to fall at times, yet He so defends every one of the elect that He does not let him die in mortal sin, or be finally swallowed up by the devil: indeed, even in every reprobate the mercy of the Creator brings it about that by the guardianship of the angels he is held back from many evils and urged on to some good.

paras.t: Spiritualiter vero ita exponendus est versus iste : In te confirmatus sum, id est, in fide et gratia tua cœpi stabiliri, ex utero, id est ex catechismo, ubi in christiana doctrina instructus sum. De ventre matris meæ, id est de ventre Ecclesiæ, utpote ex sacro Baptismate, in quo spiritualiter regeneratus sum ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto. In Baptismo enim infunditur nobis gratia, fides, spes, caritas. Tu es protector meus, me conservando in donis gratiæ gratum facientis, in Baptismo collatis.
paras.en: Spiritually, however, this verse is to be explained thus: [[70:6|By thee have I been confirmed|In te confirmatus sum]], that is, I began to be made steadfast in Thy faith and grace, [[70:6|from the womb|ex utero]], that is, from the catechism [the instruction in the faith given before baptism], where I was taught Christian doctrine. [[70:6|From my mother's womb|De ventre matris meæ]], that is, from the womb of the Church, namely from holy Baptism, in which I was spiritually born again of water and the Holy Ghost[[John 3:5||]]. For in Baptism grace, faith, hope and charity are infused into us. [[70:6|thou art my protector|Tu es protector meus]], by keeping me in the gifts of sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace "that makes pleasing" to God] bestowed in Baptism.

paras.t: In te cantatio mea semper : id est, laus mea vocalis, exsultatio cordis, et regratiatio animæ meæ, circa tua beneficia versatur, et de tua bonitate concipitur, ita quod incessabiliter te laudare desidero, in omni loco, causa ac tempore. Et si hominem laudo, vel aliquid creatum, hoc ago ad gloriam tuam, tibi omnia bona adscribens, et ad tuum honorem omnia referens. Nec aliquem laudo in malo (sicut superius dictum est, Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ): sed si quem laudo, propter virtutes et gratiæ dona hoc facio. Hoc modo Paulus suos frequenter laudavit discipulos.
paras.en: [[70:6|Of thee I shall continually sing|In te cantatio mea semper]]: that is, the praise of my voice, the exultation of my heart and the thanksgiving of my soul are busied about Thy benefits and are conceived from Thy goodness, so that I desire to praise Thee unceasingly, in every place, cause and time. And if I praise a man, or anything created, I do it to Thy glory, ascribing all good things to Thee and referring all things to Thy honour. Nor do I praise anyone in evil (as was said above, [[Ps 9:24|For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul|Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ]] [the margin gives Ps. x, 3, according to the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate this is Ps 9:24]): but if I praise anyone, I do it for his virtues and the gifts of grace. In this way Paul often praised his disciples[[Rom 1:8||]][[Rom 16:4||]].

paras.t: Tanquam prodigium factus sum multis, id est, velut portentum a multis sum reputatus, irrisus ac spretus, quoniam vita mea vitæ illorum dissimilis invenitur. Temporalia enim, carnalia et delectabilia, quæ ipsi magni pendunt, laudant, acquirunt et diligunt, ego velut stercora arbitror, ut Christo pura ac libera mente adhæream; cœlestia, invisibilia et æterna terrenis, visibilibus et transitoriis præfero; patrem, matrem, fratres, sorores, uxorem, propinquos, agros et cetera universa pro Christi amore relinquo: ideo vitam meam putant insaniam. Unde et ait divinus Apostolus: Spectaculum facti sumus mundo et angelis et hominibus; ad Philippenses quoque, Existimo, inquit, omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Hinc etiam sanctus Ezechiel ait ad populum suum: Ezechiel erit portentum vestrum.
paras.en: [[70:7|I am become unto many as a wonder|Tanquam prodigium factus sum multis]], that is, I am reckoned by many as a portent, mocked and despised, because my life is found to be unlike theirs[[Wis 2:15||]] [the margin gives Wisd. ii, 16; the life unlike other men's is at Wis 2:15]. For the temporal, carnal and pleasant things which they themselves set great store by, praise, acquire and love, I count as dung[[Phil 3:8||]], that I may cleave to Christ with a pure and free mind; things heavenly, invisible and eternal I prefer to things earthly, visible and passing; father, mother, brothers, sisters, wife, kinsfolk, lands and all things else I leave for the love of Christ[[Matt 19:29||]]: therefore they think my life madness[[Wis 5:4||]]. Whence the divine Apostle also says: [[1 Cor 4:9|We are made a spectacle to the world and to angels and to men|Spectaculum facti sumus mundo et angelis et hominibus]]; and to the Philippians too: [[Phil 3:8|I count|Existimo]], he says, [[Phil 3:8|all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge of Jesus Christ, my Lord|omnia detrimentum esse propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]. Hence too holy Ezechiel says to his people: [[Ezech 24:24|Ezekiel shall be unto you for a sign of things to come|Ezechiel erit portentum vestrum]] [portentum, "portent", the word Denis has just used to explain the psalm's "wonder"].

paras.t: Et tu adjutor fortis: id est, tu, Domine, fortiter mihi adstitisti, magnamque gratiam ac fortitudinem donasti, ita quod propter improborum irrisiones et persecutiones non recessi a te, nec ab opere bono cessavi, sicut, heu! plurimi facere solent, qui dum se ab aliis aspernari, molestari et vituperari conspiciunt, viam perfectionis arreptam relinquunt. Quocontra exhortatur nos divinus Apostolus: Per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen, adspicientes in auctorem fidei et consummatorem Jesum, qui proposito sibi gaudio, sustinuit crucem, confusione contempta. Recogitate eum, qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversus semetipsum contradictionem, ut non fatigemini animis vestris. Et rursus: Exeamus igitur ad eum extra castra, improperium ejus portantes.
paras.en: [[70:7|but thou art a strong helper|Et tu adjutor fortis]]: that is, Thou, O Lord, hast stood mightily by me and given me great grace and strength, so that for all the mockery and persecutions of the wicked I have not gone back from Thee, nor ceased from good works, as, alas, very many are wont to do, who, when they see themselves scorned, troubled and reviled by others, abandon the way of perfection they had taken up. Against this the divine Apostle exhorts us: [[Heb 12:1|let us run by patience to the fight proposed to us|Per patientiam curramus ad propositum nobis certamen]], [[Heb 12:2|Looking on Jesus, the author and finisher of faith, who, having joy set before him, endured the cross, despising the shame|adspicientes in auctorem fidei et consummatorem Jesum, qui proposito sibi gaudio, sustinuit crucem, confusione contempta]]. [[Heb 12:3|think diligently upon him that endured such opposition from sinners against himself that you be not wearied|Recogitate eum, qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversus semetipsum contradictionem, ut non fatigemini]] in your minds. And again: [[Heb 13:13|Let us go forth therefore to him without the camp, bearing his reproach|Exeamus igitur ad eum extra castra, improperium ejus portantes]] [the margin gives Ibid. xii, 3 beside these words; they are Heb 13:13].

paras.t: Deinde vir justus cupiens de tantis beneficiis gratus Domino inveniri, precatur. Repleatur os meum laude: id est, tu, Domine, mentem accende, illumina, quatenus tuam bonitatem et beneficia contemplando, os divina laude repleatur. Ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur. Et nisi tu mentem divino calore succenderis, cito fatigabitur in tua laude os corporis, imo et spiritus meus. Idcirco superius dictum est: Sicut adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea, scilicet divino amore, et labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum. Unde nunc plenius subdit, cur petat os suum laude impleri: ut cantem gloriam tuam, id est, quatenus prædicem famam tuam gloriosam, tamque excellentiam tuam cantando annuntiem, tota die magnitudinem tuam, id est, semper, quantum huic vitæ possibile est, majestatem ac dignitatem tuam decantem. Hoc nempe est divinissimum ac illustrissimum præsentis vitæ exercitium, in divinis laudibus jugiter delectari, hilariter occupari, affectuosissime immorari, cum beatissimo Isaia propheta dicendo: Domine, Deus meus tu es, exaltabo te, et confitebor nomini tuo; et iterum, Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ. Hæc est vere angelica cœliformisque vita, divinæ glorificationis meritoria, sicut et ipse Dominus affirmat: Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum.
paras.en: Then the just man, desiring to be found grateful to the Lord for such great benefits, prays: [[70:8|Let my mouth be filled with praise|Repleatur os meum laude]]: that is, do Thou, O Lord, kindle and enlighten my mind, so that, contemplating Thy goodness and Thy benefits, my mouth may be filled with divine praise. For [[Matt 12:34|out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh|Ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur]]. And unless Thou set my mind alight with divine warmth, the mouth of my body will soon grow weary in Thy praise, and indeed my spirit too. Therefore it was said above: [[Ps 62:6|Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness|Sicut adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea]], namely with divine love, [[Ps 62:6|and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips|et labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxii, 6, for lxii, 6]. Hence he now adds more fully why he asks that his mouth be filled with praise: [[70:8|that I may sing thy glory|ut cantem gloriam tuam]], that is, that I may proclaim Thy glorious fame and announce Thy excellence in song, [[70:8|thy greatness all the day long|tota die magnitudinem tuam]], that is, that I may always, as far as is possible in this life, sing of Thy majesty and dignity. For this indeed is the most divine and most glorious exercise of the present life: to delight continually in the divine praises, to be cheerfully busied in them, to dwell on them with the deepest affection, saying with the most blessed prophet Isaias: [[Is 25:1|O Lord, thou art my God|Domine, Deus meus tu es]], [[Is 25:1|I will exalt O thee, and give glory to thy name|exaltabo te, et confitebor nomini tuo]]; and again, [[Is 26:8|thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul|Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ]]. This is truly the angelic and heaven-like life, which merits being glorified by God, as the Lord Himself affirms: [[1 Kings 2:30|whosoever shall glorify me, him will I glorify|Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum]].

paras.t: Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis. Quemadmodum duplex assignata est nunc juventus, spiritualis et corporalis, sic duplex senectus est: una corporis, dum calor deficit, et corporea virtus occumbere incipit; alia vero est senectus animæ, dum spiritualis calor amoris frigescit, nec anima per gratiarum incrementa renovatur, sed in negligentia sua et vitiis inveteratur, vel tædio persecutionum gravatur, aut minus activa in bonis efficitur. Et de utraque senectute intelligi possunt hæc verba, Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis: id est, ne gratiam tuam auferas mihi, dum corporaliter senesco, aut mente deficio; sed tunc tanto benignius mihi subvenias, quanto me amplius indigere agnoscis. Et ideo, quasi exponendo quod dictum est, addit: Quum deficiet virtus mea corporalis aut spiritualis: quod maxime fieri solet et potest in agone, et tempore magnæ infirmitatis ; ne derelinquas me. In hoc versu S. Thomas singularem præcipuamque devotionem habere solebat, et in dulces lacrimas ac uberem fletum amorose resolvi. Versus enim hic mirabiliter affectuosus, dulcis et efficax est, et salubris : modo eum ita ut decet, consideremus.
paras.en: [[70:9|Cast me not off in the time of old age|Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis]]. Just as a twofold youth has now been set down, spiritual and bodily, so there is a twofold old age: one of the body, when its heat fails and bodily strength begins to sink; the other is the old age of the soul, when the spiritual heat of love grows cold, and the soul is not renewed by increase of graces, but grows old in its negligence and vices, or is weighed down by weariness of persecutions, or becomes less active in good works. And these words can be understood of both old ages, [[70:9|Cast me not off in the time of old age|Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis]]: that is, take not thy grace from me when I grow old in body or fail in mind; but succour me then the more kindly, the more thou seest me to be in need. And so, as though expounding what has been said, he adds: [[70:9|when my strength shall fail|Quum deficiet virtus mea]], bodily or spiritual (which is most wont to happen, and can happen, in the agony [that is, the last struggle before death] and in a time of great sickness), [[70:9|do not thou forsake me|ne derelinquas me]]. St Thomas [that is, Thomas Aquinas] was wont to have a singular and special devotion to this verse, and to melt lovingly into sweet tears and abundant weeping. For this verse is wonderfully full of feeling, sweet and effective, and wholesome, if only we consider it as is fitting.

paras.t: Merito autem, o Domine, peto ista a te, Quia dixerunt inimici mei mihi quidquid excogitare potuerunt ad fallendum et opprimendum me. Dæmones enim honores proponunt, mundus divitias, caro delicias. Et qui custodiebant, id est observabant, animam meam ad decipiendum, consilium fecerunt in unum, id est pari proposito et fine eodem, facti unanimes ad perpetrandum illicita ; Dicentes : Deus dereliquit eum. Quoniam enim factus sum illis prodigium, putant vitam meam Domino non placere, præsertim quum videant se in hoc sæculo prosperari ac prævalere, me vero variis calamitatibus fatigari atque deficere. Hoc namque opinantur maligni, dum justos cernunt affligi, se autem lætari ac dominari. Unde Habacuc : Quia, inquit, impius prævalet adversus justum, propterea egreditur judicium perversum. Et quia me putant a Deo derelictum, arbitrantur se obsequium præstare Deo me persequendo ; et cohortando se, dicunt : Persequimini et comprehendite eum, id est, facite ei quod vultis, quia non est qui eripiat eum de manibus vestris : ipse namque humanum auxilium sprevit, et in Deo confisus est. Non advertunt isti insensati et reprobi, quoniam sicut aurum in fornace, sic Deus probat electos ; et quia per multas tribulationes oportet nos ingredi gloriam Dei, quemadmodum apud sanctum Job inducitur : Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria, et salvabitur innocens.
paras.en: Rightly, then, O Lord, do I ask these things of thee, [[70:10|For my enemies have spoken against me|Quia dixerunt inimici mei mihi]] whatever they could devise to deceive and oppress me. For the demons hold out honours, the world riches, the flesh delights. [[70:10|and they that watched|Et qui custodiebant]], that is, observed, [[70:10|my soul|animam meam]] in order to deceive it, [[70:10|have consulted together|consilium fecerunt in unum]], that is, with like purpose and the same end, made of one mind to commit what is unlawful, [[70:11|Saying: God hath forsaken him|Dicentes : Deus dereliquit eum]]. For since I am become [[70:7|as a wonder|prodigium]] to them, they think that my life does not please the Lord, especially when they see themselves prosper and prevail in this world, but me worn out and failing under various calamities. For this is what the wicked suppose when they see the just afflicted and themselves rejoicing and lording it. Hence Habacuc: [[Hab 1:4|because|Quia]], he says, [[Hab 1:4|the wicked prevaileth against the just, therefore wrong judgment goeth forth|impius prævalet adversus justum, propterea egreditur judicium perversum]]. And because they think me forsaken by God, they suppose that they do God a service by persecuting me; and urging one another on, they say: [[70:11|pursue and take him|Persequimini et comprehendite eum]], that is, do to him what you will, [[70:11|for there is none to deliver him|quia non est qui eripiat eum]] out of your hands: for he has spurned human help and trusted in God. These senseless and reprobate men do not mark that God proves the elect as gold in the furnace, and that through many tribulations we must enter into the glory of God; as is set forth in holy Job: [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]], and [[Job 22:30|The innocent shall be saved|salvabitur innocens]].

paras.t: Deus, ne elongeris a me, auxilium differendo, gratiam subtrahendo, aut eam minorem sinendo ; sed, o Deus meus, in quo summe et plene confido, in auxilium meum respice, tanto gratiosius succurrendo, quanto illi malitiosius me subvertere enituntur : quemadmodum scriptum est, Bonus Dominus et confortans in die tribulationis, et sciens sperantes in se.
paras.en: [[70:12|O God, be not thou far from me|Deus, ne elongeris a me]], by delaying help, withdrawing grace, or letting it grow less; but, [[70:12|O my God|o Deus meus]], in whom I trust supremely and fully, [[70:12|make haste to my help|in auxilium meum respice]] [the Latin *respice* is literally "look": look to my help], succouring me the more graciously, the more maliciously they strive to overthrow me: as it is written, [[Nah 1:7|The Lord is good, and giveth strength in the day of trouble: and knoweth them that hope in him|Bonus Dominus et confortans in die tribulationis, et sciens sperantes in se]].

paras.t: Confundantur de suis sceleribus, et deficiant ab exsecutione operis mali, detrahentes animæ meæ, bonam ejus famam denigrare optantes : quod est mortale peccatum, quoniam bona fama multum pretiosa atque amabilis est, et melior cunctis divitiis, quemadmodum Salomon profitetur : Melius est nomen bonum quam unguenta pretiosa : et Ecclesiasticus : Curam habe de bono nomine ; hoc enim magis proderit tibi, quam mille thesauri. Propterea detractio est majus peccatum quam furtum. Operiantur confusione prædicta, et pudore, qui in confessione peccati maxime cooperatur ad culpæ remissionem, etiam quantum ad pœnam, qui quærunt mala mihi inferre, meque ad peccandum inducere, aut simili modo injuste affligere. De hac bona confusione apud Ezechielem scriptum est : Confundimini et erubescite super viis vestris, ait Dominus. Verumtamen, quomodo ista confusio, pudor et defectio multipliciter accipi queant, in præcedentis psalmi explanatione inductum est.
paras.en: [[70:13|Let them be confounded|Confundantur]] for their crimes, [[70:13|and come to nothing|et deficiant]] [*deficiant*, "let them fail", that is, fall away] from carrying out their evil work, [[70:13|that detract my soul|detrahentes animæ meæ]], wishing to blacken its good name: which is a mortal sin, since a good name is very precious and lovable, and better than all riches, as Solomon declares: [[Eccles 7:2|A good name is better than precious ointments|Melius est nomen bonum quam unguenta pretiosa]]; and Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 41:15|Take care of a good name|Curam habe de bono nomine]]; for this will profit thee more [[Ecclus 41:15|than a thousand treasures|quam mille thesauri]] [Denis reads *proderit*, "will profit", where the Vulgate has *permanebit*, "shall continue"]. Therefore detraction is a greater sin than theft. [[70:13|let them be covered with confusion|Operiantur confusione]], the confusion spoken of, [[70:13|and blame|et pudore]] [*pudor*, shame], which in the confession of sin works together most of all towards the remission of guilt, and even of the punishment, [[70:13|that seek my hurt|qui quærunt mala mihi]] [literally "who seek evils for me"], to bring evils upon me, and to lead me into sin, or in like manner to afflict me unjustly. Of this good confusion it is written in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:32|be confounded, and ashamed at your own ways|Confundimini et erubescite super viis vestris]], saith the Lord. But how this confusion, shame and failing may be taken in many ways has been set out in the explanation of the preceding psalm.

paras.t: Ego autem semper sperabo, id est, quantumcumque illi me persequantur verbis et factis, occulte et publice, ego nihilo minus incessanter in te confidere volo : sicut beatus Job de se fatetur, Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo. Et Salomon : Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo ; et, Exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te. Et adjiciam super omnem laudem tuam : id est, omnem laudem qua te venerari potero, vel ab aliis es laudatus, confitebor esse minorem tua dignitate, et in infinitum deficere a præconio quo tu dignus es, propter tuæ bonitatis plenitudinem prorsus immensam : idcirco, quantum mihi possibile fuerit, semper conabor te novis hymnis laudare, perfectiori laude extollere, et nunquam a tua laude cessare.
paras.en: [[70:14|But I will always hope|Ego autem semper sperabo]]: that is, however much they persecute me in word and deed, secretly and openly, I will nonetheless trust in thee unceasingly: as blessed Job confesses of himself, [[Job 13:15|Although he should kill me, I will trust in him|Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo]]. And Solomon: [[Prov 3:5|Have confidence in the Lord with all thy heart|Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo]]; and, [[Prov 20:22|wait for the Lord, and he will deliver thee|Exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te]]. [[70:14|and will add to all thy praise|Et adjiciam super omnem laudem tuam]] [literally "I will add above all thy praise"]: that is, all the praise with which I shall be able to honour thee, or with which thou hast been praised by others, I will confess to be less than thy dignity, and to fall infinitely short of the praise of which thou art worthy, because of the altogether boundless fullness of thy goodness: therefore, as far as shall be possible to me, I will always strive to praise thee with new hymns, to extol thee with more perfect praise, and never to cease from thy praise.

paras.t: Os meum annuntiabit, apud se te laudando, teque coram aliis prædicando, justitiam tuam, qua unicuique reddis quod meretur, et sine personarum acceptione omnia operaris. Te ergo, o Domine, justificabo, tua judicia approbabo, me vero accusabo et condemnabo. Potest quoque per justitiam Dei sacra Scriptura intelligi, in qua divinæ justitiæ præcepta atque consilia continentur. Unde Sapientia ait : Justi sunt omnes sermones mei, et non est in illis perversum quid neque pravum. Et ita Dei justitiam annuntiare, est sacram Scripturam docere, prædicare, aut legere. Annuntiabit quoque os meum tota die salutare tuum, id est, indesinenter competentibus horis diei, narrabo atque laudabo Dominum Christum omnium salvatorem; vel, Salutare tuum, id est salutem et salvationem quam nobis misericorditer impendisti per Christum, atque in cœlis parasti.
paras.en: [[70:15|My mouth shall shew forth|Os meum annuntiabit]], praising thee inwardly and preaching thee before others, [[70:15|thy justice|justitiam tuam]], by which thou renderest to each what he deserves, and workest all things without respect of persons. Thee, therefore, O Lord, will I justify, thy judgments will I approve, but myself will I accuse and condemn. By the justice of God may also be understood holy Scripture, in which the precepts and counsels of the divine justice are contained. Hence Wisdom says: [[Prov 8:8|All my words are just, there is nothing wicked, nor perverse in them|Justi sunt omnes sermones mei, et non est in illis perversum quid neque pravum]]. And so to shew forth the justice of God is to teach, preach or read holy Scripture. My mouth shall shew forth also, [[70:15|all the day long|tota die]], [[70:15|thy salvation|salutare tuum]] [*salutare*, "salvation", can also be read as "Saviour"]: that is, unceasingly at the fitting hours of the day I will tell of and praise the Lord Christ, the Saviour of all; or, [[70:15|thy salvation|Salutare tuum]], that is, the salvation and saving which thou hast mercifully bestowed on us through Christ, and prepared in heaven.

paras.t: Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam. Istud variis modis exponi potest. Primo sic : Non cognovi litteraturam, id est, non approbavi inanem philosophiam, et omnem scientiam extollentem se adversum scientiam Dei : non quod philosophia sit per se odibilis aut vitanda ; sed quia non debemus in ea quiescere et inaniter gloriari aut inflari, sed ad divinam doctrinam ipsam ordinare. Vel, Non cognovi litteraturam, id est, nihil me scire arbitratus sum, quando in conspectu Dei me ipsum constitui, et ad ejus sapientiam infinitam me comparavi. Vel, Non cognovi litteraturam, id est aliquam scientiam per humanam exercitationem, informationem et studium. Hoc non competit omnibus, sed Petro et Joanni, de quibus legitur, quod erant homines sine litteris et idiotæ. Dicitur etiam convenire sancto David, qui tempore suæ juventutis oves pavisse legitur, non scholas frequentasse, ut aliqui dicunt ; sed non videtur certum, quia et psalmos metro conscripsit.
paras.en: [[70:15|Because I have not known learning|Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam]] [*litteratura*, letters, that is, book-learning]. This can be expounded in various ways. First thus: [[70:15|I have not known learning|Non cognovi litteraturam]], that is, I have not approved vain philosophy, and all knowledge [[2 Cor 10:5|that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God|extollentem se adversum scientiam Dei]]: not that philosophy is hateful in itself or to be shunned, but because we ought not to rest in it, and glory in it vainly or be puffed up, but to direct it to divine doctrine. Or, [[70:15|I have not known learning|Non cognovi litteraturam]], that is, I thought that I knew nothing when I set myself in the sight of God and compared myself with his infinite wisdom. Or, [[70:15|I have not known learning|Non cognovi litteraturam]], that is, any knowledge got by human practice, instruction and study. This does not apply to all, but to Peter and John, of whom we read that they were [[Acts 4:13|illiterate and ignorant men|homines sine litteris et idiotæ]]. It is also said to fit holy David, who is read to have fed sheep in the time of his youth[[1 Kings 16:11||]][[1 Kings 17:15||]], not to have frequented schools, as some say; but this does not seem certain, since he also wrote the psalms in metre.

paras.t: Quoniam ergo his modis vel aliquo horum, non cognovi litteraturam, introibo per contemplationem supernaturalem, in potentias Domini, id est in perfectiones seu veritates divinas, easque cognoscam et alios instruam. Perfectio Dei et virtus ejus, est una ac simplex, utpote sua essentia ; sed dicuntur plures potentiæ, perfectiones virtutesque Dei, quoniam Deus in ipso suo simplicissimo esse, omnium rerum perfectiones eminentissime comprehendit. Ad harum divinarum perfectionum, quæ sunt sapientia, justitia, misericordia, contemplationem ingreditur, qui in proprio sensu non confidit, neque naturali rationi innititur, sed divinitus illustratur. Unde et Christus in Evangelio : Confiteor tibi, Pater, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis. Quid est, A sapientibus et prudentibus, nisi a litteratis? Et nonne Paulus litteratus erat, qui legem ad pedes Gamalielis didicerat? Quid ergo est, Abscondisti hæc a sapientibus, prudentibus et litteratis, nisi ab his qui in sua sapientia et litteratura inaniter gloriantur, seque sapientes et litteratos arbitrantur? Tales propter suam superbiam, divinæ illuminationis capaces non sunt, nec fiunt, nisi convertantur et efficiantur ut parvuli. Ideo namque ait sapientissimus Paulus : Si quis videtur inter vos sapiens esse, stultus fiat ut sit sapiens.
paras.en: Since therefore in these ways, or in some one of them, [[70:15|I have not known learning|non cognovi litteraturam]], [[70:16|I will enter|introibo]] by supernatural contemplation [[70:16|into the powers of the Lord|in potentias Domini]], that is, into the divine perfections or truths, and I will know them and instruct others. The perfection of God and his power is one and simple, being indeed his essence; but many powers, perfections and virtues of God are spoken of, because God in his own most simple being comprehends the perfections of all things in the most eminent way. He enters into the contemplation of these divine perfections, which are wisdom, justice, mercy, who does not trust in his own sense nor lean on natural reason, but is enlightened from above. Hence Christ too says in the Gospel: [[Matt 11:25|I confess to thee, O Father|Confiteor tibi, Pater]], [[Matt 11:25|because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones|quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]. What is [[Matt 11:25|from the wise and prudent|A sapientibus et prudentibus]], but from the lettered? And yet was not Paul lettered, who had learned the law at the feet of Gamaliel[[Acts 22:3||]]? What then is [[Matt 11:25|thou hast hid these things from the wise|Abscondisti hæc a sapientibus]], the prudent and the lettered, but from those who glory vainly in their own wisdom and learning, and think themselves wise and lettered? Such men, because of their pride, are not capable of the divine enlightenment, nor do they become so, unless they [[Matt 18:3|be converted, and become as little children|convertantur et efficiantur ut parvuli]]. For this is why the most wise Paul says: [[1 Cor 3:18|If any man among you seem to be wise|Si quis videtur inter vos sapiens esse]], [[1 Cor 3:18|let him become a fool, that he may be wise|stultus fiat ut sit sapiens]].

paras.t: Vel sic : Introibo in potentias Domini, id est, fortes Dei illuminationes, et potentes ac magnas gratias ejus recipiam, tanquam nihil de proprio sperans ingenio, sed Deo me humiliter applicando, sicque contemplabor et sciam quam potens et gloriosus sit Deus meus. Et tunc, o Domine, memorabor justitiæ tuæ solius, id est, tuam dumtaxat justitiam commemorabo, nihil de mea justitia allegabo, omne bonum, virtutem et gratiam tibi adscribam, omne malum, omnem defectum et culpam mihi attribuam, dicamque cum Apostolo : Gratia Dei sum id quod sum ; et denuo, Qui se putat aliquid esse, quum nihil sit, ipse se seducit ; et iterum, Ignorantes, inquit, Dei justitiam, et suam volentes statuere, justitiæ Dei non sunt subjecti.
paras.en: Or thus: [[70:16|I will enter into the powers of the Lord|Introibo in potentias Domini]], that is, I will receive the strong enlightenments of God and his mighty and great graces, as one hoping nothing from his own wit, but humbly applying himself to God; and so I shall contemplate and know how mighty and glorious my God is. And then, [[70:16|O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone|o Domine, memorabor justitiæ tuæ solius]]: that is, I will call to mind thy justice only, I will allege nothing of my own justice; I will ascribe all good, virtue and grace to thee, all evil, every defect and fault to myself, and I will say with the Apostle: [[1 Cor 15:10|by the grace of God, I am what I am|Gratia Dei sum id quod sum]]; and again, [[Gal 6:3|if any man think himself to be some thing, whereas he is nothing, he deceiveth himself|Qui se putat aliquid esse, quum nihil sit, ipse se seducit]]; and once more, [[Rom 10:3|not knowing|Ignorantes]], he says, [[Rom 10:3|the justice of God and seeking to establish their own, have not submitted themselves to the justice of God|Dei justitiam, et suam volentes statuere, justitiæ Dei non sunt subjecti]].

paras.t: Et quasi quis diceret, Si, o serve Dei, litteraturam non nosti, quomodo tam decora documenta atque sublimes sententias nosti atque conscribis ? respondet, ad Dominum loquens : Deus, docuisti me per inspirationem Spiritus Sancti et illuminationem supernaturalem, a juventute mea, vel corporali, vel spirituali : de quibus modo satis prædictum videtur ; et usque nunc, conservando, augendo, seu perficiendo gratiam tuam in me. Pronuntiabo mirabilia tua, quæ facis in cœlo et in terra, in operibus naturæ ac mysteriis gratiæ : maxime tamen incarnationem, passionem, et mortem tuam, o Christe, pronuntiabo.
paras.en: And as though someone were to say: If, O servant of God, thou knowest not learning, how dost thou know and write such fitting teachings and lofty sentences? he answers, speaking to the Lord: [[70:17|Thou hast taught me, O God|Deus, docuisti me]], by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost and supernatural enlightenment, [[70:17|from my youth|a juventute mea]], whether bodily or spiritual (of which enough seems to have been said already); [[70:17|and till now|et usque nunc]], by keeping, increasing or perfecting thy grace in me. [[70:17|I will declare thy wonderful works|Pronuntiabo mirabilia tua]], which thou doest in heaven and on earth, in the works of nature and the mysteries of grace; but above all, O Christ, I will declare thy incarnation, passion and death.

paras.t: Et usque in senectam spiritualem, et senium corporale, de quibus distinctio assignata est, pronuntiabo mirabilia tua. Deus, ne derelinquas me, Donec annuntiem brachium tuum, id est majestatis tuæ potentiam ; vel, Brachium tuum, id est unigenitum Filium tuum, qui est fortitudo et virtus tua : de quo Isaias dixit : Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium. Sicut et Spiritus Sanctus vocatur digitus Dei ratione sui effectus, quoniam cuncta demonstrat ; sic Filius appellatur brachium Dei, qui omnia portat et sustentat verbo virtutis suæ. Annuntiem itaque, Domine, brachium tuum generationi omni quæ ventura est usque ad finem mundi. Hoc auctor psalmi præsentis excellenter perfecit. Per librum enim Psalmorum, quem edidit et nobis reliquit, annuntiat ista indesinenter toti mundo : et quilibet nostrum hoc agit, dum quantum sibi possibile est, nomen Dei glorificat, et ejus honorem augere conatur ; atque post suam mortem divinæ legis testimonia disserit, verbo, fama et vita verum esse contestans quod fides affirmat catholica.
paras.en: [[70:18|And unto old age|Et usque in senectam]], the spiritual, [[70:18|and grey hairs|et senium]], the bodily (between which a distinction has been drawn), I will declare thy wonderful works. [[70:18|O God, forsake me not|Deus, ne derelinquas me]], [[70:18|Until I shew forth thy arm|Donec annuntiem brachium tuum]], that is, the might of thy majesty; or, [[70:18|thy arm|Brachium tuum]], that is, thy only-begotten Son, who is thy strength and power: of whom Isaias said: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles|Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium]] [the margin gives Is. xli, 10; the words are those of Is 52:10]. Just as the Holy Ghost too is called the finger of God[[Luke 11:20||]] by reason of his effect, since he shows forth all things, so the Son is called the arm of God, who bears and upholds all things by the word of his power[[Heb 1:3||]]. Let me then shew forth, O Lord, thy arm [[70:18|to all the generation that is to come|generationi omni quæ ventura est]], even to the end of the world. This the author of the present psalm has done excellently. For by the book of Psalms, which he put forth and left to us, he shews these things forth unceasingly to the whole world; and each of us does this when, as far as he can, he glorifies the name of God and strives to increase his honour; and after his death he sets forth the testimonies of the divine law, bearing witness by word, repute and life that what the catholic faith affirms is true.

paras.t: Annuntiem quoque, o Domine, Potentiam tuam, quæ vere immensa est, per quam omnia creasti, conservas et regis, et justitiam tuam, Deus, qua unicuique quod meretur, rependis : potentiam, inquam, et justitiam tuam annuntiem, non secundum quod in se est, quoniam sic omnino incognita est ; sed per comparationem ad suos sublimes effectus, videlicet usque in altissima, quæ fecisti, magnalia. Quæ autem sunt ista altissima magnalia a Deo producta ? nisi angelicorum distinctio ordinum, creatio visibilium et invisibilium, beatificatio electorum, gubernatio mundi, justificatio impii, redemptionis humanæ mysteria, et reliqua Dei prodigia, signa atque miracula. In his effectibus relucet Creatoris justitia et admiranda potentia.
paras.en: Let me shew forth also, O Lord, [[70:18|Thy power|Potentiam tuam]], which is truly boundless, by which thou hast created all things, and preservest and rulest them, [[70:19|And thy justice, O God|et justitiam tuam, Deus]], by which thou repayest to each what he deserves: thy power, I say, and thy justice let me shew forth, not as it is in itself, for so it is wholly unknown, but by comparison with its sublime effects, namely [[70:19|even to the highest great things thou hast done|usque in altissima, quæ fecisti, magnalia]]. And what are these highest great things brought forth by God, but the distinction of the angelic orders, the creation of things visible and invisible, the beatification of the elect, the government of the world, the justification of the wicked, the mysteries of man's redemption, and the other wonders, signs and miracles of God? In these effects shine the justice and the wonderful power of the Creator.

paras.t: Quum ergo tanta sint tua magnalia, o Deus, quis similis tibi ? quasi dicat, Nullus. Similitudo autem est duplex, imitativa seu imperfecta, et naturalis seu perfecta. Secundum primam similitudinem creatura similis est Creatori, præcipue homo, qui ad Dei imaginem et similitudinem factus est ; sed quantum ad similitudinem secundam, nil creatum simile est Creatori. Unde per Isaiam prophetam dicitur : Cui similem fecistis Deum ? aut quam imaginem ponetis ei ? Et Job : Ecce excelsus Deus in fortitudine sua, et nullus ei similis in legislatoribus.
paras.en: Since, then, thy great works are so great, [[70:19|O God, who is like to thee?|o Deus, quis similis tibi ?]] As if to say, None. Now likeness is twofold: imitative or imperfect, and natural or perfect. In the first kind of likeness the creature is like the Creator, above all man, who was made to the image and likeness of God[[Gen 1:26||]] [the margin gives Gen. i, 27; the words "image and likeness" are those of Gen 1:26]; but as to the second likeness, nothing created is like the Creator. Hence it is said by the prophet Isaias: [[Is 40:18|To whom then have you likened God? or what image will you make for him?|Cui similem fecistis Deum ? aut quam imaginem ponetis ei ?]] And Job: [[Job 36:22|Behold, God is high in his strength, and none is like him among the lawgivers|Ecce excelsus Deus in fortitudine sua, et nullus ei similis in legislatoribus]].

paras.t: Quantas, o Deus, ostendisti mihi per experientiam, tribulationes mundi, carnis, ac dæmonum, multas numero, et malas malitia pœnæ, acerbas ac duras, aut certe injusta seu mala intentione aliorum illatas ! Et conversus, id est placatus et mei misertus, vivificasti me vita gratiæ, auferendo a me flagella iracundiæ tuæ ; et de abyssis terræ, id est de submersione peccati, et fluctibus sæculi, iterum, id est frequenter, reduxisti me ad statum salutis et gratiæ.
paras.en: [[70:20|How great|Quantas]], O God, [[70:20|troubles|tribulationes]] of the world, the flesh and the demons [[70:20|hast thou shewn me|ostendisti mihi]] by experience, [[70:20|many|multas]] in number, [[70:20|and grievous|et malas]] [literally "and evil"] in the malice of the pain, bitter and hard, or at least inflicted through the unjust or evil intention of others! [[70:20|and turning|Et conversus]], that is, appeased and taking pity on me, [[70:20|thou hast brought me to life|vivificasti me]] with the life of grace, taking from me the scourges of thy wrath; and [[70:20|from the depths of the earth|de abyssis terræ]], that is, from the drowning of sin and the waves of the world, [[70:20|again|iterum]], that is, often, [[70:20|hast brought me back|reduxisti me]] to the state of salvation and grace.

paras.t: Multiplicasti magnificentiam tuam, id est, magnam tuam potentiam multipliciter ostendisti in me, flagellando me variis modis ; et conversus, ab ira tuæ vindictæ ad mansuetudinem tuæ dilectionis paternæ absque tui mutatione, consolatus es me infusione interioris lætitiæ, contemplatione felicitatis futuræ, seu præmiorum consideratione, et allocutione sacræ Scripturæ, in qua dicitur : Quoniam non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis ; et, Si compatimur, et conregnabimus.
paras.en: [[70:21|Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence|Multiplicasti magnificentiam tuam]]: that is, thou hast shewn thy great power in me in many ways, scourging me in various ways; [[70:21|and turning|et conversus]] from the wrath of thy vengeance to the gentleness of thy fatherly love, without any change in thyself, [[70:21|thou hast comforted me|consolatus es me]] by the pouring in of inward joy, by the contemplation of the happiness to come, or the thought of the rewards, and by the words of holy Scripture, in which it is said: [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us|Quoniam non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam, quæ revelabitur in nobis]]; and, [[Rom 8:17|if we suffer with him|Si compatimur]], [[2 Tim 2:12|we shall also reign with him|et conregnabimus]].

paras.t: Hujus autem consolationis meæ indicium est : Nam et ego confitebor tibi confessione laudis, in vasis psalmi, id est in psalmis, quæ sunt vasa laudis divinæ in ipsis contentæ ; vel, In vasis psalmi, id est in viris devotis, in quorum cordibus velut in vasis continetur laus tua ; vel, In vasis psalmi, id est in Psalterio, quod dicitur vas psalmorum ; veritatem tuam, Deus, id est, ad gloriam tuam confitebor seu laudabo veritatem tuam in divinis Scripturis traditam, vel veritatem tuam increatam, quæ est omnis veritatis fontana origo. Psallam tibi in cithara spirituali, scilicet in carnis mortificatione per citheram significata, o Domine, qui es Sanctus Israel, id est sanctificator populi te fideliter contemplantis.
paras.en: And the token of this my consolation is: [[70:22|For I will also confess to thee|Nam et ego confitebor tibi]] with the confession of praise, [[70:22|with the instruments of psaltery|in vasis psalmi]] [literally "in the vessels of the psalm"], that is, in the psalms, which are vessels of the divine praise contained in them; or, [[70:22|with the instruments of psaltery|In vasis psalmi]], that is, in devout men, in whose hearts thy praise is contained as in vessels; or, [[70:22|with the instruments of psaltery|In vasis psalmi]], that is, in the Psalter, which is called the vessel of the psalms; [[70:22|thy truth|veritatem tuam]], [[70:22|O God|Deus]]: that is, to thy glory I will confess or praise thy truth handed down in the divine Scriptures, or thy uncreated truth, which is the fountain-source of all truth. [[70:22|I will sing to thee with the harp|Psallam tibi in cithara]], the spiritual harp, namely in the mortification of the flesh, signified by the harp, O Lord, who art the [[70:22|holy one of Israel|Sanctus Israel]], that is, the sanctifier of the people that faithfully contemplates thee.

paras.t: Exsultabunt labia mea exteriora, id est, signa lætitiæ manifestabunt, quum cantavero tibi : quoniam vultu hilaris ero, secundum faciem Sanctorum, quum te ore laudavero. Vel : Exsultabunt, id est, exuberanter gaudebunt, labia mea interiora, videlicet intellectus et voluntas, quibus interiora verba et vota formantur, quum cantavero tibi, id est ad tuum honorem. Et anima mea quam redemisti per gratiam tuam a culpa, atque per sanguinis tui pretium a gehenna, exsultabit tibi cantando.
paras.en: [[70:23|My lips shall greatly rejoice|Exsultabunt labia mea]], the outward lips, that is, they shall show signs of gladness, [[70:23|when I shall sing to thee|quum cantavero tibi]]: for I shall be cheerful of countenance, after the countenance of the saints[[Jdt 16:24||]] [a phrase of Judith 16:24, where the Douay-Rheims has "in the sight of the sanctuary"], when I praise thee with my mouth. Or: [[70:23|shall greatly rejoice|Exsultabunt]], that is, shall rejoice abundantly, [[70:23|my lips|labia mea]] within, namely the understanding and the will, by which inward words and vows are formed, [[70:23|when I shall sing to thee|quum cantavero tibi]], that is, to thy honour. [[70:23|and my soul which thou hast redeemed|Et anima mea quam redemisti]] by thy grace from guilt, and by the price of thy blood from hell, shall rejoice in singing to thee.

paras.t: Sed et lingua mea interior, scilicet intellectus, tota die, id est horis aptis ac debitis, meditabitur justitiam tuam, revolvendo intra se legem tuam justissimam. Vel, Lingua mea corporea, meditabitur, id est, ex interiori cogitatione loquetur, justitiam tuam. Quum confusi, id est repulsi, victi, et reveriti, id est perterriti, fuerint qui quærunt mala mihi, id est dæmones mihi nocere optantes, vel homines mali : de quorum confusione atque repulsa gaudent boni tranquillam vitam amantes.
paras.en: [[70:24|Yea and my tongue|Sed et lingua mea]], the inner tongue, namely the understanding, [[70:24|all the day|tota die]], that is, at fit and due hours, [[70:24|shall meditate on thy justice|meditabitur justitiam tuam]], turning over within itself thy most just law. Or, [[70:24|my tongue|Lingua mea]], the bodily tongue, [[70:24|shall meditate|meditabitur]], that is, shall speak out of inward thought, [[70:24|thy justice|justitiam tuam]]. [[70:24|when they shall be confounded|Quum confusi]], that is, repulsed, overcome, [[70:24|and put to shame|et reveriti]], that is, terrified, [[70:24|that seek evils to me|fuerint qui quærunt mala mihi]], that is, the demons who desire to harm me, or wicked men: in whose confusion and repulse the good rejoice, who love a quiet life.

paras.t: Sed quia in hac vita non possumus plene erui, totaliter jugiterque ab eorum impugnatione esse securi ; idcirco versus iste anagogice exponi potest de statu futuro in patria. Tunc enim lingua nostra interior et forte etiam exterior, tota die æternitatis, id est continue et indefesse, meditabitur justitiam Dei per contemplationem clarissimam, quum confusi et reveriti fuerint, etc., quia in die judicii irreparabiliter confundentur omnes iniqui, juxta illud Isaiæ : Præcipitabit Dominus mortem in sempiternum, et opprobrium populi sui auferet. Unde et viro electo ait Dominus : Ne timeas, quia ego tecum sum ; ecce confundentur omnes qui pugnant contra te.
paras.en: But since in this life we cannot be fully delivered, nor be wholly and continually secure from their assault, this verse can therefore be expounded anagogically [that is, of the life to come] of the future state in the fatherland. For then our inner tongue, and perhaps the outer too, [[70:24|all the day|tota die]] of eternity, that is, continually and tirelessly, [[70:24|shall meditate on|meditabitur]] the justice of God by most clear contemplation, [[70:24|when they shall be confounded and put to shame|quum confusi et reveriti fuerint]], etc.; for on the day of judgment all the wicked will be confounded beyond repair, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 25:8|He shall cast death down headlong for ever|Præcipitabit Dominus mortem in sempiternum]], [[Is 25:8|and the reproach of his people he shall take away|et opprobrium populi sui auferet]]. Hence the Lord says also to the chosen man: [[Is 41:10|Fear not, for I am with thee|Ne timeas, quia ego tecum sum]]; [[Is 41:11|Behold all that fight against thee shall be confounded|ecce confundentur omnes qui pugnant contra te]].

70.title: EXPLANATIO ALLEGORICA EJUSDEM PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI DE CHRISTO.
70.title_en: Allegorical explanation of the same seventieth psalm, concerning Christ.

paras.t: Quoniam psalmus iste gloriosus atque decorus, in principio sui, verbis et sensu conformis est psalmo tricesimo, qui sic incipit sicut iste; in processu autem, similis est in aliquibus psalmo vicesimo primo, cujus exordium est, Deus, Deus meus, respice in me: quorum uterque ad litteram de Christo exponitur: idcirco studendum est, ut et præsens psalmus exponatur, quantum fieri potest, de Domino Salvatore.
paras.en: Since this glorious and beautiful psalm agrees at its beginning, in words and in sense, with the thirtieth psalm, which begins just as this one does, and further on is like in some things to the twenty-first psalm, whose opening is [[Ps 21:2|O God my God, look upon me|Deus, Deus meus, respice in me]], and since both of these are expounded literally of Christ, we must endeavour to expound the present psalm too, as far as may be, of the Lord the Saviour.

paras.t: Christus ergo secundum quod homo passibilis, et aliquo modo viator exstiterat, ad passionem propinquans, oravit ad Patrem dicendo: In te, Domine Pater, speravi, id est, omne bonum quod desideravi, teque rogavi, a te adipisci confisus sum, non per spem quæ est virtus theologica, sed per quamdam fiduciam. Spes enim quæ est virtus theologica, est exspectatio futuræ beatitudinis. Quum igitur anima Christi a suæ creationis principio beata fuerit, Deum videndo per speciem, constat quod spem talem non habuit; nihilo minus habuit quamdam præstolationem sive fiduciam: de qua in Proverbiis scribitur, Gemma gratissima, exspectatio præstolantis. Speravit namque anima Christi a Deo gloriam corporis, et alia quædam ad præmium accidentale spectantia. Quoniam ergo in te, Domine, speravi, non confundar in æternum: id est, quamvis ad tempus a Judæis despicior et illudor, ab Herode quoque et Pilato atque eorum militibus, non tamen duret diu ista confusio, sed tertia die honorer a te per resurrectionem beatam.
paras.en: Christ, then, inasmuch as he was a man capable of suffering and in some manner a wayfarer [that is, one still on the way to the heavenly homeland; the blessed who already possess it are called comprehensors], drawing near to his Passion, prayed to the Father, saying: [[70:1|In thee, O Lord|In te, Domine]] Father, [[70:1|I have hoped|speravi]]; that is, I have trusted that I shall obtain from thee every good that I have desired and asked of thee: not by the hope which is a theological virtue, but by a certain confidence. For the hope which is a theological virtue is the expectation of future beatitude. Since, then, the soul of Christ was blessed from the first moment of its creation, seeing God face to face [literally "by sight" (per speciem), that is, by direct vision, not through faith], it is plain that he had no such hope; none the less he had a certain expectation or confidence, of which it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 17:8|The expectation of him that expecteth is a most acceptable jewel|Gemma gratissima, exspectatio præstolantis]]. For the soul of Christ hoped from God for the glory of the body, and for certain other things belonging to his accidental reward [that is, joys added to the essential reward, which is the vision of God]. Since, then, [[70:1|In thee, O Lord, I have hoped|in te, Domine, speravi]], [[70:1|let me never be put to confusion|non confundar in æternum]]: that is, although for a time I am despised and mocked by the Jews[[Matt 26:67||]][[Matt 26:68||]], and also by Herod and Pilate and their soldiers[[Luke 23:11||]], yet let this confusion not last long, but on the third day let me be honoured by thee through a blessed resurrection.

paras.t: In justitia tua, id est secundum justitiam tuam, et secundum exigentiam ejus, libera me a generatione hac infideli ac pessima, de qua locutus sum: Quamdiu apud vos ero? quamdiu patiar vos? Et eripe me ab omni corporis mortalitate ac passibilitate.
paras.en: [[70:2|in thy justice|In justitia tua]], that is, according to thy justice and as it requires, [[70:2|Deliver me|libera me]] from this unbelieving and most wicked generation, of which I have said: [[Mark 9:18|how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you?|Quamdiu apud vos ero? quamdiu patiar vos?]] [[70:2|and rescue me|Et eripe me]] from all mortality and passibility of the body.

paras.t: Inclina ad me Filium tuum unicum et dilectum, aurem tuam: quod oro, non quasi incertus quod sic facies, sed quia per orationem decrevisti dare quod opto, ut ego ostendam me a te habere omne bonum quod habeo, aliisque formam orandi exhibeam. Et salva me ab omni malo pœnæ, dando etiam præmium accidentale, videlicet corporis glorificationem et ascensionem.
paras.en: [[70:2|Incline|Inclina]] [[70:2|unto me|ad me]] thy only and beloved Son, [[70:2|thy ear|aurem tuam]]: this I pray, not as though uncertain that thou wilt do so, but because thou hast decreed to give what I desire through prayer, so that I may show that I have from thee every good that I have, and may set before others a pattern of praying. [[70:2|and save me|Et salva me]] from every evil of punishment, giving me also my accidental reward, namely the glorification of my body and the ascension.

paras.t: Esto mihi in Deum protectorem, ne ante tempus a te præordinatum, a Judæis comprehendar, occidar, aut lædar: qui me præcipitare lapidareque conati sunt, sed non potuerunt quoniam nondum venit hora mea. Esto etiam mihi et in locum munitum, ut in te quasi in loco confugii securus ab omni invasione quiescam, ut salvum me facias, animam corpori reuniendo. Quoniam firmamentum meum, id est confirmator meæ humanitatis, et causa universæ fortitudinis ejus, et refugium meum es tu, id est adjutor meus in quantum homo sum, et ad quem in omni necessitate confugio. Hinc enim ait Salvator de semetipso: Non possum ego a me ipso facere quidquam; et iterum, Pater in me manens, ipse facit opera. Isaias quoque: Ecce Dominus Deus, auxiliator meus; et Jeremias: Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis; idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent.
paras.en: [[70:3|Be thou unto me a God, a protector|Esto mihi in Deum protectorem]], lest before the time foreordained by thee I be seized, slain or harmed by the Jews, who tried to cast me down headlong[[Luke 4:29||]] and to stone me[[John 8:59||]][[John 10:31||]], but could not[[Luke 4:30||]][[John 10:39||]], because my hour was not yet come[[John 8:20||]]. Be thou also unto me [[70:3|and a place of strength|et in locum munitum]], that in thee, as in a place of refuge, I may rest secure from every assault, [[70:3|that thou mayst make me safe|ut salvum me facias]], by reuniting my soul to my body. [[70:3|For thou art my firmament|Quoniam firmamentum meum]], that is, the strengthener of my humanity and the cause of all its strength, [[70:3|and my refuge|et refugium meum es tu]], that is, my helper inasmuch as I am man, and he to whom I flee in every need. For hence the Saviour says of himself: [[John 5:30|I cannot of myself do any thing|Non possum ego a me ipso facere quidquam]]; and again, [[John 14:10|the Father who abideth in me, he doth the works|Pater in me manens, ipse facit opera]]. Isaias too: [[Is 50:9|Behold the Lord God is my helper|Ecce Dominus Deus, auxiliator meus]] [the margin gives Is. i, 9; the words are Is 50:9]; and Jeremias: [[Jer 20:11|the Lord is with me as a strong warrior: therefore they that persecute me shall fall|Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis; idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent]].

paras.t: Deus meus, qui es specialissimo modo Deus meus, eripe me de manu peccatoris, id est de potestate Judæ proditoris, cujus iniquitatem cœli revelabunt, et terra adversus eum consurget; et de manu contra legem agentis et iniqui, id est populi Judæorum, de quo dixi, Nonne Moyses dedit vobis legem, et nemo ex vobis facit legem? et rursus, Quare vos transgredimini mandata Dei propter traditionem vestram?
paras.en: [[70:4|O my God|Deus meus]], who art in a most special manner my God, [[70:4|Deliver me|eripe me]] [[70:4|out of the hand of the sinner|de manu peccatoris]], that is, from the power of Judas the traitor, of whom it is said: [[Job 20:27|The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him|iniquitatem cœli revelabunt, et terra adversus eum consurget]]; [[70:4|and out of the hand of the transgressor of the law and of the unjust|et de manu contra legem agentis et iniqui]], that is, of the Jewish people, of whom I said: [[John 7:19|Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keepeth the law?|Nonne Moyses dedit vobis legem, et nemo ex vobis facit legem?]] And again: [[Matt 15:3|Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for your tradition?|Quare vos transgredimini mandata Dei propter traditionem vestram?]]

paras.t: Quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine. Omnis enim perfectio animæ Christi, a Deo infusa collataque fuit. Christus quoque omnia propter Dei honorem sustinuit, sicut superius dixit, Quoniam propter te sustinui opprobrium: sicque Deus erat causa efficiens et finalis patientiæ Christi. Domine, spes mea a juventute mea. Nam Christus per prædictam fiduciam semper certissime et immobiliter speravit in Deo. Propter quod dixit: Ego autem sciebam quoniam semper me audis.
paras.en: [[70:5|For thou art my patience, O Lord|Quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine]]. For every perfection of the soul of Christ was infused and bestowed by God. Christ also bore all things for the honour of God, as he said above [that is, in Psalm 68]: [[Ps 68:8|Because for thy sake I have borne reproach|Quoniam propter te sustinui opprobrium]]; and so God was the efficient and the final cause of Christ's patience. [[70:5|my hope, O Lord, from my youth|Domine, spes mea a juventute mea]]. For Christ, by the confidence spoken of above, always hoped in God most surely and unshakeably. Wherefore he said: [[John 11:42|And I knew that thou hearest me always|Ego autem sciebam quoniam semper me audis]].

paras.t: In te confirmatus sum ex utero: id est, in ipso Matris meæ virgineo utero, per gratiam consummatam, id est per beatificam fruitionem, fixus et roboratus sum in te, ita ut a te nunquam possim averti. Non enim solum erat anima Christi in utero Virginis sanctificata per gratiam, sed et immobilis facta per gloriam. De ventre matris meæ tu es protector meus: id est, ab instanti nativitatis meæ usque ad mortem protexisti me ab omni ruina peccati, a tentatione diaboli, et a pœnis quas Judæi mihi ante tempus inferre volebant. Quoniam enim Christus confirmatus erat in bono in Virginis utero, post nativitatem peccare nullatenus potuit. Hinc de se ipso per Isaiam prædixit: Quis est adversarius meus? accedat ad me. Quis contradicit mihi? stemus simul. Ecce quanta securitas propter protectionem divinam: propter quod nullo modo opinandum est, quod Christus expavit, quando ducebant eum ad supercilium montis, quatenus præcipitarent eum. In te cantatio mea semper: id est, te, o Deus Pater, semper laudavi, nominis tui honorem, non propriam gloriam, semper quæsivi, sicut testatus sum blasphemis Judæis: Ego non quæro gloriam meam, sed honorifico Patrem meum, et vos inhonorastis me.
paras.en: [[70:6|By thee have I been confirmed from the womb|In te confirmatus sum ex utero]]: that is, in the very virginal womb of my Mother, through consummated grace, that is, through the beatific enjoyment [of God], I was fixed and strengthened in thee, so that I can never be turned away from thee. For the soul of Christ in the Virgin's womb was not only sanctified by grace, but also made immovable by glory. [[70:6|from my mother's womb thou art my protector|De ventre matris meæ tu es protector meus]]: that is, from the instant of my birth until my death thou hast protected me from every fall into sin, from the temptation of the devil, and from the punishments which the Jews wished to inflict on me before the time. For since Christ was confirmed in good in the Virgin's womb, after his birth he could in no wise sin. Hence he foretold of himself through Isaias: [[Is 50:8|who is my adversary? let him come near to me|Quis est adversarius meus? accedat ad me]] [[Is 50:8|who will contend with me? let us stand together|Quis contradicit mihi? stemus simul]]. Behold how great a security, because of the divine protection! Wherefore it is in no way to be thought that Christ was afraid when they led him to the brow of the hill, that they might cast him down headlong[[Luke 4:29||]]. [[70:6|Of thee I shall continually sing|In te cantatio mea semper]]: that is, thee, O God the Father, I have always praised; the honour of thy name, not my own glory, I have always sought, as I testified to the blaspheming Jews: [[John 8:50|But I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]], but [[John 8:49|I honour my Father. And you have dishonoured me|honorifico Patrem meum, et vos inhonorastis me]].

paras.t: Tanquam prodigium factus sum multis, puta Judæis, de quibus scriptum est: Dicebant multi ex Judæis: Dæmonium habet et insanit, quid eum auditis? Et quum filiam archisynagogi suscitaturus dixisset, Puella non est mortua, sed dormit, deridebant eum. Unde de Christo apud Isaiam prædictum est: Inglorius erit inter viros adspectus ejus. Et tu adjutor fortis, quoniam in omni adversitate fecisti me constantem atque immobilem.
paras.en: [[70:7|I am become unto many as a wonder|Tanquam prodigium factus sum multis]], namely to the Jews, of whom it is written: [[John 10:20|many of them said: He hath a devil and is mad. Why hear you him?|Dicebant multi ex Judæis: Dæmonium habet et insanit, quid eum auditis?]] [the margin gives "Ibid. v. 20" after John 8; the words are John 10:20; Denis has "many of the Jews"]. And when he was about to raise the daughter of the ruler of the synagogue and had said, [[Luke 8:52|The maid is not dead, but sleepeth|Puella non est mortua, sed dormit]], [[Luke 8:53|they laughed him to scorn|deridebant eum]]. Hence it was foretold of Christ in Isaias: [[Is 52:14|so shall his visage be inglorious among men|Inglorius erit inter viros adspectus ejus]] [the margin gives Is. liii, 14; the words are Is 52:14]. [[70:7|but thou art a strong helper|Et tu adjutor fortis]], because in every adversity thou hast made me constant and immovable.

paras.t: Repleatur os meum laude. Christus in gratia habituali nunquam profecit, nec in ea proficere exoravit. Unde, quemadmodum Sancti in patria Deum non rogant pro gratia benefaciendi, sic nec Christus exoravit ut ex gratiæ interioris incremento ad Dei laudem prorumperet. Ideoque quod ait, Repleatur, etc., potius congratulando quod sic est, quam orando ut sic sit, intelligendum videtur. Vel orat ut corpus suum in morte ab anima separatum, denuo uniatur eidem, et ita os suum corporale in triduo mortis clausum, per resurrectionem aperiatur, laudibusque divinis impleatur. Ut cantem, inquit, gloriam tuam. Christus enim ore interiori jugiter decantavit gloriam summæ Trinitatis, laudando eam in sæculum sæculi multo sublimius quam aliquis Beatorum in patria, secundum quod comprehensor fuit: et tota die, id est incessanter, et in die æternitatis participatæ, quæ fuit mensura operationum suarum interiorum, convenientium sibi ut comprehensori, cantavit interiori melodia magnitudinem Dei, illam clarissime cognoscendo, atque dignissime extollendo. Denique etiam ante passionem et post resurrectionem cantavit ore corporali gloriam Dei, scilicet evangelicæ legis doctrinam, in qua Deus pulchre laudatur; et tota die, id est semper congruis horis, cantavit seu prædicavit magnitudinem Dei per se ipsum ac suos ministros.
paras.en: [[70:8|Let my mouth be filled with praise|Repleatur os meum laude]]. Christ never advanced in habitual grace [that is, the abiding grace that dwells in the soul], nor did he pray to advance in it. Hence, just as the Saints in the homeland do not ask God for the grace of doing well, so neither did Christ pray to break forth into the praise of God from an increase of inward grace. And so his saying, [[70:8|Let my mouth be filled|Repleatur]], etc., seems to be understood rather as rejoicing that it is so than as praying that it may be so. Or he prays that his body, separated from his soul in death, may be united to it anew, and so his bodily mouth, closed during the three days of death, may be opened through the resurrection and filled with the divine praises. [[70:8|that I may sing|Ut cantem]], he says, [[70:8|thy glory|gloriam tuam]]. For Christ with his inward mouth sang without ceasing the glory of the most high Trinity, praising it for ever and ever far more sublimely than any of the Blessed in the homeland, inasmuch as he was a comprehensor [that is, one already possessing the vision of God]; and [[70:8|all the day long|tota die]], that is, unceasingly, and in the day of participated eternity [that is, the share in God's eternity that measures the acts of the blessed], which was the measure of his inward operations befitting him as a comprehensor, he sang with an inward melody the [[70:8|greatness|magnitudinem]] of God, knowing it most clearly and extolling it most worthily. Lastly, before the Passion and after the resurrection he also sang with his bodily mouth the glory of God, namely the teaching of the Gospel law, in which God is beautifully praised; and [[70:8|all the day long|tota die]], that is, always at fitting hours, he sang or preached the greatness of God through himself and his ministers.

paras.t: Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis, etc. Dicere aliquis posset, Christum orasse hunc versum, non pro se ipso, sed pro corpore suo mystico, eo modo quo jam impassibilis factus, dixit ad Paulum, Quid me persequeris? Præsertim quum nec corporalis senectus nec spiritualis in Christo fuisse noscantur: nam juvenis occisus est, et in interioribus semper æqualiter recens virensque exstitit: propter quod viridi ligno comparavit se ipsum. Verumtamen dicere possumus, quod hoc loco per tempus senectutis, intelligatur tempus dominicæ passionis, in qua corporalis natura Christi, instar hominum antiquorum, a suo virore atque vigore occubuit. Eritque sensus, exponendo hunc versum de Christo: Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis, id est, tempore passionis non subtrahas mihi tuæ paternæ pietatis præsentiam, derelinquendo corpus in tumulo, aut animam in limbo. Non enim oravit Christus ne projiceretur a Deo, gratiam amittendo aut gloriam, quoniam se confirmatum cognovit in bono. Quum deficiet virtus mea corporalis in cruce; quando exspiravit, inclinato capite tradens spiritum; ne derelinquas me, sed audi quod dico: Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum.
paras.en: [[70:9|Cast me not off in the time of old age|Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis]], etc. Someone might say that Christ prayed this verse not for himself but for his mystical body, in the way in which, having already been made impassible, he said to Paul, [[Acts 9:4|why persecutest thou me|Quid me persequeris]]? Especially since neither bodily nor spiritual old age is known to have been in Christ: for he was slain as a young man, and inwardly he was always alike fresh and flourishing, for which reason he compared himself to green wood[[Luke 23:31||]]. Yet we can say that in this place the time of old age is understood as the time of the Lord's Passion, in which the bodily nature of Christ, like that of aged men, sank down from its freshness and vigour. And the sense, expounding this verse of Christ, will be: [[70:9|Cast me not off in the time of old age|Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis]], that is, in the time of the Passion do not withdraw from me the presence of thy fatherly love, by leaving my body in the tomb or my soul in limbo. For Christ did not pray that he might not be cast off by God through losing grace or glory, since he knew himself confirmed in good. [[70:9|when my strength shall fail|Quum deficiet virtus mea]], my bodily strength on the cross, when he expired, [[John 19:30|bowing his head, he gave up the ghost|inclinato capite tradens spiritum]]; [[70:9|do not thou forsake me|ne derelinquas me]], but hear what I say: [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]].

paras.t: Merito quoque precor ista, o Pater, quia dixerunt inimici mei Judæi mihi quidquid mali excogitare valebant, ut est illud, Numquid interficiet semetipsum? Et alibi: Homo vorax, potator vini; Hic blasphemat; multaque talia. Et qui custodiebant animam meam, id est Judæi, qui observabant vitam meam ut eam arguerent: quemadmodum in Evangelio scriptum est, Observabant si sabbatis curaret Jesus, ut accusarent eum; consilium fecerunt in unum, id est ad invicem et pari malitia, juxta illud: Consilium fecerunt, ut Jesum dolo tenerent et occiderent;
paras.en: Rightly too do I pray for these things, O Father, [[70:10|For my enemies have spoken against me|quia dixerunt inimici mei Judæi mihi]] (the Jews), whatever evil they could devise; as is that saying, [[John 8:22|Will he kill himself|Numquid interficiet semetipsum]]? and elsewhere: [[Matt 11:19|a man that is a glutton and a wine drinker|Homo vorax, potator vini]]; [[Mark 2:7|He blasphemeth|Hic blasphemat]]; and many such things. [[70:10|and they that watched my soul|Et qui custodiebant animam meam]], that is, the Jews, who watched my life so as to find fault with it: as it is written in the Gospel, [[Mark 3:2|they watched him whether he would heal on the sabbath days, that they might accuse him|Observabant si sabbatis curaret Jesus, ut accusarent eum]] [the margin gives "Ibid. ii, 2"; the words are Mark 3:2; Denis adds "Jesus"]; [[70:10|have consulted together|consilium fecerunt in unum]], that is, with one another and with equal malice, according to that saying: [[Matt 26:4|they consulted together that by subtilty they might apprehend Jesus and put him to death|Consilium fecerunt, ut Jesum dolo tenerent et occiderent]];

paras.t: dicentes: Deus dereliquit eum. Judæi namque putabant Deum recessisse a Jesu, tanquam a peccatore. Unde dicebant: Nos scimus quia hic homo peccator est; et iterum, Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit. Persequimini et comprehendite eum. Hoc est quod a Joanne dicitur: Miserunt Judæi ministros ut apprehenderent Jesum. Et in nocte Cœnæ dixerunt hæc verba suis ministris principes sacerdotum, qui eos miserunt cum Juda, ut caperent eum. Propter quod apud Jeremiam dicitur: Audivi contumelias multorum, et terrorem in circuitu: Persequimini et persequamur eum. Quia non est qui eripiat, id est, nullus est qui Jesum de vestris manibus eruat, eo quod Deus reliquerit eum. Hinc enim dicunt adversarii Christi: Contumeliis et tormento interrogemus eum, et probemus quæ ventura sunt illi. Eapropter Isaias: Nos, inquit, putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo et humiliatum.
paras.en: [[70:11|Saying: God hath forsaken him|dicentes: Deus dereliquit eum]]. For the Jews thought that God had departed from Jesus, as from a sinner. Hence they said: [[John 9:24|We know that this man is a sinner|Nos scimus quia hic homo peccator est]]; and again, [[John 9:16|This man is not of God, who keepeth not the sabbath|Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit]]. [[70:11|pursue and take him|Persequimini et comprehendite eum]]. This is what is said by John: the Jews [[John 7:32|sent ministers to apprehend him|Miserunt Judæi ministros ut apprehenderent Jesum]]. And on the night of the Supper the chief priests said these words to their ministers, whom they sent with Judas to seize him. For which reason it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 20:10|I heard the reproaches of many, and terror on every side: Persecute him, and let us persecute him|Audivi contumelias multorum, et terrorem in circuitu: Persequimini et persequamur eum]]. [[70:11|for there is none to deliver him|Quia non est qui eripiat]], that is, there is no one to rescue Jesus from your hands, because God has forsaken him. For hence the adversaries of Christ say: [[Wis 2:19|Let us examine him by outrages and tortures|Contumeliis et tormento interrogemus eum]], [[Wis 2:17|and let us prove what shall happen to him|et probemus quæ ventura sunt illi]]. Therefore Isaias: [[Is 53:4|we|Nos]], he says, [[Is 53:4|have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God and afflicted|putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo et humiliatum]].

paras.t: Deus Pater, ne elongeris a me, differendo resurrectionem meam ultra triduum. Deus meus, in auxilium meum respice, tua divina virtute cooperando meæ humanitati in redemptione generis humani, atque de manibus Judæorum me eruendo per resuscitationem ad impassibilem statum. Hoc est quod Christus ante passionem orasse apud Joannem describitur: Nunc anima mea turbata est. Et quid dicam? Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora.
paras.en: [[70:12|O God|Deus]] the Father, [[70:12|be not thou far from me|ne elongeris a me]], by putting off my resurrection beyond three days. [[70:12|O my God, make haste to my help|Deus meus, in auxilium meum respice]] [Latin respice, "look"], co-operating by thy divine power with my humanity in the redemption of mankind, and rescuing me from the hands of the Jews by raising me again to an impassible state. This is what Christ is described in John as having prayed before the Passion: [[John 12:27|Now is my soul troubled. And what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour|Nunc anima mea turbata est. Et quid dicam? Pater, salvifica me ex hac hora]].

paras.t: Confundantur et deficiant detrahentes animæ meæ. Multipliciter confusi sunt, et defecerunt Judæi, Dominum Salvatorem persequentes et occidentes. Nonne confundebantur, dum Christo in cruce pendente sol obscuratus est, terra commota, velumque templi scissum? dum etiam in die resurrectionis milites eis narrabant, quæ circa Christi sepulcrum contigerunt, et quomodo resurrexisset; dum insuper ab Apostolorum principe beatissimo Petro audierunt, Jesum Nazarenum virum approbatum a Deo in vobis, virtutibus et prodigiis et signis, quæ fecit Deus per illum in medio vestri, interemistis; dum quoque per manus Apostolorum signa magna fiebant in Jerusalem, et multa millia convertebantur ad Christum. Maxime autem confusi sunt, et penitus defecerunt in obsidione Titi ac Romanorum. Operiantur confusione et pudore, id est, undique confundantur et erubescant, intus quoad se ipsos, et foris quantum ad alios; qui quærunt mala mihi, id est Judæi, qui mihi mala culpæ imponunt, et mala pœnæ infligunt. Unde apud Jeremiam Christus ait: Confundantur qui me persequuntur, et non confundar ego; paveant illi, et non paveam ego; et duplici contritione contere eos, videlicet in præsenti et in futuro. Hæc autem a Christo dicuntur potius prænuntiando, quam imprecando. Quomodo tamen ista multipliciter possent exponi, scilicet per modum orationis, in bono, ex præhabitis innotescit.
paras.en: [[70:13|Let them be confounded and come to nothing that detract my soul|Confundantur et deficiant detrahentes animæ meæ]].
