In many ways were the Jews confounded and brought to nothing, who persecuted and slew the Lord the Saviour. Were they not confounded when, as Christ hung upon the cross, the sun was darkened[[Matt 27:45||]], the earth shaken and the veil of the temple rent[[Matt 27:51||]]? when, too, on the day of the resurrection the soldiers told them what had happened about Christ's sepulchre, and how he had risen[[Matt 28:11||]]? when, moreover, they heard from the most blessed Peter, prince of the Apostles: [[Acts 2:22|Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs, which God did by him, in the midst of you|Jesum Nazarenum virum approbatum a Deo in vobis, virtutibus et prodigiis et signis, quæ fecit Deus per illum in medio vestri]], you have [[Acts 2:23|slain|interemistis]]? when also by the hands of the Apostles great signs were done in Jerusalem[[Acts 2:43||]], and many thousands were converted to Christ[[Acts 2:41||]][[Acts 4:4||]]? But most of all were they confounded and utterly brought to nothing in the siege by Titus and the Romans. [[70:13|let them be covered with confusion and blame|Operiantur confusione et pudore]], that is, let them be confounded and put to shame on every side, inwardly as regards themselves and outwardly as regards others; [[70:13|that seek my hurt|qui quærunt mala mihi]], that is, the Jews, who lay evils of guilt upon me and inflict evils of punishment [a play on mala, "evils" (the Douay-Rheims has "my hurt"): the evil of guilt is sin, the evil of punishment is suffering]. Hence Christ says in Jeremias: [[Jer 17:18|Let them be confounded that persecute me, and let not me be confounded: let them be afraid, and let not me be afraid|Confundantur qui me persequuntur, et non confundar ego; paveant illi, et non paveam ego]]; [[Jer 17:18|and with a double destruction, destroy them|et duplici contritione contere eos]], namely in the present and in the future. Now these things are said by Christ rather by way of foretelling than of imprecation. Yet how they might be expounded in many ways in a good sense, namely as a prayer, is clear from what has been said before.

paras.t: Ego autem semper sperabo. Nam quidquid Judæi Christo dixerunt sive fecerunt, ipse in Deo mansit immobiliter sperans, certitudinaliterque ab eo exspectans resuscitari, corpore glorificari, et super alta cœlorum elevari. Et adjiciam super omnem laudem tuam, id est, omni laudi qua in lege atque Prophetis laudaris, addam evangelicæ legis præconium, et novi Testamenti Scripturam: in qua multo sublimius continentur laudes divinæ, quam in veteris legis doctrina.
paras.en: [[70:14|But I will always hope|Ego autem semper sperabo]]. For whatever the Jews said or did to Christ, he remained in God, hoping unshakeably and expecting from him with certainty to be raised again, to be glorified in body, and to be lifted up above the heights of the heavens. [[70:14|and will add to all thy praise|Et adjiciam super omnem laudem tuam]], that is, to all the praise with which thou art praised in the Law and the Prophets I will add the proclamation of the Gospel law and the Scripture of the New Testament, in which the divine praises are contained far more sublimely than in the teaching of the old law.

paras.t: Os meum annuntiabit justitiam tuam. Quamdiu Christus prædicavit in mundo, annuntiavit justitiam Dei, docendo quod Deus sit justus, nec peccatum relinquat inultum, increpando etiam peccatores, et recta præcepta saluberrimaque consilia proponendo. Propter quod ipsemet ait: Ego sum lux mundi; et, Sicut docuit me Pater, hæc loquor. Unde de ipso apud Joelem habetur: Exsultate in Domino Deo vestro, quia dedit vobis doctorem justitiæ. Et per Osee dicitur: Tempus requirendi Dominum, quum venerit qui docebit vos justitiam. Annuntiabit quoque os meum, o Deus Pater, tota die, id est, quamdiu in mundo sum, salutare tuum, id est salutem quam mundo impendis per me. Merito autem tempus quo Christus in mundo vixit, dies vocatur, quoniam Sol justitiæ hominibus luxit atque apparuit, secundum quod ipse testatur: Quamdiu in mundo sum, lux sum mundi. Et tota hac die annuntiavit Christus verbo vel opere salutare Dei, id est se ipsum seu salvationem qua ipse mundum salvavit. Et ideo ait in Evangelio: Me oportet operari opera ejus qui misit me, donec dies est. Hoc modo annuntiavit Christus salutare Dei, dicens: Qui credit in Filium Dei, habet vitam æternam; qui autem incredulus est Filio, ira Dei manet super illum; et, Ego sum via, veritas, et vita; nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me; et in alio loco, Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit.
paras.en: [[70:15|My mouth shall shew forth thy justice|Os meum annuntiabit justitiam tuam]]. As long as Christ preached in the world, he showed forth the justice of God, teaching that God is just and does not leave sin unpunished, rebuking sinners too, and setting forth right precepts and most wholesome counsels. Wherefore he himself says: [[John 8:12|I am the light of the world|Ego sum lux mundi]]; and, [[John 8:28|as the Father hath taught me, these things I speak|Sicut docuit me Pater, hæc loquor]]. Hence it is said of him in Joel: [[Joel 2:23|rejoice, and be joyful in the Lord your God: because he hath given you a teacher of justice|Exsultate in Domino Deo vestro, quia dedit vobis doctorem justitiæ]]. And it is said through Osee: [[Osee 10:12|the time to seek the Lord is, when he shall come that shall teach you justice|Tempus requirendi Dominum, quum venerit qui docebit vos justitiam]]. My mouth also, O God the Father, shall shew forth [[70:15|all the day long|tota die]], that is, as long as I am in the world, [[70:15|thy salvation|salutare tuum]], that is, the salvation which thou bestowest on the world through me. Rightly is the time in which Christ lived in the world called day, since the Sun of justice shone upon men and appeared to them, as he himself testifies: [[John 9:5|As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.|Quamdiu in mundo sum, lux sum mundi]] And all this day Christ showed forth by word or deed the salvation of God, that is, himself, or the salvation by which he saved the world. And so he says in the Gospel: [[John 9:4|I must work the works of him that sent me, whilst it is day|Me oportet operari opera ejus qui misit me, donec dies est]]. In this way Christ showed forth the salvation of God, saying: [[John 3:36|He that believeth in the Son hath life everlasting|Qui credit in Filium Dei, habet vitam æternam]]; [[John 3:36|but he that believeth not the Son|qui autem incredulus est Filio]], [[John 3:36|the wrath of God abideth on him|ira Dei manet super illum]] [the margin notes that these are the words of John the Baptist]; and, [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me|Ego sum via, veritas, et vita; nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me]]; and in another place, [[Mark 16:16|He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved|Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit]].

paras.t: Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam, id est scientiam per exercitationem et studium seu informationem humanam: juxta illud, Mirabantur Judæi dicentes, Quomodo hic litteras scit, quum non didicerit? Quoniam ergo non cognovi litteraturam per studium, sed per illuminationem divinam, idcirco introibo per contemplationem perfectam seu visionem fruitivam atque beatam, in potentias Domini, cognoscendo perfectiones et virtutes divinæ naturæ et magna opera ejus. Anima enim Christi a suæ creationis exordio, vidit per speciem divinam essentiam et perfectiones ejus potentes, non nisi per illuminationem supernaturalem. Domine, memorabor justitiæ tuæ solius: id est, nihil boni mihi ex me adscribam, secundum quod homo sum, sed omnem conversationis meæ justitiam tibi attribuam, et alios sic facere edocebo. Hoc est quod asserit Christus: Si ego glorifico me ipsum, gloria mea nihil est; et, Claritatem ab hominibus non accipio; et: Quum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite: Servi inutiles sumus; quod debuimus facere, fecimus.
paras.en: [[70:15|Because I have not known learning|Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam]] [Latin litteratura, "letters", book-learning], that is, knowledge gained by exercise and study or by human instruction: according to that saying, [[John 7:15|the Jews wondered, saying: How doth this man know letters, having never learned?|Mirabantur Judæi dicentes, Quomodo hic litteras scit, quum non didicerit?]] Since, then, I have not known learning by study, but by divine illumination, therefore [[70:16|I will enter|introibo]], by perfect contemplation, that is, by the enjoying and blessed vision, [[70:16|into the powers of the Lord|in potentias Domini]], knowing the perfections and powers of the divine nature and its great works. For the soul of Christ, from the first beginning of its creation, saw the divine essence and its mighty perfections face to face, and that only by supernatural illumination. [[70:16|O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone|Domine, memorabor justitiæ tuæ solius]]: that is, I will ascribe nothing good to myself as from myself, inasmuch as I am man, but will attribute to thee all the justice of my life, and will teach others to do the same. This is what Christ asserts: [[John 8:54|If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing|Si ego glorifico me ipsum, gloria mea nihil est]]; and, [[John 5:41|I receive not glory from men.|Claritatem ab hominibus non accipio]] And: [[Luke 17:10|when you shall have done all these things that are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which we ought to do|Quum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite: Servi inutiles sumus; quod debuimus facere, fecimus]].

paras.t: Deus, docuisti me a juventute mea et usque nunc. Deus Trinitas docuit animam Christi a primo instanti quo eam creavit, dando ei multiplicem sapientiam, utpote sapientiam beatificæ visionis, qua cognovit Deum per speciem increatam, sicut et Sancti in patria; sapientiam quoque infusam seu inditam, qua omnia novit in propriis naturis per species innatas seu concreatas, sicut et omnes angeli ante lapsum et confirmationem noverunt. Habuit etiam Christus (secundum quosdam) scientiam acquisitam seu experimentalem: de qua ait Apostolus, Didicit ex his quæ passus est, obedientiam: et sumitur ibi Discere pro Experiri, quoniam Christus ab aliis nihil didicit, sed per propriam adinventionem, secundum ponentes scientiam acquisitam in Christo. Unde de hac scientia intelligi potest quod legitur in Evangelio: Jesus proficiebat sapientia et ætate. Sed quoniam Christus a principio perfecte instructus fuit, quomodo nunc ait, Deus, docuisti me a juventute mea et usque nunc, ac si secundum successum temporis addita sibi fuisset scientia? Et respondendum, quod Deus dicitur Sanctos in patria et animam Christi semper docere, in quantum sapientiam ipsis infusam incessanter in eis conservat.
paras.en: [[70:17|Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth|Deus, docuisti me a juventute mea]] [[70:17|and till now|et usque nunc]]. God the Trinity taught the soul of Christ from the first instant in which he created it, giving it manifold wisdom: namely the wisdom of the beatific vision, by which it knew God through the uncreated form [that is, through God's own essence, by which the blessed see him directly], as do the Saints in the homeland; also infused or implanted wisdom, by which it knew all things in their own natures through innate or concreated species [that is, ideas given with the mind when it was made, not drawn from the senses], as all the angels too knew them before the fall [of the wicked angels] and the confirmation [of the good]. Christ also had (according to some) acquired or experimental knowledge [the margin cites St Thomas, Summa theologiae, III, q. 9, a. 4], of which the Apostle says: [[Heb 5:8|he learned obedience by the things which he suffered|Didicit ex his quæ passus est, obedientiam]]; and "learn" is taken there for "experience", since Christ learned nothing from others, but by his own finding, according to those who hold that there was acquired knowledge in Christ. Hence what is read in the Gospel may be understood of this knowledge: [[Luke 2:52|And Jesus advanced in wisdom and age|Jesus proficiebat sapientia et ætate]]. But since Christ was perfectly instructed from the beginning, how does he now say, [[70:17|Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth|Deus, docuisti me a juventute mea]] [[70:17|and till now|et usque nunc]], as though knowledge had been added to him in the course of time? And the answer must be that God is said always to teach the Saints in the homeland and the soul of Christ, inasmuch as he unceasingly preserves in them the wisdom infused into them.

paras.t: Pronuntiabo mirabilia tua. Christus occultissima, supernaturalissima, penitusque incomprehensibilia docuit, sicut quod Deus est unus ac trinus, quod ipse in unitate personæ sit Deus et homo, quod beatitudo nostra in divinæ essentiæ visione consistit, quod ipsemet sit resuscitaturus et judicaturus mortuos universos, et alia multa: sicque mirabilia Dei per se ipsum et discipulos pronuntiavit. Et usque in senectam et senium, id est usque ad tempus passionis meæ, pronuntiabo mirabilia tua. Unde in nocte passionis dixit Judæis: Amodo videbitis Filium hominis sedentem a dextris virtutis Dei, et venientem in nubibus cœli. Coram Pilato quoque in die passionis testatus est: Rex sum ego. Ego in hoc natus sum, et ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimonium perhibeam veritati. Vel: Usque in senectam et senium, id est usque ad ultimam mundi ætatem et finem sæculi, pronuntiabo per meos ministros mirabilia tua. Nam usque ad terminum mundi cantabunt Christiani, a Christo instructi, mirabilia Dei in novo ac veteri Testamento scripta.
paras.en: [[70:17|I will declare thy wonderful works|Pronuntiabo mirabilia tua]]. Christ taught things most hidden, most supernatural and wholly incomprehensible: as that God is one and three; that he himself, in unity of person, is God and man; that our beatitude consists in the vision of the divine essence; that he himself will raise and judge all the dead; and many other things: and so he declared the wonderful works of God through himself and his disciples. [[70:18|And unto old age and grey hairs|Et usque in senectam et senium]], that is, until the time of my Passion, [[70:17|I will declare thy wonderful works|pronuntiabo mirabilia tua]]. Hence on the night of the Passion he said to the Jews: [[Matt 26:64|hereafter you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God and coming in the clouds of heaven|Amodo videbitis Filium hominis sedentem a dextris virtutis Dei, et venientem in nubibus cœli]]. Before Pilate also, on the day of the Passion, he testified: [[John 18:37|I am a king|Rex sum ego]]. [[John 18:37|For this was I born, and for this came I into the world; that I should give testimony to the truth|Ego in hoc natus sum, et ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimonium perhibeam veritati]]. Or: [[70:18|unto old age and grey hairs|Usque in senectam et senium]], that is, until the last age of the world and the end of time, I will declare thy wonderful works through my ministers. For until the end of the world Christians, taught by Christ, will sing the wonderful works of God written in the New and the Old Testament.

paras.t: Deus Pater, ne derelinquas me in monumento aut limbo, donec annuntiem brachium tuum, id est potentiam tuam, generationi omni quæ ventura est, id est universis hominibus usque in finem sæculi nascituris. Hoc in Christo videmus impletum, quoniam post resurrectionem instruxit suos discipulos, aperiens illis sensum, ut intelligerent Scripturas; et tandem quinquagesimo die misit eis Spiritum Sanctum, qui eos in omni lingua atque sapientia erudivit. Per hoc vero quod Christus illis divinam potentiam revelavit, etiam omnem generationem venturam edocuit: quia per Apostolorum doctrinam, fidem catholicam promulgavit, mundumque convertit. Unde et Christus in Evangelio ait: Quod vobis dico, omnibus dico.
paras.en: [[70:18|O God|Deus]] the Father, [[70:18|forsake me not|ne derelinquas me]] in the tomb or in limbo, [[70:18|Until I shew forth thy arm|donec annuntiem brachium tuum]], that is, thy power, [[70:18|to all the generation that is to come|generationi omni quæ ventura est]], that is, to all men who are to be born until the end of the world. This we see fulfilled in Christ, since after the resurrection he instructed his disciples: [[Luke 24:45|he opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures|aperiens illis sensum, ut intelligerent Scripturas]]; and at length, on the fiftieth day, he sent them the Holy Ghost[[Acts 2:3||]][[Acts 2:4||]], who taught them every tongue and all wisdom. And by revealing the divine power to them, Christ taught also every generation to come, since through the teaching of the Apostles he spread abroad the Catholic faith and converted the world. Hence Christ too says in the Gospel: [[Mark 13:37|what I say to you, I say to all|Quod vobis dico, omnibus dico]].

paras.t: Potentiam tuam et justitiam tuam, Deus, usque in altissima, quæ fecisti, magnalia. In Christi incarnatione, passione, ascensione, potentia atque justitia Dei excellentissime splendent. Quod enim Deus et homo in unam convenerunt personam, infinitam esse ostendit potestatem divinam: similiter quod Christus de Virgine natus est, tantaque miracula fecisse credendus est. Justitia vero Dei relucet in hoc, quod proprio Filio non pepercit, sed pro mundi peccatis tradidit illum, ne culpa remaneret inulta. Hanc autem Dei potentiam et justitiam, Christus annuntiavit verbis et factis, protestando se esse Patri æqualem, primum principium, verumque Deum, et nihilo minus hominem verum, Patre minorem, atque passibilem. Sed et justitiam Patris Christus professus est, dum ait: Pater juste, mundus te non cognovit; ego autem te cognovi. Sic ergo Christus pronuntiavit potentiam et justitiam Dei, usque in altissima, quæ fecit, magnalia, id est per comparationem ad humanæ redemptionis mysteria, quæ sunt altissima magnalia super omnia naturalia opera Creatoris. Christus namque suam incarnationem, passionem, resurrectionem, ascensionem et Spiritus Sancti missionem, ante passionem ubertim prædixit.
paras.en: [[70:18|Thy power|Potentiam tuam]] [[70:19|And thy justice, O God, even to the highest great things thou hast done|et justitiam tuam, Deus, usque in altissima, quæ fecisti, magnalia]]. In the incarnation, Passion and ascension of Christ the power and justice of God shine forth most excellently. For that God and man came together in one person shows the divine power to be infinite; and likewise that Christ was born of a Virgin and, as we must believe, worked such great miracles. And the justice of God shines out in this, that he [[Rom 8:32|spared not even his own Son|proprio Filio non pepercit]], but delivered him up for the sins of the world, lest guilt should remain unpunished. This power and justice of God Christ proclaimed by words and deeds, declaring that he is equal to the Father[[John 10:30||]], the first beginning[[John 8:25||]], and true God[[John 10:33||]], and none the less true man, less than the Father[[John 14:28||]], and capable of suffering. And Christ professed the justice of the Father too, when he says: [[John 17:25|Just Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee|Pater juste, mundus te non cognovit; ego autem te cognovi]]. So, then, Christ declared the power and justice of God, even to the highest great things he has done, that is, in comparison with the mysteries of man's redemption, which are the highest great things, above all the natural works of the Creator. For before his Passion Christ foretold abundantly his incarnation, Passion, resurrection and ascension, and the sending of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Quantas ostendisti mihi tribulationes multas et malas, id est, persecutiones et varias pœnas mihi infligi permisisti, quemadmodum Isaias prædixit, Dominus voluit eum conterere in infirmitate; et, Dominus posuit in eo iniquitates omnium nostrum. Et Petrus: Deus, inquit, qui prænuntiavit per os omnium Prophetarum, pati Christum suum, implevit sic. Unde per Jeremiam ait: Tu, Domine, demonstrasti mihi, et cognovi; tu ostendisti mihi studia eorum. Et conversus, id est mundo per meam passionem placatus, vivificasti me, resuscitando me tertia die a mortuis; et de abyssis terræ, id est de sepulcro et inferno, iterum reduxisti me in die resurrectionis.
paras.en: [[70:20|How great troubles hast thou shewn me, many and grievous|Quantas ostendisti mihi tribulationes multas et malas]], that is, thou hast permitted persecutions and divers punishments to be inflicted on me, as Isaias foretold: [[Is 53:10|the Lord was pleased to bruise him in infirmity|Dominus voluit eum conterere in infirmitate]]; and, [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitates omnium nostrum]]. And Peter: [[Acts 3:18|God|Deus]], he says, [[Acts 3:18|before had shewed by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled|qui prænuntiavit per os omnium Prophetarum, pati Christum suum, implevit sic]]. Hence he says through Jeremias: [[Jer 11:18|thou, O Lord, hast shewn me, and I have known: then thou shewedst me their doings|Tu, Domine, demonstrasti mihi, et cognovi; tu ostendisti mihi studia eorum]]. [[70:20|and turning|Et conversus]], that is, appeased towards the world through my Passion, [[70:20|thou hast brought me to life|vivificasti me]], raising me from the dead on the third day; [[70:20|from the depths of the earth|et de abyssis terræ]], that is, from the sepulchre and from hell, [[70:20|and hast brought me back again|iterum reduxisti me]] on the day of the resurrection.

paras.t: Multiplicasti magnificentiam tuam, gloriose atque potenter me resuscitando. Nam angelus Domini descendit, et accedens revolvit lapidem; et terra mox mota est, custodes quoque perterriti, et quasi exanimes facti sunt. Sed et duo angeli sederunt juxta sepulcrum, unus ad caput, et alter ad pedes. Et conversus ab ira qua hominibus irascebaris, consolatus es me, liberando me ab omni dolore atque tristitia, quæ habui tempore passionis, et corpus meum glorificando, novaque gaudia ad accidentale præmium pertinentia, mihi post resurrectionem præstando.
paras.en: [[70:21|Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence|Multiplicasti magnificentiam tuam]], by raising me again gloriously and mightily. For [[Matt 28:2|an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and coming rolled back the stone|angelus Domini descendit, et accedens revolvit lapidem]]; and at once the earth was shaken, and the guards too were terrified and became as it were lifeless[[Matt 28:4||]]. And two angels also sat by the sepulchre, one at the head and the other at the feet[[John 20:12||]]. [[70:21|and turning to me|Et conversus]] from the anger with which thou wast angry with men, [[70:21|thou hast comforted me|consolatus es me]], freeing me from all the pain and sorrow which I had in the time of the Passion, glorifying my body, and bestowing on me after the resurrection new joys belonging to my accidental reward.

paras.t: Nam et ego Unigenitus tuus confitebor tibi, id est, laudabo te, in vasis psalmi, id est, in devotis hominibus, laudem tuam cordialiter continentibus, confitebor veritatem tuam, Deus, te per ipsos laudando, et eos ad tua præconia inflammando, quemadmodum per Isaiam prophetam locutus sum: Laudate, cœli; et exsulta, terra; jubilate, montes, laudem, quia consolatus est Dominus populum suum, et pauperum suorum miserebitur. Psallam tibi in cithara, id est in carne mea propter te crucifixa et mortua, o Domine, qui es, et cujus nomen est, Sanctus Israel: secundum quod alibi scriptum est, Redemptor noster Dominus exercituum, Sanctus Israel nomen ejus.
paras.en: [[70:22|For I will also|Nam et ego]], thy Only-begotten, [[70:22|confess to thee|confitebor tibi]], that is, I will praise thee, [[70:22|with the instruments of psaltery|in vasis psalmi]] [literally "in the vessels of the psalm", which Denis takes of men who hold God's praise], that is, in devout men who hold thy praise in their hearts, I will confess [[70:22|thy truth|veritatem tuam]], [[70:22|O God|Deus]], praising thee through them and kindling them to proclaim thee, as I spoke through the prophet Isaias: [[Is 49:13|Give praise, O ye heavens, and rejoice, O earth, ye mountains, give praise with jubilation: because the Lord hath comforted his people, and will have mercy on his poor ones.|Laudate, cœli; et exsulta, terra; jubilate, montes, laudem, quia consolatus est Dominus populum suum, et pauperum suorum miserebitur]] [[70:22|I will sing to thee with the harp|Psallam tibi in cithara]], that is, in my flesh crucified and dead for thee, O Lord, who art, and whose name is, [[70:22|holy one of Israel|Sanctus Israel]]: according as it is written elsewhere, [[Is 47:4|Our redeemer, the Lord of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.|Redemptor noster Dominus exercituum, Sanctus Israel nomen ejus]]

paras.t: Exsultabunt labia mea quum cantavero tibi. Tanto ampliori hilaritate et exsultatione semper gavisa sunt, et in æternum gaudebunt labia Christi interiora et exteriora, in laude divina, quanto ipse præ aliis Deum ardentius dilexit, clariusque cognovit. Unde legitur in Evangelio: Exsultavit Jesus Spiritu Sancto, et ait: Confitebor tibi, Pater. Et anima mea in tua laude exsultabit, quam redemisti ab omni passibilitate et loco inferiori, itemque a culpa: non illa quam habuit, quoniam omni penitus culpa carebat; sed illa quam potuisset habere, nisi præventa fuisset affluentia gratiæ tuæ, et hypostatica unione cum Verbo.
paras.en: [[70:23|My lips shall greatly rejoice, when I shall sing to thee|Exsultabunt labia mea quum cantavero tibi]]. With so much the greater gladness and exultation have the lips of Christ, inward and outward, always rejoiced in the divine praise, and will rejoice for ever, as he loved God more ardently and knew him more clearly than all others. Hence we read in the Gospel of Jesus: [[Luke 10:21|he rejoiced in the Holy Ghost and said: I confess to thee, O Father|Exsultavit Jesus Spiritu Sancto, et ait: Confitebor tibi, Pater]]. [[70:23|and my soul|Et anima mea]] shall rejoice in thy praise, [[70:23|which thou hast redeemed|quam redemisti]] from all passibility and from the lower place, and also from guilt: not from guilt which it had, since it was wholly free of all guilt, but from that which it could have had, had it not been forestalled by the abundance of thy grace and by the hypostatic union with the Word [that is, the union of the human nature with the divine in the one Person of the Word].

paras.t: Sed et lingua mea interior atque exterior, tota die æternitatis in patria, meditabitur justitiam tuam, illam laudando ac proferendo ad gloriam tuam, quum confusi et reveriti fuerint confusione perfecta atque consummata, tanquam æternaliter condemnati, qui quæserunt mala mihi: secundum sensum inductum.
paras.en: [[70:24|Yea and my tongue|Sed et lingua mea]], inward and outward, [[70:24|all the day|tota die]] of eternity in the homeland, [[70:24|shall meditate on thy justice|meditabitur justitiam tuam]], praising it and uttering it to thy glory, [[70:24|when they shall be confounded and put to shame|quum confusi et reveriti fuerint]] with a perfect and consummated confusion, as men condemned for ever, [[70:24|that seek evils to me|qui quæserunt mala mihi]]: according to the sense given above.

paras.t: Ecce psalmus præclarus ac luciformis, cœlestis harmoniæ dulcedine plenus, verba ignea sanctæ dilectionis complectens, affectuosissimas preces includens, Deum pulcherrime laudans, omnemque pusillanimitatem propulsans: psalmus utique mirabiliter consolatorius attento lectori; qui etiam de Domino Salvatore tam congruenter exponitur. Quidam vero exponunt eum ad litteram de David: quam explanationem propter prolixitatem, et quoniam parum devotionis adducit, omitto. Cum ingenti igitur alacritate et omni mentis fervore atque custodia psalmum tam fulgidum decantare conemur, præsertim quum omnium visibilium invisibiliumque adversariorum persecutiones et tentamenta, præsentis psalmi dejiciantur, vincantur, ac prosternantur virtute.
paras.en: Behold a psalm most excellent and full of light, full of the sweetness of heavenly harmony, containing fiery words of holy love, enclosing most affectionate prayers, praising God most beautifully and driving away all faintheartedness: a psalm indeed wonderfully consoling to the attentive reader, and one which is also expounded so fittingly of the Lord the Saviour. Some, however, expound it literally of David: that explanation I leave out because of its length, and because it brings little devotion. With great eagerness, then, and with all fervour and watchfulness of mind, let us strive to sing so radiant a psalm, especially since the persecutions and temptations of all adversaries, visible and invisible, are cast down, overcome and laid low by the power of this psalm.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus misericordiæ ineffabilis, ne elongeris a nobis: respice in auxilium nostrum, et ne nos derelinquas usque in senectam et senium; vivifica nos et pie consolare, et gloriæ magnitudinem tuæ fac nos perpetim digne decantare.
paras.en: Prayer. O God of unspeakable mercy, be not far from us; look to our help, and forsake us not even unto old age and grey hairs; bring us to life and lovingly comfort us, and make us for ever worthily sing the greatness of thy glory.

71.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI PRIMI : DEUS, JUDICIUM TUUM REGI DA.
71.title_en: Literal exposition of the seventy-first psalm: Give to the king thy judgment, O God.

paras.t: TITULUS psalmi est : In Salomonem. Asserunt quidam, quod David fecit hunc psalmum pro filio suo Salomone, orando pro prosperitate regni ipsius ; sed hoc nullatenus verisimile esse potest, quoniam multa in hoc psalmo continentur, quæ Salomoni nullo modo conveniunt, sicut patebit. Hieronymus autem dicit hunc psalmum a Salomone intitulatum, tanquam ab auctore, ita quod Salomon edidit psalmum præsentem. Augustinus vero et Cassiodorus (quorum positioni magis consentiendum videtur) dicunt hunc psalmum, sicut et omnes alios, a David conscriptum. Omnes quoque magni catholicique doctores, videlicet Hieronymus, Augustinus, Cassiodorus, Hugo, exponunt hunc psalmum de Christo ad litteram ; et est sensus tituli : In Salomonem, id est, psalmus iste tendit et ducit nos in Christum, per Salomonem figuratum. Salomon nempe interpretatur Pacificus : et ita Christus est verus Salomon, mundum Patri reconcilians. De quo dicit Apostolus ad Ephesios : Christus est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum, per crucem dissolvens inimicitias in semetipso; et veniens evangelizavit pacem his qui prope, et his qui procul. Et ad Romanos: Quum adhuc inimici essemus, reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem Filii ejus. Propter quod Zacharias: Ipse, inquit, portabit gloriam, et dominabitur, et erit sacerdos; et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos, videlicet inter gentiles et Judæos divinitus præelectos. De quibus ait Apostolus: Ipsis autem vocatis Judæis et Græcis, prædicamus Christum, Dei virtutem et Dei sapientiam. Christus namque est lapis angularis, in quo sibi connexi atque conjuncti sunt in unitate Ecclesiæ per fidem et caritatem Judæi atque gentiles.
paras.en: The title of the psalm is: [[71:1|on Solomon|in Salomonem]]. Some assert that David made this psalm for his son Solomon, praying for the prosperity of his reign; but this can in no way be likely, since many things are contained in this psalm which in no way befit Solomon, as will appear. Jerome, however, says that this psalm is entitled from Solomon as from its author, so that Solomon composed the present psalm. But Augustine and Cassiodorus (whose position it seems better to agree with) say that this psalm, like all the others, was written by David. All the great Catholic doctors too, namely Jerome, Augustine, Cassiodorus and Hugh, expound this psalm of Christ according to the letter; and the sense of the title is: [[71:1|on Solomon|In Salomonem]], that is, this psalm tends towards and leads us to Christ, figured by Solomon. For Solomon is interpreted *Peaceable*: and so Christ is the true Solomon, reconciling the world to the Father. Of whom the Apostle says to the Ephesians: Christ [[Eph 2:14|is our peace, who hath made both one|est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]], [[Eph 2:16|by the cross|per crucem]] dissolving [[Eph 2:16|the enmities in himself|inimicitias in semetipso]]; [[Eph 2:17|And coming, he preached peace|et veniens evangelizavit pacem]] to them that were nigh, and to them that were afar off. And to the Romans: [[Rom 5:10|when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son|Quum adhuc inimici essemus, reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem Filii ejus]]. Therefore Zacharias: He, he says, [[Zach 6:13|shall bear the glory|portabit gloriam]], and shall rule, [[Zach 6:13|and he shall be a priest|et erit sacerdos]]; [[Zach 6:13|and the counsel of peace shall be between them both|et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos]], that is, between the Gentiles and the Jews chosen beforehand by God. Of whom the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:24|But unto them that are called, both Jews and Greeks|Ipsis autem vocatis Judæis et Græcis]], we preach [[1 Cor 1:24|Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God|Christum, Dei virtutem et Dei sapientiam]]. For Christ is the corner stone[[1 Pet 2:6||]], in whom Jews and Gentiles are knit and joined to one another in the unity of the Church through faith and charity.

paras.t: AIT ergo Propheta ad Deum Patrem, seu totam beatissimam Trinitatem, cujus dona et opera indivisa consistunt: Deus, judicium tuum, id est judiciariam tuam potestatem, regi, id est Christo regi regum et Domino dominorum, da, constituendo eum judicem vivorum ac mortuorum; et justitiam tuam, id est habitum verae æquitatis, per quem in omni judicio recte procedat, da filio regis, id est Christo: qui secundum divinam generationem est filius Regis æterni, utpote tui; secundum generationem autem humanam, est filius David regis terreni. Judicare populum tuum in justitia: id est, ad hoc da Christo judicium atque justitiam, quatenus populum christianum judicet juste, discernendo ac separando eum ab infidelium plebe, et dando singulis quod merentur; ut etiam judicet et pauperes tuos, id est vere et spiritualiter pauperes: de quibus in Matthæo habetur, Beati pauperes spiritu; in judicio discretionis in præsenti, et in judicio remunerationis in futuro, quatenus nunc separet eos a divitibus et superbis voto et merito, in futuro quoque, loco et præmio.
paras.en: The Prophet therefore says to God the Father, or to the whole most blessed Trinity, whose gifts and works are undivided: [[71:2|thy judgment, O God|Deus, judicium tuum]], that is, thy judiciary power, [[71:2|to the king|regi]], that is, to Christ, the King of kings and Lord of lords[[Apoc 17:14||]], [[71:2|Give|da]], by appointing him judge of the living and the dead; and [[71:2|thy justice|justitiam tuam]], that is, the habit of true equity, by which he may proceed rightly in every judgment, give [[71:2|to the king's son|filio regis]], that is, to Christ: who according to his divine generation is the son of the eternal King, namely of thee, and according to his human generation is the son of David, an earthly king. [[71:2|To judge thy people with justice|Judicare populum tuum in justitia]]: that is, give Christ judgment and justice to this end, that he may judge the Christian people justly, discerning and separating it from the multitude of unbelievers and giving each what he deserves; that he may judge also [[71:2|and thy poor|et pauperes tuos]], that is, those who are truly and spiritually poor, of whom we read in Matthew: [[Matt 5:3|Blessed are the poor in spirit|Beati pauperes spiritu]]; [[71:2|with judgment|in judicio]] of discernment in the present, and with the judgment of reward in the future: so that he may now separate them from the rich and proud in desire and merit, and in the future also in place and reward.

paras.t: Sed mirum videtur, quomodo Propheta, qui utique fuit et est membrum Christi, præsumpserit orare pro capite, scilicet Christo, orando Patrem, ut Christo judicium det atque justitiam. Et respondendum, quod sanctus Propheta non dicit ista orando pro Christo, quasi Christus sua prece indigeat, sed ad insinuandum cordis sui affectum, quem habuit pro Christi honore et gloria. Juxta quem modum etiam inferius dicit: Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam. Denique in eo quod ait, Pauperes tuos in judicio, secernit et dividit pauperes Dei, a pauperibus mundi atque diaboli. Est enim pauper avarus, et est pauper superbus, et est pauper involuntarius: quorum nullus est pauper Dei. Est quoque pauper spiritu, pauper affectu, pauper rebus et mente, ut Deo libere vacet: et isti sunt pauperes Dei. De quibus ait Isaias propheta: Pauperes homines in Sancto Israel exsultabunt. Quod autem nunc dicit Psalmista, Deus, judicium tuum regi da, Daniel evidentissime de Christo prænuntiavit, dicens: Adspiciebam in visione noctis, et ecce in nubibus cœli quasi Filius hominis veniebat, et usque ad Antiquum dierum pervenit; et dedit ei potestatem et honorem et regnum. Quod etiam Salvator in se impletum fatetur in Evangelio, dicens: Neque enim Pater judicat quemquam, sed omne judicium dedit Filio. Et Petrus de Christo loquens: Præcepit (inquit) nobis testificari, quia ipse est qui constitutus est a Deo judex vivorum et mortuorum.
paras.en: But it seems strange how the Prophet, who indeed was and is a member of Christ, presumed to pray for the head, that is, for Christ, praying the Father to give Christ judgment and justice. And the answer is that the holy Prophet does not say these things praying for Christ, as though Christ needed his prayer, but to make known the affection of his heart which he had for Christ's honour and glory. In the same way he also says further on: [[Ps 113:9|Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory.|Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam]] Then, in saying [[71:2|thy poor with judgment|Pauperes tuos in judicio]], he sets apart and divides the poor of God from the poor of the world and of the devil. For there is the covetous poor man, and the proud poor man, and the poor man against his will: none of whom is God's poor man. There is also the poor in spirit, poor in affection, poor in goods and in mind, so as to be free for God: and these are God's poor. Of whom Isaias the prophet says: [[Is 29:19|the poor men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel|Pauperes homines in Sancto Israel exsultabunt]]. And what the Psalmist now says, [[71:2|Give to the king thy judgment, O God|Deus, judicium tuum regi da]], Daniel foretold most plainly of Christ, saying: [[Dan 7:13|I beheld, therefore, in the vision of the night, and lo, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and he came even to the ancient of days|Adspiciebam in visione noctis, et ecce in nubibus cœli quasi Filius hominis veniebat, et usque ad Antiquum dierum pervenit]]; [[Dan 7:14|And he gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom|et dedit ei potestatem et honorem et regnum]]. Which the Saviour too owns fulfilled in himself in the Gospel, saying: [[John 5:22|For neither does the Father judge any man: but hath given all judgment to the Son|Neque enim Pater judicat quemquam, sed omne judicium dedit Filio]]. And Peter, speaking of Christ: [[Acts 10:42|he commanded us|Præcepit]] (he says) [[Acts 10:42|to testify that it is he who was appointed by God to be judge of the living and of the dead|testificari, quia ipse est qui constitutus est a Deo judex vivorum et mortuorum]].

paras.t: Sed his contrariari videtur quod Christus ait, Ego non judico quemquam: quod idem beatissimus Evangelista clarius protestatur, dicendo, Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum, ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum. Considerandum est utique, quod in judicio duo pensantur, judicandi auctoritas, et judicialis auctoritatis exsecutio, seu sententiæ prolatio. Quantum ad primum horum, convenit Deo Patri seu toti Trinitati judicium, et non Christo secundum quod homo est. Unde ipse Christus: Ego, inquit, non quæro gloriam meam; est qui quærat et judicet, scilicet Deus Trinitas. Quantum vero ad secundum, quoad prolationem sententiæ, competit Christo homini judicare, sicut in Evangelio affirmat, dicens : Potestatem dedit ei Pater et judicium facere, quia Filius hominis est. Et horum utrumque Paulus breviter innuit, dicens : Deus statuit diem in quo judicaturus est orbem in æquitate, in viro quem statuit. Sic igitur constat, quomodo Deo Trinitati, et Christo homini judicium diversimode competat. Verumtamen, quod Christus ait, Ego non judico quemquam, referri potest ad tempus sui primi adventus, atque exponi de judicio remunerationis ac ultionis. Primus namque Christi adventus in humilitate fuit, venitque non ministrari aut judicare, sed ministrare ac judicari. Unde (ut legitur apud Lucam) quum Joannes et Jacobus Christo dixissent, Domine, vis dicamus ut veniat ignis de cœlo, et consumat eos (videlicet qui Dominum Jesum non receperunt)? respondit eis Jesus : Nescitis cujus spiritus estis ; Filius enim hominis non venit animas perdere, sed salvare. Hinc quoque feminam in adulterio deprehensam noluit condemnare. Quod autem Christus tam juste ac judicialiter judicaturus erat populum suum, Isaias manifestat, dicendo : Non secundum visionem oculorum judicabit, neque secundum auditum aurium arguet ; sed judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ.
paras.en: But against this there seems to be what Christ says, [[John 8:15|I judge not any man|Ego non judico quemquam]]; which the same most blessed Evangelist states more clearly, saying: [[John 3:17|God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world: but that the world may be saved by him|Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum, ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum]]. It must be considered, then, that in judgment two things are weighed: the authority to judge, and the exercise of that judicial authority, or the passing of sentence. As to the first of these, judgment belongs to God the Father, or to the whole Trinity, and not to Christ as he is man. Whence Christ himself: I, he says, [[John 8:50|seek not my own glory: there is one that seeketh and judgeth|non quæro gloriam meam; est qui quærat et judicet]], namely God the Trinity. But as to the second, as regards the passing of sentence, it belongs to Christ as man to judge, as he affirms in the Gospel, saying: [[John 5:27|he hath given him power to do judgment, because he is the Son of man|Potestatem dedit ei Pater et judicium facere, quia Filius hominis est]]. And Paul briefly touches on both, saying: [[Acts 17:31|he hath appointed a day wherein he will judge the world in equity, by the man whom he hath appointed|Deus statuit diem in quo judicaturus est orbem in æquitate, in viro quem statuit]]. So it is clear how judgment belongs in different ways to God the Trinity and to Christ as man. Yet what Christ says, [[John 8:15|I judge not any man|Ego non judico quemquam]], can be referred to the time of his first coming, and explained of the judgment of reward and of vengeance. For Christ's first coming was in humility, and he came not to be ministered unto or to judge, but to minister and to be judged[[Matt 20:28||]]. Hence (as we read in Luke), when John and James had said to Christ, [[Luke 9:54|Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?|Domine, vis dicamus ut veniat ignis de cœlo, et consumat eos]] (namely those who had not received the Lord Jesus), Jesus answered them: [[Luke 9:55|you know not of what spirit you are|Nescitis cujus spiritus estis]]; for [[Luke 9:56|The Son of man came not to destroy souls, but to save|Filius enim hominis non venit animas perdere, sed salvare]]. Hence too he would not condemn the woman taken in adultery[[John 8:11||]]. And that Christ was to judge his people so justly and judicially, Isaias shows, saying: [[Is 11:3|He shall not judge according to the sight of the eyes, nor reprove according to the hearing of the ears|Non secundum visionem oculorum judicabit, neque secundum auditum aurium arguet]]; [[Is 11:4|But he shall judge the poor with justice, and shall reprove with equity the meek of the earth|sed judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ]].

paras.t: Suscipiant montes, id est sublimes et apostolici viri ac magni prælati Ecclesiæ, pacem populo, id est gratiam veræ internæque pacis ad salutem informationemque populi, ita ut ipsi Apostoli et successores ipsorum, a Deo acquirant tam sibi quam gregi eis commisso, stabilem pacis quietem. Hoc autem in Apostolis impletum est, dum a Domino Jesu audierunt : Pacem relinquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis ; et, In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite, Pax huic domui. Suscipiant quoque et colles justitiam, id est, inferiores recipiant gratiam obediendi divinis præceptis, a superioribus assignatis. De horum montium colliumque fecunditate apud Joelem scriptum est : In die illa stillabunt montes dulcedinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, etc.
paras.en: [[71:3|Let the mountains receive|Suscipiant montes]], that is, the lofty and apostolic men and the great prelates of the Church, [[71:3|peace for the people|pacem populo]], that is, the grace of true and inward peace, for the salvation and instruction of the people; so that the Apostles themselves and their successors may obtain from God, both for themselves and for the flock committed to them, the lasting quiet of peace. And this was fulfilled in the Apostles when they heard from the Lord Jesus: [[John 14:27|Peace I leave with you: my peace I give unto you|Pacem relinquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis]]; and: [[Luke 10:5|Into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace be to this house|In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite, Pax huic domui]]. Let [[71:3|the hills|colles]] also receive [[71:3|justice|justitiam]]: that is, let those below receive the grace of obeying the divine precepts assigned to them by their superiors. Of the fruitfulness of these mountains and hills it is written in Joel: In that day [[Joel 3:18|the mountains shall drop down sweetness, and the hills shall flow with milk|stillabunt montes dulcedinem, et colles fluent lac]] and honey, etc.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta ostendit fuisse implendum, quod ipse fieri exorabat. Judicabit pauperes populi, et salvos faciet filios pauperum. In præsenti enim judicat pauperes suos judicio discretionis, ut dictum est; in die autem novissimo judicabit eos judicio beatæ remunerationis, quemadmodum ipse in Apocalypsi asserit : Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique secundum opera sua. Et humiliabit calumniatorem, id est, Christus confundet, damnabit, ac destruet omnem persecutorem justorum, omnem tyrannum et tentatorem Ecclesiæ, diabolum et Antichristum, juxta illud in Isaia : Percutiet terram virga oris sui, et spiritu labiorum suorum interficiet impium, scilicet Antichristum. De quo apud eumdem habetur : Triturabitur Moab sub eo. De quo etiam ait Apostolus : Revelabitur ille iniquus, quem Dominus Jesus interficiet spiritu oris sui. Multos vero calumniatores atque tyrannos etiam in hac vita Christus humiliavit, privando eos vita aut regno. Omnes autem in die judicii finaliter humiliabit : quia tunc omnis qui se nunc exaltat, humiliabitur, non humiliatione virtuosa, sed dejectione damnosa.
paras.en: Then the Prophet shows that what he himself was praying for was to be fulfilled. [[71:4|He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor|Judicabit pauperes populi, et salvos faciet filios pauperum]]. For in the present he judges his poor with the judgment of discernment, as has been said; but on the last day he will judge them with the judgment of blessed reward, as he himself asserts in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:12|Behold, I come quickly: and my reward is with me, to render to every, man according to his works.|Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique secundum opera sua]] [[71:4|and he shall humble the oppressor|Et humiliabit calumniatorem]] [*calumniator*: literally a false accuser, one who wrongs another by trickery], that is, Christ will confound, condemn and destroy every persecutor of the just, every tyrant and tempter of the Church, the devil and Antichrist; according to that in Isaias: [[Is 11:4|he shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked|Percutiet terram virga oris sui, et spiritu labiorum suorum interficiet impium]], namely Antichrist. Of whom we read in the same: [[Is 25:10|Moab shall be trodden down under him|Triturabitur Moab sub eo]]. Of whom the Apostle too says: [[2 Thess 2:8|that wicked one shall be revealed: whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth|Revelabitur ille iniquus, quem Dominus Jesus interficiet spiritu oris sui]]. Many oppressors and tyrants indeed Christ has humbled even in this life, depriving them of life or kingdom. But all of them he will humble finally on the day of judgment: for then [[Luke 14:11|every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled|omnis qui se nunc exaltat, humiliabitur]] who exalts himself now, not with a virtuous humbling, but with a ruinous casting down.

paras.t: Et permanebit cum sole et ante lunam, in generatione et generationem. Sicut per lunam intelligi potest Ecclesia, ita per solem, Pater æternus, qui est lumen fontale cuncta illustrans : et de utroque sole et luna hic versus exponitur. Christus enim permanet cum sole intellectuali, scilicet Deo Patre, quoniam coæternus est ei. Cum hoc sole permanet a parte ante, secundum divinam naturam, tanquam splendor gloriæ et candor lucis æternæ. Permanet quoque Christus a parte post, secundum suam humanam ac divinam naturam, cum sole materiali : quoniam sicut sol incorruptibilis est, ita et Christus incorruptibiliter perseverat. Et ante lunam utramque, puta Ecclesiam, et lunam unum planetarum, permanet Christus a parte ante, secundum suam divinam naturam, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico ipsa Sapientia testatur : Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam. Et in Proverbiis : Dominus possedit me in initio viarum suarum, antequam quidquam faceret a principio. Quando præparabat cœlos, aderam ; et eram cum eo cuncta componens. Ecce hic manifeste declaratur divinitas Christi et ejus æternitas. Propter quod dicit etiam Apostolus : Jesus Christus heri et hodie, ipse et in sæcula.
paras.en: [[71:5|And he shall continue with the sun and before the moon, throughout all generations.|Et permanebit cum sole et ante lunam, in generatione et generationem]] As the Church can be understood by the moon, so by the sun the eternal Father, who is the fountain light enlightening all things; and this verse is expounded of both sun and moon. For Christ continues with the intellectual sun, namely God the Father, since he is coeternal with him. With this sun he continues from before, according to the divine nature, as [[Heb 1:3|the brightness of his glory|splendor gloriæ]] and [[Wis 7:26|the brightness of eternal light|candor lucis æternæ]] [Latin *splendor* and *candor*: both rendered "brightness" in the Douay-Rheims]. Christ continues also from after, according to his human and his divine nature, with the material sun: since as the sun is incorruptible, so Christ too endures incorruptibly. And before either moon, that is, the Church, and the moon one of the planets, Christ continues from before according to his divine nature, as Wisdom herself testifies in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 24:5|I came out of the mouth of the most High, the firstborn before all creatures:|Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam.]] And in Proverbs: [[Prov 8:22|The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made any thing from the beginning.|Dominus possedit me in initio viarum suarum, antequam quidquam faceret a principio]] [[Prov 8:27|When he prepared the heavens, I was present|Quando præparabat cœlos, aderam]]; and [[Prov 8:30|I was with him forming all things|eram cum eo cuncta componens]]. Here the divinity of Christ and his eternity are plainly declared. Wherefore the Apostle too says: [[Heb 13:8|Jesus Christ, yesterday, and today: and the same for ever.|Jesus Christus heri et hodie, ipse et in sæcula]]

paras.t: Descendet sicut pluvia in vellus. Libro Judicum narratur, quemadmodum ad instantiam Gedeonis complutum seu rore madefactum est vellus, terra sicca manente, et postea madefacta est circumquaque terra, vellere non adaquato. Est igitur sensus : Christus rex noster descendit in uterum Virginis, sicut descendit pluvia in vellus Gedeonis. Quemadmodum enim pluvia in vellus illud descendit, ita quod per vellus non distillavit, nec aliquid divisionis aut corruptionis velleri intulit ; sic Verbum Dei de sinu Patris in Virginem veniens, eam in nullo læsit aut violavit : quoniam non de viro concepit, sed Spiritu Sancto obumbrante est imprægnata ; supernaturaliter quoque formatum est corpus Christi in Virginis alvo, juxta illud Zachariæ, Ecce ego cælabo sculpturam ejus, ait Dominus : id est, corpus ejus formabo. Et sicut stillicidia stillantia super terram. Quemadmodum guttæ leniter atque suaviter cadunt de cœlo in terram, et eam refrigerant et fecundant, sic Christus per suam incarnationem dulciter et sine strepitu descendit in Matrem Virginem, et per eam in mundum. Nam primus ejus adventus, in humilitate, paupertate ac mansuetudine fuit, secundum quod Zacharias prædixit : Exsulta satis, filia Sion ; ecce rex tuus veniet tibi justus et salvator, ipse pauper, etc. Et in Evangelio ipsemet fassus est : Filius hominis non habet ubi caput suum reclinet.
paras.en: [[71:6|He shall come down like rain upon the fleece|Descendet sicut pluvia in vellus]]. In the book of Judges it is told how, at Gedeon's urging, the fleece was rained upon, or soaked with dew, while the ground stayed dry[[Judg 6:38||]], and afterwards the ground all round was soaked, the fleece not being wetted[[Judg 6:40||]]. The sense, then, is: Christ our King came down into the Virgin's womb as the rain came down upon Gedeon's fleece. For as the rain came down upon that fleece in such a way that it did not drip through the fleece, nor brought any division or corruption to the fleece; so the Word of God, coming from the bosom of the Father into the Virgin, harmed or violated her in nothing: since she did not conceive of man, but was made fruitful by the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost[[Luke 1:35||]]; and the body of Christ was formed supernaturally in the Virgin's womb, according to that in Zacharias: [[Zach 3:9|behold I will grave the graving thereof, saith the Lord|Ecce ego cælabo sculpturam ejus, ait Dominus]]: that is, I will form his body. [[71:6|and as showers falling gently upon the earth|Et sicut stillicidia stillantia super terram]]. As drops fall gently and softly from heaven upon the earth, and refresh it and make it fruitful, so Christ through his incarnation came down sweetly and without noise into the Virgin Mother, and through her into the world. For his first coming was in humility, poverty and meekness, as Zacharias foretold: [[Zach 9:9|Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion|Exsulta satis, filia Sion]]; [[Zach 9:9|BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee, the just and saviour: he is poor|ecce rex tuus veniet tibi justus et salvator, ipse pauper]], etc. And in the Gospel he himself owned: [[Luke 9:58|the Son of man hath not where to lay his head|Filius hominis non habet ubi caput suum reclinet]].

paras.t: Oritur in diebus ejus, id est in primo Christi adventu, justitia, id est perfectio vitæ, seu fides catholica. Tempus enim Christi, est tempus gratiæ : propterea homines Christi vestigia imitantes, perfectius sanctiusque vixerunt quam Judæi tempore legis. Et ideo Christus in Evangelio ait : Nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum ; et ad Joannem Baptistam, Sic, inquit, decet nos implere omnem justitiam. In tantum enim abundavit gratia atque justitia tempore Christi, plus quam ante, ut scriptum sit apud Joannem, Nondum erat Spiritus datus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus : non quod ante nequaquam fuerat datus, sed quia tam exuberanter datus non erat.
paras.en: [[71:7|In his days|in diebus ejus]] [Denis reads *Oritur*, "springs up", for the Vulgate's *Orietur*], that is, in Christ's first coming, [[71:7|shall justice spring up|justitia]], that is, perfection of life, or the Catholic faith. For the time of Christ is the time of grace: therefore men following in Christ's footsteps lived more perfectly and holily than the Jews in the time of the Law. And so Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:20|unless your justice abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]]; and to John the Baptist: Thus, he says, [[Matt 3:15|it becometh us to fulfil all justice|decet nos implere omnem justitiam]]. For grace and justice abounded so much more in the time of Christ than before, that it is written in John: [[John 7:39|as yet the Spirit was not given, because Jesus was not yet glorified|Nondum erat Spiritus datus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus]]: not that he had in no way been given before, but that he had not been given so abundantly.

paras.t: Et abundantia pacis. Hoc est quod superius dictum est : Venite et videte opera Domini, quæ posuit prodigia super terram, auferens bella usque ad finem terræ. Et Isaias ait : Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium. Et ita ista abundantia pacis tempore Christi orta, intelligeretur de pace temporali, quæ fuit in toto mundo sub Cæsare Augusto, sub quo natus est Christus, ita quod ad unius viri imperium describeretur universus orbis. Sed quia hæc pax non duravit donec auferatur * luna, idcirco, secundum hanc expositionem, hoc quod dicitur, donec auferatur luna, referendum est ad justitiæ christianæ durationem, quæ usque in finem mundi durabit, non autem ad durationem pacis prædictæ.
paras.en: [[71:7|and abundance of peace|Et abundantia pacis]]. This is what was said above: [[Ps 45:9|Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth|Venite et videte opera Domini, quæ posuit prodigia super terram]], [[Ps 45:10|Making wars to cease even to the end of the earth|auferens bella usque ad finem terræ]]. And Isaias says: [[Is 2:4|nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they be exercised any more to war|Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium]]. And so this abundance of peace that sprang up in the time of Christ might be understood of temporal peace, which there was in the whole world under Caesar Augustus, under whom Christ was born, so that the whole world was enrolled under the rule of one man[[Luke 2:1||]]. But because this peace did not last until the moon be taken away [the margin corrects the printed *auferatur* to *auferretur*, "should be taken away"], therefore, according to this exposition, what is said, [[71:7|till the moon be taken away|donec auferatur luna]], is to be referred to the duration of Christian justice, which will last until the end of the world, and not to the duration of the peace just mentioned.

paras.t: Convenientius tamen apparet, ut hæc abundantia pacis intelligatur de magnitudine pacis internæ, in tranquillitate conscientiæ collocatæ. De qua Apostolus loquitur : Pax Christi exsultet semper in cordibus vestris. Quam Zacharias prophetavit Christum suis fidelibus esse daturum : Loquetur, inquiens, pacem gentibus. Hanc etenim pacem annuntiaverunt angeli in Christi nativitate, dicentes : Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis. Hæc pax in bonis abundat hominibus, sicut orat Apostolus : Pax Christi, quæ exsuperat omnem sensum, custodiat corda vestra et intelligentias vestras. Et ob ejus copiam, vocatus est Christus Princeps pacis. Hæc itaque abundantia pacis permanet in electis, donec auferatur luna, id est, nunquam cessabit, sicut nec luna; vel, Donec auferatur luna, id est, quousque Ecclesia militans transferatur ad societatem triumphantis Ecclesiæ, omni corruptione et mortalitate abjecta. Non quod tunc cessabit; sed quia tunc perficietur, sicut et luna semiplena perficitur: et ita, Donec, non denotat terminum pacis, sed continuationem ipsius : quemadmodum de Joseph et Maria ait Matthæus, Non cognoscebat eam, donec peperit filium suum primogenitum.
paras.en: It seems more fitting, however, that this abundance of peace be understood of the greatness of inward peace, set in tranquillity of conscience. Of which the Apostle speaks: [[Col 3:15|let the peace of Christ rejoice in your hearts|Pax Christi exsultet semper in cordibus vestris]]. Which Zacharias prophesied that Christ would give to his faithful: [[Zach 9:10|he shall speak|Loquetur]], he says, [[Zach 9:10|peace to the Gentiles|pacem gentibus]]. For this is the peace the angels announced at Christ's birth, saying: [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest: and on earth peace to men of good will.|Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra pax hominibus bonæ voluntatis]] This peace abounds in good men, as the Apostle prays: [[Phil 4:7|the peace of God, which surpasseth all understanding, keep your hearts and minds|Pax Christi, quæ exsuperat omnem sensum, custodiat corda vestra et intelligentias vestras]] [Denis reads "the peace of Christ" where the Vulgate has *pax Dei*]. And because of its fullness Christ is called [[Is 9:6|the Prince of Peace|Princeps pacis]]. This abundance of peace, then, remains in the elect [[71:7|till the moon be taken away|donec auferatur luna]], that is, it will never cease, just as the moon will not; or, [[71:7|till the moon be taken away|Donec auferatur luna]], that is, until the Church militant is carried over into the company of the Church triumphant, all corruption and mortality cast off. Not that it will cease then, but that it will then be made perfect, as the half-full moon is made full: and so *till* does not mark the end of the peace, but its continuance; as Matthew says of Joseph and Mary: [[Matt 1:25|he knew her not, till she brought forth her first born son|Non cognoscebat eam, donec peperit filium suum primogenitum]].

paras.t: Et dominabitur Christus a mari orientali usque ad mare occidentale, quia in omnem terram exivit sonus Apostolorum, et conversi sunt in omnibus finibus mundi quidam ad Christum ; et a flumine paradisi terrestris, seu Jordanis ; vel, A flumine quocumque, puta a cunctis fluminibus, accipiendo singulare pro plurali ; usque ad terminos orbis terrarum. Unde in Zacharia scriptum est : Potestas ejus a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad fines terræ. Et hæc de Christo dicuntur : Primo, quoniam omnia, etiam inanimata et irrationalia, subjecta sunt ei, prout ipse in Evangelio dicit : Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra. Secundo, quoniam omnis homo in omni mundo exsistens, velit, nolit, Christi subjectus est potestati, secundum quod ipse ait, loquens de se ipso ad Patrem : Dedisti ei potestatem omnis carnis. Tertio, quoniam in omni parte terræ habitabilis, aliqui Christo per fidem et opera obedierunt : propter quod Deus Pater ait ad Christum apud Isaiam, Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ. Et hoc est quod ait Salvator Apostolis : Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ.
paras.en: [[71:8|And he shall rule|Et dominabitur]], Christ, [[71:8|from sea|a mari]] in the east [[71:8|to sea|usque ad mare]] in the west, because the sound of the Apostles [[Ps 18:5|hath gone forth into all the earth|in omnem terram exivit]], and some in all the ends of the world were converted to Christ; [[71:8|and from the river|et a flumine]] of the earthly paradise, or of the Jordan; or, from any river, that is, from all rivers, taking the singular for the plural; [[71:8|unto the ends of the earth|usque ad terminos orbis terrarum]]. Whence it is written in Zacharias: [[Zach 9:10|his power shall be from sea to sea, and from the rivers even to the end of the earth|Potestas ejus a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad fines terræ]]. And these things are said of Christ: first, because all things, even lifeless and irrational ones, are subject to him, as he himself says in the Gospel: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]. Secondly, because every man existing anywhere in the world, willing or unwilling, is subject to Christ's power, as he himself says, speaking of himself to the Father: [[John 17:2|thou hast given him power over all flesh|Dedisti ei potestatem omnis carnis]]. Thirdly, because in every part of the habitable earth some have obeyed Christ by faith and works: wherefore God the Father says to Christ in Isaias: [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]]. And this is what the Saviour says to the Apostles: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]].

paras.t: Coram illo procident Æthiopes. Illi enim per evangelistam Matthæum conversi, Christum humiliter adoraverunt. Possunt autem per Æthiopes accipi gentiles : qui ante conversionem suam ad Christum, erant vitiorum caligine denigrati, sicut Æthiopes nigra pelle teguntur. Et inimici ejus, Christo increduli, terram lingent, id est, rebus terrenis adhærebunt, et eas præ amore sibi intime applicabunt. Unde Jeremias : Recedentes, inquit, a te, in terra scribentur. Vel sic : Inimici ejus, id est, qui Christo aliquando repugnabant, post conversionem terram lingent, id est, eam ex devotione ad Christum, osculabuntur, prosternendo se usque ad terram, propter reverentiam Christi.
paras.en: [[71:9|Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down|Coram illo procident Æthiopes]]. For they, converted through the evangelist Matthew, humbly adored Christ[[Matt 2:11||]] [by tradition St Matthew preached in Ethiopia; the margin's Matt. ii, 11 is the Magi falling down to adore the Child]. But by the Ethiopians the Gentiles can be understood, who before their conversion to Christ were blackened with the darkness of vices, as the Ethiopians are covered with a black skin. [[71:9|and his enemies|Et inimici ejus]], unbelieving towards Christ, [[71:9|shall lick the ground|terram lingent]], that is, will cleave to earthly things and, for love of them, press them closely to themselves. Whence Jeremias: [[Jer 17:13|they that depart|Recedentes]], he says, [[Jer 17:13|from thee, shall be written in the earth|a te, in terra scribentur]]. Or thus: [[71:9|his enemies|Inimici ejus]], that is, those who once resisted Christ, after their conversion [[71:9|shall lick the ground|terram lingent]], that is, will kiss it out of devotion to Christ, prostrating themselves to the ground out of reverence for Christ.

paras.t: Reges Tharsis et insulæ munera offerent ; reges Arabum et Saba dona adducent. Hoc ad litteram non solum impletum est in tribus Magis, Christo in die Epiphaniæ, aurum, thus et myrrham offerentibus, sed et in aliis multis regibus atque principibus harum terrarum, quæ multo tempore fuerunt sub fide catholica, et Christo seu Ecclesiæ diversa munera obtulerunt, videlicet spirituales corporalesque hostias.
paras.en: [[71:10|The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents: the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts:|Reges Tharsis et insulæ munera offerent ; reges Arabum et Saba dona adducent]] This was fulfilled according to the letter not only in the three Magi, who on the day of the Epiphany offered Christ [[Matt 2:11|gold, frankincense, and myrrh|aurum, thus et myrrham]], but also in many other kings and princes of those lands, which were for a long time under the Catholic faith and offered Christ, or the Church, various gifts, namely spiritual and bodily offerings.

paras.t: Et adorabunt eum omnes reges ; omnes gentes servient ei. Utraque distributionum istarum sumenda est pro generibus singularum, non pro singulis generum. Nam et de omni genere regum ac gentium, aliqui Christum adoraverunt, et ipsi ministraverunt, juxta vaticinium Danielis, dicentis : Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei. Et Michæas : Stabit et pascet in fortitudine Domini ; et convertentur, quia nunc magnificabitur in medio universæ terræ.
paras.en: [[71:11|And all kings of the earth shall adore him|Et adorabunt eum omnes reges]] [Denis's text has no *terræ*, "of the earth"]; [[71:11|all nations shall serve him|omnes gentes servient ei]]. Both of these universal statements are to be taken of every kind of individual, not of every individual of every kind [that is, "all" here means some of every sort, not every single one]. For of every kind of kings and nations some have adored Christ and served him, according to the prophecy of Daniel, who says: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]]. And Micheas: [[Mich 5:4|he shall stand, and feed in the strength of the Lord|Stabit et pascet in fortitudine Domini]]; [[Mich 5:4|and they shall be converted, for now shall he be magnified|et convertentur, quia nunc magnificabitur]] in the midst of the whole earth [Denis reads *in medio universæ terræ* where the Vulgate has "even to the ends of the earth"].

paras.t: Consequenter inducitur causa universalis dominii Christi. Quia liberabit pauperem a potente. Sed qualem pauperem? Subdit : et pauperem cui non erat adjutor alius, nisi ipse Deus. Talis pauper est omnis humilis, qui propriis viribus nequaquam innitur, sed toto affectu in Deo confidit. Hujusmodi autem pauperem Deus multipliciter liberat a potente, id est a dæmone : quem Christus in Evangelio fortem armatum appellat; et de quo apud Job scriptum est : Non est potestas super terram quæ ei comparetur, qui factus est ut nullum timeret. Vel, A potente, id est homine quocumque superbo et forti, per naturalem fortitudinem aut sæcularem potentiam aliis prævalente. Primo liberat Christus pauperes ab his potentibus, dando eis patientiam in adversis, constantiamque in bonis : sic quod illorum malignitas ipsis non nocet, imo cooperatur eis in bonum. Secundo, quoniam facit eos tentationes viriliter superare, et tanto instantius studere virtutibus, quanto amplius impugnantur. Tertio, quoniam æternaliter eos salvabit, illis in æternum damnatis. Hinc enim apud Jeremiam dicitur : Cantate Domino, laudate Dominum, quia liberavit animam pauperis de manu malorum. Et per Isaiam Dominus ait : Ego Dominus exaudiam egenum et pauperem, non derelinquam eos.
paras.en: Next the cause of Christ's universal dominion is brought in. [[71:12|For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty|Quia liberabit pauperem a potente]]. But what kind of poor man? He adds: [[71:12|and the needy that had no helper|et pauperem cui non erat adjutor]] other than God himself. Such a poor man is every humble man who in no way leans on his own strength, but trusts in God with his whole heart. Such a poor man God delivers in many ways [[71:12|from the mighty|a potente]], that is, from the demon, whom Christ in the Gospel calls [[Luke 11:21|a strong man armed|fortem armatum]], and of whom it is written in Job: [[Job 41:24|There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him who was made to fear no one|Non est potestas super terram quæ ei comparetur, qui factus est ut nullum timeret]] [the margin gives Job xii, 24; the words are Job 41:24]. Or, [[71:12|from the mighty|A potente]], that is, from any proud and strong man prevailing over others by natural strength or worldly power. First, Christ delivers the poor from these mighty ones by giving them patience in adversity and constancy in good: so that their malice does them no harm, but rather works with them for good. Secondly, because he makes them overcome temptations manfully, and strive for virtue the more earnestly the more they are attacked. Thirdly, because he will save them eternally, while those are damned for ever. Hence it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 20:13|Sing ye to the Lord, praise the Lord: because he hath delivered the soul of the poor out of the hand of the wicked.|Cantate Domino, laudate Dominum, quia liberavit animam pauperis de manu malorum]] And the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 41:17|I the Lord will hear|Ego Dominus exaudiam]] the needy and the poor, [[Is 41:17|will not forsake them|non derelinquam eos]].

paras.t: Parcet pauperi et inopi, peccata dimittendo, pœnam relaxando, et gratiam tribuendo. Unde per Malachiam ait : Parcam timentibus me, dicit Dominus, sicut parcit vir filio suo servienti sibi. Et animas pauperum salvas faciet, modo per gratiam, et in futuro per gloriam. Propter quod ait Apostolus : Altissima paupertas eorum, abundavit in divitias simplicitatis eorum.
paras.en: [[71:13|He shall spare the poor and needy|Parcet pauperi et inopi]], by forgiving sins, remitting punishment and granting grace. Whence he says by Malachias: [[Mal 3:17|I will spare|Parcam]] them that fear me, saith the Lord, [[Mal 3:17|as a man spareth his son that serveth him|sicut parcit vir filio suo servienti sibi]]. [[71:13|and he shall save the souls of the poor|Et animas pauperum salvas faciet]], now by grace, and in the future by glory. Wherefore the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 8:2|their very deep poverty hath abounded unto the riches of their simplicity|Altissima paupertas eorum, abundavit in divitias simplicitatis eorum]].

paras.t: Ex usuris et iniquitate redimet animas eorum. Christus namque per suos ministros atque vicarios, scilicet per summum Pontificem, aliosque prælatos ac principes, damnat et prohibet usuras sub æternæ damnationis periculo. Est autem alia quoque usura, ex qua suos eripit Christus, videlicet obligatio ad pœnam inferni, quæ sequitur perpetrationem peccati. Peccatum namque est quasi pecunia dæmonis, et pro eo exigit ipse a nobis pœnas perpetuas ; quas non suscepimus, sed solvimus propter iniquitatem, quam a diabolica suggestione contraximus. Ab hac usura et omni iniquitate redemit Christus pauperes suos semel pretio sanguinis sui ; quotidie quoque ab his redimit eos per infusionem gratiæ spiritualis, quæ est effectus meriti dominicæ passionis. Et honorabile nomen eorum coram illo, id est, nomen pauperum Dei, quo Christiani vocantur, coram Deo dignum est veneratione ac laude. Hoc quippe est nomen, de quo Isaias Judæos redarguens ait : Interficiet vos Dominus Deus, et servos suos vocabit nomine alio, in quo qui benedictus est super terram, benedicetur in Deo. Amen. Hoc nomen (sicut in Actibus Apostolorum Lucas commemorat) primo impositum est discipulis Christi in Antiochia.
paras.en: [[71:14|He shall redeem their souls from usuries and iniquity|Ex usuris et iniquitate redimet animas eorum]]. For Christ, through his ministers and vicars, namely through the supreme Pontiff and the other prelates and princes, condemns and forbids usury under peril of eternal damnation. There is also another usury, from which Christ rescues his own, namely the obligation to the punishment of hell which follows the committing of sin. For sin is as it were the devil's money, and for it he exacts from us everlasting punishment; which we did not take on as a loan but pay on account of the iniquity which we contracted at the devil's suggestion [Denis plays on usury: the debt of sin is paid back with interest in eternal punishment]. From this usury and from all iniquity Christ redeemed his poor once for all with the price of his blood; and every day too he redeems them from these by the infusion of spiritual grace, which is the effect of the merit of the Lord's passion. [[71:14|and their names shall be honourable in his sight|Et honorabile nomen eorum coram illo]], that is, the name of God's poor, by which they are called Christians, is worthy of veneration and praise before God. For this is the name of which Isaias says, rebuking the Jews: [[Is 65:15|the Lord God shall slay thee, and call his servants by another name|Interficiet vos Dominus Deus, et servos suos vocabit nomine alio]], [[Is 65:16|In which he that is blessed upon the earth, shall be blessed in God, amen|in quo qui benedictus est super terram, benedicetur in Deo. Amen]]. This name (as Luke records in the Acts of the Apostles) was first given to Christ's disciples at Antioch[[Acts 11:26||]].

paras.t: Et vivet, id est, Christus morte devicta, immortalis resurget et æternaliter vivet. Et dabitur ei de auro Arabiæ. Multi enim principum christianorum tale aurum (quod optimum est) Christo et ejus ministris obtulerunt ad sustentationem pauperum, constructionem ecclesiarum, et in alios pios usus. Mystice vero, per aurum signatur sapientia, per Arabiam vero gentilitas : et ita datur Christo de auro Arabiæ, dum sapientes hujus sæculi, et in naturali philosophia doctissimi, ad fidem Ecclesiæ sunt conversi, ut patet de divo Dionysio, Augustino, et aliis multis. Datur etiam Christo de auro Arabiæ, dum sibi ipsi homo non innititur, sed omnem naturalem scientiam fidei subjicit, sicut creatura subdenda est Creatori. Et adorabunt de ipso semper, id est, fideles Deum adorabunt de Christo, id est ex contemplatione bonitatis, beneficiorumque ejus. Propter beneficia namque per Christum nobis collata, Deum semper adorare et venerari debemus. Tota die, id est qualibet parte diei convenienti ac debita, benedicent ei, id est, Christum regem laudabunt.
paras.en: [[71:15|And he shall live|Et vivet]], that is, Christ, having overcome death, will rise immortal and live eternally. [[71:15|and to him shall be given of the gold of Arabia|Et dabitur ei de auro Arabiæ]]. For many Christian princes have offered such gold (which is the best) to Christ and his ministers for the support of the poor, the building of churches and other pious uses. Mystically, however, wisdom is signified by gold, and the Gentile world by Arabia: and so Christ is given [[71:15|of the gold of Arabia|de auro Arabiæ]] when the wise of this world, and those most learned in natural philosophy, are converted to the faith of the Church, as is plain in St Dionysius, Augustine and many others. Christ is given of the gold of Arabia also when a man does not lean on himself but subjects all natural knowledge to faith, as the creature is to be subject to the Creator. [[71:15|for him they shall always adore|Et adorabunt de ipso semper]], that is, the faithful will adore God for Christ, that is, from the contemplation of his goodness and of his benefits. For because of the benefits bestowed on us through Christ we ought always to adore and worship God. [[71:15|all the day|Tota die]], that is, at every fit and due part of the day, [[71:15|they shall bless him|benedicent ei]], that is, they will praise Christ the King.

paras.t: Erit rex Christus firmamentum in terra, id est causa totius firmitatis ac stabilitatis hominum in terra manentium, in summis montium, id est in profundissima doctrina Prophetarum, confirmando et illuminando suos electos in sapientia Scripturarum, illas verificans in semetipso, sicut in Evangelio Joannis habetur : Veritas per Jesum Christum facta est. Unde et ipse post resurrectionem dixit discipulis : Oportet impleri omnia, quæ scripta sunt in lege et Prophetis et Psalmis de me.
