Tu fabricatus es auroram et solem, id est Virginem gloriosam, et Christum hominem Virginis Filium, dando utrique quidquid habent in donis naturæ et gratiæ. Maria quippe, aurora vocatur : quoniam sicut aurora diem præcedit, sic ipsa Christum. Unde de ea in Canticis legitur : Quæ est ista, velut aurora consurgens? Christus quoque, etiam ut homo, sol dicitur : quoniam sicut stellæ omnes a sole lumen recipere æstimantur, sic omnes sancti a Christo lumen fidei, gratiæ et sapientiæ sortiuntur. Nam de plenitudine ejus omnes accepimus. Tu fecisti, id est, spiritualiter reformasti et regenerasti, omnes terminos terræ, id est omnes electos in finibus mundi morantes. Æstatem et ver, id est remunerationem seu præmium ac meritum, tu plasmasti. In vere enim arbores flores, in æstate autem fructus producunt : et ita per æstatem accipitur præmium ; per ver, meritum. Deus autem causat in nobis non solum præmium, sed etiam meritum, juxta illud Isaiæ : Domine, dabis pacem nobis ; omnia enim opera nostra operatus es in nobis. Per æstatem quoque intelligi possunt fervidi amatores Divinitatis ; per ver autem, novelli et incipientes in Dei obsequio.
paras.en: [[73:16|Thine is the day|Tuus est dies]], that is, spiritual men enlightened by the Sun of justice and the fountain of wisdom, [[73:16|and thine is the night|et tua est nox]], that is, the people that lives carnally. For all kinds of men are God's, by right of creation and of universal dominion. [[73:16|thou hast made the morning light and the sun|Tu fabricatus es auroram et solem]], that is, the glorious Virgin, and Christ the man, the Virgin's Son, giving to each whatever they have in the gifts of nature and of grace. For Mary is called the dawn, because as the dawn goes before the day, so she went before Christ. Hence we read of her in the Canticles: [[Cant 6:9|Who is she|Quæ est ista]] [[Cant 6:9|as the morning rising|velut aurora consurgens]]? Christ too, even as man, is called the sun: because as all the stars are thought to receive their light from the sun, so all the saints receive from Christ the light of faith, of grace and of wisdom. For [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|de plenitudine ejus omnes accepimus]]. [[73:17|Thou hast made|Tu fecisti]], that is, hast spiritually reformed and regenerated, [[73:17|all the borders of the earth|omnes terminos terræ]], that is, all the elect dwelling in the ends of the world. [[73:17|the summer and the spring|Æstatem et ver]], that is, the reward or prize, and the merit, [[73:17|were formed by thee|tu plasmasti]] [literally "thou hast formed"]. For in spring the trees bring forth flowers, and in summer fruits: and so by summer is understood the reward, by spring the merit. Now God causes in us not only the reward but also the merit, according to that word of Isaias: [[Is 26:12|Lord, thou wilt give us peace: for thou hast wrought all our works for us|Domine, dabis pacem nobis ; omnia enim opera nostra operatus es in nobis]]. By summer too can be understood the fervent lovers of the Godhead; and by spring, those who are new and beginners in the service of God.

paras.t: Memor esto hujus congregationis ecclesiasticæ : de qua dictum est. Inimicus improperavit Domino, id est, hæretici et perversi vituperaverunt doctrinam Christi atque Ecclesiæ, dicentes : Aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior ; et populus insipiens, id est Deum verum ignorans, vel factis eum se ignorare ostendens, incitavit nomen tuum, id est, te ad iracundiam provocavit : idcirco peribit, sicut de eo inducitur, Populus non intelligens vapulabit. Ne tradas, aut tradi permittas, bestiis, id est dæmonibus vel sævis hominibus, animam confitentem tibi sua peccata et tua præconia. Cetera patent ex elucidatione præhabita.
paras.en: [[73:18|Remember this|Memor esto hujus]] ecclesiastical congregation, of which mention was made[[73:2||]]. [[73:18|the enemy hath reproached the Lord|Inimicus improperavit Domino]], that is, heretics and wicked men have reviled the doctrine of Christ and of the Church, saying: [[Prov 9:17|Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread is more pleasant|Aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior]]; [[73:18|and a foolish people|et populus insipiens]], that is, one ignorant of the true God, or showing by its deeds that it does not know him, [[73:18|hath provoked thy name|incitavit nomen tuum]], that is, has provoked thee to anger: therefore it shall perish, as is said of it: [[Osee 4:14|the people that doth not understand shall be beaten|Populus non intelligens vapulabit]]. [[73:19|Deliver not up|Ne tradas]], or suffer to be delivered up, [[73:19|to beasts|bestiis]], that is, to demons or to cruel men, the soul [[73:19|that confess to thee|confitentem tibi]] [the Douay-Rheims has "the souls that confess"; Denis reads the singular, *animam confitentem*] its sins and thy praises. The rest is plain from the explanation given before.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum sententiosum et affectuosum audivimus : in quo pristina divinæ familiaritatis beneficia recoluntur, malignitas persecutorum Ecclesiæ enarratur, tribulationes justorum scribuntur, pro adversariorum correctione oratur, divina potentia ex suis effectibus demonstratur. Quemadmodum igitur condecens est, devotione congrua præsentem psalmum canamus, et informemur ex eo in omni adversitate ad Deum affectuose converti, confidenter precari, beneficia patribus nostris exhibita commemorare : quatenus consequamur similia, atque ab omni liberemur instabilitate atque angustia.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of weighty sayings and of feeling: in which the former benefits of God's familiar friendship are recalled, the malice of the Church's persecutors is told, the tribulations of the just are written down, prayer is made for the correction of her adversaries, and the divine power is shown from its effects. As it is therefore most fitting, let us sing the present psalm with due devotion, and let us be taught by it, in every adversity, to turn lovingly to God, to pray with confidence, and to recall the benefits shown to our fathers: so that we may obtain the like, and be delivered from all unsteadiness and distress.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, Rex noster ante sæcula, Christe, qui in fine sæculi operatus es salutem in redemptione Ecclesiæ tuæ, quam ab initio tuo possedisti prædestinatione, respice in testamentum sanguine tuo confirmatum, faciendo eamdem Ecclesiam tuam devotam permanere, et in securitate jugi consistere : qui cum Deo Patre et Spiritu Sancto, etc.
paras.en: Prayer. O [[73:12|God|Deus]], [[73:12|our king before ages|Rex noster ante sæcula]], O Christ, who at the end of the age hast [[73:12|wrought salvation|operatus es salutem]] in the redemption of thy Church, [[73:2|which thou hast possessed from the beginning|quam ab initio tuo possedisti]] by thy predestination, [[73:20|Have regard to thy covenant|respice in testamentum]] confirmed by thy blood, making that same Church of thine abide devout and stand in unbroken security: who with God the Father and the Holy Ghost, etc.

74.title: DECLARATIO PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI QUARTI : CONFITEBIMUR TIBI, DEUS, CONFITEBIMUR.
74.title_en: Explanation of the seventy-fourth psalm: We will praise thee, O God, we will praise.

paras.t: Denique titulus psalmi præsentis est : In finem, ne corrumpas, psalmus cantici Asaph. Quidam exponunt hunc psalmum ad litteram de populo Judæorum, redeunte a captivitate Babylonis, ut sit gratiarum actio populi inde liberati, et in Judæam reversi. Sicque sensus tituli est iste : Psalmus cantici est ipsius Asaph, ne corrumpas, id est, ne disperdas, o Domine, populum Israel, sicut fecisti in captivitate Babyloniæ. Videtur autem mihi expositio ista parum devotionis includere, modicumque dulcedinis continere : breviter tamen tangi potest hoc modo.
paras.en: Next, the title of the present psalm is: [[74:1|Unto the end, corrupt not, a psalm of a canticle for Asaph|In finem, ne corrumpas, psalmus cantici Asaph]]. Some expound this psalm literally of the Jewish people returning from the captivity of Babylon, so that it is the thanksgiving of the people set free from there and returned to Judea. And so the sense of the title is this: [[74:1|a psalm of a canticle|Psalmus cantici]] is Asaph’s own; [[74:1|corrupt not|ne corrumpas]], that is, destroy not, O Lord, the people of Israel, as thou didst in the captivity of Babylon. But this exposition seems to me to hold little devotion and to contain small sweetness; yet it can be touched on briefly in this way.

paras.t: Confitebimur tibi, Deus, nos de captivitate reversi ex licentia Darii regis Medorum et Cyri regis Persarum, quod juste castigasti nos, quia peccavimus ; confitebimur tibi, quod misericorditer reduxisti nos, imo et juste, quoniam promisisti per Jeremiam, quod post septuaginta annos eripiendi essemus de captivitate; et invocabimus nomen tuum pro gratia vitandi peccata præterita, ne denuo incidamus similia mala. Narrabimus mirabilia tua, quæ in Babylone vidimus aut cognovimus, quomodo scilicet eripuisti tres pueros de camino ardenti, et Danielem de lacu leonum, et Susannam de manibus judicum impiorum : quæ omnia in Daniele leguntur.
paras.en: [[74:2|We will praise thee, O God|Confitebimur tibi, Deus]], we who have returned from captivity by leave of Darius king of the Medes and Cyrus king of the Persians, that thou hast justly chastised us, because we have sinned; [[74:2|we will praise thee|confitebimur tibi]] [the Latin *confitebimur* means both ‘we will praise’ and ‘we will confess’] that thou hast mercifully brought us back, yea, and justly, since thou didst promise by Jeremias that after seventy years we should be delivered from captivity[[Jer 25:11||]]; [[74:2|and we will call upon thy name|et invocabimus nomen tuum]], for grace to shun our past sins, lest we fall again into like evils. [[74:2|We will relate thy wondrous works|Narrabimus mirabilia tua]], which we saw or came to know in Babylon: namely, how thou didst deliver the three children from the burning furnace[[Dan 3:1||]], and Daniel from the lions’ den[[Dan 6:1||]][[Dan 14:1||]], and Susanna from the hands of the wicked judges[[Dan 13:1||]]: all of which are read in Daniel.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta mutans personam, ait in persona Dei : Quum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo, id est, tempore a me præordinato atque disposito, judicabo justitias electorum, liberando eos de manibus injustorum, prout eorum justitiæ exigunt et merentur.
paras.en: Then the Prophet, changing the person, says in the person of God: [[74:3|When I shall take a time, I will judge justices|Quum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo]], that is, at the time foreordained and appointed by me I will judge the justices of the elect [*justitias*, ‘justices’: their just deeds and just causes], delivering them from the hands of the unjust, as their just deeds require and deserve.

paras.t: Liquefacta est terra, id est, Judæa a Chaldæis incensa est et combusta, et omnes qui habitant in ea, id est, qui morabantur in terra hac, timore Chaldæorum dissoluti sunt corde. Ego Deus confirmavi columnas ejus, id est, principes populi hujus stabilivi in bono, et in fortitudine animi inconcussa, videlicet Zorobabel, Jesum filium Josedec sacerdotem magnum, Zachariam, Aggæum, Esdram, Nehemiam.
paras.en: [[74:4|The earth is melted|Liquefacta est terra]], that is, Judea was set on fire and burnt by the Chaldeans, [[74:4|and all that dwell therein|et omnes qui habitant in ea]], that is, those who lived in this land were melted in heart for fear of the Chaldeans. [[74:4|I have established the pillars thereof|Ego Deus confirmavi columnas ejus]], that is, I have made firm in good, and in unshaken strength of soul, the princes of this people: namely Zorobabel[[1 Esd 3:2||]], Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest[[Agg 1:14||]][[Agg 2:3||]], Zacharias, Aggeus[[1 Esd 5:1||]] [the margin gives 1 Esdr. v, 4; Aggeus and Zacharias are named at 1 Esd 5:1], Esdras[[1 Esd 7:6||]], Nehemias[[2 Esd 7:7||]].

paras.t: Dixi, id est, ego Deus, non verbis sed opere, intimavi iniquis, id est superbis Babyloniis : Nolite inique agere, id est, nolite amplius regna et populum alienum opprimere, sicut hucusque fecistis; dixi et delinquentibus, id est prædictis iniquis : Nolite exaltare cornu, id est, nolite diutius regnare seu regiam potestatem exercere. Nolite extollere in altum cornu vestrum, imperando omnibus regnis, et monarchiam tenendo ; nolite loqui adversus Deum iniquitatem, blasphemando Deum Israel, et subsannando populum ejus, quemadmodum diu fecistis. Hæc omnia dixit Deus Chaldæis, non verbo sed opere : quoniam abstulit eis potestatem prosequendi opera mala, transferendo regnum eorum ad Medos ac Persas, ut in Daniele habetur, et ab Isaia et Jeremia evidentissime prænuntiatum conspicitur.
paras.en: [[74:5|I said|Dixi]], that is, I God, not in words but in deed, made known [[74:5|to the wicked|iniquis]], that is, to the proud Babylonians: [[74:5|Do not act wickedly|Nolite inique agere]], that is, oppress no more the kingdoms and a people not your own, as you have done till now; [[74:5|I said|dixi]] also [[74:5|to the sinners|delinquentibus]], that is, to the aforesaid wicked: [[74:5|Lift not up the horn|Nolite exaltare cornu]], that is, reign no longer, nor wield royal power. [[74:6|Lift not up your horn on high|Nolite extollere in altum cornu vestrum]], by ruling over all kingdoms and holding the monarchy; [[74:6|speak not iniquity against God|nolite loqui adversus Deum iniquitatem]], by blaspheming the God of Israel and mocking his people, as you have long done. All this God said to the Chaldeans, not in word but in deed: for he took from them the power to carry on their evil works, by transferring their kingdom to the Medes and Persians, as is found in Daniel[[Dan 5:28||]], and is seen to have been most plainly foretold by Isaias[[Is 13:17||]] and Jeremias[[Jer 51:1||]].

paras.t: Cur autem Deus hæc dixerit eis, subdit Propheta : Quia neque ab oriente, neque ab occidente, neque a desertis montibus, id est, quia ex nulla parte aut latere mundi, poteritis, o Babylonii, judicium divinum effugere : et hoc ideo, quoniam Deus ubique exsistens, omnia cernens, atque omnipotens, judex est. Hunc humiliat, et hunc exaltat, id est, unum deprimit, et alium elevat, secundum quod sibi placet et homines promerentur ; quia calix in manu Domini, id est, pœna seu ultio est in potestate Dei : calix, inquam, vini meri plenus mixto : id est, pœna quam Deus effundere potest in impios, est multum acerba et pungitiva, quemadmodum mixtum ex vino mero. Et inclinavit ex hoc in hoc : id est, Deus pœnam suæ vindictæ effudit de uno populo in alium, puniendo perversos successive, secundum ordinem suæ justissimæ sapientiæ; verumtamen fex ejus non est exinanita : id est, fundus seu amaritudo calicis hujus non est evacuatus, quoniam divina potestas non desinit in ulciscendo. Omnia autem hæc, et quæ restant in psalmo isto, in sequenti articulo latius exponentur.
paras.en: Why God said this to them, the Prophet adds: [[74:7|For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills|Quia neque ab oriente, neque ab occidente, neque a desertis montibus]], that is, because from no part or side of the world, O Babylonians, will you be able to escape the judgment of God; and this because [[74:8|God|Deus]], who is everywhere, sees all things and is almighty, [[74:8|is the judge|judex est]]. [[74:8|One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up|Hunc humiliat, et hunc exaltat]], that is, he lowers one and raises another, as it pleases him and as men deserve; [[74:9|For in the hand of the Lord there is a cup|quia calix in manu Domini]], that is, punishment or vengeance is in the power of God: a cup, I say, [[74:9|of strong wine full of mixture|vini meri plenus mixto]] [*merum*: pure, unmixed wine]: that is, the punishment which God can pour out upon the wicked is very bitter and stinging, like a mixture made from strong wine. [[74:9|And he hath poured it out from this to that|Et inclinavit ex hoc in hoc]]: that is, God has poured out the punishment of his vengeance from one people upon another, punishing the wicked one after another, according to the order of his most just wisdom; [[74:9|but the dregs thereof are not emptied|verumtamen fex ejus non est exinanita]]: that is, the bottom or bitterness of this cup has not been drained, since the divine power does not cease from taking vengeance. But all these things, and what remains in this psalm, will be expounded more fully in the following article.

74.title: EXPOSITIO TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI QUARTI.
74.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same seventy-fourth psalm.

paras.t: Denique, juxta tropologicum sensum, prædictus titulus ita exponitur : Psalmus cantici, id est spiritualis jucunditatis, quoniam agit de remuneratione justorum, est Asaph, id est, convenit designatis per Asaph, videlicet congregationi fidelium seu Ecclesiæ : Asaph enim congregatio interpretatur. Psalmus (inquam) conscriptus, ne tu fidelis corrumpas te ipsum per superbiam ; et spem tuam, quæ est in finem, id est tendens in Christum seu vitam æternam, evacues. Specialiter autem hic psalmus superbiam detestatur, humilitatem commendat, justum Dei judicium recolit, et omnium justam remunerationem declarat.
paras.en: Next, according to the tropological sense, the aforesaid title is expounded thus: [[74:1|a psalm of a canticle|Psalmus cantici]], that is, of spiritual joy, since it treats of the reward of the just, is Asaph’s, that is, it befits those signified by Asaph, namely the congregation of the faithful, or the Church: for Asaph is interpreted ‘congregation’. A psalm (I say) written so that thou, O faithful soul, [[74:1|corrupt not|corrumpas]] thyself through pride, nor make void thy hope, which is [[74:1|unto the end|in finem]], that is, tending towards Christ, or eternal life. Now this psalm in particular detests pride, commends humility, recalls the just judgment of God, and declares the just reward of all.

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta auctor psalmi præsentis, sive ille fuerit David, sive Asaph, in persona Ecclesiæ ait : Confitebimur tibi, Deus, confitebimur. Repetitio verbi, signum est firmi propositi ardentisque desiderii. Vel, quod primo dicit, Confitebimur, referri potest ad confessionem laudis divinæ, de qua ait Salvator, Confiteor tibi, Pater : et ista confessio manet in patria, sicut inferius dicitur, Confessio et pulchritudo in conspectu ejus. Quod vero secundo repetit, Confitebimur, referri potest ad confessionem propriæ culpæ, de qua Jacobus dicit : Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra, et orate pro invicem, ut salvemini. Itaque, Confitebimur tibi, Deus, id est, te laudabimus, tuam bonitatem æternam, immensam ac puram, ore et opere glorificando, tua beneficia summa ac liberalissima, scilicet dona naturæ et gratiæ recolendo, et tibi attribuendo. Hoc modo confitetur Deo, qui cum B. Jacobo protestatur : Omne datum optimum, et omne donum perfectum desursum est, descendens a Patre luminum. Hoc enim ad commemorationem beneficiorum Dei certum est pertinere, sicut et illud quod Paulus inducit : Quid habes quod non accepisti ? Et iterum : Sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Quod vero Jacobus subdit, Apud quem non est transmutatio nec vicissitudinis obumbratio, pertinet ad recommendationem divinæ naturæ seu bonitatis secundum se. Aut enim laudamus Deum propter se ipsum ac propriam bonitatem, aut propter beneficia sua : et ad hos duos modos confitendi Domino confessione laudis, reducuntur et spectant quæcumque in sacra Scriptura ad laudem Dei dicuntur. Et invocabimus nomen tuum, id est, te ipsum ex interno affectu, ex totis præcordiis intimisque medullis precabimur, quatenus tibi grati inveniamur, in bono conservemur, proficiamus et consummemur. Laudabimus ergo te propter beneficia jam adepta, et invocabimus te propter beneficia adipiscenda, seu propter promissa obtinenda.
paras.en: So the Prophet, the author of the present psalm, whether he was David or Asaph, speaking in the person of the Church, says: [[74:2|We will praise thee, O God: we will praise|Confitebimur tibi, Deus, confitebimur]] [the Latin *confitebimur* means both ‘we will praise’ and ‘we will confess’, and Denis draws on both senses]. The repetition of the word is a sign of firm purpose and ardent desire. Or, what he says the first time, *we will confess*, can be referred to the confession of divine praise, of which the Saviour says, [[Matt 11:25|I confess to thee, O Father|Confiteor tibi, Pater]]: and this confession abides in the fatherland, as is said further on, [[Ps 95:6|Praise and beauty are before him|Confessio et pulchritudo in conspectu ejus]] [in the Latin, *Confessio*]. But what he repeats the second time, *we will confess*, can be referred to the confession of one’s own fault, of which James says: [[Jas 5:16|Confess therefore your sins one to another: and pray one for another, that you may be saved|Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra, et orate pro invicem, ut salvemini]]. Accordingly, [[74:2|We will praise thee, O God|Confitebimur tibi, Deus]], that is, we will praise thee, glorifying by mouth and deed thy goodness, eternal, immense and pure, and recalling thy highest and most liberal benefits, namely the gifts of nature and of grace, and ascribing them to thee. In this way he confesses to God who declares with Blessed James: [[Jas 1:17|Every best gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights|Omne datum optimum, et omne donum perfectum desursum est, descendens a Patre luminum]]. For this certainly belongs to the remembrance of God’s benefits, as does that which Paul brings in: [[1 Cor 4:7|what hast thou that thou hast not received|Quid habes quod non accepisti]]? And again: [[2 Cor 3:5|our sufficiency is from God|Sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]. But what James adds, [[Jas 1:17|with whom there is no change nor shadow of alteration|Apud quem non est transmutatio nec vicissitudinis obumbratio]], belongs to the commendation of the divine nature, or goodness, in itself. For either we praise God for himself and his own goodness, or for his benefits: and to these two ways of confessing to the Lord by the confession of praise is referred, and belongs, whatever is said in holy Scripture in praise of God. [[74:2|and we will call upon thy name|Et invocabimus nomen tuum]], that is, we will pray to thee thyself with inward affection, from our whole heart and inmost marrow, that we may be found pleasing to thee, be kept in good, advance and be made perfect. So we will praise thee for benefits already obtained, and call upon thee for benefits yet to be obtained, or for the promises to be won.

paras.t: Narrabimus mirabilia tua, in veteri ac novo Testamento conscripta, laudando te Deum opificem in tuis effectibus supernaturalibus. Præsertim autem narrare debemus, vel soli coram Deo, vel etiam si ratio exigit, proximis, mirabilia Dei quæ circa unumquemque nostrum operari dignatus est, peccata nostra misericorditer indulgendo, gratiam conversionis præstando, et animas nostras olim peccatrices justificando : quod est magnum mirabile Dei, quoniam (Augustino teste) majus est impium justificare, quam cœlum et terram creare. Unde legitur : Virtutes annuntietis ejus, qui de tenebris vos vocavit in admirabile lumen suum. Maxime vero narrare, incessabiliterque commemorare debemus mirabilia Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quæ ipse pro nostra salute assumpsit, fecit, ac pertulit : utpote mysteria redemptionis humanæ, incarnationem, conversationem, vitam, doctrinam, signa, passionem, resurrectionem, ascensionemque Christi. Hinc enim scriptum est : Nonne Dominus fecit sanctos enarrare omnia mirabilia sua, quæ confirmavit Dominus omnipotens stabilis in gloria sua ?
paras.en: [[74:2|We will relate thy wondrous works|Narrabimus mirabilia tua]], written in the Old and the New Testament, praising thee, God, as the maker, in thy supernatural works. But above all we ought to relate, either alone before God or, if reason requires, to our neighbours also, the wonders of God which he has deigned to work in each one of us, mercifully forgiving our sins, granting the grace of conversion, and justifying our souls, once sinful: which is a great wonder of God, since (as Augustine witnesses) it is a greater thing to justify the ungodly than to create heaven and earth. Hence we read: [[1 Pet 2:9|that you may declare his virtues, who hath called you out of darkness into his marvelous light|Virtutes annuntietis ejus, qui de tenebris vos vocavit in admirabile lumen suum]]. Most of all we ought to relate, and unceasingly call to mind, the wonders of our Lord Jesus Christ, which he took upon himself, did and endured for our salvation: such as the mysteries of man’s redemption, the incarnation, the life among men, the life, teaching, signs, passion, resurrection and ascension of Christ. For hence it is written: [[Ecclus 42:17|Hath not the Lord made the saints to declare all his wonderful works, which the Lord Almighty hath firmly settled to be established for his glory?|Nonne Dominus fecit sanctos enarrare omnia mirabilia sua, quæ confirmavit Dominus omnipotens stabilis in gloria sua]]? [the margin gives Ecclus. xliii, 17; the passage is Ecclus 42:17]

paras.t: Deinde vox Christi inducitur. Quum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo : id est, dum tempus ad judicandum Dei sapientia institutum atque præfixum advenerit, ego judicabo justitias. Quod dupliciter explanatur. Primo sic : Justitias, id est opera quæ videntur hominibus justa, ego discutiam, an sint veraciter justa, et recta intentione peracta. Nam tam districte Deus opera justorum discutiet, ut Petrus in sua Canonica dicat : Si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt ? Secundo sic : Justitias judicabo, id est, justas sententias proferam, electos judicando judicio approbationis, et reprobos judicio condemnationis. Propter quod Salomon loquitur : Qui inspector est cordis, ipse intelligit, et servatorem animæ tuæ nihil fallet, reddetque homini juxta opera sua. Oportet autem (secundum Apostolum) nos omnes manifestari ante tribunal Christi; et unumquemque nostrum Christus judicabit sigillatim in hora propriæ mortis, universaliter vero de omnibus judicabit in die novissimo. In primo quoque suo adventu accepit Christus tempus judicandi passive et miserendi, juxta illud : Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat. In secundo autem suo adventu accipiet tempus judicandi active et vindicandi, ut ait Joannes : Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique juxta opera sua. Et Daniel : Judicium sedit, et libri aperti sunt ; et ecce in nubibus cœli quasi Filius hominis veniebat.
paras.en: Then the voice of Christ is brought in: [[74:3|When I shall take a time, I will judge justices|Quum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo]]: that is, when the time for judging, appointed and fixed beforehand by the wisdom of God, shall have come, I will judge justices. This is explained in two ways. First thus: justices, that is, the works that seem just to men, I will examine, whether they be truly just and done with a right intention. For God will examine the works of the just so strictly that Peter says in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 4:18|if the just man shall scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?|Si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt]]? Secondly thus: [[74:3|I will judge justices|Justitias judicabo]], that is, I will pronounce just sentences, judging the elect with the judgment of approval and the reprobate with the judgment of condemnation. Wherefore Solomon says: [[Prov 24:12|he that seeth into the heart, he understandeth, and nothing deceiveth the keeper of thy soul, and he shall render to a man according to his works|Qui inspector est cordis, ipse intelligit, et servatorem animæ tuæ nihil fallet, reddetque homini juxta opera sua]]. And (according to the Apostle) [[2 Cor 5:10|we must all be manifested before the judgment seat of Christ|nos omnes manifestari ante tribunal Christi]]; and Christ will judge each one of us singly in the hour of his own death, but all men together on the last day. In his first coming, too, Christ took the time of judging passively [that is, of being judged] and of showing mercy, according to that: [[Luke 19:10|the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost|Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat]]. But in his second coming he will take the time of judging actively and of taking vengeance, as John says: [[Apoc 22:12|Behold, I come quickly: and my reward is with me, to render to every, man according to his works|Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique juxta opera sua]]. And Daniel: [[Dan 7:10|the judgment sat, and the books were opened|Judicium sedit, et libri aperti sunt]]; [[Dan 7:13|and lo, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven|et ecce in nubibus cœli quasi Filius hominis veniebat]].

paras.t: Sed quam terribile erit illud judicium, pandit Propheta, subdendo : Liquefacta est terra, et omnes qui habitant in ea. Nam ante finale judicium terra et aer igne conflagrationis accendentur ac purgabuntur, hominesque tunc viventes, timore ad instar plumbi liquescent et dissolventur, prout Salvator ait : Erunt signa in sole et luna et stellis, et in terris pressura gentium, arescentibus hominibus præ timore et expectatione, quæ supervenient universo orbi. De hac terræ liquefactione futura in die judicii, de qua nunc loquitur Propheta per modum præteriti, secundum consuetudinem prophetiæ, ait beatissimus Petrus : Adveniet dies Domini tanquam fur, in quo cæli (supple, aerii) magno impetu transient, elementa vero calore solventur ; terra autem et quæ in ipsa sunt opera, exurentur. Isaias quoque : Ecce, inquit, dies Domini veniet crudelis et indignationis plenus, et iræ furorisque, ad ponendam terram in solitudinem, et peccatores ejus conterendos de ea. Ego Dominus confirmavi columnas ejus : id est, justos et viros perfectos, qui erunt circa finem mundi, tempore Antichristi, confirmabo et conservabo in gratia, ne in tantis persecutionibus atque terroribus deficiendo frangantur et cadant. Erit enim tunc tribulatio magna, qualis non fuit ab initio mundi usque modo, neque fiet. Et nisi breviati fuissent dies illi, non fieret salva omnis caro ; sed propter electos breviabuntur dies illi. Possunt quoque nomine columnarum intelligi sancti Apostoli, quos Christus post resurrectionem confirmavit in fide. Dicuntur vero viri perfecti, sapientes et sancti, columnæ mundi atque Ecclesiæ, quia per preces, doctrinas et exempla eorum, alii sustentantur.
paras.en: But how terrible that judgment will be, the Prophet shows by adding: [[74:4|The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein|Liquefacta est terra, et omnes qui habitant in ea]]. For before the final judgment the earth and the air will be kindled and purged by the fire of the conflagration, and the men then living will melt and dissolve with fear like lead, as the Saviour says: [[Luke 21:25|there shall be signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations|Erunt signa in sole et luna et stellis, et in terris pressura gentium]], [[Luke 21:26|Men withering away for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world|arescentibus hominibus præ timore et expectatione, quæ supervenient universo orbi]]. Of this melting of the earth that is to come on the day of judgment, of which the Prophet now speaks as of something past, after the custom of prophecy, most blessed Peter says: [[2 Pet 3:10|the day of the Lord shall come as a thief, in which the heavens|Adveniet dies Domini tanquam fur, in quo cæli]] (understand: of the air) [[2 Pet 3:10|shall pass away with great violence and the elements shall be melted with heat and the earth and the works which are in it shall be burnt up|magno impetu transient, elementa vero calore solventur ; terra autem et quæ in ipsa sunt opera, exurentur]]. Isaias too: [[Is 13:9|Behold|Ecce]], he says, [[Is 13:9|the day of the Lord shall come, a cruel day, and full of indignation, and of wrath, and fury, to lay the land desolate, and to destroy the sinners thereof out of it|dies Domini veniet crudelis et indignationis plenus, et iræ furorisque, ad ponendam terram in solitudinem, et peccatores ejus conterendos de ea]]. [[74:4|I have established the pillars thereof|Ego Dominus confirmavi columnas ejus]] [Denis reads ‘I the Lord have established’]: that is, the just and perfect men who will live about the end of the world, in the time of Antichrist, I will strengthen and preserve in grace, lest in such great persecutions and terrors they fail and are broken and fall. [[Matt 24:21|For there shall be then great tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the world until now, neither shall be|Erit enim tunc tribulatio magna, qualis non fuit ab initio mundi usque modo, neque fiet]]. [[Matt 24:22|And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh should be saved: but for the sake of the elect those days shall be shortened|Et nisi breviati fuissent dies illi, non fieret salva omnis caro ; sed propter electos breviabuntur dies illi]]. By the name of pillars may also be understood the holy Apostles, whom Christ after his resurrection strengthened in faith. And perfect men, wise and holy, are called pillars of the world and of the Church, because by their prayers, teachings and examples others are upheld.

paras.t: Dixi ego Christus per me ipsum, per Prophetas, per Apostolos, aliosque electos, iniquis : Nolite inique agere. Unde in Evangelio scriptum est : Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum. Et Isaias : Lavamini, mundi estote, auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis; discite bene agere, quærite judicium, subvenite oppresso. Dixi et delinquentibus, id est legem divinam prævaricantibus : Nolite exaltare cornu, id est, nolite vos ipsos jactare, nolite per superbiam intumescere et Deo repugnare. Hinc quippe scriptum est : Juravit Dominus in anima sua, Detestor ego superbiam. Et ad superbos ibidem ait : Væ qui dicitis, Numquid non in fortitudine nostra assumpsimus nobis cornua?
paras.en: [[74:5|I said|Dixi]], I Christ, by myself, by the Prophets, by the Apostles and the other elect, [[74:5|to the wicked: Do not act wickedly|iniquis : Nolite inique agere]]. Hence it is written in the Gospel: [[Matt 3:2|Do penance: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand|Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum]][[Matt 4:17||]]. And Isaias: [[Is 1:16|Wash yourselves, be clean, take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Lavamini, mundi estote, auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]]; [[Is 1:17|Learn to do well: seek judgment, relieve the oppressed|discite bene agere, quærite judicium, subvenite oppresso]]. [[74:5|I said|Dixi]] [[74:5|and to the sinners|et delinquentibus]], that is, to those who transgress the divine law: [[74:5|Lift not up the horn|Nolite exaltare cornu]], that is, do not boast of yourselves, do not swell with pride and resist God. For hence it is written: [[Amos 6:8|The Lord God hath sworn by his own soul|Juravit Dominus in anima sua]]: [[Amos 6:8|I detest the pride|Detestor ego superbiam]]. And to the proud he says in the same place: Woe, [[Amos 6:14|you that say: Have we not taken unto us horns by our own strength?|qui dicitis, Numquid non in fortitudine nostra assumpsimus nobis cornua?]]? [the margin gives Ibid. i, 14; the verse is Amos 6:14]

paras.t: Nolite extollere in altum cornu vestrum : id est, animum vestrum magnificum nolite ultra mensuram erigere ; sed facite quod docet princeps Apostolorum, Humiliamini sub potenti manu Dei, ut vos exaltet in tempore visitationis ; et quod in Ecclesiastico scriptum est, Quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus, et coram Deo invenies gratiam, etc. In altum extulerunt cornu suum, quibus Moyses dicit : Multum erigimini, filii Levi. Et Michæas : Hæc dicit Dominus : Ecce ego cogito super familiam istam malum; et non ambulabitis superbi, quoniam tempus pessimum est. Nolite loqui adversus Deum iniquitatem, laudando, amando et operando quod ille vituperat, odit et prohibet. Nolite peccata vestra palliare, excusare, defendere. Nolite contra prælatos vestros murmurare, aut vestra peccata in Creatorem retorquere, dicendo vos propter constellationem, dispositionem fatalem seu naturalem non posse peccata effugere.
paras.en: [[74:6|Lift not up your horn on high|Nolite extollere in altum cornu vestrum]]: that is, do not raise your proud spirit beyond measure; but do what the prince of the Apostles teaches, [[1 Pet 5:6|Be you humbled therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in the time of visitation|Humiliamini sub potenti manu Dei, ut vos exaltet in tempore visitationis]]; and what is written in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 3:20|The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things, and thou shalt find grace before God|Quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus, et coram Deo invenies gratiam]], etc. They lifted up their horn on high to whom Moses says: [[Num 16:7|you take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi|Multum erigimini, filii Levi]] [in the Latin, ‘you lift yourselves up too much’]. And Micheas: [[Mich 2:3|thus saith the Lord: Behold I devise an evil against this family|Hæc dicit Dominus : Ecce ego cogito super familiam istam malum]]; [[Mich 2:3|and you shall not walk haughtily, for this is a very evil time|et non ambulabitis superbi, quoniam tempus pessimum est]]. [[74:6|speak not iniquity against God|Nolite loqui adversus Deum iniquitatem]], by praising, loving and doing what he blames, hates and forbids. Do not cloak your sins, excuse them, defend them. Do not murmur against your prelates, nor turn your sins back upon the Creator, saying that because of the stars, or a disposition of fate or of nature, you cannot escape sin.

paras.t: Quia neque ab oriente, neque ab occidente, neque a desertis montibus poteritis evadere aut latere, quoniam Deus judex est : qui de se ipso apud Jeremiam asserit, Ego sum judex et testis ; et alibi per eumdem Prophetam fatetur : Si occultabitur vir in absconditis suis, et ego non videbo eum? dicit Dominus. Unde et per Malachiam Deus locutus est : Accedam ad vos in judicio, et ero testis velox maleficis. Hunc superbum Deus humiliat; et hunc, id est humilem, exaltat : sicut in Evangelio ait, Omnis qui se exaltat, humiliabitur, et qui se humiliat, exaltabitur. Præterea in præsenti Deus quosdam temporaliter exaltat, promovendo eos ad statum sublimem, et quosdam humiliat, privando eos pristino statu, potestate seu regno : ut patet de Babyloniis quos dejecit per Medos ac Persas, et de Medis ac Persis quos dejecit per Græcos, et de Græcis quos dejecit per Romanos. Et hoc agit Deus omnipotens omnium moderator regnorum, secundum ordinem suæ justitiæ. Propter quod apud Danielem scriptum est : Sit nomen Domini benedictum, quoniam ipse mutat tempora et ætates, transfert regna atque constituit. Et primo Regum : Arcus fortium superatus est, et infirmi accincti sunt robore. Dominus pauperem facit et ditat, humiliat et sublevat. Suscitat de pulvere egenum, ut sedeat cum principibus, etc. Et Ecclesiasticus : Sedes ducum superborum destruxit Deus, et sedere fecit mites pro eis. Quod expertus Nabuchodonosor ait : Juxta voluntatem suam facit, tam in virtutibus cœli, quam in habitatoribus terræ ; et non est qui resistat vultui ejus.
paras.en: [[74:7|For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills|Quia neque ab oriente, neque ab occidente, neque a desertis montibus]] will you be able to escape or lie hidden, [[74:8|For God is the judge|quoniam Deus judex est]]: who says of himself in Jeremias, [[Jer 29:23|I am the judge and the witness|Ego sum judex et testis]] [the margin gives Jer. xxiii, 23; the words are at Jer 29:23]; and elsewhere he declares by the same Prophet: [[Jer 23:24|Shall a man be hid in secret places, and I not see him, saith the Lord|Si occultabitur vir in absconditis suis, et ego non videbo eum? dicit Dominus]]? Hence God has also spoken by Malachias: [[Mal 3:5|I will come to you in judgment, and will be a speedy witness against sorcerers|Accedam ad vos in judicio, et ero testis velox maleficis]]. [[74:8|One he putteth down|Hunc superbum Deus humiliat]] (God humbles the proud), [[74:8|and another|et hunc]] (that is, the humble) [[74:8|he lifteth up|exaltat]]: as he says in the Gospel, [[Luke 14:11|every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled: and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted|Omnis qui se exaltat, humiliabitur, et qui se humiliat, exaltabitur]][[Luke 18:14||]]. Moreover, in this present life God exalts some in temporal things, promoting them to high estate, and humbles others, depriving them of their former estate, power or kingdom: as is plain from the Babylonians, whom he cast down by the Medes and Persians[[Dan 5:28||]], and from the Medes and Persians, whom he cast down by the Greeks, and from the Greeks, whom he cast down by the Romans. And this God almighty, the ruler of all kingdoms, does according to the order of his justice. Wherefore it is written in Daniel: [[Dan 2:20|Blessed be the name of the Lord|Sit nomen Domini benedictum]], for [[Dan 2:21|he changeth times and ages: taketh away kingdoms, and establisheth them|ipse mutat tempora et ætates, transfert regna atque constituit]]. And in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 2:4|The bow of the mighty is overcome, and the weak are girt with strength.|Arcus fortium superatus est, et infirmi accincti sunt robore.]] [[1 Kings 2:7|The Lord maketh poor and maketh rich, he humbleth and he exalteth:|Dominus pauperem facit et ditat, humiliat et sublevat.]] [[1 Kings 2:8|He raiseth up the needy from the dust|Suscitat de pulvere egenum]], [[1 Kings 2:8|that he may sit with princes|ut sedeat cum principibus]], etc. And Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:17|God hath overturned the thrones of proud princes, and hath set up the meek in their stead.|Sedes ducum superborum destruxit Deus, et sedere fecit mites pro eis.]] Which Nabuchodonosor, having learned it by experience, says: [[Dan 4:32|he doth according to his will, as well with the powers of heaven, as among the inhabitants of the earth: and there is none that can resist his hand|Juxta voluntatem suam facit, tam in virtutibus cœli, quam in habitatoribus terræ ; et non est qui resistat vultui ejus]] [Denis reads *vultui*, ‘face’, where the Vulgate has *manui*, ‘hand’].

paras.t: Quia calix in manu Domini. Per calicem Scriptura significat passionem seu pœnam, secundum quod Christus ait ad Patrem, Transfer calicem istum a me ; et ad filios Zebedæi, Calicem meum bibetis. Calix ergo in manu Domini, est pœna in divina potestate consistens, qua Deus potest reddere injustis tormenta. Est autem hic calix vini meri plenus mixto, id est repletus varietate diversarum pœnarum, sicut superius dictum est : Pluit super peccatores laqueos ; ignis, sulfur et spiritus procellarum, pars calicis eorum. Per vinum merum intelligit amarum saporem, seu gustum austerum, quem sentiunt peccatores ex inflictione ultionis divinæ. Alii ita exponunt : Calix, id est mensura retributionis, est in manu Domini judicis mundi : calix, inquam, vini meri, id est puri vini, per quod signatur retributio electorum in patria, in quibus nihil invenitur tristitiæ. Et calix iste est plenus mixto, id est commixtione tristitiæ et consolationis, quantum ad viatores : in quibus cum consolatione interna divinitus inspirata, miscetur tribulatio carnis seu alia quælibet pœna. In electis enim nunc miscentur virga et baculus Dei, id est correctio pœnalis et sustentatio consolativa. Vel dicitur calix iste plenus mixto, id est temperamento misericordiæ atque justitiæ : quæ in omni opere Dei contemperantur, juxta illud, Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas.
paras.en: [[74:9|For in the hand of the Lord there is a cup|Quia calix in manu Domini]]. By the cup Scripture signifies suffering or punishment, according as Christ says to the Father, [[Luke 22:42|remove this chalice from me|Transfer calicem istum a me]], and to the sons of Zebedee, [[Matt 20:23|My chalice indeed you shall drink|Calicem meum bibetis]] [the margin gives Matth. xx, 22 and 23; the words are in v. 23]. The cup in the hand of the Lord, then, is the punishment that lies in the divine power, by which God can render torments to the unjust. And this cup is [[74:9|of strong wine full of mixture|vini meri plenus mixto]], that is, filled with a variety of different punishments, as was said above: [[Ps 10:7|He shall rain snares upon sinners: fire and brimstone, and storms of winds, shall be the portion of their cup|Pluit super peccatores laqueos ; ignis, sulfur et spiritus procellarum, pars calicis eorum]]. By strong wine [*vinum merum*: pure, unmixed wine] he means the bitter savour, or harsh taste, which sinners feel from the infliction of divine vengeance. Others expound it thus: [[74:9|a cup|Calix]], that is, the measure of retribution, is [[74:9|in the hand of the Lord|in manu Domini]], the judge of the world: a cup, I say, [[74:9|of strong wine|vini meri]], that is, of pure wine, by which is signified the retribution of the elect in the fatherland, in whom no sadness is found. And this cup is [[74:9|full of mixture|plenus mixto]], that is, of a mingling of sadness and consolation, as regards wayfarers [that is, those still on their way, in this life]: in whom, with the inward consolation inspired by God, is mingled tribulation of the flesh or some other punishment. For in the elect the rod and the staff of God are now mingled, that is, correction that punishes and support that consoles. Or this cup is said to be full of mixture, that is, of a tempering of mercy and justice, which are tempered together in every work of God, according to that: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxiv, 10; the verse is Ps 24:10].

paras.t: Et inclinavit ex hoc in hoc : id est, ipse Dominus omnium justus judex, calicem suum effudit de uno populo in alium, flagellando paulatim unum per alium, sicut flagellavit Hebræos per Chaldæos, et Chaldæos per Medos, Medos quoque per Græcos, et Græcos atque Assyrios per Italicos. Vel : Inclinavit ex hoc in hoc, id est, Deus ex calice seu mensura consolationis, effudit in calicem afflictionis, et econverso, per hoc quod in viatoribus miscet consolationem tentationi seu afflictioni, et vice versa. Verumtamen fæx ejus non est exinanita : id est, inferior potus calicis Domini, scilicet pœna sine consolatione, non defecit : quoniam pœna inferni, quæ omni caret solatio, et nomine fæcis exprimitur, nunquam finitur. Bibent de hac fæce, omnes peccatores terræ, qui modo non pœnitent, quia æternaliter damnabuntur. Unde alio loco scriptum est : Malus de furore Omnipotentis bibet. Ista fæx calicis Domini, est fel atque absinthium de quibus Dominus apud Jeremiam protestatur, Ecce ego cibabo eos absinthio, et potabo eos felle.
paras.en: [[74:9|And he hath poured it out from this to that|Et inclinavit ex hoc in hoc]]: that is, the Lord himself, the just judge of all, has poured out his cup from one people upon another, scourging one by another little by little, as he scourged the Hebrews by the Chaldeans, and the Chaldeans by the Medes, the Medes too by the Greeks, and the Greeks and Assyrians by the Italians. Or: [[74:9|And he hath poured it out from this to that|Inclinavit ex hoc in hoc]], that is, God has poured from the cup or measure of consolation into the cup of affliction, and the reverse, in that in wayfarers he mingles consolation with temptation or affliction, and the other way about. [[74:9|but the dregs thereof are not emptied|Verumtamen fæx ejus non est exinanita]]: that is, the lowest draught of the Lord’s cup, namely punishment without consolation, has not run out: for the pain of hell, which lacks all comfort and is expressed by the name of dregs, never ends. [[74:9|shall drink|Bibent]] of these dregs [[74:9|all the sinners of the earth|omnes peccatores terræ]], those who do not now repent, for they will be damned eternally. Hence it is written in another place: The wicked man [[Job 21:20|shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty|de furore Omnipotentis bibet]]. These dregs of the Lord’s cup are the gall and wormwood of which the Lord declares in Jeremias: [[Jer 23:15|Behold I will feed them with wormwood, and will give them gall to drink|Ecce ego cibabo eos absinthio, et potabo eos felle]].

paras.t: Deinde Ecclesia, seu quilibet justus, de sua illuminatione et correctione Domino gratias agere cupiens, ait : Ego autem annuntiabo beneficia Dei et laudes ejus, in sæculum, id est perseveranter, quamdiu sum ; cantabo cum mentali lætitia, Deo Jacob, id est cujuslibet hominis vitia supplantantis. Eorum enim qui vitia supplantare non cessant, Deus proprie Deus vocatur. Jacob autem interpretatur supplantator.
paras.en: Then the Church, or any just man, desiring to give thanks to the Lord for his enlightenment and correction, says: [[74:10|But I will declare|Ego autem annuntiabo]] the benefits of God and his praises [[74:10|for ever|in sæculum]], that is, perseveringly, as long as I live; [[74:10|I will sing|cantabo]] with gladness of mind [[74:10|to the God of Jacob|Deo Jacob]], that is, of any man who supplants vices. For of those who never cease to supplant vices, God is properly called the God. And Jacob is interpreted ‘supplanter’.

paras.t: Sequitur autem vox Christi. Et omnia cornua peccatorum confringam, id est, omnes dignitates et exaltationes superborum et impiorum dejiciam, maxime in die novissimo : juxta quod in Isaia scriptum est, Visitabo super orbis mala, et requiescere faciam superbiam infidelium ; et apud Osee : Gloriam eorum in ignominiam commutabo. Et exaltabuntur cornua, id est virtutes et alta fiducia contemplatioque sublimis, justi : quoniam quidquid perfectionis jam invenitur in homine justo, hoc post mortem in patria vehementer perficitur, atque æterno honore præmiatur ; et in die judicii, justi anima et corpore super omnem cœlorum mobilium altitudinem locabuntur.
paras.en: Then follows the voice of Christ: [[74:11|And I will break all the horns of sinners|Et omnia cornua peccatorum confringam]], that is, I will cast down all the dignities and exaltations of the proud and the ungodly, above all on the last day: according to what is written in Isaias, [[Is 13:11|I will visit the evils of the world|Visitabo super orbis mala]], [[Is 13:11|and I will make the pride of infidels to cease|et requiescere faciam superbiam infidelium]]; and in Osee: [[Osee 4:7|I will change their glory into shame|Gloriam eorum in ignominiam commutabo]]. [[74:11|but the horns|Et exaltabuntur cornua]], that is, the virtues and high confidence and sublime contemplation, [[74:11|of the just shall be exalted|justi]]: since whatever perfection is already found in the just man is after death perfected exceedingly in the fatherland, and rewarded with everlasting honour; and on the day of judgment the just will be set, in soul and body, above all the height of the moving heavens.

paras.t: Agamus ergo quod in præsenti psalmo cantamus, Dei laudibus insistendo, nostra vitia recolendo, atque præ omnibus et in omnibus omnem superbiam abhorrendo, veramque humilitatem incessabili studio amplectendo, quoniam Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam. Ipse quoque summus et unicus noster magister : Discite, inquit, a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde. Odibilis enim (teste Scriptura) coram Deo et hominibus est superbia. Propter quod bonus pater filium instruens, ait : Superbiam nunquam in tuo animo, aut in verbo tuo dominari permittas ; in ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio. Et in libro beati Job dicitur : Vir vanus in superbiam erigitur, et tanquam pullum onagri se liberum natum putat. Porro ipsemet Christus humilitatem nos ultimo docuit verbo et opere, in Cœna novissima discipulorum pedes lavando, eisque dicendo : Qui major est in vobis, fiat sicut minor ; et qui præcessor, sicut ministrator.
paras.en: Let us therefore do what we sing in the present psalm: persevering in the praises of God, calling our vices to mind, and before all things and in all things abhorring all pride, and embracing true humility with unceasing zeal, since [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble|Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]]. He too, our highest and only master, says: [[Matt 11:29|learn|Discite]], he says, [[Matt 11:29|of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]. For [[Ecclus 10:7|Pride is hateful|Odibilis]] (as Scripture witnesses) [[Ecclus 10:7|before God and men|coram Deo et hominibus est superbia]]. Wherefore a good father, instructing his son, says: [[Tob 4:14|Never suffer pride to reign in thy mind, or in thy words: for from it all perdition took its beginning|Superbiam nunquam in tuo animo, aut in verbo tuo dominari permittas ; in ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio]]. And in the book of blessed Job it is said: [[Job 11:12|A vain man is lifted up into pride, and thinketh himself born free like a wild ass's colt.|Vir vanus in superbiam erigitur, et tanquam pullum onagri se liberum natum putat]] Moreover Christ himself taught us humility last of all by word and deed, at the Last Supper, washing the disciples’ feet and saying to them: [[Luke 22:26|he that is the greater among you, let him become as the younger: and he that is the leader, as he that serveth|Qui major est in vobis, fiat sicut minor ; et qui præcessor, sicut ministrator]].

paras.t: Precatio. Singulari pœnitentia, Domine, confitemur tibi, confitemur ; peccatis nostris propitiare, ut percepta indulgentia, dignos nos efficias sancti nominis tui invocatione : ut pro salute nostra in sæculum tibi Deo Jacob cantemus in gaudio et exsultatione.
paras.en: Prayer. With singular penitence, O Lord, we confess to thee, we confess: be merciful to our sins, that, having received pardon, thou mayest make us worthy of the invocation of thy holy name; that for our salvation we may sing for ever to thee, the God of Jacob, in joy and exultation.

75.title: EXPLANATIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI QUINTI : NOTUS IN JUDÆA DEUS.
75.title_en: Literal explanation of the seventy-fifth psalm: In Judea God is known.

paras.t: Præterea titulus psalmi præsentis est : In finem, in carminibus, psalmus Asaph, canticum ad Assyrios. Psalmus nunc declarandus, secundum doctores Hebræos atque catholicos, ad litteram loquitur de admiranda victoria populi Judæorum tempore Ezechiæ, quam Deus contulit eis de Assyriis, quando percussit angelus Domini in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia hominum : quo viso, fugit Sennacherib. Hanc ergo liberationem prænoscens in spiritu auctor psalmi præsentis, fecit hunc psalmum, cujus titulus ita exponitur : Psalmus præsens, in finem, id est in Christum nos dirigens, in laudibus, quoniam continet laudem Dei, quam decantando in Deum dirigimur, est ipsius Asaph, vel sicut auctoris secundum quosdam, vel sicut cantoris ; vel, Asaph, id est Synagogæ, tanquam pro ejus ædificatione conscriptus : et est canticum, id est spiritualem exsultationem includens, scriptum ad Assyrios conterendos, id est de Assyriorum dejectione pertractans.
paras.en: Moreover, the title of the present psalm is: [[75:1|Unto the end|In finem]], in songs [the print reads *in carminibus*, "in songs", with the variant *laudibus* in the margin; the Vulgate has *in laudibus*, "in praises"], [[75:1|a psalm for Asaph: a canticle to the Assyrians|psalmus Asaph, canticum ad Assyrios]]. The psalm now to be explained, according to the Hebrew and the Catholic doctors, speaks literally of the wonderful victory of the people of the Jews in the time of Ezechias, which God gave them over the Assyrians, when the angel of the Lord slew in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand men; at the sight of which Sennacherib fled[[4 Kings 19:35||]][[2 Par 32:21||]][[Is 37:36||]]. Foreseeing this deliverance in spirit, then, the author of the present psalm made this psalm, whose title is explained thus: the present psalm, [[75:1|Unto the end|in finem]], that is, directing us to Christ, [[75:1|in praises|in laudibus]], because it contains the praise of God, by singing which we are directed to God, is [[75:1|for Asaph|Asaph]] himself, either as its author, according to some, or as its singer; or, *Asaph*, that is, of the Synagogue, as written for its edification; and it is [[75:1|a canticle|canticum]], that is, containing spiritual exultation, written [[75:1|to the Assyrians|ad Assyrios]] to crush them, that is, treating of the overthrow of the Assyrians.

paras.t: Ait ergo : Notus in Judæa, id est in terra et populo Judæorum, Deus: Aliis namque nationibus ad idololatriam declinantibus, permansit in populo Judæorum cultus unius veri summique Dei. In Israel magnum nomen ejus. Per Israel eosdem designat, quos per Judæam, quia Judæi erant filii Jacob, qui dictus est Israel. Vel per Israel specialiter exprimit decem tribus, quæ tempore Ezechiæ nondum translatæ erant : et quamvis illæ pro majori parte ad idololatriam essent conversæ, adorantes vitulos aureos, quos fecit Jeroboam ; multi tamen manserunt in populo illo Deum verum colentes, quorum unus erat Tobias, ut patet in libro Tobiæ. Unde scriptum est : Dixit Dominus ad Eliam, Dereliqui mihi in Israel septem millia virorum, quorum genua non sunt curvata ante Baal. Sic ergo, In Judæa, id est in populo tribus Juda et Benjamin, inter quos etiam morabantur Levitæ, quoniam Jeroboam fecit sibi sacerdotes de extremis populorum ; et item, In Israel, id est in populo decem tribuum credente et Deum colente, magnum fuit nomen ejus, scilicet Dei, quoniam magnitudinem Dei noverunt, et Deus eis ostendit potentiam suam et magnificentiam, tam mirabiliter occidendo Assyrios. Dicitur enim nomen alicujus magnum illic, ubi magna ejus virtus ostenditur, et ipse clare cognoscitur. Et horum veritas liquet ex eo, quod Moyses ait populo isti : Te elegit Dominus Deus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram ; et rursus : Ecce ostendit nobis Dominus Deus noster majestatem et magnitudinem suam.
paras.en: He says, then: [[75:2|In Judea|Notus in Judæa]], that is, in the land and people of the Jews, [[75:2|God is known|Deus]]: for while other nations turned aside to idolatry, the worship of the one true and supreme God remained among the people of the Jews. [[75:2|his name is great in Israel|In Israel magnum nomen ejus]]. By *Israel* he means the same as by *Judea*, for the Jews were the sons of Jacob, who was called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]]. Or by *Israel* he expresses in particular the ten tribes, which in the time of Ezechias had not yet been carried away; and although for the greater part they had turned to idolatry, worshipping the golden calves that Jeroboam made, yet many remained among that people who worshipped the true God, one of whom was Tobias, as is plain in the book of Tobias[[Tob 1:5||]][[Tob 1:6||]]. Hence it is written: The Lord said to Elias, [[3 Kings 19:18|I will leave me seven thousand men in Israel, whose knees have not been bowed before Baal|Dereliqui mihi in Israel septem millia virorum, quorum genua non sunt curvata ante Baal]][[Rom 11:4||]]. So then, [[75:2|In Judea|In Judæa]], that is, among the people of the tribes of Juda and Benjamin, among whom the Levites also dwelt, since Jeroboam made himself [[3 Kings 12:31|priests of the lowest of the people|sacerdotes de extremis populorum]]; and again, [[75:2|in Israel|In Israel]], that is, among the people of the ten tribes that believed and worshipped God, [[75:2|his name is great|magnum fuit nomen ejus]], that is, God's, because they knew the greatness of God, and God showed them his power and magnificence in slaying the Assyrians so wonderfully. For someone's name is said to be great in the place where his great power is shown and he himself is clearly known. And the truth of these things is plain from what Moses says to this people: [[Deut 7:6|The Lord thy God hath chosen thee, to be his peculiar people of all peoples that are upon the earth|Te elegit Dominus Deus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram]]; and again: [[Deut 5:24|Behold the Lord our God hath shewn us his majesty and his greatness|Ecce ostendit nobis Dominus Deus noster majestatem et magnitudinem suam]].

paras.t: Et factus est in pace locus ejus : id est, terra Judææ, quæ impugnabatur a rege Assyriorum, pacem adepta est, occiso regis exercitu ; et habitatio ejus, scilicet Dei, facta est in Sion, id est in templo, in monte Sion constructo. Reddita namque pace, rex piissimus Ezechias cum sacerdotibus et populo devotissime Deo gratias retulit atque servivit in templo ; et sic Deus per gratiam magnam habitavit in templo suo : secundum quod Habacuc ait, Dominus in templo sancto suo.
paras.en: [[75:3|And his place is in peace|Et factus est in pace locus ejus]]: that is, the land of Judea, which was being attacked by the king of the Assyrians, obtained peace when the king's army was slain; [[75:3|and his abode|et habitatio ejus]], that is, God's, was established [[75:3|in Sion|in Sion]], that is, in the temple built on mount Sion. For when peace was restored, the most pious king Ezechias with the priests and the people most devoutly gave thanks to God and served him in the temple[[2 Par 29:1||]][[2 Par 30:1||]] [the margin reads "II Par. xxx et xxx", presumably for chapters 29 and 30]; and thus God by great grace dwelt in his temple, according to what Habacuc says: [[Hab 2:20|the Lord is in his holy temple|Dominus in templo sancto suo]].

paras.t: Ibi, videlicet in terra Judææ, Dominus confregit potentias arcuum, scutum et gladium, id est omnia bellica instrumenta Assyriorum, et bellum, id est bellatores regis Sennacherib. Vel, Bellum, id est prælium ejus, dissipavit. Confregit autem Deus hæc bellica instrumenta, impediendo ea ab actu per interfectionem bellatorum ; vel ipsi Judæi confregerunt hæc arma pro magna parte, sicut et cetera spolia.
paras.en: [[75:4|There|Ibi]], that is, in the land of Judea, [[75:4|hath he broken the powers of bows|confregit potentias arcuum]], namely the Lord, [[75:4|the shield, the sword|scutum et gladium]], that is, all the weapons of war of the Assyrians, [[75:4|and the battle|et bellum]], that is, the warriors of king Sennacherib. Or, *the battle*, that is, he scattered his battle. Now God broke these weapons of war by keeping them from use through the slaying of the warriors; or the Jews themselves broke these arms for the most part, as they did the rest of the spoils.

paras.t: Illuminans tu mirabiliter, id est, lucem miserationum tuarum mirabili pietate nobis immittens atque infundens, a montibus æternis, id est ab angelis sanctis : qui dicuntur montes æterni, quoniam sublimes sunt et immortales. Ab his Deus Judæos mirabiliter illustravit, quoniam per preces atque ministeria angelorum Judæos custodientium, Deus concessit istam victoriam. Quamvis etenim scriptum sit, Egressus est autem angelus Domini, et percussit in castris Assyriorum, etc., credendum est tamen, quod angeli singuli singulos Judæos sigillatim custodientes, orabant Deum pro illo triumpho.
paras.en: [[75:5|Thou enlightenest wonderfully|Illuminans tu mirabiliter]], that is, sending and pouring into us the light of thy mercies with wonderful kindness, [[75:5|from the everlasting hills|a montibus æternis]], that is, from the holy angels, who are called everlasting hills because they are lofty and immortal. From them God wonderfully enlightened the Jews, since it was through the prayers and ministries of the angels who guarded the Jews that God granted this victory. For although it is written, [[Is 37:36|And the angel of the Lord went out and slew in the camp of the Assyrians|Egressus est autem angelus Domini, et percussit in castris Assyriorum]], etc.[[4 Kings 19:35||]], yet it is to be believed that the angels, each guarding one of the Jews individually, prayed God for that triumph.

paras.t: Turbati sunt omnes insipientes corde : id est, ministri perversi et perfidi regis, videlicet Assyrii idola honorantes, corde perterriti sunt et corpore interfecti per gladium angeli. Vel, Omnes insipientes corde turbati dicuntur, quoniam gentes in circuitu Judææ morantes, audita dejectione Sennacherib, obstupuerunt de tam admirabili plaga. Unde etiam longo post tempore dum Nabuchodonosor obsideret Jerusalem, non putabant gentes vicinæ Judææ, quod Nabuchodonosor prævaleret, propter memoriam dejectionis Sennacherib. Propter quod Jeremias ait in Threnis : Non crediderunt reges terræ, quod ingrederetur hostis per portas Jerusalem. Dicitur quoque illuminatio ista mirabiliter facta, quoniam corpora Assyriorum fuerunt redacta in cineres.
paras.en: [[75:6|All the foolish of heart were troubled|Turbati sunt omnes insipientes corde]]: that is, the servants of the perverse and faithless king, namely the Assyrians who honoured idols, were terrified in heart and slain in body by the sword of the angel. Or, [[75:6|all the foolish of heart|Omnes insipientes corde]] are said to be [[75:6|troubled|turbati]], because the nations dwelling round about Judea, when they heard of the overthrow of Sennacherib, were astounded at so wonderful a stroke. Hence also, long afterwards, when Nabuchodonosor was besieging Jerusalem, the nations neighbouring Judea did not think that Nabuchodonosor would prevail, because of the memory of the overthrow of Sennacherib. Therefore Jeremias says in the Lamentations: [[Lam 4:12|The kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world would not have believed, that the adversary and the enemy should enter in by the gates of Jerusalem|Non crediderunt reges terræ, quod ingrederetur hostis per portas Jerusalem]]. This enlightening is also said to have been done [[75:5|wonderfully|mirabiliter]], because the bodies of the Assyrians were reduced to ashes.

paras.t: Dormierunt Assyrii divina virtute occisi, somnum suum, id est somnum mortis : a quo nemo suscitat, nisi Deus ; et nihil invenerunt omnes viri divitiarum in manibus suis : id est, prædicti Assyrii qui divites erant propter spolia, quæ in multis terris a se vastatis collegerant, quum essent occisi, nullum habuerunt subsidium aut profectum ex suis divitiis ; sed opera eorum sequebantur eos, non autem divitiæ, sicut superius de divite dictum est : Quoniam quum interierit, non sumet omnia ; neque descendet cum eo gloria ejus.
paras.en: [[75:6|They have slept|Dormierunt]], namely the Assyrians slain by the divine power, [[75:6|their sleep|somnum suum]], that is, the sleep of death, from which no one awakens but God; [[75:6|and all the men of riches have found nothing in their hands|et nihil invenerunt omnes viri divitiarum in manibus suis]]: that is, the aforesaid Assyrians, who were rich because of the spoils which they had gathered in the many lands they had laid waste, when they were slain had no help or profit from their riches; but [[Apoc 14:13|their works follow them|opera eorum sequebantur eos]], and not their riches, as was said above of the rich man: [[Ps 48:18|For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; nor shall his glory descend with him|Quoniam quum interierit, non sumet omnia ; neque descendet cum eo gloria ejus]].

paras.t: Ab increpatione tua, id est a districta tua ultione, o Deus Jacob patriarchæ, qui dicis : Ego sum Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob : hoc nomen mihi est in æternum, et hoc memoriale meum in generatione et generationem ; dormitaverunt dormitione mortis : de qua in libro Job scriptum est, Dives quum dormierit, nihil secum auferet ; et Christus, Lazarus amicus noster dormit ; qui ascenderunt equos, id est ministri et milites regis Assyriorum.
paras.en: [[75:7|At thy rebuke|Ab increpatione tua]], that is, at thy strict vengeance, [[75:7|O God of Jacob|o Deus Jacob]] the patriarch, who sayest: I am [[Ex 3:6|the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob|Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob]]: [[Ex 3:15|this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations|hoc nomen mihi est in æternum, et hoc memoriale meum in generatione et generationem]]; [[75:7|they have all slumbered|dormitaverunt]] with the slumber of death, of which it is written in the book of Job, [[Job 27:19|The rich man when he shall sleep shall take away nothing with him|Dives quum dormierit, nihil secum auferet]]; and Christ says, [[John 11:11|Lazarus our friend sleepeth|Lazarus amicus noster dormit]]; [[75:7|that mounted on horseback|qui ascenderunt equos]], that is, the servants and soldiers of the king of the Assyrians.

paras.t: Tu terribilis es, propter vindictam tuæ justitiæ, et imperscrutabilem profunditatem judiciorum tuorum. Propter quod sanctus Job ait : Semper quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum. Et quis resistet tibi ? quasi diceret, Nullus. Quemadmodum etiam apud Jeremiam inducitur : Quis similis mei ? et quis sustinebit me ? dicit Dominus ; et quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo ? Ex tunc, id est, ex tempore quo occidisti Assyrios, ira tua, id est ultio tuæ justitiæ, evidenter innotuit.
paras.en: [[75:8|Thou art terrible|Tu terribilis es]], because of the vengeance of thy justice and the unsearchable depth of thy judgments. Therefore holy Job says: [[Job 31:23|I have always feared God as waves swelling over me|Semper quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum]]. [[75:8|and who shall resist thee?|Et quis resistet tibi ?]] as if to say, No one. As is also said in Jeremias: [[Jer 49:19|who is like to me? and who shall abide me?|Quis similis mei ? et quis sustinebit me ?]] saith the Lord; [[Jer 49:19|and who is that shepherd that can withstand my countenance?|et quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo]][[Jer 50:44||]] [[75:8|from that time|Ex tunc]], that is, from the time when thou didst slay the Assyrians, [[75:8|thy wrath|ira tua]], that is, the vengeance of thy justice, was plainly made known.

paras.t: De cœlo auditum fecisti judicium : id est, justam ultionem, quam exercuisti in omnem exercitum Assyriorum, audiri fecisti in terra de cœlo, id est virtute cœlesti, qua hanc ultionem fecisti. Sicut enim hæc ultio de cœlo facta est ministerio angeli, sic dicitur audita de cœlo, quoniam virtus cœlestis, quæ fuit causa exsistentiæ hujus ultionis, exstitit etiam causa promulgationis ipsius. Vel sic : De cœlo auditum fecisti judicium, id est, audiri fecisti ab hominibus judicium cœleste : sic quoque quod dicitur, De cœlo judicium, tantum est dicere, ac si dicatur, Judicium cœleste. Hoc autem cœleste judicium fuit, quod Dominus de rege atque exercitu Assyriorum peregit, occidendo tantam catervam. Vel sic : De cœlo auditum fecisti judicium, id est, cœlitus revelasti judicium istud. Revelavit enim Deus Isaiæ, quæ futura erant regi huic et populo ejus ; imo Isaias frequenter in libro visionum suarum inde vaticinatur. Isaias quoque id ipsum Ezechiæ prædixit.
paras.en: [[75:9|Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven|De cœlo auditum fecisti judicium]]: that is, the just vengeance which thou didst execute on the whole army of the Assyrians thou hast caused to be heard on earth from heaven, that is, by the heavenly power by which thou didst work this vengeance. For as this vengeance was done from heaven by the ministry of an angel, so it is said to be heard from heaven, because the heavenly power which was the cause of this vengeance's coming to be was also the cause of its being made known. Or thus: [[75:9|Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven|De cœlo auditum fecisti judicium]], that is, thou hast caused men to hear a heavenly judgment; so too the words *judgment from heaven* amount to saying *heavenly judgment*. And this heavenly judgment was what the Lord wrought upon the king and army of the Assyrians, slaying so great a host. Or thus: [[75:9|Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven|De cœlo auditum fecisti judicium]], that is, thou didst reveal this judgment from heaven. For God revealed to Isaias what was to befall this king and his people; indeed Isaias often prophesies of it in the book of his visions. Isaias also foretold this very thing to Ezechias[[Is 37:21||]] [the margin gives Is. xxxvii, 21–35].

paras.t: Terra tremuit, id est, populus Judæorum propter adventum Assyriorum vehementer expavit. Vel dicitur terra tremuisse, propter multitudinem exercitus Assyriorum : quemadmodum primo Machabæorum habetur, Commota est terra a voce exercituum. Et quievit, id est, populus terræ Judææ a suo pavore cessavit, occisis Assyriis.
paras.en: [[75:9|the earth trembled|Terra tremuit]], that is, the people of the Jews was sorely afraid at the coming of the Assyrians. Or the earth is said to have trembled because of the multitude of the army of the Assyrians, as is found in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 9:13|the earth shook at the noise of the armies|Commota est terra a voce exercituum]]. [[75:9|and was still|Et quievit]], that is, the people of the land of Judea ceased from its fear when the Assyrians had been slain.

paras.t: Quum exsurgeret in judicium Deus, id est, in actum judicandi procederet, committendo angelo suo, ut prædictum populum trucidaret, ut salvos faceret omnes mansuetos terræ, id est, quatenus Ezechiam regem mitem et sanctum cum populo suo de manu Assyriorum erueret.
paras.en: [[75:10|When God arose in judgment|Quum exsurgeret in judicium Deus]], that is, when he went forth to the act of judging, committing it to his angel to slaughter the aforesaid people, [[75:10|to save all the meek of the earth|ut salvos faceret omnes mansuetos terræ]], that is, in order to rescue Ezechias, a meek and holy king, together with his people from the hand of the Assyrians.

paras.t: Quoniam cogitatio hominis, id est cor et meditatio cordis regis Ezechiæ et cujuslibet servi ipsius, eum in virtutibus sequentis, confitebitur tibi confessione laudis, gratias tibi agendo de liberatione tam gratiosa ; et reliquiæ cogitationis, id est memoriæ hujus facti, nascentes in ipso Ezechia ac populo suo, posterisque eorum, ex prima cogitatione facti istius, diem festum agent tibi, id est, occasio erunt, ut solenniter recolatur liberatio talis a populo Ezechiæ, imo et ab aliis qui norunt tam mirabile opus : quia nos omnes hoc miraculum audientes, diem quodammodo festum agimus, contemplando et admirando Deum in opere tam præclaro.
paras.en: [[75:11|For the thought of man|Quoniam cogitatio hominis]], that is, the heart and the meditation of the heart of king Ezechias and of each of his servants who followed him in virtue, [[75:11|shall give praise to thee|confitebitur tibi]] with the confession of praise, giving thanks to thee for so gracious a deliverance; [[75:11|and the remainders of the thought|et reliquiæ cogitationis]], that is, the remembrances of this deed, springing up in Ezechias himself and his people and their descendants from the first thought of this deed, [[75:11|shall keep holiday to thee|diem festum agent tibi]], that is, they will be the occasion for such a deliverance to be solemnly recalled by the people of Ezechias, and indeed by others who know of so wonderful a work: for all of us, hearing of this miracle, in a manner keep holiday, contemplating and admiring God in so glorious a work.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta alloquitur populum Judæorum ab Assyriis liberatum, quatenus Deo sint grati, aitque : Vovete pro gratiarum actione vota spontanea, et reddite, id est, vota persolvite, Domino Deo vestro, omnes qui in circuitu ejus affertis munera, id est, qui ex omni terra circa Jerusalem et in gyro ipsius ac templi, in quo Deus esse et habitare asseritur, convenitis, ut Domino hostias immoletis :
paras.en: Then the Prophet addresses the people of the Jews delivered from the Assyrians, that they may be grateful to God, and says: [[75:12|Vow ye|Vovete]] free-will vows in thanksgiving, [[75:12|and pay|et reddite]], that is, discharge your vows, [[75:12|to the Lord your God|Domino Deo vestro]], [[75:12|all you that are round about him bring presents|omnes qui in circuitu ejus affertis munera]], that is, you who gather from all the land about Jerusalem, round about it and the temple, in which God is said to be and to dwell, to sacrifice victims to the Lord:

paras.t: Domino, inquam, Terribili et, pro id est, ei qui aufert spiritum principum, occidendo magnos sicut et parvos, terribili apud reges terræ, qui audientes dejectionem Sennacherib, Deum Israel formidabant. Unde et Nabuchodonosor ait : Nunc igitur laudo, magnifico et glorifico Regem cœli, quoniam omnia opera ejus sunt vera. Et Darius : Paveant, inquit, habitantes in universa terra Deum Danielis, quia ipse est liberator et salvator, faciens signa et mirabilia in cœlo et in terra.
paras.en: to the Lord, I say, [[75:12|To him that is terrible|Terribili]], and (*and* stands for *that is*) [[75:13|to him who taketh away the spirit of princes|ei qui aufert spiritum principum]], slaying the great as well as the small, [[75:13|to the terrible with the kings of the earth|terribili apud reges terræ]], who, hearing of the overthrow of Sennacherib, dreaded the God of Israel. Hence Nabuchodonosor also says: I [[Dan 4:34|do now praise, and magnify, and glorify the King of heaven: because all his works are true|Nunc igitur laudo, magnifico et glorifico Regem cœli, quoniam omnia opera ejus sunt vera]]. And Darius: [[Dan 14:42|Let all|Paveant]], he says, [[Dan 14:42|the inhabitants of the whole earth fear the God of Daniel|habitantes in universa terra Deum Danielis]], for [[Dan 6:27|He is the deliverer, and saviour, doing signs and wonders in heaven, and in earth|ipse est liberator et salvator, faciens signa et mirabilia in cœlo et in terra]] [the margin gives Dan. xiv, 42, where the king is Cyrus; the words that follow, with "in heaven", are from the decree of Darius, Dan 6:26–27].

75.title: EXPOSITIO MORALIS EJUSDEM IN PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI QUINTI.
75.title_en: Moral exposition of the same seventy-fifth psalm.

paras.t: Juxta intellectum autem moralem, exponendus est psalmus hic de statu Ecclesiæ christianæ, videlicet de quolibet homine, populo, seu communitate christifideli, a multis periculis liberata, atque ex hoc Deum magnifice collaudante, et alios ad sanctam devotionem ac gratitudinem invitante.
paras.en: According to the moral sense, this psalm is to be explained of the state of the Christian Church, that is, of any faithful Christian man, people or community delivered from many dangers, and therefore praising God magnificently and inviting others to holy devotion and gratitude.

paras.t: Eritque sensus tituli superius positi, talis : Psalmus Asaph, id est congregationi fidelium, significatæ per Asaph, conveniens, atque in finem (qui Christus est) tendens ac dirigens in laudibus, ita ut ipsa Ecclesia ex promptitudine voluntatis et impetu sanctæ dilectionis, Deo laudes concinat, et non ex tristitia seu necessitate, quoniam hilarem datorem diligit Deus : estque psalmus iste canticum, id est laus spiritualis jucunditatis, ad Assyrios, id est ad dirigentes, eos videlicet qui cor suum ad Dominum dirigunt. Assyrii namque, dirigentes interpretantur.
