So then they are captives, as Peter declares: The wicked [[2 Pet 2:19|are the slaves of corruption|servi sunt corruptionis]]: [[2 Pet 2:19|For by whom a man is overcome, of the same also he is the slave|a quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est]].

paras.t: Et conclusit in gladio infidelium populum suum christianum, quem Sarraceni in Terra sancta sæpe occiderunt et expulerunt. Potest quoque nomine gladii intelligi impugnatio tentatoris, seu perversitas animæ se ipsam necantis, imo et totum hominem spiritualiter occidentis gladio consensus illiciti. Et hereditatem suam sprevit: id est, plebem christianam, quæ merito foret hereditas Dei, tanquam ejus sanguine empta, ab infidelibus non protexit, nec a culpa retraxit.
paras.en: [[77:62|And he shut up|Et conclusit]] [[77:62|under the sword|in gladio]] of the infidels [[77:62|his people|populum suum]], the Christian people, whom the Saracens have often slain and driven out in the Holy Land. By the name of *sword* may also be understood the assault of the tempter, or the perversity of the soul that kills itself, nay, that slays the whole man spiritually with the sword of unlawful consent. [[77:62|and he despised his inheritance|Et hereditatem suam sprevit]]: that is, the Christian people, which would rightly be the inheritance of God, as bought with his blood, he did not protect from the infidels, nor draw back from sin.

paras.t: Juvenes eorum comedit ignis concupiscentiæ carnalis: sicut Osee ait, Spiritus fornicationis decepit eos; et virgines eorum vanæ et fatuæ non sunt lamentatæ: quia non est qui earum vanitatem deploret ex compassione caritatis fraternæ, sed laudantur peccatrices in vanitatibus animæ suæ.
paras.en: [[77:63|Fire consumed their young men|Juvenes eorum comedit ignis]], the fire of carnal concupiscence: as Osee says, [[Osee 4:12|the spirit of fornication hath deceived them|Spiritus fornicationis decepit eos]]; [[77:63|and their maidens|et virgines eorum]], vain and foolish, [[77:63|were not lamented|non sunt lamentatæ]]: for there is none to bewail their vanity out of the compassion of brotherly charity, but sinful women are praised in the vanities of their soul[[Ps 9:24||]] [the margin gives Ps. v, 3 and following, in the Hebrew numbering; Denis is adapting Ps 9:24 (Ps 10:3 in the Hebrew), "the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul"].

paras.t: Sacerdotes eorum in gladio ceciderunt. Gladius spiritualis, secundum Apostolum, est verbum Dei. Est igitur sensus: Sacerdotes Christianorum, proprii oris prædicatione occisi sunt intus. Dum enim docent quæ ipsi non implent, mortaliter peccant: et ita se ipsos damnant, spiritualiterque occidunt. Unde Apostolus ait: In quo alium judicas, te ipsum condemnas; eadem enim facis. Et Job dicit: Os tuum condemnabit te, et non ego, et labia tua respondebunt tibi. Et viduæ eorum non plorabantur: sicut ait Apostolus, Vidua quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est. Viduæ ergo non plorantur, dum earum carnales deliciæ non deflentur pio compassionis affectu.
paras.en: [[77:64|Their priests fell by the sword|Sacerdotes eorum in gladio ceciderunt]]. The spiritual sword, according to the Apostle, is [[Eph 6:17|the word of God|verbum Dei]]. The sense, then, is: the priests of the Christians have been slain within by the preaching of their own mouth. For when they teach what they themselves do not fulfil, they sin mortally: and so they condemn themselves and slay themselves spiritually. Whence the Apostle says: [[Rom 2:1|wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself|In quo alium judicas, te ipsum condemnas]]; [[Rom 2:1|For thou dost the same things|eadem enim facis]]. And Job says: [[Job 15:6|Thy own mouth shall condemn thee, and not I: and thy own lips shall answer thee|Os tuum condemnabit te, et non ego, et labia tua respondebunt tibi]]. [[77:64|and their widows did not mourn|Et viduæ eorum non plorabantur]] [Denis takes *non plorabantur* as "were not mourned"]: as the Apostle says, The widow [[1 Tim 5:6|that liveth in pleasures is dead while she is living|quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est]]. Widows, then, are not mourned when their carnal pleasures are not wept for with the loving affection of compassion.

paras.t: Et percussit inimicos suos in posteriora, id est, extrema atque finali pœna eos damnavit, quemadmodum Dominus per Jeremiam ait quibusdam: Dabo vos in opprobrium sempiternum et ignominiam æternam, quæ nunquam oblivione delebitur. Idcirco nunc additur, opprobrium sempiternum dedit illis, projiciendo eos in lacum carceris gehennalis. Propter quod in Jeremia Dominus loquitur: Dabo eos in vexationem et maledictionem et stuporem, et in sibilum, et in opprobrium, eo quod non audierint verba mea.
paras.en: [[77:66|And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts|Et percussit inimicos suos in posteriora]], that is, he condemned them with the last and final punishment, as the Lord says through Jeremias to some: [[Jer 23:40|I will bring an everlasting reproach upon you, and a perpetual shame which shall never be forgotten|Dabo vos in opprobrium sempiternum et ignominiam æternam, quæ nunquam oblivione delebitur]]. Therefore it is now added, [[77:66|he put them to an everlasting reproach|opprobrium sempiternum dedit illis]], casting them into the pit of the prison of hell. For which reason the Lord speaks in Jeremias: [[Jer 29:18|I will give them up unto affliction|Dabo eos in vexationem]], [[Jer 29:18|to be a curse, and an astonishment, and a hissing, and a reproach|et maledictionem et stuporem, et in sibilum, et in opprobrium]], [[Jer 29:19|Because they have not hearkened to my words|eo quod non audierint verba mea]] [the margin gives Jer. xxiv, 9, a like passage; Denis's words are those of Jer 29:18–19].

paras.t: Consequenter agit Propheta, de populo ad regnum Christi veraciter pertinente. Et repulit Deus tabernaculum, id est posteritatem, domum, familiam, Joseph, id est populi Judæorum, in lege sibi finem et sufficientiam constituentis, qui se putat sine gratia Christi per legem posse salvari. Merito quoque per Joseph populus Judæorum signatur. Primo, quoniam Joseph ceteris Patriarchis fratribus suis sanctitate atque imperio eminebat. Secundo, quoniam Joseph interpretatur additamentum: et ita per eum designantur Judæi, quibus temporalium bonorum promittebantur augmenta. Et tribum Ephraim non elegit. Ephraim interpretatur frugifer seu fructificatio: per quem significatur idem populus qui per Joseph, in quantum terrenis fructibus inhiabat. Sed elegit tribum Juda, id est populum christianum, Domino confitentem devote et pure propter bona cœlestia ac divina, videlicet montem Sion, id est militantem Ecclesiam, quem dilexit, juxta illud Apostoli: Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut illam sanctificaret.
paras.en: Next the Prophet treats of the people that truly belongs to the kingdom of Christ. [[77:67|And he rejected the tabernacle|Et repulit Deus tabernaculum]], that is, the posterity, house and family, [[77:67|of Joseph|Joseph]], that is, of the Jewish people, which makes the law its end and sufficiency, and thinks it can be saved by the law without the grace of Christ. And the Jewish people is fittingly signified by Joseph. First, because Joseph stood out above the other Patriarchs, his brothers, in holiness and in rule. Secondly, because Joseph is interpreted *increase*: and so by him are signified the Jews, to whom increase of temporal goods was promised. [[77:67|and chose not the tribe of Ephraim|Et tribum Ephraim non elegit]]. Ephraim is interpreted *fruitful* or *fruit-bearing*: by whom is signified the same people as by Joseph, in so far as it gaped after earthly fruits. [[77:68|But he chose the tribe of Juda|Sed elegit tribum Juda]], that is, the Christian people, confessing the Lord devoutly and purely for the sake of heavenly and divine goods [Juda is interpreted *confession* or *praise*], namely [[77:68|mount Sion|montem Sion]], that is, the Church militant, [[77:68|which he loved|quem dilexit]], according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved the church and delivered himself up for it|Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea]], [[Eph 5:26|That he might sanctify it|ut illam sanctificaret]].

paras.t: Et ædificavit sicut unicornium, id est, sicut ædificari decuit domum Christifidelium, unum verum Deum colentium, sanctificium suum, id est Ecclesiam militantem, seu populum christianum: quem ædificavit, faciendo sibi in cordibus nostris habitaculum aptum per fidem et gratiam Spiritus Sancti. De hac quippe ædificatione ait Christus per Amos: Suscitabo tabernaculum David quod cecidit, et reædificabo aperturas murorum ejus. Hoc sanctificium Deus ædificavit in terra quam fundavit in sæcula, id est in universo mundo, sicut apud Malachiam testatur: Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus; et in omni loco offertur nomini meo oblatio munda, videlicet Sacramentum altaris. Et hæc terra est fundata in sæcula, quoniam, sicut Ecclesiastes ait, Terra in æternum stat.
paras.en: [[77:69|And he built|Et ædificavit]] [[77:69|as of unicorns|sicut unicornium]] [*unicornis*, "one-horned": Denis takes it of those who worship the one God], that is, as it was fitting that the house of Christ's faithful, who worship the one true God, should be built, [[77:69|his sanctuary|sanctificium suum]], that is, the Church militant, or the Christian people: which he built by making for himself in our hearts a fit dwelling through faith and the grace of the Holy Ghost. For of this building Christ says through Amos: [[Amos 9:11|I will raise up the tabernacle of David, that is fallen: and I will close up the breaches of the walls thereof|Suscitabo tabernaculum David quod cecidit, et reædificabo aperturas murorum ejus]]. This sanctuary God built [[77:69|in the land which he founded for ever|in terra quam fundavit in sæcula]], that is, in the whole world, as he testifies in Malachias: [[Mal 1:11|from the rising of the sun even to the going down, my name is great among the Gentiles, and in every place|Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus; et in omni loco]] [[Mal 1:11|there is offered to my name a clean oblation|offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]], namely the Sacrament of the altar. And this land is founded for ever, since, as Ecclesiastes says, [[Eccles 1:4|the earth standeth for ever|Terra in æternum stat]].

paras.t: Et elegit Deus Trinitas David servum suum, id est Christum hominem: qui secundum quod homo est, servus Dei atque electus est, quemadmodum in Isaia Dominus ait: Ecce servus meus, suscipiam illum; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea. Quod evangelista Matthæus de Christo dictum allegat. Christum ergo Deus elegit, ut sit caput et princeps universalis Ecclesiæ, dux, pastor, judex et Dominus omnium electorum. Propter quod Dominus ait: Salvabo gregem meum; et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum qui pascat eum, David servum meum, id est Christum, ut omnes exponunt. Et sustulit eum, scilicet Christum, Deus Trinitas, de gregibus ovium, id est, præ omnibus electis exaltavit glorificavitque eum, quemadmodum Sponsa decantat: Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus. De post fetantes accepit eum: id est, postquam oves suas in hoc mundo spiritualiter fecundavit, redemit, et confirmavit, recepit eum Pater in cœlos ad dexteram suam. Propter quod Christus ait ad Patrem: Opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem; nunc autem ad te venio. Vel, De post fetantes accepit eum, quia Christus primo missus est ad oves perditas domus Israel, quibus reparatis, quoad electos, misit discipulos suos per totum mundum ad oves ex gentibus congregandas, sicut ipse ait: Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere.
paras.en: [[77:70|And he chose|Et elegit]], God the Trinity did, [[77:70|his servant David|David servum suum]], that is, Christ as man: who, according as he is man, is the servant of God and chosen, as the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him: my elect, my soul delighteth in him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam illum; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea]]. This the evangelist Matthew alleges as said of Christ[[Matt 12:18||]]. God therefore chose Christ to be the head and universal prince of the Church, the leader, shepherd, judge and Lord of all the elect. For which reason the Lord says: [[Ezech 34:22|I will save my flock|Salvabo gregem meum]]; [[Ezech 34:23|And I WILL SET UP ONE SHEPHERD OVER THEM, and he shall feed them, even my servant David|et suscitabo super eum pastorem unum qui pascat eum, David servum meum]], that is, Christ, as all expound it. [[77:70|and took him|Et sustulit eum]], namely Christ, God the Trinity did, [[77:70|from the flocks of sheep|de gregibus ovium]], that is, he exalted and glorified him above all the elect, as the Bride sings: [[Cant 5:10|My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands|Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus]]. [[77:70|he brought him from following the ewes great with young|De post fetantes accepit eum]]: that is, after he had made his sheep spiritually fruitful in this world, redeemed them and strengthened them, the Father received him into heaven at his right hand. For which reason Christ says to the Father: [[John 17:4|I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do|Opus consummavi quod dedisti mihi ut facerem]]; [[John 17:13|And now I come to thee|nunc autem ad te venio]]. Or, [[77:70|he brought him from following the ewes great with young|De post fetantes accepit eum]], because Christ was first sent [[Matt 15:24|to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|ad oves perditas domus Israel]]; and when these had been restored, as regards the elect, he sent his disciples throughout the whole world to gather the sheep from among the Gentiles, as he himself says: [[John 10:16|And other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere]].

paras.t: Accepit autem Deus Christum, pascere, id est ut pasceret, Jacob servum suum, id est populum christianum vitia conculcantem; et Israel hereditatem suam, id est eumdem populum spiritualia contemplantem, et ad vitam æternam electum. Et pavit eos Christus in mundo corporaliter vivens, scientia et doctrina: et hoc, in innocentia cordis sui, quoniam ipse iniquitatem non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus, sicut in Isaia legitur. Et in intellectibus manuum suarum deduxit eos. Ipse nempe est virtus et sapientia Patris, qui de se ipso discipulis dixit: Vos vocatis me, Magister et Domine; et bene dicitis: […] sum etenim. Et iterum: Nolite, ait, vocari Rabbi: unus est enim magister vester, Christus; omnes autem vos fratres estis. Christus ergo deduxit oves suas in intellectibus manuum suarum, id est in doctrina et sanctitate, quoniam cœpit facere et docere. Pascit autem, deducitque Christus oves suas per se ipsum, per vicarios suos, Ecclesiarum prælatos et prædicatores, per angelos sanctos. Ipse enim solus gratiam influit; angeli vero nos ad eam disponunt, nosque illuminant: quod etiam homines facere possunt, quemadmodum Paulus ad Corinthios loquitur: Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit, Deus autem incrementum dedit.
paras.en: And God took Christ [[77:71|To feed|pascere]], that is, that he might feed, [[77:71|Jacob his servant|Jacob servum suum]], that is, the Christian people trampling on vices [Jacob means *supplanter*]; [[77:71|and Israel his inheritance|et Israel hereditatem suam]], that is, the same people contemplating spiritual things [Israel is interpreted *a man seeing God*], and chosen for eternal life. [[77:72|And he fed them|Et pavit eos]], Christ did, living bodily in the world, with knowledge and teaching: and this [[77:72|in the innocence of his heart|in innocentia cordis sui]], since he [[Is 53:9|hath done no iniquity|iniquitatem non fecit]], [[1 Pet 2:22|neither was guile found in his mouth|nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus]], as we read in Isaias [Denis's words are partly those of 1 Pet 2:22, which the margin also gives]. [[77:72|and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands|Et in intellectibus manuum suarum deduxit eos]] [*in intellectibus*, literally "in the understandings"]. For he is the power and the wisdom of the Father, who said of himself to the disciples: [[John 13:13|You call me Master and Lord. And you say well|Vos vocatis me, Magister et Domine; et bene dicitis]]: […] [[John 13:13|for so I am|sum etenim]]. And again: [[Matt 23:8|be not you|Nolite]], he says, [[Matt 23:8|called Rabbi|vocari Rabbi]]: [[Matt 23:8|For one is your master|unus est enim magister vester]], Christ [Denis adds *Christus* from Matt 23:10]; [[Matt 23:8|and all you are brethren|omnes autem vos fratres estis]]. Christ therefore conducted his sheep by the skilfulness of his hands, that is, in teaching and holiness, since he [[Acts 1:1|began to do and to teach|cœpit facere et docere]]. And Christ feeds and conducts his sheep through himself, through his vicars, the prelates and preachers of the Churches, and through the holy angels. For he alone pours in grace; but the angels dispose us to it and enlighten us: which men also can do, as Paul says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 3:6|I have planted, Apollo watered: but God gave the increase|Ego plantavi, Apollo rigavit, Deus autem incrementum dedit]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmum prolixum audivimus, in superficie planum, in interioribus suis mysteriis plenum: quem expedit prompte intelligere, quoniam compendiose includit quæ in diversis libris Moysis dispendiose tractantur. Ceterum, nunc omissa, præcedenti expositione vel plane omnia patescunt, vel de facili intelligi queunt.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a long psalm, plain on the surface, full of mysteries within: which it profits us to understand readily, since it contains in brief what is treated at length in the various books of Moses. As for what has now been passed over, by the preceding exposition it is all either plain or easily understood.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, qui omnium misereris, et lapsos ad te redeuntes paterna pietate suscipere non desinis: recordare, quæsumus, quia caro sumus, et abunda ut avertas iram, et non accendas contra nos omnem iram tuam; sed mitiga eam, et largire nobis indeficientem gratiam tuam.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, who hast mercy on all, and never ceasest to receive with fatherly kindness the fallen who return to thee: remember, we beseech thee, that we are flesh, and abound so as to turn away thy anger, and kindle not against us all thy wrath; but soften it, and bestow on us thy unfailing grace.

78.title: ELUCIDATIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI OCTAVI : DEUS, VENERUNT GENTES.
78.title_en: Literal explanation of the seventy-eighth psalm: O God, the heathens are come.

paras.t: Sensus tituli psalmi jam declarandi, videlicet, Psalmus Asaph, ex præcedentibus clarus est.
paras.en: The sense of the title of the psalm now to be explained, namely, [[78:1|A psalm for Asaph|Psalmus Asaph]], is clear from what has gone before.

paras.t: Advertendum vero, quod ter leguntur Judæi repulsi, loquendo de repulsione eorum graviori et magis famosa : quarum prima facta est per Chaldæos, secunda per Antiochum regem, tertia per Romanos. Quod autem hic psalmus scriptus non sit de repulsione eorum per Romanos inducta, Augustinus in expositione psalmi hujus satis ostendit. Illis namque non convenit, quod in secundo versu psalmi istius habetur, videlicet, Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum escas volatilibus cœli, carnes sanctorum tuorum bestiis terræ. Erant enim Judæi a Romanis occisi, infideles, obstinati ac reprobi. Cassiodorus ergo et Hugo exponunt hunc psalmum de oppressione Judæorum ab Antiocho introducta. Sed istud Nicolao de Lyra non placet, propter id quod in fine primi versus hujus psalmi habetur, Posuerunt Jerusalem in pomorum custodiam : loco cujus habet Hebraica veritas, Posuerunt Jerusalem in acervum ; translatio quoque Hieronymi, Posuerunt Jerusalem in acervis lapidum. Per quod designari videtur destructio civitatis et templi : quæ ab Antiocho facta non invenitur ; sed polluit templum, statuendo in eo idolum abominandum. Verumtamen ista objectio facillime solvitur. Nam civitas et templum destructa dicuntur, vel propter occisionem populi et sacerdotum, vel propter destructionem quarumdam partium civitatis Jerusalem : quæ tempore Antiochi maxime impugnata est, partimque destructa, ut patet in libris Machabæorum. Ubertim enim in divinis Scripturis per habitatores intelliguntur habitacula, et per partem totum exprimitur. Non ergo oportet hunc psalmum ad litteram dumtaxat intelligi de Judæorum dejectione, et templi ac civitatis destructione, factis tempore Chaldæorum. Mihi quoque videtur, quod de utraque eorum devastatione apte ac litteraliter possit intelligi, quoniam ad utramque littera facile applicatur ; et sicut unam, sic et aliam credere possumus sancto Prophetæ divinitus fuisse revelatam, ac per hoc de utraque simul prophetat. Nam qua ratione dicitur vaticinatus in psalmo præsenti de una, dici potest prophetasse de alia.
paras.en: But it should be noted that the Jews are read to have been cast off three times, speaking of their heavier and more famous casting-off: the first of these was by the Chaldeans, the second by king Antiochus, the third by the Romans. That this psalm was not written of their casting-off brought about by the Romans, Augustine shows well enough in his exposition of this psalm. For what is said in the second verse of this psalm does not fit them, namely: [[78:2|They have given the dead bodies of thy servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: the flesh of thy saints for the beasts of the earth|Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum escas volatilibus cœli, carnes sanctorum tuorum bestiis terræ]]. For the Jews slain by the Romans were unbelievers, obstinate and reprobate. Cassiodorus, therefore, and Hugh expound this psalm of the oppression of the Jews brought about by Antiochus. But this does not please Nicholas of Lyra, because of what is said at the end of the first verse of this psalm, [[78:1|they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit|Posuerunt Jerusalem in pomorum custodiam]]: in place of which the Hebrew truth [that is, the Hebrew original] has, They have made Jerusalem a heap; and Jerome's translation too, They have made Jerusalem into heaps of stones. By this the destruction of the city and of the temple seems to be signified: which is not found to have been done by Antiochus; rather, he defiled the temple, setting up in it the abominable idol[[1 Mach 1:57||]]. Yet this objection is very easily answered. For the city and the temple are said to have been destroyed either because of the slaughter of the people and of the priests, or because of the destruction of certain parts of the city of Jerusalem, which in the time of Antiochus was most fiercely attacked, and in part destroyed, as appears in the books of Machabees. For in the divine Scriptures the dwellings are often meant by the inhabitants, and the whole is expressed by a part. So we need not understand this psalm, according to the letter, solely of the overthrow of the Jews and the destruction of the temple and of the city that came about in the time of the Chaldeans. To me, too, it seems that it can fitly and literally be understood of both their devastations, since the letter is easily applied to either; and as we can believe that the one was revealed by God to the holy Prophet, so we can believe the other was too; and so he prophesies of both at once. For by whatever reason he is said to have foretold the one in the present psalm, he can be said to have prophesied of the other.

paras.t: Ait ergo Propheta in persona congregationis fidelium : Deus, venerunt gentes, videlicet Babylonii et Antiochus cum suis, in hereditatem tuam, id est in Judæam, quæ erat terra divino cultui præelecta, et filiis Israel a Deo specialiter atque hereditarie condonata. Vel, In hereditatem tuam, id est in populum Judæorum. Unde per Isaiam Dominus ait : Benedictus populus meus Ægypti, et opus manuum mearum Assyrius ; hereditas autem mea Israel. Polluerunt templum sanctum tuum. Nam Chaldæi polluerunt et destruxerunt templum a Salomone constructum ; Antiochus vero cum suis, polluit templum a Zorobabel et populo a captivitate Babylonica redeunte ædificatum. Dicuntur autem hi templum polluisse, quia fecerunt in eo quæ erant per legem prohibita, ponendo in eo idola, vel gentes introducendo in ipsum. Unde Jeremias : Vidit (inquit) gentes ingressas in sanctuarium tuum, de quibus præceperas ne ingrederentur in ecclesiam. De hac pollutione templi, primo libro Machabæorum scriptum est : Accepit Antiochus altare aureum et omnia vasa ejus, et comminuit omnia. Rursusque : Ædificavit Antiochus rex abominandum idolum desolationis super altare Dei : nempe (ut alibi dicitur) posuit in templo statuam Jovis.
paras.en: The Prophet therefore says, in the person of the congregation of the faithful: [[78:1|O God, the heathens are come|Deus, venerunt gentes]], namely the Babylonians, and Antiochus with his men, [[78:1|into thy inheritance|in hereditatem tuam]], that is, into Judea, which was the land chosen out for the worship of God, and given by God to the children of Israel in a special way and as an inheritance. Or, [[78:1|into thy inheritance|In hereditatem tuam]], that is, into the Jewish people. Hence the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 19:25|Blessed be my people of Egypt, and the work of my hands to the Assyrian: but Israel is my inheritance|Benedictus populus meus Ægypti, et opus manuum mearum Assyrius ; hereditas autem mea Israel]]. [[78:1|they have defiled thy holy temple|Polluerunt templum sanctum tuum]]. For the Chaldeans defiled and destroyed the temple built by Solomon[[4 Kings 25:9||]]; but Antiochus with his men defiled the temple built by Zorobabel and by the people returning from the Babylonian captivity[[1 Mach 1:57||]]. And these are said to have defiled the temple because they did in it things forbidden by the law, setting up idols in it, or bringing the Gentiles into it. Hence Jeremias: [[Lam 1:10|she hath seen|Vidit]], he says, [[Lam 1:10|the Gentiles enter into her sanctuary, of whom thou gavest commandment that they should not enter into thy church|gentes ingressas in sanctuarium tuum, de quibus præceperas ne ingrederentur in ecclesiam]]. Of this defiling of the temple it is written in the first book of Machabees: Antiochus [[1 Mach 1:23|took away the golden altar|Accepit Antiochus altare aureum]], and [[1 Mach 1:23|all the vessels thereof|omnia vasa ejus]], [[1 Mach 1:23|and he broke them all in pieces|et comminuit omnia]]. And again: [[1 Mach 1:57|king Antiochus set up the abominable idol of desolation upon the altar of God|Ædificavit Antiochus rex abominandum idolum desolationis super altare Dei]]: that is (as is said elsewhere), he set up in the temple a statue of Jupiter[[2 Mach 6:2||]].

paras.t: Posuerunt Jerusalem, id est domos ejus ac templum, in pomorum custodiam, id est, tam vilem eam reputaverunt, sicut reputatur domuncula in qua custodiuntur poma. Vel, In pomorum custodiam : quia sicut custodia pomorum, id est domus in qua poma servantur, relinquitur atque destruitur pomis sublatis, sic isti civitatem Jerusalem destruxerunt, et eam a propriis incolis relinqui fecerunt. Propter quod in primo libro Machabæorum legitur : Misit rex principem tributorum ; et accepit spolia civitatis, et succendit eam igni, et destruxit domos ejus et muros ejus in circuitu. Ex quo constat, objectionem Nicolai prætactam, nullam esse. Et iterum ait Scriptura loco præallegato : Fugerunt habitatores Jerusalem propter eos, et facta est habitatio exterorum. Unde et Isaias : Relinquetur, inquit, filia Sion velut umbraculum in vinea, et sicut tugurium in cucumerario.
paras.en: [[78:1|they have made Jerusalem|Posuerunt Jerusalem]], that is, its houses and the temple, [[78:1|as a place to keep fruit|in pomorum custodiam]]: that is, they held it as cheap as one holds the little hut in which fruit is kept. Or, [[78:1|as a place to keep fruit|In pomorum custodiam]]: because, as the keeping-place of fruit, that is, the house in which fruit is stored, is abandoned and pulled down once the fruit has been taken away, so these men destroyed the city of Jerusalem, and made its own inhabitants abandon it. For which reason we read in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 1:30|the king sent the chief collector of his tributes|Misit rex principem tributorum]]; and [[1 Mach 1:33|he took the spoils of the city, and burnt it with fire, and threw down the houses thereof, and the walls thereof round about|accepit spolia civitatis, et succendit eam igni, et destruxit domos ejus et muros ejus in circuitu]]. From this it is plain that the objection of Nicholas touched on above is of no weight. And again Scripture says in the place cited before: [[1 Mach 1:40|the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled away by reason of them and the city was made the habitation of strangers|Fugerunt habitatores Jerusalem propter eos, et facta est habitatio exterorum]]. Hence Isaias too: [[Is 1:8|shall be left|Relinquetur]], he says, [[Is 1:8|the daughter of Sion|filia Sion]] [[Is 1:8|as a covert in a vineyard, and as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers|velut umbraculum in vinea, et sicut tugurium in cucumerario]].

paras.t: Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum, id est corpora Judæorum occisa, escas volatilibus cœli ; carnes sanctorum tuorum, id est cadavera meliorum ac perfectiorum famulorum tuorum, dederunt in escam bestiis terræ : non enim sepelierunt ea, sed projecerunt ea ad devorandum avibus cœli et bestiis terræ. Propter quod Jeremias ait de valle filii Ennom : Non vocabitur amplius, Vallis filii Ennom, sed, Vallis occisionis.
paras.en: [[78:2|They have given the dead bodies of thy servants|Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum]], that is, the slain bodies of the Jews, [[78:2|to be meat for the fowls of the air|escas volatilibus cœli]]; [[78:2|the flesh of thy saints|carnes sanctorum tuorum]], that is, the corpses of thy better and more perfect servants, they gave as food [[78:2|for the beasts of the earth|bestiis terræ]]: for they did not bury them, but cast them out to be devoured by the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth. For which reason Jeremias says of the valley of the son of Ennom: [[Jer 7:32|it shall no more be called|Non vocabitur amplius]] [[Jer 7:32|the valley of the son of Ennom: but the valley of slaughter|Vallis filii Ennom, sed, Vallis occisionis]].

paras.t: Effuderunt sanguinem eorum tanquam aquam in circuitu Jerusalem, et non erat qui sepeliret. Propter quod libro primo Machabæorum habetur : Effuderunt sanguinem innocentem per circuitum sanctificationis. Et non erat qui sepeliret occisos, præ multitudine corporum occisorum. Nam sicut secundo libro Machabæorum habetur, Erant in toto triduo octoginta millia occisi ab Antiocho.
paras.en: [[78:3|They have poured out their blood as water, round about Jerusalem and there was none to bury them|Effuderunt sanguinem eorum tanquam aquam in circuitu Jerusalem, et non erat qui sepeliret]]. For which reason we have in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 1:39|they shed innocent blood round about the sanctuary|Effuderunt sanguinem innocentem per circuitum sanctificationis]]. [[78:3|and there was none to bury them|Et non erat qui sepeliret]] that were slain, because of the multitude of the bodies of the slain. For, as we have in the second book of Machabees, [[2 Mach 5:14|there were slain in the space of three whole days fourscore thousand|Erant in toto triduo octoginta millia occisi]] by Antiochus.

paras.t: Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris : quod consequenter clarius dicitur : subsannatio et illusio his, qui in circuitu nostro sunt. Gentiles enim in circuitu Judææ morantes, videlicet Ammonitæ, Moabitæ, Idumæi, Philistæi, etc., communiter gloriari solebant, quando filiis Israel aliquid adversitatis evenit : tunc deridebant eos, et subsannabant. Et ideo Nehemias induxit : Audi, Deus noster, quia facti sumus despectui. In libro quoque Machabæorum legitur : Sanctificatio Jerusalem, scilicet templum, desolata est sicut solitudo ; dies festi ejus conversi sunt in luctum, sabbata ejus in opprobrium, honores ejus in nihilum. Secundum gloriam ejus, multiplicata est ignominia ejus.
paras.en: [[78:4|We are become a reproach to our neighbours|Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris]]: which is next said more clearly, [[78:4|a scorn and derision to them that are round about us|subsannatio et illusio his, qui in circuitu nostro sunt]]. For the Gentiles dwelling round about Judea, namely the Ammonites, Moabites, Idumeans, Philistines, etc., commonly used to glory whenever some adversity befell the children of Israel: then they derided them and scorned them. And so Nehemias put it: [[2 Esd 4:4|Hear thou our God, for we are despised|Audi, Deus noster, quia facti sumus despectui]]. In the book of Machabees too we read: The [[1 Mach 1:41|sanctuary|Sanctificatio]] of Jerusalem, that is, the temple, [[1 Mach 1:41|was desolate like a wilderness, her festival days were turned into mourning, her sabbaths into reproach, her honours were brought to nothing|desolata est sicut solitudo ; dies festi ejus conversi sunt in luctum, sabbata ejus in opprobrium, honores ejus in nihilum]]. [[1 Mach 1:42|Her dishonour was increased according to her glory|Secundum gloriam ejus, multiplicata est ignominia ejus]].

paras.t: Deinde sequitur vox populi ita afflicti, lamentabiliter et querulose ad Dominum proclamantis : Usquequo, Domine, irasceris in finem ? id est, quamdiu vindicabis peccata nostra, tamque prolixe nos vastari permittes ? quasi dicant, Noli tam diu populo tuo irasci. Accendetur velut ignis zelus tuus ? id est, quamdiu indignatio tua tam vehementer ulciscetur se de nobis, tradendo nos in potestatem crudelium hominum ?
paras.en: Then follows the voice of the people thus afflicted, crying out to the Lord lamentably and plaintively: [[78:5|How long, O Lord, wilt thou be angry for ever|Usquequo, Domine, irasceris in finem]]? that is, how long wilt thou punish our sins, and allow us to be laid waste for so long? as if they said: Be not angry so long with thy people. [[78:5|shall thy zeal be kindled like a fire|Accendetur velut ignis zelus tuus]]? that is, how long shall thy indignation so vehemently avenge itself upon us, by delivering us into the power of cruel men?

paras.t: Effunde iram tuam in gentes quæ te non noverunt : id est, vindictam quam in nobis exerces, aufer clementer a nobis cultoribus tuis, te per fidem scientibus, eamque exerce in prædictis hominibus idololatris te ignorantibus ; et in regna Chaldæorum, et eorum quibus imperabat Antiochus, quæ nomen tuum non invocaverunt, sed deos vanos, quos coluerunt.
paras.en: [[78:6|Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that have not known thee|Effunde iram tuam in gentes quæ te non noverunt]]: that is, the vengeance which thou exercisest upon us, take mercifully away from us thy worshippers, who know thee by faith, and exercise it upon the aforesaid idolatrous men who know thee not; [[78:6|and upon the kingdoms|et in regna]] of the Chaldeans, and of those over whom Antiochus ruled, [[78:6|that have not called upon thy name|quæ nomen tuum non invocaverunt]], but upon vain gods, whom they worshipped.

paras.t: Quia comederunt Jacob : id est, populum ex Jacob patriarcha puero tuo dilecto natum, consumpserunt in ore gladii, aut alia morte, quemadmodum a manducante cibus consumitur. Unde Jeremias propheta ait : Primus Assur comedit eum ; iste novissimus Nabuchodonosor exossavit eum. Et locum ejus desolaverunt : quoniam urbes Judææ destruxerunt, vel populum ejus effugaverunt. Secundum quod primo libro Machabæorum scriptum est : Exclamavit Mathathias voce magna, dicens : Omnis qui zelum habet legis, exeat post me. Et fugit ipse et filii ejus in montes, et reliquerunt quæcumque habebant in civitate. Oratur autem hoc loco pro punitione adversariorum, non ex odio, sed zelo justitiæ vel ex caritate, quatenus in præsenti corrigantur, atque a malis prohibeantur, ne quotidie addant peccata peccatis, et postmodum gravius condemnentur.
paras.en: [[78:7|Because they have devoured Jacob|Quia comederunt Jacob]]: that is, the people born of Jacob the patriarch, thy beloved servant, they have consumed with the edge of the sword or by some other death, as food is consumed by one who eats it. Hence Jeremias the prophet says: [[Jer 50:17|first the king of Assyria devoured him|Primus Assur comedit eum]]; [[Jer 50:17|last this Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon hath broken his bones|iste novissimus Nabuchodonosor exossavit eum]] [the margin gives Jer. i, 17, which does not fit; the words are Jer 50:17 (l, read as i)]. [[78:7|and have laid waste his place|Et locum ejus desolaverunt]]: for they destroyed the cities of Judea, or put its people to flight. According to what is written in the first book of Machabees: [[1 Mach 2:27|Mathathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying|Exclamavit Mathathias voce magna, dicens]]: [[1 Mach 2:27|Every one that hath zeal for the law|Omnis qui zelum habet legis]], [[1 Mach 2:27|let him follow me|exeat post me]]. [[1 Mach 2:28|So he and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that they had in the city.|Et fugit ipse et filii ejus in montes, et reliquerunt quæcumque habebant in civitate]] Now prayer is made in this place for the punishment of the adversaries, not out of hatred, but out of zeal for justice or out of charity, so that they may be corrected in this present life and kept back from evil, lest they daily add sins to sins[[Ecclus 3:29||]], and afterwards be more heavily condemned.

paras.t: Ne memineris iniquitatum nostrarum antiquarum, quas nos ipsi et patres nostri multo tempore perpetravimus. Dicitur autem Deus iniquitatum nostrarum remisisse, dum eas in nobis ulciscitur ; dum vero indulget, oblivisci asseritur, quum tamen ejus cognitio æternaliter invariabilis perseveret. Cito anticipent nos misericordiæ tuæ, id est, effectus tuæ pietatis æternæ præveniant nos, ne incidamus judicium tuum, et ne justitiæ tuæ effectus præoccupent nos, faciendo nobis sicut meruimus. Hoc autem oramus, quia pauperes facti sumus nimis, quoniam templo et possessionibus ac urbibus spoliati sumus. In spiritualibus quoque inopes sumus, exigentibus vitiis nostris. Gratiam enim et spiritualium bonorum copiam, peccando perdidimus. Peccatum enim, spiritualis paupertatis atque miseriæ causa est, juxta illud Salomonis : Miseros facit populos peccatum. Ecclesiastes quoque : Qui in uno peccaverit, multa bona perdet. Propterea propriam mentis inopiam ignoranti, spiritualiterque excæcato propter carentiam gratiæ, in Apocalypsi dicitur : Dicis, Quia dives sum ; et nescis quia tu es miser et miserabilis, et pauper et cæcus et nudus.
paras.en: [[78:8|Remember not our former iniquities|Ne memineris iniquitatum nostrarum antiquarum]], which we ourselves and our fathers committed over a long time. Now God is said to remember our iniquities [the transcription reads *remisisse*, “to have remitted”; the sense, set against “forget”, requires *meminisse*, “to remember”] when he punishes them in us, and when he pardons he is said to forget them, though his knowledge abides eternally unchangeable. [[78:8|let thy mercies speedily prevent us|Cito anticipent nos misericordiæ tuæ]], that is, let the effects of thy eternal goodness go before us [prevent: in the old sense of coming before], lest we fall into thy judgement, and lest the effects of thy justice come upon us first, by dealing with us as we have deserved. And this we pray, [[78:8|for we are become exceeding poor|quia pauperes facti sumus nimis]], since we have been stripped of the temple, of our possessions and of our cities. In spiritual things too we are needy, as our vices have deserved. For by sinning we have lost grace and the abundance of spiritual goods. For sin is the cause of spiritual poverty and misery, according to that saying of Solomon: [[Prov 14:34|sin maketh nations miserable|Miseros facit populos peccatum]]. And Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 9:18|he that shall offend in one, shall lose many good things|Qui in uno peccaverit, multa bona perdet]] [the margin gives Eccle. iv, 18; the words are Eccles 9:18]. Therefore to one who does not know the poverty of his own mind, and is spiritually blinded for want of grace, it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:17|thou sayest: I am rich|Dicis, Quia dives sum]]; [[Apoc 3:17|and knowest not that thou art wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|et nescis quia tu es miser et miserabilis, et pauper et cæcus et nudus]].

paras.t: Ob hanc nimiam paupertatem dixit Mathathias : Ecce sancta nostra, et pulchritudo nostra, et claritas nostra desolata est.
paras.en: Because of this exceeding poverty Mathathias said: [[1 Mach 2:12|behold our sanctuary, and our beauty, and our glory is laid waste|Ecce sancta nostra, et pulchritudo nostra, et claritas nostra desolata est]].

paras.t: O quanta est virtus versiculi hujus, atque duorum versiculorum sequentium ! Vere enim omnem humanum sensum virtus eorum transcendit, et deficit lingua ab elocutione laudis eorum. Sed et quam bonum est, propriam paupertatem agnoscere, sicque indesinenter in Oratione dominica proclamare, Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie ! Admiranda est virtus orationis versuum horum ; et omnino saluberrimum est, mentali affectu cum attentione ingenti, cum præcordiali sapore, hos sacros versus depromere : quoniam possibilius foret cœlum et terram perire, quam talem orationem inefficacem exsistere.
paras.en: O how great is the power of this little verse, and of the two little verses that follow [Denis counts Help us … deliver us and And forgive us … for thy name's sake as two verses; both are v. 9 here]! Truly their power passes all human understanding, and the tongue fails in uttering their praise. And how good it is to acknowledge one's own poverty, and so to cry out unceasingly in the Lord's Prayer, [[Luke 11:3|Give us this day our daily bread|Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie]]! The power of the prayer of these verses is to be wondered at; and it is altogether most wholesome to bring forth these sacred verses with the affection of the mind, with very great attention, and with a relish from the depths of the heart: for it would be more possible for heaven and earth to perish than for such a prayer to be without effect.

paras.t: Adjuva nos, Deus salutaris noster, id est salvator noster et causa nostræ salutis. Tu enim dixisti, Sine me nihil potestis facere ; nec sumus sufficientes aliquid cogitare a nobis quasi ex nobis, sed universa sufficientia nostra ex te est. Itaque adjuva nos, confortando naturam nostram per gratiam, dando in adversis patientiam, in tentatione victoriam, in persecutione ereptionem, mittendo quoque ad nostrum subsidium cives cœlestes angelos sanctos ; et per preces ac merita omnium tibi placentium, tribue nobis quod nostra non meretur oratio, nec propria obtinet vita. Et propter gloriam nominis tui, Domine, libera nos : id est, idcirco et ad hunc finem eripe nos a tribulationibus cunctis, omnibusque peccatis atque periculis, quatenus misericordia tua glorificetur in nobis ab omnibus, tuque misericors prædiceris, et ob hoc a cunctis lauderis et honoreris. Hæc est ordinatissima deprecatio. Quamvis enim propriam liberationem et beatitudinem debeamus a Deo deposcere, tamen hanc ipsam nostram redemptionem debemus ad Dei honorem referre, Deumque precari ut propter se ipsum et nominis sui honorem nos audiat. Nam de ipso Salomon dicit : Universa propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus. Sic orando Deum honoramus, ideoque ab eo exaudiri et honorari meremur, quemadmodum ipse testatur : Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum. Deus enim gloriosus et sanctus, ad sui ipsius laudem et gloriam omnes electos creavit, secundum quod ipse alibi asserit : Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum. Semper igitur toto affectu et intentione sincera, ordinemus ad Dei honorem et gloriam, quidquid pro nobis ipsis vel aliis postulamus ; nec unquam reflectamur ad nos ipsos per privatum amorem, neque gloriemur in nobis per stultissimam vanitatem.
paras.en: [[78:9|Help us, O God, our saviour|Adjuva nos, Deus salutaris noster]], that is, our saviour and the cause of our salvation. For thou hast said: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]; and it is not [[2 Cor 3:5|that we are sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves|sumus sufficientes aliquid cogitare a nobis quasi ex nobis]], but all our sufficiency is from thee. Help us, then, by strengthening our nature with grace, giving patience in adversity, victory in temptation, rescue in persecution, and sending to our aid the citizens of heaven, the holy angels; and through the prayers and merits of all who please thee, grant us what our prayer does not deserve, nor our own life obtain. [[78:9|and for the glory of thy name, O Lord, deliver us|Et propter gloriam nominis tui, Domine, libera nos]]: that is, for this reason and to this end rescue us from all tribulations, and from all sins and dangers, that thy mercy may be glorified in us by all, and thou be proclaimed merciful, and for this be praised and honoured by all. This is a most well-ordered prayer. For although we ought to ask of God our own deliverance and beatitude, yet we ought to refer this very redemption of ours to the honour of God, and to beseech God to hear us for his own sake and for the honour of his name. For Solomon says of him: [[Prov 16:4|The Lord hath made all things for himself|Universa propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus]]. By praying thus we honour God, and so deserve to be heard and honoured by him, as he himself testifies: [[1 Kings 2:30|whosoever shall glorify me, him will I glorify|Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum]]. For God, glorious and holy, created all the elect for his own praise and glory, as he himself declares elsewhere: [[Is 43:7|every one that calleth upon my name, I have created him for my glory|Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum]]. Let us therefore always, with all our affection and with a sincere intention, direct to the honour and glory of God whatever we ask for ourselves or for others; and let us never turn back upon ourselves through private love, nor glory in ourselves through most foolish vanity.

paras.t: Et propitius esto peccatis nostris, pœnam relaxando, et culpam penitus indulgendo, propter nomen tuum, id est propter te ipsum et propriam bonitatem, quoniam tu dixisti : Non propter vos ego faciam, notum sit vobis, sed propter nomen sanctum meum.
paras.en: [[78:9|and forgive us our sins|Et propitius esto peccatis nostris]], by remitting the punishment and wholly pardoning the guilt, [[78:9|for thy name's sake|propter nomen tuum]], that is, for thine own sake and thine own goodness; for thou hast said: [[Ezech 36:32|It is not for your sakes that I will do this|Non propter vos ego faciam]], [[Ezech 36:32|be it known to you|notum sit vobis]], [[Ezech 36:22|but for my holy name's sake|sed propter nomen sanctum meum]].

paras.t: Et hoc fac, o Domine Deus, Ne forte dicant in gentibus, id est inter gentiles et insipientes : Ubi est Deus eorum ? id est, jam apparet quod Deus eorum ipsos salvare non potest, aut eorum cultum contemnit. Ne ergo tibi, o Domine, tanta irrogetur injuria, audi nos, sicut per Isaiam dixisti : Propter me ego faciam, ut non blasphemer. Et innotescat in nationibus, id est in prædictis gentilibus, coram oculis nostris, id est tam manifeste ut nobis patescat, ultio sanguinis servorum tuorum, qui effusus est : id est, effusionem sanguinis innocentis populi nostri vindica in paganis præfatis. Orat Propheta in persona populi Judæorum, pro ultione homicidiorum in Jerusalem et in Judæa factorum. Unde secundo libro Machabæorum orat hic populus : Afflige opprimentes nos, et contumeliam facientes in superbia. Quod etiam Moyses prædixit Deum esse facturum : Sanguinem, inquiens, sanctorum suorum ulciscetur, et vindictam retribuet in hostes eorum.
paras.en: And do this, O Lord God, [[78:10|Lest they should say among the Gentiles|Ne forte dicant in gentibus]], that is, among the heathen and the foolish: [[78:10|Where is their God?|Ubi est Deus eorum ?]] that is, it is plain now that their God cannot save them, or despises their worship. So, lest so great a wrong be done to thee, O Lord, hear us, as thou hast said by Isaias: [[Is 48:11|for my own sake will I do it, that I may not be blasphemed|Propter me ego faciam, ut non blasphemer]] [the margin gives only Is. xlviii; the words are Is 48:11]. [[78:10|And let him be made known among the nations|Et innotescat in nationibus]], that is, among the aforesaid heathen, [[78:10|before our eyes|coram oculis nostris]], that is, so plainly that it may be evident to us, [[78:10|By the revenging the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed|ultio sanguinis servorum tuorum, qui effusus est]]: that is, avenge upon the aforesaid pagans the shedding of the innocent blood of our people. The Prophet prays, in the person of the Jewish people, for vengeance for the murders committed in Jerusalem and in Judea. Hence in the second book of Machabees this people prays: [[2 Mach 1:28|Punish them that oppress us, and that treat us injuriously with pride.|Afflige opprimentes nos, et contumeliam facientes in superbia]] Which Moses also foretold that God would do: [[Deut 32:43|he will revenge the blood|Sanguinem]], he says, [[Deut 32:43|of his servants|sanctorum suorum ulciscetur]] [Denis reads sanctorum, of his saints, where the Vulgate has servorum, of his servants], [[Deut 32:43|and will render vengeance to their enemies|et vindictam retribuet in hostes eorum]].

paras.t: Introeat in conspectu tuo gemitus compeditorum : id est, captivorum tuorum suspiria pie exaudi, et eos de captivitatibus eripe. Multos enim Judæorum captivaverant servi Antiochi atque Chaldæi. Secundum magnitudinem brachii tui, id est secundum magnam tuam potentiam, posside filios mortificatorum, id est nos, quorum patres a gentilibus istis occisi sunt, ita ut protegas atque conserves nos, sicut custoditur possessio propria ab herede.
paras.en: [[78:11|Let the sighing of the prisoners come in before thee|Introeat in conspectu tuo gemitus compeditorum]]: that is, graciously hear the sighs of thy captives, and rescue them from their captivity. For the servants of Antiochus, and the Chaldeans, had taken many of the Jews captive. [[78:11|According to the greatness of thy arm|Secundum magnitudinem brachii tui]], that is, according to thy great power, [[78:11|take possession of the children of them that have been put to death|posside filios mortificatorum]], that is, of us, whose fathers were slain by these heathen; so that thou protect and preserve us, as one's own possession is guarded by its heir.

paras.t: Et redde vicinis nostris : de quibus superius dictum est, Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris ; septuplum, id est perfectam vindictam : septenario enim designatur perfectio ; in sinum eorum : id est, tam evidenter et tam infallibiliter pœna cadat super eos, et recipiatur ab eis, ne evadant, quam infallibiliter recipit homo quod in gremium ejus projicitur. Hoc enim non resilit. Improperium ipsorum, id est pœnam pro improperio, quod exprobraverunt tibi, Domine, dicendo de nobis : Ubi est Deus eorum ?
paras.en: [[78:12|And render to our neighbours|Et redde vicinis nostris]]: of whom it was said above, [[78:4|We are become a reproach to our neighbours|Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris]]; [[78:12|sevenfold|septuplum]], that is, perfect vengeance, for perfection is signified by the number seven; [[78:12|in their bosom|in sinum eorum]]: that is, let the punishment fall upon them and be received by them so plainly and so surely that they escape not, as surely as a man receives what is thrown into his lap, for that does not bounce back. [[78:12|the reproach|Improperium ipsorum]] of them, that is, the punishment for the reproach [[78:12|wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord|quod exprobraverunt tibi, Domine]], when they said of us: [[Ps 113:10|Where is their God?|Ubi est Deus eorum ?]]

paras.t: Nos autem populus tuus peculiaris, et oves pascuæ tuæ : de quibus alibi dixisti, Ego ipse pascam oves meas, salvabo gregem meum, in montibus Israel pascam eas ; confitebimur tibi in sæculum, id est, diu et perseveranter laudabimus te, gratias tibi canendo pro nostra liberatione. In generationem et generationem annuntiabimus laudem tuam, id est, in generatione nostra quoadusque vivimus, laudabimus te per nos ipsos ; in generationibus autem futuris, laudabimus te per filios seu fidei nostræ imitatores, quibus relinquimus materiam te laudandi, dum beneficia tua nobis exhibita, eis insinuamus verbo aut scripto.
paras.en: [[78:13|But we thy people|Nos autem populus tuus]], thy peculiar people, [[78:13|and the sheep of thy pasture|et oves pascuæ tuæ]]: of whom thou hast said elsewhere: [[Ezech 34:15|I will feed my sheep|Ego ipse pascam oves meas]]; [[Ezech 34:22|I will save my flock|salvabo gregem meum]]; [[Ezech 34:13|I will feed them in the mountains of Israel|in montibus Israel pascam eas]]; [[78:13|will give thanks to thee for ever|confitebimur tibi in sæculum]], that is, we will praise thee long and perseveringly, singing thanks to thee for our deliverance. [[78:13|We will shew forth thy praise, unto generation and generation|In generationem et generationem annuntiabimus laudem tuam]], that is, in our own generation, as long as we live, we will praise thee ourselves; and in the generations to come we will praise thee through our children, or the imitators of our faith, to whom we leave matter for praising thee, when we make known to them, by word or in writing, the benefits thou hast shewn us.

78.title: EXPLANATIO TROPOLOGICA EJUSDEM PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI OCTAVI.
78.title_en: Tropological explanation of the same seventy-eighth psalm.

paras.t: Ecclesia insuper Christi et quilibet Christianus, merito potest et debet hunc psalmum cantare lamentabili voce, propter amissionem Terræ sanctæ : præsertim quoniam ipsa sacra urbs Jerusalem, in qua Christi sepulcrum est, cum ipso venerandissimo et sanctissimo Christi sepulcro in manus Sarracenorum est data, atque ab eis diu possessa. Et ad hoc applicari potest hic psalmus hoc modo :
paras.en: Moreover, the Church of Christ and every Christian may rightly, and ought to, sing this psalm with a mournful voice, on account of the loss of the Holy Land: above all because the holy city of Jerusalem itself, in which is the sepulchre of Christ, has been given into the hands of the Saracens together with that most venerable and most holy sepulchre of Christ, and has long been held by them. And the psalm may be applied to this in the following way:

paras.t: Deus. Dei Unigenite Jesu Christe, qui es verus Deus et vita æterna, venerunt gentes, videlicet Sarraceni seu pagani legem Mahometi sequentes, in hereditatem tuam, id est in civitatem Jerusalem, ab imperatore Ælio reædificatam, vel in populum hujus civitatis christifidelem, qui est hereditas tua. Polluerunt templum sanctum tuum, id est ecclesiam in qua sepulcrum tuum continetur : quoniam templum illud irreverenter tractant, nec Christi cultum in eo fieri sinunt. Posuerunt Jerusalem in pomorum custodiam, occidentes in ea aut expellentes de ea omnem Christianum. Et de Christianorum in ea atque in Terra sancta multoties occisorum cadaveribus loquitur versus sequens : Posuerunt morticina, etc., secundum sensum in præcedenti elucidatione introductum. Effuderunt sanguinem eorum, scilicet Christianorum Sarraceni, tanquam aquam, id est valde abundanter, in circuitu Jerusalem, et in civitatibus per gyrum ejus jacentibus. Hoc, proh dolor ! factum est nimis frequenter, quemadmodum chronica testantur. Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris. Omnes enim terræ circa Terram sanctam situatæ, et legi Mahometi subjectæ, videlicet Philistiim, Ammonitæ, Moabitæ, etc., contemnunt nos, et nobis illudunt, quod Terra sancta et Christi sepulcrum, eorum potestati subduntur.
paras.en: [[78:1|O God|Deus]]: O only-begotten Son of God, Jesus Christ, who art true God and life everlasting, [[78:1|the heathens are come|venerunt gentes]], namely the Saracens, or pagans following the law of Mahomet, [[78:1|into thy inheritance|in hereditatem tuam]], that is, into the city of Jerusalem, rebuilt by the emperor Ælius [that is, Hadrian, Ælius Hadrianus, who rebuilt the city as Ælia Capitolina], or into the Christian people of this city, which is thy inheritance. [[78:1|they have defiled thy holy temple|Polluerunt templum sanctum tuum]], that is, the church in which thy sepulchre is contained: for they treat that temple without reverence, and do not suffer the worship of Christ to be carried on in it. [[78:1|they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit|Posuerunt Jerusalem in pomorum custodiam]], killing in it or driving out of it every Christian. And the following verse speaks of the dead bodies of the Christians many times slain in it and in the Holy Land: [[78:2|They have given the dead bodies|Posuerunt morticina]], etc., in the sense brought forward in the preceding explanation. [[78:3|They have poured out their blood|Effuderunt sanguinem eorum]], that is, the Saracens have poured out the blood of the Christians, [[78:3|as water|tanquam aquam]], that is, very abundantly, [[78:3|round about Jerusalem|in circuitu Jerusalem]], and in the cities lying round about it. This, alas! has happened all too often, as the chronicles bear witness. [[78:4|We are become a reproach to our neighbours|Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris]]. For all the lands situated around the Holy Land and subject to the law of Mahomet, namely the Philistines, the Ammonites, the Moabites, etc., despise us and mock us, because the Holy Land and the sepulchre of Christ are subjected to their power.

paras.t: Effunde iram tuam in gentes, videlicet in Sarracenos, quæ te non noverunt per fidem et cultum, sed immundissimi hominis ritui serviunt, et legem vanissimam servant, et in regna Sarracenorum, quæ nomen tuum non invocaverunt, quia nec sperant in te, sed in omni angustia Mahometum invocant. Orat ergo hoc loco Ecclesia pro recuperatione Terræ sanctæ, et expulsione gentilium inde. Quia comederunt Jacob, id est populum christianum, fidem et simplicitatem Jacob patriarchæ sectantem, et locum ejus, id est urbes Terræ sanctæ et civitatem Jerusalem, desolaverunt, id est, incolas christianos inde ejecerunt, et paganis hominibus loca sancta impleverunt.
paras.en: [[78:6|Pour out thy wrath upon the nations|Effunde iram tuam in gentes]], namely upon the Saracens, [[78:6|that have not known thee|quæ te non noverunt]] by faith and worship, but serve the rite of a most unclean man and keep a most empty law, [[78:6|and upon the kingdoms|et in regna]] of the Saracens [[78:6|that have not called upon thy name|quæ nomen tuum non invocaverunt]], for they do not hope in thee, but in every distress call upon Mahomet. Here, then, the Church prays for the recovery of the Holy Land and the expulsion of the Gentiles from it. [[78:7|Because they have devoured Jacob|Quia comederunt Jacob]], that is, the Christian people, which follows the faith and simplicity of the patriarch Jacob; and [[78:7|his place|locum ejus]], that is, the cities of the Holy Land and the city of Jerusalem, they [[78:7|have laid waste|desolaverunt]], that is, they have cast the Christian inhabitants out of them, and filled the holy places with pagan men.

paras.t: Sed quoniam tantam miseriam Christiani meruerunt, propter pessimam suam vitam, maxime in Terra sancta, quæ quum adhuc a Christianis in pace habitaretur, Christiani in ipsa sceleratissime vixerunt; propterea orat modo Ecclesia pro indulgentia peccatorum tantorum et antiquorum, quatenus remissione percepta, terrenam Jerusalem readipiscatur, et ad cœlestem Jerusalem perducatur.
paras.en: But since the Christians deserved so great a misery by their most wicked life, above all in the Holy Land, where, while it was still dwelt in by Christians in peace, the Christians lived most wickedly; therefore the Church now prays for the pardon of sins so great and so old, so that, having received remission, she may regain the earthly Jerusalem and be brought to the heavenly Jerusalem.

paras.t: Denique omnia hæc generalius possunt exponi hoc modo : Deus, venerunt gentes, id est infideles seu infideliter conversantes, in hereditatem tuam, id est in populum tuum electum et christifidelem : quemadmodum lupi oves impugnare solent et dissipare. Talibus enim electis ait Christus : Ecce ego mitto vos sicut agnos inter lupos ; et, In mundo pressuram habebitis. Polluerunt templum sanctum tuum : quia Ecclesiam multipliciter destruxerunt, dehonestaverunt, et opera nefaria commiserunt in ea, non solum pagani, sed etiam hæretici, maxime Ariani. Posuerunt Jerusalem, id est militantem Ecclesiam, in qua est visio pacis, et locus internæ quietis, in pomorum custodiam, expellendo de ea ministros altaris, ipsamque comminuentes.
paras.en: Finally, all these things may be expounded more generally in this way: [[78:1|O God, the heathens are come|Deus, venerunt gentes]], that is, unbelievers, or those who live in an unbelieving way, [[78:1|into thy inheritance|in hereditatem tuam]], that is, into thy chosen and Christian people, as wolves are wont to attack and scatter sheep. For to such chosen ones Christ says: [[Luke 10:3|Behold I send you as lambs among wolves|Ecce ego mitto vos sicut agnos inter lupos]]; and, [[John 16:33|In the world you shall have distress|In mundo pressuram habebitis]]. [[78:1|they have defiled thy holy temple|Polluerunt templum sanctum tuum]]: for they have in many ways destroyed the Church, dishonoured her, and committed wicked deeds in her: not only pagans, but heretics too, above all the Arians. [[78:1|they have made Jerusalem|Posuerunt Jerusalem]], that is, the Church militant, in which is the vision of peace [the name Jerusalem was interpreted as “vision of peace”] and the place of inward rest, [[78:1|as a place to keep fruit|in pomorum custodiam]], by driving the ministers of the altar out of her and breaking her in pieces.

paras.t: Sequens autem versiculus, de corporibus plurimorum martyrum ad litteram convenienter exponitur : imo interdum in tantum desæviit rabies persecutorum, ut corpora martyrum sepulta effoderent, comburerent, dissiparent, vel avibus cœli ac bestiis terræ ad devorandum projicerent.
paras.en: The following verse is fittingly expounded, according to the letter, of the bodies of very many martyrs: indeed, at times the fury of the persecutors raged so far that they dug up the buried bodies of the martyrs, burned them, scattered them, or threw them to the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth to be devoured.

paras.t: Effuderunt tyranni atque eorum satellites, sanguinem eorum, videlicet martyrum, tanquam aquam in circuitu Jerusalem, id est per omnem gyrum Ecclesiæ, utpote per totum mundum ubi christiana viguit fides. Ecclesia namque per universum orbem diffunditur ; et sæpe imperatores Romani ordinaverunt et præceperunt ut omnes Christiani trucidarentur ubicumque invenirentur, quatenus nomen et memoria Christi omnino deficeret. Et non erat qui sepeliret occisos. Hoc namque sub pœna mortis erat frequenter prohibitum, ne quis Christianos martyrizatos sepelire præsumeret. Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris, etc. Hoc, secundum sensum præhabitum, dicit Ecclesia quilibetque fidelis in persona Christianorum, juxta vel inter gentiles, hæreticos, seu persecutores morantium, qui Christianos sæpe subsannant, præcipue dum in præliis prævalent eis.
paras.en: [[78:3|They have poured out|Effuderunt]], namely the tyrants and their henchmen, [[78:3|their blood|sanguinem eorum]], that is, the blood of the martyrs, [[78:3|as water, round about Jerusalem|tanquam aquam in circuitu Jerusalem]], that is, throughout the whole circuit of the Church, namely throughout the whole world, wherever the Christian faith has flourished. For the Church is spread throughout the whole world; and the Roman emperors often ordained and commanded that all Christians should be slaughtered wherever they were found, so that the name and memory of Christ might fail altogether. [[78:3|and there was none to bury|Et non erat qui sepeliret]] the slain. For it was frequently forbidden, under pain of death, that anyone should presume to bury the martyred Christians. [[78:4|We are become a reproach to our neighbours|Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris]], etc. This, in the sense given before, the Church and every faithful soul says in the person of the Christians who dwell beside or among Gentiles, heretics or persecutors, who often scoff at the Christians, above all when they prevail against them in battle.

paras.t: Effunde iram tuam in gentes, etc. Orat Ecclesia, inimicos suos diligens, pro punitione et dejectione adversariorum suorum in præsenti sæculo, ne pereant in futuro.
paras.en: [[78:6|Pour out thy wrath upon the nations|Effunde iram tuam in gentes]], etc. The Church, loving her enemies, prays for the punishment and casting down of her adversaries in the present world, that they may not perish in the world to come.

paras.t: Et innotescat in nationibus coram oculis nostris ultio sanguinis servorum tuorum qui effusus est. Orat Ecclesia pro ultione sanguinis martyrum, eo modo quo et in Apocalypsi habetur : Animæ interfectorum clamabant voce magna : Usquequo, Domine, sanctus et verus, non vindicas sanguinem nostrum de his qui habitant in terra? Unde et Christus in Evangelio loquitur : Deus non faciet vindictam servorum suorum clamantium ad se die ac nocte? Dico vobis, quia cito faciet vindictam eorum.
paras.en: [[78:10|And let him be made known among the nations before our eyes, By the revenging the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed|Et innotescat in nationibus coram oculis nostris ultio sanguinis servorum tuorum qui effusus est]]. The Church prays for the avenging of the blood of the martyrs, in the way that is also found in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 6:9|the souls of them that were slain|Animæ interfectorum]] [[Apoc 6:10|cried with a loud voice|clamabant voce magna]]: [[Apoc 6:10|How long, O Lord (Holy and True)|Usquequo, Domine, sanctus et verus]], dost thou not [[Apoc 6:10|revenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth|vindicas sanguinem nostrum de his qui habitant in terra]]? Whence Christ too says in the Gospel: [[Luke 18:7|And will not God revenge|Deus non faciet vindictam]] his servants [Denis has servorum, “servants”, for the Gospel's “elect”] [[Luke 18:7|who cry to him day and night|clamantium ad se die ac nocte]]? [[Luke 18:8|I say to you that he will quickly revenge them|Dico vobis, quia cito faciet vindictam eorum]].

paras.t: Introeat in conspectu tuo, id est, exaudiatur a te, gemitus compeditorum, qui propter justitiam corporaliter ligantur et incarcerantur, vel vinculis divinæ ac fraternæ dilectionis constringuntur in tantum, ut etiam pro hostibus et persecutoribus fideliter orent, teque omnipotentem Deum ligare et prohibere dicantur, sicut tu ipse ad Moysen dicis : Cerno quod populus iste, scilicet filii Israel, duræ cervicis sit : dimitte me, ut irascatur furor meus contra eos, et deleam eos. Sed quid fecit Moyses sanctus ? Non acquievit tibi, quin potius ligatum te tenuit, dicens : Aut dimitte populo hanc noxam, aut si non facis, dele me de libro tuo quem scripsisti. Libenter, o Domine, hoc modo vinctus teneris vinculis sancti amoris. Tu enim es amor, et nullus te ita ligat, nisi cujus tu mentem tam vehementer inflammas.
paras.en: Let there [[78:11|come in before thee|Introeat in conspectu tuo]], that is, let there be heard by thee, [[78:11|the sighing of the prisoners|gemitus compeditorum]], who for justice' sake are bound and imprisoned in body; or who are so bound by the bonds of divine and brotherly love that they pray faithfully even for their enemies and persecutors, and are said to bind thee, the almighty God, and to hold thee back; as thou thyself sayest to Moses: [[Ex 32:9|I see that this people|Cerno quod populus iste]], namely the children of Israel, [[Ex 32:9|is stiffnecked|duræ cervicis sit]]: [[Ex 32:10|Let me alone, that my wrath may be kindled against them, and that I may destroy them|dimitte me, ut irascatur furor meus contra eos, et deleam eos]]. But what did holy Moses do? He did not yield to thee, but rather held thee bound, saying: [[Ex 32:31|either forgive them this trespass|Aut dimitte populo hanc noxam]], [[Ex 32:32|Or if thou do not, strike me out of the book that thou hast written|aut si non facis, dele me de libro tuo quem scripsisti]]. Gladly, O Lord, art thou held fast in this way by the bonds of holy love. For thou art love, and no one binds thee so, save him whose mind thou dost so vehemently inflame.

paras.t: Vel, Gemitus compeditorum, id est servorum tuorum mortalium, multis necessitudinibus humanæ corruptibilitatis et vinculis præsentis miseriæ, quotidianorumque lapsuum miserabiliter vinctorum, atque in carcere corporis hujus gementium, et cum Paulo clamantium : Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus ? Et rursus : Cupio dissolvi, et esse cum Christo.
paras.en: Or, [[78:11|the sighing of the prisoners|Gemitus compeditorum]], that is, of thy mortal servants, wretchedly bound by the many necessities of human corruptibility and the chains of the present misery and of daily falls, and groaning in the prison of this body, and crying out with Paul: [[Rom 7:24|Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?|Infelix ego homo ! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus]] And again: I desire [[Phil 1:23|to be dissolved and to be with Christ|dissolvi, et esse cum Christo]].

paras.t: Secundum magnitudinem brachii tui posside, per indesinentem custodiam et gratiæ multiplicationem, filios mortificatorum, id est nos omnes, qui sumus filii spirituales Apostolorum et martyrum ac reliquorum Sanctorum, pro nomine tuo corporaliter occisorum, vel quotidie afflictorum, et in laboribus pœnitentiæ, exercitiisque spiritualis vitæ incessabiliter interfectorum, quemadmodum ait Apostolus: Semper mortificationem Jesu in corpore nostro circumferentes, ut et vita Jesu manifestetur in carne nostra mortali.
paras.en: [[78:11|According to the greatness of thy arm, take possession|Secundum magnitudinem brachii tui posside]], by unceasing guarding and the multiplying of grace, of [[78:11|the children of them that have been put to death|filios mortificatorum]], that is, of all of us, who are the spiritual children of the Apostles and martyrs and the other Saints, who were slain in body for thy name, or are daily afflicted, and are ceaselessly put to death in the labours of penance and the exercises of the spiritual life [mortificatorum, “of them that have been put to death”, is the word behind the Apostle's “mortification” that follows], as the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 4:10|Always bearing about in our body the mortification of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be made manifest|Semper mortificationem Jesu in corpore nostro circumferentes, ut et vita Jesu manifestetur]] [[2 Cor 4:11|in our mortal flesh|in carne nostra mortali]].

paras.t: Postremo inducitur vox Ecclesiæ, Domino regratiantis pro beneficiis ejus : Nos autem populus tuus, a te Christo christianus vocatus, tuo sanguine liberatus, genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta, populus acquisitionis, qui fecisti nos Deo nostro regnum et sacerdotes ; et oves pascuæ tuæ, id est, qui sacramentis tuis reficimur, aqua sapientiæ a te potamur, pane vitæ cibamur, gratia tua roboramur et crescimus, et tua gubernatione subsistimus, atque ad finem beatum pertingimus ; confitebimur tibi in sæculum. Cetera ex præcedenti elucidatione clarissime elucescunt.
paras.en: Lastly the voice of the Church is brought in, giving thanks to the Lord for his benefits: [[78:13|But we thy people|Nos autem populus tuus]], called Christian after thee, O Christ, set free by thy blood[[Acts 20:28||]], [[1 Pet 2:9|a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation, a purchased people|genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta, populus acquisitionis]], thou who [[Apoc 5:10|hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests|fecisti nos Deo nostro regnum et sacerdotes]]; [[78:13|and the sheep of thy pasture|et oves pascuæ tuæ]], that is, we who are refreshed by thy sacraments, given the water of wisdom to drink by thee, fed with the bread of life, strengthened by thy grace and made to grow, who subsist by thy governance and come to the blessed end; [[78:13|will give thanks to thee for ever|confitebimur tibi in sæculum]]. The rest shines out most clearly from the preceding explanation.

paras.t: Decet autem nos psalmum hunc pro reparatione Terræ sanctæ quotidie cum affectuosissima mente depromere, quia et hoc vere sanctum est, et Deo gratissimum, pro hac tam pia intentione orare. Et si non exaudimur pro hoc, Deus tamen qui nostrum desiderium approbat, in aliis copiosam nobis mercedem impendet.
paras.en: And it befits us to pour forth this psalm daily, with a most loving mind, for the recovery of the Holy Land; for this too is truly holy, and most pleasing to God: to pray with so devout an intention. And if we are not heard in this, yet God, who approves our desire, will bestow on us an abundant reward in other things.

paras.t: Precatio. Preces nostras, quæsumus, Domine, placatus intende, ne memineris iniquitatum nostrarum antiquarum propter nomen tuum laudabile et gloriosum : ut te præstante, ab omnibus liberi offensis, jugiter operibus invigilemus æquitatis.
paras.en: Prayer. Graciously give ear to our prayers, we beseech thee, O Lord: [[78:8|Remember not our former iniquities|ne memineris iniquitatum nostrarum antiquarum]], for thy praiseworthy and glorious name's sake; that by thy gift, set free from all offences, we may ever keep watch in works of justice.

79.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI SEPTUAGESIMI NONI: QUI REGIS ISRAEL, INTENDE.
79.title_en: Literal exposition of the seventy-ninth psalm: Give ear, O thou that rulest Israel.

paras.t: Habet interea psalmus jam declarandus hunc titulum : In finem, pro his qui commutabuntur, testimonium Asaph pro Assyriis : id est, psalmus præsens in Christum, qui est finis præcepti ac legis, nos erigens, est testimonium Asaph, id est congregationis fidelium, Christi incarnationem fideliter recipientium ; scriptusque est pro his qui commutabuntur, id est ad instructionem et utilitatem eorum qui toto corde convertuntur ad Dominum, puta pro Assyriis, id est vitam suam coram Deo recte dirigentibus. Assyrii namque dirigentes interpretantur. Non enim sumitur hoc loco nomen, Assyriis, pro populo illo de quo in Threnis asserit Jeremias : Ægypto dedimus manum et Assyriis : de quo in libro Regum habetur.
paras.en: Meanwhile the psalm now to be explained has this title: [[79:1|Unto the end, for them that shall be changed, a testimony for Asaph|In finem, pro his qui commutabuntur, testimonium Asaph]] for the Assyrians [the words "for the Assyrians" are not in the Vulgate or Douay-Rheims title; they come from the Septuagint's]. That is, the present psalm, raising us up to Christ, who is the end of the precept and of the law, is the testimony of Asaph, that is, of the congregation of the faithful who faithfully receive the incarnation of Christ; and it is written for them that shall be changed, that is, for the instruction and profit of those who are converted to the Lord with their whole heart: for instance, for the Assyrians, that is, for those who direct their life aright before God. For Assyrians is interpreted "directing". For the name Assyrians is not taken in this place for that people of whom Jeremias says in the Lamentations: [[Lam 5:6|We have given our hand to Egypt, and to the Assyrians|Ægypto dedimus manum et Assyriis]]; of whom we read in the book of Kings[[4 Kings 17:1||]].

paras.t: Psalmus igitur iste, secundum doctores catholicos, de primo Christi adventu, videlicet de incarnatione Salvatoris, ad litteram scriptus est. Incarnatio autem Christi, salus est totius mundi, seu omnium electorum, qui unquam in mundo fuerunt, exsistunt, et erunt. Una quoque est omnium fidelium Ecclesia, eorum videlicet qui fuerunt ante legem, sub lege, et tempore gratiæ. Hæc autem Ecclesia nomine vineæ designatur, quoniam Deus eam colit, fecundat, et regit. Sed quoniam tempore legis Mosaicæ pene omnes declinabant ad idololatriam, idcirco pro tempore illo per vineam Domini designabatur Synagoga, seu congregatio Judæorum. Tempore quoque evangelicæ legis, per vineam Domini intelligenda est Christianorum Ecclesia, quoniam extra Ecclesiam Christi nemo potest salvari, quemadmodum ait Salvator : Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et arescet. Sancti igitur veteris Testamenti, Christi incarnationem vehementissime desiderantes, Deum orabant ut vineam suam, quam sæpe per angelos sanctos et homines virtuosos visitaverat, per se ipsum visitare dignaretur apparendo in carne. Hoc nempe desiderare audebant, quoniam Deus eis hoc promisit, quemadmodum apud Isaiam testatur : Propter hoc sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ipse qui loquebar, ecce adsum. Unde et iterum beatissimus Isaias prophetavit : Dominus judex noster, Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster, ipse veniet et salvabit nos. Per Zachariam quoque : Lauda et lætare, filia Sion, quia ecce ego venio, et habitabo in medio tui.
paras.en: This psalm, then, according to the Catholic doctors, was written literally about the first coming of Christ, namely about the incarnation of the Saviour. Now the incarnation of Christ is the salvation of the whole world, that is, of all the elect who ever have been, are, and will be in the world. And there is one Church of all the faithful, namely of those who were before the law, under the law, and in the time of grace. This Church is designated by the name of a vineyard, because God tends it, makes it fruitful, and rules it. But since in the time of the law of Moses almost all were turning aside to idolatry, for that time the Synagogue, or congregation of the Jews, was designated by the vineyard of the Lord. In the time of the law of the Gospel, too, the vineyard of the Lord is to be understood as the Church of Christians, since outside the Church of Christ no one can be saved, as the Saviour says: [[John 15:6|If any one abide not in me, he shall be cast forth as a branch and shall wither|Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et arescet]]. The saints of the Old Testament, then, most vehemently desiring the incarnation of Christ, prayed God that he would deign to visit his vineyard, which he had often visited through the holy angels and virtuous men, by himself, by appearing in the flesh. They dared to desire this because God had promised it to them, as he testifies in Isaias: [[Is 52:6|Therefore my people shall know my name in that day: for I myself that spoke, behold I am here|Propter hoc sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ipse qui loquebar, ecce adsum]]. Hence the most blessed Isaias prophesied again: [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king|Dominus judex noster, Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster]]: he will come and [[Is 33:22|will save us|salvabit nos]]. And through Zacharias: [[Zach 2:10|Sing praise, and rejoice, O daughter of Sion: for behold I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee|Lauda et lætare, filia Sion, quia ecce ego venio, et habitabo in medio tui]].

paras.t: Atque duo primi versus ad Ecclesiam Dei pertinent, quæ erat tempore legis scriptæ : qui tamen allegorice exponuntur de Ecclesia Dei, quæ est tempore gratiæ.
