Hence it is read in the book of Numbers: [[Num 20:13|This is the Water of contradiction, where the children of Israel strove with words against the Lord|Hæc est aqua Contradictionis, ubi jurgati sunt filii Israel contra Dominum]]. This can also be referred especially to Moses and Aaron, who at about this place offended God by unbelief, for which they were forbidden to enter the land of promise, the Lord saying to them: [[Num 20:12|Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring these people into the land, which I will give them|Quia non credidistis mihi, ut sanctificaretis me coram filiis Israel, non introducetis hos populos in terram quam dabo eis]] [the margin gives Num. xx and then 13 beside this line; verse 13 is the Water of contradiction, the words quoted here are verse 12].

paras.t: Audi, populus meus peculiaris, verba legis meæ auribus cordis et corporis, et contestabor te, id est, testis ero verborum meorum, operumque tuorum : juxta illud, Ego sum judex et testis, ait Dominus. Israel, id est plebs Israelitica, si audieris me, id est, si præcepta legis meæ impleveris, non erit in te deus recens, quem colas : quia nil temporale aut creatum pro Deo recipies ; neque adorabis deum alienum, sed me solum, verum, æternumque Deum.
paras.en: [[80:9|Hear, O my people|Audi, populus meus]], my own peculiar people, the words of my law with the ears of heart and body, [[80:9|and I will testify to thee|et contestabor te]]: that is, I will be witness of my words and of thy works, according to that saying: [[Jer 29:23|I am the judge and the witness, saith the Lord|Ego sum judex et testis, ait Dominus]] [the margin reads Jer. xxiv, 23; the words are Jer 29:23]. [[80:9|O Israel|Israel]], that is, the people of Israel, [[80:9|if thou wilt hearken to me|si audieris me]], that is, if thou fulfil the precepts of my law, [[80:10|there shall be no new god in thee|non erit in te deus recens]] for thee to worship, because thou wilt take nothing temporal or created for God; [[80:10|neither shalt thou adore a strange god|neque adorabis deum alienum]], but me alone, the true and eternal God[[Ex 20:3||]].

paras.t: Ego enim sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti, et adhuc plura beneficia dare paratus sum. Nam dilata os tuum, id est, desiderium tuum aperi ad recipiendum, et os corporale ad petendum, et implebo illud gratia mea, dando tibi quod postulas.
paras.en: [[80:11|For I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt|Ego enim sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti]][[Ex 20:2||]], and I am ready to give yet more benefits. For [[80:11|open thy mouth wide|dilata os tuum]], that is, open thy desire to receive, and thy bodily mouth to ask, [[80:11|and I will fill it|et implebo illud]] with my grace, giving thee what thou askest.

paras.t: Consequenter ostenditur populi ingratitudo. Et non audivit populus meus aure cordis vocem meam, id est verba præceptorum meorum ; et Israel non intendit mihi, id est, non advertit neque curavit me. Sed mirum apparet, quod Deus populum rebellem et inobedientem appellat populum suum, præsertim quum de tali populo per Osee prophetam dicat : Non populus meus vos, et ego non Deus vester. Et respondendum, sicut nunc sæpius dictum est, quod populus Judæorum (etiam reprobus) dicitur populus Dei, in quantum a Deo præ ceteris gentibus vocati erant, et multis beneficiis ejus honorificati. Ideo namque Dominus apud Jeremiam ait : Sicut adhæret lumbare ad lumbos viri, sic agglutinavi mihi domum Israel, ut esset mihi in populum, et in nomen, et in laudem, et in gloriam ; et non audierunt. Sic quoque dicuntur dilecti a Deo, secundum quod Dominus apud eumdem ait : Quid est, quod dilectus meus in domo mea fecit scelera multa? Non quod vere atque finaliter dilecti erant a Deo, de quo dictum est supra, Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem ; sed quantum ad beneficia eis a Deo exhibita in præsenti, dicuntur dilecti.
paras.en: Next the ingratitude of the people is shown. [[80:12|But my people heard not|Et non audivit populus meus]] with the ear of the heart [[80:12|my voice|vocem meam]], that is, the words of my commandments; [[80:12|and Israel hearkened not to me|et Israel non intendit mihi]], that is, did not heed me nor care for me. But it seems strange that God calls a rebellious and disobedient people his people, especially since he says of such a people through the prophet Osee: [[Osee 1:9|you are not my people, and I will not be yours|Non populus meus vos, et ego non Deus vester]]. We must answer, as has now often been said, that the Jewish people (even the reprobate) is called the people of God inasmuch as they had been called by God before the other nations and honoured with many of his benefits. For this is why the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 13:11|as the girdle sticketh close to the loins of a man|Sicut adhæret lumbare ad lumbos viri]], [[Jer 13:11|so have I brought close to me|sic agglutinavi mihi]] the house of Israel, [[Jer 13:11|that they might be my people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory|ut esset mihi in populum, et in nomen, et in laudem, et in gloriam]]; [[Jer 13:11|but they would not hear|et non audierunt]]. So too they are called beloved of God, as the Lord says in the same prophet: [[Jer 11:15|What is the meaning that my beloved hath wrought much wickedness in my house|Quid est, quod dilectus meus in domo mea fecit scelera multa]]? Not that they were truly and finally beloved of God, of whom it was said above: [[Ps 5:7|Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity|Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem]]; but they are called beloved with regard to the benefits shown them by God in the present life.

paras.t: Hujus autem ingratitudinis gravissima pœna mox subditur : Et dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum : id est, gratiam meam eis subtraxi : qua subtracta, non præservantur a culpa, sed concupiscentias suas sequuntur, et proprias cogitationes et inclinationes sectantur. Propter quod additur : ibunt in adinventionibus suis, id est, in erroribus suis et vitiis a se excogitatis vivent et perdurabunt.
paras.en: And the most grievous punishment of this ingratitude is added at once: [[80:13|So I let them go according to the desires of their heart|Et dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum]]: that is, I withdrew my grace from them; and once it is withdrawn they are not preserved from sin, but follow their concupiscences and pursue their own thoughts and inclinations. For which reason it is added: [[80:13|they shall walk in their own inventions|ibunt in adinventionibus suis]], that is, they will live and continue in their errors and in vices devised by themselves.

paras.t: Si populus meus audisset me, id est legem meam, Israel si in viis meis, id est in observantiis mandatorum meorum, ambulasset ; Pro nihilo, id est tanquam nihil seu gratis, forsitan, id est certitudinaliter, dummodo ipsi in viis meis perseverassent, inimicos eorum humiliassem, id est septem gentes terræ promissionis, et ceteros gentiles eorum hostes dejecissem, atque potestati eorum subjugassem, sicut per Moysen sæpe promisi ; et super tribulantes eos, id est super persecutores eorum, mitissem manum meam, id est, potestatem meam et ultionem justitiæ meæ extendissem.
paras.en: [[80:14|If my people had heard me|Si populus meus audisset me]], that is, my law, [[80:14|if Israel|Israel si]] [[80:14|had walked|ambulasset]] [[80:14|in my ways|in viis meis]], that is, in the keeping of my commandments; [[80:15|soon|Pro nihilo]] [the Latin, *pro nihilo forsitan*, is literally "for nothing, perhaps", and Denis glosses each part], that is, as though for nothing, or freely; *perhaps*, that is, certainly, provided they had persevered in my ways, [[80:15|have humbled their enemies|inimicos eorum humiliassem]], that is, I would have cast down the seven nations of the land of promise and the other gentiles their foes, and subjected them to their power, as I often promised by Moses[[Ex 3:8||]][[Ex 13:5||]][[Ex 23:23||]][[Ex 33:2||]] [the margin adds "and elsewhere"]; [[80:15|and laid my hand|mitissem manum meam]] [[80:15|on them that troubled them|super tribulantes eos]], that is, upon their persecutors, that is, I would have stretched out my power and the vengeance of my justice.

paras.t: Inimici Domini, id est Judæi ingrati : de quibus Moyses loquitur, Audite, rebelles et increduli ; mentiti sunt ei, id est ad injuriam ejus, quia non impleverunt quod spoponderunt dicentes, Omnia quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus. Nam paulo post vitulum aureum adoraverunt. Et erit tempus eorum in sæcula : id est, damnatio et pœna eorum in æternum durabit, quoniam in inferno sine fine cruciabuntur. Unde Dominus dixit ad Moysen : Ego in die ultionis visitabo et hoc peccatum eorum.
paras.en: [[80:16|The enemies of the Lord|Inimici Domini]], that is, the ungrateful Jews, of whom Moses speaks: [[Num 20:10|Hear, ye rebellious and incredulous|Audite, rebelles et increduli]]; [[80:16|have lied to him|mentiti sunt ei]], that is, to his injury, because they did not fulfil what they promised, saying: [[Ex 24:7|All things that the Lord hath spoken, we will do|Omnia quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus]]. For a little after, they worshipped the golden calf. [[80:16|And their time shall be for ever|Et erit tempus eorum in sæcula]]: that is, their damnation and punishment will last for ever, since they will be tormented in hell without end. Hence the Lord said to Moses: [[Ex 32:34|I in the day of revenge will visit this sin also of theirs|Ego in die ultionis visitabo et hoc peccatum eorum]].

paras.t: Et cibavit eos, id est non obstante prædicta ingratitudine Judæorum, Deus cibavit illos ex adipe frumenti, scilicet pane cœlesti seu manna : quod adeo dulce fuit, ac si de simila et adipe factum fuisset. Vel sic : Cibavit eos ex adipe frumenti : quoniam postquam ingressi sunt terram promissionis tritico abundantem, aluit eos pane de simila tritici facto. Et de petra melle saturavit eos, id est melle emanante de petra. Nam terra promissionis dicitur lacte et melle manare. Apes namque in rupibus terræ promissionis mellificant, et ita de locis petrosis mel satis copiose colligitur.
paras.en: [[80:17|And he fed them|Et cibavit eos]], that is, notwithstanding the aforesaid ingratitude of the Jews, God fed them [[80:17|with the fat of wheat|ex adipe frumenti]], namely with the bread of heaven, or manna, which was as sweet as if it had been made of fine flour and fat. Or thus: [[80:17|he fed them with the fat of wheat|Cibavit eos ex adipe frumenti]], because after they had entered the land of promise, abounding in wheat, he nourished them with bread made of fine wheat flour. And [[80:17|filled them with honey out of the rock|Et de petra melle saturavit eos]], that is, with honey flowing from the rock. For the land of promise is said to flow with milk and honey; for bees make honey in the rocks of the land of promise, and so honey is gathered quite plentifully from rocky places.

80.title: EXPLANATIO EJUSDEM PSALMI OCTOGESIMI TROPOLOGICA SIVE MORALIS.
80.title_en: Tropological or moral explanation of the same eightieth psalm.

paras.t: SPIRITUALEM denique intellectum sequendo, titulus psalmi hujus, in principio præcedentis expositionis positus, ita exponitur : Psalmus iste in finem, qui Christus est, nos dirigens, proponitur et cantatur ipsi Asaph, id est congregationi fidelium per Asaph designatæ ; et agit hic psalmus pro torcularibus, id est de tribulationibus, seu Ecclesiis pressura tribulationum afflictis, quibus mali separantur a bonis : quæ separatio designata est quinta sabbati, id est quinta die hebdomadæ : in qua ex aqua producti sunt pisces avesque ; remanseruntque pisces in aqua, et aves conscenderunt in aera. Per quod præfiguratum est, quod in Ecclesia Christi contingit. Omnes enim Christiani in fonte Baptismatis spiritualiter producuntur et regenerantur ; sed quidam eorum manent in terra transitoriis inhærendo, ceteri volant in altum amando cœlestia.
paras.en: Lastly, following the spiritual sense, the title of this psalm, set down at the beginning of the preceding exposition, is explained thus: this psalm is set forth and sung [[80:1|Unto the end|in finem]], who is Christ, directing us, [[80:1|for Asaph himself|ipsi Asaph]], that is, for the congregation of the faithful designated by Asaph; and this psalm treats [[80:1|for the winepresses|pro torcularibus]], that is, of tribulations, or of Churches afflicted by the pressure of tribulations, by which the wicked are separated from the good. This separation is designated by *on the fifth day of the week* [*quinta sabbati*: words of the title as Denis reads it, not in the Douay-Rheims], that is, on the fifth day of the week, on which fishes and birds were brought forth from the water; and the fishes remained in the water, while the birds went up into the air. By this was prefigured what comes to pass in the Church of Christ. For all Christians are spiritually brought forth and born again in the font of Baptism; but some of them remain on the earth by clinging to passing things, while the others fly on high by loving heavenly things.

paras.t: Itaque, o universi filii ecclesiasticæ congregationis, Exsultate Deo adjutori nostro, videlicet summæ Trinitati, simplici Deo, jubilate Deo Jacob, id est supplantantium vitia. Per Jacob namque, qui interpretatur supplantator, conculcatores vitiorum intelliguntur. Versiculus iste spirituali hilaritate redundat. Est enim exhortatio jucundissima, admonitio saluberrima, doctrina prorsus angelica. Quid enim tam cœliforme, angelicum, deiforme ac splendidum, sicut in Deo exsultare et Domino jubilare, congaudendo infinitæ perfectioni Creatoris, infinitæ beatitudini Divinitatis, infinitæ jucunditati supergloriosissimæ Trinitatis? Hoc nempe est præclarissimum exercitium summæ virtutis, videlicet caritatis divinæ, quo esse non potest sublimius in sæculo isto. Quanto enim dignitati et gloriæ Domini Dei nostri cordialius congratulamur, tanto eum ardentius diligere comprobamur; quo autem Deum calidiori mente amamus, eo deiformiores ac nobiliores consistimus, quoniam summa nobilitas mentis creatæ est amor divinus, id est actualis dilectio superbenedictæ Divinitatis.
paras.en: Therefore, O all you sons of the Church's congregation, [[80:2|Rejoice to God our helper|Exsultate Deo adjutori nostro]], namely to the supreme Trinity, the one simple God; [[80:2|sing aloud to the God of Jacob|jubilate Deo Jacob]], that is, of those who supplant vices. For by Jacob, which is interpreted *supplanter*, are understood those who trample vices underfoot. This little verse overflows with spiritual gladness. For it is a most joyful exhortation, a most wholesome admonition, a teaching altogether angelic. For what is so heavenly, angelic, godlike and splendid as to rejoice in God and to sing aloud to the Lord, rejoicing together with the infinite perfection of the Creator, the infinite beatitude of the Godhead, the infinite delight of the most supremely glorious Trinity? This indeed is the most excellent exercise of the highest virtue, namely of divine charity, than which nothing can be more sublime in this world. For the more heartily we rejoice with the dignity and glory of the Lord our God, the more ardently we are shown to love him; and the more fervent the mind with which we love God, the more godlike and noble we become, since the highest nobility of a created mind is divine love, that is, the actual love [that is, love in act, not only as a habit] of the supremely blessed Godhead.

paras.t: Sumite psalmum, id est, bonam operationem a gratia Dei accipite : quam operationem non nisi a Deo habere potestis, quoniam (sicut ait Apostolus) ipse est qui operatur in nobis et velle et perficere pro bona voluntate, id est ex sua voluntate benigna. Ad quem Isaias loquens : Domine, inquit, dabis pacem nobis; omnia enim opera nostra operatus es nobis. Unde et Christus ait discipulis : Sicut palmes a semetipso non potest ferre fructum, nisi manserit in vite; sic nec vos, nisi in me manseritis. Et date tympanum, id est, dulcem reddite sonum, Dei auribus beneplacentem : qui utique non est proprie sonus sensibilis atque exterior, sed intellectualis, videlicet mortificatio carnis, et castitas sancta, quæ etiam est odor bonus. Quemadmodum namque tympanum, id est corium in ligno expansum, non nisi percussum dulciter sonat; sic caro castigationibus pœnitentialium flagellorum lassata et attenuata, Domino placet, et sua operatio coram Altissimo sonat. Sumite quoque psalterium jucundum cum cithara. Psalterium quod a superioribus sonat, et decem chordas habet, designat Decalogum legis divinitus datum. Cithara vero habens sex chordas, et ab inferioribus sonans, significat sex opera misericordiæ. Est igitur sensus : Sumite psalterium jucundum cum cithara, id est, divinæ legis præcepta implete, vacando cœlestibus : sed cum cithara, quatenus simul exerceatis opera misericordiæ, quoniam non debetis sic esse intenti cœlestibus, ut negligatis succurrere proximorum necessitatibus.
paras.en: [[80:3|Take a psalm|Sumite psalmum]], that is, receive good working from the grace of God: a working which you cannot have except from God, since (as the Apostle says) it is he [[Phil 2:13|who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish, according to his good will|qui operatur in nobis et velle et perficere pro bona voluntate]] [the margin reads Philipp. 13; the verse is Phil 2:13; Denis has "in us"], that is, out of his own kindly will. Speaking to him Isaias says: [[Is 26:12|Lord|Domine]], he says, [[Is 26:12|thou wilt give us peace: for thou hast wrought all our works for us|dabis pacem nobis; omnia enim opera nostra operatus es nobis]]. Hence Christ too says to the disciples: [[John 15:4|As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abide in the vine, so neither can you, unless you abide in me|Sicut palmes a semetipso non potest ferre fructum, nisi manserit in vite; sic nec vos, nisi in me manseritis]]. [[80:3|and bring hither the timbrel|Et date tympanum]] [*date tympanum*, literally "give the timbrel"], that is, give back a sweet sound, well pleasing to God's ears: which is not properly a sensible and outward sound, but an intellectual one, namely the mortification of the flesh and holy chastity, which is also a good odour. For as a timbrel, that is, a hide stretched over wood, does not sound sweetly unless it is struck, so the flesh, wearied and worn down by the chastisements of penitential scourges, pleases the Lord, and its working sounds before the Most High. Take also [[80:3|the pleasant psaltery with the harp|psalterium jucundum cum cithara]]. The psaltery, which sounds from its upper part and has ten strings, designates the Decalogue of the law given by God. The harp, having six strings and sounding from its lower part, signifies the six works of mercy. The sense, then, is: Take [[80:3|the pleasant psaltery with the harp|psalterium jucundum cum cithara]], that is, fulfil the precepts of the divine law by giving yourselves to heavenly things; but *with the harp*, so that at the same time you practise the works of mercy, since you ought not to be so intent on heavenly things as to neglect to help the needs of your neighbours.

paras.t: Buccinate, o Christifideles, id est, audacter et amorose sonate Dei præconia, vestra peccata, et proximorum documenta, ita ut Deum laudetis, vos ipsos vituperetis, et proximos instruatis; in neomenia, id est in exordio illuminationis vestræ a Sole justitiæ, scilicet in insigni die solennitatis vestræ interioris, quando videlicet Spiritus Sanctus venit ad vos, et mansionem sibi facit in vobis : tunc enim gratiam vobis concessam, aliis libenter debetis communicare. Sic autem buccinate tuba, id est verbo Dei : quia præceptum in Israel est, id est, Ecclesiæ Christianorum Deum per fidem speculanti, divinitus jussum est taliter facere. Christus enim in Evangelio damnat servum, qui talentum sibi concessum abscondit. Et Paulus vult, ut singuli non quæ nostra sunt quæramus, sed quæ aliorum. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque? Denique excellentissimus apostolici ordinis princeps, evidentius atque præclarius loquens : Unusquisque, inquit, sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei.
paras.en: [[80:4|Blow up the trumpet|Buccinate]], O faithful of Christ, that is, sound boldly and lovingly the praises of God, your own sins, and instruction for your neighbours, so that you praise God, blame yourselves, and teach your neighbours; [[80:4|on the new moon|in neomenia]], that is, at the beginning of your enlightening by the Sun of justice, namely [[80:4|on the noted day of your solemnity|in insigni die solennitatis vestræ]] within you, when, that is, the Holy Ghost comes to you and makes his abode in you[[John 14:23||]]: for then you ought gladly to share with others the grace granted to you. In this way, then, [[80:4|Blow up the trumpet|buccinate tuba]], that is, with the word of God, [[80:5|For it is a commandment in Israel|quia præceptum in Israel est]]: that is, the Church of Christians, which beholds God by faith, has been commanded by God to do so [Israel is taken as "seeing God"]. For Christ in the Gospel condemns the servant who hid the talent granted him[[Matt 25:25||]] [the margin gives Matt. xxv, 24–30]. And Paul wills that each of us seek not the things that are ours, but those that are other men's[[1 Cor 10:24||]] [Denis's wording is closer to Phil 2:4]. For this reason it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 41:17|wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is there in them both?|Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?]][[Ecclus 20:32||]] [the margin gives both places; Denis's *abscondita* is the reading of 41:17]. Lastly the most excellent prince of the apostolic order, speaking more plainly and more clearly: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man|Unusquisque]], he says, [[1 Pet 4:10|hath received grace, ministering the same one to another: as good stewards of the manifold grace of God|sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei]].

paras.t: Testimonium in Joseph posuit illud, id est in populo ex gentilitate ad Christum converso, et Ecclesiæ addito. Joseph enim interpretatur augmentum; sicque per eum signantur ex gentibus Christo per fidem adaucti : et his Deus testatus est præceptum prædictum, ut patet ex auctoritatibus allegatis. Quum exiret de terra Ægypti, id est, quum gentiles in Christum credentes, egrederentur de pristinis suis obscuritatibus, vitiis et ignorantiis. Linguam quam non noverat, audivit, id est, tunc audire cœperunt evangelicam prædicationem, apostolicamque doctrinam, ante ipsis prorsus ignotam. Propter quod Athenienses ad Paulum dixerunt : Volumus scire quæ est hæc nova, quæ a te dicitur, doctrina. Nova enim quædam infers auribus nostris. Tunc quoque quum sic de Ægypto exiit hic populus, Deus divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus, id est a pondere vitiorum, a servitute peccati, a jugo mundi, carnis, atque diaboli. Talibus enim clamat Christus : Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos. Manus ejus, id est operationes populi hujus, antequam converteretur ad Deum, in cophino, id est in vasis immunditiarum ac sordium vitiorum, servierunt legi peccati, imo peccato ac dæmoni. Dum enim peccator vitiis immoratur, manus operationum suarum tenet in vase peccati, id est in actione inordinata, seu voluntate perversa, in quibus culpa fundatur.
paras.en: [[80:6|He ordained it for a testimony in Joseph|Testimonium in Joseph posuit illud]], that is, in the people converted to Christ from the gentiles and added to the Church. For Joseph is interpreted *increase*; and so by him are signified those from among the gentiles who have been added to Christ by faith: and to these God has testified the commandment spoken of, as is plain from the authorities cited. [[80:6|when he came out of the land of Egypt|Quum exiret de terra Ægypti]], that is, when the gentiles who believed in Christ went out of their former darkness, vices and ignorance. [[80:6|he heard a tongue which he knew not|Linguam quam non noverat, audivit]], that is, they then began to hear the preaching of the Gospel and the teaching of the Apostles, wholly unknown to them before. For this reason the Athenians said to Paul: [[Acts 17:19|May we know what this new doctrine is, which thou speakest of?|Volumus scire quæ est hæc nova, quæ a te dicitur, doctrina]] [Denis has *Volumus scire*, "We wish to know"] [[Acts 17:20|For thou bringest in certain new things to our ears|Nova enim quædam infers auribus nostris]]. Then too, when this people thus went out of Egypt, God [[80:7|removed his back from the burdens|divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus]], that is, from the weight of vices, from the bondage of sin, from the yoke of the world, the flesh and the devil. For to such Christ cries: [[Matt 11:28|Come to me all you that labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you|Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos]]. [[80:7|his hands|Manus ejus]], that is, the works of this people before it was converted to God, [[80:7|in baskets|in cophino]], that is, in vessels of uncleanness and of the filth of vices, [[80:7|had served|servierunt]] the law of sin, or rather sin and the devil. For while the sinner lingers in vices, he keeps the hands of his works in the vessel of sin, that is, in disordered action or a perverse will, in which guilt is grounded.

paras.t: Deinde Christus ait Ecclesiæ, cuilibetque devoto : In tribulatione, id est persecutione, tentatione, seu alia quacumque molestia, invocasti me : quod est tutissimum saluberrimumque remedium. Idcirco quandocumque affligimur, sive a dæmone, sive a malis hominibus, sive a propriis passionibus, Deum invocare debemus cum omni fiducia atque constantia, et ita efficiemur securi : nam exaudiemur, sicut subjungitur. Et liberavi te; exaudivi te in abscondito tempestatis, tempore diabolicæ suggestionis seu intimæ afflictionis, quando ad alium nullum confugere poteras. Denique hoc debet esse summa et unica consolatio omni afflicto, quod certissimum est Deum maxime adesse afflictis, quoniam promptus est succurrere eis, sicut superius dictum est : Juxta est Dominus his qui tribulato sunt corde. Inferius quoque ipse testatur : Cum ipso sum in tribulatione. Propterea viri perfecti in tribulationibus gaudent, et in eis libenter exsistunt propter præsentiam Dei, sed pro patientia et fortitudine animi Dominum deprecantur. Probavi te apud aquam Contradictionis, id est apud quamcumque adversitatem et resistentiam, qua tibi in bono resistitur ab hostibus tuæ salutis, videlicet mundo, carne et diabolo. Adversitas enim et resistentia, quam sustinet homo in via Dei ab his qui moliuntur eum a bono opere avertere, declarant an homo vere fideliterque Deo adhæreat. Unde Moyses ait: Adduxit te Dominus, ut affligeret atque tentaret, et notum fieret utrum custodires mandata illius, an non. Et ista est ratio cur Deus permittit famulos suos talia impedimenta pati, videlicet ut probentur, et innotescat utrum sincere quærant justitiam, sicque gratiam ampliorem acquirant, et aliis in exemplum proponantur. Propter quod scriptum est : Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos.
paras.en: Then Christ says to the Church and to every devout soul: [[80:8|in affliction|In tribulatione]], that is, in persecution, temptation, or any other trouble whatever, [[80:8|Thou calledst upon me|invocasti me]]: which is the safest and most wholesome remedy. Therefore whenever we are afflicted, whether by the devil, or by wicked men, or by our own passions, we ought to call upon God with all confidence and constancy, and so we shall be made secure; for we shall be heard, as follows: [[80:8|and I delivered thee|Et liberavi te]]; [[80:8|I heard thee in the secret place of tempest|exaudivi te in abscondito tempestatis]], in the time of the devil's suggestion or of inward affliction, when thou couldst flee to no one else. Indeed this ought to be the highest and only consolation of everyone afflicted: that it is most certain that God is most of all present to the afflicted, since he is ready to help them, as was said above: [[Ps 33:19|The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart|Juxta est Dominus his qui tribulato sunt corde]]. Further on, too, he testifies: [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione]]. Therefore perfect men rejoice in tribulations and willingly remain in them because of the presence of God, but they pray to the Lord for patience and fortitude of soul. [[80:8|I proved thee at the waters of contradiction|Probavi te apud aquam Contradictionis]], that is, at any adversity and resistance by which thou art resisted in good by the enemies of thy salvation, namely the world, the flesh and the devil. For the adversity and resistance which a man endures in the way of God from those who strive to turn him away from good works show whether he truly and faithfully cleaves to God. Hence Moses says: [[Deut 8:2|the Lord thy God hath brought thee|Adduxit te Dominus]] [[Deut 8:2|to afflict thee and to prove thee, and that the things that were known in thy heart might be made known, whether thou wouldst keep his commandments or no|ut affligeret atque tentaret, et notum fieret utrum custodires mandata illius, an non]]. And this is the reason why God permits his servants to suffer such hindrances: that they may be proved, and it may be made known whether they sincerely seek justice, and so may gain more abundant grace and be set forth to others as an example. For this reason it is written: [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace, he hath proved them, and as a victim of a holocaust, he hath received them|Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit eos]] [Denis reads "the Lord hath proved the elect"].

paras.t: Audi, populus meus, qui a me Christianus vocaris; qui etiam Israel diceris, id est Deum per fidem conspiciens. Tu ergo si audieris me, implendo præcepta mea, ita ut Deum tota anima, toto corde, et tota fortitudine diligas, non erit in te Deus recens, id est, me non derelinques, nec aliis magis quam mihi adhærebis. Non servies creaturæ potius quam Creatori; non magis amabis ventris ingluviem, carnis luxuriam, mundi honorem, temporalia bona sive pecuniam, quam me summum atque incommutabile bonum. Qui enim castitatem relinquit et voluptati deservit, recentem suscipit deum : quoniam luxuriosi deus est sua dilecta, gulosi deus est venter; avari, pecunia. Quod enim quis amplius cogitat, amat et colit, hoc deus ipsius esse convincitur. Ego enim Unigenitus Dei propter te incarnatus, sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti, id est de hoc sæculo nequam, videlicet de caligine culpæ et tenebris ignorantiæ, per mortis meæ meritum et sanguinis pretium, per gratiam baptismalem, per virtutum infusionem, et Spiritus Sancti multiplicem illustrationem.
paras.en: [[80:9|Hear, O my people|Audi, populus meus]], who art called Christian after me; who art also called Israel, that is, beholding God by faith. Thou therefore, [[80:9|if thou wilt hearken to me|si audieris me]] by fulfilling my precepts, so as to love God with thy whole soul, thy whole heart and thy whole strength[[Deut 6:5||]], [[80:10|there shall be no new god in thee|non erit in te Deus recens]], that is, thou wilt not forsake me, nor cleave to others more than to me. Thou shalt not serve the creature rather than the Creator[[Rom 1:25||]]; thou shalt not love the greed of the belly, the lust of the flesh, the honour of the world, temporal goods or money more than me, the highest and unchangeable good. For he who abandons chastity and gives himself up to pleasure takes up a new god: since the god of the lustful man is his beloved, the god of the glutton is his belly[[Phil 3:19||]], and the god of the covetous man is money. For what a man thinks of, loves and worships most, that is shown to be his god. [[80:11|For I|Ego enim]], the Only-begotten of God made flesh for thee, [[80:11|am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt|sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti]], that is, out of this wicked world[[Gal 1:4||]], namely out of the darkness of guilt and the shadows of ignorance, by the merit of my death and the price of my blood, by the grace of Baptism, by the infusion of the virtues, and by the manifold enlightening of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Dilata os tuum, et implebo illud, id est, ad gratiam te dispone, et eam recipies. Misericordiam meam implora, et faciam tecum misericordiam; invita me ad cordis tui hospitium, et ingrediar illud. Ego enim sto ad ostium, et pulso. Ora pro illuminatione interna, et dabo tibi sapientiæ claritatem, quemadmodum spondet Apostolus meus, dicens : Si quis indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, et dabitur ei. Postulet autem in fide nihil hæsitans. Ad minus enim recipiet illam quæ est donum Spiritus Sancti, quam habet omnis qui gratiam gratum facientem sortitus est. Itaque, Dilata os tuum, id est, aperi cor tuum, obicemque depone, et implebo illud, quia non est abbreviata manus mea, ut salvare non valeat.
paras.en: [[80:11|open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it|Dilata os tuum, et implebo illud]], that is, dispose thyself for grace, and thou shalt receive it. Implore my mercy, and I will shew mercy to thee; invite me to the lodging of thy heart, and I will enter it. For [[Apoc 3:20|I stand at the gate and knock|sto ad ostium, et pulso]]. Pray for inward enlightening, and I will give thee the clearness of wisdom, as my Apostle promises, saying: [[Jas 1:5|if any of you want wisdom, let him ask of God|Si quis indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo]], [[Jas 1:5|And it shall be given him|et dabitur ei]]. [[Jas 1:6|But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering|Postulet autem in fide nihil hæsitans]]. For at the least he will receive that wisdom which is a gift of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]], which everyone has who has obtained sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God]. And so, [[80:11|open thy mouth wide|Dilata os tuum]], that is, open thy heart and lay aside the obstacle, and I will fill it; for my hand is not shortened that it cannot save[[Is 59:1||]].

paras.t: Et non audivit populus meus, qui solo nomine Christianus est, seu per fidem, et non per caritatem; qui se dicit nosse Deum, et factis negat ; vocem meam, id est præcepta et exhortationem sacræ Scripturæ. Sic enim reprobi dicuntur populus Christi, quomodo ipse in Evangelio ait cuidam : Amice, quomodo huc intrasti, non habens vestem nuptialem ? Et sicut de aliquibus dicitur : In propria venit, et sui eum non receperunt.
paras.en: [[80:12|But my people heard not|Et non audivit populus meus]], who are Christian in name only, or by faith and not by charity; who say they know God, and deny him by their deeds[[Tit 1:16||]]; [[80:12|my voice|vocem meam]], that is, the precepts and exhortation of Holy Scripture. For the reprobate are called the people of Christ in the way that he himself in the Gospel says to someone: [[Matt 22:12|Friend, how camest thou in hither not having on a wedding garment?|Amice, quomodo huc intrasti, non habens vestem nuptialem]] And as it is said of some: [[John 1:11|He came unto his own: and his own received him not|In propria venit, et sui eum non receperunt]].

paras.t: Idcirco, et dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum. Hæc est maxima ultio Dei, dum hominem exigentibus suis peccatis sibi ipsi relinquit. Hoc enim tam malum est, quam bonum est a Domino conservari, in præsenti vita filialiter corrigi, a vitiis cohiberi. Unde certissimum signum divinæ reprobationis atque futuræ damnationis est, nunc in omnibus prosperari ad libitum, a Deo relinqui juxta proprium desiderium, nec flagellari cum filiis adoptionis. Ideo namque Dominus ait : Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo. Apostolus quoque ad Hebræos : Quis filius quem non corripit pater ? Quod si extra disciplinam estis, cujus participes facti sunt omnes : ergo adulteri, et non filii estis. Et hoc quoque Salomon monet : Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias ; et ne deficias, quum ab eo corriperis. Quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi. Si ergo beati esse optamus, in præsenti vita pro nostris excessibus castigari desideremus, pensantes prudentissima mente illud in libro beati Job : Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino. Increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes, quia ipse vulnerat, et medetur. Hinc insuper angelus dixit Tobiæ : Quia acceptus eras Domino, necesse fuit ut tentatio probaret te. Unde ex persona omnium electorum testatur alia scriptura : Non sicut in aliis nationibus Dominus patienter exspectat, ut eas, quum judicii dies advenerit, in plenitudine peccatorum puniat : ita et in nobis statuit, ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis, ita demum in nos vindicet. Propter quod nunquam misericordiam suam a nobis amovet ; corripiens vero in adversis, populum suum non derelinquit. His autem verbis præmittit quod sæpius allegatum recordor : Etenim multo tempore non sinere peccatoribus ex sententia agere, sed statim ultiones adhibere, magni beneficii est indicium.
paras.en: Therefore, [[80:13|So I let them go according to the desires of their heart|et dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum]]. This is the greatest vengeance of God, when, as his sins demand, he leaves a man to himself. For this is as evil as it is good to be kept by the Lord, to be corrected as a son in the present life, to be held back from vices. Hence the surest sign of divine reprobation and of future damnation is to prosper now in all things at one's pleasure, to be left by God to one's own desire, and not to be scourged with the sons of adoption. For this is why the Lord says: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo]]. The Apostle too, to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:7|what son is there whom the father doth not correct?|Quis filius quem non corripit pater]] [[Heb 12:8|But if you be without chastisement, whereof all are made partakers, then are you bastards and not sons|Quod si extra disciplinam estis, cujus participes facti sunt omnes : ergo adulteri, et non filii estis]]. And Solomon too gives this warning: [[Prov 3:11|My son, reject not the correction of the Lord: and do not faint when thou art chastised by him|Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias ; et ne deficias, quum ab eo corriperis]]. [[Prov 3:12|For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth: and as a father in the son he pleaseth himself|Quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi]]. If then we long to be blessed, let us desire to be chastised in the present life for our excesses, weighing with a most prudent mind that saying in the book of blessed Job: [[Job 5:17|Blessed is the man whom God correcteth: refuse not, therefore, the chastising of the Lord|Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino. Increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes]] [[Job 5:18|For he woundeth, and cureth|quia ipse vulnerat, et medetur]]. Hence, moreover, the angel said to Tobias: [[Tob 12:13|because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove thee|Quia acceptus eras Domino, necesse fuit ut tentatio probaret te]]. Hence another scripture testifies in the person of all the elect: [[2 Mach 6:14|not as with other nations|Non sicut in aliis nationibus]] [[2 Mach 6:14|whom the Lord patiently expecteth, that when the day of judgment shall come, he may punish them in the fulness of their sins|Dominus patienter exspectat, ut eas, quum judicii dies advenerit, in plenitudine peccatorum puniat]] [[2 Mach 6:15|Doth he also deal with us, so as to suffer our sins to come to their height, and then take vengeance on us|ita et in nobis statuit, ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis, ita demum in nos vindicet]]. [[2 Mach 6:16|And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us: but though he chastise his people with adversity he forsaketh them not|Propter quod nunquam misericordiam suam a nobis amovet ; corripiens vero in adversis, populum suum non derelinquit]]. And before these words it sets what I remember having cited quite often: [[2 Mach 6:13|For it is a token of great goodness, when sinners are not suffered to go on in their ways for a long time, but are presently punished|Etenim multo tempore non sinere peccatoribus ex sententia agere, sed statim ultiones adhibere, magni beneficii est indicium]].

paras.t: Si populus meus audisset, etc., pro nihilo forsitan inimicos eorum visibiles et invisibiles humiliassem : quoniam ego superbos humilio, et ego dæmones superbientes vehementer humilio, dum eos a servis meis humilibus vinci fugarique facio. Ideo namque dicit Apostolus : Deus pacis conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter. Et super tribulantes eos misissem manum meam, electos protegendo, et illos opprimendo, saltem post terminum vitæ præsentis.
paras.en: [[80:14|If my people had heard me|Si populus meus audisset]], etc., [[80:15|I should soon have humbled their enemies|pro nihilo forsitan inimicos eorum visibiles et invisibiles humiliassem]], visible and invisible: since I humble the proud, and I vehemently humble the proud demons, when I make them be overcome and put to flight by my humble servants. For this is why the Apostle says: [[Rom 16:20|the God of peace crush Satan under your feet speedily|Deus pacis conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter]] [Denis has *conteret*, "will crush"]. [[80:15|and laid my hand on them that troubled them|Et super tribulantes eos misissem manum meam]], by protecting the elect and crushing those others, at least after the end of the present life.

paras.t: Inimici Domini, id est mali Christiani : de quibus ait in Evangelio, Inimicos meos, qui noluerunt me super se regnare, adducite huc, et occidite coram me ; mentiti sunt ei, id est, promissionem illam fregerunt, quam in fonte Baptismatis fecerunt, promittentes se abrenuntiaturos Satanæ et ejus operibus. Omnes quoque, qui post confessionem, pœnitentiam et sacram communionem, ad pristina vitia revertuntur, nec student coram Deo ambulare sollicite, inimici sunt Christi, mentiunturque ei. Et erit tempus damnationis eorum in sæcula, id est in æternum, quoniam ibunt in ignem æternum. Non est tamen hoc ita sumendum, quasi post diem extremi judicii tempus erit. Nam primi mobilis motu cessante, cessabit et tempus, juxta illud in Apocalypsi : Angelus levavit manum suam ad cœlum, et juravit per Viventem in sæculorum sæcula, quia tempus ultra non erit.
paras.en: [[80:16|The enemies of the Lord|Inimici Domini]], that is, wicked Christians, of whom he says in the Gospel: [[Luke 19:27|those my enemies, who would not have me reign over them, bring them hither and kill them before me|Inimicos meos, qui noluerunt me super se regnare, adducite huc, et occidite coram me]]; [[80:16|have lied to him|mentiti sunt ei]], that is, they have broken the promise they made in the font of Baptism, when they promised to renounce Satan and his works. All those too who after confession, penance and holy communion go back to their former vices, and do not take care to walk solicitously before God[[Mich 6:8||]], are enemies of Christ and lie to him. [[80:16|and their time shall be for ever|Et erit tempus damnationis eorum in sæcula]] [Denis reads *tempus damnationis eorum*, "the time of their damnation"], that is, for eternity, since they shall go into everlasting fire. This is not, however, to be taken as if there will be time after the day of the last judgment. For when the motion of the first movable [that is, the outermost heaven, whose turning was held to measure all time] ceases, time too will cease, according to that saying in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 10:5|the angel|Angelus]] [[Apoc 10:5|lifted up his hand to heaven|levavit manum suam ad cœlum]], [[Apoc 10:6|And he swore by him that liveth for ever and ever|et juravit per Viventem in sæculorum sæcula]]: [[Apoc 10:6|That time shall be no longer|quia tempus ultra non erit]].

paras.t: Et cibavit Christus eos, scilicet Christianos, ex adipe frumenti, id est Sacramento corporis sui sub forma panis triticei ; et de petra melle : id est, mel quo designatur dulcis effectus Sacramenti corporis Christi, videlicet consolatio spiritualis, infusio gratiæ sacramentalis, impinguatio mentis : hoc melle fluente de petra, id est Christo, seu merito passionis et sanguinis ejus (nam per meritum Christi datur nobis quidquid gratiæ participamus), saturavit eos, saturitate interiori, dando eis desiderium cordis sui.
paras.en: [[80:17|And he fed|Et cibavit]] Christ [[80:17|them|eos]], namely Christians, [[80:17|with the fat of wheat|ex adipe frumenti]], that is, with the Sacrament of his body under the form of wheaten bread; and [[80:17|with honey out of the rock|et de petra melle]]: that is, the honey by which is designated the sweet effect of the Sacrament of Christ's body, namely spiritual consolation, the infusion of sacramental grace, the enriching of the mind: with this honey flowing from the rock, that is, from Christ, or from the merit of his passion and blood (for by the merit of Christ is given us whatever grace we share in), he [[80:17|filled them|saturavit eos]] with an inward fullness, giving them the desire of their heart.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum spirituali doctrina repletum, et divina beneficia recolentem, hominum ingratitudinem, Dei quoque vindictam breviter commemorantem, audivimus. Elaboremus itaque omnia hæc ad nostram informationem trahere, Deo exsultare et jubilare, divinorum beneficiorum reminisci, Sacramenti Christi gratiam adipisci, summe ac diligentissime præcaventes, ne tam inæstimabilibus beneficiis Christi inveniamur ingrati. Quæ autem nunc omissa sunt, in præcedenti expositione patent.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a psalm full of spiritual teaching, recalling the divine benefits and briefly recounting the ingratitude of men and also the vengeance of God. Let us strive, then, to draw all these things to our own instruction: to rejoice and sing aloud to God, to remember the divine benefits, to obtain the grace of Christ's Sacrament, taking the greatest and most diligent care not to be found ungrateful for such inestimable benefits of Christ. What has been left out now is set out in the preceding exposition.

paras.t: Precatio. Fac, Domine, populum tuum vocem tuam audire ; dilata os nostrum, et imple illud laude gratiæ tuæ : ut in tribulatione præsentis vitæ te invocantes nos exaudias, et ab omni impetu inimicorum ac tempestatis æternæ subducas.
paras.en: Prayer. Make thy people, O Lord, hear thy voice; open wide our mouth, and fill it with the praise of thy grace: that thou mayest hear us when we call upon thee in the tribulation of this present life, and withdraw us from every assault of enemies and of the everlasting tempest.

81.title: ELUCIDATIO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI PRIMI : DEUS STETIT IN SYNAGOGA DEORUM.
81.title_en: Explanation of the eighty-first psalm: God hath stood in the congregation of gods.

paras.t: Brevis hic psalmus, brevi et facili titulo prænotatur, dum dicitur, Psalmus Asaph. Dicitur enim Psalmus Asaph, vel quia ab eo compositus est, vel quoniam congregationi per Asaph designatæ proponitur. Ad litteram quoque dicitur psalmus iste esse conscriptus contra judices injustos, eorum perversitatem redarguens, divinamque justitiam contra eorum injustitiam postulans.
paras.en: This short psalm is headed by a short and easy title, in that it is called [[81:1|A psalm for Asaph|Psalmus Asaph]] [Latin *Psalmus Asaph*, which can mean "of Asaph" or "for Asaph"]. For it is called a psalm of Asaph either because it was composed by him, or because it is set before the congregation signified by Asaph. According to the letter, too, this psalm is said to have been written against unjust judges, rebuking their perversity and calling for God's justice against their injustice.

paras.t: Ait ergo: Deus stetit in synagoga deorum. Deus incorporeus et immensus, in quo nullus est situs aut locus secundum naturam divinitatis, dicitur in synagoga deorum (id est in congregationibus judicum) stetisse et stare, quoniam ipse ubique est, et omnium verba ac opera intuetur, pensat et judicat: maxime tamen et distinctissime judicum corda, verba et facta considerat. Dicuntur autem judices dii, juxta illud in Exodo: Ad deos utriusque causa perveniet, id est ad judices. Unde et iterum Moyses: Diis, inquit, non detrahes. In medio autem, id est, Deus in medio universorum exsistens; vel, In medio, id est secundum æqualitatem justitiæ; deos, id est judices, dijudicat, id est, impios judices reprobat, et bonos a malis discernit. Unde in libro Sapientiæ scriptum est: Audite, reges; et discite, judices finium terræ. Quoniam data est vobis a Deo potestas, qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes vestras scrutabitur: quoniam quum essetis ministri regni illius, non recte judicastis, neque custodistis legem justitiæ. Horrende et cito apparebit vobis, quoniam judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet.
paras.en: He says, then: [[81:1|God hath stood in the congregation of gods|Deus stetit in synagoga deorum]]. God, who is without body and without measure, and in whom, according to the nature of the Godhead, there is no position or place, is said to have stood and to stand [[81:1|in the congregation of gods|in synagoga deorum]] (that is, in the assemblies of judges), because he is everywhere, and beholds, weighs and judges the words and works of all; but most of all, and most distinctly, he considers the hearts, words and deeds of judges. Now judges are called gods, according to that saying in Exodus: [[Ex 22:9|the cause of both parties shall come to the gods|Ad deos utriusque causa perveniet]], that is, to the judges. Whence Moses again: [[Ex 22:28|Thou shalt not speak ill|non detrahes]], he says, [[Ex 22:28|of the gods|Diis]]. And [[81:1|being in the midst of them|In medio autem]], that is, God being in the midst of all things; or, [[81:1|in the midst|In medio]], that is, according to the evenness of justice; [[81:1|he judgeth|dijudicat]] [[81:1|gods|deos]], that is, judges: that is, he condemns wicked judges, and distinguishes the good from the bad. Whence it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 6:2|Hear, therefore, ye kings|Audite, reges]]; [[Wis 6:2|learn ye that are judges of the ends of the earth|discite, judices finium terræ]]. [[Wis 6:4|For power is given you by the Lord|Quoniam data est vobis a Deo potestas]], [[Wis 6:4|who will examine your works: and search out your thoughts|qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes vestras scrutabitur]]: [[Wis 6:5|Because being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged rightly, nor kept the law of justice|quoniam quum essetis ministri regni illius, non recte judicastis, neque custodistis legem justitiæ]]. [[Wis 6:6|Horribly and speedily will he appear to you: for a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule.|Horrende et cito apparebit vobis, quoniam judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet]]

paras.t: Usquequo, o judices impii, judicatis judicio approbationis iniquitatem, illam excusando, laudando aut occultando, et facies peccatorum sumitis, id est, personas malorum acceptatis, justificando causam eorum amore propinquitatis aut munerum, vel timore potestatis ipsorum? Hoc valde iniquum est, et contra documentum gloriosi regis Josaphat, cujus verba omnium judicum plenissime instructiva sunt. Scriptum est enim de eo: Præcepit Josaphat judicibus: Videte quid faciatis. Non enim hominum judicium exercetis, sed Domini; et quodcumque judicaveritis, in vos redundabit. Sit timor Domini vobiscum, et cum diligentia cuncta facite.
paras.en: [[81:2|How long|Usquequo]], O wicked judges, [[81:2|will you judge unjustly|judicatis judicio approbationis iniquitatem]] [Latin *judicatis iniquitatem*, literally "do you judge iniquity"], that is, pass iniquity with a judgment of approval, excusing, praising or concealing it, [[81:2|and accept the persons of the wicked|et facies peccatorum sumitis]], that is, show favour to the persons of evil men, justifying their cause out of love of kinship or of gifts, or out of fear of their power? This is very unjust, and against the teaching of the glorious king Josaphat, whose words are most fully instructive for all judges. For it is written of him: Josaphat charged the judges: [[2 Par 19:6|Take heed what you do: for you exercise not the judgment of man, but of the Lord: and whatsoever you judge, it shall redound to you|Videte quid faciatis. Non enim hominum judicium exercetis, sed Domini; et quodcumque judicaveritis, in vos redundabit]]. [[2 Par 19:7|Let the fear of the Lord be with you, and do all things with diligence|Sit timor Domini vobiscum, et cum diligentia cuncta facite]].

paras.t: Deinde Prophêta admonet judices ad emendationem. Judicate, id est, justum judicium facite, egeno et pupillo, qui se ipsos defendere nequeunt contra potentes et divites; humilem et pauperem spiritu, non avarum aut impium, justificate, id est, justum esse dictate, sicut veraciter est. Eripite pauperem de violenta impetitione potentis, et egenum de manu, id est injusta potestate, peccatoris liberate.
paras.en: Next the Prophet admonishes the judges to amend. [[81:3|Judge|Judicate]], that is, give just judgment, [[81:3|for the needy and fatherless|egeno et pupillo]], who cannot defend themselves against the powerful and the rich; [[81:3|do justice to|justificate]] [[81:3|the humble and the poor|humilem et pauperem]] in spirit, not the covetous or the wicked: that is, declare him just, as he truly is [Latin *justificate*, "justify"]. [[81:4|Rescue the poor|Eripite pauperem]] from the violent assault of the powerful, [[81:4|and deliver the needy out of the hand|et egenum de manu]], that is, out of the unjust power, [[81:4|of the sinner|peccatoris liberate]].

paras.t: Talis judex erat beatus Job, qui de se ipso testatur: Quum sederem quasi rex circumstante exercitu, eram tamen mœrentium consolator. Oculus fui cæco, et pes claudo. Pater eram pauperum, et causam quam ignorabam, diligentissime investigabam. Et hoc est quod Dominus admonet apud Isaiam: Quærite judicium, subvenite oppresso, judicate pupillo, defendite viduam.
paras.en: Such a judge was blessed Job, who testifies of himself: [[Job 29:25|when I sat as a king, with his army standing about him, yet I was a comforter of them that mourned|Quum sederem quasi rex circumstante exercitu, eram tamen mœrentium consolator]] [the margin gives Job xxix, 15, 16; these first words are from Job 29:25]. [[Job 29:15|I was an eye to the blind, and a foot to the lame.|Oculus fui cæco, et pes claudo]] [[Job 29:16|I was the father of the poor: and the cause which I knew not, I searched out most diligently.|Pater eram pauperum, et causam quam ignorabam, diligentissime investigabam]] And this is what the Lord urges in Isaias: [[Is 1:17|seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge for the fatherless, defend the widow|Quærite judicium, subvenite oppresso, judicate pupillo, defendite viduam]].

paras.t: Consequenter inducitur causa erroris et injustitiæ judicum injustorum. Nescierunt regulas juris, neque intellexerunt subtiliter intentionem legislatoris seu legum; sed sicut sonant, sic eas intelligunt: in tenebris cordis et operum, id est in cogitationibus rudibus atque injustis operibus, ambulant; movebuntur, id est, Christum judicem formidabunt, saltem in die judicii, omnia fundamenta terræ, id est omnes principes terreni, qui aliorum fundamenta atque columnæ esse deberent. Vel. Movebuntur omnia fundamenta terræ, id est, elementum terræ movebitur: quoniam, ut dicit Sapiens, Deus armabit creaturam ad ultionem inimicorum, et pugnabit cum illo orbis terrarum contra insensatos.
paras.en: Next is brought in the cause of the error and injustice of unjust judges. [[81:5|They have not known|Nescierunt]] the rules of law, [[81:5|nor understood|neque intellexerunt]] with any subtlety the intention of the lawgiver or of the laws; but as they sound, so they understand them; [[81:5|they walk on|ambulant]] [[81:5|in darkness|in tenebris]] of heart and of works, that is, in crude thoughts and unjust works; [[81:5|all the foundations of the earth|omnia fundamenta terræ]], that is, all earthly princes, who ought to be the foundations and pillars of others, [[81:5|shall be moved|movebuntur]], that is, shall dread Christ the judge, at least on the day of judgment. Or: [[81:5|all the foundations of the earth shall be moved|Movebuntur omnia fundamenta terræ]], that is, the element of earth shall be moved[[Luke 21:26||]]: because, as the Wise Man says, God [[Wis 5:18|will arm the creature for the revenge of his enemies|armabit creaturam ad ultionem inimicorum]], [[Wis 5:21|and the whole world shall fight with him against the unwise|et pugnabit cum illo orbis terrarum contra insensatos]].

paras.t: Quamvis, o judices mali, tam indigni sitis propter vestram abusionem atque malitiam, tamen Ego dixi: Dii estis, quia per Moysen vocavi vos deos, propter potestatem desuper vobis datam, et quia ad vos sermo Dei dirigitur. Hæc verba Christus allegat, loquens Judæis: In lege (inquit) vestra scriptum est: Ego dixi, Dii estis. Quod quare dicatur, subjungit: Illos dixit deos, ad quos sermo Dei factus est.
paras.en: Though you, O evil judges, are so unworthy because of your abuse of power and your malice, yet [[81:6|I have said: You are gods|Ego dixi: Dii estis]], since through Moses I called you gods[[Ex 22:28||]], because of the power given you from above, and because the word of God is addressed to you. Christ cites these words, speaking to the Jews: In your law (he says) it is written: [[John 10:34|I said, you are gods|Ego dixi, Dii estis]]. And why this is said, he adds: [[John 10:35|he called them gods to whom the word of God was spoken|Illos dixit deos, ad quos sermo Dei factus est]].

paras.t: Dicuntur autem judices dii, non per naturam, sed per divinæ proprietatis participationem, videlicet quoniam aliis providere et præesse debent: quod Deo proprie competit. Et filii excelsi omnes. Hoc dupliciter accipi potest, secundum quod excelsi, accipi potest singulariter et pluraliter. Si enim singulariter accipiatur, sensus est: Vos, judices, estis filii Excelsi, scilicet Dei sublimis, quia ad ejus imaginem conditi estis. Si vero sumatur pluraliter, sensus est: Vos judices estis filii excelsi, id est sublimes, quoniam ceteris filiis hominum præsidetis ac imperatis.
paras.en: Now judges are called gods, not by nature, but by a sharing in a property of God, namely because they must provide for others and rule over them, which belongs properly to God. [[81:6|and all of you the sons of the most High|Et filii excelsi omnes]]. This can be taken in two ways, according as *excelsi* can be taken as singular or as plural [that is, as "of the Most High" or as "high, exalted ones"]. For if it is taken as singular, the sense is: You, judges, are sons of the Most High, that is, of God on high, because you were made to his image[[Gen 1:27||]]. But if it is taken as plural, the sense is: You judges are high sons, that is, exalted ones, because you preside over and command the other sons of men.

paras.t: Vos autem sicut homines ceteri moriemini, in anima dum peccaveritis, atque in corpore dum hora a Deo præfixa advenerit; nec poterit vos a morte eripere vestra potestas; et sicut unus de principibus, id est angelis apostaticis et superbis, cadetis, nunc in foveam culpæ et postmodum in lacum mortis æternæ, nisi modo vixeritis juste.
paras.en: [[81:7|But you like men|Vos autem sicut homines]], the rest of them, [[81:7|shall die|moriemini]]: in the soul when you sin, and in the body when the hour fixed by God has come; nor will your power be able to snatch you from death; and [[81:7|like one of the princes|et sicut unus de principibus]], that is, the apostate and proud angels, you [[81:7|shall fall|cadetis]], now into the pit of sin and afterwards into the lake of eternal death, unless you now live justly.

paras.t: Et quoniam ultio ista a nullo infligi potest nisi a Deo, qui solus est Dominus dominorum, et princeps ac judex regum ac judicum terræ; ideo, quatenus nullum malum maneat impunitum, Asaph implorat divinum judicium. Surge, Deus, id est, ad actum justitiæ tuæ procede, sine motu ac mutatione; judica terram, id est omnes habitantes in terra, seu homines universos, per Jesum Christum quem constituisti judicem universorum; quoniam tu hereditabis in omnibus gentibus: id est, omnes gentes tanquam hereditatem quamdam tibi subjicies, præsertim in die judicii, quia ex tunc erunt electi perfecte immobiliterque subjecti ordini tuæ misericordiæ, reprobi vero ordini tuæ justitiæ: quoniam culpa tunc erit per pœnam ad quamdam justam ordinationem redacta.
paras.en: And since this vengeance can be inflicted by none but God, who alone is [[Apoc 17:14|Lord of lords|Dominus dominorum]], and the prince and judge of the kings and judges of the earth[[Apoc 1:5||]][[Heb 12:23||]], therefore, so that no evil may remain unpunished, Asaph implores the judgment of God. [[81:8|Arise, O God|Surge, Deus]], that is, go forth to the act of thy justice, without motion or change; [[81:8|judge thou the earth|judica terram]], that is, all who dwell on the earth, or all men, through Jesus Christ, whom thou hast appointed judge of all[[Acts 10:42||]]; [[81:8|for thou shalt inherit among all the nations|quoniam tu hereditabis in omnibus gentibus]]: that is, thou shalt subject all nations to thyself as a kind of inheritance, especially on the day of judgment, because from then on the elect will be perfectly and immovably subject to the order of thy mercy, and the reprobate to the order of thy justice: since sin will then have been brought by punishment into a certain just order.

paras.t: Augustinus autem et eum sequentes, exponunt hunc psalmum de Christo et sacerdotibus ac Scribis Judæorum, ut sit sensus: Deus, id est Christus Dei Filius homo factus: de quo ait Joannes, Hic est verus Deus et vita æterna; stetit corporalibus pedibus suis in synagoga deorum: quia frequenter in synagogis ac templo Judæorum prædicavit, atque miracula fecit, quemadmodum dixit ad Annam: Ego semper docui in synagoga et in templo, quo omnes Judæi conveniunt. Et quum factus esset annorum duodecim, inventus in templo a Matre, dixit: Nesciebatis quia in his quæ Patris mei sunt, oportet me esse? Quod etiam a Malachia prophetatum est ita: Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis. Dicuntur autem sacerdotes dii, propter rationem prædictam, quia erant principes et judices populi. In medio autem synagogæ Christus Deus et homo, deos, id est sacerdotes et primos Judæorum, dijudicat, id est, redarguit, reprobat et condemnat. Sæpe enim (ut Evangelistæ testantur) Christus in templo sacerdotes increpavit. Propter quod Malachias de Christo loquens: Ipse, inquit, quasi ignis conflans, et quasi herba fullonum, etc., purgabit filios Levi, et colabit eos quasi aurum.
paras.en: Augustine, however, and those who follow him, expound this psalm of Christ and of the priests and Scribes of the Jews, so that the sense is: [[81:1|God|Deus]], that is, Christ, the Son of God made man, of whom John says: [[1 John 5:20|This is the true God and life eternal|Hic est verus Deus et vita æterna]]; [[81:1|hath stood|stetit]] on his bodily feet [[81:1|in the congregation of gods|in synagoga deorum]], because he often preached and worked miracles in the synagogues and temple of the Jews, as he said to Annas: [[John 18:20|I have always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, whither all the Jews resort|Ego semper docui in synagoga et in templo, quo omnes Judæi conveniunt]]. And when he was twelve years old and was found by his Mother in the temple, he said: [[Luke 2:49|Did you not know that I must be about my father's business?|Nesciebatis quia in his quæ Patris mei sunt, oportet me esse?]] This was also prophesied by Malachias, thus: [[Mal 3:1|presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple|Statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis]]. Now the priests are called gods for the reason given above, because they were the princes and judges of the people; and [[81:1|in the midst|In medio autem]] of the synagogue Christ, God and man, [[81:1|judgeth|dijudicat]], that is, rebukes, rejects and condemns, [[81:1|gods|deos]], that is, the priests and the chief men of the Jews. For (as the Evangelists testify) Christ often rebuked the priests in the temple[[Matt 23:1||]]. Wherefore Malachias, speaking of Christ: [[Mal 3:2|he|Ipse]], he says, [[Mal 3:2|is like a refining fire, and like the fuller's herb|quasi ignis conflans, et quasi herba fullonum]], etc., [[Mal 3:3|he shall purify the sons of Levi, and shall refine them as gold|purgabit filios Levi, et colabit eos quasi aurum]].

paras.t: Insuper Propheta sacerdotes magistratusque templi redarguens, ait: Usquequo judicatis iniquitatem, id est, quamdiu judicando approbabitis verba et dicta eorum qui Domino Salvatori obloquuntur, dicentes eum esse seductorem, et facies peccatorum sumitis, id est, falsos testes laudatis et acceptatis, qui falsum testimonium contra Christum locuti sunt?
paras.en: Further, the Prophet, rebuking the priests and magistrates of the temple, says: [[81:2|How long will you judge unjustly|Usquequo judicatis iniquitatem]], that is, how long will you approve by your judgment the words and sayings of those who speak against the Lord the Saviour, saying that he is a seducer[[Matt 27:63||]], [[81:2|and accept the persons of the wicked|et facies peccatorum sumitis]], that is, praise and accept the false witnesses who spoke false witness against Christ[[Matt 26:59||]][[Matt 26:60||]][[Matt 26:61||]]?

paras.t: Judicate egeno et pupillo, id est Christo: qui erat egenus, quoniam non habuit ubi caput reclinaret; et pupillus, quoniam sicut in cœlis habuit Patrem sine matre, ita in terris Matrem sine patre. Humilem et pauperem, id est Christum, qui ait, Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde, justificate, id est, justum esse asserite, et nolite contra eum blasphemias dicere. Eripite pauperem Christum de morte, et non Barabbam homicidam atque latronem: cujus contrarium, o principes sacerdotum, fecistis, persuadentes populo ut peterent Barabbam, Jesum vero perderent; et egenum Christum de manu peccatoris, scilicet Judæ proditoris, Pilati vel Caiphæ, liberate.
paras.en: [[81:3|Judge for the needy and fatherless|Judicate egeno et pupillo]], that is, for Christ: who was needy, because he had not [[Matt 8:20|where to lay his head|ubi caput reclinaret]]; and fatherless, because, as in heaven he had a Father without a mother, so on earth he had a Mother without a father; [[81:3|do justice to|justificate]] [[81:3|the humble and the poor|Humilem et pauperem]], that is, to Christ, who says: [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]; that is, declare him just, and do not speak blasphemies against him. [[81:4|Rescue the poor|Eripite pauperem]], Christ, from death, and not Barabbas, the murderer and robber: the contrary of which you did, O chief priests, when you [[Matt 27:20|persuaded the people that they should ask Barabbas and make Jesus away|persuadentes populo ut peterent Barabbam, Jesum vero perderent]]; [[81:4|and deliver the needy|et egenum]], Christ, [[81:4|out of the hand of the sinner|de manu peccatoris]], namely of Judas the traitor, of Pilate or of Caiphas.

paras.t: Nescierunt hi principes Judæorum Jesum esse Christum, quoniam excæcavit eos malitia eorum. Et si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent. Unde Petrus loquens Judæis: Fratres, ait, scio quia per ignorantiam fecistis, sicut et principes vestri. Neque intellexerunt doctrinam ipsius esse a Deo, sed dixerunt: Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram. Miracula quoque ipsius, principi dæmonum adscripserunt. In tenebris perfidiæ ambulant: propterea movebuntur omnia fundamenta terræ: id est, terra Judæorum tam horribiliter vastabitur, destruetur, et comburentur civitates ipsius, habitatoresque occidentur, quod præ nimia perturbatione videbitur ipsa terra moveri et interius concuti: quæ omnia a Romanis facta sunt loco et genti Judæorum, in ultionem sanguinis Christi, quemadmodum Christus prædixit.
paras.en: [[81:5|They have not known|Nescierunt]], these princes of the Jews, that Jesus was the Christ, because [[Wis 2:21|their own malice blinded them|excæcavit eos malitia eorum]]. And [[1 Cor 2:8|if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory|si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent]]. Whence Peter, speaking to the Jews: [[Acts 3:17|brethren|Fratres]], he says, [[Acts 3:17|I know that you did it through ignorance: as did also your rulers|scio quia per ignorantiam fecistis, sicut et principes vestri]]; [[81:5|nor understood|Neque intellexerunt]] that his doctrine was from God, but they said: [[Luke 23:2|We have found this man perverting our nation|Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram]]. His miracles too they ascribed to the prince of devils[[Matt 12:24||]]; [[81:5|they walk on|ambulant]] [[81:5|in darkness|In tenebris]] of unbelief: therefore [[81:5|all the foundations of the earth shall be moved|movebuntur omnia fundamenta terræ]]: that is, the land of the Jews will be laid waste so horribly and destroyed, its cities burnt and its inhabitants slain, that for the exceeding great turmoil the very earth will seem to be moved and shaken within: all of which was done by the Romans to the place and nation of the Jews, in vengeance for the blood of Christ, as Christ foretold[[Luke 19:43||]][[Luke 19:44||]].

paras.t: Ego dixi: Dii estis. Hoc de Judæorum principibus dicitur, propter rationem de aliis judicibus assignatam.
paras.en: [[81:6|I have said: You are gods|Ego dixi: Dii estis]]. This is said of the princes of the Jews, for the reason given in the case of the other judges.

paras.t: Surge, Deus, id est, tu, Unigenite Dei, qui in morte occubuisti, et in sepulcro dormisti, surge tertia die a mortuis; judica terram, id est, justo judicio damna hos terrenos atque carnales Judæos, quemadmodum alibi protestaris: Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea. Dies enim ultionis in corde meo, annus retributionis meæ venit. Quoniam tu hereditabis in omnibus gentibus: id est, populo Judæorum excæcato et derelicto, tu per prædicationem Apostolorum totum mundum hereditarie possidebis, regnando per fidem et gratiam in cordibus omnium gentium, ad fidem catholicam conversarum, quemadmodum de te ait Scriptura: Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei.
paras.en: [[81:8|Arise, O God|Surge, Deus]], that is, thou, Only-begotten of God, who didst lie down in death and sleep in the sepulchre, arise on the third day from the dead; [[81:8|judge thou the earth|judica terram]], that is, by just judgment condemn these earthly and carnal Jews, as thou declarest elsewhere: [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]]. [[Is 63:4|For the day of vengeance is in my heart, the year of my redemption is come|Dies enim ultionis in corde meo, annus retributionis meæ venit]] [the margin reads Is. lxxiii, 3, 4, for lxiii; Denis reads *annus retributionis*, "the year of my recompense", where the Douay-Rheims has "redemption"]. [[81:8|for thou shalt inherit among all the nations|Quoniam tu hereditabis in omnibus gentibus]]: that is, the people of the Jews being blinded and forsaken, thou shalt possess the whole world as an inheritance through the preaching of the Apostles, reigning by faith and grace in the hearts of all nations converted to the Catholic faith, as Scripture says of thee: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]].

paras.t: Hunc versum allegat Augustinus contra hæreticos, præcipue contra Donatistas, probans ex eo, quod Christus ex morte resurgens, non solum in uno angulo terræ seu modico populo, ut erat pars Donati, sed in toto mundo, in cunctisque gentibus per fidem regnaret. Adducitque Augustinus ad hoc verba Christi, quæ post resurrectionem dixit Apostolis: Eritis, inquiens, mihi testes in Jerusalem et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ. Ex quo sequi videtur, quod psalmus iste, secundum Augustinum, ad litteram de Christo passo et resurgente, atque principibus sacerdotum loquatur: maxime, quoniam (secundum Augustinum) argumentum per Scripturas pro fide non valet, nisi in sensu litterali.
paras.en: Augustine cites this verse against the heretics, especially against the Donatists, proving from it that Christ, rising from death, was to reign by faith not only in one corner of the earth or among a small people, as the party of Donatus was, but in the whole world and in all nations. And for this Augustine adduces the words of Christ which he spoke to the Apostles after the resurrection: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be|Eritis]], he says, [[Acts 1:8|witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|mihi testes in Jerusalem et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]]. From this it seems to follow that this psalm, according to Augustine, speaks in the literal sense of Christ suffering and rising again, and of the chief priests: above all because (according to Augustine) an argument from the Scriptures is of no force for the faith except in the literal sense.

paras.t: Postremo exhortandi essent ex psalmo præsenti pastores ovium Christi et judices populi christiani, ut in omni judicio circumspecti, cauti et justi consistant, pensantes se Judicem habere in cœlis, qui usque ad novissimum quadrantem exiget rationem ab eis, de omnibus quæ circa subditos commiserunt aut omiserunt.
paras.en: Lastly, the shepherds of Christ's sheep and the judges of the Christian people should be exhorted from the present psalm to be circumspect, careful and just in every judgment, considering that they have a Judge in heaven who will exact an account from them, to [[Matt 5:26|the last farthing|novissimum quadrantem]], of all that they have committed or omitted towards those under them.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus, a quo omnis justa operatio procedit et fortis consistit, justifica nos spiritu justitiæ et fortitudinis: ut non iniquitatem judicantes, nec facies peccatorum sumentes, justa et tibi placita semper peragere studeamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, from whom every just work proceeds and in whom it stands strong, justify us by the spirit of justice and fortitude: so that we may not [[81:2|judge unjustly|iniquitatem judicantes]] nor [[81:2|accept the persons of the wicked|facies peccatorum sumentes]], but may ever strive to accomplish what is just and pleasing to thee.

82.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI OCTOGESIMI SECUNDI : DEUS, QUIS SIMILIS ERIT TIBI ?
82.title_en: Exposition of the eighty-second psalm: O God, who shall be like to thee?

paras.t: […] iste est : Canticum, psalmus Asaph : id est, canticum præsens est psalmus Asaph, vel quia ab eo est editus, vel quia congregationi fidelium, per Asaph (qui interpretatur congregatio) designatæ, proponitur. Præsens enim psalmus ad litteram scriptus est de diversis hostibus populi Judæorum, et orat Propheta pro justa dejectione et pœna adversariorum populi sui.
paras.en: […] is this: [[82:1|A canticle of a psalm for Asaph|Canticum, psalmus Asaph]] [Denis reads *Canticum, psalmus Asaph*, "A canticle, a psalm of Asaph"]; that is, the present canticle is a psalm of Asaph, either because it was composed by him, or because it is set before the congregation of the faithful, which is signified by Asaph (which is interpreted *congregation*). For the present psalm was written, in the literal sense, about the various enemies of the people of the Jews, and the Prophet prays for the just overthrow and punishment of the adversaries of his people.

paras.t: Ait itaque : Deus æterne atque omnipotens, Deus Israel, Deus patrum nostrorum, quis similis erit tibi, similitudine univoca, essentiali et perfecta? Nullus utique, quoniam tu solus cuncta in infinitum excedis, et tui comparatione, est totus mundus quasi pulvis exiguus. De te enim veraciter scriptum est : Domine Deus, Creator omnium, terribilis et fortis, justus et misericors, qui solus es rex bonus, solus præstans, solus justus, omnipotens et æternus. Job quoque : Digne eum invenire non possumus; magnus fortitudine et judicio et justitia, et enarrari non potest : ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes, qui sibi videntur esse sapientes. Est tamen quædam similitudo imitativa, imperfecta, atque gratuita : et secundum hanc similis est creatura Creatori, sicut et omnis effectus assimilatur suæ causæ. Unde et Dominus : Faciamus, inquit, hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram. Ad hanc quoque deiformem similitudinem invitamur in novo ac veteri Testamento. Dominus namque ait : Sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum. Et Salvator : Perfecti estote, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est.
paras.en: He says, then: [[82:2|O God,|Deus]] eternal and almighty, God of Israel, God of our fathers, [[82:2|who shall be like to thee|quis similis erit tibi]] with a univocal likeness, essential and perfect [that is, a likeness in which the same nature is had in the same sense and in full]? None at all, since thou alone exceedest all things infinitely, and in comparison with thee the whole world is [[Is 40:15|as a little dust|quasi pulvis exiguus]]. For of thee it is truly written: [[2 Mach 1:24|O Lord God, Creator of all things, dreadful and strong, just and merciful, who alone art the good king|Domine Deus, Creator omnium, terribilis et fortis, justus et misericors, qui solus es rex bonus]], [[2 Mach 1:25|Who alone art gracious, who alone art just, and almighty, and eternal|solus præstans, solus justus, omnipotens et æternus]]. Job too: [[Job 37:23|We cannot find him worthily: he is great in strength, and in judgment, and in justice, and he is ineffable|Digne eum invenire non possumus; magnus fortitudine et judicio et justitia, et enarrari non potest]]: [[Job 37:24|Therefore men shall fear him, and all that seem to themselves to be wise, shall not dare to behold him|ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes, qui sibi videntur esse sapientes]]. There is, however, a certain likeness of imitation, imperfect and freely given: and according to this the creature is like the Creator, as every effect too is made like its cause. Hence the Lord too: [[Gen 1:26|Let us make|Faciamus]], he says, [[Gen 1:26|man to our image and likeness|hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram]]. To this godlike likeness we are also invited in the New and the Old Testament. For the Lord says: [[Lev 11:44|Be holy because I am holy|Sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum]][[Lev 19:2||]]. And the Saviour: [[Matt 5:48|Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect|Perfecti estote, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est]].

paras.t: Quoniam ergo non est tibi similis, ne taceas, id est, noli dissimulare injurias tibi ac populo tuo illatas, sed vindica eas, neque compescaris, Deus, id est, ne videaris compesci sustinendo blasphemias perfidorum, sed omnipotentiam tuam ulciscendo declara.
