Quoniam ecce inimici tui, videlicet adversarii nostri pagani, sonuerunt, id est, irrationabiliter contra te locuti sunt, et tubis in prælio cecinerunt, atque cum fremitu super nos famulos tuos irruerunt ; et qui oderunt te, scilicet inimici prædicti, extulerunt caput, id est, cervicem contra te erexerunt, præsumptuose cogitando, superbe loquendo, contumaciterque agendo.
paras.en: Since, therefore, there is none like to thee, [[82:2|hold not thy peace|ne taceas]], that is, do not pass over in silence the wrongs done to thee and to thy people, but avenge them, [[82:2|neither be thou still, O God|neque compescaris, Deus]] [*compescaris*, literally "be held back"], that is, do not seem to be held back, bearing with the blasphemies of the faithless, but show forth thy almighty power by taking vengeance. [[82:3|For lo, thy enemies|Quoniam ecce inimici tui]], namely our pagan adversaries, [[82:3|have made a noise|sonuerunt]], that is, have spoken against thee without reason, and have sounded their trumpets in battle, and have rushed with uproar upon us thy servants; [[82:3|and they that hate thee|et qui oderunt te]], namely the enemies aforesaid, [[82:3|have lifted up the head|extulerunt caput]], that is, have raised their neck against thee, thinking presumptuously, speaking proudly, and acting stubbornly.

paras.t: Super populum tuum, puta Judæos, malignaverunt, id est, fecerunt malum consilium, tractantes populum tuum omnino exstinguere, et cogitaverunt adversus sanctos tuos, Prophetas et Nazaræos, ac reliquos religiosos. Dixerunt : Venite, et disperdamus, id est, diversimode perdamus, eos de gente, id est de aliis populis, occidendo eos, ne amplius inter populos demorentur. Nec solum voluerunt vitam populi tui exstinguere, verum etiam ejus memoriam tollere : ideo additur, et non memoretur nomen Israel ultra, id est, tam funditus destruamus civitates et templum ac populum Hebræorum, ut nemo de cetero recordetur eorum, neque reliquiæ aliquæ eorum permanerent.
paras.en: [[82:4|against thy people|Super populum tuum]], namely the Jews, [[82:4|They have taken a malicious counsel|malignaverunt]] [the Latin runs *Super populum tuum malignaverunt consilium*, literally "against thy people they have made malicious a counsel"], that is, they have formed an evil plan, plotting to wipe out thy people altogether, [[82:4|and have consulted against thy saints|et cogitaverunt adversus sanctos tuos]], the Prophets and Nazarites and the other religious. [[82:5|They have said: Come and let us destroy|Dixerunt : Venite, et disperdamus]], that is, let us destroy in divers ways, [[82:5|them, so that they be not a nation|eos de gente]] [*de gente*, literally "from the nation"], that is, from among the other peoples, by killing them, so that they may no longer dwell among the peoples. And they wished not only to extinguish the life of thy people, but also to take away its memory: therefore it is added, [[82:5|and let the name of Israel be remembered no more|et non memoretur nomen Israel ultra]], that is, let us destroy the cities and the temple and the people of the Hebrews so utterly that no one will remember them any more, and no remnant of them remain.

paras.t: Quoniam cogitaverunt unanimiter, id est pari consensu in malo ; simul adversum te testamentum, id est forte pactum et male propositum, disposuerunt tabernacula Idumæorum, id est habitatores Idumææ, videlicet nati ex semine Esau : qui alio nomine dictus est Edom, a quo Idumæi nomen sortiti sunt; et Ismaelitæ, id est populi nati de Ismaele filio Abrahæ, fratre Isaac. Quemadmodum enim Esau persequebatur Jacob, volens eum occidere, sicut habetur in Genesi; et Ismael Isaac, ut dicit Apostolus ad Galatas : sic Idumæi persequebantur Judæos de Jacob descendentes; similiter Ismaelitæ. Propter quod ait Abdias propheta : Propter iniquitatem in fratrem tuum Jacob operiet te confusio, et peribis in æternum. In die quando capiebant alieni exercitum ejus, tu quoque eras quasi unus ex eis. Moab, id est Moabitæ nati de Moab filio Lot, et Agareni, id est filii Abrahæ ex Agar ancilla Saræ. Quæ Agar alio nomine appellatur Cetura, ut aliqui dicunt : quæ legitur peperisse multos filios Abrahæ post mortem Saræ conjugis suæ, sicut in Genesi patet.
paras.en: [[82:6|For they have contrived with one consent|Quoniam cogitaverunt unanimiter]], that is, with equal agreement in evil; [[82:6|they have made a covenant together against thee|simul adversum te testamentum]], that is, a strong pact and an evil design [the Latin runs *simul adversum te testamentum disposuerunt*, with the peoples named next as the subject], [[82:7|The tabernacle of the Edomites|tabernacula Idumæorum]], that is, the inhabitants of Idumea, namely those born of the seed of Esau, who by another name was called Edom[[Gen 25:30||]], from whom the Idumeans took their name; [[82:7|and the Ishmahelites|et Ismaelitæ]], that is, the peoples born of Ismael the son of Abraham, the brother of Isaac[[Gen 25:12||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxv, 15, in the list of Ismael's sons; Ismael is named son of Abraham at 25:12]. For just as Esau persecuted Jacob, wishing to kill him, as we have it in Genesis[[Gen 27:41||]], and Ismael persecuted Isaac, as the Apostle says to the Galatians[[Gal 4:29||]], so the Idumeans persecuted the Jews descended from Jacob, and likewise the Ismaelites. For which reason Abdias the prophet says: [[Abd 1:10|for the iniquity against thy brother Jacob, confusion shall cover thee, and thou shalt perish for ever|Propter iniquitatem in fratrem tuum Jacob operiet te confusio, et peribis in æternum]]. [[Abd 1:11|In the day|In die]] [[Abd 1:11|when strangers carried away his army captive|quando capiebant alieni exercitum ejus]], [[Abd 1:11|thou also wast as one of them|tu quoque eras quasi unus ex eis]]. [[82:7|Moab|Moab]], that is, the Moabites born of Moab the son of Lot, [[82:7|and the Agarens|et Agareni]], that is, the sons of Abraham by Agar, the handmaid of Sara. This Agar, as some say, is called by another name Cetura[[Gen 25:1||]], who is read to have borne Abraham many sons after the death of Sara his wife, as is plain in Genesis[[Gen 25:2||]].

paras.t: Gebal, sic dictus, et Ammon, id est Ammonitæ filii Ammon, filii Lot, et Amalec, id est Amalecitæ de Amalec nati. Qui Amalec primo impugnavit filios Israel, quando egrediebantur Ægyptum et in deserto meabant, ut dicitur in Exodo, ubi sic legitur : Quum elevaret Moyses manus, vincebat Israel ; si autem paululum remisisset, vincebat Amalec. Alienigenæ, id est Philistæi : nam in Hebræo habetur, Philistæi : qui erant Judæis valde molesti ; cum habitantibus Tyrum, id est cum Tyriis. Quamvis etiam Tyrii confœderati essent Hebræis tempore Hiram regis sui, qui habuit fœdus cum David et Salomone, ut legitur secundo et tertio Regum : postea tamen ruptum est fœdus pacis eorum. Etenim Assur venit cum illis, id est, Assyrii facti sunt in adjutorium filiis Lot, id est Moabitis et Ammonitis : ex quo videtur, quod filii Lot fuerunt principales adversarii Israelitarum in prælio de quo agitur hic.
paras.en: [[82:8|Gebal|Gebal]], so called [that is, a people of that name], [[82:8|and Ammon|et Ammon]], that is, the Ammonites, sons of Ammon the son of Lot[[Gen 19:38||]], [[82:8|and Amalec|et Amalec]], that is, the Amalecites born of Amalec. This Amalec was the first to attack the children of Israel, when they were going out of Egypt and journeying in the desert, as is said in Exodus[[Ex 17:8||]], where we read thus: [[Ex 17:11|when Moses lifted up his hands, Israel overcame; but if he let them down a little, Amalec overcame|Quum elevaret Moyses manus, vincebat Israel ; si autem paululum remisisset, vincebat Amalec]]. [[82:8|the Philistines|Alienigenæ]] [in the Latin *Alienigenæ*, "foreigners"], that is, the Philistines: for in the Hebrew it reads *Philistines*: they were very troublesome to the Jews; [[82:8|with the inhabitants of Tyre|cum habitantibus Tyrum]], that is, with the Tyrians. For although the Tyrians too were in alliance with the Hebrews in the time of Hiram their king, who had a league with David and Solomon, as we read in the second and third books of Kings[[2 Kings 5:11||]][[3 Kings 5:12||]], yet afterwards their league of peace was broken. [[82:9|Yea, and the Assyrian also is joined with them|Etenim Assur venit cum illis]], that is, the Assyrians [[82:9|are come to the aid of the sons of Lot|facti sunt in adjutorium filiis Lot]], namely of the Moabites and Ammonites: from which it appears that the sons of Lot were the chief adversaries of the Israelites in the war spoken of here.

paras.t: Fac illis, o Deus Israel, sicut Madian et Sisaræ, sicut Jabin in torrente Cison. Quoniam liber iste metrice scriptus est, contingit sæpe in eo variari ordinem rerum gestarum in narratione, sicut et nunc. Nam in libro Judicum legitur Jabin rex Chanaan oppressisse filios Israel ; habuitque principem militiæ Sisaram. Porro in eodem libro leguntur filii Israel dati in manus Madianitarum. Orat ergo Propheta ut Deus dejiciat prædictos inimicos populi sui, qui erant tempore regum Juda et Israel vel postea, sicut debellavit Madianitas et Sisaram. Madianitas namque miraculose debellavit per Gedeonem et trecentos viros ejus. Similiter exercitum Jabin regis Chanaan expugnavit per manum Barac. Et Jahel uxor Haber Cinæi, clavum infixit in tempus Sisaræ, eumque occidit. Sicut Jabin in torrente Cison : nam juxta torrentem Cison percussus est populus Jabin a filiis Israel. Unde Debora prophetes dixit ad Barac : Vade, et educ exercitum in montem Thabor ; ego autem adducam omnem multitudinem ejus. In hoc quoque torrente quidam submersi leguntur, juxta illud : Torrens Cison traxit cadavera eorum.
paras.en: [[82:10|Do to them|Fac illis]], O God of Israel, [[82:10|as thou didst to Madian and to Sisara: as to Jabin at the brook of Cisson|sicut Madian et Sisaræ, sicut Jabin in torrente Cison]]. Since this book is written in metre, it often happens in it that the order of events is varied in the telling, as here too. For in the book of Judges we read that Jabin king of Chanaan oppressed the children of Israel, and had Sisara as the captain of his army[[Judg 4:2||]]; and further on in the same book the children of Israel are read to have been given into the hands of the Madianites[[Judg 6:1||]] [so in Judges Sisara comes before Madian, while the psalm names Madian first]. The Prophet therefore prays that God may cast down the aforesaid enemies of his people, who were in the time of the kings of Juda and Israel or after, as he overthrew the Madianites and Sisara. For he overthrew the Madianites miraculously through Gedeon and his three hundred men[[Judg 7:1||]]. Likewise he defeated the army of Jabin king of Chanaan by the hand of Barac. And Jahel, the wife of Haber the Cinite, drove a nail into the temple of Sisara and killed him[[Judg 4:17||]][[Judg 4:21||]]. [[82:10|as to Jabin at the brook of Cisson|Sicut Jabin in torrente Cison]]: for it was beside the torrent Cison that the people of Jabin were smitten by the children of Israel. Hence Debbora the prophetess said to Barac: [[Judg 4:6|Go, and lead an army to Mount Thabor|Vade, et educ exercitum in montem Thabor]]; [[Judg 4:7|And I will bring|ego autem adducam]] [[Judg 4:7|all his multitude|omnem multitudinem ejus]]. In this torrent too some are read to have been drowned, according to that text: [[Judg 5:21|The torrent of Cison dragged their carcasses|Torrens Cison traxit cadavera eorum]].

paras.t: Disperierunt in Endor, quia prope locum sic dictum occisi sunt ; facti sunt ut stercus terræ, quia insepulti manserunt, et pro nihilo reputabantur.
paras.en: [[82:11|Who perished at Endor|Disperierunt in Endor]], because they were slain near the place so called; [[82:11|and became as dung for the earth|facti sunt ut stercus terræ]], because they remained unburied and were counted as nothing.

paras.t: Pone principes eorum, scilicet Idumæorum, Ismaelitarum, Moabitarum, Agarenorum, etc., de quibus dictum est paulo ante, sicut Oreb et Zeb, id est, eos occide, quemadmodum occidisti Oreb et Zeb, et Zebee et Salmana principes Madianitarum, quos occidisti per Gedeonem et adjutores ipsius. Oreb enim et Zeb Ephratæi decollaverunt ; Zebee autem et Salmana ipsemet Gedeon interfecit, ut scribitur in libro Judicum.
paras.en: [[82:12|Make their princes|Pone principes eorum]], namely those of the Edomites, the Ismaelites, the Moabites, the Agarens, etc., of whom mention was made a little before, [[82:12|like Oreb, and Zeb|sicut Oreb et Zeb]], that is, slay them as thou didst slay Oreb and Zeb, [[82:12|and Zebee, and Salmana|et Zebee et Salmana]], princes of the Madianites, whom thou didst slay through Gedeon and his helpers. For the Ephraimites [Latin *Ephratæi*] beheaded Oreb and Zeb[[Judg 7:25||]], while Gedeon himself slew Zebee and Salmana[[Judg 8:21||]], as is written in the book of Judges.

paras.t: Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam : id est, fac illos instabiles, currentes, et non perficientes, quemadmodum rota movetur motu circulari, in quo non est finem certum accipere ; et pone eos sicut stipulam ante faciem venti, quatenus sicut stipula a vento movetur et cadit, sic ipsi tua virtute succumbant. Sicut ignis qui comburit silvam igne succensam, seu ligna silvæ in ignem projecta, et sicut flamma comburens montes, id est loca montana quæ igne succenduntur cum habitaculis suis ; ita persequeris illos prænominatos, videlicet Moab, Agarenos, Gebal et Ammon, in tempestate tua, id est in ira furoris tui, id est in districta ultione justitiæ tuæ. Hoc totum impletum est. Nam sicut ignis consumit ligna silvarum, sic Deus frequenter consumpsit hostes populi sui Israel, ut patet in occisione exercitus regis Assyriorum ac aliis multis. Et in ira tua turbabis eos, vertendo eos in fugam, aut terrendo, occidendove eos. Potest quoque hæc pœna, sicut et sequens, referri ad damnationem inferni, et ad pœnam futuri judicii.
paras.en: [[82:14|O my God, make them like a wheel|Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam]]: that is, make them unsteady, running and never reaching the end, as a wheel is moved with a circular motion, in which no fixed end is to be found; and make them [[82:14|as stubble before the wind|sicut stipulam ante faciem venti]], so that as stubble is moved by the wind and falls, so they may give way before thy power. [[82:15|As fire which burneth the wood|Sicut ignis qui comburit silvam]] set alight with fire, or the timber of the wood thrown into the fire, [[82:15|and as a flame burning mountains|et sicut flamma comburens montes]], that is, mountain places which are set alight by fire together with their dwellings; [[82:16|So shalt thou pursue them|ita persequeris illos]], those named before, namely Moab, the Agarens, Gebal and Ammon, [[82:16|with thy tempest|in tempestate tua]], that is, in the wrath of thy fury, that is, in the strict vengeance of thy justice. All this has been fulfilled. For as fire consumes the timber of the woods, so God often consumed the enemies of his people Israel, as is plain in the slaughter of the army of the king of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 19:35||]] [the margin gives IV Reg. xii, 35; the slaughter of the Assyrian army is at 4 Kings 19:35] and in many other cases. [[82:16|and shalt trouble them in thy wrath|Et in ira tua turbabis eos]], by turning them to flight, or by terrifying or slaying them. This punishment too, like the next, can also be referred to the damnation of hell and to the punishment of the judgment to come.

paras.t: Imple facies eorum ignominia, ita ut manifeste dejiciantur, omnibusque innotescat quod victi sunt ; et quærent nomen tuum, Domine. Quidam enim gentilium videntes populum Judæorum tam mirabiliter prævalere, et se tam inopinate divina virtute succumbere, ad Deum Israel convertebantur.
paras.en: [[82:17|Fill their faces with shame|Imple facies eorum ignominia]], so that they may be openly cast down, and it may be known to all that they are vanquished; [[82:17|and they shall seek thy name, O Lord|et quærent nomen tuum, Domine]]. For some of the Gentiles, seeing the people of the Jews prevail so wonderfully, and themselves give way so unexpectedly before the divine power, were converted to the God of Israel.

paras.t: Erubescant et conturbentur in sæculum sæculi, in die finalis judicii : sicut de impiis dicitur, Turbabuntur timore horribili ; et in libro Judicum, Sic pereant inimici tui, Domine. Et confundantur et pereant. Sæpe eumdem sensum resumit ad designandum zelum justitiæ, qua adversus malignos movetur. Non enim ex impatientia aut rancore, sed ex zelo justitiæ et pro Dei honore ista precatur.
paras.en: [[82:18|Let them be ashamed and troubled for ever and ever|Erubescant et conturbentur in sæculum sæculi]], on the day of the final judgment: as it is said of the wicked, [[Wis 5:2|shall be troubled with terrible fear|Turbabuntur timore horribili]]; and in the book of Judges, [[Judg 5:31|So let all thy enemies perish, O Lord|Sic pereant inimici tui, Domine]]. [[82:18|and let them be confounded and perish|Et confundantur et pereant]]. He often takes up the same sense again, to show the zeal for justice by which he is moved against the wicked. For he prays for these things not out of impatience or rancour, but out of zeal for justice and for the honour of God.

paras.t: Et cognoscant, per experientiam suæ damnationis in futuro, seu per experientiam pœnæ in sæculo isto, quia nomen tibi Dominus, id est, quod tu vere et digne Dominus appellaris, tanquam universorum princeps, provisor et judex, cujus in ditione cuncta sunt posita, qui singulis tribuis quod merentur, qui per Isaiam testatus es : Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum ; gloriam meam alteri non dabo. Cognoscant quoque, quoniam tu solus Altissimus in omni terra, id est, quod non solum Judæa in tua potestate consistit, sed quod omnia regna terræ et dii eorum tuo imperio sunt subjecta : sicut et Ezechias rex ait : Deus Israel, tu es Deus solus omnium regnorum terræ.
paras.en: [[82:19|And let them know|Et cognoscant]], by the experience of their damnation in the world to come, or by the experience of punishment in this world, [[82:19|that the Lord is thy name|quia nomen tibi Dominus]], that is, that thou art truly and worthily called Lord, as the prince, provider and judge of all things, in whose dominion all things are placed[[Esth 13:9||]], who renderest to each what he deserves, who hast testified through Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name: I will not give my glory to another|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum ; gloriam meam alteri non dabo]]. Let them know also that [[82:19|thou alone art the most High over all the earth|tu solus Altissimus in omni terra]], that is, that not only Judea stands in thy power, but that all the kingdoms of the earth and their gods are subject to thy rule: as king Ezechias too says: [[Is 37:16|God of Israel|Deus Israel]], [[Is 37:16|thou alone art the God of all the kingdoms of the earth|tu es Deus solus omnium regnorum terræ]].

82.title: EXPOSITIO MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI OCTOGESIMI SECUNDI.
82.title_en: Moral exposition of the same eighty-second psalm.

paras.t: Moralem autem intelligentiam prosequendo, longe subtilior ac fructuosior est psalmi præsentis expositio : sic enim materia psalmi hujus, est secundus Christi adventus et persecutio dura ac gravis fidelium a perversis. Triplex autem fuit Ecclesiæ persecutio. Prima erat in gladio tyrannorum ; secunda, in verbis hæreticorum ; tertia, in malis operibus fratrum fallacium. Quarta restat, quæ ex omnibus istis constabit, videlicet persecutio Antichristi, qui potestate armorum, verbis disputationum, operibus simulatarum virtutum, fideles persequetur, occidet, et plurimos fallet. Quatenus igitur tempus illud gravissimæ persecutionis abbrevietur, orat nunc Asaph pro secundo Christi adventu, seu acceleratione finalis judicii : quando, secundum Apostolum, Dominus Jesus spiritu oris sui occidet, et illustratione adventus sui damnabit seu destruet Antichristum : de quo et Isaias, Spiritu (inquit) labiorum suorum interficiet impium.
paras.en: Following the moral sense, the exposition of the present psalm is far subtler and more fruitful: for taken so, the matter of this psalm is the second coming of Christ and the hard and grievous persecution of the faithful by the wicked. Now the persecution of the Church has been threefold. The first was by the sword of tyrants; the second, by the words of heretics; the third, by the evil works of false brethren. A fourth remains, which will be made up of all these, namely the persecution of Antichrist, who by the power of arms, by the words of disputations, and by the works of feigned virtues will persecute the faithful, slay them, and deceive very many. So that the time of that most grievous persecution may be shortened[[Mark 13:20||]], Asaph now prays for the second coming of Christ, that is, for the hastening of the final judgement: when, according to the Apostle, [[2 Thess 2:8|the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth|Dominus Jesus spiritu oris sui occidet]], and [[2 Thess 2:8|with the brightness of his coming|illustratione adventus sui]] will condemn, or [[2 Thess 2:8|destroy|destruet]], Antichrist; of whom Isaias also says: [[Is 11:4|with the breath|Spiritu]] (he says) [[Is 11:4|of his lips he shall slay the wicked|labiorum suorum interficiet impium]].

paras.t: Admirans itaque Asaph virtutem et gloriam quibus Christus in judicio apparebit, ita orditur : Deus, quis similis erit tibi? id est, o unice Fili Patris æterni, Domine Christe, universorum judex, quis similis tibi in sapientia discernendi inter bonum et malum? Nullus utique, juxta illud in Job : Ecce Deus magnus, vincens scientiam nostram. Quis similis tibi in æquitate cunctis reddendi quod promerentur? Nullus utique, quia de te scriptum est : Non est apud Dominum Deum nostrum iniquitas, nec personarum acceptio, nec acceptio munerum. Quis similis tibi in potestate exsequendi sententiam justi judicii? Nullus utique, quia de te ait sermo divinus : Potestas ejus, potestas æterna quæ non auferetur, et regnum ejus quod non corrumpetur.
paras.en: Marvelling, then, at the power and glory in which Christ will appear at the judgement, Asaph begins thus: [[82:2|O God, who shall be like to thee?|Deus, quis similis erit tibi?]] That is: O only Son of the eternal Father, Lord Christ, judge of all, who is like to thee in wisdom to discern between good and evil? No one, surely, according to that saying in Job: [[Job 36:26|Behold, God is great, exceeding our knowledge|Ecce Deus magnus, vincens scientiam nostram]]. Who is like to thee in equity, to render to all what they deserve? No one, surely, for of thee it is written: [[2 Par 19:7|there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor desire of gifts|Non est apud Dominum Deum nostrum iniquitas, nec personarum acceptio, nec acceptio munerum]] [Denis reads "nor acceptance of gifts" where the Vulgate has "nor desire of gifts"]. Who is like to thee in power to carry out the sentence of just judgement? No one, surely, for of thee the divine word says: [[Dan 7:14|his power is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed|Potestas ejus, potestas æterna quæ non auferetur, et regnum ejus quod non corrumpetur]].

paras.t: Quum ergo, o Christe, sis talis tantusque judex, ne taceas, jam regnans in cœlo, aut in secundo tuo adventu judicioque futuro, quemadmodum in primo tuo adventu a judicio tacuisti, dicens : Ego non judico quemquam ; et iterum : Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum. Neque compescaris, Deus, id est, ne retraharis ab ultione justissima ; sed verum esse ostende quod de te profitetur divina Scriptura : Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas ; opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet eis.
paras.en: Since, then, O Christ, thou art so great a judge, [[82:2|hold not thy peace|ne taceas]], now that thou reignest in heaven, or in thy second coming and the judgement to come, as at thy first coming thou didst keep silent from judging, saying: [[John 8:15|I judge not any man|Ego non judico quemquam]]; and again: [[John 3:17|God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world: but that the world may be saved by him|Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum]]. And [[82:2|neither be thou still, O God|Neque compescaris, Deus]], that is, do not hold back from most just vengeance; but show to be true what the divine Scripture declares of thee: [[Job 34:10|far from God be wickedness, and iniquity from the Almighty|Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas]]; [[Job 34:11|For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them|opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet eis]].

paras.t: Quoniam ecce inimici tui, videlicet mali Christiani, hæretici, Judæi, pagani, sonuerunt, id est, irrationabiliter voces iniquas protulerunt, verba vana, vacua et perversa effando. Et ideo non ait, Locuti sunt, sed, Sonuerunt, quoniam non more hominum rationabiliter sunt locuti, sed more ferarum irrationabilem strepitum effuderunt, murmurando, contradicendoque tibi : quod tempore Antichristi maxime fiet. Tunc namque Antichristiani in liberam vocem prorumpent, sed irrationabilem prorsus, ut sonitus magis vocetur quam sermo. Et qui oderunt te, id est, qui malitiam diligunt et vitia amant, extulerunt caput, sicut superbi caput suum erigere solent. Vel, Extulerunt caput, id est propriam rationem, confidentes in suo ingenio, atque se ipsos sapientes esse putantes. Vel, Extulerunt caput, id est, Antichristum exaltaverunt, credentes esse filium Dei, et Dominum Jesum blasphemantes : idcirco non ait, Capita, sed, Caput, quoniam omnes in unum filium perditionis, scilicet Antichristum, consentient.
paras.en: [[82:3|For lo, thy enemies|Quoniam ecce inimici tui]], namely bad Christians, heretics, Jews and pagans, [[82:3|have made a noise|sonuerunt]], that is, have irrationally uttered wicked words, pouring out speech vain, empty and perverse. And so he does not say *They have spoken*, but *They have made a noise*, because they have not spoken reasonably, as men do, but have poured out an irrational din, as beasts do, murmuring and gainsaying thee: which will happen above all in the time of Antichrist. For then the followers of Antichrist will break out into free speech, but speech so wholly irrational that it should be called noise rather than discourse. [[82:3|and they that hate thee|Et qui oderunt te]], that is, who love malice and are fond of vices, [[82:3|have lifted up the head|extulerunt caput]], as the proud are wont to raise their head. Or, [[82:3|have lifted up the head|Extulerunt caput]], that is, their own reason, trusting in their own wit and thinking themselves wise[[Rom 1:22||]]. Or, [[82:3|have lifted up the head|Extulerunt caput]], that is, they have exalted Antichrist, believing him to be the Son of God, and blaspheming the Lord Jesus: and therefore he does not say *heads*, but *head*, because all will agree together in one son of perdition, namely Antichrist.

paras.t: S. Augustinus affirmat, quod nullius pene conscientia potest Deum odisse ; sed quia frequenter ait Scriptura, quod peccatores Deum odio habent, debemus absolute concedere, quod impii Deum habeant odio. Quemadmodum enim divinis præceptis obtemperantes, Deum amare dicuntur ; sic Deo rebelles, eum utique odio habent. Nonne Deum odivit, de cujus ore semel audivi, quum eum ad meliora hortarer, atque divinæ majestatis beatitudinem commendarem, Mallem, inquit, Deum non esse, quam me vestram vitam, videlicet Cartusiensis ordinis conversationem, debere subire? Quomodo ergo verum est quod asserit Augustinus? Et respondendum, sicut et S. Thomas respondet, quod aliquis dicitur Deum odisse dupliciter : primo, secundum se ipsum ; secundo, ratione sui effectus. Primo modo pene nullus Deum odit, quum ipse sit pura infinitaque bonitas ; sed secundo modo multi Deum odiunt, videlicet propter pœnas quas pro peccatis infligit, vel quia eorum voluntati placentia prohibet, displicentia jubet.
paras.en: St Augustine affirms that hardly anyone's conscience can hate God; but since Scripture often says that sinners hate God[[Ps 20:9||]][[Ps 73:23||]], and elsewhere, we must grant without qualification that the wicked hate God. For as those who obey the divine commandments are said to love God, so those who rebel against God surely hate him. Did not he hate God from whose mouth I once heard, when I was exhorting him to better things and commending to him the blessedness of the divine majesty: "I would rather," he said, "that God did not exist than that I should have to take up your life," that is, the way of life of the Carthusian order? How then is what Augustine asserts true? The answer is, as St Thomas also answers, that a man is said to hate God in two ways: first, as he is in himself; secondly, by reason of his effects. In the first way hardly anyone hates God, since he is pure and infinite goodness; but in the second way many hate God, namely because of the punishments he inflicts for sins, or because he forbids what pleases their will and commands what displeases it.

paras.t: Super populum tuum, id est contra Christianos, malignaverunt consilium tyranni et fratres falsi, quatenus eos vel blandimentis alliciant, vel pœnis et minis deterreant, aut aliquo modo a Deo avertant, lædant, aut occidant ; et cogitaverunt adversus sanctos tuos : quia non solum mediocres famulos tuos, sed et viros perfectos subvertere quærunt, imitantes in hoc caput suum diabolum, de quo Dominus ait ad sanctum Job : Absorbebit fluvium, et non mirabitur, et habet fiduciam quod influat Jordanis in os ejus. Ubi per fluvium designantur animæ sæculares, vagæ atque instabiles, quas absorbet diabolus, nec inde miratur, id est, hoc pro magno non reputat ; per Jordanem vero intelliguntur animæ religiosæ ac sanctæ, quas confidit dæmon se posse decipere. Ideo membra ejus, videlicet reprobi, non solum communem populum christianum, sed et sanctos fallere student.
paras.en: [[82:4|against thy people|Super populum tuum]], that is, against the Christians, the tyrants and false brethren [[82:4|have taken a malicious counsel|malignaverunt consilium]], so as either to entice them with blandishments, or to frighten them off with punishments and threats, or in some way to turn them away from God, to harm them, or to kill them; [[82:4|and have consulted against thy saints|et cogitaverunt adversus sanctos tuos]]: for they seek to overthrow not only thy middling servants but also perfect men, imitating in this their head, the devil, of whom the Lord says to holy Job: [[Job 40:18|he will drink up a river, and not wonder: and he trusteth that the Jordan may run into his mouth|Absorbebit fluvium, et non mirabitur, et habet fiduciam quod influat Jordanis in os ejus]] [the margin gives Job xi, 18; the passage is Job 40:18]. Here by the river are signified worldly souls, wandering and unstable, which the devil drinks up, and does not wonder at it, that is, he does not reckon it a great thing; but by the Jordan are understood religious and holy souls, which the demon trusts he can deceive. Therefore his members, namely the reprobate, strive to deceive not only the common Christian people but the saints as well.

paras.t: Dixerunt isti adversarii tui, o Domine : Venite, et disperdamus eos, scilicet Christianos, de gente : id est, omnes interficiamus, ne quisquam eorum de cetero inter gentes commoretur ; et non memoretur nomen Israel, id est militantis Ecclesiæ, ultra. Multi namque tyranni conati sunt cultum et fidem atque memoriam populi christiani prorsus auferre.
paras.en: [[82:5|They have said|Dixerunt]], these adversaries of thine, O Lord: [[82:5|Come and let us destroy them|Venite, et disperdamus eos]], namely the Christians, [[82:5|so that they be not a nation|de gente]]: that is, let us kill them all, so that none of them may dwell any longer among the nations; [[82:5|and let the name of Israel be remembered|et non memoretur nomen Israel]], that is, of the Church militant, [[82:5|no more|ultra]]. For many tyrants have tried to do away altogether with the worship, the faith and the memory of the Christian people.

paras.t: Simul adversum te testamentum disposuerunt tabernacula Idumæorum et Ismaaelitæ, Moab et Agareni, Gebal et Ammon, etc. Quemadmodum populi isti adversati sunt Synagogæ Judæorum, sic designati per eos adversantur Ecclesiæ Christianorum. Qui autem intelligantur per populos istos, pensare debemus ex interpretationibus nominum horum. Sicut in Genesi legitur, dum natus esset Esau, apparuit totus in modum pellis hispidus atque sanguineus : propterea vocatum est nomen ejus Edom. Idumæi ergo ab Edom nomen sortiti, interpretantur sanguinei seu terreni : per quos designantur avari, terrenarum rerum amatores inordinati. Ismaelitæ interpretantur inobedientes : per quos hoc loco designantur, qui propriam voluntatem sequuntur, non Deo, sed sibimetipsis obtemperantes : per quos significantur gulosi, qui non Christo, sed suo ventri deserviunt. Moab interpretatur, ex patre : per quem designantur perversi, ex Deo secundum naturam exorti, sed propter malitiam ex patre diabolo nati : quibus Christus ait, Vos ex patre diabolo estis. Per quem exprimuntur luxuriosi, quoniam filia major ipsius Lot, genuit Moab ex patre proprio. Agareni interpretantur, alieni seu advenæ : per quos figurantur falsi fratres, qui solo nomine inter electos computantur, sicut Joannes asserit : In nobis erant, sed non erant ex nobis ; nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum. Gebal interpretatur, vallis vana : sicque per eum explicantur fallaciter humiles atque hypocritæ, de quibus in libro Job habetur : Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei. Et in Ecclesiastico : Est qui nequiter se humiliat ; interiora autem ejus plena sunt dolo. Talibus ait Salvator : Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus, Deus autem novit corda vestra ; quia quod hominibus altum est, abominatio est ante Deum. Per Ammon, qui interpretatur, populus turbidus, designati sunt iracundi, quoniam ira rationem perturbat, et hominem stulto assimilat. Propter quod Ecclesiastes dicit : Ne sis velox ad irascendum, quia ira in sinu stulti requiescit ; et Job, Virum stultum interficit iracundia. Per Amalec, quem genuit Eliphaz primogenitus Esau, et interpretatur, populus lingens, significantur adulatores fallaciter blandientes. Quo vitio se caruisse ostendit Apostolus, dicens : Neque aliquando fuimus in sermone adulationis.
paras.en: [[82:6|they have made a covenant together against thee|Simul adversum te testamentum disposuerunt]], [[82:7|The tabernacle of the Edomites, and the Ishmahelites: Moab, and the Agarens|tabernacula Idumæorum et Ismaaelitæ, Moab et Agareni]], [[82:8|Gebal, and Ammon|Gebal et Ammon]], etc. As these peoples opposed the Synagogue of the Jews, so those signified by them oppose the Church of the Christians. And who are to be understood by these peoples we must weigh from the interpretations of their names. As is read in Genesis, when Esau was born he appeared [[Gen 25:25|hairy like a skin|totus in modum pellis hispidus]] all over, and blood-red; and for this reason his name was called Edom [the name Edom is given at Gen 25:30]. The Edomites, then, who take their name from Edom, are interpreted "bloody" or "earthy": by them are signified the covetous, inordinate lovers of earthly things. The Ishmaelites are interpreted "disobedient": by them are signified in this place those who follow their own will, obeying not God but themselves: and by them are signified the gluttons, who [[Rom 16:18|serve not Christ our Lord but their own belly|non Christo, sed suo ventri deserviunt]]. Moab is interpreted "from the father": by him are signified the perverse, who sprang from God according to nature, but through malice are born of their father the devil: to whom Christ says, [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]. By him too the lustful are expressed, since the elder daughter of Lot himself bore Moab by her own father[[Gen 19:33||]][[Gen 19:37||]]. The Agarens are interpreted "strangers" or "newcomers": by them are figured false brethren, who are counted among the elect in name only, as John declares: They were among us, [[1 John 2:19|but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have remained with us|sed non erant ex nobis ; nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum]] [Denis reads "they were among us" where the Vulgate has "they went out from us"]. Gebal is interpreted "vain valley" [that is, a lowliness that is empty]: and so by it are set forth the falsely humble and the hypocrites, of whom it is said in the book of Job: [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God|Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei]]. And in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 19:23|There is one that humbleth himself wickedly, and his interior is full of deceit|Est qui nequiter se humiliat ; interiora autem ejus plena sunt dolo]] [the margin gives Ecclus. xiv, 23; the passage is Ecclus 19:23]. To such the Saviour says: [[Luke 16:15|you are they who justify yourselves before men, but God knoweth your hearts. For that which is high to men is an abomination before God|Vos estis qui justificatis vos coram hominibus, Deus autem novit corda vestra ; quia quod hominibus altum est, abominatio est ante Deum]]. By Ammon, which is interpreted "a troubled people", are signified the wrathful, since anger troubles the reason and makes a man like a fool. For this reason Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 7:10|Be not quickly angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of a fool|Ne sis velox ad irascendum, quia ira in sinu stulti requiescit]]; and Job: [[Job 5:2|Anger indeed killeth the foolish|Virum stultum interficit iracundia]] [Denis reads *virum*, "the foolish man", where the Vulgate has *vere*, "indeed"]. By Amalec, whom Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau begot[[Gen 36:12||]], and which is interpreted "a licking people", are signified flatterers, who fawn deceitfully. The Apostle shows that he was free of this vice, saying: [[1 Thess 2:5|neither have we used at any time the speech of flattery|Neque aliquando fuimus in sermone adulationis]].

paras.t: Alienigenæ, id est Philistæi, qui interpretantur, cadentes potione : per quos designantur vitiis atque luxuria ebrii ; cum habitantibus Tyrum, id est cum invidis. Tyrus enim interpretatur angustia : invidi autem in se ipsis torquentur, quasi loco angusto conclusi. Hi utique omnes populo præelecto ad vitam repugnant. Etenim Assur venit cum illis. Per Assur, qui interpretatur deprimens seu elatus, significatur diabolus, qui in profundum peccando prolapsus est, et in mentis tumorem erectus ; qui etiam rex est super omnes filios superbiæ, sicut in libro Job scriptum est. Facti sunt in adjutorium filiis Lot, id est declinantibus. Lot namque interpretatur declinans : quo signantur apostatæ angeli, qui cum principe suo Lucifero declinaverunt a Deo. Dæmonum vero adjutores sunt homines impii jam prædicti, quemadmodum justi adjutores seu cooperatores sunt Dei.
paras.en: [[82:8|the Philistines|Alienigenæ]] [the Latin has *alienigenæ*, "men of another race"], that is, the Philistines, which is interpreted "falling by drink": by them are signified those drunk with vices and with lust; [[82:8|with the inhabitants of Tyre|cum habitantibus Tyrum]], that is, with the envious. For Tyre is interpreted "straitness": and the envious are tormented within themselves, as though shut up in a narrow place. All these, surely, fight against the people chosen beforehand for life. [[82:9|Yea, and the Assyrian also is joined with them|Etenim Assur venit cum illis]] [the Latin has "Assur came with them"]. By Assur, which is interpreted "pressing down" or "lifted up", is signified the devil, who by sinning fell into the depth, and was raised up into swelling of mind; and of whom it is also written in the book of Job: [[Job 41:25|he is king over all the children of pride|rex est super omnes filios superbiæ]]. [[82:9|they are come to the aid of the sons of Lot|Facti sunt in adjutorium filiis Lot]], that is, of those who turn aside. For Lot is interpreted "turning aside": by which are signified the apostate angels, who with their prince Lucifer turned aside from God. And the helpers of the demons are the wicked men already named, just as the just are the helpers, or fellow workers, of God.

paras.t: Deinde orat Ecclesia pro dejectione et justa punitione istorum, potius futura tormenta prædicendo, quam mala imprecando, vel conformando se divinæ justitiæ, vel orando ut in præsenti castigentur, ne æternaliter condemnentur, aut diutius vivendo gravius prævaricentur, et ne bonum commune, atque Ecclesiam diutius persequi permittantur. Fac illis sicut Madian et Sisaræ, etc. Madian, qui erat filius Abrahæ ex Cetura, interpretatur, relinquens judicium : quo figurantur qui se ipsos non judicant, neque Dei futurum judicium metuunt : propter quod salvari non poterunt, secundum quod in libro Job quidam dicit, Numquid qui non amat judicium, sanari potest? Per Sisaram, qui interpretatur, exclusio gaudii, illi signantur qui propter mundi et carnis suæ delicias, æternæ beatitudinis gaudia a se ipsis excludunt, sicut de talibus ait Dominus Jesus : Væ vobis qui nunc ridetis, quia lugebitis et flebitis. Salomon quoque : Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia. Est tamen quædam spiritualis lætitia non abjicienda, de qua dicit Apostolus : Gaudete in Domino semper. Per Jabin, qui interpretatur sapiens, intelliguntur carnaliter sapientes, quibus ab Isaia dicitur : Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris. Per Cison, quod interpretatur duritia, intelliguntur obstinati in malo, seu induratio cordis.
paras.en: Next the Church prays for the casting down and just punishment of these, foretelling torments to come rather than calling down evils; either conforming herself to the divine justice, or praying that they may be chastised in the present, lest they be condemned eternally, or lest by living longer they transgress more grievously, and lest they be allowed to persecute the common good and the Church any longer. [[82:10|Do to them as thou didst to Madian and to Sisara|Fac illis sicut Madian et Sisaræ]], etc. Madian, who was the son of Abraham by Cetura[[Gen 25:2||]], is interpreted "forsaking judgement": by which are figured those who do not judge themselves and do not fear the judgement of God to come: for which reason they cannot be saved, according to what someone says in the book of Job: [[Job 34:17|Can he be healed that loveth not judgment?|Numquid qui non amat judicium, sanari potest?]] By Sisara, which is interpreted "shutting out of joy", are signified those who for the delights of the world and of their flesh shut out from themselves the joys of eternal blessedness, as the Lord Jesus says of such: [[Luke 6:25|Woe to you that now laugh: for you shall mourn and weep|Væ vobis qui nunc ridetis, quia lugebitis et flebitis]]. Solomon too: [[Eccles 7:5|The heart of the wise is where there is mourning, and the heart of fools where there is mirth|Cor sapientium ubi tristitia, et cor stultorum ubi lætitia]]. Yet there is a certain spiritual joy not to be cast away, of which the Apostle says: [[Phil 4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always|Gaudete in Domino semper]]. By Jabin, which is interpreted "wise", are understood the carnally wise, to whom Isaias says: [[Is 5:21|Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes|Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris]]. By Cison, which is interpreted "hardness", are understood the obstinate in evil, or hardness of heart.

paras.t: Orat ergo Ecclesia, ut persecutoribus suis fiat sicut peccatoribus nunc prædictis sæpius factum est ; præcipue tamen ista petuntur contra exercitum Antichristi. Pone principes eorum, scilicet persecutorum Ecclesiæ, sicut Oreb et Zeb et Zebee, etc. Per Oreb, qui interpretatur siccitas, designantur aridi a gratia Dei : de qua ariditate scriptum est, O pastor et idolum derelinquens gregem, brachium ejus ariditate siccabitur, id est, operatio ejus gratia Dei privabitur. Per Zeb, qui interpretatur lupus, significantur rapaces. Per Zebee, qui interpretatur, victima lupi, figurantur qui peccando facti sunt præda diaboli. Per Salmana, qui interpretatur, umbra commotionis, seu, in pravitate perfectus, signantur instabiles, seu cum diabolo unum corpus effecti, qui simul cum illo projiciendi sunt in caminum ignis æterni.
paras.en: The Church prays, then, that it may be done to her persecutors as was often done to the sinners just named; yet these things are asked above all against the army of Antichrist. [[82:12|Make their princes|Pone principes eorum]], namely of the persecutors of the Church, [[82:12|like Oreb, and Zeb, and Zebee|sicut Oreb et Zeb et Zebee]], etc. By Oreb, which is interpreted "dryness", are signified those dried up from the grace of God: of which dryness it is written: [[Zach 11:17|O shepherd, and idol, that forsaketh the flock|O pastor et idolum derelinquens gregem]], [[Zach 11:17|his arm shall quite wither away|brachium ejus ariditate siccabitur]], that is, his working shall be deprived of the grace of God. By Zeb, which is interpreted "wolf", are signified the rapacious. By Zebee, which is interpreted "the wolf's victim", are figured those who by sinning have become the prey of the devil. By Salmana, which is interpreted "shadow of commotion", or "perfect in wickedness", are signified the unstable, or those made one body with the devil, who are to be cast together with him into the furnace of everlasting fire.

paras.t: Omnes principes eorum, id est, capitaneos peccatorum jam prænominatorum, justos vastantium ; qui principes dixerunt : Hereditate possideamus sanctuarium Dei, id est terram, possessiones, ecclesias Christianorum, vel potius ipsos Christianos, subjiciendo eos nostro imperio, legi et cultui. Populus namque fidelis sanctuarium Dei vocatur, juxta illud Apostoli : Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos. Cetera exponenda sunt sicut in præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: [[82:12|All their princes|Omnes principes eorum]], that is, the captains of the sinners already named, who lay waste the just; the princes [[82:13|Who have said|qui principes dixerunt]]: [[82:13|Let us possess the sanctuary of God for an inheritance|Hereditate possideamus sanctuarium Dei]], that is, the land, the possessions, the churches of the Christians, or rather the Christians themselves, by subjecting them to our rule, law and worship. For the faithful people is called the sanctuary of God, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 3:17|the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos]]. The rest is to be expounded as in the preceding article.

paras.t: Psalmus iste contra iniquos satis terribiliter invehitur ; et quam inæstimabili confusione ac pœna in futuro judicio sint plectendi, qui modo non convertuntur, in ipso ostenditur. Quod vero hic dicitur, Imple facies eorum ignominia, accipi potest de tarda et infructuosa pœnitentia reproborum, non ex amore justitiæ, sed timore pœnarum de peccato dolentium : de quorum pœnitentia in libro Sapientiæ scriptum est : Dicentes intra se, pœnitentiam agentes, et præ angustia spiritus gementes ; et sequitur : Talia dixerunt in inferno. Denique versus iste, Imple facies eorum ignominia, accipi potest in bono ; eritque sensus : Da, Domine, ut in præsenti refutentur et contemnantur ac vituperentur, secundum quod peccatores sunt, quatenus ex ipsa sua ignominia cessent peccare. Quemadmodum enim per adulationem et laudem falsissimam roboratur peccator in culpa, ita per ignominiam sibi illatam, a malo retrahitur, dum se ab omnibus argui contuetur. Et ita salubriter quærent nomen tuum, Domine, per pœnitentiam salutarem et veram compunctionem. Pertinere quippe videtur hoc ad eos, de quibus in Evangelio scriptum est : Compelle intrare.
paras.en: This psalm inveighs against the wicked terribly enough; and it shows with what inestimable confusion and punishment those who do not now turn back are to be struck at the judgement to come. But what is said here, [[82:17|Fill their faces with shame|Imple facies eorum ignominia]], can be taken of the late and fruitless repentance of the reprobate, who grieve over sin not from love of justice but from fear of punishment: of whose repentance it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:3|Saying within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit|Dicentes intra se, pœnitentiam agentes, et præ angustia spiritus gementes]]; and there follows: [[Wis 5:14|Such things as these the sinners said in hell|Talia dixerunt in inferno]]. Lastly, this verse, [[82:17|Fill their faces with shame|Imple facies eorum ignominia]], can be taken in a good sense; and the sense will be: Grant, O Lord, that in the present they may be rebuked, despised and reproached, as the sinners they are, so that through their very shame they may cease to sin. For as a sinner is strengthened in his fault by flattery and most false praise, so by shame brought upon him he is drawn back from evil, when he sees himself reproved by all. [[82:17|and|Et]] so, to their salvation, [[82:17|they shall seek thy name, O Lord|quærent nomen tuum, Domine]], by saving penance and true compunction. For this seems to belong to those of whom it is written in the Gospel: [[Luke 14:23|compel them to come in|Compelle intrare]].

paras.t: Precatio. Deus supernæ majestatis, cui non est similis, propter multitudinem peccatorum non disperdas nos de gente electorum ; sed clementi bonitate facias nomen nostrum memorari in Israel in æternum.
paras.en: Prayer. O God of supernal majesty, to whom none is like: do not for the multitude of our sins [[82:5|destroy|disperdas]] us from the nation of the elect; but in thy merciful goodness cause our [[82:5|name|nomen]] to be [[82:5|remembered|memorari]] in Israel for ever.
